roles.title: Physician Assistants
aliases: Emergency Medicine Physician Assistant (Emergency Medicine PA)
Family Medicine PA (Family Medicine Physician Assistant)
Surgical Critical Care Physician Assistant (Surgical Critical Care PA)
Urgent Care PA (Urgent Care Physician Assistant)
roles.description: Provide healthcare services typically performed by a physician, under the supervision of a physician. Conduct complete physicals, provide treatment, and counsel patients. May, in some cases, prescribe medication. Must graduate from an accredited educational program for physician assistants.

tasks.label: Make tentative diagnoses and decisions about management and treatment of patients.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

tasks.label: Interpret diagnostic test results for deviations from normal.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

tasks.label: Prescribe therapy or medication with physician approval.

tasks.label: Obtain, compile, and record patient medical data, including health history, progress notes, and results of physical examination.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Outpatient primary care or specialty clinic visit: the PA interviews the patient about the chief complaint, history of present illness, past medical/surgical/family/social history, medications and allergies, reconciles the med list, and records a SOAP/office note plus exam findings and orders in the EHR before the next patient.

Hospital inpatient rounding: the PA compiles overnight events, vitals, nursing notes, lab and imaging results and consultant recommendations from the chart, then writes a daily progress note and updates the problem list and assessment/plan for the attending.

Emergency department or urgent care intake: the PA takes a rapid history from the patient, EMS crew or family member (sometimes an incomplete or unreliable historian), pulls prior visit records, and documents the H&P and disposition note under time pressure and frequent interruption.

Comprehensive H&P for a surgical pre-op, hospital admission, or new specialty consult: the PA gathers outside records, prior operative and pathology reports and imaging, obtains a detailed history, and dictates or types a long structured H&P that must satisfy documentation and billing requirements.

Non-face-to-face records work: telehealth or telephone encounters, reviewing and abstracting faxed or scanned outside records into the chart, completing forms, physicals and disability/insurance documentation, and closing out unfinished notes at the end of the day.

tasks.label: Examine patients to obtain information about their physical condition.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Primary-care clinic exam room: comprehensive/annual physical of an ambulatory adult — general inspection, vitals, HEENT with otoscope and ophthalmoscope, neck and lymph node palpation, cardiac and pulmonary auscultation, abdominal palpation/percussion, extremity, skin and focused neurologic exam, findings interpreted and documented.

Office or urgent-care focused problem exam: sore throat, ear pain, cough, rash, abdominal pain, or ankle sprain — pharyngeal and otoscopic inspection, chest auscultation, targeted palpation for tenderness, joint range-of-motion and stability testing, neurovascular check; patient may be in pain and only partly cooperative.

Emergency department exam of an undifferentiated or injured patient on a gurney: primary/secondary survey, wound inspection and probing, abdominal and chest exam, spine and extremity palpation, pupil and mental-status assessment, often with gowning, monitors, noise, and time pressure.

Hospital inpatient rounding or post-operative bedside exam: patient supine in bed with IV lines, drains, dressings and telemetry — wound and incision inspection, lung and abdominal exam, edema and calf assessment, often requiring repositioning of a weak or elderly patient.

Specialty-clinic focused exam: orthopedic joint special tests, full-body dermatologic skin survey with dermatoscope, breast/pelvic or genitourinary exam, or detailed cardiac/vascular exam, requiring specific hands-on maneuvers, draping, and consent/rapport.

Exam outside a controlled clinical facility: house call or home-visit assessment, skilled-nursing/assisted-living bedside exam, mobile or occupational health screening, or sports-sideline evaluation — variable lighting, furniture, and patient positioning taken as found.

sources.system: Telemedical examination cabin (MITI / TU Munich, Franka Emika arms)
sources.developer: Technical University of Munich, University Hospital rechts der Isar (MITI Research Group)
sources.title: Toward telemedical diagnostics—clinical evaluation of a robotic examination system for emergency patients
sources.claim: A full telemedical examination cabin with robotic arms performed vital signs, auscultation, percussion, palpation, oral inspection and swabbing on 20 real emergency-department patients, but every robot movement was commanded in real time by a remote physician using a lead robot — i.e., continuous teleoperation, not autonomy.
sources.transferJustification: Directly the task: robotic auscultation, percussion and palpation of chest and abdomen on emergency patients. It shows the most complete robotic physical-exam platform to date is fully teleoperated, so it cannot support a positive judgment.

sources.system: Unitree G1 humanoid clinical surrogate (UCSD ARClab)
sources.developer: University of California San Diego (Atar, Liang, Richter, Yip et al.)
sources.title: Humanoids in Hospitals: A Technical Study of Humanoid Robot Surrogates for Dexterous Medical Interventions
sources.claim: A Unitree G1 humanoid was evaluated on seven clinical procedures including physical-examination tasks (stethoscope auscultation, ultrasound, laryngoscopy, needle tasks) in a lab/simulation setting; all execution was through bimanual teleoperation by a human operator.
sources.transferJustification: Covers physical-examination sub-tasks with the same instruments a PA uses; establishes that humanoid execution of exam maneuvers is teleoperated, so it cannot substantiate autonomous completion.

sources.system: Collaborative robotic platform for autonomous auscultation
sources.developer: Lopes, Coelho & Silva (ISEP / Polytechnic of Porto)
sources.title: Development of a Collaborative Robotic Platform for Autonomous Auscultation
sources.claim: A UR3e arm with RGB-D vision autonomously locates auscultation points on a person and places an electronic stethoscope, tested on a handful of subjects in a laboratory; the system only captures sounds for a physician to interpret and performs no other exam component.
sources.transferJustification: Auscultation is one component of the physical exam; the system is autonomous but covers only stethoscope placement in a lab, with no inspection, palpation, percussion, special testing, or clinical interpretation, so it does not complete any whole exam instance.

sources.developer: Tsinghua University / Beijing Tsinghua Changgung Hospital research group
sources.title: Beyond hospital reach: Autonomous lightweight ultrasound robot for liver sonography
sources.claim: An autonomous lightweight ultrasound robot with an AI agent acquired standard liver imaging planes on volunteers and patients in a hospital ultrasound department, autonomously positioning and scanning after being mounted on the abdomen.
sources.transferJustification: Related task (sonographic imaging on a patient's body) showing state-of-the-art autonomous patient contact in a hospital. It does not transfer to the PA exam: it is a single instrumented imaging protocol on a prepared abdomen, not multi-system inspection, palpation, percussion, otoscopy, joint testing, or bedside clinical judgment.

tasks.label: Administer or order diagnostic tests, such as x-ray, electrocardiogram, and laboratory tests.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

tasks.label: Instruct and counsel patients about prescribed therapeutic regimens, normal growth and development, family planning, emotional problems of daily living, and health maintenance.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

tasks.label: Perform therapeutic procedures, such as injections, immunizations, suturing and wound care, and infection management.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Routine immunization or medication injection for a cooperative adult in a primary care/urgent care exam room: verify patient and order, take a prefilled or drawn-up dose (flu, Tdap, B12, depo, IM ketorolac/steroid), select and prep the deltoid or gluteal site, inject, bandage, watch for reaction and document.

Immunizations/injections in children or anxious, uncooperative or frail patients: several vaccines in one visit, a squirming infant or toddler held by a parent, distraction and restraint, small limb sites, rapid reassessment after the shot.

Traumatic laceration repair in urgent care or an ED: infiltrate lidocaine, irrigate and explore the wound for foreign bodies, trim or undermine edges if needed, place interrupted or layered sutures (or staples/adhesive) on face, scalp, hand or extremity, dress and instruct the patient.

Wound care visits in clinic or at the hospital bedside: remove a soiled dressing, assess and measure a surgical, diabetic-foot, venous or pressure wound, cleanse and sharply debride devitalized tissue, pack undermined areas, apply the appropriate dressing/offloading, culture if infected.

Abscess and infection management procedures: incision and drainage of a skin abscess or paronychia after local anesthesia, expressing purulence, irrigation, packing or loop drain placement, wound culture, removal of an infected nail or foreign body, and follow-up rechecks.

Joint and soft-tissue injections/aspirations in an orthopedic, sports-medicine or family clinic: position the patient, palpate landmarks or use ultrasound, aspirate a knee or bursal effusion, inject corticosteroid, viscosupplement or trigger-point anesthetic, dress the site and check tolerance.

sources.system: Aletta Autonomous Robotic Phlebotomy Device (ADOPT trial)
sources.title: Vitestro Publishes Landmark Peer-Reviewed Multicenter Clinical Study of Autonomous Robotic Phlebotomy in Clinical Chemistry
sources.claim: Vitestro's Aletta autonomous robotic phlebotomy device performed needle insertion and blood collection on 1,633 patients across three hospital outpatient phlebotomy departments in a multicenter trial, with 94.5% first-stick success and a 0.6% mild adverse-event rate.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: diagnostic venipuncture. It is the same physical act as a PA injection - aseptic percutaneous needle placement into a seated patient's arm in a clinic room - at a higher precision requirement (a millimetre-scale vein rather than deltoid muscle), and Aletta runs the whole workflow (tourniquet, site selection, puncture, bandage) autonomously at human first-stick rates.

sources.title: Vitestro Raises $70 Million in Oversubscribed Series B Financing to Advance Autonomous Robotic Phlebotomy and Commercial Readiness
sources.claim: Aletta is CE-marked and being deployed in ... settings in Europe as of March 2026 (not FDA-authorized in the US), i.e. an autonomous needle-procedure robot in routine hospital/laboratory use.
sources.transferJustification: Same related task as above (venipuncture); establishes the deployment maturity of the cited system inside institution-run clinical facilities.

sources.title: Aletta® - Vitestro
sources.claim: Aletta executes the complete patient-facing needle procedure end to end rather than a sub-step, with one supervisor able to oversee up to three devices.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: venipuncture; shows the robot completes the whole needle procedure with only intermittent human supervision, the transfer-relevant property for an injection encounter.

sources.title: Robot performs autonomous needle-less injection | Robotics and Automation
sources.claim: Cobionix's Cobi platform autonomously performed an intramuscular injection (needle-free jet injection), using vision and LiDAR to detect the patient and select the injection site, with no healthcare professional involved in the act.

sources.title: ARTAS ® Robotic Hair Restoration Treatments
sources.claim: The ARTAS iX robotic system, FDA-cleared and installed in hair-restoration clinics, uses image guidance to identify and punch out follicular units from a seated patient's scalp and to create recipient sites - repeated automated skin-penetrating instrument work on a conscious patient under physician supervision.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic follicular unit extraction. Like an injection it is repeated, image-guided percutaneous puncture of a conscious patient's skin in an ordinary clinic treatment room, executed by the machine at clinically accepted quality; corroborates that autonomous skin-puncture procedures are commercially fielded in E2 settings.

sources.title: Robot performs first laparoscopic surgery without human help | ScienceDaily
sources.claim: The most advanced autonomous soft-tissue suturing system, STAR, sutured bowel in anesthetized pigs in a research operating room; no autonomous system has been shown repairing skin lacerations in patients.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous soft-tissue suturing. Cited to bound rather than support laceration repair: the work is in animals in a research OR with human-placed fluorescent markers and covers none of the anesthesia, irrigation, exploration or dressing steps of a traumatic wound repair.

sources.system: DLR MIRO/MICA robotic waterjet debridement system
sources.developer: DLR Institute of Robotics and Mechatronics / University of Freiburg
sources.title: Robotic waterjet wound debridement – Workflow adaption for clinical application and systematic evaluation of a novel technology
sources.claim: Robotic autonomous wound debridement has been evaluated only on simulated contaminated wounds with a DLR MIRO/MICA waterjet setup in the laboratory, not on patients.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: sharp/waterjet wound debridement. Cited to bound the wound-care instance: it is a bench study on simulated wounds and does not substantiate a bedside wound-care visit.

tasks.label: Visit and observe patients on hospital rounds or house calls, updating charts, ordering therapy, and reporting back to physician.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Hospitalist / internal-medicine ward rounds: PA works through a list of 12-18 inpatients on a med-surg floor, enters each room, reviews overnight events with the patient and nurse, performs a focused exam (heart/lung auscultation, abdominal palpation, edema and mental-status check, IV site inspection), correlates with labs and telemetry, writes the daily progress note in the EHR, enters orders (PT/OT consult, medication changes, fluids, imaging), and presents the patient to the attending physician.

Surgical service post-op rounds: early-morning rounds on post-operative inpatients, including lifting gowns/blankets and taking down dressings to inspect incisions, checking drain output and JP bulbs, removing staples or lines, assessing pain and ambulation, redressing wounds, updating operative-day progress notes, ordering diet advancement and physical therapy, and reporting findings to the surgeon before the OR day starts.

ICU / step-down critical care rounds: PA assesses intubated or line-dependent patients (vent settings, sedation level, pressors, central lines, catheters), performs neuro and cardiopulmonary exam on a patient surrounded by equipment and often restrained or unresponsive, participates in multidisciplinary rounds, documents the daily assessment/plan, and adjusts orders with the intensivist.

Specialty consult and follow-up rounds: PA travels between units (ED, floors, telemetry) to see a handful of consult patients for cardiology, orthopedics, infectious disease or similar, takes a focused history, performs the relevant targeted exam (joint range of motion, wound/hardware check, cardiac exam), writes the consult or follow-up note, orders therapy or testing, and communicates recommendations to the attending and primary team.

Skilled nursing facility / post-acute rounds: PA rounds on nursing-home or rehab residents in their rooms, many with dementia or limited mobility, performs bedside or chairside exams (skin/pressure-ulcer checks, lungs, extremities), reviews nursing notes and vitals, updates the facility chart, orders labs, therapy or medication changes, and reports to the supervising physician.

House calls / home-based primary care: PA drives to a homebound patient's private residence with a portable bag (stethoscope, BP cuff, pulse oximeter, glucometer, wound supplies), navigates a cluttered home with pets and family present, examines the patient in bed or a recliner, checks medications on the kitchen table, charts on a laptop, orders home health therapy or DME, and reports back to the physician.

sources.title: Diligent Robotics hits 1M picks with Moxi robot in healthcare settings - The Robot Report
sources.claim: Moxi, the most widely deployed autonomous hospital mobile manipulator in the US, autonomously navigates hospital corridors and elevators but performs supply and pharmacy deliveries — non-patient-facing logistics — not patient assessment.
sources.transferJustification: Related task (intra-hospital logistics) shows autonomous mobility in the same E2 hospital environment, but it involves no patient contact, no examination, and no clinical documentation, so it does not transfer to a rounding visit.

sources.title: InTouch Health Receives FDA Clearance For The RP-VITA Remote Presence Robot
sources.claim: The only FDA-cleared robot for bedside patient encounters navigates autonomously but exists to place a remote human physician at the bedside; all clinical observation, judgment and documentation is done by the remote doctor.
sources.transferJustification: Related task (remote consult rounds) occurs in the same hospital setting, but the robot is a video conduit: it cannot touch, examine, chart, or order, and the clinical work remains with the teleoperating physician.

sources.system: Robotic auscultation platform (6-DoF cobot arm, LiDAR camera, spring-loaded stethoscope end-effector)
sources.developer: University of Tokyo / collaborators (Tsumura et al.)
sources.title: Toward Fully Automated Robotic Platform for Remote Auscultation
sources.claim: Research robotic auscultation platforms can autonomously locate and place a stethoscope on a seated cooperative subject's chest, but this is a single sub-step of the exam performed on a lab bench rig, with no history-taking, wound check, charting, or ordering.
sources.transferJustification: Related task (auscultation) is one component of the focused bedside exam in rounds; it substantiates only autonomous stethoscope placement on a cooperative seated subject in a fixtured lab cell, not a whole rounding visit on a hospitalized patient.

sources.system: Unitree G1 humanoid surrogate with bimanual teleoperation system
sources.title: Humanoids in Hospitals: A Technical Study of Humanoid Robot Surrogates for Dexterous Medical Interventions
sources.claim: State-of-the-art humanoid attempts at direct clinical tasks including physical examination were carried out entirely under bimanual teleoperation by human operators, not autonomously.
sources.transferJustification: Related task (robot-performed physical examination and bedside interventions) is the physical core of rounds; however it is teleoperated throughout, so by the autonomy rule it cannot support a positive judgment at any tier.

sources.system: Automatic robot-driven wound 3D reconstruction system (7-DoF arm, RGB-D camera, 3D scanner)
sources.title: Automatic Robot-Driven 3D Reconstruction System for Chronic Wounds (Sensors)
sources.claim: A robot arm with an RGB-D camera and 3D scanner can autonomously scan and reconstruct chronic wounds, evaluated on models and on real patients in a clinical centre, but it only measures wound geometry — it does not remove or reapply dressings, assess drains, chart, or order therapy.
sources.transferJustification: Related task (wound assessment) matches the post-op incision check in surgical rounds, but the system performs non-contact measurement of an exposed wound presented to a fixed arm; it does not take down dressings or produce the clinical output of a rounding visit.

sources.system: Dr. Spot (Boston Dynamics Spot with contactless vital-sign sensing)
sources.developer: MIT / Brigham and Women's Hospital / Boston Dynamics
sources.title: Researchers develop dog-like robot nurse to remotely measure patients' vital signs | CNN Business
sources.claim: A quadruped robot fitted with cameras and a tablet was used to take contactless vital signs and enable a physician's remote interview with patients, in a research/pilot deployment where a clinician drove the interaction.
sources.transferJustification: Related task (vital-sign collection at the bedside) is a small part of a rounding visit; the robot was driven by clinicians and captured only vitals, providing no exam, documentation, orders, or hand-off.

tasks.label: Provide physicians with assistance during surgery or complicated medical procedures.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: First-assisting an open general, vascular, or cardiothoracic case in a hospital OR: positioning and draping the patient, holding and dynamically adjusting retractors, providing suction and sponge exposure, clamping and cutting sutures, assisting hemostasis, harvesting vein or closing fascia and skin, all while responding to the surgeon's verbal and non-verbal cues over a 1-4 hour case in a sterile field with bleeding, smoke, and shifting anatomy.

Assisting a laparoscopic or robotic-assisted case (cholecystectomy, hernia, colectomy, hysterectomy, prostatectomy): helping insufflate and place ports, driving/cleaning the laparoscope, providing counter-traction and grasping tissue through an assistant port, passing sutures and clips, exchanging instruments at the bedside during a da Vinci case, retrieving the specimen, and closing port sites.

Assisting an orthopedic or spine case in a hospital or ambulatory surgery center OR: positioning and holding the limb through range of motion, holding self-retaining and hand-held retractors against heavy soft tissue, irrigating and suctioning during reaming/sawing, mixing and delivering cement, assisting reduction and implant placement, then layered closure.

Assisting a bedside or procedure-suite complicated procedure: central line or chest tube placement in the ICU/ED, cardiac catheterization or EP procedure in the cath lab, endoscopy, or bronchoscopy — preparing and handing sterile equipment, holding the ultrasound probe or wire, applying pressure to the access site, managing sheaths/catheters, and dressing the site under fluoroscopy or ultrasound with the patient awake or sedated.

Assisting a cesarean section or other OB/GYN procedure in a labor-and-delivery OR, often urgent or emergent: retracting the bladder blade, applying fundal pressure, assisting delivery of the infant, suctioning amniotic fluid and blood, packing and exteriorizing the uterus, and closing the uterus, fascia, and skin under time pressure.

sources.system: FDA-cleared surgical robots (49 systems, incl. da Vinci, Senhance, Mako, TSolution One)
sources.developer: Various (Intuitive Surgical, Asensus, Stryker, Think Surgical, etc.)
sources.title: Levels of autonomy in FDA-cleared surgical robots: a systematic review — npj Digital Medicine
sources.claim: A 2024 systematic review of every surgical robot cleared by the FDA from 2015-2023 found that essentially all cleared systems operate under continuous surgeon control; none exhibit the high-level or full autonomy that would be needed to substitute for a human surgical assistant.
sources.transferJustification: Directly on point: these are the robotic systems present in the OR where the PA assists. It establishes that commercially available OR robots require direct, continuous surgeon control and cannot substitute for an assistant's independent judgment and action.

sources.title: Moon Surgical receives FDA clearance for ScoPilot on Maestro, industry's first AI-enhanced intraoperative capability, powered by NVIDIA Holoscan
sources.claim: The most advanced commercially deployed 'AI' surgical-assistant capability, Moon Surgical's ScoPilot on the Maestro system, holds and repositions the laparoscope but remains under the surgeon's direction and covers only camera-holding — one sub-step of the PA's first-assist role.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: laparoscopic camera holding, one duty of a PA assisting a minimally invasive case. It does not transfer to the full instance because the surgeon still directs the scope and the system performs none of the retraction, suction, suturing, specimen retrieval, or closure the assist role requires.

sources.system: SRT-H (Surgical Robot Transformer-Hierarchy) and STAR (Smart Tissue Autonomous Robot)
sources.title: Johns Hopkins teaches robot to perform a gallbladder removal on a realistic patient — The Robot Report
sources.claim: The most autonomous surgical robots demonstrated to date operate on animal or ex vivo tissue in research settings, execute a single phase of a procedure, and require human voice commands and corrections during the run; they perform surgeon tasks rather than the assistant role and have not been deployed on human patients.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous execution of surgical steps (dissection, clipping, cutting, suturing) on tissue. It bounds the state of the art — the closest autonomous tissue manipulation is a lab demo on animal/ex vivo tissue for one procedure phase, far short of performing an assistant's full role on a human patient.

sources.system: Robotic Scrub Nurse (RSN) with instrument prediction; Gestonurse
sources.developer: University hospital research groups (e.g., RWTH/Charité collaborators; Purdue University)
sources.title: Robotic scrub nurse to anticipate surgical instruments based on real-time laparoscopic video analysis — PMC
sources.claim: Robotic 'scrub nurse' systems that autonomously hand instruments to the surgeon remain research prototypes evaluated in laboratory or simulated settings, and cover only instrument handover, not tissue handling or exposure.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: intraoperative support by handing instruments. It does not transfer to the PA assist instance, which requires manipulating patient tissue (retraction, suction, suturing, closure) rather than passing tools, and these systems are unvalidated prototypes rather than deployed OR equipment.

tasks.label: Supervise and coordinate activities of technicians and technical assistants.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

tasks.label: Order medical and laboratory supplies and equipment.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

emergingTasks.label: Refer patients to other healthcare providers.
emergingTasks.status: Proposed for future data collection; not treated as established task evidence

roles.title: Anesthesiologist Assistants
roles.description: Assist anesthesiologists in the administration of anesthesia for surgical and non-surgical procedures. Monitor patient status and provide patient care during surgical treatment.

tasks.label: Provide airway management interventions including tracheal intubation, fiber optics, or ventilary support.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Routine elective adult case in a hospital OR or ambulatory surgery center: pre-oxygenate by face mask, bag-mask ventilate after induction, perform direct or video laryngoscopy and place an endotracheal tube, confirm with capnography/auscultation, secure the tube and start mechanical ventilation. Normal-to-moderately-difficult airway, patient supine on the OR table under the time pressure of apnea.

Short ambulatory case: insert a supraglottic airway (LMA/i-gel) after induction, seat and test it for seal and adequate ventilation, tape it, and maintain spontaneous or pressure-support ventilation, reseating or converting to intubation if the seal or airway is inadequate.

Ventilatory support of an already-intubated patient through a long case or a post-op ICU period: select the mode, set and continually titrate tidal volume, rate, PEEP and FiO2 to end-tidal CO2 and SpO2 targets, and readjust for pneumoperitoneum, position changes and lung-compliance changes.

Anticipated or encountered difficult airway: obese, restricted neck movement, limited mouth opening, or airway tumor. Awake or asleep flexible fiberoptic intubation through the mouth or nose, or hyperangulated video laryngoscopy with bougie/rigid stylet, often with topicalization and sedation and an anesthesiologist standing by.

Urgent or emergent airway: rapid-sequence induction for a full-stomach or trauma patient, airway management outside the main OR (ICU, ED, labor and delivery, endoscopy suite), rescue of laryngospasm, desaturation or a failed airway, or a pediatric airway. Soiled airway, unstable physiology, non-standard bed and lighting.

Emergence and extubation: suction the oropharynx and tube, assess return of airway reflexes and adequate spontaneous ventilation, remove the tube or SGA at the right moment, then support the airway with jaw thrust, oral airway and mask oxygen and treat obstruction or laryngospasm until the patient is safe for PACU.

sources.system: Robot-assisted tracheal intubation system based on a soft actuator
sources.developer: academic group (Int J Comput Assist Radiol Surg)
sources.title: A robot-assisted tracheal intubation system based on a soft actuator
sources.claim: A robotic arm plus hydraulically actuated soft bending actuator performed fully autonomous tracheal intubation, guided by object detection of airway landmarks and visual servoing, but only on an intubation training manikin on the bench.

sources.title: Introducing the world's first intubation robot — McGill Newsroom
sources.claim: The first robotic tracheal intubations in patients used the Kepler Intubation System, a video laryngoscope mounted on a robotic arm driven by a human operator with a joystick from a remote ...; it is not autonomous.

sources.title: First robotic tracheal intubations in humans using the Kepler intubation system (British Journal of Anaesthesia)
sources.claim: In the first human series, the Kepler robotic intubation system was used in 12 elective patients and succeeded in 11; the authors described it as a pilot requiring further study of safety and performance.

sources.title: Evaluation of a Novel, Image-Guided Robotic Intubation System (Anesthesia & Analgesia)
sources.claim: The most clinically advanced robotic intubation product, FDA-cleared Spiro-VISTA, is a handheld servo-operated flexible scope plus video laryngoscope that a clinician drives with a joystick; it succeeded in 30 difficult-airway patients, but the human operator performs the procedure.

sources.developer: UC Santa Barbara (Haggerty, Hawkes et al.)
sources.title: A soft robotic device for rapid and self-guided intubation (Science Translational Medicine)
sources.claim: A soft robotic intubation device that self-guides a tube into the trachea reached 100% success in manikins and cadavers, but it is inserted and advanced by a human user and has been tested only on cadavers, not living patients.

sources.title: Emerging technologies in airway management: a narrative review of intubation robotics and anatomical structure recognition algorithms
sources.claim: A 2025 review of intubation robotics concludes that autonomous intubation systems still require physician supervision and that multicenter randomized trials against conventional technique have yet to be done.

sources.title: Artificial intelligence-assisted tracheal intubation in humans: a prospective observational study of diagnostic accuracy (Anaesthesia)
sources.claim: Robotic-assisted intubation results obtained in manikins with the REALITI device did not carry over to human patients, per a 2026 Anaesthesia paper on AI-assisted intubation.

sources.title: Feasibility study on full closed-loop control ventilation (IntelliVent-ASV) in ICU patients with acute respiratory failure
sources.claim: INTELLiVENT-ASV, a fully automated closed-loop ventilation mode on commercial Hamilton ICU ventilators, ventilated 100 consecutive ICU patients from inclusion to extubation, automatically selecting oxygenation and ventilation settings without needing a switch to another mode.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: continuous machine titration of tidal volume, rate, PEEP and FiO2 to etCO2/SpO2 targets in intubated ICU and post-cardiac-surgery patients is the same ventilatory-support work the anesthesiologist assistant performs on an intubated patient, on the same equipment class, same monitored variables and same targets.

sources.title: Effect of Automated Closed-Loop Ventilation Versus Conventional Ventilation (ACTiVE) — ClinicalTrials.gov NCT04593810
sources.claim: Closed-loop INTELLiVENT-ASV is a commercially available fully automated ventilation mode and has been run against conventional ventilation in randomized ICU trials, requiring fewer manual adjustments while remaining safe and effective.
sources.transferJustification: Same transfer as above: automated titration of ventilator settings for intubated patients in a hospital critical-care setting is the ventilatory-support component of this task.

tasks.label: Assist anesthesiologists in monitoring of patients, including electrocardiogram (EKG), direct arterial pressure, central venous pressure, arterial blood gas, hematocrit, or routine measurement of temperature, respiration, blood pressure or heart rate.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Pre-induction setup in a hospital OR: the AA applies standard monitors to an awake patient on the OR table — peels and places 3–5 EKG electrodes at anatomic landmarks, wraps the NIBP cuff on the upper arm, clips the pulse-oximeter probe, connects cables, cycles the cuff and confirms clean tracings before induction.

Continuous intraoperative vigilance during a case: watching EKG, plethysmograph, capnograph, NIBP/arterial pressure, temperature and ventilator data, interpreting trends, answering alarms, and physically fixing artifacts (re-seating a pulse-ox probe, re-adhering a lead under the drapes, re-siting or re-cycling the cuff, repositioning a temperature probe) while charting values for the anesthesiologist.

Invasive hemodynamic monitoring in the OR: assembling and de-airing pressure tubing/transducer kits for an arterial line and central venous catheter, leveling to the phlebostatic axis, zeroing, checking waveform fidelity (square-wave test), fast-flushing a damped arterial trace, and reconciling arterial pressure with cuff readings during positioning changes.

Intraoperative blood sampling and point-of-care testing: aspirating a waste volume and heparinized sample from the arterial-line stopcock or in-line reservoir on an anesthetized, draped patient, flushing the line, filling and running an ABG/hematocrit cartridge on a bedside analyzer, and reporting values to the anesthesiologist.

Post-induction placement of supplemental monitors on the anesthetized patient: inserting an esophageal temperature probe, applying processed-EEG (BIS) forehead electrodes, siting train-of-four nerve-stimulator electrodes on the ulnar/facial nerve, and placing a forced-air warming blanket — often with limited access around drapes, arms tucked and the surgical field already prepped.

Monitoring in non-OR anesthetizing locations (endoscopy suite, cath lab, interventional radiology/MRI, labor and delivery): applying and maintaining MRI-safe or radiolucent monitors, working around fluoroscopy equipment and moving tables, and watching the patient from outside the room or through a window.

sources.title: Aletta for Laboratory specialists - Vitestro
sources.claim: Vitestro's Aletta autonomous robotic phlebotomy device performs venous blood draws without a phlebotomist, using near-infrared/ultrasound/Doppler imaging and a needle-insertion robot, with 95% first-time success in an EU multicenter trial and CE marking for routine blood-collection use.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: diagnostic venipuncture on a seated outpatient with the arm immobilized in the device. It is the closest robotic capability to the AA's blood-sampling instance, but it draws venous blood into tubes at a blood-collection station; it does not sample from an indwelling arterial line on a draped, anesthetized patient in an OR, nor run ABG/hematocrit analysis, so it does not complete that instance.

sources.title: K162042 510(k) Summary - accessdata.fda.gov
sources.claim: The OptiScanner 5000 is an FDA-cleared bedside instrument that automatically withdraws a blood sample through an indwelling central venous catheter, centrifuges it and measures plasma glucose in surgical intensive care patients.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated sampling of blood from an indwelling catheter with on-board analysis at the bedside. It shows machine-controlled fluid handling on a catheterized patient, but it is a single-analyte closed fluidic instrument (plasma glucose from a CVC); it does not obtain arterial samples, produce blood-gas or hematocrit results, or apply and maintain any of the other monitors in this task.

sources.system: Dr. Spot (Boston Dynamics Spot with contactless vital-sign sensing)
sources.developer: MIT, Boston Dynamics, Brigham and Women's Hospital
sources.title: Mobile Robotic Platform for Contactless Vital Sign Monitoring (PMC)
sources.claim: A quadruped robot fitted with cameras measured skin temperature, respiratory rate and ... of patients in a hospital COVID triage tent, but the robot was driven by clinical staff rather than operating autonomously.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: acquiring vital signs from a patient with a mobile robot. It is teleoperated and contact-free (camera-based triage measurements), so it cannot support a positive judgment and does not perform contact monitor application, invasive-line handling or intraoperative vigilance.

sources.developer: Tsinghua University with Beijing Tsinghua Changgung Hospital
sources.title: Beyond hospital reach: Autonomous lightweight ultrasound robot for liver sonography (arXiv)
sources.claim: An autonomous ultrasound robot placed and servoed a probe against human subjects' skin to acquire diagnostic views, deployed in the ultrasound department ... a hospital.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous force-controlled placement of a sensor on a patient's skin in a hospital. Transfer is limited: it presses a single probe on the exposed abdomen of a cooperative subject, whereas this task requires siting adhesive electrodes, cuffs and probes, connecting cables and maintaining them on a draped anesthetized patient; no such demonstration exists.

tasks.label: Control anesthesia levels during procedures.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Maintenance of general anesthesia for a routine elective adult case (ASA I-III: ortho, general surgery, GYN, urology) in a hospital operating room: titrating volatile agent or propofol/remifentanil infusions, opioid and relaxant to keep depth appropriate through incision, changing stimulation and closure, then emergence.

Sedation / monitored anesthesia care for short outpatient procedures at an ambulatory surgery center, endoscopy suite, cataract room or other procedure room: titrating propofol with adjuncts to a target sedation level in a spontaneously breathing patient.

Elective major/complex surgery in a hemodynamically stable patient (on-pump cardiac, major vascular, thoracic with one-lung ventilation, craniotomy) in a hospital OR: depth control through bypass, positioning and long duration, with invasive monitoring.

Emergency or high-acuity unstable case (trauma, hemorrhage/massive transfusion, ruptured aneurysm, septic shock, ASA IV emergency, difficult airway, rapid-sequence induction): anesthetic depth must be titrated minute-to-minute against collapsing hemodynamics and unreliable depth monitoring.

Pediatric case (infants and children for ENT, ortho, imaging, general pediatric surgery): weight-based dosing, inhalational induction, narrow margins, rapid uptake and washout, depth control through short high-stimulus procedures.

Obstetric anesthesia on labor and delivery: maintaining a labor epidural at an adequate level through progressing labor, and managing block level, sedation and pressor support during cesarean under neuraxial anesthesia.

sources.system: Automated TIVA control system (Nagata/Shigemi; precursor of ROP-1680 AsisTIVA)
sources.title: Anesthesia Management via an Automated Control System for Propofol, Remifentanil, and Rocuronium Compared to Management by Anesthesiologists: An Investigator-Initiated Study
sources.claim: Investigator-initiated randomized trial in Japanese hospital operating rooms: a closed-loop system driving syringe pumps for propofol, remifentanil and rocuronium (BIS and train-of-four feedback) kept all three components of anesthesia adequately controlled for a greater share of surgical time than anesthesiologists titrating manually.

sources.title: Pharmacokinetic–Pharmacodynamic Simulation of Muscle Relaxation Antagonistic Conditions for Post-Operative Recurarization Prevention
sources.claim: The automated TIVA syringe-pump control system was regulatory-approved in Japan in 2022 and commercially released in 2023 by Nihon Kohden as ROP-1680 AsisTIVA, i.e. an automated anesthetic-titration product sold for use in operating rooms.

sources.title: Anesthesia management using ROP-1680 AsisTIVA : a case report
sources.claim: Clinical case report of AsisTIVA in routine use: the system is certified for use at three Japanese university hospitals and automatically controls propofol and remifentanil to a BIS target and rocuronium to a train-of-four target during surgery.

sources.title: Evaluation of a novel closed-loop total intravenous anaesthesia drug delivery system: a randomized controlled trial
sources.claim: Randomized controlled trial of 186 surgical patients: an automated anesthesia drug-delivery robot administered propofol, remifentanil and rocuronium under closed-loop control (BIS and Analgoscore feedback) and maintained target depth of anesthesia and analgesia in a university hospital OR.
sources.transferJustification: Also relied on for the sedation/MAC instance: maintaining a set depth by closed-loop propofol titration against an EEG depth index is the same actuation, drug and monitor used to hold a procedural sedation level, at a shallower target, in the same institutional procedure rooms.

sources.title: A Multicenter Evaluation of a Closed-Loop Anesthesia Delivery System: A Randomized Controlled Trial
sources.claim: Multicentre randomized controlled trial in India: a BIS-guided closed-loop anesthesia delivery system performed both induction and maintenance of propofol anesthesia automatically for adults having major surgery, compared with manual titration by attending anesthesiologists.
sources.transferJustification: Also relied on for the sedation instance: automated propofol titration to an EEG-derived depth target is the same pump actuation and feedback used to hold a sedation level during a short procedure.

sources.title: Closed-loop isoflurane administration with bispectral index in open heart surgery: randomized controlled trial with manual control
sources.claim: Randomized controlled trial in open-heart surgery: closed-loop, BIS-guided automated delivery of an inhaled volatile agent (isoflurane) was feasible and effective versus manual control, showing automated control extends to vapour-based anesthesia and to cardiac cases.

sources.title: Evaluation of Automated Delivery of Propofol Using a Closed-Loop Anesthesia Delivery System in Patients Undergoing Thoracic Surgery: A Randomized Controlled Study
sources.claim: Randomized study in major thoracic surgery: automated propofol TIVA delivered by the closed-loop system gave consistent depth of anesthesia with ... consumption than manual delivery in a hospital OR.

sources.title: The Feasibility of a Completely Automated Total IV Anesthesia Drug Delivery System for Cardiac Surgery
sources.claim: Pilot study of fully automated three-drug anesthesia in 20 elective cardiac surgery patients with cardiopulmonary bypass: the anesthesia drug-delivery robot completed the case without manual override in 80% of patients, four cases being lost to technical problems with the system.

sources.title: Clinical evaluation of bispectral index-guided closed-loop infusion of propofol for preschool children: A multi-center randomized controlled study
sources.claim: Multi-centre randomized controlled study in preschool children: BIS-guided closed-loop propofol infusion controlled depth of anesthesia more accurately and smoothly than the comparator in hospital operating rooms.

sources.title: Evaluation of closed-loop anesthesia delivery for propofol anesthesia in pediatric cardiac surgery
sources.claim: Closed-loop propofol anesthesia delivery was evaluated against manual control in children undergoing cardiac surgery; BIS control within target and intraoperative hemodynamic stability were similar between automated and manual groups.

sources.developer: KK Women's and Children's Hospital, Singapore (Sia group)
sources.title: Comparison of computer-integrated patient-controlled epidural analgesia with no initial basal infusion versus moderate basal infusion for labor and delivery: A randomized controlled trial
sources.claim: Randomized trials on labor wards: a computer-integrated epidural pump automatically adjusts the background local-anesthetic infusion to the parturient's changing analgesic need as labor progresses, maintaining analgesia with minimal clinician supplementation.
sources.transferJustification: Related task (maintaining the level of a neuraxial block by pump titration) transfers to controlling anesthesia level during obstetric procedures: same drug route, same pump actuation, same monitored endpoint of block adequacy, on the same labor unit.

sources.title: Closed-loop double-vasopressor automated system vs manual bolus vasopressor to treat hypotension during spinal anaesthesia for caesarean section: a randomised controlled trial
sources.claim: Randomized controlled trial during cesarean delivery under spinal anesthesia: an automated vasopressor delivery system dosed phenylephrine or ephedrine from continuous non-invasive arterial pressure feedback, replacing manual bolus titration by the anesthesia provider.
sources.transferJustification: Related task (automated haemodynamic support during neuraxial anesthesia) is the accompanying titration work of the cesarean instance; same monitors, same infusion actuators, same obstetric operating room.

sources.title: Automation and Anesthesia | HealthLeaders Media
sources.claim: Computer-assisted personalized sedation hardware received FDA premarket approval and was put into clinical service in a US hospital endoscopy unit, delivering propofol sedation for routine colonoscopy and EGD in place of an anesthesia professional for low-risk patients.
sources.transferJustification: Corroborates that automated propofol-sedation hardware has been fielded in a structured procedure suite; treated as non-decisive because the degree of autonomous up-titration is not established.

tasks.label: Administer anesthetic, adjuvant, or accessory drugs under the direction of an anesthesiologist.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Induction of general anesthesia in a hospital OR: the AA checks and draws up (or picks pharmacy-prefilled, labeled) syringes of induction agent, opioid and neuromuscular blocker, connects each to the IV stopcock, pushes them in sequence at the anesthesiologist's direction while airway management proceeds, and flushes/documents. Includes the occasional pediatric inhalational mask induction variant.

Maintenance of general anesthesia in the OR over a 1-3 hour case: continuously administering the anesthetic agent by setting/adjusting the vaporizer and fresh-gas flow on the anesthesia machine (most US cases) and/or running maintenance IV infusions, titrating to depth, hemodynamics and surgical stimulation.

Ad hoc administration of hemodynamic (accessory) drugs in response to intraoperative vital signs in the OR: pressor boluses or infusions (phenylephrine, ephedrine, norepinephrine), vasodilators, anticholinergics, titrated moment-to-moment to blood-pressure/heart-rate targets under the anesthesiologist's direction.

Other adjuvant/accessory drug boluses at points in an OR case: antibiotic dose and redose, antiemetics, dexamethasone, ketorolac, supplemental opioid, muscle-relaxant top-ups, reversal agents (neostigmine/glycopyrrolate, sugammadex) — each selected from the cart or drug tray, verified, injected into the IV port and documented.

Sedation/MAC drug administration outside the OR in a hospital procedure suite (GI endoscopy, cath/EP lab, interventional radiology, ophthalmology): propofol/sedative infusion plus small boluses titrated to sedation depth and respiratory status through the case.

Neuraxial/regional drug administration in the OR or L&D: injecting local anesthetic and adjuncts through an epidural or peripheral nerve-block catheter (loading dose, intraoperative top-ups) and setting up/maintaining the catheter infusion after the anesthesiologist places the catheter.

sources.system: GE HealthCare Aisys CS2 with End-tidal (Et) Control
sources.title: Clinical Study Shows Targeted End-tidal Control Anesthesia Delivery Improves Efficiency and Accuracy to Help Optimize Patient Care | GE HealthCare
sources.claim: GE HealthCare's End-tidal Control software on the Aisys CS2 anesthesia delivery system automatically actuates fresh-gas flow and vaporizer output to reach and hold clinician-set end-tidal oxygen and anesthetic-agent concentrations; it holds FDA premarket approval and was evaluated in the MASTER trial across four U.S. hospitals in 210 adult surgical patients under general inhaled anesthesia.

sources.system: AAS-GE (RL-based automated anesthesia system for GI endoscopy)
sources.developer: Zhengzhou Central Hospital / Zhengzhou University group (China)
sources.title: Reinforcement learning based automated anesthesia system for gastrointestinal endoscopy with a multicenter randomized trial - npj Digital Medicine
sources.claim: A reinforcement-learning automated anesthesia system (AAS-GE) drove a micro infusion pump to deliver ciprofol sedation autonomously during gastrointestinal endoscopy in a prospective multicenter RCT at four hospitals in China (418 patients, 2025), with hypoxemia rates and other safety outcomes non-inferior to clinician-managed sedation.

sources.title: FDA Grants Premarket Approval (PMA) For The SEDASYS System For Healthy Patients Undergoing Sedation During Routine Colonoscopy And EGD Procedures
sources.claim: The SEDASYS computer-assisted personalized sedation system received FDA premarket approval in 2013 for computer-controlled IV propofol delivery for minimal-to-moderate sedation during colonoscopy ..., and was commercially deployed in a small number of U.S. hospital endoscopy suites before J&J discontinued it in 2016.

sources.system: CLADS (closed-loop anesthesia delivery system, BIS-guided propofol)
sources.developer: G.D. Puri / PGIMER Chandigarh (India); multicenter Indian trials
sources.title: Evaluation of Automated Delivery of Propofol Using a Closed-Loop Anesthesia Delivery System in Patients Undergoing Thoracic Surgery: A Randomized Controlled Study - PubMed
sources.claim: The Closed-Loop Anesthesia Delivery System (CLADS) automatically delivered propofol for both induction and maintenance of TIVA in thoracic surgery patients in a randomized controlled trial, requiring zero manual infusion adjustments versus ~9.6 per hour in the manual group, with equivalent depth-of-anesthesia performance indices.

sources.title: A technical description of a novel pharmacological anesthesia robot | Journal of Clinical Monitoring and Computing
sources.claim: McSleepy is a closed-loop 'pharmacological anesthesia robot' that automatically administers hypnotic, opioid and neuromuscular blocking drugs from connected infusion pumps using BIS, analgoscore and phonomyography feedback, controlling induction, maintenance and emergence; clinical results in patients were reported in the OR at McGill-affiliated hospitals.

sources.developer: Coeckelenbergh, Joosten, Rinehart, Cannesson et al.
sources.title: Closed-loop anesthesia: foundations and applications in contemporary perioperative medicine | Journal of Clinical Monitoring and Computing
sources.claim: A 2024 peer-reviewed review of closed-loop anesthesia states that for over twenty years clinical studies have shown closed-loop drug delivery superior to manual control for stabilizing single variables and safely administering therapies (EEG-propofol, blood pressure-vasopressor, fluid responsiveness-fluids), while noting a trained practitioner must remain present and ready to retake control.

sources.developer: Coeckelenbergh, Soucy-Proulx, Joosten, Rinehart et al.
sources.title: Tight control of mean arterial pressure using a closed loop system for norepinephrine infusion after high-risk abdominal surgery: a randomized controlled trial - PubMed
sources.claim: A closed-loop vasopressor controller autonomously titrated norepinephrine infusion in patients after high-risk abdominal surgery in a randomized trial, maintaining a mean-arterial-pressure target better than manual nurse titration and reducing hypotension.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: continuous titration of a vasoactive accessory drug to a blood-pressure target. The same controller class has been used intraoperatively; it covers the dosing decision and delivery of the accessory drugs an AA gives for hypotension, though only via an already-connected infusion line.

sources.date: 2019-07-31 (product line in commercial use; Staubli collaboration 2020)
sources.title: ARxIUM: New RIVA Automated IV Compounding System | Healthcare Packaging
sources.claim: ARxIUM's RIVA is a fully automated IV compounding robot with a Staubli robotic arm that draws drug from vials and fills syringes and IV bags inside an enclosed ISO Class 5 aseptic cell; it is commercially installed in hospital pharmacies.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: the vial-to-syringe drug preparation step that precedes bedside administration. It shows robotic handling of vials and syringes exists only inside a purpose-built enclosed aseptic cell, not at an OR bedside among people and sterile fields.

sources.developer: Sng, Sia et al., KK Women's and Children's Hospital, Singapore
sources.title: Comparison of computer-integrated patient-controlled epidural analgesia with no initial basal infusion versus moderate basal infusion for labor and delivery: A randomized controlled trial - PubMed
sources.claim: Computer-integrated patient-controlled epidural analgesia (CIPCEA) ... an epidural drug delivery pump that automatically adjusts the background local-anesthetic infusion from the patient's demand history; it was evaluated in randomized trials in the labor ward at KK Women's and Children's Hospital, Singapore.

tasks.label: Pretest and calibrate anesthesia delivery systems and monitors.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Start-of-day complete pre-use checkout of an anesthesia workstation in a hospital operating room: power up and start the machine's automated self-test, hang and connect a new breathing circuit and reservoir bag, occlude the Y-piece for the leak/compliance test, verify pipeline and E-cylinder pressures (open cylinder valves with a wrench), confirm vaporizers are filled and seated, inspect CO2 absorbent, check scavenging, suction, and availability of a self-inflating backup bag, then document the checkout.

Pre-case setup and verification of physiologic monitors in the OR: power up the monitor, plug in ECG/SpO2/NIBP/temperature cables and agent-analyzer sampling line, verify each module reads and traces correctly, set alarm limits for the case, and assemble, flush, and zero invasive pressure transducer sets for arterial/central lines.

Abbreviated between-case checkout during a turnover day: swap the breathing circuit/mask/filter, re-run the abbreviated leak and ventilation test, re-check vaporizer levels and absorbent color, confirm suction and monitor function, all under time pressure with room turnover activity around the machine.

Sensor-level calibration/verification per manufacturer procedure: calibrate the galvanic oxygen cell to room air (or verify self-calibration), run flow-sensor calibration, and zero/span the gas analyzer bench (agent and CO2), confirming readings against reference values and logging results.

Checkout at a non-OR anesthetizing location (endoscopy suite, cath lab, MRI suite, dental/office-based surgery): a portable or MRI-conditional anesthesia machine and transport monitor in a cramped, less standardized room, including gas supply (cylinder or pipeline) verification, circuit and suction setup, and monitor checks.

Pre-case testing of ancillary anesthesia equipment: suction canister and tubing, video laryngoscope/light source and blades, capnography adapters, infusion and syringe pumps (self-test and programming), nerve stimulator, fluid/patient warmer, and confirming the difficult-airway cart and defibrillator are functional.

sources.system: Built-in automated checkout routines of modern anesthesia gas machines (workstation self-test)
sources.title: Anesthesia Gas Machine — Checkout (University of Detroit Mercy Nurse Anesthesia)
sources.claim: Modern anesthesia workstations run built-in electronic checkout routines, but the routine requires a human operator to perform manual steps such as occluding the breathing circuit for the leak test, switching ventilation modes, and checking suction and the emergency oxygen cylinder supply.
sources.transferJustification: Directly describes the task; establishes that the machine's own automation does not complete the checkout and that manual manipulation steps remain.

sources.title: Anesthesia Machine Checkout | Anesthesia Key
sources.claim: Key checkout items, notably the state of the CO2 absorbent, are not covered by any automated routine and must be inspected by a person.
sources.transferJustification: Same task; documents which checkout elements remain outside automated self-test coverage.

sources.date: 2026-07 (product page retrieved; product line commercial since ~2019)
sources.title: DSX Docking Station | Automated Gas Monitor Maintenance & Calibration
sources.claim: Commercial docking stations automatically bump-test and calibrate portable gas-detection instruments: once an instrument is docked, the station applies calibration gas, performs the calibration on schedule, and records certificates without an operator running the procedure.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: scheduled span calibration and functional (bump) verification of electrochemical/IR gas sensors. Same object class and operation as calibrating an anesthesia O2 cell or zeroing/spanning a gas analyzer bench — expose the sensor to a known gas, adjust span, log the result — performed in a purpose-built docking fixture (E1).

sources.title: Swisslog Healthcare Partners with Diligent Robotics to Enhance Hospital Logistics
sources.claim: The largest deployed fleet of mobile ... in US hospitals performs only fetch-and-deliver logistics (supplies, medications, lab samples) in corridors and units; no clinical equipment testing or calibration is part of its deployed task set.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous mobile manipulation inside hospitals (E2). Shows the deployed envelope of hospital robots is transport of standardized items, not multi-step equipment checkout requiring hose connection, valve turning and instrument reading.

sources.system: Humanoid-based laparoscopic teleoperation framework (contemporary humanoid robots)
sources.title: In vivo feasibility study of humanoid robots in surgery | Nature
sources.claim: State-of-the-art humanoid robots evaluated for operating-room work perform surgical tasks only under teleoperation, in benchtop, dry-lab and in vivo porcine studies, and are not clinically deployed.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: humanoid manipulation of clinical instruments in an OR context. Establishes that general-purpose humanoids working in ORs are teleoperated, so they cannot support a positive autonomy judgment for equipment checkout.

sources.developer: University of Liverpool (Burger, Cooper et al.)
sources.title: A mobile robotic chemist — University of Strathclyde research portal
sources.claim: A free-roaming mobile robot autonomously operated human-scale laboratory instruments over eight days, running 688 experiments in a chemistry lab built for people.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous operation of instruments in a structured human work facility. Transfer fails for this task, however: the robot handled rigid vials at taught, fixed instrument stations, not compliant breathing hoses, vaporizers, cylinder valves, transducer sets or on-screen checkout dialogs in an occupied OR.

tasks.label: Respond to emergency situations by providing cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR), basic cardiac life support (BLS), advanced cardiac life support (ACLS), or pediatric advanced life support (PALS).

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Intraoperative crisis under anesthesia in a hospital OR (e.g., sudden bradycardia/asystole, hemorrhagic arrest): the AA recognizes the deterioration on monitors, calls for help, begins chest compressions on the operating table, pushes ACLS drugs through existing IV lines, charges and applies defibrillation amid a sterile field, ventilates 100% O2 through the circuit, and works with the anesthesiologist and surgical team until ROSC or termination.

Code blue / rapid-response call elsewhere in the hospital (ward, PACU, ED, ICU): the AA arrives with the airway/code cart, positions the patient, performs bag-mask ventilation and assists or performs intubation, takes turns on compressions, verifies pulse and rhythm, and administers ACLS medications at a crowded bedside.

Perioperative emergency short of arrest requiring BLS/ACLS-level intervention: anaphylaxis, laryngospasm with desaturation, can't-intubate/can't-ventilate airway, aspiration, or malignant hyperthermia in the OR — the AA supports the airway, ventilates, gives vasopressors/epinephrine, sets up infusions, and prevents progression to arrest.

Pediatric (PALS) emergency in a children's OR or procedural suite: infant/child with bradycardia or arrest after induction — weight-based drug dosing and dilution, small-airway management with correct mask/tube sizes, two-thumb or one-hand compressions on a small chest, and rapid escalation with the pediatric anesthesia team.

Emergency at an off-site or ambulatory anesthetizing location (endoscopy suite, cath lab, MRI/CT, office-based or freestanding surgery center, labor and delivery): limited help and equipment, patient may need to be moved out of the scanner/procedure room, AA runs BLS/ACLS while awaiting EMS or the hospital code team.

sources.date: 2026-07 (product page; device family in clinical use since ~2019)
sources.title: LUCAS 3, v3.1 chest compression system | Stryker
sources.claim: Commercial mechanical CPR device delivers guideline-consistent chest compressions automatically once clinicians interrupt CPR, place the backboard and strap the device onto the patient; it performs only the compression component and does not assess the patient, manage the airway, give drugs, or decide therapy.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: mechanical chest compressions during CPR. It covers only one sub-step of the instance and requires humans to position and apply it, so it cannot complete the whole resuscitation.

sources.developer: Yonsei University Wonju College of Medicine, Research Institute of Resuscitation Science
sources.title: Efficacy of Cardiopulmonary Resuscitation Using Automatic Compression—Defibrillation Apparatus: An Animal Study and A Manikin-Based Simulation Study
sources.claim: Research apparatus combining mechanical chest compression with automated rhythm analysis and defibrillation, tested in pigs and in manikin simulations where healthcare providers still ran the BLS scenario and applied the device; no autonomous airway management, drug delivery, or clinical decision-making.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: compressions plus defibrillation, the two most mechanizable parts of ACLS. Even combined, it is applied by clinicians and omits airway, drugs, and algorithm decisions, so completion of the instance is not substantiated.

sources.system: Unitree G1 humanoid bimanual teleoperation system
sources.title: Humanoids in Hospitals: A Technical Study of Humanoid Surrogates for Dexterous Medical Interventions
sources.claim: Humanoid robot performing emergency interventions including bag-valve-mask ventilation and handling of intubation tools on manikins, conducted entirely by bimanual teleoperation, with reported limits in force output and sensing.
sources.transferJustification: Closest robotic attempt at bedside emergency interventions (ventilation, airway tools). Being fully teleoperated on manikins, it cannot support a positive judgment for autonomous resuscitation.

sources.developer: academic group publishing in Science Translational Medicine
sources.title: A soft robotic device for rapid and self-guided intubation | Science Translational Medicine
sources.claim: Operator-guided soft robotic intubation device achieved rapid tracheal tube placement in manikin and cadaver testing; the device is hand-held and self-guiding but is inserted and operated by a human clinician.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: emergency airway intubation, a core part of resuscitation. Human-operated, so it does not show a robot autonomously securing an airway during a code.

sources.developer: reported by Amsterdam UMC and collaborators in Clinical Chemistry
sources.title: Performance, Safety, and Patient Experience of an Autonomous Robotic Phlebotomy Device: A Multicenter Trial
sources.claim: Autonomous robotic phlebotomy device completed venipuncture end-to-end (vein imaging, tourniquet, needle insertion, tube handling, bandaging) on patients in a multicenter clinical trial at outpatient blood-draw stations, demonstrating autonomous needle work on humans but nothing resembling emergency resuscitation.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous needle placement in a cooperative, seated patient at a fixed station. It marks the frontier of autonomous patient-contact robotics and does not transfer to time-critical, whole-body resuscitation of an unstable patient.

tasks.label: Collect and document patients' pre-anesthetic health histories.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

tasks.label: Administer blood, blood products, or supportive fluids.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Hospital OR, routine elective case: AA selects a 1 L crystalloid bag from the anesthesia cart, checks solution/expiry, spikes it with an administration set, primes and de-airs the tubing, hangs it on the pole, connects the luer to the patient's IV catheter hub or pump, opens the clamp/sets the rate, and confirms free flow with no infiltration.

Intraoperative titration/bolus through an already-running line: in response to hypotension, low stroke volume or blood loss, the AA gives repeated 250-500 mL crystalloid/colloid boluses (roller clamp wide open, pressure bag, or pump bolus), reassesses hemodynamics, and repeats or stops.

Elective transfusion in the OR (e.g., orthopedic, hepatic, cardiac case): AA retrieves the PRBC unit from the OR cooler/blood bank, performs the two-person patient-ID and unit verification, spikes the unit with a filtered blood set, runs it through a fluid warmer, connects and infuses, and watches for transfusion reaction while documenting.

Hemorrhage/massive transfusion in trauma, obstetric or vascular cases: AA loads multiple units of PRBC/FFP/platelets and crystalloid into a rapid infuser (Belmont/Level 1), manages warming, air detection and line pressure, swaps units continuously under time pressure in a crowded OR.

Mid-case replacement and specialty containers: AA changes an emptied bag, hangs 5% albumin or a premixed additive/electrolyte bag, or reconstitutes and hangs a supportive infusion, re-priming or spiking a second line while surgery continues.

Off-site anesthetizing location (endoscopy suite, cath lab, MRI, L&D): AA sets up and administers fluids with a portable pole/pump in a cramped room with limited access to the patient and no dedicated anesthesia workstation.

sources.system: Closed-loop (CL) goal-directed fluid administration system (learning intravenous resuscitator, Rinehart/Joosten)
sources.developer: Rinehart, Joosten, Cannesson et al. (UC Irvine / Erasme Hospital); Sironis controller
sources.title: A Pilot Study Assessing a Closed-Loop System for Goal-Directed Fluid Therapy in Abdominal Surgery Patients (J. Pers. Med. 2022)
sources.claim: Closed-loop goal-directed fluid therapy systems (the Rinehart/Joosten 'learning intravenous resuscitator' lineage) automatically titrate intravenous fluid administration to the patient during surgery, driving an infusion pump from continuous hemodynamic monitoring without human intervention.

sources.system: Automated closed-loop goal-directed fluid therapy system
sources.developer: Lilot/Piriou et al. (Lyon) with Rinehart/Joosten closed-loop controller
sources.title: Comparison of cardiac output optimization with an automated closed-loop goal-directed fluid therapy versus non standardized manual fluid administration during elective abdominal surgery: first prospective randomized controlled trial
sources.claim: In a prospective randomized controlled trial in elective abdominal surgery at an academic medical center, an automated closed-loop system connected to a cardiac-output monitor delivered fluid boluses to intraoperative patients and was compared against anesthesiologist-managed manual fluid administration.

sources.title: New Automated Robot System in Renown Health
sources.claim: Robotic IV compounding cells autonomously manipulate IV bags, vials and syringes — gripping bags, piercing ports and transferring fluid — inside a sealed purpose-built ISO Class 5 enclosure in hospital pharmacies; a US health system put one into production in 2025.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: aseptic IV bag/syringe preparation. It shows machine handling of the same containers and port punctures in a fixtured cell, but the cell contains no patient; nothing in it connects a primed set to a patient's IV hub, runs a blood warmer, or watches for a transfusion reaction, so it does not transfer to bedside administration.

sources.title: Vitestro introduces autonomous robotic device for blood collection
sources.claim: An autonomous robotic phlebotomy device performs ultrasound-guided needle insertion into a patient's vein and completes a blood draw without a human operator, clinically validated in thousands of draws in blood-collection settings.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: obtaining vascular access. It shows autonomous needle-to-vein work on a seated, cooperative patient in a draw chair, but it withdraws blood into vacuum tubes; it does not spike or hang units, connect infusion sets, warm or infuse products, or monitor an anesthetized surgical patient.

sources.developer: US Army Institute of Surgical Research collaborators
sources.title: In vivo evaluation of an adaptive resuscitation controller using whole blood and crystalloid infusates for hemorrhagic shock
sources.claim: A closed-loop adaptive resuscitation controller autonomously infused whole blood and crystalloid to target mean arterial pressure in an anesthetized swine hemorrhagic-shock model, i.e., autonomous machine-controlled delivery of blood was shown only in animals in a laboratory.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated hemorrhage resuscitation. Delivery is through lines a human placed, in swine, with no product verification, unit changes, or reaction monitoring, so it does not substantiate transfusing a human surgical patient.

sources.title: FDA 510(k) K233984 — Acumen Assisted Fluid Management Software
sources.claim: The commercially cleared intraoperative fluid technology in US operating rooms is advisory only: the software recommends boluses and a clinician decides and physically administers them.

tasks.label: Verify availability of operating room supplies, medications, and gases.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Pre-case check at the anesthesia workstation in a hospital OR: open the anesthesia cart drawers and confirm airway equipment (blades, tubes, stylets, masks), syringes, IV supplies and circuits are present for the scheduled case; confirm O2/air/N2O pipeline hoses are connected and the backup E-cylinder pressure is adequate; pull replacements for anything missing before the patient arrives.

Case medication availability: confirm the drugs required for the case (induction agents, relaxants, vasoactives, antibiotics, emergency drugs, controlled substances) are stocked in the anesthesia cart/automated dispensing cabinet, unexpired and in adequate quantity; obtain missing items from the OR satellite pharmacy or Pyxis and document controlled-substance withdrawal.

Between-case turnover in the same OR: under time pressure, verify the workstation was restocked (syringes, airway gear, circuit, suction canister, drugs) and replace what the previous case consumed before the next patient is brought in.

Specialty or low-frequency items: verify availability of difficult-airway cart contents, pediatric-sized equipment, rare or emergency drugs (dantrolene, lipid emulsion, nitric oxide), or blood products; often requires checking other storage locations or calling pharmacy/blood bank for a specific case.

Off-site anesthetizing location (endoscopy suite, cath lab, MRI, labor and delivery, ambulatory surgery center): verify the portable O2 cylinder pressure, suction, monitoring supplies and the transport drug/emergency kit in a room not permanently set up for general anesthesia.

sources.title: ORB: Operating Room Bot, Automating Operating Room Logistics through Mobile Manipulation
sources.claim: CMU's Operating Room Bot is an autonomous mobile manipulator that retrieves and restocks OR supply items (boxes, bottles) between carts and storage shelves in an OR logistics test environment, at 80% retrieval and 96% restocking success — a research demo, below clinical reliability.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: item-level OR supply retrieval/restocking. It bears on whether a robot could audit and replenish anesthesia supplies in an OR as found; the reported success rates and lab setting show the capability is not yet at worker quality in a real OR.

sources.title: How Diligent's Robots Are Making a Difference in Texas Hospitals - IEEE Spectrum
sources.claim: Moxi is a commercially deployed autonomous mobile manipulator working in hospitals, picking supplies from supply closets and delivering them; its deployed workflows are fetch-and-deliver logistics, not verification/auditing of OR stock.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: hospital supply fetching in the same E2 setting (hospital corridors and supply rooms). It shows what deployed hospital robots actually do — transport, not stock verification in the OR — supporting the negative E2 judgments.

sources.title: AutoStore installs 300th warehouse system in North America at Medline facility
sources.claim: AutoStore robotic goods-to-person storage and retrieval systems operate at scale in medical-surgical supply distribution, with fleets of robots maintaining bin-level stock and retrieving items to picking workstations inside a purpose-built robotic grid.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic storage/retrieval and stock accounting of the very medical-surgical supplies an anesthetist checks. With stock fixtured in machine-held bins (the E1 counterfactual), confirming an item is available and producing it is exactly what the system does, at commercial reliability.

sources.title: Pharmacy automated dispensing system - BoxPicker - Swisslog Healthcare - robotic
sources.claim: Swisslog BoxPicker is a fully automated robotic pharmacy storage and retrieval system used in hospital pharmacies that tracks medication inventory, guides picking by expiry date, and produces drug expiry reports.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: verifying which medications are on hand and unexpired, and dispensing them. Same objects (unit-dose vials/ampoules incl. controlled substances) and same acceptance criterion (right drug present, in date) as the anesthetist's medication availability check, performed inside a purpose-built robotic enclosure.

sources.title: The Next Step in Robotic Inspection | Boston Dynamics
sources.claim: Boston Dynamics' Spot runs autonomous inspection missions in industrial facilities and, with the Levatas computer-vision add-on, reads analog gauges site-wide, trends the readings and raises alerts on abnormal values.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous reading of analog pressure gauges on plant assets. Verifying that an O2 cylinder or pipeline gauge shows adequate pressure is the same perceptual act on the same class of dial instrument, with the gauge in a fixed, known location.
