sources.title: Simbe Tally shelf-scanning robot achieves UL 3300 certification
sources.claim: Simbe's Tally is an autonomous shelf-scanning robot deployed across roughly a thousand stores that repeatedly audits stock and reports out-of-stocks and misplaced items.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous verification that stocked items are present at expected locations. Applied to standardized, openly presented supply racks (the E1 presentation), this is the same presence/quantity check the anesthetist performs on supply stock.

sources.title: Autonomous warehouse drones streamline inventory control | TechTarget
sources.claim: Autonomous Verity drones perform lights-out inventory counting in warehouses, flying racking aisles and reconciling stock against system records, cutting inventory audit labour by about half in customer deployments.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous stock verification against a required list in a racked, labelled storage area — the same 'is the required item present in the expected quantity' judgment, when stock is presented in machine-readable fixed locations.

sources.system: AGA Riihimäki automated cylinder filling plant / Linde robotic cylinder handling
sources.title: AGA renews Finnish filling site, now world's first fully automated industrial gas fill plant | gasworld
sources.claim: Industrial gas cylinder handling and filling is done by robots in fully automated plants, where cylinders are sorted, picked, moved, optically inspected and filled without manual handling.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic handling and fill-state checking of compressed-gas cylinders. Confirming that a cylinder holds adequate gas (and swapping an empty one) is the gas half of this task; in a purpose-built cell that handling and checking is already fully machine-executed.

tasks.label: Assist anesthesiologists in performing anesthetic procedures, such as epidural or spinal injections.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Labor epidural or combined spinal-epidural in a labor & delivery room: AA readies the epidural cart and drugs, sits the laboring patient up and physically holds her flexed and still through contractions, opens the sterile kit and hands syringes/catheter/filter to the anesthesiologist, injects test and loading doses on direction, tapes and secures the catheter, and monitors BP/fetal tracing, treating hypotension.

Spinal or epidural for a surgical case in the OR (C-section, orthopedic, urologic): AA positions and supports the awake patient sitting or lateral on the OR table, assists sterile prep and drape, passes the spinal needle/local, aspirates and injects on direction, then lays the patient supine, applies monitors/oxygen, and manages the resulting sympathectomy.

Ultrasound-guided peripheral nerve block in a preop holding/block area: AA sets up the block tray and local anesthetic, gives light sedation and monitors the patient, positions and holds the limb, holds the ultrasound probe or injects the syringe while the anesthesiologist advances the needle, aspirates between increments, then dresses the site.

Assisting invasive line placement during an anesthetic in the OR (arterial line, central venous catheter): AA preps skin, opens and hands the kit, holds the ultrasound probe, flushes/zeroes the transducer, hands sutures and dressing, and watches the monitor and airway while the anesthesiologist works.

Assisting airway/induction procedures in the OR: AA hands laryngoscope, tube and stylet, performs external laryngeal manipulation or cricoid pressure, provides mask ventilation, hands suction and bougie during difficult or awake fiberoptic intubation, confirms placement and secures the tube.

sources.system: Autonomous spinal robotic system (JHU BIGSS / Margalit et al.)
sources.title: Autonomous Spinal Robotic System for Transforaminal Lumbar Epidural Injections: A Proof of Concept of Study
sources.claim: An autonomous robotic system placed transforaminal lumbar epidural injections, but only in a lumbar spine phantom as a proof of concept; it performs the injection itself rather than any assisting role, and has not been used on patients.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: performing (not assisting) a neuraxial injection. Cited to show the closest robotic capability to epidural needle work is a phantom-only demonstration; it involves no live patient, no patient positioning/support, and no sterile hand-off workflow, so it cannot substantiate the assistant's whole task.

sources.title: Technical communication: First robotic ultrasound-guided nerve blocks in humans using the Magellan system - PubMed
sources.claim: The only robotic ultrasound-guided nerve blocks performed in humans were done with a remote control center (joystick teleoperation) by the anesthesiologist, not autonomously.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: regional block needle placement in humans. Teleoperated, so it cannot support a positive judgment; also covers the physician's needle work rather than the assistant's positioning, sterile supply, monitoring and dressing duties.

sources.title: For the First Time, Newly Developed Robot Assists Doctors and Nurses in Operating Room
sources.claim: The one robotic instrument server used in a real operating room passed instruments on voice command and explicitly had no direct patient contact; it did not position patients, maintain a sterile field around a patient, or monitor them.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: intraoperative instrument hand-off, one sub-step of the AA's assisting role. Cited to show that even this sub-step, in a real OR, was voice-commanded and deliberately excluded patient contact, so it does not carry over to the whole procedural-assist instance.

sources.title: Diligent Robotics completes 300,000 pharmacy deliveries with Moxi - The Robot Report
sources.claim: The largest deployed fleet of autonomous hospital mobile manipulators performs logistics runs (supplies, medications, lab samples) inside hospital corridors and elevators; it does no patient-side or sterile procedural work.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous mobile manipulation inside a hospital (E2). Shows what autonomy in hospitals reliably covers today — fetch-and-carry logistics — with no manipulation of patients, sterile kits, or needles, so it does not transfer to bedside anesthetic-procedure assistance.

sources.title: Vitestro's robotic blood drawing device meets trial endpoints
sources.claim: An autonomous venipuncture device achieved 95% first-stick success in a pivotal clinical trial, but it works only with the patient's arm immobilized in a purpose-built device and performs the puncture itself rather than assisting a clinician.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous needle insertion into a live human. Cited as the strongest current evidence of patient-contact needle robotics; it requires a fixtured limb in a dedicated machine and a superficial vein target, and covers none of the assistant's positioning, sterile hand-off, injection-on-cue or monitoring duties.

sources.developer: Technical University of Munich / Wagner et al.
sources.title: Robotic scrub nurse to anticipate surgical instruments based on real-time laparoscopic video analysis - PubMed
sources.claim: Robotic scrub nurses that anticipate and hand over surgical instruments remain research systems evaluated on laparoscopic video, proposed as a way to supplement human scrub nurses rather than deployed clinically.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: instrument handover in surgery, a sub-step of the AA's assisting role. Prototype-stage, video-driven anticipation only; no patient handling, no drug injection, no monitoring, so it cannot substantiate completion of a whole anesthetic-procedure assist.

tasks.label: Assist in the provision of advanced life support techniques including those procedures using high frequency ventilation or intra-arterial cardiovascular assistance devices.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Intraoperative cardiac arrest / ACLS in the operating room: the AA responds to sudden hemodynamic collapse under the anesthesiologist's direction — starts and swaps out chest compressions on a draped, tilted patient on the OR table, ventilates with 100% O2, applies defibrillator pads and charges/shocks, draws and pushes epinephrine and other code drugs into running lines, checks pulses/rhythm and reports to the team, all in a crowded sterile OR within seconds-to-minutes.

Cardiac OR case with mechanical circulatory support (intra-aortic balloon pump, Impella, or ECMO): the AA helps prepare and prime the console/lines, assists the anesthesiologist and perfusionist during device insertion (positioning, sterile handoffs, transducing pressures), confirms balloon timing/augmentation on the arterial waveform, manages heparinization and vasoactive infusions, then transports the supported patient to ICU with the pump running.

Case requiring high-frequency ventilation (jet ventilation for ENT/airway laser or thoracic surgery, or HFOV in a pediatric/neonatal or ARDS patient): the AA sets up and connects the jet/oscillator circuit to the ETT or supraglottic catheter, sets driving pressure, frequency and inspiratory time, watches chest excursion and airway pressures, sends and responds to blood gases, and troubleshoots barotrauma/entrainment problems.

Code-team or rapid-response call outside the OR (ward, radiology/MRI suite, endoscopy, PACU, ED): the AA brings the airway bag, positions the deteriorating patient's head, performs bag-mask ventilation and assists with or performs rapid-sequence intubation, secures the tube, assists with compressions and drug delivery, and helps move the patient to ICU on a transport ventilator.

Hemodynamic rescue of an unstable patient short of arrest: the AA places or assists with an arterial line and large-bore/central access, levels and zeroes transducers, sets up rapid infusers and blood products, spikes and titrates vasopressor/inotrope infusions to pressure targets, and applies external pacing or a cardioverter when needed, in the OR or ICU.

sources.system: Soft robotic self-guided intubation device (Haggerty et al., University of Utah)
sources.developer: University of Utah / collaborators (Science Translational Medicine)
sources.title: A soft robotic device for rapid and self-guided intubation | Science Translational Medicine
sources.claim: A soft robotic intubation device self-guides an endotracheal tube into the trachea without visualization, but has only been tested in airway models, manikins and human cadavers — not in living patients — and is a single sub-step of airway management, still hand-held and initiated by a human user.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: emergency tracheal intubation, a component of the advanced life support instances (OR code, rapid response). It does not transfer to whole-instance completion: the device is placed by a human, works only on cadavers/manikins, and covers none of the ventilation, circulation, drug or device-management steps of the task.

sources.title: LUCAS 3, v3.1 chest compression system | Stryker
sources.claim: Mechanical chest compression devices deliver automated piston compressions and are used clinically in hospitals and EMS, but a clinician must interrupt manual CPR to position and strap the device on the patient, and the device performs only compressions — not rhythm assessment, ventilation, defibrillation or drug delivery.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: delivering chest compressions during cardiac arrest, one sub-step of the OR-code instance. Transfer is limited: the machine is carried, positioned and started by clinicians and does not perform the rest of the resuscitation, so it cannot complete the instance whole.

sources.title: AURA-CVC: Autonomous Ultrasound-guided Robotic Assistance for Central Venous Catheterization
sources.claim: An end-to-end autonomous robotic pipeline for ultrasound-guided central venous catheterization has been demonstrated only on a high-fidelity phantom, not on patients, indicating vascular-access autonomy is still pre-clinical.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: ultrasound-guided vascular cannulation, a sub-step of the invasive-access instance. It does not substantiate the instance: the demonstration is on a phantom, covers needle placement only, and excludes transducer setup, infusion management and pressure-guided titration.

sources.title: Corindus Seeking Neurovascular Intervention Clearance for CorPath GRX Vascular Robotic System | DAIC
sources.claim: Robotic intravascular systems that manipulate guidewires and catheters inside arteries are FDA-cleared and used in cath labs, but they are physician-controlled from a console (teleoperated), and their indication is coronary/peripheral intervention rather than bedside life-support device management.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: intra-arterial catheter/device manipulation, closest analogue to assisting IABP/Impella placement. Transfer fails on autonomy — the operator drives every wire and catheter movement from a console — so it cannot support a positive judgment.

sources.title: Humanoid robots could take on low-risk operating room tasks before assisting surgical teams
sources.claim: As of mid-2026 humanoid robots in the operating ... are discussed only as a prospective, low-risk-task-first integration; there is no reported deployment of a humanoid performing anesthesia-team patient care or resuscitation duties.
sources.transferJustification: Cited to show the state of general-purpose robots in ORs: forward-looking statements about low-risk tasks only, with no demonstrated resuscitation or anesthesia-assistant capability.

tasks.label: Monitor and document patients' progress during post-anesthesia period.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

tasks.label: Collect samples or specimens for diagnostic testing.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Intraoperative blood sample drawn from an indwelling arterial line during a case (ABG/electrolytes/lactate/hemoglobin, ACT in cardiac cases): patient anesthetized and draped on the OR table, AA accesses the sampling port aseptically, withdraws and discards or returns dead-space volume, fills a heparinized syringe or tube, clears bubbles, flushes the line, labels the specimen and runs it on the in-room/POC analyzer or sends it.

Intraoperative blood sample drawn from an existing central venous catheter or peripheral IV (glucose, hemoglobin, coags, type and screen): access under or beside surgical drapes with limited patient access, waste draw, filling of vacuum tubes or a syringe, flush, labeling, hand-off to the circulating nurse or POC device.

Preoperative blood specimen from an awake, cooperative patient in pre-op holding or PACU: venipuncture or a draw taken at the moment of IV catheter insertion, tubes filled for lab testing (type and screen, CBC, glucose, beta-hCG), labeled at the bedside and sent to the hospital lab.

Arterial puncture (radial, sometimes brachial/femoral) for a blood gas in a patient with no arterial line - pre-op, PACU or during a MAC case - palpation or ultrasound guidance, heparinized syringe, hemostasis held afterwards.

Non-blood specimens: urine drawn from a Foley catheter port or a voided sample, tracheal aspirate/secretions suctioned through the endotracheal tube for culture, gastric contents via OG tube, occasional wound or nasal swab; collected in the OR, pre-op or PACU and sent to the lab.

sources.title: Vitestro Publishes Landmark Peer-Reviewed Multicenter Clinical Study of Autonomous Robotic Phlebotomy in Clinical Chemistry
sources.claim: Aletta, an autonomous robotic phlebotomy device, performed diagnostic venipuncture on 1,633 patients across three hospital outpatient phlebotomy departments with a 94.5% first-stick success rate, 0.3% hemolysis and 0.6% adverse events, published in Clinical Chemistry.

sources.title: Automated Phlebotomy Firm Vitestro Eyes 2027 Commercial Launch of Robotic Blood Draw Device
sources.claim: Trade press on the same trial records the system's limits and status: it failed to find a suitable vein in 110 of 1,743 subjects; CE-marked units placed in Dutch and Danish hospitals have so far been used within clinical trials rather than routine care, with European commercial launch planned for 2027.

sources.title: Vitestro unveils Aletta robotic phlebotomy device - CAP TODAY
sources.claim: The Aletta device carries a CE mark and performs the whole venipuncture sequence itself - tourniquet, skin prep, ultrasound-guided vein selection, needle insertion, tube filling - rather than a single sub-step.

sources.title: Glucose Time-In-Range Development Evaluation (protocol, OptiScanner 5000 Indications for Use)
sources.claim: The FDA-cleared OptiScanner 5000 is a bedside machine that, through a dedicated tube-set plumbed to a patient's central venous catheter, automatically withdraws whole blood samples every 15 minutes, centrifuges them and measures plasma glucose; its clearance is limited to trending in surgical ICU patients.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated collection of a blood specimen from an indwelling central venous catheter for a diagnostic measurement. Same objects (catheter hub, dead-space handling, flush) and the same purpose as an anesthesiologist assistant drawing an intraoperative line specimen, except the blood is delivered to the machine's own analyzer through a dedicated line rather than into labeled tubes.

sources.title: OptiScan reels in $20M for broad rollout of automated bedside glucose monitoring system | Fierce Biotech
sources.claim: After FDA clearance this automated bedside sampling/analysis system was placed in hospitals in the US and ... (the developer is listed as no longer an active company as of 2026).
sources.transferJustification: Same related task as above - machine-controlled specimen withdrawal from an indwelling vascular catheter for diagnostic measurement - showing it ran in real hospital critical-care rooms, though always with the catheter dedicated to the device's own tube-set.

sources.title: Arterial Blood Gas | Respiratory Therapy (product roundup)
sources.claim: VIA Medical marketed a bedside monitor plumbed into a patient's vascular catheter that automatically draws the blood sample into its sensor, analyses blood gases, chemistry and hematocrit, and reinfuses the blood - machine-performed sampling from an indwelling line for diagnostic testing.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated in-line arterial/venous sampling plus analysis - the same physical operation (dead-space clearing, sample withdrawal, flush/reinfusion) an anesthesiologist assistant performs when drawing an ABG from an arterial line, but with the line dedicated to the machine.

sources.developer: VIA Medical Corp (evaluation by University of Utah Dept. of Anesthesiology)
sources.title: Evaluation in volunteers of the VIA V-ABG automated bedside blood gas, chemistry, and hematocrit monitor - PubMed
sources.claim: Peer-reviewed volunteer evaluation of the automated VIA V-ABG bedside monitor found its blood gas results clinically acceptable against CLIA proficiency standards, with sodium, potassium and hematocrit also meeting performance criteria.
sources.transferJustification: Establishes that machine-collected in-line samples yield results of the quality a clinician's hand-drawn ABG specimen would deliver; same analytes, same patients-with-catheters, same diagnostic purpose as the intraoperative arterial-line draw.

sources.system: Culex Automated Blood Collection System (Culex NxT)
sources.title: Home - BASi Culex Automated Blood Collection System
sources.claim: The commercially sold Culex automated blood collection system autonomously withdraws timed blood samples through an indwelling catheter, handles dead-space and heparinized flush, and deposits the samples into vials for analysis, in a purpose-built sampling station.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: unattended, scheduled specimen collection from an indwelling vascular catheter into containers for laboratory analysis - the same fluid-handling operation as a line draw, but demonstrated only where the subject and catheter are presented to the machine in a purpose-built station (preclinical laboratory), which is why it supports E1 and not E2.

sources.system: HAMEL (Hematic Auto-Management and Extraction for arterial Line)
sources.title: Hematic auto-management and extraction for arterial line (HAMEL), a blood-preserving arterial line system: an animal study
sources.claim: State of the art for arterial-line sampling: a 2023 animal study of an automated blood-preserving arterial line system reports that dead-space clearing and flushing were automated but the sampling itself is still performed by hand, with automation of the A-line valve only a future goal.
sources.transferJustification: Directly about the instance task (drawing lab specimens from an arterial line); cited as evidence that no fielded system performs the OR-style arterial-line draw autonomously in the human workflow.

tasks.label: Provide clinical instruction, supervision or training to staff in areas such as anesthesia practices.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Precepting an anesthesiologist assistant student or newly hired AA during live OR cases: observing their conduct of induction, monitoring and emergence, giving running verbal guidance and corrections, and debriefing after the case.

In-servicing OR, PACU or procedural-suite nurses and techs on anesthesia-related practices: machine checkout, monitor setup, airway cart contents, new drug or infusion-pump protocols — explaining and answering questions at the equipment.

Scheduled didactic or simulation-lab teaching: lecture or case-conference presentation to students/staff, or running and debriefing a simulated crisis scenario (malignant hyperthermia, difficult airway) in a sim center.

Informal coaching and supervisory oversight: answering questions in the hallway or workroom, reviewing anesthesia records and documentation with a trainee, completing competency checklists and written performance evaluations.

Hands-on skill demonstration to a trainee — showing mask ventilation, laryngoscopy/intubation, or IV/arterial line technique on a manikin or, with supervision, on a consented patient — then watching the trainee repeat it and correcting technique.

tasks.label: Participate in seminars, workshops, or other professional activities to keep abreast of developments in anesthesiology.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Attending a hospital department grand rounds, morbidity-and-mortality conference, or in-service lecture on a new anesthetic agent or monitoring modality; listening, taking notes, asking questions, logging CME credit.

Completing online/self-paced continuing medical education modules or webinars (e.g., AAAA or ASA offerings) required to maintain NCCAA certification, including reading journal articles and passing post-tests.
Traveling to a national or state professional society annual meeting (AAAA, ASA) to attend lecture sessions, poster halls, and vendor exhibits, and to network with colleagues.

Participating in a hands-on workshop or simulation-lab session at a conference or hospital sim center — e.g., ultrasound-guided line placement, difficult-airway devices, or crisis-resource-management scenarios on a manikin.
Serving on a departmental committee, journal club, or professional society working group that reviews new guidelines and disseminates practice updates to colleagues.

tasks.label: Assist in the application of monitoring techniques, such as pulmonary artery catheterization, electroencephalographic spectral analysis, echocardiography, or evoked potentials.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Operating room, general/cardiac case: AA applies processed-EEG depth-of-anesthesia monitoring — preps the forehead skin, peels and presses on the adhesive multi-electrode sensor strip around drapes, ET tube and IV lines, snaps in the cable, checks impedance/signal quality, and troubleshoots artifact (cautery, head repositioning) during the case.

Cardiac/vascular or ICU case: AA assists the anesthesiologist with pulmonary artery (Swan-Ganz) or central line catheterization — opens sterile kits and passes items to the sterile field, assembles/primes and zeroes the pressure transducer sets, positions the patient (Trendelenburg, head turn), runs the monitor and calls out RA/RV/PA/wedge waveforms as the catheter is floated, then secures and dresses lines and sets up the cardiac-output computer.

Cardiac OR: AA assists with intraoperative transesophageal echocardiography — checks and preps the probe (leak/bite check, lubricant, bite block), assists the anesthesiologist during blind esophageal insertion in the anesthetized, intubated patient, secures the probe and cables, sets up the echo machine and archives loops, then removes and high-level disinfects the probe.

Spine/neuro or aortic case with intraoperative neuromonitoring: AA assists the neuromonitoring team applying evoked-potential monitoring — helping place and tape subdermal needle or surface electrodes on scalp and limbs, corkscrew/bite-block placement for MEPs, routing and securing lead bundles clear of the field, and adjusting anesthetic technique when signals degrade.

Any OR/ICU: AA sets up, levels, zeroes, calibrates and troubleshoots invasive hemodynamic monitoring hardware — arterial-line transducer assembly and flush bag pressurization, re-leveling to the phlebostatic axis after table position changes, square-wave testing, fixing damped waveforms, loose stopcocks and air bubbles mid-case.

sources.system: Robotic TEE system (dual-subsystem probe manipulator with UR5 arm)
sources.developer: Academic research group (paper in Int. J. Computer Assisted Radiology and Surgery / PubMed)
sources.title: Robotic transesophageal echocardiography: system design and deep learning-based kinematic modeling
sources.claim: State-of-the-art robotic transesophageal echocardiography systems manipulate the TEE probe under teleoperation and are described only as a foundation for future semi-autonomous systems; probe insertion into the patient remains manual.
sources.transferJustification: Directly the echocardiography instance: it is the closest robotic system to intraoperative TEE, and shows the manipulation is teleoperated rather than autonomous.

sources.developer: Tsinghua University / Chinese PLA General Hospital
sources.title: Towards expert-level autonomous carotid ultrasonography with large-scale learning-based robotic system (Nature Communications)
sources.claim: A fully autonomous robotic ultrasound ... performs carotid scanning on human subjects at expert level in a clinical validation, i.e., autonomous probe placement and image acquisition on intact skin is achievable, but only for non-invasive surface scanning of a cooperative, stationary subject.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous ultrasound image acquisition on a patient. It bounds what autonomous medical ultrasound robots do today — surface scanning of the neck — and does not extend to inserting a TEE probe into an anesthetized patient's esophagus or to the AA's sterile setup and assist role.

sources.developer: University of Texas at Austin / UCLA
sources.title: Printed E-tattoo Ink-credible at Reading Brainwaves / On-scalp printing of personalized electroencephalography e-tattoos (Cell Biomaterials)
sources.claim: A 5-axis robotic microjet printer applies EEG sensors directly onto a human scalp from a 3D head scan and records usable EEG, but it is a laboratory demonstration on seated volunteers with buzz-cut hair and does not produce the standard disposable depth-of-anesthesia sensor used in the OR.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: machine application of EEG electrodes to a human head. Transfer is partial only — the robot deposits ink on a still, seated volunteer's shaved scalp rather than applying and cabling an adhesive BIS/SedLine strip on a draped, intubated patient.

sources.title: Safety and efficacy of a novel robotic transcranial doppler system in subarachnoid hemorrhage (Scientific Reports)
sources.claim: An FDA-cleared, commercially deployed robotic transcranial Doppler system autonomously moves the transducers to find and track cerebral artery signals in hospital patients, but a human operator still fits the headset on the patient's head.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: applying a neuromonitoring modality to a hospital patient. It shows the deployed state of the art automates only signal search within a human-applied headset, not the AA's sensor application, sterile setup or catheter-assist work.

sources.developer: Johns Hopkins University / Siemens Healthineers collaborators
sources.title: AURA-CVC: Autonomous Ultrasound-guided Robotic Assistance for Central Venous Catheterization (IJCARS)
sources.claim: An end-to-end autonomous ultrasound-guided robotic central venous catheterization pipeline has been validated only on a high-fidelity commercial phantom, not on patients, and still involves operator feedback.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: central venous access, the first step of pulmonary artery catheterization. It shows robotic autonomy here is phantom-stage, so it cannot substantiate the AA's sterile-field assist, transducer priming and waveform-guided floating of a PA catheter in a patient.

sources.system: AI-GUIDE (Artificial Intelligence Guided Ultrasound Interventional Device)
sources.title: AI-Enabled, Ultrasound-Guided Handheld Robotic Device for Femoral Vascular Access
sources.claim: A handheld AI-guided robotic vascular access device performs the needle puncture robotically but requires a human to hold and place the device on the subject; results are from phantom and live porcine studies.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: obtaining large-vein access for hemodynamic monitoring. It is human-held and human-positioned, so it cannot stand in for an unattended robot completing the catheterization-assist instance.

roles.title: Podiatrists
aliases: Doctor of Podiatric Medicine and Surgery (DPM and Surgery)
roles.description: Diagnose and treat diseases and deformities of the human foot.

tasks.label: Treat bone, muscle, and joint disorders affecting the feet and ankles.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Podiatry office visit for a common musculoskeletal complaint (plantar fasciitis, Achilles/posterior tibial tendinopathy, metatarsalgia, arthritic joint pain): hands-on exam and palpation of the painful structures, then in-office conservative treatment - low-Dye strapping, felt/foam accommodative padding applied to the foot, shoe/insole modification, fitting an off-the-shelf brace or night splint, hands-on stretching instruction, and adjustment at follow-up. Adult patient seated in an exam chair, skin condition variable, patient moves and reacts to pain.

In-office injection or aspiration for a bone/joint/soft-tissue disorder: corticosteroid-anesthetic injection into the plantar fascia insertion, a Morton's neuroma web space, or the first MTP/subtalar/ankle joint; sometimes ultrasound-guided; includes skin prep, palpation- or image-based needle placement into a small target near nerves and vessels, joint aspiration, post-injection dressing and instructions. Clinic exam room, awake patient.

Custom functional foot orthosis episode: biomechanical and gait examination, subtalar-neutral plaster casting or 3D scanning of the foot, writing the prescription, then at the dispense visit fitting the finished device in the patient's shoes, grinding/heat-adjusting posts and edges chairside, and re-checking gait for a symptomatic flatfoot, cavus foot, or arthritic forefoot.

Immobilization and fracture/sprain management in clinic: closed reduction of a displaced toe or metatarsal fracture, application of a below-knee fiberglass cast, posterior splint, total contact cast for a Charcot foot, or fitting and adjusting a CAM walker boot; wrapping around a moving, painful limb with correct tension and padding, plus cast removal with an oscillating saw at follow-up.

Podiatric surgery in a hospital OR or ambulatory surgery center: bunionectomy/Lapidus, hammertoe correction, osteotomy with screw or plate fixation, ankle fracture ORIF, arthrodesis, tendon repair or ankle arthroplasty - sterile prep and draping, incision, soft-tissue dissection around neurovascular structures, bone cutting and realignment, hardware placement under fluoroscopy, closure and postoperative splinting.

Bedside/off-site treatment of a musculoskeletal foot problem: nursing-home round or house call for a frail or immobile patient - offloading padding for a deformity, brace or boot fitting, joint range-of-motion assessment and manipulation, shoe modification - performed at a bedside or in a living room with no dedicated equipment, variable lighting and clutter.

sources.system: Robotic-assisted foot and ankle surgery (state-of-the-field review)
sources.developer: Multiple developers, review published in Frontiers/PMC10590355
sources.title: Robotic-assisted foot and ankle surgery: a review of the present status and the future
sources.claim: A peer-reviewed review of robotic-assisted foot and ankle surgery finds that intraoperative robotic use in this subspecialty is confined to guiding percutaneous screw fixation of tarsal bones, with the surgeon performing the operation.
sources.transferJustification: Directly on point: it surveys robotic capability for surgical treatment of foot and ankle bone/joint disorders, which is the surgical instance of this task.

sources.title: Comparison of Robot-Assisted Percutaneous Cannulated Screws Versus Open Reduction and Internal Fixation in Calcaneal Fractures
sources.claim: TiRobot is used clinically to guide percutaneous cannulated screw fixation of calcaneal fractures; the robot positions a drill guide from imaging while the surgeon reduces the fracture, drills and inserts screws, so the procedure is surgeon-performed with robotic guidance.
sources.transferJustification: Same task family (operative treatment of a hindfoot bone disorder); shows the most advanced clinical foot/ankle robotic application is guidance for one sub-step, not autonomous completion of the operation.

sources.title: SRT-H: A hierarchical framework for autonomous surgery via language-conditioned imitation learning
sources.claim: The frontier of autonomous surgery as of mid-2025 is a learned policy performing a soft-tissue cholecystectomy on ex vivo pig gallbladders in a laboratory on a da Vinci platform; no autonomous system operates on live human bone or joints.
sources.transferJustification: Related task (autonomous surgery) used to bound capability: ex vivo animal soft tissue in a lab does not transfer to bunionectomy or osteotomy with fixation on a live patient.

sources.title: Robotic guidance for ultrasound-guided percutaneous procedures: a prospective multispecialty feasibility study
sources.claim: The most advanced clinically evaluated robotic needle system for ultrasound-guided percutaneous procedures is a handheld device the clinician holds and aims, with the robot driving the needle along the operator's planned trajectory rather than selecting the target and performing the procedure itself.
sources.transferJustification: Related task (image-guided needle placement in patients) bounding the injection instance: the operator holds and aims the device, so it cannot autonomously complete a podiatric joint or neuroma injection.

sources.system: Ultrasound-guided robotic system for autonomous percutaneous intervention
sources.developer: Mohan, Agrawal and Patel (Worcester Polytechnic Institute)
sources.title: Preliminary Evaluation of an Ultrasound-Guided Robotic System for Autonomous Percutaneous Intervention
sources.claim: Autonomous robotic needle targeting has only been validated on agar phantoms with several millimetres of targeting error, not on patients.
sources.transferJustification: Related task (autonomous needle placement) bounding the injection instance; phantom-only validation with millimetre-scale error does not transfer to injecting a neuroma or small foot joint in a patient.

sources.system: M6 MLS Therapy Laser (robotized multi-target device)
sources.developer: ASA Laser / Cutting Edge Laser Technologies
sources.title: M6 MLS Therapy Laser - Cutting Edge Lasers
sources.claim: The automated hardware actually installed in podiatry offices for musculoskeletal complaints is a therapy laser whose optical head is motorised to scan a target area automatically; a clinician positions the emitter over the foot and selects the preset protocol, and the device delivers only one adjunct modality within a treatment plan.
sources.transferJustification: Used in podiatry clinics for plantar fasciitis and tendinopathy, but it is a human-positioned, preset applicator delivering one adjunct modality, so it cannot substantiate completion of a conservative-care instance.

tasks.label: Diagnose diseases and deformities of the foot using medical histories, physical examinations, x-rays, and laboratory test results.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Outpatient podiatry office visit for a painful foot/ankle condition (plantar fasciitis, Morton's neuroma, metatarsalgia, Achilles tendinopathy). The podiatrist takes the history, has the patient remove shoes, palpates to localize point tenderness, tests joint range of motion and strength, watches stance and gait, orders and reads in-office weight-bearing x-rays, and records a diagnosis.

Diabetic/vascular foot assessment in the clinic exam room: inspect skin and interdigital spaces, 10 g monofilament and tuning-fork sensory testing at multiple sites, palpate dorsalis pedis/posterior tibial pulses or use Doppler, probe an ulcer for depth/bone, and integrate labs (CBC, ESR/CRP, HbA1c, wound culture) and x-ray to diagnose neuropathy, ischemia, ulcer stage or osteomyelitis.

Skin and nail complaint in the clinic (onychomycosis, verruca, tinea, ingrown nail with paronychia): visual and tactile inspection of nails and plantar skin, debriding or clipping a nail/skin specimen for KOH/PAS or culture, and correlating the returned laboratory result with the clinical picture to reach a diagnosis.

Structural/biomechanical evaluation in the clinic (hallux valgus, hammertoe, adult or pediatric flatfoot, in-toeing, equinus): manual assessment of joint reducibility, subtalar and ankle range of motion, muscle testing, static alignment and gait/pressure analysis, plus angle measurement on weight-bearing radiographs, to diagnose and grade the deformity.

Bedside consult in a hospital ward or skilled nursing facility for a non-ambulatory patient (severe diabetic foot infection, gangrene, Charcot arthropathy, heel pressure injury): examine the foot with the patient in bed, remove dressings, assess perfusion and probe wounds, and combine findings with imaging and laboratory results to render the diagnosis.

sources.system: Fully autonomous robotic ultrasound system for thyroid scanning
sources.developer: South China University of Technology (Su et al., Nature Communications)
sources.title: A fully autonomous robotic ultrasound system for thyroid scanning | Nature Communications
sources.claim: A fully autonomous robotic ultrasound arm scanned the thyroid region of human participants without human assistance and flagged malignant nodules - the closest robotic analogue to an autonomous clinical examination, but it acquires images of one anatomic region and does not take a history, palpate for tenderness, test sensation, or integrate x-rays and laboratory results into a diagnosis.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous robotic examination of a patient. It shows a robot can contact a patient and gather diagnostic data autonomously, but transfer to podiatric diagnosis fails: no history-taking, no palpation for point tenderness, no sensory or range-of-motion testing, and no multi-source clinical diagnosis.

sources.system: Autonomous lightweight ultrasound robot for liver sonography
sources.developer: Research team evaluated at Beijing Tsinghua Changgung Hospital
sources.title: Beyond hospital reach: Autonomous lightweight ultrasound robot for liver sonography
sources.claim: An autonomous lightweight ultrasound robot was deployed in a hospital ultrasound department to perform liver sonography tasks autonomously, showing robots can operate on patients inside a structured clinical facility, but the output is image acquisition and organ localization, not a diagnosis assembled from history, hands-on foot examination, radiographs and labs.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous robotic patient examination inside an E2 hospital facility. It bounds current capability - image capture of a large abdominal organ - and does not extend to the tactile, multi-modal diagnostic reasoning of a podiatric examination.

sources.developer: University of Cambridge / Imperial College London
sources.title: Face mediated human-robot interaction for remote medical examination | Scientific Reports
sources.claim: Robotic palpation of patients remains a laboratory research problem: reported systems are teleoperated master-slave platforms or learning prototypes tested on phantoms, not autonomous clinical examiners, so no cited robot can perform the palpation that localizes foot pathology.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: palpation-based physical examination, a core component of every podiatric diagnostic instance. The system is human-driven teleoperation on a robotic phantom, so it cannot support autonomous completion of any instance.

sources.developer: Academic prototype reported in Journal of Medical and Biological Engineering (ScienceDirect)
sources.title: A Novel Robotic Monofilament Test for Diabetic Neuropathy - ScienceDirect
sources.claim: The only foot-specific robotic examination device found is a prototype robotic monofilament inspector for diabetic neuropathy screening - a single sensory sub-test, not a diagnosis, and not a deployed clinical product.
sources.transferJustification: Directly related sub-step of the diabetic foot instance (monofilament sensory testing). It covers one screening test only, is an old unvalidated prototype with unestablished autonomy, and produces no diagnosis integrating exam, imaging and labs.

sources.developer: Synyi AI with Almoosa Health Group
sources.title: World's first AI medical clinic opens in Saudi Arabia with Dr Hua system | Business Standard
sources.claim: Autonomous clinical diagnosis systems now in service, such as the Synyi AI 'Dr Hua' clinic, are software agents without physical embodiment; human doctors review the plans and any hands-on examination remains human, so they are not robotic systems and cannot substantiate physical completion of the examination.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: clinical diagnosis. Explicitly non-robotic (software only) and physician-reviewed, so under the rules it cannot support a positive judgment for a task whose examination component requires acting on the patient.

tasks.label: Advise patients about treatments and foot care techniques necessary for prevention of future problems.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

tasks.label: Prescribe medications, corrective devices, physical therapy, or surgery.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

tasks.label: Surgically treat conditions such as corns, calluses, ingrown nails, tumors, shortened tendons, bunions, cysts, or abscesses.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Office procedure room: partial or total nail avulsion with chemical (phenol) matrixectomy for a painful ingrown toenail. Podiatrist injects a digital block, applies a tourniquet, elevates and splits the nail plate, avulses the offending border, curettes granulation tissue, phenolizes the matrix, obtains hemostasis and dresses the toe. Patients range from healthy teens to diabetic/vascular-compromised elderly.

Office exam room: sharp excisional debridement of painful corns, intractable plantar keratoses and hyperkeratotic callus with scalpel/curette on an unanesthetized live foot, often on insensate diabetic feet where a nucleated lesion may overlie a pre-ulcer or ulcer; depth judged by feel, paring to healthy skin without bleeding.

Office/minor-procedure room: incision and drainage of a paronychia or foot abscess, excision of a small ganglion/inclusion cyst, or curettage/excision of a verruca or small benign lesion under local anesthesia, with specimen handling, packing or suturing and dressing.

Ambulatory surgery center or hospital OR: bunionectomy (e.g., Austin/Lapidus) or hammertoe correction under sedation with ankle block; skin incision, capsulotomy and dissection around neurovascular structures, osteotomy, realignment, screw/plate fixation, capsule repair, layered closure and dressing/boot.

Hospital OR / ASC: soft-tissue reconstructive work such as gastrocnemius recession or tendon lengthening/transfer for equinus or deformity, and excision of soft-tissue tumors (plantar fibroma, neuroma, larger cysts), requiring dissection around nerves and vessels, tensioning judgment and layered closure.

sources.title: Johns Hopkins teaches robot to perform a gallbladder removal on a realistic patient - The Robot Report
sources.claim: Johns Hopkins' SRT-H robot autonomously performed one lengthy phase of a gallbladder ... lifelike/ex-vivo model - not a whole operation and not on a live human patient.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous soft-tissue surgery. It marks the frontier for machine-executed dissection and cutting of tissue, but falls short of podiatric surgery because only one phase of a procedure was executed, on a lifelike/ex-vivo model rather than a live patient.

sources.title: FDA OKs Think Surgical's TSolution One robotic knee surgery system - The Robot Report
sources.claim: Think Surgical's TSolution One is an FDA-cleared active robot that autonomously mills bone for total knee replacement; only the bone-preparation step is automated inside an operation otherwise performed by the surgeon.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous bone cutting in orthopedic surgery, analogous to the osteotomy step of a bunionectomy. Transfer is limited to that sub-step; the robot never opens, dissects, fixates or closes, so it cannot deliver a whole podiatric procedure.

sources.system: DLR MIRO robot with ERBEJET 2 waterjet debridement system
sources.developer: German Aerospace Center (DLR) and clinical collaborators
sources.title: Robotic waterjet wound debridement - Workflow adaption for clinical application and systematic evaluation of a novel technology (PLOS ONE)
sources.claim: A DLR MIRO robot arm actuating a waterjet probe autonomously planned and executed wound debridement, but only on a porcine skin model in the laboratory; the authors state in vivo trials are still needed.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous debridement of skin tissue, the closest published analogue to scalpel debridement of corns and calluses. It does not transfer: the work was ex-vivo porcine skin in a lab, with no live, pain-sensitive, bleeding human foot and no clinical acceptance.

sources.title: Ulta Beauty Introduces Five-Step Robotic Manicure by Robotics Firm 10Beauty
sources.claim: 10Beauty's autonomous manicure machine is deployed commercially in Ulta Beauty stores and works on customers' live hands, but performs only cosmetic steps and files nails without blades.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous machine work on human nails. It does not transfer to nail surgery: no anesthesia, no cutting of living tissue, no nail-plate avulsion or matrix ablation, and no sterile surgical standard of care.

tasks.label: Refer patients to physicians when symptoms indicative of systemic disorders, such as arthritis or diabetes, are observed in feet and legs.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

tasks.label: Make and fit prosthetic appliances.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Impression/capture visit in the clinic exam room: podiatrist positions the patient's foot (e.g., subtalar neutral, non-weightbearing), takes a plaster slipper cast, foam-box impression or 3D scan of both feet, records biomechanical findings, and writes the device prescription (shell material, posting, additions).

Dispensing/fitting visit: podiatrist seats the finished orthosis or appliance in the patient's own shoes, checks heel cup seating, arch contact and shoe fit, watches the patient stand and walk, then grinds the shell, bevels edges, or adds pads chairside until the patient accepts the fit, and gives break-in instructions.

Bench fabrication of the prescribed device in an in-office or central lab: produce the positive model or digital design, mill or thermoform the shell over it, trim and grind the periphery, add rearfoot/forefoot posts, met pads and top cover, and finish to the prescription.

Follow-up modification with the patient present: patient returns with a hot spot, arch irritation or heel slippage; podiatrist identifies the offending area on the device, grinds a relief, adds a heel lift, met pad or extrinsic post, refits in the shoe and re-checks gait.

Partial-foot prosthesis, toe filler, or accommodative diabetic device for an amputated or ulcer-risk foot: hand-mold/impress the residual foot, fabricate the filler and accommodative insole with relief over the at-risk area, fit into a therapeutic shoe, inspect skin and pressure-check the fit.

sources.system: Roboticom ORTIS / ORTIS Pro robotic milling system
sources.title: Ortis™ Roboticom: high precision robot for orthopedic applications
sources.claim: ORTIS is a commercially sold 7-axis robotic milling system installed in orthopedic (O&P) production facilities that carves positive and negative models and components for custom orthoses and prostheses from plaster, foam and polyurethane under program control.
sources.transferJustification: Covers the 'make' step of the podiatrist's task: the workpiece is fixtured in the robot cell and the appliance model/shell is carved to the digital prescription, the same objects and precision as bench fabrication of a foot orthosis.

sources.system: HP Arize Orthotic Solution (Multi Jet Fusion production)
sources.title: New Arize Custom Orthoses to Help Podiatrists Relieve Foot Pain for Millions | HP Official Site
sources.claim: HP's Arize solution has podiatrists scan the patient in-clinic and then manufactures the finished custom orthosis on HP Multi Jet Fusion 3D printers in a production facility, delivering the device back to the clinic for fitting.
sources.transferJustification: Substantiates automated fabrication ('make') of the prescribed appliance; the scanning and the subsequent patient fitting remain clinician steps.

sources.system: HP Arize 3D-printed custom orthoses vs traditionally fabricated custom foot orthoses
sources.developer: HP Inc. / University of South Carolina investigators
sources.title: Pilot, Randomized Comparison of Traditionally Fabricated Custom Foot Orthoses vs HP Arize 3D-Printed Orthoses for Plantar Fasciitis
sources.claim: A 2026 pilot randomized trial found machine-manufactured (3D-printed) custom orthoses matched traditionally fabricated custom orthoses on patient satisfaction with fit and comfort and on functional improvement, supporting that automated fabrication reaches acceptable clinical quality.
sources.transferJustification: Quality benchmark for the fabrication instance: shows the machine-made appliance is accepted in place of the hand-made one by patients and clinicians.

sources.system: Mosaic Orion / Array automated orthotics 3D printing platform
sources.title: Automated Orthotics Manufacturing | Orthotics Production Automation | Mosaic
sources.claim: Mosaic sells Orion/Array, purpose-built automated 3D printing systems for orthotics labs with automated build-plate placement and part removal and a finished-parts cart, producing custom insoles with minimal-to-zero manual finishing.
sources.transferJustification: Directly the fabrication step of the task: automated machine handling and production of the custom foot orthosis inside a purpose-built production cell.

sources.system: Amfit CAD/CAM Mill (with Contact Digitizer / Impress Scanner)
sources.date: 2026-03 (product page); system commercial for many years
sources.title: Products - Amfit
sources.claim: Amfit sells a CAD/CAM milling machine used in podiatry offices and central fabrication labs that mills finished custom EVA orthotics and positive models from a captured foot shape, with the mill performing most of the shaping work.
sources.transferJustification: Shows the in-office variant of the fabrication instance is performed by a fixtured milling machine from a captured foot shape.

tasks.label: Correct deformities by means of plaster casts and strapping.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Office exam room: adult with plantar fasciitis or flexible flatfoot/posterior tibial tendon dysfunction. Podiatrist positions the foot in the corrected (inverted/plantarflexed) position and applies a low-Dye or reverse-6 strapping with anchor strips and adhesive tape directly to skin, adjusting tension to hold the arch without wrinkling, blistering or compromising circulation; patient seated/prone on exam chair, foot moving slightly.

Office exam room: forefoot/digital deformity padding and strapping — felt or foam pads (metatarsal, dancer's, bunion shield) cut to shape and taped in place, or hammertoe/hallux valgus splinting with tape buddy-strapping, on an often deformed, callused, or edematous foot.

Wound/limb-salvage clinic: total contact cast or below-knee plaster/fiberglass cast for a diabetic neuropathic ulcer or acute Charcot foot. Includes removing the previous cast with an oscillating saw, inspecting and dressing the wound, applying stockinette, felt padding over bony prominences, and molding a well-fitted cast with the ankle held at 90 degrees on an insensate limb where a pressure point can cause a new ulcer.

Hospital/surgical center or clinic: below-knee cast, splint or Jones compression dressing applied after bunion/rearfoot surgery or for an acute deformity/fracture, with the corrected alignment held while plaster/fiberglass sets, over a limb that may be anesthetized, swollen, or with surgical dressings and pins in place.

Pediatric clinic: serial casting (Ponseti-style or for metatarsus adductus) on an infant or small child — manual manipulation of the deformity to the corrected position, above-knee or below-knee plaster applied and molded while the child squirms and cries, then removed and repeated at weekly intervals.

Mobile/house-call or nursing-home bedside visit: strapping or a light cast/splint applied to a frail or bedbound patient's foot in a resident room or living room, with the patient in bed or a recliner, variable lighting, no exam chair, and supplies carried in a bag.

sources.system: UCSD autonomous tape-handling framework for robotic wound redressing (dVRK/dexterous-hand setup)
sources.developer: University of California San Diego (Liang, Shen, Zhang, Atar, Richter, Yip)
sources.title: Towards Autonomous Tape Handling for Robotic Wound Redressing
sources.claim: The most advanced published work on robotic handling of adhesive medical tape addresses only sub-steps (tape detachment and placement) and is demonstrated on a manikin in a laboratory, not on patients; wound care itself remains an entirely manual clinician task.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: applying adhesive tape/dressing to a body surface, the closest published analogue to podiatric strapping. It shows the frontier is isolated sub-steps on a manikin hip in a lab, well short of positioning a deformed foot and applying a tensioned strapping or a molded cast.

sources.title: Massage Envy Introduces Aescape Robotic Massage at Select Franchised Locations
sources.claim: Autonomous robots do make force-controlled contact with human bodies in commercial human-work facilities (spa/wellness studios), showing human-contact autonomy exists, but the system only presses on the back and legs and performs no material handling, wrapping, or limb correction.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous, force-regulated contact with a human body in a structured facility. It substantiates safe human contact only; it involves no deformable-material manipulation, no wrapping around a limb, and no corrective positioning, so it cannot substantiate casting or strapping.

sources.system: Bimanual robot-assisted dressing (spherical-coordinate strategy for tight-fitting garments)
sources.developer: University of York / Honda Research Institute EU
sources.title: Bimanual Robot-Assisted Dressing: A Spherical Coordinate-Based Strategy for Tight-Fitting Garments
sources.claim: Robotic manipulation of deformable garments onto human limbs remains a laboratory research problem, with current work still focused on basic strategies for getting a sleeve over an arm.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: manipulating compliant material onto a human limb. Even loose-garment donning is unsolved outside the lab, indicating no system can wrap tensioned tape or plaster around a foot held in a corrected position.

tasks.label: Perform administrative duties, such as hiring employees, ordering supplies, or keeping records.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

tasks.label: Educate the public about the benefits of foot care through techniques such as speaking engagements, advertising, and other forums.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

tasks.label: Treat deformities using mechanical methods, such as whirlpool or paraffin baths, and electrical methods, such as short wave and low voltage currents.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Hydrotherapy/whirlpool foot bath in a podiatry office or hospital wound-care room: podiatrist sets water temperature and additives, seats the patient, immerses the deformed/ulcerated foot, agitates for 10-20 minutes while watching skin color and patient tolerance, then lifts, towel-dries and inspects the foot before dressing.

Paraffin wax bath for a stiff, arthritic or contracted foot: melt/temper the wax, test temperature, repeatedly dip or paint the foot to build a wax glove, wrap in plastic and towel, wait, then peel off the wax and follow with stretching/manipulation.

Low-voltage electrical modality in the clinic (galvanic/high-volt stimulation, TENS, interferential, iontophoresis): palpate to find the treatment site, prep skin, peel and stick adhesive electrodes on specific points of the foot/ankle, ramp current to patient tolerance, monitor and adjust during the session, then remove electrodes and inspect skin.

Energy-modality applicator held or positioned over the foot: short-wave diathermy drum, therapeutic ultrasound head moved through coupling gel, or low-level laser scanned over the plantar fascia/joint; podiatrist screens for contraindications, sets dose and duration, positions the applicator on the target and monitors warmth/pain during delivery.

Hands-on mechanical treatment of the deformity: soft-tissue massage and mobilization/stretching of the forefoot or plantar fascia, or a radial shockwave probe pressed and moved over the tender point with pressure guided by the patient's verbal feedback, in the clinic treatment room.

Modality treatment delivered away from the office: portable e-stim, warm soak or massage/mobilization at a nursing-home bedside or on a house call, in a room with variable furniture, lighting and floor space and a frail, sometimes uncooperative patient.

sources.system: M6 MLS Robotic Therapy Laser (ASA Laser / Cutting Edge Lasers)
sources.developer: ASA Srl / Cutting Edge Laser Technologies
sources.title: Robotic M6 MLS Therapy Laser
sources.claim: The M6 MLS therapy laser is a commercial clinic device (sold into podiatry practices) whose robotized articulated arm and scanning head deliver a timed photobiomodulation dose over a target treatment area hands-free after the clinician positions it, i.e. machine-controlled delivery of an energy modality onto a patient's limb.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotized delivery of a physical-agent (laser) modality. It transfers to the ONET modality task because the physical act is the same class - an applicator held over the foot delivering timed energy at a set dose - in the same podiatry treatment room; only the energy type differs from short-wave diathermy.

sources.system: M6 Robotic MLS Therapy Laser (podiatry distribution)
sources.title: M6 Robotic MLS Therapy Laser - Progressive Podiatry
sources.claim: The same robotized M6 laser is marketed and used in podiatry practices for automatic applications over wide treatment areas of the foot and lower limb.
sources.transferJustification: Same transfer as above: it establishes that the robotized applicator is used on podiatry patients in podiatry clinics, the setting of this task.

sources.developer: Lin et al., academic group (published in Frontiers in Robotics and AI)
sources.title: Autonomous robotic ultrasound scanning system: a key to enhancing image analysis reproducibility and observer consistency in ultrasound imaging
sources.claim: A fully autonomous robotic ultrasound scanning system placed and moved a probe on a live human volunteer under closed-loop contact-force control and image visual servoing, matching or beating physicians on reproducibility - i.e. autonomous force-controlled application of a treatment-style applicator to human tissue.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous diagnostic ultrasound scanning. It transfers to therapeutic ultrasound/diathermy application because the physical act is identical - pressing and sweeping a coupled applicator over skin at a regulated contact force - though demonstrated on the neck rather than the foot and in a research setting.

sources.title: FDA clears Axilum Robotics' system for TMS positioning
sources.claim: Axilum's TMS-Cobot is an FDA-cleared clinical robot that positions and maintains a therapeutic stimulation coil in contact with a patient's head during treatment sessions, compensating for patient motion, in ordinary clinic rooms.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robot-held therapeutic stimulation applicator on a patient. Autonomy is operator-in-the-loop (the clinician retains real-time control and selects the target), so it is treated as teleoperated and used only as context, not to support a positive judgment.

sources.title: I Tried Aescape, the High-Tech Robot Massage-Here's My Review
sources.claim: Aescape, the most widely deployed autonomous body-contact therapy robot (Equinox gyms, Hyatt hotels), delivers force-controlled massage after a 3D body scan, but its treatment envelope excludes the feet, hands, arms, neck and anterior body.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous mechanical soft-tissue therapy on a human body. It bounds what deployed massage robots can do - back and posterior legs on a fixed table - and explicitly excludes the foot, so it cannot substantiate foot massage/mobilization.

sources.developer: I-SUPPORT EU consortium (NTUA, UCL and partners)
sources.title: I-Support: A robotic platform of an assistive bathing robot for the elderly population
sources.claim: The I-SUPPORT project built a prototype soft-arm robotic shower system that washes an elderly user's back and lower limbs in a clinical bathroom; it remained a research prototype evaluated in validation studies with mixed operation modes rather than a deployed system.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic washing of the lower limbs. It is the nearest system to hydrotherapy administration, but it is a prototype with operator-dependent modes and does not set, monitor or terminate a therapeutic bath or dry and inspect the foot, so it supports a negative judgment.

roles.title: Occupational Therapists
aliases: Acute Care OT (Acute Care Occupational Therapist)
Home Care Occupational Therapist (Home Care OT)
Pediatrics and Acute Care Occupational Therapist
roles.description: Assess, plan, and organize rehabilitative programs that help build or restore vocational, homemaking, and daily living skills, as well as general independence, to persons with disabilities or developmental delays. Use therapeutic techniques, adapt the individual's environment, teach skills, and modify specific tasks that present barriers to the individual.

tasks.label: Test and evaluate patients' physical and mental abilities and analyze medical data to determine realistic rehabilitation goals for patients.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Acute-care hospital initial OT evaluation at the bedside: therapist reviews the chart (imaging, labs, weight-bearing/cardiac precautions, lines and drains), interviews patient/family about prior level of function, screens orientation and cognition, performs hands-on manual muscle testing, range-of-motion, tone, sensation and coordination testing, guards the patient through bed mobility, sit-to-stand and a grooming/dressing trial, then synthesizes findings into discharge-oriented rehabilitation goals documented in the EHR.

Inpatient rehab facility or skilled nursing comprehensive OT evaluation: standardized functional scoring (Section GG/FIM-style ADL performance), balance and transfer testing, upper-extremity impairment measures, perceptual/cognitive testing, ADL simulation in a training kitchen/bathroom, integration with team medical data (stroke/TBI/ortho history) to set measurable short- and long-term rehab goals for the stay.

Outpatient orthopedic or hand-therapy clinic evaluation: review of operative report and physician protocol, goniometric joint measurement, grip and pinch dynamometry, monofilament/sensory testing, edema and volumetric measures, provocative special tests, pain and self-report outcome measures, then setting realistic functional/return-to-work goals.

Pediatric school-based or early-intervention evaluation: administering norm-referenced standardized tests (fine-motor, visual-motor, sensory processing), observing the child in classroom or play context, handling test manipulatives and handwriting samples, reviewing medical/developmental records, and writing measurable IEP/IFSP goals.

Home health OT evaluation in the patient's own residence: assessing ADL/IADL performance in the client's actual bathroom, kitchen and stairs, hands-on strength/ROM/balance testing amid clutter, pets and variable lighting, reviewing hospital discharge paperwork and medication lists, and setting home-safety and independence goals.

sources.system: Kinarm (Kinarm Standard Tests, exoskeleton and end-point robots)
sources.date: 2020 (paper); product in continuous clinical-research use through 2026
sources.title: Statistical measures of motor, sensory and cognitive performance across repeated robot-based testing (J NeuroEngineering Rehabil)
sources.claim: The Kinarm robotic exoskeleton/end-point system autonomously administers a validated battery of reaching, position-sense and cognitive-motor tasks and outputs normative-referenced impairment scores, but it covers only isolated arm sensorimotor parameters, requires a clinician/technician to seat and strap the subject in, and does not perform strength/ADL testing, chart interpretation, or rehabilitation goal setting.
sources.transferJustification: Related task = instrumented robotic measurement of upper-limb sensorimotor and neurocognitive function, one component of an OT physical/mental evaluation. It does not transfer to the whole task: no manual muscle testing, sensation, ADL observation, medical-record synthesis, or goal formulation.

sources.title: Evaluation of finger strength and spasticity in hemiplegic patients using hand-finger robotic device: A validity and reliability study
sources.claim: The Amadeo hand-finger robotic system produces valid and reliable measurements of finger strength and spasticity in hemiplegic patients, showing robots can quantify selected impairment variables when the hand is fixtured into the device by a clinician.
sources.transferJustification: Related task = robotic quantification of hand strength/tone, a sub-measure within an OT hand evaluation. Transfer is partial only: the device measures one fixtured body segment and cannot conduct the remainder of an evaluation or set rehabilitation goals.

sources.developer: SoftBank Robotics platform, used by university/clinical research group (Frontiers in Psychology study)
sources.title: Humanoid robots for psychological assessment in mild cognitive impairment: from evaluation to the future of AI-driven data prediction systems
sources.claim: A humanoid robot (Pepper) has been used to administer standardized cognitive screening (MMSE) to patients with mild cognitive impairment in a clinical study, showing robot-delivered verbal test administration is feasible; the interaction is screen/voice based and involves no physical testing of the patient.
sources.transferJustification: Related task = administering a standardized mental-status screen, part of the 'mental abilities' half of this task. It does not transfer to the physical half (hands-on strength, ROM, sensation, transfers, ADL performance) nor to rehabilitation goal determination.

tasks.label: Plan, organize, and conduct occupational therapy programs in hospital, institutional, or community settings to help rehabilitate persons with disabilities because of illness, injury or psychological or developmental problems.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Acute care / inpatient rehab hospital: OT plans and runs individualized daily sessions for stroke, TBI, or post-surgical patients at bedside or in an ADL suite - bed mobility and transfers with guarding, self-care retraining (dressing, grooming, toileting), graded upper-extremity and functional activity, line/precaution management, patient and family education, and continuous progression of the plan of care.

Skilled nursing / long-term care facility: OT organizes and conducts individual and small-group programs for frail elderly residents - functional mobility and transfer training, dressing and feeding retraining, adaptive equipment and wheelchair positioning, contracture and skin management, restorative and falls-prevention groups, with residents who have dementia and fluctuating cooperation.

Outpatient clinic including hand therapy: OT conducts a course of treatment for tendon repairs, fractures, arthritis, or neuro clients - graded therapeutic activity and exercise, manual techniques, custom orthosis fabrication and fitting, work-simulation tasks, and instruction in a home program, adjusting the plan visit to visit.

School-based pediatric OT: therapist plans and delivers programs in classrooms, therapy rooms, cafeterias and playgrounds - fine-motor/handwriting work, sensory-regulation activities, self-care and feeding, adapting classroom tasks and seating, and coaching teachers and aides, with children who may be dysregulated or resistant.

Home health / community visits: OT travels to a client's private home to plan and conduct the program in situ - ADL/IADL retraining in the client's own bathroom and kitchen, safe transfers and equipment set-up, home-hazard modification, and caregiver training, amid pets, clutter and variable layouts.

Behavioral / mental health setting: OT plans and runs life-skills and coping programs on a psychiatric unit or in a day program or clubhouse - cooking, money management, medication routines, vocational and community-reintegration groups - managing group dynamics and behavioral risk.

sources.title: Clinical Integration of the ArmeoPower: Sheltering Arms Rehabilitation Hospital - Hocoma Knowledge Platform
sources.claim: ArmeoPower, a commercial robotic arm-therapy device, is integrated into inpatient rehabilitation sessions at a US rehab hospital, but is used as a tool inside a therapist-run session, with the therapist positioning the patient and delivering the remaining functional/carryover portion.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robot-delivered upper-limb motor training inside an OT session. It covers only the repetitive-movement sub-step of conducting an OT program; setup, planning, ADL/carryover training and safety supervision remain with the therapist.

sources.title: Benefits of Robot-Assisted Upper-Limb Rehabilitation from the Subacute Stage after a Stroke of Varying Severity: A Multicenter Randomized Controlled Trial
sources.claim: Multicenter RCT found robot-assisted upper-limb therapy delivered on rehabilitation robots produced ADL and motor gains comparable to conventional occupational therapy, but the robots delivered a defined exercise protocol under clinician management, not a whole OT program.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robot-mediated motor rehabilitation in clinics. Shows equivalence only for a limb-training modality with the patient strapped into a device; it does not establish planning, organizing, or conducting a full OT program.

sources.title: Rehabilitation robotics and allied digital technologies: opportunities, barriers and solutions for improving their clinical implementation. A position paper from the Fit for Medical Robotics Initiative
sources.claim: A 2025 position paper on clinical implementation of rehabilitation robotics describes robotic gyms in which one therapist supervises several patients simultaneously - deployed rehab robots reduce therapist time per patient but still require on-site therapist supervision and workflow management.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: organizing robot-assisted therapy delivery in a clinic. It documents that the state of practice keeps a human therapist planning and supervising, so it cannot substantiate unsupervised completion of the task.

sources.title: THERAPIST: Towards an Autonomous Socially Interactive Robot for Motor and Neurorehabilitation Therapies for Children
sources.claim: THERAPIST is a research socially assistive robot that autonomously plans and adapts motor/neurorehabilitation game sessions for children, demonstrated in a controlled clinical/lab room rather than deployed as a service.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous coaching of a pediatric rehabilitation exercise game. It engages and motivates but performs no hands-on facilitation, ADL retraining, orthotics, or safety handling, so it cannot carry a full OT program.

sources.title: Texas School Adopts Milo and robots4autism Curriculum for Students with Autism
sources.claim: Milo, a commercial social robot deployed in US schools, delivers a scripted social-skills curriculum to students with autism with a human facilitator present; it does not deliver fine-motor, sensory or self-care occupational therapy programming.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robot-delivered therapeutic curriculum in schools. Content is social-communication instruction delivered alongside an adult facilitator, not the hands-on motor/self-care programming school OTs plan and conduct.

sources.title: A Randomized Trial Using PARO with Minimal Caregiver Involvement on Older Adults with Dementia in Group Homes
sources.claim: PARO, an FDA-recognized Class II therapeutic robot, is used in nursing homes and group homes as an autonomous companion device within psychosocial care programs; it provides comfort and engagement, not skills training or program planning.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robot-mediated therapeutic activity in long-term care. It substantiates only an adjunct engagement device; no ADL retraining, positioning, adaptive-equipment work or program organization is performed.

sources.system: Home robotic rehabilitation device (Don Gnocchi home pilot)
sources.developer: IRCCS Fondazione Don Carlo Gnocchi / Campus Bio-Medico
sources.title: A robotic rehabilitation intervention in a home setting during the Covid-19 outbreak: a feasibility pilot study in patients with stroke
sources.claim: Home-based robotic rehabilitation for stroke remains at feasibility-pilot scale, with devices delivering exercise sessions to a small cohort in their homes under study conditions.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: delivering rehabilitation exercise in a client's home. It is a supervised feasibility pilot of a single exercise modality, not autonomous conduct of a home OT program including ADL retraining and home modification.
