roles.description: Assess, plan, organize, and participate in rehabilitative programs that improve mobility, relieve pain, increase strength, and improve or correct disabling conditions resulting from disease or injury.

tasks.label: Plan, prepare, or carry out individually designed programs of physical treatment to maintain, improve, or restore physical functioning, alleviate pain, or prevent physical dysfunction in patients.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Outpatient orthopedic/MSK clinic: 30-60 min individually designed treatment session for a post-op or musculoskeletal patient (knee/shoulder/spine) — hands-on joint and soft-tissue mobilization, guided therapeutic exercise with manual resistance, tactile cueing and form correction, movement retraining, modalities, and in-session progression/regression of the plan of care based on pain and response.

Acute care hospital inpatient: bedside session with a medically complex patient (lines, drains, weight-bearing and sternal precautions, orthostatic and fall risk) — bed mobility, edge-of-bed sitting, sit-to-stand and transfers with physical assistance, short ambulation with a walker, continuous monitoring of vitals, pain and tolerance, terminating or advancing on clinical judgment.

Post-op orthopedic inpatient / short-stay rehab: protocol-driven progressive ambulation training in a ward corridor after hip or knee surgery — repeated supervised walks on forearm crutches or a walker, progressing distance, correcting gait pattern and weight-bearing, monitoring tolerance and documenting progress; the patient has already been instructed in use of the device.

Inpatient rehab unit or SNF, neurologic/geriatric patient (stroke, TBI, SCI, deconditioning): session of transfers, sit-to-stand practice, hands-on facilitation and manual guarding, balance and functional gait training over varied surfaces and stairs, with real-time adaptation to tone, neglect, fatigue and cognition.

Clinic or rehab-gym session in which the prescribed program is delivered as a high-repetition device/robot-assisted training block: the patient is set up on an upper-limb rehabilitation robot or a body-weight-supported/robotic gait trainer at a prescribed assistance level and performs hundreds of repetitions with feedback, per the therapist's plan.

Home health visit or community/pediatric setting: PT treats in the patient's own home (or a school/early-intervention room), improvising with available furniture, thresholds, stairs and clutter — transfers, gait on carpet and uneven surfaces, strengthening, handling and play-based facilitation for a child, plus caregiver training.

sources.title: Rehabilitation: THERY robot accompanies gait training on forearm supports (MEDICA interview with Dr. Christian Sternitzke)
sources.claim: THERY, a mobile autonomous robot from TEDIRO, leads hospital and rehab-clinic patients through gait training on forearm crutches without a therapist present, using camera-based motion capture to monitor the exercise and give real-time feedback.

sources.developer: TEDIRO Healthcare Robotics GmbH / QuickBird Medical
sources.title: Rehabilitation: THERY robot accompanies gait training on forearm supports (MEDICA interview)
sources.claim: With THERY the therapist designs and individualizes the training plan in a cloud therapy-management system; the patient logs in at the robot with a chip and the robot then runs, records and evaluates that individualized program.

sources.title: Gang-Roboter THERY als Medizinprodukt zugelassen – QuickBird Medical liefert Softwarebasis
sources.claim: THERY received CE marking as a medical device in January 2025, described as one of the first approved autonomous mobile robots in healthcare, intended to help patients relearn walking after lower-limb surgery.

sources.developer: TEDIRO Healthcare Robotics GmbH with BG Klinikum Bergmannstrost Halle
sources.title: Roboter THERY im BG Klinikum Bergmannstrost in Halle
sources.claim: THERY entered clinical use at BG Klinikum Bergmannstrost Halle on 29 April 2025 with its first approved application: robot-accompanied self-training on forearm crutches; therapists were present for the first three months to learn which patients suit the robot.

sources.title: Robot-Assisted Training as Self-Training for Upper-Limb Hemiplegia in Chronic Stroke: A Randomized Controlled Trial (Stroke)
sources.claim: In a multicenter RCT at Japanese rehabilitation centers, chronic stroke patients performed 40-minute blocks of robot-assisted self-training on the ReoGo-J upper-limb device, the robot supplying passive and active-assist control matched to each patient's level.

sources.title: Unsupervised Robot-Assisted Therapy at Home After Stroke: a Pilot Feasibility Study
sources.claim: Stroke inpatients of a rehabilitation ... were trained to use the ReHandyBot hand-rehabilitation robot with progressively decreasing supervision and then continued unsupervised therapy, showing device-delivered repetitive training can run without a therapist present.

sources.title: Lokomat Robotic Gait Training – Physiopedia
sources.claim: The Lokomat is a driven gait orthosis with body-weight support used in rehabilitation hospitals that moves the patient's legs on a treadmill and automatically reduces assistance as walking ability recovers; the patient must first be harnessed and strapped into the exoskeleton by staff.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robot-delivered locomotor training. It transfers to the device-based training block instance because the same patient population, movement amplitudes and safety requirements are involved once the patient is fixtured in the orthosis.

sources.title: Aescape raises $83M to bring robotic massager to more locations – The Robot Report
sources.claim: Aescape's massage table uses AI-driven robotic arms with heated end effectors to deliver an automated bodywork session; the system is installed commercially in Equinox gym locations.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous soft-tissue massage of a prone client on a fixed table. It bears on the manual-therapy component of an outpatient PT session, but covers only relaxation-grade posterior soft tissue work — no joint mobilization, no exercise instruction, no in-session clinical reassessment.

tasks.label: Perform and document an initial exam, evaluating data to identify problems and determine a diagnosis prior to intervention.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Outpatient orthopedic/sports clinic: new patient with knee, shoulder, or low-back complaint. PT takes subjective history, observes posture and gait, measures ROM with goniometer/inclinometer, performs manual muscle testing, palpates for tenderness and tissue quality, applies special orthopedic tests (e.g., Lachman, impingement, SLR) and joint-mobility assessment, administers outcome measures, then synthesizes findings into a PT diagnosis, prognosis, and plan of care documented in the EMR.

Acute-care hospital bedside evaluation of a post-op or medically complex inpatient with lines, drains, and precautions: chart review, vitals/cognition screen, strength and sensation screen, bed mobility, sit-to-stand and transfer testing with hands-on guarding, short gait trial with assistive device, then diagnosis of mobility impairment, discharge-disposition recommendation, and documentation.

Skilled nursing facility or inpatient rehab evaluation of an older adult after fall or functional decline: transfer and balance testing (e.g., Berg, TUG), lower-extremity strength and ROM, skin/edema inspection, cognition and safety judgment, assistive-device fitting decisions, with hands-on guarding of an unsteady patient, followed by diagnosis, goal setting, and documentation.

Home health initial evaluation in the patient's own residence: exam performed on the patient's furniture, in cluttered rooms and on the home's stairs, including home-safety/environmental assessment, mobility and transfer testing with physical assistance, medication/vitals screen, plus diagnosis, plan of care, and regulatory documentation.

Pediatric/school-based or neurologic specialty evaluation: developmental or neuromotor exam (tone and reflex testing, motor milestone or gait/balance assessment, standardized batteries) requiring hands-on handling of a child or a neurologically impaired adult, with interpretation into a diagnosis and plan documented for the school or clinic record.

sources.system: Kinarm Exoskeleton Lab / Kinarm Standard Tests
sources.title: Kinarm Standard Tests - Kinarm | Interactive Robotics Brain Injury Research
sources.claim: Kinarm is a commercial robotic exoskeleton lab that runs standardized protocols to quantify sensorimotor, proprioceptive and cognitive function; it covers only a narrow quantitative sub-step of an exam, requires a clinician to seat, strap and set up the participant, and yields research/impairment metrics rather than a physical therapy diagnosis and plan.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic quantitative assessment of arm sensorimotor function. It does not transfer to the full initial exam: no history taking, palpation, special orthopedic tests, functional mobility or transfer testing, no hands-on guarding, and no PT diagnosis/plan-of-care documentation; the patient must be positioned in the device by a human.

sources.system: Social robot-led physiotherapy (Pepper-class social robot with RL policy)
sources.developer: Heriot-Watt University / University of Edinburgh researchers
sources.title: Policy Learning for Social Robot-Led Physiotherapy (arXiv 2509.11297)
sources.claim: State-of-the-art social robots in physiotherapy are aimed at autonomously guiding patients through prescribed exercise sessions, with policies trained in simulation using healthcare practitioners as patient proxies; no examination, hands-on testing, or diagnosis is performed.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robot-led exercise coaching in rehabilitation. It does not transfer to the initial exam: the robot never contacts the patient, performs no ROM/strength/palpation measurement, and produces no evaluation or diagnosis; validation was in simulation with practitioner proxies.

sources.system: Ergodic-exploration autonomous robotic palpation framework (robotic manipulator with force/torque sensor)
sources.title: Autonomous Robotic Tissue Palpation and Abnormalities Characterisation via Ergodic Exploration
sources.claim: Autonomous robotic palpation, the closest robotic analogue to a therapist's hands-on tissue assessment, is validated only on silicone phantoms with embedded inclusions in a lab, not on patients in clinical settings.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic palpation for stiffness/abnormality mapping. Transfer fails: work is on inert silicone phantoms in a lab bench setup, not living patients, and it addresses only one exam sub-step, with no ROM, strength, functional mobility, or diagnostic synthesis.

sources.title: Validated Evaluations Modules - Exer AI
sources.claim: Automated range-of-motion and strength assessment in physical therapy is currently delivered by camera-based software on phones/tablets (e.g., Exer AI), which is not an embodied robotic system and still requires a human to position the patient, perform hands-on tests, and author the evaluation.
sources.transferJustification: Cited only to show the automated portion of PT examination is software-only computer vision; it is not a physically embodied machine acting on the world, so it cannot substantiate completion at any environment tier.

tasks.label: Record prognosis, treatment, response, and progress in patient's chart or enter information into computer.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

tasks.label: Instruct patient and family in treatment procedures to be continued at home.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Outpatient orthopedic clinic: after a knee or shoulder rehab session, the PT explains and demonstrates the home exercise program (sets, reps, frequency, precautions), watches the patient perform each exercise, corrects form verbally, and hands over a printed or app-delivered exercise sheet plus follow-up instructions.

Acute care or inpatient rehab discharge teaching: the PT instructs the patient and a family caregiver on safe bed/chair transfers, use of a walker or cane on stairs, precautions (e.g., hip precautions, weight-bearing status), and a home mobility program, checking teach-back before discharge.

Home health visit: in the patient's residence, the PT teaches a spouse or adult child how to carry out passive range-of-motion, positioning, transfer assistance, and a progressive exercise program between visits, adapting instructions to the home's furniture, stairs, and equipment.

Pediatric or neurologic caseload: the PT instructs parents/caregivers in handling, stretching, splint or orthosis wear schedules, and play-based exercises for a child with cerebral palsy or a patient post-stroke, including written schedules and coaching on how to recognize problems.

Telehealth/video visit or phone follow-up: the PT reviews and updates the home program with the patient and a family member on camera, observes exercise performance remotely, answers questions, and sends revised written or video instructions.

tasks.label: Evaluate effects of treatment at various stages and adjust treatments to achieve maximum benefit.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Outpatient orthopedic/sports clinic: mid-episode re-assessment of a musculoskeletal patient (e.g., 6 weeks post-ACL reconstruction, rotator cuff repair, low back pain). PT re-measures knee/shoulder ROM with goniometer, performs manual muscle testing and joint-mobility/special tests by hand, palpates for effusion and tissue response, watches gait/squat mechanics, questions the patient about pain and function, compares to baseline and goals, then progresses or regresses exercises, changes manual technique or modality, updates the home program, and documents the re-evaluation.

Acute care hospital: at the start of and during each bedside session the PT re-evaluates response to prior mobility treatment - checks vitals and lines/drains, tests bed mobility, sit-to-stand and gait with hands-on guarding, grades assistance level and distance, judges fatigue/orthostatic response, then adjusts the session (device selection, distance, assist level), the frequency, and discharge recommendation, and documents it.

Skilled nursing facility or inpatient rehab: weekly/biweekly progress reassessment of an older adult with multiple comorbidities - functional outcome measures (TUG, gait speed, Berg balance, FIM/section GG levels), strength and transfer testing with hands-on guarding, review of tolerance and pain, then revision of the plan of care (goals, frequency, equipment) and team communication.

Home health: PT re-evaluates the homebound patient in the patient's own house - reassesses gait/stairs/transfers in cluttered, variable rooms, checks vitals, wound/edema, and adherence to the home exercise program, then adjusts exercises, assistive device, and environment recommendations and updates the plan of care.

Neurologic rehab gym (stroke, SCI, MS, pediatric CP) using technology-assisted therapy such as body-weight-supported treadmill, robotic gait trainer or upper-limb robot: PT evaluates the patient's response to the training block - tone/spasticity, skin and strap tolerance, active contribution, carryover to overground/functional tasks - and adjusts device parameters (guidance force, body-weight support, speed, difficulty) and the wider program.

sources.system: Lokomat (Hocoma) with L-FORCE / L-ROM / L-STIFF assessment tools
sources.title: Assessing Stiffness, Joint Torque and ROM for Paretic and Non-Paretic Lower Limbs during the Subacute Phase of Stroke Using Lokomat Tools
sources.claim: The commercial Lokomat gait exoskeleton includes in-device measurement tools (L-FORCE, L-ROM, L-STIFF) that quantify joint torque, range of motion and stiffness at baseline and follow-up in stroke patients; the patient must be set up in the exoskeleton by clinicians and clinicians interpret the results and change the therapy.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: instrumented re-measurement of ROM/strength inside a rehab robot is the measurement sub-step of PT re-assessment. It does not transfer to the whole task because it captures only in-device sagittal-plane parameters and the clinician still interprets them, examines pain/palpation/function, and revises the plan.

sources.title: Assessment-driven selection and adaptation of exercise difficulty in robot-assisted therapy: a pilot study with a hand rehabilitation robot
sources.claim: A hand rehabilitation robot (ReHapticKnob, ETH Zurich) used robotic assessments to customize exercises and an automated routine adapted exercise difficulty from session to session across a four-week therapy course in six subacute stroke patients - the closest demonstrated automated 'evaluate effect then adjust treatment' loop, but limited to one device's exercise parameters in a research pilot.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated progression of exercise difficulty is a narrow analogue of 'adjust treatments'. Transfer is incomplete - the routine adjusts only in-device difficulty for six pilot patients, and does not perform the clinical re-examination (pain, palpation, functional tests, safety) or revise the plan of care.

sources.system: Real-time adaptive assist-as-needed controller for upper-extremity rehabilitation robot
sources.developer: Academic research group (published in PLOS ONE)
sources.title: Evaluation of a novel real-time adaptive assist-as-needed controller for robot-assisted upper extremity rehabilitation following stroke
sources.claim: A pilot clinical study with five chronic stroke patients showed an EMG-based adaptive assist-as-needed controller that automatically modulates robot assistance in real time during upper-extremity robot therapy; adaptation is confined to assistance level within the device.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: within-session automatic tuning of robot assistance resembles 'adjusting treatment', but it is a control-parameter change on a fixtured limb, not a staged clinical re-evaluation and revision of the therapy program.

sources.system: ROBERT (Life Science Robotics, KUKA LBR Med based)
sources.title: 5 things you need to know about the ROBERT by Life Science Robotics
sources.claim: ROBERT, a commercially deployed hospital rehabilitation robot for early mobilization, is programmed by the therapist, who performs the initial movement and sets the therapeutic parameters; the robot then repeats the motion. Assessment of the patient's response and any change of treatment remain with the therapist.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robot-delivered limb mobilization in hospitals. It shows the state of deployed clinical rehab robotics - the human clinician still evaluates the effect of treatment and re-programs the device - so it does not substantiate autonomous completion of this task.

sources.title: Equinox Locations Add Aescape, a Fully Automated Massage Bed
sources.claim: Aescape is a fully automated robotic massage table deployed commercially in Equinox fitness clubs; it scans the user's body ... delivers targeted hands-on bodywork with adaptive pressure, but it does not perform clinical re-assessment of treatment effects or revise a therapy plan.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous hands-on soft-tissue treatment of a human body in a structured facility. Transfer fails for this task because Aescape only tailors pressure to user-selected preferences on a prone, fixtured client; it performs no goniometry, strength or functional testing, and makes no plan-of-care decisions.

tasks.label: Confer with the patient, medical practitioners, or appropriate others to plan, implement, or assess the intervention program.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

tasks.label: Administer manual exercises, massage, or traction to help relieve pain, increase patient strength, or decrease or prevent deformity or crippling.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Outpatient orthopedic clinic: hands-on manual therapy for a patient with neck, back, shoulder or knee pain — graded accessory joint mobilization/manipulation, region-specific soft-tissue and scar mobilization, muscle-energy and manual-resistance techniques, continuously modulated by palpatory feedback and the patient's verbal response within a 10-20 minute segment of the visit.

Outpatient clinic: general therapeutic massage/soft-tissue work for pain and muscle tightness — patient lies prone/supine on a standard treatment plinth while the therapist works the back, shoulders, glutes and legs at a chosen pressure for 10-20 minutes, before or after exercise.

Acute hospital ward or skilled nursing facility, bedside: passive range-of-motion and prolonged manual stretching of a dependent or minimally cooperative patient (post-op, ICU, stroke, advanced dementia) in bed or a recliner, to maintain joint range and prevent contracture/deformity.

Home health visit: manual stretching, passive/active-assisted limb exercise and light massage for a homebound patient in a bedroom or living room of varying layout, with the patient in a bed, recliner or chair and household clutter and pets present.

Inpatient/outpatient neuro-rehab gym: high-repetition assisted limb or gait exercise for a stroke or spinal-cord-injury patient — therapist manually guides the arm through reaching reps or facilitates stepping — to build strength and motor control over a 30-45 minute session.

Outpatient clinic: cervical or lumbar traction — therapist positions and harnesses the patient on a traction table, sets force, hold/rest times and duration, and monitors the pull for symptom response over 10-15 minutes.

sources.title: Aescape raises $83M to bring robotic massager to more locations - The Robot Report
sources.claim: Aescape's AI massage table performs fully autonomous massage on paying customers and was rolled out commercially from a New York pilot to 60 Equinox club locations.
sources.transferJustification: Related task = commercial table massage. Transfers to a PT-administered massage segment: same object (a human body prone/supine on a treatment table), same modality (graded pressure soft-tissue work over back, glutes and legs), same kind of institution-controlled treatment room.

sources.title: Massage Envy Introduces Aescape Robotic Massage at Select Franchised Locations
sources.claim: The same autonomous massage robot is being installed in Massage Envy franchise clinics, delivering 30- or 60-minute targeted or full-body sessions in which the machine adapts to the body's contours and chosen pressure.
sources.transferJustification: Related task = clinic-based massage service. A massage franchise clinic is a structured human treatment facility comparable to an outpatient PT clinic; the physical act (pressure applied to back/legs of a person on a table) is the same as the PT massage segment.

sources.title: Singapore's first robot masseuse 'EMMA' starts work | EurekAlert!
sources.claim: The Emma massage robot entered regular clinical service at a Singapore clinic, autonomously delivering back and knee therapeutic massage using force sensing and AI-computed pressure, alongside human clinicians.
sources.transferJustification: Related task = tuina/therapeutic massage of the back and knee in a clinic. Same body regions and pressure ranges a PT uses for pain-relief soft-tissue work, delivered in a licensed clinic treatment room.

sources.title: [MEDICA] The Top Five Orthopedic Robots for Rehabilitation - MedicalExpo e-Magazine
sources.claim: Capsix's iYU is an autonomous robotic massage device (KUKA LBR Med arm with 3D body scanning) sold to and used by physiotherapists and health ... to complement their therapeutic treatments.

sources.title: Neuro-Rehabilitation Robotics & Technology — Barrow Neurological Institute
sources.claim: At Barrow Neurological Institute, therapists load the patient's arm and hand into the InMotion robot, which then delivers highly repetitive guided, assisted or resisted movement therapy that adapts to the patient's ability.

sources.developer: Harmonic Bionics (assets acquired by Bioness Medical, 2025)
sources.title: Harmonic Bionics Installs First of Two Harmony SHR Robotic Rehabilitation Systems Purchased by Top Neurological Hospital in Phoenix
sources.claim: A bilateral upper-extremity rehabilitation exoskeleton that moves the patient's arm and shoulder through therapy motions has been purchased and installed for routine inpatient and outpatient clinical use at a US neurological hospital following FDA registration.

sources.title: Clinical Application of a Robotic Ankle Training Program for Cerebral Palsy Compared to the Research Laboratory Application: Does It Translate to Practice?
sources.claim: The IntelliStretch robotic device delivered passive stretching plus active movement training to patients with cerebral palsy in a routine outpatient clinic, producing improvements across ICF domains — i.e., robot-delivered stretching of a strapped-in limb translated from lab to clinical practice.
sources.transferJustification: Related task = robot-delivered passive stretching of a contracture-prone joint. This is the same physical act as a PT's manual passive stretching to prevent deformity, on the same joints and at therapeutic torque levels; the limb is strapped into the device rather than held by hands.

sources.system: Continuous passive motion (CPM) machines (e.g., Kinetec Performa, Chattanooga OptiFlex)
sources.title: Clinical evaluation of usefulness and effectiveness of sitting type continuous passive motion machines in patients with total knee arthroplasty (BMC Musculoskeletal Disorders)
sources.claim: Continuous passive motion machines are standard post-operative equipment that move a patient's limb through a pre-defined arc to deliver passive range-of-motion exercise, used in hospitals, clinics and rented for home use.
sources.transferJustification: Related task = machine-delivered passive range of motion after surgery. It substitutes for the PT's manual passive ROM/stretching to maintain range and prevent stiffness and soft-tissue contracture, on the same joints, once the limb is placed in the carriage.

sources.system: Triton DTS / Triton MP-1 traction system
sources.title: Spinal Decompression Therapy, Spinal Traction, Lumbar Decompression - Phoenix Physical Therapy
sources.claim: Motorized traction systems in physical therapy clinics apply the prescribed traction force under electronic motor control in intermittent or static mode once the patient is belted onto the table.
sources.transferJustification: Related task = mechanical spinal traction. It is the machine form of the traction named in this task; the device generates and modulates the therapeutic pull that the PT would otherwise apply manually, after a human harnesses the patient.

tasks.label: Obtain patients' informed consent to proposed interventions.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

tasks.label: Test and measure patient's strength, motor development and function, sensory perception, functional capacity, or respiratory or circulatory efficiency and record data.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Outpatient orthopedic/sports clinic evaluation or re-evaluation: hands-on goniometric range-of-motion measurement at several joints, manual muscle testing against therapist resistance, palpation, girth/edema measures, joint-specific special tests (e.g., Lachman, impingement), with findings scored and typed into the EMR.

Instrumented performance-testing session in a clinic or human-performance lab: patient seated/strapped into an isokinetic dynamometer or robotic limb-assessment station for a single limb or joint (e.g., quadriceps/hamstring peak torque for return-to-sport, upper-limb force/ROM after stroke); the device's printed data report is the record.

Acute care hospital bedside assessment: gross strength testing of a patient in bed, bed mobility and transfer capacity, tolerance to activity with heart rate, blood pressure, SpO2 and respiratory rate/exertion measured before, during and after mobilization, with lines and drains present; recorded in the chart.

Inpatient rehab or skilled nursing facility standardized functional capacity measures: Timed Up and Go, 10-meter gait speed, 5x sit-to-stand, Berg Balance, 6-minute walk test in a corridor, with the therapist instructing, guarding the patient against falls, timing, and scoring into the outcome-measure record.

Neurologic rehabilitation evaluation (adult stroke/SCI/MS or pediatric developmental): motor function and developmental milestones, tone (Modified Ashworth), reflexes, coordination, and sensory perception testing including light touch, pinprick, monofilament and limb position sense across dermatomes and limbs, documented.

Home health visit: strength, balance, functional capacity and vital-sign response assessed in the patient's own home using available furniture and hallways, with clutter, pets and family present; data recorded on a laptop or tablet.

sources.system: Kinarm Standard Tests (Kinarm exoskeleton / end-point robot)
sources.title: Kinarm Standard Tests - Kinarm | Interactive Robotics Brain Injury Research
sources.claim: The Kinarm exoskeleton/end-point robot administers a suite of standardized sensory, motor and cognitive tasks (e.g., robot moves one arm while the subject mirror-matches with the other to quantify position sense) and produces quantitative impairment measures in a dedicated Kinarm Lab station.
sources.transferJustification: Directly the task: robotic quantification of sensory perception (limb position sense, kinesthesia), motor function and muscle tone, with automatic data capture. Requires the subject to be seated and strapped into the robot by an operator.

sources.title: Test–retest reliability of KINARM robot sensorimotor and cognitive assessment: in pediatric ice hockey players (J NeuroEng Rehabil)
sources.claim: Subjects strapped into the two-armed KINARM robot perform automated upper-extremity tasks with the robot recording performance; test-retest reliability of the resulting sensorimotor and cognitive metrics has been quantified in pediatric athletes.
sources.transferJustification: Same task class (testing motor function and sensory perception and recording data); establishes that the measurement protocol runs automatically once the patient is positioned in the device.

sources.title: Software - Lokomat - Hocoma
sources.claim: The Lokomat driven gait orthosis includes built-in assessment tools that measure hip and knee range of motion, isometric force of flexion/extension muscle ..., and joint stiffness, with session reports displayed, saved or printed.
sources.transferJustification: Directly the task for lower-limb strength and ROM measurement with automatic recording, but only with the patient harnessed and their legs strapped into the exoskeleton by therapists.

sources.title: Enhanced rehabilitation for unstable pelvic tile C fractures: integrating mechanotherapy and early intervention (J Orthop Surg Res)
sources.claim: In a clinical rehabilitation study of pelvic fracture patients, muscle strength was measured with the Lokomat's integrated force sensors (L-FORCE) rather than by manual muscle testing.
sources.transferJustification: Directly the task: instrumented strength measurement replacing the therapist's manual measurement, in a hospital rehabilitation department, with the patient fixtured in the device.

sources.title: Technical Data Sheet - ArmeoPower - Hocoma
sources.claim: The ArmeoPower motorized arm exoskeleton objectively assesses joint range of motion, isometric torque, movement workspace and ... generates therapy reports for the patient's record.
sources.transferJustification: Directly the task for upper-limb strength/ROM measurement and data recording, but only inside the motorized orthosis into which a therapist straps the patient's arm.

sources.date: 2025-09 (product pages); product line in clinical use for 30+ years
sources.title: System 4 | Robotic dynamometer | Biodex (Atlas Medic) / System 4 Pro | Biodex
sources.claim: The Biodex System 4 motorized (robotic) dynamometer runs automated isometric/isokinetic test protocols on a strapped-in patient and generates objective, reproducible strength reports used for return-to-play and work-capacity decisions in clinics.
sources.transferJustification: Directly the task for quantitative strength (and functional-capacity) testing of one joint with automatic data recording; the patient must be seated, aligned and strapped by a clinician first.

sources.system: 'Dr. Spot' mobile robotic vital-sign platform (Boston Dynamics Spot)
sources.developer: MIT / Boston Dynamics / Brigham and Women's Hospital
sources.title: Dog-like robot measures patients' vital signs remotely – Physics World
sources.claim: A Boston Dynamics Spot quadruped fitted with cameras and sensors was used by MIT, Boston Dynamics and Brigham and Women's Hospital to measure skin temperature, breathing rate, ... two metres, in healthy volunteers, under remote control in a hospital triage tent.
sources.transferJustification: Closest robotic evidence for measuring respiratory/circulatory efficiency; it is teleoperated, tested on healthy volunteers, and does not test strength or functional capacity, so it cannot support a positive judgment.

tasks.label: Administer treatment involving application of physical agents, using equipment, moist packs, ultraviolet or infrared lamps, or ultrasound machines.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Outpatient orthopedic/PT clinic: therapist retrieves a hydrocollator moist heat pack (or cold pack), wraps it in terry covers/towels, positions the patient prone or supine on a plinth, drapes the pack over the low back/neck/shoulder, checks skin and sensation, monitors 15-20 min, removes it and re-inspects the skin.

Outpatient clinic: therapeutic ultrasound to a shoulder, knee or heel - expose the area, apply coupling gel, move the soundhead in continuous overlapping strokes at set frequency/intensity/duty cycle for 5-10 minutes while asking about warmth or discomfort, then wipe the gel and check the skin.

Outpatient clinic: electrical stimulation (TENS, NMES, interferential or high-volt) - clean and prepare the skin, peel and adhere self-adhesive electrodes over the target muscles/motor points, secure leads, ramp intensity to patient tolerance, monitor and adjust during the 15-20 min bout, then remove electrodes and inspect skin.

Clinic application of a non-contact energy agent - infrared/radiant heat lamp, low-level laser/photobiomodulation, UV lamp or diathermy - positioning the emitter at the prescribed distance over the exposed treatment area, setting dose/time, and supervising the timed exposure of a patient lying on a table.

Inpatient hospital ward or skilled nursing facility: modality (moist heat, cold pack or e-stim) applied at the bedside to a patient in a hospital bed with lines, drains, bed rails and variable positioning; therapist rolls in portable equipment, positions and drapes the patient, applies and removes the agent.

Home health visit: therapist brings portable equipment into the patient's home, applies a heat/cold pack or a portable TENS/e-stim unit on a couch or bed in a cluttered room, instructs the caregiver, monitors the session and removes the agent.

sources.system: Intelligent moxibustion rehabilitation robot (Shanghai Junkong Robotics / SUES, Prof. Xiong Genliang)
sources.developer: Shanghai University of Engineering Science / Shanghai Junkong Robotics Co., Ltd.
sources.title: Intelligent Robot for Moxibustion Has Come-Reducing Burn Risks & Easing Doctors' Workload, With Sales Over 100 Million yuan
sources.claim: Intelligent moxibustion robot deployed in hospital treatment rooms applies a burning moxa stick (radiant heat) over acupoints on a patient's back for ~30 min; therapist selects points on an iPad and one therapist can direct eight robots; robot does 3D acupoint localization, infrared temperature control, adaptive distance ... retracts on patient motion.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: applying a radiant-heat physical agent (moxa/infrared heat) to a defined body region of a prone patient for a timed session with skin-temperature monitoring, in a rehabilitation hospital treatment room - the same objects (heat emitter over exposed skin), the same cm-level targeting and the same setting as PT infrared-lamp/superficial-heat administration.

sources.title: Aescape raises $83M to bring robotic massager to more locations - The Robot Report
sources.claim: Aescape's Aertable, a fully autonomous two-arm robotic massage table with heated end effectors, scans the client's body and delivers a complete session to a client lying on the table; commercially deployed at Equinox spas and expanding to hotels and sports facilities.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous, force-controlled contact of a heated tool with a client's back and limbs while they lie on a treatment table - comparable body mapping, contact-force precision and human-contact safety to placing and holding a thermal agent or applicator on a patient during a PT modality session.

sources.developer: Lin et al., Frontiers in Robotics and AI
sources.title: Autonomous robotic ultrasound scanning system: a key to enhancing image analysis reproducibility and observer consistency in ultrasound imaging
sources.claim: auto-RUSS performs fully autonomous ultrasound probe scanning on human subjects using force-feedback control (target ~2 N contact force) and image visual servoing, with contact force benchmarked against eight ultrasound physicians scanning a volunteer's thyroid.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: sweeping a gel-coupled ultrasound transducer over a human body region at controlled contact force and speed - the same handpiece, skin coupling and cm-level coverage needed to administer therapeutic ultrasound, which additionally requires no diagnostic image interpretation.

sources.title: RABBIT: A Robot-Assisted Bed Bathing System with Multimodal Perception and Integrated Compliance
sources.claim: RABBIT autonomously executes washing, rinsing and drying of a person's forearm in bed, pressing a moist cloth-covered compliant end effector against the skin using multimodal perception; demonstrated with a user with severe mobility ....
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomously bringing a warm, moist implement into sustained compliant contact with a patient's exposed skin and then removing it - comparable object (wet cloth/pack), comparable coarse body-segment targeting and comparable human-contact safety to applying and removing a moist hot pack or cold pack.

sources.title: Robotic TMS | Neurolite Advanced Medical Solutions
sources.claim: Axilum Robotics' TMS robots automatically position a stimulation coil against the patient's head and compensate in real time for patient movement during a stimulation session; CE-marked and FDA 510(k)-cleared for clinical TMS therapy.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotically positioning and holding a therapy applicator against a patient in a clinic treatment room for the duration of an energy-delivery session while tracking patient motion - the same applicator-to-body-site targeting and session monitoring as administering a physical-agent modality with equipment.

sources.title: M6 MLS Therapy Laser - Cutting Edge Lasers
sources.claim: The ASA M6 MLS therapy laser is a robotized ... whose motorized column, arm and 5-axis laser head automatically scan a programmed treatment area on the patient, delivering laser therapy in physical therapy and pain-management clinics.
sources.transferJustification: Same task family: automatic delivery of a non-contact physical agent (laser/light energy) over a defined body region of a patient lying in a clinic treatment room, with the clinician setting parameters and the machine executing the timed application.

tasks.label: Construct, maintain, or repair medical supportive devices.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Inpatient room or outpatient gym: PT fits and adjusts an ambulatory assistive device to an individual patient - sets telescoping walker/crutch/cane height to the wrist crease, swaps or repositions handgrips and axillary pads, replaces worn tips, tightens wing nuts and push-pin legs, then has the patient stand and ambulate to verify fit and stability, re-adjusting as needed.

Clinic/therapy department: routine maintenance and minor repair of varied patient devices and clinic supportive equipment - tighten or replace wheelchair bolts, footplates, armrests and anti-tippers, inflate or swap casters, replace frayed brace straps, buckles and Velcro, re-pad a splint liner, spot-heat a plastic AFO with a heat gun to relieve a pressure point, replace crutch tips and walker glides. Device make/model and wear state vary; the PT diagnoses what is wrong before fixing it.

Outpatient/hand or neuro clinic: construct a custom immobilization or support orthosis directly on the patient - heat low-temperature thermoplastic, drape and mold it to the wrist/hand/ankle in the corrected position, trim and flare edges, attach straps and padding, check skin and pressure points, then remold as needed. Includes serial casting for contracture.

Clinic or in-house orthotics bench: fabricate or modify a custom foot orthosis / shoe insert - capture the foot shape (foam impression or scan), produce the shell (heat-press, mill or print), grind and bevel edges, add rearfoot/forefoot posts, heel lifts and metatarsal pads, bond a top cover, and check the fit inside the patient's shoe.

Home health or community visit: adjust or repair the patient's own walker, wheelchair, brace, or bath/transfer equipment in the patient's home - cluttered and variable layout, no shop or bench, unknown device models, improvising fixes and supports from available materials (tape, foam, tennis balls, hardware on hand).

sources.system: PioCreat IPX2 3D printer + FS A002 plantar scanner
sources.title: Clinics can now produce 3D printed insoles in 35 minutes with PioCreat's system - 3D Printing Industry
sources.claim: PioCreat sells a clinic-deployable custom insole system pairing an automated plantar scanner with an enclosed FDM printer that produces a pair of adult custom insoles in about 35 minutes, covering foot data capture through final production in one digital workflow.
sources.transferJustification: Directly the fabrication half of the task: constructing a custom foot orthosis. The machine performs the shell construction; the enclosed printer is a purpose-built machine environment.

sources.title: 3D Printed Casts Can Now Be Made In-Clinic, Thanks to This Turnkey Solution | Additive Manufacturing
sources.claim: ActivArmor's turnkey scan-design-print package for custom rigid casts and splints is in production use in many US clinics, including military and VA facilities, producing the device at point of care rather than at a central lab.
sources.transferJustification: Same task: constructing a custom rigid supportive/immobilization device shaped to a patient's limb, substituting for hand-molded thermoplastic splinting.

sources.title: Atlanta VAHCS Pioneers 3D-Printed Medical Devices for Veteran Care
sources.claim: Atlanta VA Health Care System deployed the ActivArmor system to produce customized 3D-printed casts and splints, with the devices used by services including Physical Therapy, Orthopedics and Podiatry.
sources.transferJustification: Confirms the machine-fabricated device is accepted in place of a therapist-fabricated one in a US rehabilitation setting, including physical therapy.

sources.system: In-hospital 3D scanning + high-speed 3D printed cast workflow
sources.title: In-hospital production of 3D-printed casts for non-displaced wrist and hand fractures
sources.claim: Peer-reviewed prospective study: 20 patients with wrist/hand fractures received in-hospital 3D-printed patient-specific casts made by scanning plus high-speed printing; all achieved fracture union with no pressure sores or ..., printing workflow averaging 161 minutes.
sources.transferJustification: Establishes worker-quality clinical acceptability of a machine-constructed custom immobilization device relative to the hand-molded plaster/thermoplastic device a therapist would build.

sources.title: Post Process Support Removal Solutions for 3D Printing | GoEngineer
sources.claim: Commercial automated post-processing machines perform support removal, powder removal and ... 3D-printed parts without manual benchwork, and are in production use at medical/orthodontic device labs.
sources.transferJustification: Covers the trim/deburr/finish steps of orthosis construction that would otherwise be manual, supporting whole-instance completion of machine fabrication.

sources.title: Delcam's dancing feet: express custom orthotics, 3D scanned and milled in minutes - DEVELOP3D
sources.claim: A CAD/CAM chain takes a 3D foot scan straight into a CNC milling machine to cut custom orthotic blanks, sold as a portable in-clinic solution.
sources.transferJustification: Directly the construction of a custom foot orthosis shell by a machine in a fixtured, purpose-built cutting envelope.

sources.system: Autonomous unscrewing cell (UR10e + Intel RealSense D405 + mechatronic screwdriver)
sources.developer: academic research group (Robotics and Computer-Integrated Manufacturing)
sources.title: Robotic system for automated disassembly of electronic waste: Unscrewing - ScienceDirect
sources.claim: A research robotic cell autonomously removes screws from varied electronic devices using vision and a custom screwdriver end effector; the authors note the same capability is relevant to repair and remanufacturing, but the demonstrated scope is the unscrewing step, not diagnosing and completing a repair.
sources.transferJustification: Closest located robotic evidence for device repair. It covers only fastener removal on electronics in a lab cell, not fault diagnosis, part replacement, reassembly and function check on heterogeneous mobility equipment.

tasks.label: Evaluate, fit, or adjust prosthetic or orthotic devices or recommend modification to orthotist.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Outpatient rehab clinic / gym: PT checks a lower-limb prosthesis during gait training — inspects the residual limb for redness and breakdown, adds or removes sock ply, adjusts suspension/liner and shoe, watches the patient walk, judges alignment and socket fit, and phones or writes the prosthetist with a modification request.

Inpatient rehab unit: PT dons and adjusts an AFO/KAFO on a stroke or neuro patient with spasticity and edema — positions the foot in the brace, seats the heel, sets strap tension, adds padding, checks skin after 20 minutes for pressure points, verifies shoe fit and gait, and recommends trim-line or plantarflexion-stop changes to the orthotist.

Acute care hospital bedside/post-op: PT sizes, applies and adjusts off-the-shelf devices — knee immobilizer, CAM walking boot, cervical collar, TLSO or shoulder sling — on a patient in bed with lines, drains, dressings and pain, then re-checks fit with the patient standing and educates the patient/family.

Home health visit: PT arrives at a private home, finds the patient wearing a brace or prosthesis incorrectly or with skin irritation, re-fits it in a cluttered bedroom or on a sofa, adjusts or trims straps and padding with hand tools, and documents a modification request to the orthotist.

Pediatric outpatient clinic or school therapy room: PT fits and adjusts AFOs/SMOs on a child with cerebral palsy who may be uncooperative or moving — checks growth and skin tolerance, adjusts straps and inserts, tests fit in shoes and during walking, and coordinates changes with the orthotist.

sources.system: Close-fitting dressing assistance robot (semantic visual-attention state estimation)
sources.title: Close-Fitting Dressing Assistance Based on State Estimation of Feet and Garments with Semantic-based Visual Attention
sources.claim: Research robot autonomously puts socks onto unseen human feet in a laboratory setting — the closest demonstrated robotic capability to donning a close-fitting device on a patient's limb; it does not evaluate fit, inspect skin, adjust straps or judge gait.
sources.transferJustification: Donning a sock on a human foot is the nearest analogue to donning an AFO or prosthetic liner: same body region, deformable object, compliant contact with a person. It falls short because the demo is a lab bench task with limited success rates and no fit evaluation, strap adjustment, skin check or gait assessment.

sources.title: WalkON Suit F1 is a Next Generation Exoskeleton That Can Walk Itself, Help Paraplegics
sources.claim: A wearable exoskeleton walks itself to a seated user and docks from the front so the user can don it without human assistance — device self-attachment, not a robot fitting an orthosis to a patient or evaluating its fit.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: self-donning of a powered lower-limb orthosis. It does not transfer to this task because the machine is the device itself, purpose-mated to one trained user, and performs no clinical evaluation, skin inspection, strap/alignment adjustment or modification recommendation for arbitrary braces and prostheses.

sources.system: Motor-driven adjustable cable-panel prosthetic socket with automatic size control
sources.developer: University of Washington (Weathersby, Garbini, Sanders et al.)
sources.title: Automatic Control of Prosthetic Socket Size for People With Transtibial Amputation: Implementation and Evaluation
sources.claim: A motor-actuated prosthetic socket automatically adjusts its own size during treadmill walking to maintain fit, based on an embedded sensor — an actuated device performing one sub-step (volume management), tested in a laboratory with 10 participants.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: maintaining prosthetic socket fit, a component of 'adjust prosthetic device.' It does not carry over to the whole task: it is a bespoke instrumented socket adjusting itself on a treadmill, not a system that evaluates fit on a patient, dons or modifies devices, or reports to an orthotist.

sources.title: Swisslog Healthcare Partners with Diligent Robotics to Enhance Hospital Logistics
sources.claim: The largest deployed fleet of mobile ... in US hospitals performs only logistics — delivering medications and lab samples — with no patient-contact clinical tasks such as fitting or adjusting braces.
sources.transferJustification: Cited to establish the state of deployed hospital robotics: even the most widely deployed clinical mobile manipulator does not touch patients, so no deployed system substantiates orthotic/prosthetic fitting on a person.

tasks.label: Teach physical therapy students or those in other health professions.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Serving as clinical instructor for a DPT student on a clinical affiliation in an outpatient orthopedic clinic: modeling an evaluation, then observing the student examine and treat patients, questioning clinical reasoning, giving verbal/written feedback, and completing performance evaluations.

Delivering an in-service or continuing-education session to nursing staff, aides, occupational therapists, or athletic trainers in a hospital or skilled nursing facility (e.g., safe patient transfers, body mechanics, fall prevention, gait-belt and lift use), combining a talk with a demonstration.

Giving didactic classroom or online lecture content in a DPT or PTA program: presenting kinesiology, pathology, or evidence-based practice material, answering questions, writing and grading exams and case assignments.

Leading a hands-on skills lab in a DPT program: demonstrating palpation, joint mobilization, manual muscle testing or gait-training technique on a student model, then circulating to correct students' hand placement, force, and positioning by touch and observation.

Ad-hoc bedside teaching during patient care in an acute or inpatient rehab setting: explaining and demonstrating a technique to a student, resident, nurse, or aide at the point of care and correcting their execution in real time.

tasks.label: Direct group rehabilitation activities.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Outpatient orthopedic/neuro clinic gym: PT directs a concurrent small group (2-4 patients) through their individualized exercise circuits — setting up bands, weights, steps and mat tables, demonstrating each exercise, circulating to correct form by hand, spotting unstable patients, progressing or regressing loads on the fly, and documenting each patient's participation.

Skilled nursing facility or inpatient rehab unit: PT leads a Medicare-style group therapy session (about 4 frail patients) in the rehab gym — seated and standing strengthening, balance and transfer practice, applying gait belts, assisting patients in and out of wheelchairs, guarding continuously against falls, adapting exercises for each patient's precautions.

Hospital wellness center or clinic class for 8-15 medically stable ambulatory participants (fall-prevention/balance, Parkinson's, arthritis, cardiac or pulmonary rehab): PT leads warm-up and station circuit from the front, demonstrates, cues verbally, monitors exertion/vitals and symptoms, and steps in physically to steady or correct at-risk participants.

Aquatic therapy group in a facility therapy pool: PT directs 4-8 patients from deck or in the water, fits flotation belts and noodles, assists entry/exit via steps or lift, provides manual cueing and support in the water, monitors for fatigue and safety.

Pediatric group PT in a school gym or pediatric clinic: 3-6 children run an obstacle course and motor-skills games; PT sets up mats, balls and equipment, physically facilitates movement patterns, catches/supports children, and manages behavior and attention.

Community-based group session in a venue taken as found (church hall, senior apartment community room, park, or community outreach site): PT carries in equipment, improvises the layout to the space, works around uneven surfaces, bystanders and varying chairs, and leads and guards the class.

sources.system: NAO humanoid autonomous robot-to-group exercise coach
sources.developer: Aldebaran/SoftBank NAO platform; university research group (IJALR study)
sources.title: An Autonomous Robot-to-Group Exercise Coach at a Senior Living Community: A Study in Human-Robot Interaction
sources.claim: A NAO humanoid robot acted as an autonomous group exercise instructor at a senior ..., guiding six residents through leg, hand and neck exercises in a single on-site research session; no hands-on assistance, guarding or individualized therapeutic progression was involved.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robot-led group exercise coaching for seniors. It is the nearest analogue to directing group rehabilitation, but transfer is limited: the robot only demonstrates and verbally cues seated/standing exercises in a one-off study, and does not set up equipment, correct form by hand, guard against falls, or individualize a plan of care.

sources.system: Salt (autonomous socially assistive exercise-facilitation robot, Nejat lab)
sources.developer: Autonomous Systems and Biomechatronics Lab, University of Toronto
sources.title: Long-Term Exercise Assistance: Group and One-on-One Interactions between a Social Robot and Seniors (Robotics 12(1):9)
sources.claim: An autonomous socially assistive robot facilitated long-term one-on-one and group exercise sessions with seniors in a care residence, monitoring heart rate and adapting encouragement; sessions were wellness exercise facilitation with staff/researchers present, not skilled therapy with physical assistance.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous robot facilitation of group exercise in long-term care. Objects (people doing seated/standing exercises) and environment (care-facility activity room) are comparable, but the robot provides no manual cueing, no fall guarding, no equipment handling, and no clinical progression, so it does not carry over to a PT-directed rehabilitation group.

sources.title: News on Aging | ILC-Japan (interview on PALRO in nursing care facilities)
sources.claim: PALRO, a small humanoid used as a recreation and exercise leader, is commercially deployed in roughly 900 Japanese nursing care facilities, where it runs pre-programmed recreation and exercise routines for groups of residents with care staff present.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robot-led group recreation and exercise sessions in eldercare facilities. It shows scaled deployment of group-activity leading, but the content is recreation-level exercise supervised by human staff, with no therapeutic prescription, no physical assistance, and no responsibility for patient safety, so it does not transfer to PT-directed rehabilitation groups.

sources.title: A Robot for Every Home? Japan Is Using Bots as Companions and Caretakers (Pulitzer Center)
sources.claim: PALRO functions as an exercise instructor among other recreation roles at a Tokyo senior care facility, leading residents in activities during scheduled recreational programs.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: leading group exercise/recreation for elderly residents. Confirms the deployed role is entertainment-and-exercise leading in a care facility, not skilled rehabilitation direction; no hands-on therapy or safety guarding is performed.

sources.system: Social robot-delivered Otago Exercise Program (Pepper-class social robot)
sources.developer: Wayne State University / Henry Ford Health research team
sources.title: Effect of Robotic Delivery of Physical Activity and Fall Prevention Exercise in Older Adults: A Pilot Cohort Study (Cureus)
sources.claim: A pilot cohort study delivered a modified Otago fall-prevention exercise program to five community-dwelling older adults via a social robot, three times weekly for four weeks; delivery was one-on-one, feasibility-stage, and did not include hands-on correction or guarding.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robot delivery of a therapeutic fall-prevention exercise program. Closest evidence to PT-prescribed exercise, but it is one-on-one, n=5, feasibility-stage, with no group management, no manual facilitation and no documented autonomy, so it cannot substantiate completing a PT-directed group session.

roles.title: Radiation Therapists
aliases: Computed Tomography Simulation Therapist (CT Simulation Therapist)
Radiation Oncology Registered Nurse (Radiation Oncology RN)
roles.description: Provide radiation therapy to patients as prescribed by a radiation oncologist according to established practices and standards. Duties may include reviewing prescription and diagnosis; acting as liaison with physician and supportive care personnel; preparing equipment, such as immobilization, treatment, and protection devices; and maintaining records, reports, and files. May assist in dosimetry procedures and tumor localization.

tasks.label: Position patients for treatment with accuracy, according to prescription.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Breast/chest-wall external beam fraction in a hospital or freestanding linac vault: ambulatory patient helped onto an inclined breast board, arms raised into arm rests, gown adjusted, torso rolled/straightened to tattoos and lasers, chin turned, then imaging/surface guidance and couch correction to the prescribed isocenter; often deep-inspiration breath-hold coaching.

Pelvis/abdomen fraction (prostate, gynecologic, rectal, bladder): patient supine or prone on vac-lok/knee-and-ankle immobilization, clothing lowered, hips squared to lasers and tattoos, bladder/bowel status checked, daily CBCT match to fiducials or bone and 6DoF couch correction to prescription.

Head-and-neck or brain fraction: patient's head placed in the indexed headrest, thermoplastic mask warmed and clipped down, shoulders pulled inferiorly, bite block or mouthpiece placed, then kV/CBCT match with rotational (6DoF) correction to sub-2 mm tolerance.

High-precision SRS/SBRT or particle-therapy fraction: cooperative patient in a stereotactic mask, frame or body immobilization (sometimes abdominal compression), sub-millimeter tolerance, multiple imaging/verification cycles and fine 6DoF or robotic-positioner corrections between fields.

Frail, obese, post-operative or non-ambulatory patient (often an inpatient on a stretcher or in a wheelchair, sometimes in pain or with drains and lines): therapists physically transfer the patient with a slide board or hoist, support painful limbs, coax the patient into a reproducible position, and re-adjust by hand when imaging shows gross rotation the couch cannot correct; frequently palliative or emergent.

Pediatric, cognitively impaired or highly anxious patient: therapists coax, distract and reassure, physically steady a moving patient, work around anesthesia staff and monitoring lines when the child is sedated, and repeatedly re-position between imaging checks.

sources.developer: BEC GmbH (Buck Engineering & Consulting) with KUKA
sources.title: Medical Robotics — BEC GmbH - robotic solutions
sources.claim: BEC's exacure is a certified medical-device robotic patient positioning system (ceiling-mounted 7-axis industrial robot carrying the treatment couch) installed and used clinically at the MedAustron particle therapy centre; an integrated optical tracker checks couch position 500 times per second and applies corrections in real time.

sources.title: BEC uses KUKA robots in particle-based radiotherapy
sources.claim: KUKA case study confirms the exacure patient positioning system uses ceiling-mounted KUKA robot kinematics to align the patient to the therapy beam very precisely, with an on-board medPhoton imaging system moving along the patient bed.

sources.system: Elekta Synergy remote/automatic treatment couch with XVI cone-beam CT
sources.title: Accuracy of automatic couch corrections with on-line volumetric imaging - PubMed
sources.claim: Automatic remote couch adjustment following cone-beam CT localization was characterized and placed in clinical service on four Elekta Synergy linacs; patients whose isocenter displacement exceeded tolerance were corrected by remote automatic couch movement, with sub-millimetre couch motion accuracy verified by optical tracking and a verification CBCT.

sources.system: 6DoF robotic couch with Elekta XVI CBCT
sources.title: Positioning accuracy during VMAT of gynecologic malignancies and the resulting dosimetric impact by a 6-degree-of-freedom couch in combination with daily kilovoltage cone beam computed tomography
sources.claim: In routine clinical VMAT for gynecologic cancer, after automatic bone-anatomy matching of the daily CBCT the 6-degree-of-freedom robotic couch was automatically shifted in all three translations and three rotations, with a verification CBCT confirming the accuracy of the automatic correction across 573 scans.

sources.system: HexaPOD evo RT System with iGUIDE
sources.title: Radiation Oncology Accessories Catalog - Elekta
sources.claim: The HexaPOD evo RT System is a commercially sold computer-controlled robotic treatment couch top with six degrees of freedom that automatically imports XVI positional-error correction values into iGUIDE and performs remote positioning correction with sub-millimetre accuracy.

sources.developer: clinical study, Fox Chase Cancer Center / Mass General Brigham
sources.title: Room to Move: Enhancing Head and Neck Radiotherapy With a Six-Degree-of-Freedom Couch
sources.claim: A 2026 clinical series of 214 head-and-neck fractions on a 6DoF couch documents the limit of robotic couch correction: the couch permits at most 3 degrees of rotation, and larger misalignments required therapists to re-enter the room and manually adjust the patient before re-imaging.

sources.system: FAST 3D Camera / FAST Integrated Workflow (Somatom CT)
sources.title: FAST 3D Camera for CT patient positioning - Siemens Healthineers
sources.claim: Siemens Healthineers' FAST 3D Camera, shipped on FDA-cleared Somatom CT scanners, uses AI/deep learning to sense the patient lying on the table and drive the table to the correct isocenter and scan range automatically, improving centring from 19±10 mm manually to 5±3 mm.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: positioning a patient who is already lying on a table to a prescribed isocenter in a hospital imaging room. The machine senses the patient's body surface and drives the patient support automatically — the same act as driving a treatment couch to the prescribed position — though it does not place or arrange the patient's body.

tasks.label: Administer prescribed doses of radiation to specific body parts, using radiation therapy equipment according to established practices and standards.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Routine daily external-beam photon fraction (breast, prostate, pelvis, brain, palliative bone) on a linac in a hospital or freestanding radiation-oncology vault. Cooperative ambulatory patient on the couch in standard immobilization; therapist verifies identity, prescription and fraction number in the record-and-verify system, acquires kV/CBCT localization imaging, applies the couch correction, delivers the IMRT/VMAT plan from the console while monitoring via CCTV/audio, and closes the treatment record.

SRS/SBRT or motion-managed fraction (frameless cranial SRS, lung/liver SBRT, deep-inspiration breath-hold breast) delivered to sub-millimetre tolerance with intrafraction imaging, real-time tracking or gating, beam holds for motion, and repeat verification imaging between arcs. Same institutional treatment vault.

Treatments requiring hands-on in-room work at the machine during the session: attaching an electron applicator with a custom cutout, laying bolus or compensators on the patient's skin, placing shielding, marking fields, and re-entering the vault between fields to change accessories or angles (electrons, superficial/orthovoltage, TBI, multi-field palliative setups).

Fraction delivered to a patient who cannot cooperate reliably: frail or in severe pain, confused/demented, claustrophobic, a paediatric patient under anaesthesia, or a patient who moves, coughs or becomes distressed mid-beam. Requires reassurance, entering the room to reposition or steady the patient, adjusting for pain, and aborting/resuming treatment safely.

HDR brachytherapy fraction in a shielded brachytherapy suite: planned dwell positions and times are loaded into the remote afterloader, connections to the applicator are confirmed, and the source is driven out to treat the target while the team monitors from the console and responds to interlocks and emergency retraction.

sources.title: Robot-assisted system for precision radiation | KUKA Global
sources.claim: The CyberKnife is a clinically deployed robotic radiation delivery system: a linac on a KUKA industrial robot plus a robot-guided RoboCouch that positions the patient to the planned ... automatically, without manual alignment.

sources.title: CYBERKNIFE TREATMENT DELIVERY SYSTEM Technical Specifications
sources.claim: Accuray's technical specification states the RoboCouch automatically positions the patient in six degrees of freedom, and that combined with the robotic linac manipulator the system delivers treatment from scores of non-coplanar beam angles.

sources.title: Image-Guided Robotic Radiosurgery | Neupsy Key
sources.claim: Peer-reviewed description of CyberKnife: an x-ray image-guidance system repeatedly images the target during treatment and the robot corrects target-position changes in real time to sub-millimetre accuracy, so dose is administered under closed-loop machine control.

tasks.label: Follow principles of radiation protection for patient, self, and others.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Linac vault daily cycle at an outpatient/hospital radiation oncology center: morning radiation-safety checks (door interlock kills beam, beam-on warning lights, emergency-off buttons, room audio/video monitoring), wearing and exchanging the personal OSL/film dosimeter, and for each of 20-40 fractions per day verifying the vault is clear of family/staff, closing and interlocking the shielded door, retreating to the console, watching the patient on CCTV and intercom during beam-on, and interrupting the beam if the patient moves or is in distress.

Applying patient-contact protective measures before a fraction: positioning eye, thyroid, gonadal/testicular shields or shielding drapes on the patient, placing bolus, and verifying identity, treatment site, field and prescription (and pregnancy status where applicable) so the wrong tissue or wrong patient is not irradiated.

Machine-side custom shielding hardware: retrieving the individual patient's electron cutout or shielding block tray from storage, confirming it is the correct device for that field, and inserting/mounting it correctly oriented in the treatment head accessory slot or applicator before beam-on.

Radiation-safety communication and access control with people other than the patient: instructing family and visitors to remain outside during beam-on, fitting/handing a lead apron to a caregiver who must stay with a pediatric or confused patient, controlling who enters the controlled area, and giving post-treatment radiation precautions to implant or radiopharmaceutical patients and their households.

HDR brachytherapy or sealed-source session: setting up portable lead shields, applying time-distance-shielding while working near the loaded applicator, keeping a survey meter at hand, confirming after each fraction that the source has fully retracted into the safe, posting controlled-area signage, and escorting the patient out.

Area radiation monitoring rounds in the department: walking the vault, maze, control area and adjacent occupied spaces with a calibrated survey meter (or checking fixed area monitors), reading and logging dose rates, and flagging any elevated reading to the physicist/RSO.

sources.title: Making Radiation Mapping Safer & More Reliable | Boston Dynamics
sources.claim: Spot, a legged mobile robot carrying radiation-detection payloads, performs autonomous radiation mapping routes in nuclear power plant facilities, replacing human survey walks with a detector.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: routine area radiation survey in an institution-controlled facility. It transfers to a radiation-oncology monitoring round because the act is identical — carry a calibrated detector along a defined route inside a controlled facility, log dose rates, and flag elevated readings.

sources.title: CARMA II: A ground vehicle for autonomous surveying of alpha, beta and gamma radiation
sources.claim: CARMA II is an autonomous ground vehicle that surveys nuclear facilities for alpha, beta ... produces radiation heatmaps, a job otherwise done by human survey operators.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: contamination/dose-rate survey of a controlled nuclear facility. The measurement, route-following and logging are the same operations a therapist performs on a departmental survey round; objects (handheld detector, fixed monitors) and precision requirements are comparable.

sources.title: Videos | Remtec | Robotics & Automation
sources.claim: A commercially integrated FANUC SCARA cell autonomously identifies small rigid parts with vision and inserts them, correctly oriented, into a specific fixture, then swaps fixture models from a nested drawer.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: vision-identified pick-and-insert of a small rigid part into a keyed fixture in a fenced cell. Mounting a patient-specific electron cutout or block tray in an accessory slot is the same class of operation — identify the correct part, orient it, insert to a few tenths of a millimetre — when the applicator is presented fixtured as a purpose-built cell would present it.

instances.label: Routine daily curative external-beam fraction on a C-arm/O-ring linac for an ambulatory adult (breast, prostate, pelvis): greet and identify the patient, position supine on the couch to skin marks/tattoos with standard immobilization (breast board, knee bolster, Vac-Lok), acquire daily kV/CBCT image guidance, evaluate the match and apply couch shifts, leave the room, deliver a multi-field IMRT/VMAT fraction while monitoring by CCTV/intercom, record the fraction, assist patient off the couch.

Mask-immobilized head-and-neck or thoracic fraction: fit the thermoplastic mask and index it to the couch, add bolus where prescribed, tight (<3 mm) setup tolerance with daily CBCT or orthogonal kV, 6-DoF corrections, manage patient anxiety/claustrophobia and secretions, deliver and record.

Palliative or supportive-care fraction for a frail, sedated, in-pain or non-ambulatory inpatient: transfer from wheelchair/stretcher with a lift or two-person assist, coax the patient into an approximate position they may not be able to hold, simple AP/PA or opposed fields, frequent pauses to reposition or comfort the patient, coordination with nursing/transport.

High-precision stereotactic session (SRS/SBRT, gated or breath-hold, cranial frame/mask, abdominal compression, fiducial or surface tracking): long setup, repeat imaging, breath-hold coaching, continuous intrafraction motion monitoring and beam gating, often with physicist or physician present for the first fraction.

Session that deviates from routine: patient reports new pain, skin breakdown, nausea or device/anatomy change; image match falls outside tolerance or shows anatomic change; machine interlock or fault occurs. Therapist must assess, stop or modify, contact the physician/nurse/dosimetrist, document, and decide whether to treat, re-setup, or reschedule.

instances.label: Morning warm-up and daily dosimetric constancy check of a C-arm linac in a hospital radiation oncology vault: deliver warm-up MU, run the daily output/energy/flatness-symmetry constancy test (QA device on couch or vendor self-check), compare to baselines, record pass/fail before the first patient.

Daily safety and mechanical checks on the same linac: door interlock and beam-off test, emergency-off buttons, beam-on indicator lights, audio/video intercom, radiation area monitor, room laser localization and ODI at isocenter, collision interlocks, couch and hand-pendant motion, checklist documentation.

Daily/weekly checks of imaging and localization systems: kV/MV/CBCT panel deployment and image quality, imaging-vs-treatment isocenter coincidence, couch positioning/repositioning accuracy, Winston-Lutz on SRS days, SGRT/gating device function; phantom set up on the couch and results reviewed.

Checks during the treatment day between patients: verifying accessories and applicators (electron cones, blocks, bolus, immobilization devices, couch tops) are intact and seated, responding to interlocks/faults, inspecting the machine, confirming proper operation before resuming treatment, escalating to physics/service.

Daily checks on specialty treatment units the therapist runs or assists with: HDR afterloader (source position, channel/transfer-tube checks, survey meter), ring-gantry/helical or PET-guided linac, MR-linac, Gamma Knife or proton unit daily QA with the vendor detector/phantom placed on the couch.

Daily checks of the CT or MR simulator in the radiation oncology department: scanner warm-up/constancy scan of the QA phantom on the flat couch top, image-quality and geometric checks, simulation laser alignment verification, documentation.
