tasks.label: Observe and reassure patients during treatment and report unusual reactions to physician or turn equipment off if unexpected adverse reactions occur.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Routine daily external-beam fraction on a linac: the therapist sits at the control console outside the vault, watches the patient on closed-circuit video and listens over the intercom while the beam is on, checks for motion or distress between fields, and speaks a few reassuring words; the session ends uneventfully.

Anxious, claustrophobic, or pediatric-but-unsedated patient (e.g., thermoplastic head-and-neck mask): the therapist coaches and reassures over the intercom throughout, may hold the beam and re-enter to calm the patient, and documents the difficulty for the care team.

Acute event during beam-on - coughing fit, nausea/vomiting, chest pain, panic, or seizure seen on the monitor: the therapist immediately interrupts the beam at the console, enters the room, and reports the reaction to the nurse and radiation oncologist.

High-risk delivery (SBRT/SRS, sedated or anesthetized pediatric patient, breath-hold/gated treatment): the therapist monitors respiration traces, surface-guidance/motion signals, and camera views along with anesthesia staff, halting delivery if the patient moves out ... tolerance or reacts adversely.

Observing and reporting cumulative treatment reactions noticed at the machine (skin desquamation, mucositis, worsening pain, weight loss) and relaying them to the physician or nurse for the weekly on-treatment review.

tasks.label: Educate, prepare, and reassure patients and their families by answering questions, providing physical assistance, and reinforcing physicians' advice regarding treatment reactions or post-treatment care.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Routine daily treatment visit in a hospital/cancer-center radiation oncology department: the therapist greets the patient in the waiting area, escorts them into the treatment vault, gives a hand/arm for support onto the treatment couch, adjusts gown and blankets, answers the patient's questions about fatigue, skin redness or bowel/bladder symptoms, reinforces the oncologist's advice on managing them, and reassures the patient during setup.

First-day / simulation education session: the therapist walks a newly diagnosed patient and one or two accompanying family members through the treatment course - positioning, immobilization mask or vac-bag, tattoo marks, what sensations to expect, skin-care and diet instructions - hands over written instruction sheets, answers unscripted questions, and gauges understanding, escalating clinical questions to the nurse or physician.

Frail, elderly, obese, post-operative or mobility-impaired patient: physical assistance transferring from wheelchair or stretcher onto the treatment couch (often slide board, ceiling lift, or a two-person lift), supporting painful limbs, arranging pillows/knee cushions, managing oxygen tubing or drains, and continuously reassuring a patient who is in pain, confused, or fearful.

Highly distressed patient: claustrophobic head-and-neck patient being masked, a breath-hold breast patient needing coaching, or a pediatric patient with anxious parents present - requires sustained calming talk, hand-holding, pausing and restarting the setup, explaining to the family, and deciding when to fetch the nurse, physician or anesthesia.

End-of-treatment and post-treatment instruction: on the last fraction the therapist reviews post-treatment skin care, the expected timeline for side effects to peak and resolve, follow-up appointment logistics, reinforces the physician's discharge advice, and answers questions from the patient and family members in the department or by phone afterwards.

sources.transferJustification: Related task: hospital inpatient education and reassurance. Closest existing evidence to the education/reassurance half of this task; it shows scripted, adjunct-only delivery in a structured hospital ward and no physical assistance to the patient.

sources.title: Serve Robotics to Acquire Diligent Robotics, Expanding Physical AI Platform Beyond the Sidewalk

sources.transferJustification: Related task: hospital materials logistics. It establishes the state of the art for mobile robots inside E2 healthcare facilities - navigation and object transport only - showing that deployed hospital robots do not perform patient-facing physical assistance or counselling.

sources.claim: The best-known patient-transfer robot able to lift a person from a bed into a ... remained an experimental laboratory prototype, controlled by a caregiver through tactile/force input, and was never commercialized for clinical use.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: transferring a patient between bed and wheelchair, the same physical act as helping a frail radiotherapy patient onto the treatment couch. It shows this capability exists only as an operator-driven prototype, not as an autonomous worker-quality system.

sources.developer: Karlsruhe Institute of Technology, SARAI Lab
sources.title: Frontiers | Autonomy in socially assistive robotics: a systematic review
sources.claim: A 2025 systematic review of autonomy in socially assistive robotics finds that social-robot applications, including healthcare ones, commonly depend on a hidden human operator (Wizard-of-Oz) for sensing and dialogue rather than full autonomy.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: social interaction and counselling by robots generally. It establishes that reported social-robot 'conversations' with patients are frequently human-operated, so such demonstrations cannot substantiate autonomous completion of patient education and reassurance.

instances.label: CT-simulation suite: therapist fabricates a thermoplastic head/neck or brain immobilization mask on the patient — heats the sheet in a water bath, drapes and stretches the hot pliable material over the face/shoulders, smooths it to the contour, clips it to the baseplate/headrest, indexes it to the couch and labels/marks it while the patient lies still.

CT-simulation suite: therapist builds and fits body immobilization — evacuating a Vac-Lok cushion or pouring/molding an alpha cradle around the patient, assembling breast board/wing board angles, knee and foot supports, arm holders, then indexing all components to the couch and recording the setup.

Linac treatment vault, per fraction: therapist retrieves the patient's devices and prepares the machine — mounts headrest/baseplate/vac bag at the indexed couch position, clips the mask over the patient, attaches the electron applicator with its custom cutout or loads a wedge/tray, and lays bolus onto the patient's skin over the treatment site.

Mold room / device fabrication bench: constructing custom electron cutouts and shielding blocks — cutting the Styrofoam mold from the planned field shape and casting Cerrobend, or ordering/producing a milled or printed cutout, then mounting it in the applicator frame and verifying the field shape.

Device fabrication bench: constructing custom bolus for a chest wall, nose, scalp or extremity — shaping/stacking Superflab sheets, molding wax to the contour, or designing and 3D printing a patient-specific bolus, then checking thickness and fit before treatment.

Treatment room / clinic: preparing patient protection devices — custom lead eye or gonadal shields, lead sheet shielding over a pacemaker or a previously irradiated area, testicular clamshells — cut or selected to size and positioned on or around the patient before the fraction.

tasks.label: Help physicians, radiation oncologists, or clinical physicists to prepare physical or technical aspects of radiation treatment plans, using information about patient condition and anatomy.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: CT-simulation session in the hospital sim suite: transfer the patient onto the flat-top couch, position limbs and head per the physician's site-specific setup, mold and fit a custom immobilization device (thermoplastic head/shoulder mask, vac-lok bag, breast board, knee/ankle stocks), index it, place radiopaque BBs, acquire the (4D)CT dataset, mark or tattoo reference points, and export images and setup data for planning. Patients may be frail, in pain, obese, claustrophobic or unable to hold still.

Assisting the radiation oncologist during simulation/tumor localization: wiring surgical scars and palpable masses, placing markers and clinical setup marks where the physician indicates, measuring patient separations and contours, photographing the setup, documenting clinical field borders and bolus/shielding instructions for the planner, with the patient on the couch and the physician directing verbally.

Mold-room fabrication of a patient-specific treatment accessory from the digital plan: producing custom bolus (3D-printed or shaped sheet), electron cutouts and shielding blocks, or compensators from the field shape/surface exported by the planning system, then checking and labelling the device for treatment.

Assisting the physicist with pre-treatment dosimetric verification of the plan at the linac: setting up the QA phantom/detector array or running a phantomless portal-dosimetry delivery of the patient's plan, delivering the measurement fields and returning the gamma/dose result before the first fraction.

Machine-side plan verification (dry run) with the patient present: positioning the patient in the approved immobilization at the treatment unit, applying planned shifts, acquiring kV/CBCT verification imaging, checking gantry/couch clearance and reproducibility, mounting accessories (bolus, cutout, breast board), and feeding problems back to the physician/dosimetrist for plan changes.

Workstation work in the planning office/console area: importing and checking images and contours, entering and verifying prescription, plan and field parameters in the record-and-verify system, checking MU/second-check output, DRRs and setup notes, and preparing plan documentation for physician and physicist review. No physical manipulation is required.

sources.system: Machine Performance Check (MPC) on TrueBeam/Halcyon linacs

tasks.label: Photograph treated area of patient and process film.

instances.label: Daily/weekly verification ("port") imaging of the treatment field on the linac: with the patient immobilized on the treatment couch inside the vault, the therapist obtains an MV portal or kV/CBCT image of the treated area, has it processed/registered against the reference DRR, and stores it in the record for physician review before the beam is delivered.

Setup and identification photographs at CT-simulation or first fraction: digital photos of the treated area showing skin marks/tattoos, immobilization devices and patient position (plus a face photo for ID), captured in the sim or treatment room and uploaded into the oncology information system for daily reproducibility.

On-treatment documentation photo of the skin in the treated area (erythema, moist desquamation, bolus effect) during weekly review: patient seated or standing, partially undressed, variable body sites (breast/axilla, head and neck, perineum), close-up framing with a label or scale, image filed to the chart.

Legacy film workflow: load/place a port-film cassette in the beam, expose it during treatment, carry the cassette to the darkroom, run the film through the automatic processor, label it and hang/scan it for the oncologist's approval.

Non-standard photography: hand-held close-ups of awkward setups — electron cone or scalp field, frog-leg or prone groin field, brachytherapy applicator in situ, pediatric or wheelchair-bound patient — where the therapist must work around drapes, devices and body habitus to frame and light the shot.

sources.title: The CyberKnife radiosurgery system for lung cancer - PubMed
sources.claim: The CyberKnife robotic radiosurgery system uses ceiling-mounted kV X-ray sources and flat-panel detectors to acquire live digital radiographs of the treated target during treatment in hospital treatment vaults.
sources.transferJustification: This is the modern form of the task's "photograph treated area of patient": verification imaging of the treated volume, with digital processing replacing film development.

sources.title: Dosimetric impact of intra-fraction prostate motion under a tumour-tracking system in hypofractionated robotic radiosurgery
sources.claim: During clinical prostate SBRT the CyberKnife automatically acquires orthogonal kV images, processes them to compute target displacement, and corrects position without operator intervention, repeatedly through the fraction.

sources.title: ExacTrac Dynamic: SRS & SBRT with submillimetric accuracy | Brainlab
sources.claim: Brainlab ExacTrac Dynamic, a commercial room-mounted stereoscopic X-ray plus thermal-surface system, automatically images and verifies the patient's internal anatomy and corrects deviations in six degrees of ... during treatment.

sources.title: Impact of intrafraction fiducial tracking on planning target margins during prostate stereotactic body radiotherapy using Brainlab ExacTrac Dynamic with robotic couch correction
sources.claim: A clinical institution reports routine use of ExacTrac Dynamic stereoscopic X-ray intrafraction imaging with 6DoF robotic couch correction for prostate SBRT patients, showing the automated imaging workflow in routine hospital service.

sources.title: Evaluation of image-guided and surface-guided radiotherapy for breast cancer patients treated in deep inspiration breath-hold: A single institution experience
sources.claim: AlignRT surface-guided radiotherapy uses ceiling-mounted camera pods in the treatment room to capture and continuously process optical images of the patient's skin surface over the treated area throughout the fraction; in routine clinical use since 2018 at the reporting centre.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: optical surface capture of the treatment area. It transfers to the setup-photograph instance because the same room-mounted cameras photograph the treated area of the patient without a human framing the shot and the image is automatically processed and recorded against the reference.

sources.system: Optical surface imaging patient identification (AlignRT-class system)
sources.title: A novel method for radiotherapy patient identification using surface imaging
sources.claim: Optical surface imaging captured in the radiotherapy treatment room has been used to automatically identify the patient by comparing the daily surface image of the treatment area with the stored reference image.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated patient identification from a captured surface image. It substitutes for the ID/setup photograph placed in the treatment record, using an automatically captured and processed image of the patient in the treatment position.

sources.title: Automated triage of cancer-suspicious skin lesions with 3D total-body photography | npj Digital Medicine
sources.claim: The VECTRA WB360 3D total-body photography booth captures the patient's entire skin surface with 92 cameras under standardized lighting in a single near-instantaneous capture and automatically processes the images to map and characterize skin lesions; used in dermatology clinics.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: clinical photography of a patient's skin and automated image processing. It transfers to photographing a treated skin area because the object (human skin surface, including reactions such as erythema), the imaging modality (standardized colour photography) and the deliverable (a processed, archived clinical image) match; the patient must, however, be brought to the fixed booth.

sources.title: What Is Automatic Film Processing? | FujiFilm NDT
sources.claim: Automatic film processors are electromechanical machines that transport an inserted sheet of film through developer, fixer, wash and dry stages and deliver a finished radiograph without manual chemical handling.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: industrial/radiographic film development. The identical machine class and film stock are used for radiotherapy port and simulation films, so the "process film" half of the task carries over directly.

sources.title: Portal films and automatic film handling systems - INIS-IAEA
sources.claim: Automatic daylight film handling systems were used in radiotherapy departments to unload cassettes and process portal/simulation films without darkroom manual handling.

instances.label: CT-simulation session in the cancer center sim suite: therapist works alongside the radiation oncologist and dosimetrist — lifts/positions the patient on the flat sim couch, fabricates and fits immobilization (thermoplastic mask, vac-lok bag, breast board, knee/head rests), aligns to room lasers, places radiopaque wires/BBs on scars and palpable disease at the physician's direction, runs the scan, sets isocenter and marks/tattoos the skin, takes setup photos, and pushes images to planning.

Image-guided tumor localization at the treatment unit: therapist assists physician/physicist at first-day localization or ongoing IGRT — acquires kV pair/CBCT/MR images, registers to the planning reference, determines and applies couch corrections (including 6DoF), verifies match with the physician, and manages motion (gating, breath-hold, fiducial or surface tracking).

Planning-support work with the dosimetrist in the clinic: taking patient separations/contours and surface measurements, verifying transferred images and setup parameters, performing a dry-run/verification setup of the new plan on the treatment machine, mounting and checking accessories, and taping in-vivo dosimeters (diodes/OSLDs) on the patient for dose verification.

Preparing beam-modifying and dosimetry accessories called for by the plan, in the mold room: cutting electron cutouts/shielding block foam from digitized outlines exported from the planning system, pouring/mounting alloy blocks on trays, building or 3D-printing patient-specific bolus and surface applicators, labeling and QC-checking against the plan.

Special and brachytherapy procedures: assisting the physician in the brachytherapy suite or OR during applicator/catheter/interstitial needle placement, prepping and handing sterile instruments and dummy markers, positioning the patient for orthogonal films/CT localization of the implant, connecting transfer tubes to the HDR afterloader, or assisting with SRS frame placement and TBI setup.

sources.claim: Accuray's Synchrony technology on the CyberKnife (robotic-arm-mounted linac) and Radixact continuously localizes the moving target from in-treatment imaging and automatically repositions the beam in real time, without human ... during delivery; commercially deployed in hospital treatment vaults worldwide.
sources.transferJustification: Same task: machine-performed tumor localization and physical correction, the technical core of the therapist's assistance during localization at the treatment unit.

tasks.label: Train or supervise student or subordinate radiotherapy technologists.

instances.label: Clinical supervision of a radiation therapy student at the linear accelerator in a hospital radiation oncology department: watching the student position and immobilize the patient, checking setup against the plan and imaging, correcting technique verbally, and debriefing afterward.

Orienting and instructing a newly hired or junior therapist at the treatment console: explaining the record-and-verify system, IGRT/imaging workflow, machine operation and interlocks, and departmental procedure while the trainee performs the steps.

Day-to-day supervision of subordinate therapists on a treatment unit: assigning patients and rooms, answering questions during the day, reviewing treatment charts and QA documentation, correcting errors, and escalating issues to the physicist or radiation oncologist.

Formal competency assessment and documentation for a student in an accredited program: completing clinical competency checklists, oral/written quizzing on anatomy, dose and safety, writing performance evaluations, and conferring with the clinical coordinator.
In-service or classroom instruction: presenting a new protocol, radiation safety topic, or equipment update to students and staff, including Q&A and distribution of written materials.

tasks.label: Store, sterilize, or prepare the special applicators containing the radioactive substance implanted by the physician.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Before a scheduled HDR gynecologic treatment, the therapist pulls the prescribed applicator set (tandem-and-ovoids, tandem-and-ring, or vaginal cylinder) from clinic storage in the brachytherapy suite, checks each metal piece for damage, assembles it to the prescribed size/angle, runs the check cable/QA jig through each channel, and sets out matching transfer tubes ready for the physician's insertion.

After a procedure, used reusable applicators, cylinders, needles and transfer tubes are wiped at point of use, transported to the sterile processing department, decontaminated (lumen brushing, ultrasonic, washer-disinfector), inspected, reassembled into their labeled tray/peel pouch, steam-sterilized, and returned as a sterile, documented set.

Routine storage and inventory control: returning sterile applicator sets to labeled cabinets in the brachytherapy suite, securing source containers/afterloader in the shielded safe, logging source and applicator inventory, and doing periodic wipe tests and integrity checks required by the radioactive materials license.

Preparing radioactive sources into the applicator/needles for a permanent implant (I-125/Pd-103 prostate seed case): behind shielding, building seed-and-spacer trains per the plan, verifying source strength/count, and loading them into the implant needles for the physician.

Intraprocedural work in the OR/brachytherapy suite: opening sterile applicator packs onto the sterile field, passing applicators, needles and obturators to the physician during the implant, and connecting the inserted applicator to the afterloader transfer tubes on the patient before treatment.

sources.title: Getinge transforms sterile reprocessing with Automatiq - a full range of logistic automation modules
sources.claim: Getinge's Automatiq family provides robotic loading/unloading of washer-disinfectors and steam sterilizers plus a self-navigating mobile robot that moves instrument loads between stations in hospital central sterile supply departments.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: machine reprocessing of reusable surgical instruments. Brachytherapy applicators are reusable stainless-steel instruments reprocessed on the same washer-disinfector/steam-sterilizer equipment and racks, so automated loading, transport and cycle running carries over.

sources.system: Getinge Automation System / Automatiq automated solutions
sources.title: Automated Solutions - Getinge
sources.claim: Getinge's installed CSSD automation moves clean goods automatically out of the washer-disinfector and onward to the next station, with human staff still performing sorting, inspection and packing.
sources.transferJustification: Same related task as above; it also shows the residual manual steps (sorting/inspection/packing) that keep hospital CSSD work from being robot-completed as found.

sources.system: Autonomous instrument tray assembly system (Stäubli TX2-60L + YOLO12/ResNet perception)
sources.developer: University of Louisville / Chitalia lab et al.
sources.title: Towards Autonomous Instrument Tray Assembly for Sterile Processing Applications
sources.claim: A fully automated robotic cell ... Stäubli TX2-60L arm, vision-based instrument recognition and 3D-printed holders sorts surgical instruments and packs them into sterile trays, with fewer instrument collisions than human-assembled trays.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: identifying and assembling metal surgical instruments into their correct sterile tray. Applicator sets are the same class of rigid metal instruments handled in the same trays, so identification, grasping and correct placement transfer.

sources.system: Pulse-oximeter refurbishing and repackaging system (12-station indexing dial with vision-guided robots and Kanga pouch sealer)

sources.claim: A production machine reprocesses used reusable pulse-oximeter sensors: vision-guided SCARA and six-axis robots refurbish and functionally test the device, then a gantry loads it into a Tyvek pouch and a pouching machine seals it, at one part per six seconds with automatic changeover.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic assembly, inspection and sterile-barrier pouching of small reusable medical devices in a fixtured cell. Applicator preparation and packaging involve comparable small rigid components, tolerances and peel-pouch packaging.

sources.claim: Clinical remote afterloading systems automatically transfer the sealed radioactive source between a shielded storage safe and each treatment applicator via a motor- or pneumatically-driven transport system, removing manual source handling.

sources.title: I-125 seed calibration using the SeedSelectron® afterloader: a practical solution to fulfill AAPM-ESTRO recommendations
sources.claim: The SeedSelectron afterloader automatically builds seed/spacer trains per the treatment plan from sterilized I-125 seed and spacer cartridges and loads them for implantation, used intraoperatively for prostate brachytherapy.

sources.title: A technical evaluation of the Nucletron FIRST system: Conformance of a remote afterloading brachytherapy seed implantation system to manufacturer specifications and AAPM Task Group report recommendations
sources.claim: Technical evaluation of the Nucletron FIRST system found the seedSelectron builds needle configurations of seeds and spacers and includes a diode array that verifies the build sequence and assays seed source strength, replacing manual seed-train building and physicist assay.

sources.title: Automated Pharmacy Storage System - Swisslog BoxPicker
sources.claim: BoxPicker is a robotic, high-density automated storage and retrieval system installed in hospital pharmacies that fully automates storage and retrieval of packaged items, controls access and maintains inventory.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: secure, access-controlled robotic put-away, inventory tracking and retrieval of packaged clinical items. Storing sterile applicator sets and source containers involves comparable objects, handling precision and audit/inventory requirements.

sources.title: Serve Robotics to Acquire Diligent Robotics, Expanding Physical AI Platform Beyond the Sidewalk
sources.claim: Diligent Robotics' Moxi mobile manipulators operate autonomously in hospitals, with nearly 100 robots having completed over 1.25 million deliveries of supplies, medications and lab samples across 25+ U.S. hospital facilities.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous hospital logistics. It bounds what robots do in hospital settings as found — point-to-point transport of totes and supplies, not assembly, reprocessing or handling of brachytherapy applicators.

tasks.label: Assist in the preparation of sealed radioactive materials, such as cobalt, radium, cesium, or isotopes, for use in radiation treatments.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Hospital brachytherapy suite with an HDR Ir-192/Co-60 remote afterloader: before the day's treatments the therapist assists in readying the sealed source - confirming the decayed source strength at the console, running the source-position, dwell-time and transit QA with the check cable/ruler or well-chamber jig, verifying the source leaves and returns to the shielded safe, and documenting the checks.

Operating room or hot lab for a permanent LDR prostate implant: verify/assay the I-125 or Pd-103 seeds supplied in vendor shielded cartridges against the certificate, sort seeds and spacers to the plan, and load them into implant needles or strands behind shielding while keeping seed counts for source accountability.

Source receipt and accountability in the department hot lab: unpack the shipping cask for a new HDR source or seed order, survey the package with a meter, perform wipe/leak tests and count the samples, log the sources into inventory, place them in the shielded safe, assist the vendor engineer at the quarterly HDR source exchange, and package the decayed source for return shipment.

Episcleral (COMS/Eye Physics) plaque for ocular melanoma: behind an L-block, seat and glue 8-24 I-125 seeds into the slots of the Silastic seed carrier per the plan, verify the loading pattern radiographically, sterilize and deliver the loaded plaque to the OR, then recover, count and inventory the seeds after plaque removal.

Legacy LDR/PDR intracavitary gynecologic case using Cs-137 pellets or tubes: select the prescribed active/inactive source configuration, load the source carrier or afterloader channels behind shielding, move it in a shielded transport container to the shielded room, and return the sources to the safe afterwards.

sources.title: Evaluation of an automatic needle-loading system - PubMed
sources.claim: The Isoloader is a commercial computerized workstation that automatically assays individual I-125 seeds with a built-in solid-state detector and loads them into surgical needles, taking seeds from a shielded vendor cartridge; used in hospital prostate-implant procedures.

sources.title: A technical evaluation of the Nucletron FIRST system: Conformance of a remote afterloading brachytherapy seed implantation system to manufacturer specifications and AAPM Task Group report recommendations
sources.claim: The seedSelectron afterloader automatically builds the seed/spacer train for each implant needle from sterilized seed and spacer cartridges according to the treatment plan and assays every seed with a calibrated diode, operating in the operating room during prostate implants.

sources.title: GEC-ESTRO ACROP recommendations on calibration and traceability of LE-LDR photon-emitting brachytherapy sources at the hospital level
sources.claim: European guidance on hospital-level calibration of LDR seeds describes the seedSelectron as an automatic seed loader supplied with cartridges of up to 100 ..., confirming continuing clinical/commercial use of automated seed loading.

sources.system: HDR remote afterloader (e.g., Varian BRAVOS, Elekta Flexitron, E&Z BEBIG SagiNova)
sources.title: High Dose Rate Brachytherapy (HDR) - Oncology Medical Physics
sources.claim: HDR remote afterloaders are motor-driven, computer-controlled machines that transport the sealed radioactive source out of an internal shielded safe through fixtured transfer tubes to programmed positions and back, i.e. the machine performs the physical loading of the sealed source for treatment.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: delivery-side source transport. It substantiates that the sealed source itself is handled and positioned for treatment entirely by machine inside a purpose-built shielded device, which is the source-handling core of preparing sealed sources for treatment.

sources.developer: Canadian Organization of Medical Physicists / CPQR
sources.title: COMP report: CPQR technical quality control guidelines for brachytherapy remote afterloaders
sources.claim: National QC guidance for brachytherapy remote afterloaders states that with these systems staff do not directly handle the radioactive ..., confirming that source manipulation for treatment is machine-performed in clinics.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: routine source handling for treatment delivery. It shows the sealed-source handling step of this task is already executed by the machine rather than by staff hands.

sources.system: Automated daily QA program on Varian Bravos afterloader

sources.title: Automated daily check QA of treatment channel adjustments (TCA), active, and dummy source positioning using bravos after loader

sources.system: DMG256 monolithic silicon strip detector HDR QA system

roles.title: Recreational Therapists
roles.description: Plan, direct, or coordinate medically-approved recreation programs for patients in hospitals, nursing homes, or other institutions. Activities include sports, trips, dramatics, social activities, and crafts. May assess a patient condition and recommend appropriate recreational activity.

tasks.label: Instruct patient in activities and techniques, such as sports, dance, music, art, or relaxation techniques, designed to meet their specific physical or psychological needs.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Group adapted-exercise / movement class (chair exercises, stretching, balance work) for 6-12 residents in the day room of a nursing home, inpatient rehab unit or psychiatric unit; therapist demonstrates each movement, cues residents by name, paces the session and adjusts for individual mobility limits and fatigue.

Music or dance-based session in a facility common room: leading a sing-along with familiar songs, movement-to-music/chair dancing, or a rhythm activity; therapist demonstrates, models tempo and movements, and keeps a mixed-ability group engaged.

Instruction in relaxation / stress-management techniques (diaphragmatic breathing, progressive muscle relaxation, guided imagery, mindfulness) one-on-one at bedside or in a small group room on a behavioral-health, oncology or dementia-care unit; verbal guidance plus modeled breathing and posture.

Art, craft or expressive-arts instruction (painting, ceramics, collage, adaptive knitting) in a facility activity room: therapist lays out and adapts tools (built-up grips, easels), demonstrates technique, and gives hand-over-hand or physical-positioning assistance to patients with hemiparesis, tremor or low vision.

Adapted sports / active games instruction in a facility gym, courtyard or hallway (bowling with a ramp, bocce, balloon volleyball, basketball toss, wheelchair sport skills): therapist sets out equipment, positions and transfers patients, demonstrates the skill, physically guards and assists grip/swing, retrieves balls.

Community-based or in-home leisure-skill instruction: teaching a patient to use adaptive equipment at a public bowling alley, park, pool or gym during a community-reintegration outing, or teaching leisure/relaxation skills during a home visit, in settings taken as found.

sources.title: Robots can help improve mental wellbeing at work – as long as they look right
sources.claim: Over four weeks in a real workplace, employees were guided through wellbeing exercises (positive-psychology/relaxation practice) by QTrobot or Misty II robots acting as coaches, delivered by the robots themselves rather than a human.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: guiding a person through structured relaxation/positive-psychology exercises. The delivery mode (verbal instruction plus modeled pacing, no object manipulation) and indoor institutional room match rec-therapy relaxation instruction.

sources.system: VITA multi-modal LLM-based robotic coach on QTrobot
sources.developer: University of Cambridge (Spitale, Gunes) with LuxAI QTrobot
sources.title: VITA: A Multi-modal LLM-based System for Longitudinal, Autonomous, and Adaptive Robotic Mental Well-being Coaching
sources.claim: The VITA system let a QTrobot coach autonomously adapt its delivery of wellbeing exercises to each user's facial valence and speech behaviour, validated in a four-week real-world study with 17 participants in a workplace, with significant wellbeing improvements.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: adaptive one-to-one coaching in psychological wellbeing techniques; shows autonomous per-person adaptation, the element rec-therapy relaxation instruction requires beyond a fixed script.

sources.title: Autonomous Sanitiser and Assistant Lio – Digital Innovation Hubs (DIH-HERO)
sources.claim: The Lio mobile manipulator is deployed and operating autonomously in healthcare institutions in Germany and Switzerland, where its duties include activating patients with entertainment and sport activities alongside fetching and handing over objects.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: leading engagement/activation activities with residents in care institutions while also grasping and handing over objects, showing that facility activity-leading plus limited object handover is done autonomously in E2 settings.

sources.title: Zora, The First Social Robot Already Widely Used In Healthcare
sources.claim: The widely used Zora care robot leads exercise, dance and music sessions in care homes only under staff control from a tablet, i.e. its activity sessions are human-operated rather than autonomous.

tasks.label: Conduct therapy sessions to improve patients' mental and physical well-being.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Group recreation/leisure therapy session in a skilled nursing or assisted-living day room: therapist sets up the room and materials, gathers and escorts 8–15 residents (many in wheelchairs, several with dementia), leads seated exercise, music, bingo or reminiscence, cues and redirects individuals, hands out and retrieves balls/instruments/cards, watches for fatigue, agitation and fall risk, gives hands-on assist, cleans up and documents each participant's response to goals.

One-on-one session on a hospital inpatient unit (acute rehab, psychiatry, pediatrics) or at bedside: therapist brings adapted materials, engages one patient in a leisure/coping activity (card or video game, art, guided relaxation, pet visit), works around IV lines and precautions, provides physical assist, transfer or repositioning, grades and adapts the activity in real time to tolerance and affect, then documents.

Physically active session in a rehab gym, therapeutic pool, or facility grounds: adaptive sports (wheelchair basketball, bowling, boccia), aquatic recreation, or exercise circuit; therapist fits adaptive gear and life jackets, performs transfers, spots and guards against falls, sets and resets equipment, paces the group, and intervenes physically when a participant is unsafe.

Community reintegration outing with a small patient group: van loading and driving, bus or store training, restaurant meal, park or museum trip; therapist pushes wheelchairs over curbs and uneven ground, manages money and social interactions, supervises safety in uncontrolled public space, and handles behavioral escalation or medical events away from the facility.

Behavioral health, substance-use, or pediatric group in a treatment facility: expressive arts/crafts, team-building games, stress-management group; therapist preps and counts restricted supplies (scissors, cords), facilitates group process, gives hand-over-hand help to some participants, de-escalates conflict, and cleans up and reconciles supplies afterward.

sources.title: Aging Japan: Robots May Have Role in Future of Elder Care (VOA)
sources.claim: SoftBank's Pepper humanoid was fielded in roughly 500 Japanese elder-care homes to run games, exercise routines and simple conversation with groups of residents — the closest existing deployment to a robot 'leading' a recreation session.
sources.transferJustification: Robot-led group exercise/recreation in a nursing home is the same activity type as instance 1 (group recreation session); cited to test whether the robot can carry the session, not a sub-step.

sources.title: Inside Japan's long experiment in automating eldercare — MIT Technology Review
sources.claim: Ethnographic study of a Japanese care home found Pepper's afternoon recreation sessions required a care worker to boot it up and wheel it into place, played a prerecorded routine, and only worked when a staff member stood beside the robot copying and echoing it; residents disengaged within weeks.

sources.system: Pepper with Care Prevention Gymnastics Exercises (CPGE) application
sources.title: Rehabilitation care with Pepper humanoid robot: A qualitative case study of older patients with schizophrenia and/or dementia in Japan
sources.claim: The most favorable published account of Pepper as a recreation leader describes a fixed 40-minute pre-authored gymnastics program, and states the system cannot move or respond on ... the patients present.

sources.title: Robots rise to meet the challenge of caring for old people (Nature)
sources.claim: Stevie, the socially assistive robot piloted at Knollwood Military Retirement Community where it hosted bingo and sing-alongs, ran only some preprogrammed actions and was otherwise operated by researchers on site.
sources.transferJustification: Hosting bingo/sing-alongs for residents is the group-activity component of instance 1; the source establishes the demonstration was human-controlled, so it cannot support a positive judgment.

sources.system: ARI humanoid with SPRING (H2020) software architecture
sources.developer: PAL Robotics / SPRING consortium (Inria and partners)
sources.title: Socially Pertinent Robots in Gerontological Healthcare (International Journal of Social Robotics)
sources.claim: State of the art for autonomous social humanoids in a geriatric care facility is multi-modal conversation and greeting/guidance during trials in a Paris day-care gerontological facility — not delivery of a planned therapeutic recreation session with physical assistance.
sources.transferJustification: Closest autonomous system operating in the same E2 setting as instances 1–2; establishes the ceiling of autonomous capability there is conversation, not conducting a therapy session.

sources.title: Inside Japan's long experiment in automating eldercare — MIT Technology Review
sources.claim: PARO, the therapeutic seal robot deployed in nursing homes for animal-assisted-type therapy, responds autonomously to touch and sound but in practice required staff to closely supervise its use with residents and did not substitute for staff-led activity.
sources.transferJustification: PARO is used within recreational/animal-assisted therapy sessions (instances 1–2); cited to show the robot supplies a stimulus a human still administers and supervises.

sources.title: QTRobot - autistic children's friend (Luxembourg government)
sources.claim: QTrobot, a commercially sold autonomous social robot used in autism therapy, is deployed as a mediator inside sessions run by a human therapist rather than as the provider of the session.
sources.transferJustification: Robot-assisted therapy sessions for children are analogous to instance 5 (pediatric/behavioral-health group); the source shows the robot's role is adjunct, with the clinician conducting the session.

tasks.label: Plan, organize, direct, and participate in treatment programs and activities to facilitate patients' rehabilitation, help them integrate into the community, and prevent further medical problems.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Skilled nursing / long-term care facility: therapist plans and runs a scheduled group session (seated exercise/ball toss, bingo, music, reminiscence, crafts) for 8-15 residents in the activity room, many with dementia or in wheelchairs. Gathers and escorts residents, sets up and hands out materials, leads and paces the activity, physically assists and redirects individual participants, watches for falls/choking/agitation, then documents participation and response in the care plan.

Inpatient rehabilitation or acute hospital unit: individual therapeutic recreation session with a stroke, TBI, or spinal-cord patient in the therapy gym or bedside. Sets up adaptive equipment (card holder, adapted game, functional leisure task), guides practice, gives hands-on assistance including transfers and positioning, observes precautions and fatigue, modifies the activity in real time, documents progress toward goals.

Behavioral health / psychiatric or substance-use unit: leads a therapeutic group (leisure education, stress management, cooperative games, expressive arts) with 6-12 patients. Screens supplies for safety/contraband, structures and directs the activity, manages group dynamics, redirects or de-escalates disruptive behavior, processes the experience verbally with the group, documents clinical observations.

Community reintegration outing: plans and leads a small group of patients on a trip (grocery store, restaurant, city bus, park, bowling alley). Loads wheelchairs and equipment into a van, navigates uncontrolled public spaces, supervises safety and medical needs, coaches community and social skills in the moment, handles unexpected events, returns and documents.

Adaptive sports, aquatics, or fitness program at the facility gym or pool: fits and adjusts adaptive equipment (sport wheelchair, adaptive cycle, flotation devices), assists pool-lift transfers, physically spots and supports participants, adapts rules to ability levels, monitors exertion and medical response.

Program planning and organization block: builds the monthly activity calendar and individualized treatment plans from assessments, orders and prepares supplies, coordinates volunteers, transport and interdisciplinary schedules, and physically stages equipment and rooms for the coming sessions.

sources.system: Zora (Zora Bots software on Aldebaran NAO/Pepper)
sources.title: Zora, The First Social Robot Already Widely Used In Healthcare | RoboticsTomorrow
sources.claim: Zora (NAO/Pepper software package) is marketed to skilled nursing facilities to lead exercise/physical-therapy classes, but it is driven by care staff through a tablet rather than running the session autonomously.
sources.transferJustification: Closest commercial analogue to the 'direct and participate in group activity' element of this task; cited to show the leading system is operated step-by-step by staff, so it cannot support an autonomous positive judgment.

sources.developer: Trinity College Dublin (Conor McGinn team) / Akara
sources.title: The Robot That Could Change the Senior Care Industry (TIME)
sources.claim: Stevie II, a socially assistive robot tested at Knollwood Military Retirement Community, called bingo numbers during an activity session, but the human activities assistant remained fully occupied running the room and the robot came with researcher handlers.
sources.transferJustification: Directly the group-activity element of the task in a long-term care setting; shows only a narrow sub-step (number calling) is offloaded while the human worker still performs the session.

sources.title: Potential Legal Issues and Care Implications during Care-Prevention Gymnastic Exercises for the Elderly Using Pepper in Long Term Health Care Facilities
sources.claim: Pepper robots are used in Japanese long-term care facilities to run a fixed 40-minute 'body-brain gymnastics' recreation program with residents; the program is pre-authored content played by the robot with facility staff present, and the paper analyses the resulting safety/legal implications for staff.
sources.transferJustification: Same activity type as instance 1 (group exercise recreation in a care facility); cited because the robot delivers scripted content only and does not assess, assist, or supervise residents.

sources.title: Aging Japan: Robots May Have Role in Future of Elder Care (VOA)
sources.claim: At Tokyo's Shin-tomi nursing home, a Pepper humanoid leads groups of residents in exercise sessions alongside about 20 other robot models, with care staff running and supervising the sessions.
sources.transferJustification: Real deployment of robot-fronted group exercise recreation in a nursing home, the highest-weight instance setting; establishes what deployed systems actually do (front a scripted routine) versus running the whole therapy session.

sources.title: The Use of PARO to Decrease Agitation in Persons With Dementia and/or Delirium (ClinicalTrials.gov NCT05565703)
sources.claim: PARO, a commercially deployed therapeutic seal robot used in nursing homes and long-term care, responds autonomously to touch, sound and handling, but is used as a therapy tool applied by a health care provider for a predetermined purpose and fixed time, not as a program planner or director.
sources.transferJustification: PARO is the most widely deployed autonomous robot in recreational-therapy practice; it participates as an object of therapy but performs none of the planning, directing, assisting or documenting that constitute the task.

sources.system: humanlike social robot in robot-assisted group activity (nursing-home pilot)
sources.developer: FHNW / Digital Stadt Bern research team (Tanner, Urech, Schulze, Manser)
sources.title: Older Adults' Engagement and Mood During Robot-Assisted Group Activities in Nursing Homes: Development and Observational Pilot Study (JMIR Rehabil Assist Technol)
sources.claim: A pilot study in four nursing homes found residents engaged in leisure group activities (singing, storytelling, exercises) demonstrated and guided by a ...; the work is an observational pilot of engagement/mood, not a demonstration of unattended session delivery.
sources.transferJustification: Directly the group recreation element of the task; cited as the research frontier, which remains an engagement pilot with staff present rather than autonomous end-to-end delivery of a therapy program.

tasks.label: Observe, analyze, and record patients' participation, reactions, and progress during treatment sessions, modifying treatment programs as needed.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

tasks.label: Develop treatment plan to meet needs of patient, based on needs assessment, patient interests, and objectives of therapy.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

tasks.label: Obtain information from medical records, medical staff, family members and the patients, themselves, to assess patients' capabilities, needs and interests.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

tasks.label: Confer with members of treatment team to plan and evaluate therapy programs.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

tasks.label: Counsel and encourage patients to develop leisure activities.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

tasks.label: Encourage clients with special needs and circumstances to acquire new skills and get involved in health-promoting leisure activities, such as sports, games, arts and crafts, and gardening.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Assisted living community or adult day program: therapist leads a verbally-driven group leisure activity (bingo, trivia, music quiz, seated chair exercise) for 8-25 largely cooperative, mostly ambulatory participants who are already gathered in the activity room with cards/props pre-placed; the therapist calls the game, paces it, and gives praise and encouragement to keep people engaged.

Skilled nursing / memory-care unit: group craft, sensory, gardening or ball-toss session for residents with moderate-to-severe dementia; therapist sets up and distributes supplies, gives hand-over-hand prompting, positions wheelchairs, redirects wandering or agitated residents, and adapts the activity in real time for safety.

Inpatient rehabilitation or acute hospital: one-on-one bedside or therapy-gym session teaching a patient post-stroke, TBI or spinal cord injury a new adapted leisure skill (adaptive gardening, card holder, adapted craft, adaptive sport equipment, aquatics); includes transfer/guarding, positioning, setting up adaptive equipment, grading the activity, and building motivation.

Behavioral health, psychiatric or substance-use treatment unit: leisure-education and teambuilding group (games, expressive arts, exercise) with clients who may be withdrawn, resistant, or escalated; therapist motivates reluctant participants, manages group dynamics and safety, and links activity to treatment goals.

School, pediatric clinic or day program for people with developmental disabilities/autism: teaching a new play, sport, or arts-and-crafts skill (throwing/catching, board game turn-taking, painting, planting seedlings) with hand-over-hand assistance, sensory adaptation, reinforcement, and behavior support.

Community reintegration outing: therapist takes a small group or individual to a park, community garden, bowling alley, adaptive sports event, gym or farmers market; encourages the client to try the activity, negotiates unfamiliar terrain and equipment, manages mobility devices, bystanders, and transport.

sources.system: Tangy (socially assistive robot, University of Toronto ASBLab)
sources.developer: University of Toronto Autonomous Systems and Biomechatronics Lab (G. Nejat)
sources.title: A user-study with Tangy the Bingo facilitating robot and long-term care residents (IEEE)
sources.claim: The socially assistive robot Tangy autonomously facilitated multi-user Bingo sessions with groups of elderly residents in a real long-term care facility.

sources.title: The Game Changer: The Role of Persuasive Socially Assistive Robots in the Sustained Engagement and Motivation of Older Adults in a Cognitive Activity
sources.claim: In two long-term-care studies the autonomous robot Tangy facilitated Trivia and Bingo games and delivered praise and encouragement, with residents showing high engagement and compliance.

sources.developer: Techmetics Robotics (deployed at The Salvation Army Peacehaven)
sources.title: Singapore is turning to AI to care for its rapidly aging population (Rest of World)
sources.claim: The humanoid robot Dexie has been in service two years at a Singapore nursing home, running pre-programmed routines that lead morning exercise, bingo and sing-along sessions for groups of residents with dementia.

sources.title: News on Aging: The Future of the Robot-led Nursing Care (ILC-Japan)
sources.claim: The commercially sold PALRO robot serves as the exercise instructor at a Japanese adult day-care facility, leading the group warm-up and oral-motor exercise segments of the daily functional-training program.

sources.developer: CARESSES consortium / SoftBank Robotics (Univ. of Bedfordshire evaluation)
sources.title: Robot care home trial claims 'significant' mental health benefits (Care Home Professional)
sources.claim: In the CARESSES trial, autonomous Pepper robots were placed with older adults in UK and Japanese care homes for up to 18 hours over two weeks and improved residents' mental health.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robot-led social/leisure engagement of institutionalised older adults. It shows an autonomous social robot can sustain conversation and suggest activities in a care-home room, the same setting and client group as group recreation leadership, though it involves no object handling.

sources.developer: EC-FP7 DREAM consortium (Univ. of Portsmouth, VUB, Babes-Bolyai et al.)
sources.title: Robot-enhanced therapy: development and validation of a supervised autonomous robotic system for autism spectrum disorders therapy
sources.claim: A supervised-autonomous NAO robot delivered robot-enhanced therapy sessions to children with autism in a clinical trial, with results reported as equivalent to standard human therapy on the targeted intervention tasks.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robot-delivered skill-teaching (turn-taking, imitation, joint attention) with children who have developmental disabilities. It is the closest evidence to encouraging skill acquisition in play, but it is table-top interaction under therapist supervision with no handling of craft, sport or gardening materials.

sources.title: Robotic Technology Successfully Engaging Children With Autism (Autism Digest)
sources.claim: MOVIA's robot-assisted instruction system for children with autism is only semi-autonomous: a human facilitator drives lesson selection and participation from a laptop.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robot-mediated teaching of games and social skills to children with special needs; cited to show the commercially fielded systems in this space still require a human facilitator, so they cannot substantiate autonomous completion.

tasks.label: Prepare and submit reports and charts to treatment team to reflect patients' reactions and evidence of progress or regression.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

tasks.label: Develop discharge plans for patients.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

roles.title: Respiratory Therapists
aliases: NICU RT (Neonatal Intensive Care Unit Respiratory Therapist)
roles.description: Assess, treat, and care for patients with breathing disorders. Assume primary responsibility for all respiratory care modalities, including the supervision of respiratory therapy technicians. Initiate and conduct therapeutic procedures; maintain patient records; and select, assemble, check, and operate equipment.

tasks.label: Set up and operate devices, such as mechanical ventilators, therapeutic gas administration apparatus, environmental control systems, or aerosol generators, following specified parameters of treatment.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Aerosol/nebulizer or MDI therapy on a med-surg floor, ED, or pulmonary clinic: retrieve the ordered unit-dose drug, open and assemble the nebulizer cup/T-piece/mouthpiece or aerosol mask, instill medication, connect tubing to a wall flowmeter or compressor, set flow, place the mouthpiece/mask on a seated or supine patient (often coughing, confused, or a crying child), coach breathing, monitor for 10-15 minutes, then disconnect, bag the device, and chart the response.

Initiating and running invasive mechanical ventilation in an ICU/ED: wheel the ventilator to the bedside, assemble the patient circuit with heated-wire humidifier, water bag spike, filters and inline suction, plug into wall O2/air/power, run the machine self-test and leak check, dial mode/Vt/rate/PEEP/FiO2 per the physician order or protocol, connect the wye to the patient's endotracheal or tracheostomy tube, verify chest rise/ETCO2/graphics, set alarms, and adjust settings after blood gases.

Initiating noninvasive support at the bedside (BiPAP/CPAP or high-flow nasal cannula) on a dyspneic ward, ED, or step-down patient: size and select the interface, assemble circuit and heated humidifier, set IPAP/EPAP or flow and FiO2, seat the mask on the patient's face and adjust headgear straps for a seal without pressure points, coach the anxious patient, correct leaks, and titrate over the following minutes.

Therapeutic gas administration in the hospital: setting up flowmeters, regulators and portable cylinders, placing nasal cannula/simple or non-rebreather mask/tracheostomy collar on the patient, changing transport cylinders, or setting up specialty gas delivery (inhaled nitric oxide with analyzer and backup, heliox, oxyhood/incubator environmental control in the nursery) and verifying delivered concentrations.

Home or subacute setup by a home-care/DME respiratory therapist: deliver and set up a home ventilator, CPAP/BiPAP, oxygen concentrator or trach/suction equipment in a private residence with unpredictable layout, pets, clutter and variable power outlets; assemble circuit, set prescribed parameters, verify function and alarms, and instruct the patient/caregiver.

sources.title: Safety and efficacy of a fully closed-loop control ventilation (IntelliVent-ASV) in sedated ICU patients with acute respiratory failure
sources.claim: A closed-loop ventilation mode commercially available on Hamilton ICU ventilators automatically adjusts ventilation and oxygenation ... once a clinician has assembled the circuit, connected the patient and started the mode; it automates titration only, not physical setup or patient connection.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automatic adjustment of ventilator settings. It covers only the 'operate/titrate' sub-step of the task; the machine performs no assembly, no interface placement and no connection to the patient.

sources.title: Automated oxygen titration and weaning with FreeO2 in patients with acute exacerbation of COPD
sources.claim: A closed-loop oxygen delivery device automatically adjusts oxygen flow through a nasal cannula to a SpO2 target in hospitalized COPD patients, but the cannula and tubing are placed on the patient by a clinician.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated oxygen titration. Substantiates only machine control of gas flow after a human sets up the circuit and applies the cannula; it does not substantiate the physical setup portion of this task.

sources.system: Telerobotic ICU ventilator operating system (Johns Hopkins)
sources.title: Telerobotic Operation of Intensive Care Unit Ventilators
sources.claim: The demonstrated way to have a machine change ICU ventilator settings without a clinician in the room is a small Cartesian robot bolted over the ventilator touchscreen and driven remotely by a human operator - i.e., teleoperation, not autonomous setup or operation.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: operating a ventilator's controls. Directly relevant hardware, but human-in-the-loop teleoperation, so it cannot support a positive judgment; it also performs no circuit assembly or patient connection.

sources.title: Autonomous Robot Performs COVID-19 Nasal Swab Tests
sources.claim: An autonomous robot can locate a patient's face and nostril by machine vision and insert a swab in a clinical screening setting - the closest demonstrated autonomous robotic physical interaction with a patient's airway - but it handles one rigid single-purpose tool with the subject positioned in a dedicated fixture.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous instrument placement on a cooperative patient's face. Shows the current frontier of patient-contact autonomy; it does not extend to assembling multi-component circuits, sealing and strapping a ventilation mask, or connecting a wye to an endotracheal tube.

sources.title: Development of a Novel Anesthesia Airway Management Robot
sources.claim: A research prototype robot with continuum arms and a mask-fastening module was built to hold and fasten an anesthesia mask on a face and perform mask positive-pressure ventilation, evaluated in bench and simulated-ventilation experiments rather than routine patient care.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: applying and sealing a ventilation mask on a face. Closest demonstration to NIV mask fitting, but it is a bench/simulation prototype with unestablished autonomy, so it cannot support completion at worker quality.

sources.developer: Foxconn with NVIDIA / Taichung Veterans General Hospital
sources.title: Could AI nursing robots help healthcare staffing shortages?
sources.claim: Autonomous hospital service robots deployed on wards perform logistics - medication and supply delivery and patient guidance - and are not shown assembling or connecting respiratory devices to patients.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous mobile work inside a hospital (E2 setting). Establishes that fielded hospital robots operate at the logistics level, with no bedside device setup or patient contact.

sources.system: IMA Automation medical device assembly lines
sources.date: accessed 2026-07; product line in commercial use
sources.title: IMA MED-TECH - Technologies for Medical Devices
sources.claim: Purpose-built automation cells commercially assemble flexible medical tubing to luer/male connectors and end caps and test the assemblies, showing that tube-to-connector joining is feasible when parts are fixtured and presented by a machine-built line.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated assembly of flexible medical tubing and tapered connectors in a fenced production cell. Comparable objects to a breathing circuit, but only the equipment-side sub-step; no live patient can be presented as a fixtured workpiece in such a cell.

tasks.label: Monitor patient's physiological responses to therapy, such as vital signs, arterial blood gases, or blood chemistry changes, and consult with physician if adverse reactions occur.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Adult ICU, mechanically ventilated patient: RT rounds at the bedside, reads monitor vitals and ventilator waveforms/settings, auscultates breath sounds, assesses work of breathing and secretions, draws an arterial blood gas from the indwelling arterial line, runs it on the point-of-care analyzer, interprets pH/PaO2/PaCO2 and electrolytes/lactate trends, and pages the intensivist when oxygenation or acid-base status deteriorates.

Hospital medical-surgical floor or ED: RT gives an aerosolized bronchodilator and monitors physiological response pre- and post-treatment — heart rate, respiratory rate, SpO2, breath sounds by stethoscope, observing for tachycardia, tremor, arrhythmia, or paradoxical bronchospasm — documents in the EHR and notifies the physician if an adverse reaction occurs.

Hospital floor/ED patient without an arterial line: RT performs a modified Allen test, does a radial arterial puncture with a heparinized syringe, holds pressure, handles the sample anaerobically, runs it on the blood gas analyzer, and telephones the physician with critical values and recommended therapy changes.

NICU/PICU: fragile neonate or small child on CPAP or a ventilator; RT checks transcutaneous CO2 and SpO2, observes chest rise, retractions, and color, obtains a capillary heel-stick or umbilical-line gas, correlates with ventilator changes, and alerts the neonatologist to desaturation or rising CO2.

Home care or long-term care visit: RT visits a patient on home oxygen or a home ventilator, takes spot vital signs and pulse oximetry (including ambulatory oximetry), assesses breathing and response to the current prescription in a cluttered, non-standard residence, and contacts the prescribing physician about desaturation or intolerance.

Rapid response, code, or intra-hospital transport: acutely deteriorating patient; RT continuously assesses vitals, SpO2 and end-tidal CO2 while bagging or managing the transport ventilator, obtains a stat blood gas, and communicates findings and recommendations to the physician in real time amid a crowded team.

sources.title: Performance, Safety, and Patient Experience of an Autonomous Robotic Phlebotomy Device: A Multicenter Trial | Clinical Chemistry
sources.claim: Vitestro's Aletta autonomous robotic phlebotomy device performs venous blood draws without a human operator, using multimodal imaging, with the patient's arm placed into the fixtured device; it was evaluated in a multicenter trial at Dutch hospitals/labs and CE-marked for European launch.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: diagnostic venous blood collection. It is the closest demonstrated robotic analog to obtaining a blood sample for gas/chemistry analysis, but transfer to this task is limited: the device draws from superficial veins of a cooperative, self-positioned arm at a fixed station, whereas ABG sampling requires arterial puncture (or arterial-line draw) on a bedridden patient, anaerobic sample handling, immediate interpretation, and physician escalation.

sources.system: Dr. Spot (Boston Dynamics Spot with contactless vital-sign payload)
sources.developer: MIT / Brigham and Women's Hospital / Boston Dynamics
sources.title: Brigham and Women's Hospital tests MIT's 'Dr. Spot' robot for contactless vital signs monitoring - Becker's Hospital Review
sources.claim: The MIT/Brigham 'Dr. Spot' quadruped carried camera-based contactless vital-sign sensing (skin temperature, respiratory rate, SpO2, heart rate) in an emergency department triage setting, but the robot was remote controlled by clinicians, not autonomous.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: contactless acquisition of vital signs, a component of monitoring physiological response. It does not substantiate completion here because operation was remote-controlled and limited to camera-based signals on cooperative triage patients, with no blood sampling, auscultation, or clinical escalation.

sources.system: Autonomous ultrasound-guided robotic percutaneous intervention system (research prototype)
sources.title: Preliminary Evaluation of an Ultrasound-Guided Robotic System for Autonomous Percutaneous Intervention
sources.claim: As of late 2024, a survey within a research paper presenting a fully autonomous ultrasound-guided needle-placement system states that no ultrasound-guided robotic system for percutaneous intervention had been validated for fully autonomous end-to-end needle placement in humans; the presented system was evaluated on phantoms.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous image-guided needle insertion, the core physical act of arterial blood gas sampling. It shows the capability remains at phantom-stage research, so it cannot substantiate autonomous arterial puncture on patients.

sources.title: Effectiveness, efficacy and safety of INTELLiVENT–ASV, a closed-loop ventilation mode for ICU patients - a systematic review (European Respiratory Society)
sources.claim: INTELLiVENT-ASV is a commercially available closed-loop ventilation mode that automatically titrates tidal volume, FiO2 and PEEP from physiologic signals (SpO2, EtCO2) in ICU patients; it adjusts therapy but does not perform bedside patient assessment, blood sampling, or physician consultation.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: closed-loop titration of ventilator therapy from continuous physiologic signals. It covers only the automated-response portion of monitoring within a single machine's own sensors; it performs no arterial blood gas sampling, no auscultation or hands-on assessment, and no escalation to a physician, so it cannot complete an instance.

sources.system: Smart patient-care robot (BLE-beacon localization + D* lite navigation prototype)
sources.title: Development of smart patient care robot with enhanced autonomous navigation through path optimization in hospital wards | Scientific Reports
sources.claim: A 2026 research prototype patient-care robot for hospital wards combines autonomous LiDAR navigation with basic temperature and heart-rate measurement and medication delivery; the reported contribution and validation concern navigation success through doorways, not clinical monitoring performance on patients.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous ward rounding with routine vital-sign capture. It does not substantiate completion because validation is limited to navigation metrics, the sensing is basic temperature/heart rate, and there is no breath-sound assessment, blood gas work, or clinical escalation.

sources.system: Proxima in-line arterial blood gas analyser
sources.title: Point-of-Care Blood Gas Analysis | Technology Networks
sources.claim: Bedside arterial blood gas analysis in the ICU is performed by in-line point-of-care analyzers such as Sphere Medical's Proxima, but the caregiver withdraws the blood into the sensor and interprets the result; the analyzer has no manipulator and does not assess the patient.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: obtaining and analyzing an arterial blood gas at the bedside. The instrument automates the assay only; sample withdrawal is caregiver-initiated and interpretation/escalation remain human, so it cannot substantiate robotic completion of the monitoring instance.

tasks.label: Read prescription, measure arterial blood gases, and review patient information to assess patient condition.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Adult ICU patient with an indwelling arterial line: RT reads the physician order in the EHR, draws a sample from the closed in-line sampling system (waste withdrawal, heparinized syringe fill, flush), expels air, mixes, runs it on a bedside/POC blood gas analyzer, then correlates pH/PaO2/PaCO2 with ventilator settings, vitals and chart to assess the patient.

Adult inpatient on a medical/surgical or step-down unit with no arterial line: RT verifies the order, assesses circulation (modified Allen test), palpates the radial artery on a patient who may be obese, edematous, hypotensive or agitated, performs a percutaneous arterial puncture at ~45 degrees, holds pressure 5 minutes, checks for hematoma, runs and interprets the sample.

Emergency department, code blue or rapid response: urgent ABG on an unstable, poorly perfused, sometimes moving patient amid a crowded bedside; sample must be obtained and resulted within minutes and integrated with the clinical picture to guide intubation/ventilation decisions.

NICU/PICU: arterial (umbilical/radial) or capillary heel-stick blood gas on a neonate or small child, sub-millimetre vessels, minimal blood volume permitted, thermal and infection precautions; result reviewed against ventilator/CPAP settings and the infant's chart.

Hospital blood gas laboratory shift: RT receives ABG syringes delivered from the units, verifies patient/order identity, checks sample integrity (clots, air bubbles, time on ice), mixes and loads the analyzer, runs QC/calibration, reports and calls critical values, and reviews patient information to interpret the result.

Outpatient setting (pulmonary function lab, pulmonary or hyperbaric clinic): seated cooperative ambulatory patient, scheduled radial arterial puncture for ABG on room air or during oxygen titration, sample run on lab analyzer and interpreted alongside PFT results and the chart.

sources.title: Performance, Safety, and Patient Experience of an Autonomous Robotic Phlebotomy Device: A Multicenter Trial (Clinical Chemistry)
sources.claim: Vitestro's Aletta autonomous robotic phlebotomy device performs venous blood draws autonomously (near-infrared, ultrasound and Doppler guidance) on seated outpatients in hospital phlebotomy departments, with a 94.5% first-stick success rate in a 1633-patient multicenter trial; it is venipuncture only, not arterial puncture.
sources.transferJustification: Related task = diagnostic venipuncture. It shows autonomous needle insertion is feasible in a structured hospital outpatient facility, but transfer to this task is NOT established: the device targets superficial antecubital veins in a seated cooperative patient whose arm is positioned in the device, whereas an ABG requires puncture of a deep pulsatile radial artery, collateral-circulation assessment, anaerobic heparinized-syringe handling and minutes of post-puncture compression, usually on a patient lying in an ICU/ED bed.

sources.system: MagicNurse / Aixam / Hagong intelligent blood collection robots
sources.developer: various Chinese manufacturers (review in Frontiers in Bioengineering and Biotechnology)
sources.title: Intelligent blood collection robot: key technologies, clinical applications, and future challenges
sources.claim: Review of commercially deployed 'intelligent blood collection robots' (MagicNurse, Aixam, Hagong) in Chinese hospitals shows they perform automated venous blood collection; no commercial robot is described as performing arterial puncture for blood gas sampling.
sources.transferJustification: Related task = venous blood collection in hospital draw stations. Cited to establish that the state of the art in autonomous needle-in-patient robots is venous sampling of cooperative seated patients; the review documents no arterial blood gas sampling robot, so it does not substantiate completion of this task.

sources.title: New Robot Does Superior Job Sampling Blood (Rutgers University)
sources.claim: A Rutgers-led handheld automated venipuncture device completed the first-in-human trial of automated blood drawing, with 87% overall success on 31 participants; arterial line placement was named only as possible future work.
sources.transferJustification: Related task = automated venipuncture with image-guided needle insertion in humans. It reaches only superficial veins under research-trial conditions and the developers list arterial line placement as a future extension, so it does not substantiate autonomous arterial blood gas sampling.

sources.system: Ultrasound-guided robotic blood drawing system (6-DoF arm with 3-DoF end-effector)
sources.title: Ultrasound-Guided Robotic Blood Drawing and In Vivo Studies on Submillimetre Vessels of Rats
sources.claim: An image-guided 6-DoF robotic vascular access system was evaluated in vivo only on rat tail veins (~0.7 mm), achieving 95% first-attempt success — autonomous sub-millimetre vessel cannulation remains at the animal-laboratory research stage.
sources.transferJustification: Related task = robotic small-vessel blood sampling, relevant because neonatal blood gas sampling involves sub-millimetre vessels; however the work is confined to anesthetized rats in a laboratory, so it cannot substantiate a patient-side arterial blood gas draw.

sources.title: AI-Enabled, Ultrasound-Guided Handheld Robotic Device for Femoral Vascular Access
sources.claim: AI-GUIDE, the leading AI/ultrasound-guided arterial (femoral) vascular access device, is a handheld tool that a human operator must place and aim on the patient; it has been evaluated on phantoms and animal models rather than operating autonomously at the bedside.
sources.transferJustification: Related task = arterial vascular access. It is the closest arterial-puncture automation, but it is held and positioned by a clinician (continuous human control of placement) and is pre-clinical, so it cannot support a positive judgment of autonomous completion of an arterial blood gas draw.
