tasks.label: Provide emergency care, such as artificial respiration, external cardiac massage, or assistance with cardiopulmonary resuscitation.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Code blue on an inpatient ward or ICU: the RT responds with the airway bag, opens/positions the airway, delivers bag-valve-mask ventilation with 100% O2, suctions secretions/emesis, assists the physician with intubation (hands the tube, confirms placement by EtCO2 and auscultation, secures it), then ventilates and transitions the patient to a transport ventilator, all while coordinating with the code team around a crowded bed.

Emergency department resuscitation of an adult in arrest, trauma or peri-arrest respiratory failure: RT sets up and checks airway/suction/oxygen equipment, provides mask ventilation, assists rapid-sequence intubation, manages ventilation during procedures, and works shoulder-to-shoulder with a large team in a crowded resuscitation bay.

Rotating into the compressor role during a prolonged in-hospital code: performing sustained external cardiac massage on an adult patient on a bed/backboard in 2-minute cycles at guideline rate and depth, pausing for rhythm and pulse checks.

Neonatal or pediatric resuscitation: delivery-room newborn resuscitation with T-piece/mask positive-pressure ventilation, small-volume suctioning, two-thumb chest compressions on a neonate, intubation assistance and surfactant, or a pediatric code on the floor/PICU.

Rapid response / pre-arrest respiratory emergency on a hospital floor: acute respiratory distress or hypoxemia, RT assesses work of breathing and gas exchange, fits and initiates NIV/BiPAP or high-flow nasal cannula, provides assisted mask ventilation if the patient deteriorates, and stabilizes for transfer to ICU.

Emergency care outside the controlled unit: arrest or airway emergency during critical-care interfacility transport (ambulance/helicopter), in a hospital lobby/parking area, or on a home-care visit, where the RT manages the airway and ventilation and may perform compressions in a cramped, uncontrolled space.

sources.date: 2026-07 (product page retrieved); device family in commercial use since 2003
sources.title: LUCAS 3, v3.1 chest compression system | Stryker
sources.claim: The LUCAS 3 mechanical chest compression system is a commercially deployed device that, once placed on a patient by a rescuer, delivers machine-controlled external cardiac massage at guideline depth and rate for as long as needed.
sources.transferJustification: Not a related task: external cardiac massage is named explicitly in this task; the device performs the compression itself, though a human must position the patient and apply the device.

sources.title: US LUCAS 3 Chest Compression System – Instructions For Use
sources.claim: The LUCAS 3 instructions for use document operator-selectable automatic compression modes (30:2 with a ventilation pause, or continuous), i.e. the compression cycle runs under machine control without step-by-step human actuation.

sources.title: Automated CPR Solutions | ZOLL Medical
sources.claim: ZOLL's AutoPulse is a commercially sold, battery-powered automated chest compression system used in both prehospital and in-hospital resuscitation, including during in-hospital transport and long codes.

sources.system: Mechanical chest compression devices (LUCAS, AutoPulse) vs manual CPR
sources.title: Mechanical versus manual chest compressions for cardiac arrest (Cochrane review)
sources.claim: Systematic review evidence concludes that mechanical chest compression devices are an acceptable substitute for manual compressions in defined settings, supporting worker-equivalent quality for the compression role only (not for airway or clinical management).

sources.developer: Jolife AB / Physio-Control (study by Singapore General Hospital EMS)
sources.title: Prompt use of mechanical cardiopulmonary resuscitation in out-of-hospital cardiac arrest: the MECCA study report
sources.claim: In clinical use the mechanical CPR device must be applied to the patient by the human crew after manual CPR has begun; the machine then runs the compression cycle itself while humans deliver ventilations.

sources.system: LUCAS mechanical CPR in the emergency department
sources.title: Early mechanical cardiopulmonary resuscitation can improve outcomes in patients with non-traumatic cardiac arrest in the emergency department
sources.claim: Mechanical CPR devices are also used inside hospitals, including emergency departments, for non-traumatic cardiac arrest, but they are applied by the clinical team to a patient already on a bed or backboard.

sources.system: Robot-assisted tracheal intubation system with soft actuator
sources.title: A robot-assisted tracheal intubation system based on a soft actuator
sources.claim: Autonomous robotic tracheal intubation has only been demonstrated on training manikins in laboratory proof-of-concept work, not on patients in clinical resuscitations.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: emergency airway management/intubation, a core part of the RT's role in a code. Transfer fails: the demonstration is on a rigid manikin in a lab, not a real airway with secretions, trismus or anatomic variation, so it cannot substantiate completion of the emergency-care instance.

sources.system: Teleoperated humanoid robots in medical task demonstrations
sources.developer: academic survey (arXiv, Humanoid Robots as First Assistants in Endoscopic Surgery)
sources.title: Humanoid Robots as First Assistants in Endoscopic Surgery
sources.claim: Humanoid robots performing emergency medical interventions such as bag-valve-mask ventilation have been shown only in mannequin experiments and under teleoperation.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: bag-valve-mask ventilation, the RT's central action in a code. Transfer fails: the demonstrations are teleoperated and on mannequins, so under the autonomy rule they cannot support a positive judgment.

tasks.label: Work as part of a team of physicians, nurses, or other healthcare professionals to manage patient care by assisting with medical procedures or related duties.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: ICU or ED bedside: RT joins the physician/nurse team for an emergent endotracheal intubation — preoxygenates with bag-valve-mask, hands laryngoscope/tube/stylet and applies suction on request, confirms placement by capnography and auscultation, secures the tube, initiates and titrates mechanical ventilation, reports to the team and documents. Patient may be agitated, obese, bleeding, or crashing.

Code blue / rapid response on a general ward or ED: RT takes the airway role during CPR — mask ventilation with two-person technique, assists intubation, coordinates ventilation with compressions and pauses, suctions vomit/secretions, transitions patient to a ventilator after ROSC, all while communicating with the code leader in a crowded room.

Daily multidisciplinary ICU rounds and collaborative ventilator management: RT presents the respiratory plan, performs spontaneous breathing trials, changes vent settings and modes per the team's plan, suctions the airway, checks circuits and alarms, and helps nurses turn, prone, or mobilize an intubated patient with lines and tubes attached.

Assisting at other bedside procedures: bronchoscopy, tracheostomy tube change, chest tube insertion, or tracheostomy/PEG at bedside — RT sets up and hands equipment, manages the airway and oxygenation, provides suction, adjusts ventilator during the procedure, monitors the patient's saturation and waveform, and troubleshoots problems in real time with the proceduralist.

Intra-hospital transport of a critically ill ventilated patient to CT/MRI/OR or between units with a nurse and physician: RT switches the patient to a transport ventilator or manual bagging, secures the airway and circuit, maneuvers the bed and equipment through corridors and elevators, manages the airway during imaging or transfer, and re-establishes ventilation at the destination.

Labor & delivery / NICU team work: RT attends a high-risk delivery with the neonatal team, provides positive-pressure ventilation with a T-piece resuscitator or mask on a newborn, assists with intubation and surfactant administration, places the infant on CPAP or a ventilator, and stabilizes for transfer to the NICU.

sources.date: 2024-11 (milestone report); fleet in 25+ US hospitals as of 2025
sources.title: Moxi reaches milestone of 100,000 autonomous elevator rides in hospitals - The Robot Report
sources.claim: The most widely deployed hospital mobile manipulator, Diligent Robotics' Moxi, operates autonomously in hospital corridors doing logistics (supplies, lab specimens, medications) and is explicitly non-patient-facing; it does not assist clinicians at the bedside during procedures.
sources.transferJustification: Closest deployed hospital robot to 'related duties' of a care team; cited to show the deployed state of the art is corridor logistics, not bedside procedural assistance, so it cannot substantiate completion of these instances.

sources.title: Moxi - ROBOTS: Your Guide to the World of Robotics
sources.claim: Moxi's marketed scope is non-patient-facing clinical support tasks, confirming no bedside procedural role.
sources.transferJustification: Establishes the boundary of deployed hospital robot capability (logistics only), relevant because the RT instances all require patient-facing manipulation and airway management.

sources.developer: Liang et al., UC San Diego (published in Nature)
sources.title: In vivo feasibility study of humanoid robots in surgery (project page)
sources.claim: The first in-vivo demonstration of a humanoid robot assisting/performing surgical steps (porcine laparoscopic cholecystectomy) was run through a teleoperation console, not autonomously.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: a humanoid assisting with an invasive bedside/OR procedure using standard human medical equipment. It is teleoperated, so under the autonomy rule it cannot support a positive judgment for RT procedural assistance.

sources.developer: Academic group (published in Communications Medicine, Nature Portfolio)
sources.title: Robotic scrub nurse to anticipate surgical instruments based on real-time laparoscopic video analysis
sources.claim: Autonomous robotic scrub-nurse prototypes that anticipate and hand over instruments succeed on only about 72% of handovers and are evaluated in laboratory/simulated settings, far below the reliability an employer would accept at a live bedside.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: handing instruments and supplies to a proceduralist, the manipulation core of 'assisting with medical procedures'. Performance level and lab-only evaluation show the sub-step, let alone the whole instance, is not completed at worker quality.

sources.developer: Haggerty et al. (Stanford/UCSF-affiliated team), Science Translational Medicine
sources.title: A soft robotic device for rapid and self-guided intubation | Science Translational Medicine
sources.claim: State-of-the-art autonomous airway-device robotics has been validated only in manikins and cadavers, not on live patients as part of a clinical team.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: securing an airway, the central physical act the RT supports during intubation and codes. Demonstration is on models/cadavers and covers only tube placement, so it cannot substantiate whole-instance team assistance on live patients.

sources.title: Closed-loop ventilation mode (IntelliVent®-ASV) in intensive care unit: a randomized trial - PubMed
sources.claim: Closed-loop ventilation modes automate ventilator setting adjustment and weaning in ICUs, reducing manual interventions, but they are ventilator control software acting only on gas delivery — they do not perform the bedside physical and team-coordination work of the instance.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: ventilator titration and weaning that the RT contributes to on rounds. It automates one sub-step within a fixed device and cannot suction, reposition patients, manage circuits, or interact with the team.

sources.title: Clinical trial to verify the safety of an automatic electric airway suction system: a multicenter prospective randomized study
sources.claim: An automatic airway suction system has been trialed in ICU patients, but it addresses a single sub-step (secretion removal through an existing artificial airway) rather than team-based procedural assistance.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: airway suctioning performed by RTs during procedures and rounds. It is a fixed single-function device on an already-placed airway, so it cannot complete any whole instance of team-based procedural assistance.

tasks.label: Make emergency visits to resolve equipment problems.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Hospital ICU/step-down: RT is paged urgently to a ventilated patient whose ventilator is alarming or malfunctioning. At the bedside the RT assesses the patient, traces the cause (kinked or disconnected circuit, water in tubing, mucus plug, failed flow/oxygen sensor, exhalation valve fault), hand-bags the patient if needed, suctions, swaps the circuit or the whole ventilator, re-enters settings, and confirms adequate ventilation.

Hospital general ward, ED, PACU or procedural suite: emergency call for an oxygen-delivery or noninvasive-support failure — dead wall outlet/flowmeter, empty or leaking cylinder or regulator, HFNC heater fault, BiPAP not triggering, large mask leak. RT arrives with backup equipment, diagnoses at the bedside amid staff and family, replaces components, verifies delivered FiO2/pressures and patient stability.

Home care RT makes an after-hours emergency visit to a private residence: home ventilator, trach patient's circuit/humidifier, or oxygen concentrator has failed or is alarming. Unfamiliar cluttered layout, pets, questionable wiring; RT assesses the patient, troubleshoots or exchanges the device, restores backup power/cylinder, and re-instructs the family caregiver.

Skilled nursing / long-term acute care / subacute vent unit: RT is dispatched on an emergency call to a resident's room to resolve a ventilator, concentrator, or suction-unit failure, coordinating with facility nursing staff and documenting the fix.

Urgent bench triage in the hospital equipment/clean workroom: a device pulled from an emergency is checked out — leak and calibration test, sensor or battery replacement, filter/valve swap — and either returned to service quickly or tagged for biomed, with a tested replacement staged for the unit.

sources.title: Physical artificial intelligence in nursing: Robotics - Nursing Outlook
sources.claim: A 2025 peer-reviewed review of physical AI/robotics in nursing states that bedside robotics today is largely human-operated or preprogrammed with limited autonomy and has not transferred to direct patient care, because patient care environments are varied and unstructured.
sources.transferJustification: Covers the closely related task class of robots performing hands-on bedside patient-care work in hospitals; it establishes that no fielded system autonomously manipulates patient-attached equipment, so nothing transfers to emergency respiratory equipment troubleshooting.

sources.title: When Collaborative Robots Meet the Bedside: Nurses Informing Emerging Artificial Intelligence Technology - PMC (Delaware Journal of Public Health)
sources.claim: A three-year hospital collaborative-robot pilot at ChristianaCare found value only in non-urgent delivery workflows; the cobots could not meaningfully augment clinical bedside work.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous hospital cobots handling supplies and equipment on patient units. Transfer fails explicitly — the same robots proved limited to non-urgent transport and could not take on clinical, time-critical bedside work.

sources.title: Serve Robotics to Acquire Diligent Robotics, Expanding Physical AI Platform Beyond the Sidewalk
sources.claim: Diligent Robotics' Moxi mobile manipulator is deployed at scale in US hospitals, autonomously navigating corridors and elevators to fetch and deliver supplies, medications and equipment — but its demonstrated work is transport, not diagnosing or repairing respiratory devices.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous mobile manipulation inside hospitals (E2). Navigation and simple grasping transfer, but the emergency equipment task requires patient assessment, fault diagnosis and fine manipulation of circuits and airways, which Moxi has never been shown to do.

sources.developer: Johns Hopkins University / University of Maryland
sources.title: Telerobotic Operation of Intensive Care Unit Ventilators - Frontiers in Robotics and AI
sources.claim: The most advanced robot shown interacting with an ICU ventilator is a teleoperated Cartesian device clamped to the ventilator touchscreen that a clinician drives from outside the room; it only presses screen controls and cannot handle circuits, cylinders, suction or patient assessment.
sources.transferJustification: Directly related task (manipulating a ventilator's controls in the ICU). It is continuously teleoperated and limited to touchscreen input, so it cannot support a positive judgment for resolving equipment failures.

tasks.label: Determine requirements for treatment, such as type, method and duration of therapy, precautions to be taken, or medication and dosages, compatible with physicians' orders.

tasks.label: Inspect, clean, test, and maintain respiratory therapy equipment to ensure equipment is functioning safely and efficiently, ordering repairs when necessary.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Bedside rounds in an occupied ICU/med-surg room: with the patient connected, the RT checks the running ventilator (settings, alarms, graphics, exhalation valve), drains condensate and inspects the circuit for leaks/disconnects, tops up the humidifier chamber, verifies O2 flowmeter, suction regulator and cylinder pressure, swaps out a suspect device, tags it and files a repair request. Cluttered room with lines, furniture and family present.

Equipment/clean-utility room preparation and pre-use verification: retrieve a ventilator, BiPAP or high-flow unit from storage, install patient circuit, HME/filters and humidifier, attach test lung, run the machine's self-test/leak and compliance checks, verify alarms and battery, wipe the chassis, apply a 'ready for use' tag and log it; same for transport ventilators, resuscitation bags and cylinders.

Cleaning, disinfection and reprocessing of reusable respiratory equipment between patients: strip and discard used circuits, wipe/disinfect device surfaces, disassemble masks, non-disposable circuits, resuscitation bags, PFT valves and mouthpieces, deliver them to reprocessing, run and verify washer-disinfector or pasteurizer cycles, inspect for damage, reassemble and restock.

Point-of-care/blood gas laboratory: perform and document scheduled calibration and quality control on blood gas and co-oximetry analyzers, verify QC results against ranges, and flag out-of-control instruments for service.

Pulmonary function lab / bench verification: 3-L syringe volume calibration and leak checks on spirometers and body plethysmographs, verification of capnographs, oximeters and flow sensors against test lungs and gas-flow analyzers, with documentation and repair requests.

Home care / DME field visit: in a patient's residence, inspect and clean a home ventilator, CPAP/BiPAP or oxygen concentrator, change filters and water chambers, verify pressures and alarms, download compliance data, and arrange repair or replacement. Layout, clutter, pets and cleanliness vary house to house.

sources.system: Automation NTH FLEXBASE automated assembly cell (Hamilton Medical flow sensor tubes)
sources.title: Therapeutic Device Assembly - Ventilation Technology - Automation Nth
sources.claim: Automation NTH built a fully guarded, fully automated cleanroom assembly cell for Hamilton Medical's ventilator flow-sensor tube assemblies: robots and intelligent feeders handle coiled flexible medical tubing, apply adhesive, and AI vision confirms proper tube insertion and label correctness, with under 1% rejects at a 10-second cycle.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: factory assembly and vision verification of ventilator breathing-tubing assemblies. It transfers to RT equipment prep because the objects are the same class (flexible respiratory tubing, connectors, flow sensors), the precision is comparable (vision-verified insertion of tube into port), and it runs in a purpose-built guarded cell, which is exactly the E1 counterfactual.

sources.system: Staubli TX2-90 / TS2-60 ventilator HME filter production cell
sources.title: Manufacturing a vital component for ventilators | Staubli
sources.claim: A two-robot cleanroom cell built by MGA Technologies/Infiplast with Staubli robots assembles ventilator HME filter housings from molded parts, ultrasonically welds them, then presents them for functional testing and labelling and sorts compliant from non-compliant parts.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: assembling, functionally testing and pass/fail-sorting a respiratory-circuit component. The objects (HME filters, circuit housings) are the same consumables an RT installs and checks, and the accept/reject-and-label step mirrors 'test, then tag ready-for-use or send for repair' inside a purpose-built cell.

sources.system: Tessy Automation / Epson robotic assembly and test line
sources.developer: Tessy Automation (Tessy Plastics) with Epson robots
sources.title: Robots Automate Assembly, Testing of Medical Devices | ASSEMBLY
sources.claim: Tessy Automation built a fully automatic 31-foot line using Epson SCARA and six-axis robots that assembles a critical-care blood-flow measuring device and performs two in-line functional quality tests (torque and flow) before unloading finished assemblies.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robot-fed in-line functional (flow) testing of a critical-care device with automatic pass/fail. It transfers to 'test respiratory equipment' because the measurement class (flow/pressure verification against limits) and the fixtured presentation match a bench pre-use or calibration check.

sources.system: SDC (Steven Douglas Corp.) medical tube handling and assembly machine
sources.title: Custom Medical Tube Handling & Robotic Assembly Solutions - SDC
sources.claim: A purpose-built cell with three 6-axis FANUC robots automatically feeds, cuts, clamps and assembles extruded medical tubing to ports, with machine-vision incoming inspection, tube-length verification and sensor-based error proofing that segregates failed parts.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic manipulation of floppy extruded medical tubing into ports plus vision inspection. This is the hardest manipulation element of assembling and inspecting a breathing circuit, demonstrated at production reliability in a fixtured cell.

sources.system: SteelcoBelimed ATS Automatic Transfer System and R-APPIT packing robot
sources.title: Automation - SteelcoBelimed
sources.claim: Commercial hospital central sterile processing lines use automatic loading conveyors and an ATS shuttle that autonomously moves wash carts into free washer-disinfectors or sterilizers, plus an R-APPIT packing robot that wraps, tapes and labels processed trays.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: mechanized handling and machine cleaning/disinfection of reusable medical devices in a reprocessing line. The reusable respiratory items an RT cleans (masks, non-disposable circuits, bags, valves) are processed on the same racked-cart, validated-cycle equipment.

sources.title: What is a Medical Washer-Disinfector? Learn More | STERIS
sources.claim: Medical washer-disinfectors perform the cleaning and thermal disinfection of reusable medical devices automatically once racks are loaded, running OEM-validated pre-programmed cycles.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated cleaning/disinfection of reusable devices. It is the same physical operation an RT relies on for respiratory accessories, and the machine performs the cleaning itself once the work is presented in racks (the E1 presentation).

sources.system: Commercial washer-disinfector / pasteurizer for respiratory equipment
sources.title: Care, cleaning and disinfection of respiratory equipment (WHO)
sources.claim: WHO guidance on respiratory equipment states that heat-tolerant respiratory equipment is disinfected by machine, using a commercial washer-disinfector or pasteurizer rather than by manual disinfection.
sources.transferJustification: Establishes that the accepted-quality cleaning modality for the exact objects in this task (respiratory equipment) is an automated machine cycle, so the cited reprocessing automation applies to respiratory items and not only to surgical instruments.

sources.system: Siemens Healthineers RAPIDPoint 500/500e blood gas system
sources.title: RAPIDPoint 500 Systems - Siemens Healthineers
sources.claim: Point-of-care blood gas analyzers deployed in hospitals run their calibration and quality control automatically on a schedule with onboard QC and no operator involvement; the cartridge-based system is described as maintenance-free with a self-cleaning probe.

sources.title: Hopkins researchers develop a robotic system to remotely control ventilators
sources.claim: A robot built at Johns Hopkins to let clinicians operate ventilator touchscreens from outside patient rooms is remotely controlled by the respiratory therapist through a tablet, not autonomous.

sources.title: Swisslog Healthcare Partners with Diligent Robotics to Enhance Hospital Logistics
sources.claim: The largest deployed fleet of hospital mobile manipulators, Diligent Robotics' Moxi, performs autonomous fetch-and-deliver logistics in more than 25 US ...; its demonstrated work is transport of supplies and specimens, not inspection, testing or servicing of clinical equipment.

sources.system: Autonomous wiping and UV-C disinfection robot
sources.developer: Korea Institute of Machinery and Materials (research team)
sources.title: Transforming hospital sanitation: Autonomous robots for wiping and UV-C disinfection | ScienceDaily
sources.claim: A research team demonstrated an autonomous hospital sanitation robot that navigates and uses a manipulator to physically wipe surfaces plus UV-C for corners; it addresses surface disinfection only, not disassembly, cleaning or functional testing of clinical devices.

tasks.label: Perform bronchopulmonary drainage and assist or instruct patients in performance of breathing exercises.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Adult medical/surgical inpatient ward: RT performs chest physiotherapy on a cooperative patient with pneumonia, atelectasis or bronchiectasis — auscultates, positions the patient in postural drainage postures in the hospital bed (side-lying, head-down), manually percusses and vibrates the affected lung segments for several minutes each, coaches huff/cough, re-auscultates and documents. Patient may be on nasal oxygen and have IV lines.

ICU: sedated or ventilated patient with retained secretions — RT coordinates with nursing to turn the patient (endotracheal tube, central lines, drains, pressors), delivers percussion/vibration to dependent segments, monitors SpO2, ventilator pressures and hemodynamics for intolerance, then suctions the endotracheal tube to remove mobilized secretions and reassesses.

Mechanical airway-clearance session: RT fits a high-frequency chest wall oscillation vest onto the patient (or sets up intrapulmonary percussive ventilation / mechanical insufflation-exsufflation), connects hoses/circuit, selects frequency, pressure and duration, stays with the patient through the 20-30 minute session with cough breaks, then removes and cleans equipment. Ward, pediatric unit or outpatient clinic.

Post-operative or medical inpatient at the bedside: RT instructs and assists with breathing exercises — raises the patient upright, hands over and demonstrates the incentive spirometer, guides sustained maximal inspirations, places the patient's hands for diaphragmatic breathing, provides a splinting pillow for cough, verifies volumes and technique, sets hourly goals and documents.

Outpatient pulmonary clinic or pulmonary rehabilitation program: RT teaches and coaches a COPD/asthma patient (individually or in a small group) in pursed-lip and diaphragmatic breathing, paced breathing, huff coughing and inspiratory muscle training — demonstrating, observing and correcting technique, checking SpO2/dyspnea response, and reinforcing over repeated sessions.

Home-care visit (cystic fibrosis, neuromuscular disease, tracheostomy or pediatric patient): RT works in the family's home, performing manual CPT in whatever furniture and space are available and teaching the patient and caregivers to perform percussion/drainage positions, use of the vest or cough assist, and breathing exercises.

sources.system: Intelligent percussion-based sputum clearance robot (robotic arm with damped vibrating percussion head, Kinect perception, admittance force control)
sources.developer: Chen Diansheng et al., Beihang University / Hunan Intelligent Rehabilitation Robot and Auxiliary Equipment Engineering Technology Research Center (China)
sources.title: Design and Implementation of an Intelligent Percussion-Based Sputum Clearance Robot — Chinese Journal of Mechanical Engineering
sources.claim: A research prototype robot autonomously detects the anatomy of a patient's back (posture recognition, segmentation, spine/scapula exclusion), plans a percussion path following the clinical 'outside-to-inside, bottom-to-top' rule, and applies force-controlled vibratory percussion for sputum clearance; tested in the laboratory and in the ICU of Shengjing Hospital.

sources.system: TotalCare SpO2RT 2 ICU Bed (CLRT + Percussion & Vibration module)
sources.title: TotalCare SpO2RT 2 ICU Bed | Hillrom
sources.claim: Commercially sold ICU beds automatically rotate the patient side to side into drainage postures (continuous lateral rotation therapy) and deliver programmed percussion and vibration therapy to the thorax; the clinician sets angle, frequency, intensity and duration and the bed then runs the therapy cycles on the patient unattended.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: machine-delivered bronchopulmonary drainage. The bed reproduces the two physical acts of the RT's chest physiotherapy — placing the thorax in drainage positions and applying percussion/vibration to the chest wall — on the same patients, with the patient fixtured in the machine.

sources.title: Baxter Launches Progressa+ Next Gen ICU Bed to Help Address Complex Critical Care Needs
sources.claim: The successor critical-care bed with in-bed percussion, vibration and continuous lateral rotation therapy has been launched commercially and is in use in US hospitals; a vendor survey covered 60 clinicians using it in four US facilities.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: machine-delivered chest percussion/vibration and postural drainage. Same physical act on the same body region as manual CPT, delivered to hospital inpatients as an accepted substitute for hand percussion.

sources.title: Massage Envy Introduces Aescape Robotic Massage at Select Franchised Locations
sources.claim: An autonomous two-armed robotic table performs full-body massage, including force-controlled deep-tissue work on the posterior torso of a person lying prone, and is deployed commercially at fitness clubs, spa/recovery studios, hotels and massage franchise locations.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous, force-limited robotic manipulation of the human back on a purpose-built table. Shows that scanning a person's back and applying repeated controlled mechanical force at commercial reliability and safety is a fielded capability — the same contact regime as chest percussion/vibration when the patient is presented to the machine.

sources.system: NAO-based socially assistive robot with sensor interface (heart rate, gait)
sources.developer: University of Hertfordshire / Fundación Cardioinfantil-Instituto de Cardiología (Bogotá)
sources.title: A Socially Assistive Robot for Long-Term Cardiac Rehabilitation in the Real World — Frontiers in Neurorobotics
sources.claim: A fully autonomous socially assistive humanoid robot was deployed for 2.5 years in the outpatient cardiac rehabilitation programme of a cardiology clinic, guiding and continuously monitoring patients through 36-session exercise programmes with immediate sensor-based feedback; adherence and recovery heart rate were better than conventional staff-run sessions.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robot-delivered instruction, pacing and monitoring of a prescribed therapeutic exercise session for cardiopulmonary patients in a clinic. Comparable to coaching breathing exercises — demonstration, cueing, physiological monitoring and corrective feedback — with the patient stationed at an exercise position.

sources.developer: Yujin Robot / University of Auckland (Broadbent et al.)
sources.title: Using Robots at Home to Support Patients With Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease: Pilot Randomized Controlled Trial (JMIR)
sources.claim: In a randomized controlled trial, an autonomous tabletop home robot programmed with a COPD clinical pathway prompted and guided patients through rehabilitation exercises and inhaler/medication use and measured pulse oximetry and spirometry weekly at home; it improved medication adherence and exercise frequency but did not reduce hospitalizations.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: machine-delivered respiratory self-management coaching (exercise prompting, inhaler technique, oximetry/FEV monitoring) to COPD patients. Bears on instructing breathing exercises, but it only reminded and played videos — it did not observe or correct technique.

tasks.label: Demonstrate respiratory care procedures to trainees or other healthcare personnel.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Bedside teaching in a hospital ICU/step-down unit: the RT demonstrates a procedure on an actual ventilated patient to an RT student, new-hire RT, or ICU nurse — e.g., in-line endotracheal suctioning, ventilator circuit change, cuff-pressure check, mode/parameter adjustment on a Servo-U or Puritan Bennett vent — narrating rationale, maintaining sterile technique, watching the patient's tolerance, and answering questions in real time.

Skills-lab / simulation-center demonstration on a high-fidelity manikin during an in-service or student rotation: bag-valve-mask ventilation, intubation assist, tracheostomy care and tube change, ABG puncture on a simulated arm; the RT performs each step slowly, breaks it down, then coaches the learner through a return demonstration and corrects hand position and technique.

Unit-based equipment in-service to nursing/other staff on the floor: demonstrating assembly and correct use of high-flow nasal cannula, BiPAP/CPAP mask fitting and leak correction, nebulizer and MDI-with-spacer technique, oxygen delivery devices, and portable suction — often improvised at a nurses' station or empty patient room with the actual device.

Classroom/laboratory teaching in a respiratory therapy degree program (RT serving as clinical instructor or lab adjunct): demonstrating pulmonary function testing, chest physiotherapy/postural drainage, blood-gas analyzer operation, and equipment troubleshooting to a group of students, with hands-on supervision of student practice.

Home-care or long-term-care setting: RT demonstrates home ventilator, tracheostomy suctioning, or CPAP/oxygen concentrator operation and troubleshooting to home-health nurses, aides, or family caregivers in the patient's residence, adapting to the home's layout, clutter, pets, and the specific device the patient owns.

sources.system: Unitree G1 humanoid with bimanual teleoperation system (UCSD ARCLab / UCSD Health)
sources.developer: UC San Diego (Atar, Liang, Joyce, Richter, Yip) with UCSD School of Medicine clinicians
sources.title: Humanoids in Hospitals: A Technical Study of Humanoid Surrogates for Dexterous Medical Interventions
sources.claim: The most advanced demonstration of a humanoid robot performing respiratory-care-type procedures (bag-valve-mask ventilation, endotracheal intubation, tracheostomy) uses full bimanual teleoperation by a human operator, not autonomy, and reports remaining force and sensing limitations.
sources.transferJustification: Closest available related task: a robot physically performing airway/ventilation procedures with clinical tools. It does not transfer to autonomous demonstration because every trial was human-teleoperated and confined to lab manikin scenarios.

sources.title: Serve Robotics to Acquire Diligent Robotics, Expanding Physical AI Platform Beyond the Sidewalk
sources.claim: The largest fleet of autonomous hospital robots performs only materials logistics — fetching and delivering medications, lab samples and supplies through hospital corridors — not clinical procedures or staff instruction.
sources.transferJustification: Related task is autonomous mobile manipulation inside the same E2 setting (hospital units). It establishes what autonomy in hospitals currently covers — delivery and simple pick-and-place — and does not extend to performing or teaching respiratory procedures.

sources.title: Hopkins researchers develop a robotic system to remotely control ventilators
sources.claim: Even the narrow sub-step of adjusting ventilator settings by robot is implemented as a teleoperated screen-tapping device remotely driven by the respiratory therapist, not an autonomous system.
sources.transferJustification: Related task is direct manipulation of ICU ventilator controls, a core element of what an RT would demonstrate. It cannot support a positive judgment because a human RT drives every action remotely.

sources.system: The Swab Robot (UR5-based fully automatic throat swab robot)
sources.title: Case study on force compliant robot arm controller for nasopharyngeal swab insertion
sources.claim: Autonomous robotic manipulation near the human airway exists only as a single narrow motion (oropharyngeal/nasopharyngeal swabbing) with a dedicated fixture and head-positioning setup, far short of multi-step respiratory care procedures.
sources.transferJustification: Related task is autonomous instrument insertion into a human airway. It does not transfer: it is one scripted insertion with the head fixtured, with no equipment assembly, no patient assessment, and no instructional interaction with a learner.

tasks.label: Perform pulmonary function and adjust equipment to obtain optimum results in therapy.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Hospital ICU, invasively ventilated adult: RT assesses respiratory mechanics and gas exchange (plateau pressure, compliance, driving pressure, SpO2, etCO2, ABG) and titrates ventilator settings - FiO2, PEEP, tidal volume/pressure support, rate - toward lung-protective and weaning targets across the shift, including spontaneous-breathing-trial readiness.

Hospital ward/ED/ICU patient already on nasal cannula or simple mask oxygen: RT monitors saturation and repeatedly adjusts oxygen flow to hold SpO2 in the ordered target range, weaning flow down as the patient improves and increasing it during desaturation episodes.

Bedside aerosol and airway-clearance therapy: RT assembles nebulizer/MDI-spacer/IPPB/high-frequency chest wall oscillation equipment, charges the drug, applies the mouthpiece or face mask to the patient, sets and adjusts flow/pressure/frequency, then assesses response (auscultation, peak flow, work of breathing) and re-adjusts device or interface.

Pulmonary function laboratory study on an ambulatory patient: verify daily calibration with a 3-L syringe/biologic control, seat and posture the patient, attach filter/mouthpiece and nose clips, vigorously coach repeated maximal FVC, lung-volume and DLCO maneuvers until ATS/ERS acceptability and repeatability criteria are met, administer bronchodilator and repeat.

Bedside pulmonary function measures on a non-ventilated inpatient or pre-op patient: bedside spirometry, peak flow, vital capacity and MIP/NIF with a manometer; coach patient effort, maintain the mouthpiece/mask seal, and adjust therapy (incentive spirometer goal, oxygen device) based on the values obtained.

Initiating and titrating noninvasive ventilation/CPAP-BiPAP at the hospital bedside or in a sleep lab (a minority of these visits occur in the patient's home for home-care/DME patients): select and fit the interface, adjust straps to control leak and skin pressure, set and titrate IPAP/EPAP/backup rate and humidification, and confirm synchrony and comfort.

sources.title: Closed-loop ventilation mode (IntelliVent-ASV) in intensive care unit: a randomized trial - PubMed
sources.claim: INTELLiVENT-ASV, a fully closed-loop mode on commercial Hamilton ICU ventilators, automatically selects and continuously adjusts ventilation and oxygenation settings; in a randomized ICU trial it needed far fewer manual adjustments than conventional ventilation with comparable efficacy and safety.

sources.title: INTELLiVENT-ASV Intelligent ventilation mode | Hamilton Medical
sources.claim: INTELLiVENT-ASV is a shipping commercial option or standard mode across Hamilton's ICU and transport ventilator line, i.e. deployed hospital equipment rather than a research prototype.

sources.developer: Hamilton Medical / Sainte Musse Hospital Toulon
sources.title: Feasibility study on full closed-loop control ventilation (IntelliVent-ASV) in ICU patients with acute respiratory failure
sources.claim: In 100 consecutive unselected ICU patients with acute respiratory failure, the closed-loop ventilator ran the patient's ventilation and oxygenation settings autonomously from enrollment through extubation, with safety events and need to revert to conventional modes tracked.

sources.title: Automatic oxygen flow titration in spontaneously breathing children: An open-label randomized controlled pilot study - PubMed
sources.claim: FreeO2, a closed-loop oxygen titration device, autonomously adjusts oxygen flow to a spontaneously breathing patient from continuous SpO2 and keeps saturation in the prescribed target range better than manual titration by clinicians (randomized trial).

sources.title: Oxygen Therapy Innovation: OxyNov's FreeO2 Device Goes National
sources.claim: FreeO2 is a regulator-approved product in routine hospital use (Quebec, then Canada-wide from 2024), continuously adjusting prescribed oxygen flow to hold patients in the SpO2 target range.

sources.title: Automated oxygen control with O2matic during admission with exacerbation of COPD - PMC
sources.claim: O2matic, a CE-marked closed-loop oxygen controller, autonomously titrated ward oxygen for admitted COPD patients and held SpO2 in the target interval far more of the time than manual control by nursing staff.

sources.system: Automatic Swab Robot (Lifeline Robotics, UR3/UR5 arms)
sources.developer: Lifeline Robotics / University of Southern Denmark
sources.title: Throat swabbing robot developed for COVID-19 testing by Danish startup
sources.claim: An autonomous two-arm robot performs oropharyngeal swabbing: the patient rests their head in a fixed rest, the robot picks up the ..., uses vision to find the swab target in the mouth, swabs, and caps the sample jar.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: instrument-to-mouth patient contact at a purpose-built station, the closest demonstrated analogue to placing a spirometer mouthpiece. Transfer is only partial - it shows tool placement but not nose-clip application, coaching of maximal forced efforts, or judging ATS/ERS maneuver acceptability, which determine whether a pulmonary function study is usable.

tasks.label: Educate patients and their families about their conditions and teach appropriate disease management techniques, such as breathing exercises or the use of medications or respiratory equipment.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

tasks.label: Conduct tests, such as electrocardiograms (EKGs), stress testing, or lung capacity tests, to evaluate patients' cardiopulmonary functions.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Full pulmonary function study in a hospital or outpatient PFT lab: verify orders and patient ID, measure height/weight, seat the patient, hand and seal the mouthpiece and apply a nose clip, coach loud forceful spirometry maneuvers to ATS/ERS acceptability and repeatability, close the body-box door for lung volumes, run DLCO with breath-hold, administer bronchodilator and repeat, reject artifactual efforts and report.

12-lead resting EKG at the bedside or in a clinic room: identify patient, expose and prep the chest (wipe/shave, position breast tissue), palpate landmarks to place six precordial and four limb electrodes, connect lead wires, quiet the patient, obtain an artifact-free tracing, re-run if wandering baseline or lead reversal, remove electrodes and route the tracing.

Bedside lung-capacity/respiratory-mechanics measurement on an inpatient or ICU patient: bedside spirometry, vital capacity, negative inspiratory force/MIP via a mask or in-line adapter on a ventilator circuit or tracheostomy, with a weak, sedated, or poorly cooperative patient, coordinating with the ventilator and monitoring for desaturation.

Exercise-based cardiopulmonary evaluation in a hospital lab: treadmill/cycle EKG stress test or CPET — skin prep and stress-lead placement, fitting a face mask or mouthpiece with nose clip, serial blood-pressure and rhythm monitoring during exercise, coaching effort, watching for symptoms/arrhythmia and stopping the test, plus recovery monitoring; includes six-minute walk tests with pulse oximetry.

Testing outside a controlled facility: home-care or mobile visits for portable spirometry, peak-flow/oximetry hookups, or worksite/occupational-health screening spirometry — layout differs at every site, patient positioning improvised on household furniture, pets and family present, variable lighting and power.

sources.title: Vitestro's robotic blood drawing device meets trial endpoints
sources.claim: Vitestro's autonomous robotic phlebotomy device performs venipuncture on patients whose arm is placed in a purpose-built cradle, using imaging guidance, and met a 95% first-stick endpoint in a multicenter trial — the closest existing case of an autonomous robot performing a patient-contact clinical procedure.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: an autonomous robot acting on a patient's body in a clinical setting. Transfer fails for this task — the device handles one needle insertion into a fixtured forearm and does not place multiple adhesive electrodes by palpated thoracic landmarks, fit mouthpieces/nose clips, or coach and grade forced-expiratory maneuvers, so it does not substantiate completion of an EKG or lung-capacity test even in a purpose-built setting.

sources.system: auto-RUSS (7-DOF arm with force control and ultrasound visual servoing)
sources.developer: First Affiliated Hospital of Sun Yat-Sen University / collaborators
sources.title: Autonomous robotic ultrasound scanning system: a key to enhancing image analysis reproducibility and observer consistency in ultrasound imaging
sources.claim: A force-controlled autonomous robotic ultrasound scanning system ... () performed repeated autonomous scans of a human volunteer's thyroid in a research/hospital lab, showing autonomous, landmark-guided contact of a sensor with a person's body surface.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous placement and sliding of a sensor on a patient's skin under force control. Transfer fails: the demonstration is a single probe on a supine volunteer's neck in a lab, with no handling of peel-and-stick electrodes, no chest-landmark palpation, no patient instruction or effort grading, and no complete diagnostic study delivered to clinical standard.

sources.title: Study: Robotic Arm Can be Used for Remote Echocardiograms
sources.claim: Robotic systems actually used for cardiopulmonary diagnostics on patients in hospitals are remotely operated by a clinician, not autonomous: a 5G robotic-arm echocardiography system examined 51 outpatient cardiology patients under remote human control.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robot-performed cardiopulmonary diagnostic examination on patients in a clinic. It cannot support a positive judgment because the robot is continuously teleoperated by a sonographer, which the rating rules exclude.

sources.developer: Lifeline Robotics (University of Southern Denmark spin-off)
sources.title: Throat swabbing robot developed for COVID-19 testing by Danish startup
sources.claim: Lifeline Robotics built an automatic throat-swab robot that autonomously collects an oropharyngeal sample from a seated person, illustrating that autonomous robot-patient procedures remain single, tightly constrained contact actions.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous robot performing a patient-contact diagnostic sampling procedure with the patient's head held in a fixed position. Transfer fails for cardiopulmonary testing, which requires multi-site electrode placement, deformable-object handling, verbal coaching of maximal respiratory effort, and real-time judgment of test acceptability — none demonstrated.

sources.title: Could AI nursing robots help healthcare staffing shortages?
sources.claim: Robots deployed in hospitals today are logistics and guidance platforms (supply and specimen delivery, ward navigation, patient guidance); no deployed hospital robot conducts diagnostic cardiopulmonary testing on patients.
sources.transferJustification: Same environment (hospital wards, an E2 setting) but a different task: delivery and guidance rather than patient testing; cited to show the deployed state of hospital robotics does not include conducting EKGs, spirometry, or stress tests.

tasks.label: Perform endotracheal intubation to maintain open airways for patients who are unable to breathe on their own.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Emergency department resuscitation/trauma bay: RT performs rapid-sequence intubation of a crashing adult (hypoxia, hypotension, possible C-collar, blood/secretions in airway), using video or direct laryngoscopy, with a code team crowding the bed; must confirm placement by waveform capnography and secure the tube within seconds-to-a-minute.

ICU bedside: elective/semi-urgent intubation of a critically ill adult in acute hypoxemic or hypercapnic respiratory failure; patient pre-oxygenated and sedated/paralyzed by the team, RT laryngoscopes, passes a 7.0-8.0 ETT, confirms depth, inflates cuff, secures tube and connects to the ventilator.

In-hospital code blue on a general ward or during intrahospital transport: cardiac arrest with ongoing chest compressions, patient in a hospital bed or on the floor, vomit/secretions present, intubation performed between compression cycles.

Neonatal/pediatric intubation in the delivery room, NICU, or PICU: 2.5-3.5 mm uncuffed tube in a preterm or term newborn, millimetre-level depth tolerance, Miller blade, often during resuscitation with an unstable, moving infant.

Anticipated or encountered difficult airway in the OR/ICU: obese or anatomically difficult patient, limited mouth opening or neck movement, blood/emesis obscuring the view; requires bougie, stylet manipulation, external laryngeal manipulation, or rescue supraglottic device before successful tube placement.

Transport/field intubation by an RT on a critical-care transport or flight team: patient at a referring bedside, in an ambulance or helicopter, cramped and moving space, limited lighting and positioning, non-standard equipment layout.

sources.developer: Thomas M. Hemmerling / McGill University Health Centre
sources.title: First robotic tracheal intubations in humans using the Kepler intubation system, BJA
sources.claim: The Kepler Intubation System is a joystick-teleoperated robotic arm holding a video laryngoscope; it performed the first robotic oral tracheal intubations in 12 anesthetized elective surgical patients in an operating room, with 91% success and a human assistant required to open the mouth.

sources.developer: UC Santa Barbara (Haggerty, Hawkes) with Vine Medical and collaborators
sources.title: UCSB-designed soft robot intubation device could save lives (The Current, UCSB)
sources.claim: The soft robotic intubation system (SRIS) is a hand-held, electronics-free everting-tube device that self-guides an endotracheal tube; it was tested only in manikins and cadavers, is operated throughout by a human clinician or EMT, and has not yet entered clinical trials or FDA clearance.

sources.developer: Chinese academic group (Int J Comput Assist Radiol Surg)
sources.title: A robot-assisted tracheal intubation system based on a soft actuator (PubMed)
sources.claim: A robot-assisted tracheal intubation system using a soft actuator performed automated intubation, but validation was limited to a benchtop airway manikin; no live-patient use is reported.

sources.system: Autonomous Robotic AI-Guided Endotracheal Intubation device
sources.developer: William Gormley, Brigham and Women's Hospital / Mass General Brigham
sources.title: Portable AI-Guided Intubation Device Advances with Brigham Ignite Support
sources.claim: An autonomous AI-guided robotic intubation device intended for emergency airways outside the clinic remains at the prototype stage at Brigham and Women's Hospital as of early 2025, with no patient use reported.

tasks.label: Teach, train, supervise, or use the assistance of students, respiratory therapy technicians, or assistants.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Bedside clinical supervision of a respiratory therapy student or new technician during ICU/floor rounds: watching the trainee perform ventilator checks, suctioning, or aerosol therapy, asking questions, correcting technique verbally, and co-signing the trainee's documentation. Output is the trainee's demonstrated competence and an approved chart entry.

Delegating and overseeing assistance: assigning routine therapies (nebulizer treatments, incentive spirometry, equipment stocking, transports) to a technician or assistant across the shift, prioritizing the workload, answering questions by phone/in person, and verifying the work was done and charted.

Formal in-service or competency training in a hospital classroom/skills lab on new equipment (e.g., a new ventilator, HFNC, or transport device), including a demonstration on a test lung or manikin, a return-demonstration by staff, and signing off competency checklists.

Preceptorship of a newly hired therapist over an orientation period on the unit: planning the assignment mix, progressively releasing responsibility, giving feedback, and completing written performance evaluations for the department manager.
Serving as clinical/didactic faculty or guest instructor for a respiratory therapy degree program: lecturing, running lab practice on simulators, and grading student clinical performance evaluations.

tasks.label: Use a variety of testing techniques to assist doctors in cardiac or pulmonary research or to diagnose disorders.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Arterial blood gas draw at the bedside in an ICU, ED, or ward: RT verifies the order, performs a modified Allen test, palpates and punctures the radial artery of a possibly edematous, hypotensive, agitated or ventilated patient with a heparinized syringe, expels air, caps and labels the sample, holds pressure ~5 minutes for hemostasis, then runs the sample on a blood gas analyzer and reports results with FiO2 and vent settings.

Full pulmonary function lab session: RT registers the patient, measures height/weight, explains and demonstrates the maneuver, applies mouthpiece and nose clip, forcefully coaches repeated FVC/FEV1 efforts to ATS/ERS acceptability and repeatability, seats the patient in a body plethysmograph or performs helium dilution for lung volumes, runs single-breath DLCO, administers bronchodilator via MDI/spacer, repeats post-bronchodilator testing, and flags unacceptable trials.

Bedside or clinic spirometry and bedside diagnostic measures: pre/post-bronchodilator screening spirometry in a pulmonary clinic or on a hospital ward, peak flow, negative inspiratory force and vital capacity measurement on a weaning or neuromuscular patient, cuff-leak test, capnography check - coaching an ill or poorly cooperative patient through effort-dependent maneuvers at the bedside.

Exercise-based cardiopulmonary testing: RT preps and places ECG electrodes on the chest, applies BP cuff, pulse oximeter and mask/mouthpiece headgear, calibrates the metabolic cart, runs a treadmill/cycle CPET or a six-minute walk test, monitors SpO2, ECG and Borg dyspnea scores, and stops the test for symptoms or desaturation.

Assisting a physician with diagnostic bronchoscopy: setting up and checking the scope, suction and monitoring equipment, positioning the patient, managing oxygen and sedation monitoring, suctioning and instilling lavage aliquots, handling and labeling BAL/biopsy specimens, and responding to desaturation or bleeding.

Sleep-lab or research protocol data collection: applying polysomnography electrodes, belts, cannula and oximeter and monitoring overnight, or collecting research data for a physician study (metabolic cart measurements, exhaled nitric oxide, walk tests, arterial sampling at protocol time points) with strict protocol documentation.

sources.title: Robotic Phlebotomy Study Signals Automation Shift for Clinical Labs - Dark Daily
sources.claim: Vitestro's Aletta is an autonomous robotic ... that images veins and performs venipuncture without an operator guiding the needle; a multicenter trial in outpatient phlebotomy rooms reported near-human first-stick success. It performs venous draws only, not arterial puncture, and does not coach patients through respiratory maneuvers.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous venous blood sampling on seated outpatients. It is the closest demonstrated patient-contact sampling robot, but transfer to the RT task fails: arterial blood gas puncture targets a deep pulsatile vessel (Doppler in such devices is used to avoid arteries), uses a heparinized syringe with air expulsion and immediate transport, is performed on ICU/ED patients in beds rather than in a fixtured draw chair, and requires several minutes of manual compression for hemostasis.

sources.system: Autonomous swab robot (naso- and oropharyngeal sampling)
sources.developer: Chinese university research group (published in Scientific Reports)
sources.title: Autonomous swab robot for naso- and oropharyngeal COVID-19 screening | Scientific Reports
sources.claim: An autonomous naso-/oropharyngeal swab robot completed sampling on volunteers and patients in clinical studies, showing robots can autonomously contact a cooperative seated patient to collect a diagnostic specimen, but only for a shallow, low-risk, single-motion sample.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous patient-contact specimen collection in a screening booth. It shows contact with a cooperative patient is feasible, but it does not transfer to arterial puncture, effort-coached spirometry/DLCO, multi-sensor montages, or bronchoscopy assistance, which require multi-step manipulation, active patient coaching, and real-time clinical judgment.

sources.system: Contemporary humanoid robots evaluated for surgical tasks
sources.title: In vivo feasibility study of humanoid robots in surgery | Nature
sources.claim: State-of-the-art humanoid robots performing clinical/surgical manipulation tasks in vivo do so under teleoperation, not autonomously, and are described as pre-clinical.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robot performance of skilled procedural clinical manipulation alongside clinicians. It is the most general test of whether a general-purpose robot could stand in for an RT during procedures such as bronchoscopy assistance; the result is that such work remains teleoperated, so it cannot support a positive judgment.

sources.title: Current Status and Pending Developments of Robotic Tele-Echocardiography | JACC: Cardiovascular Imaging
sources.claim: Robotic cardiac ultrasound systems used on patients are remote/teleoperated reproductions of a sonographer's hand motions; fully autonomous robot-assisted scanning remains prospective.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic cardiopulmonary diagnostic testing performed on a patient's body. It is the closest analogue to a robot conducting a cardiac diagnostic test; the evidence shows these systems remain human-driven, so they cannot substantiate autonomous completion of the RT's testing instances.

sources.title: Portable PFT Machine | Lung Volume & DLCO Testing | PulmOne
sources.claim: Commercial 'fully automatic' pulmonary function systems automate gas analysis and computation, but the test must still be administered to the patient by a staff member; no robot applies the mouthpiece/nose clip or coaches the forced maneuver.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated pulmonary function measurement. It is an instrument rather than a robotic system - it does not act on the patient - and the vendor's own description presumes a human staff member conducts the test, confirming the physical and coaching portion of PFT is not automated.

tasks.label: Monitor cardiac patients, using electrocardiography devices, such as a holter monitor.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: ICU/critical-care bedside: RT caring for a ventilated patient applies or replaces 3-/5-lead ECG electrodes on a diaphoretic, hairy, edematous chest crowded with lines and dressings, connects leads to the bedside monitor, clears lead-off and artifact alarms, watches the rhythm during suctioning/vent changes, and escalates arrhythmias to the team.

Ward or ED 12-lead ECG: RT takes the cart to the bedside, exposes and preps the chest (wipe, shave if needed), palpates intercostal spaces and places 10 electrodes at correct anatomic landmarks, acquires an artifact-free tracing on a possibly restless patient, verifies quality, and delivers/uploads it for physician read.

Emergency/transport: during a code, intubation, or intra-hospital transport, RT rapidly attaches monitor/defib electrodes and leads to a moving or uncooperative patient, keeps the rhythm visible on the transport monitor en route, manages cables and reattaches lost leads, and responds to rhythm changes.

Cardiopulmonary diagnostic lab: RT hooks up ECG leads for an exercise stress test, 6-minute walk, or sleep/PFT study, keeps electrodes adherent during exertion and movement, continuously monitors rate and rhythm, and halts the test for ischemic changes or dangerous arrhythmias.

Outpatient/ambulatory monitoring clinic: RT preps skin, applies Holter/event-monitor electrodes and recorder, secures wires and instructs the patient on the diary and care of the device; later removes the device, downloads and scans the recording, and flags findings.

sources.title: Performance, Safety, and Patient Experience of an Autonomous Robotic Phlebotomy Device: A Multicenter Trial
sources.claim: Vitestro's Aletta is an autonomous robotic ... evaluated in a multicenter clinical trial with a 94.5% first-stick success rate; it performs a precise patient-contact procedure on a fixtured arm in blood-collection settings. It is the closest autonomous patient-contact clinical robot but does not handle adhesive ECG electrodes, torso landmarking, or rhythm monitoring.
sources.transferJustification: Related task (venipuncture) shows autonomous skin-contact procedures are feasible in clinical facilities, but the objects (single needle into a fixtured arm) and targeting differ from peeling and adhering 10 electrodes at torso landmarks, snapping lead wires, troubleshooting artifact, and continuously monitoring rhythm; capability does not transfer.

sources.title: Humanoids in Hospitals: A Technical Study of Humanoid Surrogates for Dexterous Medical Interventions
sources.claim: The only published attempt to have a humanoid robot perform bedside clinical tasks (auscultation, ventilation, ultrasound-guided needle tasks) in hospital workflows relied on teleoperation, not autonomy.
sources.transferJustification: Related task (bedside physical exam and procedures on patients) is the nearest robotic work to ECG hookup and monitoring; because it is teleoperated it cannot support a positive judgment for autonomous completion.

sources.system: Autonomous lightweight ultrasound robot for liver sonography
sources.developer: Tsinghua University / Beijing Tsinghua Changgung Hospital collaborators
sources.title: Beyond hospital reach: Autonomous lightweight ultrasound robot for liver sonography
sources.claim: An autonomous ultrasound robot performed skin-contact probe scanning on human patients in a hospital ultrasound department, showing force-controlled contact with human torsos under machine control; it images anatomy but does not apply electrodes or monitor cardiac rhythm.
sources.transferJustification: Related task (placing a sensor against a patient's torso under force control) shares the contact and anatomy-targeting element, but it involves a rigid handheld probe and no adhesive electrode handling, wire management, signal-quality troubleshooting, or continuous rhythm surveillance and clinical escalation.

sources.system: Humanoid sensing robot with leech-inspired origami (LIO) dry electrodes
sources.developer: Simon Fraser University (Woo Soo Kim lab)
sources.title: Humanoid Robots Could Reach Out and Take Patient's Blood Pressure - Robotics 24/7
sources.claim: A research humanoid with leech-inspired origami dry electrodes in its fingertips can pick up ECG and PPG signals by touching a person's fingers to estimate blood pressure; it is a laboratory prototype and autonomy of the contact procedure is not established.
sources.transferJustification: Related task (robotic acquisition of an ECG signal from a person) is the closest robotic ECG work found, but it is fingertip dry-contact in a lab, with unclear autonomy, and does not deliver clinical 12-lead or continuous cardiac monitoring.

tasks.label: Transport patients to the hospital or within the hospital.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Intra-hospital transport of a mechanically ventilated adult ICU patient to CT/MRI and back: RT gathers a transport ventilator or bag-valve device, full O2 cylinder, portable monitor and airway kit; disconnects the patient from the wall ventilator, secures the endotracheal tube and lines, pushes the ICU bed with an RN through corridors and elevators, helps slide the patient onto the scanner table, manages ventilation and alarms during the scan, then returns and reconnects the patient.

Urgent transfer of a newly intubated or unstable patient between units (ED to ICU, OR/cath lab to ICU): RT bags or ventilates the patient with a transport ventilator while the team moves the stretcher/bed quickly, suctions the airway, re-secures the tube if it migrates, and responds to desaturation or hemodynamic changes en route.

Neonatal or pediatric transport inside the hospital (delivery room to NICU, NICU to OR or imaging) with the infant in a transport isolette/warmer on CPAP, HFNC or an infant ventilator: RT sets up and monitors the tiny circuit, protects the airway, manages heat and humidity, and moves the isolette with the nursing team.

Interfacility critical-care transport as part of a ground ambulance or rotor-wing team ('transport patients to the hospital'): RT packages the patient at the sending facility, loads and secures the stretcher into the vehicle, manages ventilator, oxygen supply and airway over the road or flight in a moving, vibrating, space-constrained cabin, and hands off at the receiving hospital.

Transport of a stable, spontaneously breathing patient on low-flow supplemental oxygen within the hospital (to the pulmonary function lab, hyperbaric suite, step-down unit, or lobby for discharge): RT checks and hangs a portable O2 cylinder, transitions the patient off wall oxygen, assists the bed-to-wheelchair transfer, watches work of breathing and SpO2 en route, and re-establishes therapy at the destination.

Escort-type transport of an ambulatory, room-air patient in a wheelchair between hospital departments (e.g., moving a pulmonary clinic or PFT patient from the lab to the front entrance): the patient can sit, stand and transfer independently and needs no equipment handling or respiratory support, only safe conveyance along mapped indoor corridors.

sources.claim: WHILL's autonomous drive system is commercially deployed in US and Japanese airport terminals, autonomously carrying passengers along pre-mapped routes with collision avoidance and returning empty to base.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: conveying a seated person through a busy, institutionally controlled indoor facility. It transfers to escorting an ambulatory hospital patient by wheelchair along mapped corridors (same payload, same walking-speed navigation among pedestrians), but it presumes a passenger who transfers independently and needs no clinical equipment or monitoring.

sources.developer: WHILL Inc. / University of Tsukuba (with Mitsubishi Electric)
sources.title: Safety and feasibility of in-hospital autonomous transportation using a driverless mobility for patients with musculoskeletal disorders
sources.claim: A prospective clinical study at University of Tsukuba Hospital autonomously transported 51 outpatients with gait disturbance 100 m through hospital corridors in a WHILL driverless wheelchair with no collisions or adverse events.
sources.transferJustification: Direct evidence for conveying a seated patient inside a hospital, but only for ambulatory outpatients needing no equipment: the study excluded patients unable to walk, involved no oxygen, monitoring or transfer assistance, and covered a flat 100 m straight run without elevators.

sources.claim: The only in-hospital patient-transport robot in a US pilot, Rovex's Rovi stretcher-towing robot, was still moving empty stretchers during its BayCare pilot and had not yet moved patients; teleoperation is built in for edge cases.
sources.transferJustification: Closest system to the task (towing a hospital stretcher through corridors), cited to show the state of the art: as of mid-2026 it moves empty stretchers only, is limited by design to low-risk patients who can lie still, and provides no respiratory care.

sources.title: Swisslog Healthcare Partners with Diligent Robotics to Enhance Hospital Logistics
sources.claim: Autonomous mobile robots fielded at scale in US hospitals perform supply, lab and pharmacy deliveries, not patient movement or clinical care.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous navigation of hospital corridors and elevators at deployment scale. Navigation transfers, but the payload is supplies in a cart; nothing in the deployment involves moving a patient, handling a ventilator or oxygen, or monitoring respiratory status.

sources.developer: Johns Hopkins University and collaborators (Frontiers in Robotics and AI)
sources.title: Telerobotic Operation of Intensive Care Unit Ventilators
sources.claim: Robotic systems that operate ICU ventilators are teleoperated by a clinician from outside the room, not autonomous ventilator managers.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: machine interaction with a mechanical ventilator, the core respiratory-care element of transporting a ventilated patient. It shows the state of the art is remote human control of the ventilator interface, so it cannot support autonomous completion of a ventilated transport.

sources.transferJustification: Related task: physically transferring a patient between bed, stretcher and wheelchair, a required step in most respiratory-therapist transports. The leading system is human-guided via tactile sensors on healthy subjects, so this step is not autonomously demonstrated.

roles.description: Assess, plan, or implement fitness programs that include exercise or physical activities such as those designed to improve cardiorespiratory function, body composition, muscular strength, muscular endurance, or flexibility.

tasks.label: Explain exercise program or physiological testing procedures to participants.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

tasks.label: Provide clinical oversight of exercise for participants at all risk levels.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Phase II outpatient cardiac rehab floor in a hospital-affiliated center: exercise physiologist oversees 6-12 telemetry-monitored moderate/high-risk patients on treadmills, cycles and arm ergometers — places/troubleshoots ECG electrodes and telemetry, takes exercise and recovery blood pressures with a cuff and stethoscope, reads rhythm strips, collects RPE and symptoms, titrates workload, stops exercise and initiates emergency response (crash cart, CPR/AED) when angina, ischemic ST change, arrhythmia or hypotension appear.

Supervision of low-risk, apparently healthy or stable clients on a hospital wellness-center or corporate fitness floor: pre-session symptom/health screening, watching technique and exertion across several clients at once, spotting free-weight sets, checking HR/BP when indicated, modifying or halting the session for dizziness, chest discomfort or musculoskeletal pain, and documenting the session.

Pulmonary rehab / frail high-risk patients in a clinic gym: managing supplemental oxygen and tubing, clipping and reading pulse oximetry during walking and cycling, conducting supervised 6-minute walk tests, applying a gait belt and physically guarding or supporting unsteady patients, pacing with pursed-lip breathing coaching, and stopping for desaturation or dyspnea.

Clinical exercise (graded stress) testing support in a testing lab with a supervising physician: skin prep and 12-lead electrode placement, cuff placement and manual auscultated BP at each stage on a moving treadmill, monitoring ECG and symptoms against termination criteria, physically steadying the patient at test end and during recovery, emergency readiness.

Group exercise session for a special population (e.g., cancer survivors, diabetes, seniors) held off-site at a community center, church hall or park: variable layout and equipment, mixed risk levels, circulating among participants to check exertion, correct movement, take spot BP/HR readings, and manage adverse events without on-site telemetry or a crash cart.

Home-based / remotely monitored cardiac or exercise rehab oversight: participant exercises at home while the physiologist monitors wearable HR/ECG and video, coaches intensity by phone or video, screens symptoms, and escalates to in-person or emergency care when readings or symptoms are abnormal.

sources.system: NAO socially assistive robot (patient-robot interface, Fundación Cardioinfantil cardiac rehab study)

sources.transferJustification: Related task: robot-assisted supervision of cardiac rehab exercise. It is the nearest analogue to clinical oversight, but the paper shows the robot only supplied motivational monitoring/feedback while staff performed the clinical acts, so it does not substantiate whole-instance completion.

sources.system: NAO socially assistive robot cardiac rehab system (control and robot conditions)
