tasks.label: Integrate behavioral, developmental, improvisational, medical, or neurological approaches into music therapy treatments.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: School or early-intervention setting: therapist decides how to blend a behavioral approach (operant reinforcement schedules, discrete target behaviors, data collection agreed with the IEP/BCBA team) with a developmental approach when structuring a session series for a child with autism or a developmental disability, and writes the rationale into the treatment plan.

Hospital medical setting (NICU, oncology, pre/post-procedure, ICU, palliative care): therapist integrates a medical approach into treatment by aligning music interventions with the patient's diagnosis, precautions, medications, vital-sign responses and physician/nursing goals, deciding which clinical model governs the session.

Inpatient or outpatient neurorehabilitation (stroke, TBI, Parkinson's): therapist selects and integrates standardized Neurologic Music Therapy protocols (e.g., rhythmic auditory stimulation for gait, melodic intonation therapy for aphasia, therapeutic instrumental music performance) into the rehab plan of care and coordinates them with PT/OT/SLP goals.

Adult behavioral-health or substance-use program: therapist integrates improvisational/psychodynamic models (e.g., clinical improvisation, Nordoff-Robbins-informed work) with cognitive-behavioral elements, judging in the moment which frame to apply and documenting the integrated rationale for the group or individual.

Long-term care / memory care for older adults with dementia: therapist integrates neurological and behavioral approaches (music-evoked autobiographical memory, entrainment, antecedent-based behavior management for agitation) into an ongoing treatment plan negotiated with nursing staff and family.

Private practice or supervisory work away from the client: therapist articulates the integrated theoretical approach in written treatment plans, progress notes, insurance/funding justifications, and teaches interns or practicum students how approaches are combined for a given caseload.

tasks.label: Confer with professionals on client's treatment team to develop, coordinate, or integrate treatment plans.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

tasks.label: Select or adapt musical instruments, musical equipment, or non-musical materials, such as adaptive devices or visual aids, to meet treatment objectives.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: In a hospital unit, skilled nursing facility, or special-education school, the therapist chooses instruments and equipment for an upcoming session from a rolling cart or storage closet - guitar, hand drum, egg shakers, ocean drum, chime bars, tone bells - matching the client's goals, cognitive level, motor ability, arousal state, and infection-control rules; loads the cart, wheels it to the room, wipes down instruments, and arranges them within the client's reach.

Clinic or school therapy room: physically adapting an instrument for a client with motor impairment - fitting a Velcro or elastic hand strap to a mallet, sliding foam tubing over a beater to thicken the grip, mounting a paddle drum or tambourine on an adjustable stand at the client's midline, weighting or bracing a drum, retuning a guitar to an open tuning or fitting an adaptive pick - then trying it with the client and revising the fit until they can produce sound independently.

Preparing or modifying non-musical materials for a specific client or group: large-print or color-coded lyric sheets and notation, picture-symbol choice boards, laminated visual schedules, tactile/sensory props and scarves - deciding content and format for the client's vision, literacy, and comprehension, then printing, cutting, laminating, Velcro-backing, and organizing them into the session kit.

Selecting and configuring adaptive music technology in the facility: switch-adapted instruments and switch mounting, iPad/app-based instruments, Soundbeam/Skoog-type devices, amplification and speaker placement for hearing- or vision-impaired clients, cabling, and calibrating sensitivity or range to the individual client's available movement.

Home and community work (hospice bedside in a private residence, home-based early intervention, community group room): packing a portable set of instruments before the visit and then adapting on the spot to the room as found and the patient's position - laying a lap harp on a bedbound patient's chest, swapping in quieter instruments for a shared space, propping an instrument on pillows, improvising with household objects.

sources.title: Serve Robotics to Acquire Diligent Robotics, Expanding Physical AI Platform Beyond the Sidewalk
sources.claim: Moxi is a commercially deployed hospital mobile manipulator that autonomously navigates hospital corridors and delivers supplies, medications and lab samples; its manipulation is limited to picking up and dropping off totes/bags, pressing buttons and opening doors, not selecting or modifying clinical items.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous fetch-and-deliver of supplies inside a structured hospital (E2). It shows transport of pre-packed items is solved, but does not transfer to selecting instruments against treatment objectives or modifying them, which need clinical judgment and bespoke fine manipulation Moxi has never demonstrated.

sources.title: BMW Group advances the use of Physical AI in production with Figure 03 project in Spartanburg
sources.claim: Figure 03 humanoids autonomously pick unsorted rigid parts out of bulk containers and sequence them into trolleys inside a BMW assembly/logistics hall - the most advanced deployed 'pick the right item and kit it' capability, on standardized industrial parts in a facility engineered around the robot.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: kitting/sequencing specified parts. Transfer fails here because the pick list is supplied by the production system, the parts are rigid catalogued items, and no clinical selection criterion or instrument modification is involved.

sources.title: Figure Humanoid Robots Sort Packages Non-Stop in 24/7 Demo
sources.claim: The most sustained autonomous humanoid manipulation demonstrated to date is repetitive single-object handling (scanning and placing parcels on a conveyor) in a purpose-built warehouse cell, not varied bespoke assembly or fitting work.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: long-duration autonomous object handling. It bounds current autonomy - one repeated motion on uniform items in a fixtured cell - so it does not substantiate assembling straps, foam grips or mounts onto instruments, or fitting them to a person.

sources.title: Teleop, not autonomy, is the path for 1X's NEO humanoid
sources.claim: Consumer home humanoids remain teleoperated for anything complex; no humanoid has been shown completing a household chore end to end autonomously, which is the class of work the home/hospice instance requires.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: general household manipulation in unstructured private homes (E3). Negative transfer - if unassisted chores in homes are not yet autonomous, bedside selection and improvised adaptation of instruments in a patient's home is not either.

sources.title: A Music-Therapy Robotic Platform for Children With Autism: A Pilot Study
sources.claim: Robots in music therapy exist only as session participants: a NAO robot that autonomously localizes and strikes a xylophone and plays songs with children with autism. It handles a pre-positioned instrument and never selects, modifies or fits therapy materials.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: a robot playing an instrument within a music-therapy session. It is the closest published robotic work in this occupation and shows the state of the art stops at playing a fixed instrument - no system chooses or adapts instruments to treatment objectives.

sources.title: Automatic Laminators | Fully Automated Feeding, Laminating & Trimming Machines
sources.claim: Office/school automation covers only a sub-step of preparing visual aids: fully automatic roll-fed laminators feed, laminate and trim sheets hands-off, but a human still designs the aid, loads the material, and does the cutting, Velcro-backing and assembly.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated finishing of printed materials. Only a sub-step of the visual-aid instance; the machine does not decide content or format for a client, nor assemble and Velcro the finished aid, so it cannot complete the instance.

tasks.label: Compose, arrange, or adapt music for music therapy treatments.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Memory-care / skilled nursing group session: therapist adapts familiar songs from the clients' era — transposing to a comfortable vocal key, simplifying chord voicings, slowing tempo, shortening verses — and produces a lead sheet or annotated songbook page used to guide the session.

Pediatric hospital or school setting: therapist composes an original therapeutic song with or for a client (e.g., a coping song, procedural-support song, or goodbye song), writing lyrics and a simple melody/chord progression tailored to the child's goals and preferences.

Group ensemble or adaptive instrument work (drum circle, tone-chime choir, adapted keyboard group): therapist arranges a piece into color-coded, number-coded, or single-note parts matched to each participant's motor and cognitive ability, producing written or charted parts.

Neurologic rehabilitation: therapist composes or adapts music for specific clinical parameters — metronome-locked tempos for rhythmic auditory stimulation gait training, melodic-intonation phrases for aphasia, or sedative/entrainment music at set BPM for NICU or pain management — documented in the treatment plan.

Off-session preparation and production: therapist creates backing tracks, karaoke/accompaniment recordings, transposed notation files, or a legacy/recorded song product for a client using notation and DAW software, delivered as sheet music or an audio file.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: In-service workshop for interdisciplinary staff at a hospital, hospice, or long-term care facility: the music therapist presents slides on music therapy's evidence base, scope of practice, and referral criteria, answers clinical questions, and may play a brief recorded or live musical example to illustrate a technique.

Educational session for a potential client group or their families — e.g., a parent group at a special-education school, a dementia caregiver support group, or a veterans' group — describing what music therapy sessions involve, expected outcomes, cost and scheduling, followed by discussion.

Community outreach talk or health-fair/booth presentation at a public library, civic club, church, or community center, introducing the general public to music therapy, distributing brochures, and fielding informal questions.

Guest lecture or continuing-education presentation to professional peers or students: a university class, a state association conference session, or a CEU workshop covering assessment methods, documentation, and case examples.

Virtual or recorded information session — a webinar for a hospital system's staff, an online orientation for a school district, or a recorded overview posted for referral sources — delivered by videoconference with slides and Q&A chat.

tasks.label: Apply selected research findings to practice.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Inpatient rehabilitation hospital: therapist reads recent literature (e.g., on rhythmic auditory stimulation for post-stroke gait), judges its applicability to current caseload, and revises tempo/entrainment protocols and session goals in treatment plans accordingly.

Medical hospital (NICU/oncology/ICU): therapist selects evidence-based protocols and dosing parameters from published guidelines and research reviews, writes them into individualized treatment plans and documentation, and justifies them to nursing and physician staff.

Long-term care, memory care, or hospice: therapist chooses an evidence-supported intervention and outcome measure for a client with dementia, cites the supporting research in care-plan/IDT meetings, and adjusts practice based on outcomes literature.
School or early-intervention setting: therapist applies research on music-based interventions for autism and communication goals to IEP goal writing, session structure, and data-collection methods.

Program/administrative context: therapist presents new research findings in an in-service or supervision session, updates department policy, protocol manuals, or internship curricula so practice reflects current evidence.

tasks.label: Adapt existing or develop new music therapy assessment instruments or procedures to meet an individual client's needs.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: School or clinic-based pediatric caseload: therapist takes a standardized music therapy assessment battery (e.g., IMTAP, SEMTAP) and revises items, prompts, response criteria and scoring sheets for a nonverbal child with autism, producing a written individualized assessment protocol and data sheet for the client's file.

Long-term care / memory care: therapist adapts an observational assessment (e.g., MiDAS-style engagement measures) into a simplified, shorter observation-and-rating procedure for a resident with advanced dementia and hearing loss, documenting revised behavioral anchors and session-by-session tracking forms.

Medical/neurorehab hospital unit: therapist develops a new bedside assessment procedure (task selection, timing, rating scale) for a stroke or TBI patient with aphasia, aligning music-based tasks and outcome measures with the interdisciplinary care plan and charting requirements.

Behavioral health / psychiatric or corrections setting: therapist creates or revises a self-report and behavior-observation instrument (e.g., mood, coping, group participation ratings) tailored to an adult client's reading level, symptoms and treatment goals, and writes the accompanying administration procedure.

Hospice / palliative or private practice: therapist devises an abbreviated, low-burden assessment procedure and family interview questions for a client with limited stamina, including criteria for reassessment and documentation of quality-of-life outcomes.

tasks.label: Apply current technology to music therapy practices.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Clinic, hospital unit, or school therapy room: therapist brings a tablet/laptop and app-based music tools (GarageBand, ThumbJam, therapy apps), selects and configures the app for the client's goals, positions and holds the device for the client, plays along on acoustic or electronic instruments, and adapts the tech in real time to the client's responses.

Special-education classroom or rehab facility: therapist sets up adaptive/assistive music technology for clients with significant motor impairments — Soundbeam sensors, capability switches mounted to a wheelchair tray, eye-gaze or MIDI controllers — calibrates sensor range and switch placement to the individual's available movement, and adjusts throughout the session.

Hospital room or clinic mini-studio: therapist runs a digital recording/songwriting project — sets up mic, interface and stand at bedside or in a room, records the client's voice and instruments into a DAW, edits and mixes, and delivers the finished file/CD (e.g., legacy song for a hospice patient) to family.

Telehealth session from a clinic office: therapist configures video platform, audio interface, mic and digital instruments, shares screen/backing tracks, troubleshoots latency and client-side audio, and delivers a music therapy session to a client located elsewhere.

Nursing home / memory-care day room: therapist sets up a PA or Bluetooth speaker, amplified keyboard or loop pedal, loads personalized playlists on tablets or MP3 players (e.g., Music & Memory style), runs an amplified group session with 8-15 residents, and trains staff to use the devices between sessions.

Private home (hospice or early-intervention visit): therapist arrives with portable technology — tablet, speaker, recording gear, adaptive switch — sets it up in a cluttered living room or bedroom around furniture, medical equipment, pets and family members, and uses it in the session.

sources.system: NAO robot-based music-therapy platform (Feng et al.)
sources.developer: University of Denver / research team (Frontiers in Robotics and AI)
sources.title: A Music-Therapy Robotic Platform for Children With Autism: A Pilot Study
sources.claim: A NAO humanoid robot was programmed to autonomously localize and play a xylophone and run music-therapy interaction sessions with children with ASD in a research pilot; it is a laboratory/clinic research platform, not a deployed system, and covers only scripted turn-taking modules rather than a therapist's full technology-mediated session.
sources.transferJustification: Closest analog to a music therapist applying technology in session: a robot delivering music-based therapeutic interaction. It falls short because the platform performs pre-programmed xylophone/turn-taking modules under researcher supervision, does not set up or adapt client-specific technology, and was evaluated only in a pilot.

sources.title: Robic, the therapy robot that facilitates rehabilitation sessions
sources.claim: Inrobics' Robic (NAO-based) autonomously runs motor and cognitive rehabilitation exercise sessions in Spanish clinical institutions, but it is explicitly positioned as a therapist assistant whose session content a human therapist must program, and it does not perform music therapy or equipment setup.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robot-delivered rehabilitation therapy sessions inside a structured clinical facility (E2). Transfer fails for this task because the human therapist still authors and configures the session, and the robot neither sets up nor adapts music technology to a client.

sources.system: Co-STAR (Cognitive Stimulation Therapy by an Autonomous Robot)
sources.title: Co-STAR: Cognitive Stimulation Therapy by an Autonomous Robot for Dementia -- A One-Week In-Home Study
sources.claim: Co-STAR, a Misty robot with tablet, autonomously delivered individual cognitive stimulation therapy sessions in nine dementia patients' homes for one week; participants completed only about half of scheduled sessions and family members often had to initiate them.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous robot-delivered structured therapy activity via tablet in unstructured homes (E3). It does not substantiate this task: CST activities are caregiver-level scripted prompts, the robot handles no equipment setup, adherence was ~50%, and it makes no clinical musical adaptation.

tasks.label: Treat sick or injured animals by prescribing medication, setting bones, dressing wounds, or performing surgery.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Companion-animal clinic outpatient visit: a sick dog or cat is examined on the exam-room table, restrained by an assistant, and treated medically — injectable antibiotics/analgesics, subcutaneous fluids, ear/eye treatment, plus writing and dispensing a prescription with owner instructions.

Routine soft-tissue surgery in the clinic's surgical suite: anesthetized patient clipped and draped; ovariohysterectomy/castration, mass removal, laceration repair, or dental extractions, from first incision through hemostasis, closure, and recovery.

Wound and fracture management: debriding and lavaging a bite wound or degloving injury, placing a drain and bandage, or reducing and stabilizing a fracture with a splint/cast or internal fixation (plate, pin, screw) in a clinic or referral orthopedic suite.

Large-animal field call: treating a cow, horse, or small ruminant in a barn aisle, chute, or pasture — wound suturing, lameness/abscess treatment, injectable drug administration, casting a limb — with variable footing, lighting, and an unrestrained or minimally restrained patient.

Emergency stabilization of an acutely injured or critically ill animal in an ER hospital: IV catheter placement, wound packing and pressure, chest tap/tube, emergency drug administration under time pressure on a struggling or collapsing patient.

sources.title: Robot Performs First Realistic Surgery Without Human Help — Johns Hopkins Technology Ventures
sources.claim: STAR performed an autonomous laparoscopic intestinal anastomosis on a live pig in 2022, but only that surgical sub-step, with specially marked tissue, in a highly controlled lab environment following a predetermined plan; surgeons handled exposure, anesthesia, and closure.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous soft-tissue surgery on a porcine patient, the closest analogue to veterinary soft-tissue surgery (comparable tissue, instruments, and precision). It shows autonomy exists only for an isolated intracorporeal step under marked, lab-controlled conditions, not a whole procedure.

sources.title: Johns Hopkins' Robot Performs First Autonomous Surgery — BioHealth Innovation
sources.claim: SRT-H autonomously executed a lengthy phase of gallbladder removal on pig cadaver tissue in a research lab in July 2025; it performed a phase of the operation, not a complete procedure on a live patient from prep to closure.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous minimally invasive soft-tissue surgery on porcine anatomy, the nearest analogue to veterinary abdominal surgery. It bounds the state of the art at an autonomously executed phase on cadaveric tissue in a lab, short of a whole live-patient operation.

sources.system: Image-guided surgical drilling robot for canine transcondylar screw placement
sources.developer: University of Cambridge (Kershaw, Larby, Forni, Allen)
sources.title: Use of image-guided robotic-assisted drilling for transcondylar screw placement in the canine humerus (Veterinary Surgery)
sources.claim: The only image-guided robotic system reported for canine orthopedic surgery drilled transcondylar screw holes in 3D-printed synthetic humeri in a laboratory study; the authors state cadaver evaluation is needed before any clinical use in live dogs.

sources.system: Articulated robotic surgical system (da Vinci-type) used in veterinary surgery
sources.developer: Intuitive Surgical / Cornell University College of Veterinary Medicine (Nicole Buote)
sources.title: Cornell Veterinary Podcast: Making the Most of Minimally-Invasive Surgery
sources.claim: Robotic surgery that is actually performed on live veterinary patients in hospitals is surgeon-controlled (master-slave) rather than autonomous; Cornell reported the first live robotic gastropexy on ... dog in the US.

sources.system: Autonomous tape-handling framework for robotic wound redressing
sources.developer: UC San Diego (Xiao Liang, Michael Yip et al.)
sources.title: Towards Autonomous Tape Handling for Robotic Wound Redressing (arXiv:2510.06127)
sources.claim: Automation of wound redressing remains at the level of isolated subtasks (adhesive tape detachment and placement) in laboratory experiments; wound care is still performed manually by trained clinicians.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: bandaging/dressing wounds on a patient. Objects (tape, dressings, deformable skin) and required gentleness match veterinary wound dressing; the paper shows only a subtask is automated, so the whole dressing task is unsupported.

tasks.label: Inoculate animals against various diseases, such as rabies or distemper.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Small-animal clinic wellness visit: a conscious dog or cat on an exam table, restrained by owner/technician; the vet assesses the patient, draws the rabies/DHPP or FVRCP dose, tents skin at the prescribed site (e.g., cat vaccines in a distal limb), injects SQ/IM, records the certificate and watches for reaction.

High-volume, shelter or mobile vaccine clinic: dozens of dogs and cats per session, many unowned, fractious or feral (handled in traps or squeeze cages), unknown health history, in a shelter treatment room or a pop-up clinic space.

Beef or dairy cattle work: dozens to hundreds of head run through a squeeze chute, headgate or headlock line at a ranch, feedlot or dairy; multiple products given SQ in the neck triangle per BQA guidance, with dust, manure, and animals shifting in the restraint.

Ambulatory equine (and small ruminant) call: vaccinating horses for rabies/EWT/WNV in a private barn aisle, paddock or boarding stable; horse held by an owner or groom; footing, lighting and layout differ at every stop.

Poultry production/hatchery immunization: in-ovo vaccination of 18-day embryos and day-old chick vaccination on a hatchery line, plus flock-level vaccination programs the poultry vet performs or directly supervises.

Zoo, exotic and captive-wildlife vaccination: rabies/distemper doses to zoo carnivores, ferrets, rabbits or rehab wildlife using squeeze cages, manual restraint, pole syringe or dart, with species-specific dosing and safety constraints.

sources.title: Pharm Robotics inoculates dairy cows at large farm - The Robot Report
sources.claim: Pharm Robotics' SureShot uses an RFID gate that stops and restrains cows leaving the milking parlor while a FANUC industrial arm with a needle-free injector administers the cow's due vaccines/hormones; trade press reports it operating at a large dairy and deploying to early customer sites.

sources.title: Pharm Robotics advances automated dairy cow healthcare - The Robot Report
sources.claim: 2025 update: SureShot uses a FANUC CRX-20 cobot with 3D vision and force-based shot confirmation and autonomously delivers an individualized regimen per cow; the newest full-stack milestone reported is fully automated shots on a model cow, i.e. live-animal autonomy is still being proven out.

sources.title: How to Break through the Bottlenecks of in Ovo Vaccination in Poultry Farming (Vaccines, MDPI)
sources.claim: Zoetis' Embrex Inovoject is a commercially deployed, fully automated in-ovo vaccination machine that punches and injects vaccine into chicken embryos on hatchery egg flats at up to 70,000 eggs per ....

sources.title: Vaccination - Maskon
sources.claim: Maskon (Skala Maskon) sells a fully automatic fish vaccination machine that grades and injects live smolt intraperitoneally or intramuscularly at up to 40,000 fish per hour with one operator, in salmon hatcheries worldwide.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: machine vaccination of live food-production animals. It shows vision-guided needle placement into live vertebrates is routine when the animals are anaesthetised and conveyed to the machine, i.e. a purpose-built E1 line; it does not address conscious mammals on an exam table.

sources.title: Cobi robot autonomously performs needle-less vaccinations - New Atlas
sources.claim: Cobionix's Cobi platform performed an intramuscular (needle-free jet) injection on a human subject autonomously - reported as the first robot to do so - as a 2021 university-spinoff demonstration.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robot-administered vaccination. The subject is a cooperative, stationary human arm and the demonstration is a one-off; it does not substantiate restraining and dosing a conscious dog, cat, horse or zoo carnivore at clinical reliability.

sources.system: Stereo-vision robotic mouse tail-vein injection system
sources.title: Development of a Stereo-vision based High-throughput Robotic System for Mouse Tail Vein Injection (arXiv)
sources.claim: A stereo-vision robotic system autonomously performs tail-vein injection in live, non-anaesthetised mice held in a purpose-built holding mechanism inside a bench-top machine.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous needle injection into a live restrained mammal. It is confined to a 45 cm bench machine built around a mouse-sized holder; nothing in it transfers to restraining and injecting 2-90 kg conscious dogs, cats or horses.

sources.system: Digital-twin automated cattle vaccination pipeline (Detectron2 + PPO, Franka Panda)
sources.title: AUTOMATED CATTLE INJECTIONS: A ROBOTIC AND DIGITAL TWIN APPROACH TO FEEDLOT EFFICIENCY (OpenReview)
sources.claim: Robotic cattle vaccination for feedlots is, as of late 2025, being developed and validated in NVIDIA Isaac Sim digital twins of a cow in a chute rather than as a fielded physical system.

tasks.label: Examine animals to detect and determine the nature of diseases or injuries.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Small-animal clinic exam room: veterinarian performs a full physical exam on a dog or cat (wellness or presenting complaint) — TPR, cardiac/pulmonary auscultation, abdominal palpation, lymph node and skin palpation, otoscopy, ophthalmic and oral exam, brief orthopedic/neurologic screen — on a conscious, often anxious or squirming patient held by a technician, and forms a problem list/differential diagnosis.

Emergency/urgent-care hospital: triage and examination of an acutely ill or injured pet (trauma, collapse, dyspnea, vomiting, wounds) — assessing perfusion and mucous membranes, localizing pain by palpation, evaluating fractures/lacerations, thoracic and abdominal auscultation, sometimes point-of-care ultrasound (AFAST/TFAST) — under time pressure on an unstable, sometimes fractious or painful animal.

Dairy or beef operation: individual sick-cow and herd-check examinations with the animal in a headlock, chute or palpation rail — rectal palpation and transrectal ultrasound, temperature, rumen and lung auscultation, udder and hoof/leg examination, ketosis/metritis workup — in a barn or working facility with farm staff restraining animals.

Equine or mixed ambulatory call on a farm, pasture or boarding barn: lameness workup (limb and hoof palpation, hoof testers, flexion tests, gait evaluation on varied surfaces), colic exam (rectal palpation, nasogastric intubation, gut auscultation), dental or wound assessment — variable footing, lighting and restraint, animal may be fractious.

Poultry or swine production barn: flock/herd-level health investigation — walking the house observing bird or pig behavior, gait, respiration and lesions, catching and hands-on examining representative animals, and performing field necropsies of culls/dead animals to determine the causative disease; also ante-mortem inspection of livestock at plants.

Shelter, exotic-pet, zoo or laboratory-animal setting: intake or routine health exam of a rabbit, reptile, bird, small mammal, non-human primate or rodent colony animal — species-specific handling or chemical restraint, body condition, hydration, oral/beak/shell exam, palpation and auscultation, detection of subtle prey-species disease signs.

sources.title: Robotics for poultry farming: challenges and opportunities
sources.claim: Scout (formerly ChickenBoy, Faromatics/AGCO) is a ceiling-rail autonomous robot deployed in commercial broiler houses that detects sick and dead birds and environmental problems using cameras and sensors, but works without any direct contact with the birds — it issues alerts rather than performing a hands-on examination or determining a disease's nature.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated flock health surveillance in a poultry house. It overlaps with the veterinarian's flock walk-through only in detecting abnormal/dead birds; it cannot catch, restrain, palpate or necropsy birds, so it cannot determine the nature of a disease.

sources.system: Autonomous inspection robot for dead laying hens
sources.developer: academic (Computers and Electronics in Agriculture authors)
sources.title: Autonomous inspection robot for dead laying hens in caged layer house
sources.claim: A research inspection robot moves autonomously along fixed rails above caged laying hens and uses multimodal imaging to detect abnormal and dead hens; it is a detection-only monitoring platform in a caged layer house, not a diagnostic examination system.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated detection of sick/dead birds in a layer house. Transfer to the veterinary exam is limited to visual triage; no contact, restraint or lesion-level diagnosis is performed.

sources.system: Fully autonomous robotic ultrasound system (thyroid RUSS)
sources.title: A fully autonomous robotic ultrasound system for thyroid scanning
sources.claim: A fully autonomous robotic ultrasound ... scanned the thyroid of human volunteers without human assistance, producing images close to clinician-acquired scans — the closest demonstrated autonomous 'hands-on' patient examination, but performed on a cooperative, motionless, hairless human in a laboratory/clinical rig and covering a single imaging modality rather than a whole physical exam.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: sonographic examination of a patient. Transfer to veterinary examination fails on the key conditions — the animal is unrestrained, furry, moving and may bite, and the vet's task requires palpation, auscultation, otoscopy and a diagnostic conclusion, not one scan.

sources.title: iApp: An Autonomous Inspection, Auscultation, Percussion, and Palpation Platform
sources.claim: The iApp platform automates parts of a physical examination (inspection, auscultation, percussion, palpation) with custom hardware, but it is described as a conceptual system evaluated on healthy human subjects for classifying abdominal regions, not for detecting or characterizing disease in animals.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated human physical examination. It is the nearest analogue to a hands-on clinical exam, but it was validated on healthy, still, cooperative humans and outputs region classification, not a disease determination.

sources.title: Humanoid Robots Controlled By Surgeons Did World-First Operation On Live Pigs
sources.claim: The most advanced robotic system operating on live animals as of mid-2026 — humanoid robots removing gallbladders from live pigs in a preclinical trial published in Nature — was under continuous surgeon teleoperation, indicating that animal-facing robotic clinical work remains human-controlled.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic clinical intervention on a live animal. Because it is teleoperated, it cannot support a positive judgment, and it shows the autonomy gap for hands-on animal procedures.

sources.title: Revolutionizing Dairy Farming: How Robots Benefit Cows & Farmers
sources.claim: Lely Astronaut automatic milking robots autonomously attach to and milk cows in commercial dairy barns and collect dozens of per-teat parameters, notifying the farmer when an issue is detected — an automated screening alert, not a veterinary examination or diagnosis.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated in-parlour health screening of dairy cows in a purpose-built robot box. It flags candidate problems but performs no clinical examination and reaches no diagnosis, so it cannot substitute for the veterinarian's exam.

sources.system: Automatic milking system mastitis detection (DeLaval, Lely, GEA)
sources.title: Machine learning-based clinical mastitis detection in dairy cows using milk electrical conductivity and somatic cell count
sources.claim: Published evaluations show automatic milking systems' automated mastitis detection falls well short of clinical diagnostic quality, with sensitivity of roughly 61–78% for conductivity-based detection in DeLaval and Lely systems.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated detection of a single bovine disease at the milking robot. Even for that one condition, accuracy is far below what an employer would accept from a veterinarian's examination.

sources.title: Laser-equipped underwater drones keep farmed salmon healthy
sources.claim: Stingray submersible robots autonomously identify sea lice on free-swimming salmon in commercial sea pens and fire a laser at them; deployed at scale in Norwegian and Scottish salmon farms. This is autonomous detection of one visible external parasite, not a health examination determining the nature of disease.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated detection of ectoparasites on live production animals. It handles one pre-specified visible lesion class on fish; it cannot palpate, auscultate or reach a diagnosis across disease presentations.

tasks.label: Collect body tissue, feces, blood, urine, or other body fluids for examination and analysis.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Companion-animal practice: drawing blood from a conscious dog or cat (jugular, cephalic or saphenous vein) in the exam room or treatment area, with a technician restraining the animal; fur parted or clipped, vein raised, needle/vacutainer or syringe used, correct volume into the right tubes without hemolysis, tubes labeled for in-house or reference-lab analysis.

Companion-animal practice: other diagnostic sample collection — ultrasound-guided or blind cystocentesis, urinary catheterization or free-catch urine; fine-needle aspirate of a cutaneous or lymph-node mass; skin scrape, ear swab, or punch/incisional biopsy under local or sedation; slides made or samples put in formalin/tubes.

Fecal sample collection: rectal loop or swab from a dog, cat, foal or calf in the clinic; picking a fresh voided stool from a floor, litter box, kennel run, or pen; grab sample per rectum from a cow or horse; sample bagged, labeled, and submitted for float/PCR/culture.

Food-animal / equine ambulatory work: blood sampling cattle in a chute or head-gate (coccygeal or jugular) for brucellosis/BVD/pregnancy testing, ear-notch tissue samples, swine or small-ruminant bleeds in pens, poultry flock sampling — outdoors or in barns, dusty, animals moving, dozens to hundreds of animals per visit.
Dairy herd work: collecting milk samples from lactating cows for analysis (somatic cell count, milk-recording panels, progesterone/metabolic markers) in the milking parlor or robotic milking barn.

Laboratory-animal / research veterinary work: serial or single blood collection from rodents (tail vein, saphenous) or catheterized dogs/minipigs in a vivarium procedure room, animals in restrainers or purpose-built sampling cages, samples timed and aliquoted for pharmacokinetic or clinical-pathology analysis.

sources.system: Ultrasound-guided robotic vascular access (RVA) system, 6-DoF arm + 3-DoF end-effector (Tongji University group)
sources.title: Ultrasound-Guided Robotic Blood Drawing and In Vivo Studies on Submillimetre Vessels of Rats (arXiv:2504.05329)
sources.claim: A benchtop image-guided robot performed ultrasound-guided blood drawing in vivo from the sub-millimetre tail veins of 40 rats positioned on a holding platform, with 95% first-attempt success and 'minimal human intervention'.
sources.transferJustification: Same task (drawing a venous blood sample from a live animal for analysis) on a laboratory rodent presented on a fixture; supports the lab-animal instance at the fixtured, purpose-built tier.

sources.title: Vitestro raises $70m to fuel blood-drawing robot's global commercial readiness
sources.claim: An autonomous robotic phlebotomy device performs venipuncture and blood collection on human patients using AI-guided Doppler ultrasound; CE-marked in 2024 and placed in European healthcare settings from March 2025, with reported 95% first-stick success.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous venipuncture on a cooperative human arm in a phlebotomy chair. It does not transfer to conscious dogs, cats or cattle — the device is engineered around a human forearm, and no demonstration exists on a furred, unrestrained, non-cooperative animal.

sources.system: Culex Automated Blood Sampling System (Culex NxT / Raturn)
sources.title: Home — BASi Culex Automated Blood Collection System
sources.claim: A commercially sold laboratory instrument automates the collection of blood ... awake, freely moving lab animals (mice, rats, and large animals) via a previously implanted catheter in a purpose-built tethered cage system.
sources.transferJustification: Same task (blood collection for analysis) but only after a human surgically implants the catheter, and only inside a purpose-built sampling cage; supports the lab-animal instance at the purpose-built tier only.

sources.system: Fluispotter wearable automated serial blood sampling device
sources.title: A novel device for serial venous blood sampling in a canine model
sources.claim: A wearable automated device performed serial jugular blood sampling in Beagle dogs over 22-hour periods without manual venipuncture, via an indwelling catheter placed beforehand.
sources.transferJustification: Same task (venous blood collection from a dog) but the venous access is established manually by a veterinarian first; the machine only withdraws through the existing catheter, so it does not complete a clinic blood draw end to end.

sources.system: Herd Navigator (with DeLaval VMS milking robot)
sources.title: Dynamic Changes in Progesterone Concentration in Cows' Milk Determined by the At-Line Milk Analysis System Herd Navigator
sources.claim: A fully automated at-line milk analysis system takes milk samples during robotic milking and analyses them on-farm (progesterone, LDH, BHB, urea); it is commercially available in combination with a DeLaval milking robot.

sources.developer: Lely / DeLaval and other AMS manufacturers
sources.title: Devices used by automated milking systems are similarly accurate in estimating milk yield and in collecting a representative milk sample compared with devices used by farms with conventional milk recording
sources.claim: Peer-reviewed comparison found that the sampling devices built into automated (robotic) milking systems collect a representative milk sample about as accurately as devices used for conventional milk recording.

sources.title: Lely refines Astronaut A5 Next robotic milker
sources.claim: Commercial robotic milkers locate the teats of a free-moving cow with laser and camera teat detection and attach the milking cups autonomously in a milking box inside the barn.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous attachment to a live, unrestrained cow to harvest milk, the physical act underlying automated milk sampling for analysis in the dairy instance.

sources.system: Stereo-vision based high-throughput robotic mouse tail vein injection system
sources.title: Development of a Stereo-vision based High-throughput Robotic System for Mouse Tail Vein Injection
sources.claim: A stereo-vision robotic system inserted a needle into the tail vein of non-anesthetized mice held in a purpose-built holding mechanism, succeeding in 37 of 40 animals (92.5%).
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous needle placement in the tail vein of an awake rodent restrained by a fixture — the same vascular-access skill and precision required for rodent blood collection, in the same fixtured laboratory setting.

tasks.label: Operate diagnostic equipment, such as radiographic or ultrasound equipment, and interpret the resulting images.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Small-animal clinic: vet takes survey radiographs (thoracic, abdominal, or orthopedic) of an awake or lightly sedated dog or cat - restraining/positioning the patient in lateral and VD recumbency on the X-ray table, collimating, setting technique, checking image quality, retaking views, then reading the study and recording findings.

Small-animal clinic dental suite: full-mouth intraoral radiographic series (10-14 views) on an anesthetized dog or cat - repeatedly placing and angling a sensor inside the mouth, aiming the tube head per tooth group, then interpreting for root pathology, resorption and bone loss and planning extractions.

Small-animal clinic: vet performs an ultrasound exam (complete abdominal study, focused AFAST/TFAST in an emergency, bladder or pregnancy scan, or basic echo) on a clipped, gelled, awake or sedated patient in a padded V-trough - sweeping the probe, adjusting depth/gain, capturing cines, and interpreting in real time.

Equine ambulatory call: portable digital radiography of a horse's distal limb in a barn aisle or stall - positioning plate holder and tube around a standing, sometimes fractious horse, multiple oblique projections, variable light and footing, then reading images on a laptop on site.

Cattle herd work: transrectal ultrasound pregnancy checks and reproductive exams on cows restrained in a chute or headlocks on a farm - arm-in-rectum probe placement, dozens to hundreds of animals per session, real-time interpretation of uterus and ovaries called out to the producer.

Exotic, avian, or zoo/wildlife imaging: radiographs or ultrasound of a bird, reptile, rabbit, or anesthetized zoo animal, using improvised restraint, tiny or unusual anatomy, non-standard positioning, and species-specific interpretation.

sources.title: New sector-wide initiative introduces Genus Focus for in-ovo sexing in Switzerland to end chick culling
sources.claim: Orbem's Genus Focus is a commercially deployed, fully automated MRI imaging line that images live poultry embryos inside eggs conveyed through the machine and classifies them with AI at up to 24,000 eggs per hour, with no human operating the scanner or reading the images.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated diagnostic imaging of animal subjects plus automated interpretation. It shows a machine acquiring clinical-modality images (MRI) of biological subjects presented to it by conveyance and reaching a decision from those images unattended - the acquisition-and-read half of the veterinary task when the subject arrives fixtured. Subjects are far simpler than a dog, so it supports only a purpose-built (E1) setting.

sources.title: Hendrix Genetics and Orbem Launch MRI-Based In-Ovo Sexing
sources.claim: The same system is described as MRI-based imaging plus classification technology integrated with hatchery automation equipment, i.e. imaging hardware and interpretation software running as one unattended line.
sources.transferJustification: Same related task: machine-controlled acquisition of images of animal subjects with automated interpretation inside a purpose-built facility.

sources.title: New Research Validates SignalPet's AI in Radiographic Interpretation
sources.claim: SignalPET's AI reads canine and feline radiographs in routine clinical use at large scale, establishing that the interpretation half of this task is performed by machine in production.
sources.transferJustification: Software, not a robotic system; cited only for the image-interpretation component, which must be completed alongside machine acquisition for the instance to be whole.

sources.title: SignalPET Introduces SignalPET 360°: A Comprehensive Radiology Platform Designed for Modern Veterinary Practice
sources.claim: SignalPET 360 automatically screens each study for 66 pathologies across thoracic, abdominal, musculoskeletal ... radiographs and issues an immediate report without a human reader in that layer.
sources.transferJustification: Software component evidence for the interpretation half; the breadth of findings shows it addresses the reads a general-practice veterinarian makes from radiographs.

sources.title: Vetology AI Radiology Evaluations | Patterson Veterinary
sources.claim: Vetology's commercially distributed veterinary radiology AI reports agreement in the low 90s percent with board-certified radiologist overreads, indicating machine interpretation near the quality bar a practice accepts.
sources.transferJustification: Software; cited for interpretation quality on canine and feline radiographic studies, the read the veterinarian would otherwise produce.

sources.system: Autonomous lightweight ultrasound robot (Beijing Tsinghua Changgung Hospital deployment)
sources.developer: Tsinghua University School of Biomedical Engineering
sources.title: Beyond hospital reach: Autonomous lightweight ultrasound robot for liver sonography
sources.claim: A research autonomous ultrasound robot acquired standard liver imaging planes and detected pathology in human patients in a hospital ultrasound department - the closest demonstrated autonomous ultrasound acquisition on a living subject, but single-organ, human-skin and prototype-stage.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous ultrasound scanning of a living subject. It is human, single-organ, on bare skin, and prototype maturity, so it does not substantiate a complete multi-organ veterinary ultrasound study through clipped fur on an animal patient.

sources.title: Tools for automating the imaging of zebrafish larvae - PubMed
sources.claim: A commercial laboratory instrument automatically loads, positions and orients live sedated zebrafish larvae and captures images of them, showing machine handling and imaging of live animals inside a purpose-built instrument.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated positioning and imaging of live vertebrate animals with automated image capture in a purpose-built instrument. Subjects are millimetre-scale larvae imaged optically, so it supports only the E1 claim that presented animal subjects can be imaged unattended.

sources.title: Equine veterinary CT scanner - EQUINA® - Asto CT
sources.claim: Asto CT Equina is a commercially installed veterinary CT with a pivoting robotic gantry that images mildly sedated standing horses' limbs and head/neck; the horse is led in and positioned by people and the exam is operator-run.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: machine-controlled image acquisition on a large-animal patient in a dedicated imaging room. Autonomy over the whole exam (handling, protocol, interpretation) is not established, so it is treated as operator-run and cannot support a positive judgment.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

tasks.label: Counsel clients about the deaths of their pets or about euthanasia decisions for their pets.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

tasks.label: Advise animal owners regarding sanitary measures, feeding, general care, medical conditions, or treatment options.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

tasks.label: Euthanize animals.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Companion-animal euthanasia in a small-animal clinic/hospital exam room: vet assesses the patient, gives an IM/SC sedative, places a cephalic IV catheter in a fur-covered, sometimes fractious or debilitated dog or cat, injects an overdose of pentobarbital, auscultates to confirm cardiac death, and handles the body - usually with the owner present and touching the animal.

In-home euthanasia by a mobile/house-call veterinarian: pet on its own bed, sofa or lawn in a private residence with family and other pets around; sedation by injection, then IV or intra-hepatic/intra-renal pentobarbital, confirmation of death, and removal of the body.

Shelter or high-volume humane-society euthanasia: successive dogs and cats, many unsocialized or feral, restrained by staff or in a squeeze/trap; IV, intraperitoneal or (post-sedation) intracardiac pentobarbital, confirmation of death for each animal, carcass handling and controlled-drug logging.

On-farm or field euthanasia of a horse or food animal: downer dairy cow in a barn or pen, injured horse in a paddock or roadside trailer, sick pig or small ruminant; method is gunshot or penetrating captive bolt plus an adjunctive step, or a large-volume IV barbiturate via the jugular; vet must approach and restrain the animal, apply the method at a precise anatomical landmark, confirm death, and advise on carcass disposal.

Laboratory-rodent euthanasia in an institutional vivarium: mice or rats euthanized in their home cages or a chamber with a gradual-fill CO2 protocol per AVMA guidelines, followed by confirmation of death and, per IACUC policy, a secondary physical method before carcass disposal or tissue collection.

Zoo, exotic or wildlife euthanasia: injured deer at a roadside, a bird or reptile in an exotics practice, or a large zoo animal in its enclosure or holding area; may require remote-delivery sedation (darting), then lethal injection or free-bullet/captive-bolt, plus death confirmation under variable, sometimes hazardous field conditions.

sources.system: Euthanex EZ-DOCK SMARTBOX Euthanasia Station (and TT-8100 SMARTBOX tabletop chamber)
sources.date: 2025 (product in commercial sale; SMARTBOX line marketed for years)
sources.title: Humane Euthanasia | EZ-DOCK SMARTBOX | Station
sources.claim: Commercial, fully automated CO2 euthanasia station for laboratory rodents in vivaria: home cages are docked to the unit, which automatically runs the AVMA-compliant charge/dwell/exhaust euthanasia cycle with the lid locked until purge is complete.

sources.title: Quietek CO2 Induction Systems - Next Advance - Laboratory Instruments
sources.claim: Fully automated benchtop CO2 induction/euthanasia instrument in worldwide laboratory use since 2013; the machine controls flow rate and timing to meet AVMA rodent euthanasia requirements once the cage/chamber is presented to it.

sources.system: Automated IVC-rack CO2 euthanasia system (McIntyre et al., JAALAS)
sources.developer: Memorial Sloan-Kettering Cancer Center laboratory animal group
sources.title: Automated mouse euthanasia in an individually ventilated caging system: system development and assessment - PubMed
sources.claim: Peer-reviewed development and validation of a logic-controlled CO2 system built into an individually ventilated caging rack that euthanizes mice in their home cages, up to 70 cages at once, without handling by staff.

sources.title: Pharm Robotics inoculates dairy cows at large farm - The Robot Report
sources.claim: Autonomous industrial robot arm that identifies dairy cows by RFID, holds each cow in a bumper restraint in the milking-parlor lane and injects vaccines/reproductive drugs, then releases the cow; deployed at early commercial dairy customer sites.
sources.transferJustification: Related task = routine SC/IM injection of a restrained large animal. It shows a robot can place a needle in a restrained cow, but euthanasia requires a lethal jugular barbiturate dose or a precisely landmarked captive bolt/gunshot plus an adjunctive step and confirmation of death, none of which this system performs; performance therefore does not carry over to euthanasia.

sources.title: Vitestro raises $70m to fuel blood-drawing robot's global commercial readiness - Medical Device Network

sources.transferJustification: Related task = autonomous venipuncture, the closest demonstrated analogue to IV euthanasia injection. It works only on a cooperative, consenting human arm clamped in a purpose-built cuff with imaged veins; nothing extends it to fur-covered, moving, multi-species animal patients or to lethal-dose delivery and death confirmation, so it does not substantiate completion of this task.

instances.label: Dairy herd reproductive program management day: on a commercial dairy the veterinarian works a string of 60-150 cows locked in headlocks or a palpation rail — transrectal ultrasound/palpation for pregnancy diagnosis, fetal aging, twins, ovarian structures and uterine health of fresh/problem cows — then updates the synchronization protocol, cull/rebreed lists and repro targets in herd software.

Executing the timed-AI synchronization protocol on a large dairy: on each scheduled day, identify every cow enrolled in the Ovsynch/Presynch program and administer the correct GnRH or prostaglandin injection at the correct interval, with accurate treatment records and near-100% protocol compliance; cows are handled through the parlor or headlocks.

Companion-animal nutrition program in a small-animal clinic: obesity or therapeutic-diet case — take diet history, weigh the patient, palpate and assign a body condition/muscle condition score, calculate resting energy requirement and target weight, select and prescribe a diet and feeding plan, counsel the owner, and re-weigh/adjust at recheck visits.

Field reproduction programs in food-animal, equine and companion practice: bull/ram breeding soundness exams (scrotal measurement, electroejaculation, semen evaluation) and estrus-synchronization plus fixed-time AI and preg-checking of beef cows in a ranch chute; mare follicular ultrasound, insemination timing and embryo flush/transfer at a breeding farm; canine progesterone timing and transcervical AI in a clinic.

Livestock nutrition program planning and audit on a dairy or feedlot: sample and interpret forage analyses, evaluate the TMR at the bunk (particle size, sorting, refusals), body-condition-score groups of cows, review intake and production data with the nutritionist, and set revised ration and feeding-schedule specifications for the transition and lactating groups.

Implementing the preweaning calf nutrition program on a dairy: deliver the prescribed milk/milk-replacer volumes at the correct concentration and temperature on the prescribed schedule to individually identified calves, record intakes, and step down amounts through the weaning transition.

tasks.label: Conduct postmortem studies and analyses to determine the causes of animals' deaths.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Small-animal clinic postmortem: a dog or cat dies unexpectedly in hospital or is brought in by an owner; the veterinarian performs a gross necropsy in the clinic treatment/back room — external exam, opening thoracic and abdominal cavities, in-situ organ inspection, weighing/sectioning heart, lungs, liver, kidneys, GI tract, collecting formalin-fixed tissue and fluid samples, then interpreting findings with the clinical history and reporting a cause of death to the owner and referring clinician.

Veterinary diagnostic laboratory necropsy floor (state/university VDL): mixed-species caseload (calves, horses, dogs, birds, small ruminants) on stainless tables and hoists, some autolyzed or frozen; systematic dissection with knife, bone saw and enterotomy, description of gross lesions, collection of a standard tissue set for histopathology plus bacteriology/virology/toxicology, followed by slide review and a written case report assigning cause of death.

On-farm field necropsy of livestock: an ambulatory veterinarian works on a dead cow, calf, sheep or pig lying in a pasture, muddy lot, or barn alley, in variable weather, with only a knife, gloves and sample containers; must position/open the carcass, evaluate lesions (pneumonia, bloat, abomasal displacement, toxicosis, lightning strike, predation), collect samples for the lab, and advise the producer on herd implications.

Poultry or swine production postmortem: veterinarian performs rapid sequential necropsies on dozens of dead birds or piglets at the barn, service lab bench, or company diagnostic room, scoring gross lesions (airsacculitis, enteritis, ascites, ileitis) across the group to reach a flock- or herd-level cause-of-death diagnosis and sample selection.

Wildlife, zoo or marine-mammal postmortem in the field: a stranded seal on a beach, a deer or waterfowl die-off during an avian influenza or EHD event, or a large zoo animal necropsied outdoors; carcass position, size, decomposition and biosecurity constraints vary widely, and the veterinarian must dissect, sample for pathogens/toxins, and determine cause of death under field conditions.

sources.developer: Institute of Forensic Medicine, University of Zurich
sources.title: Virtobot--a multi-functional robotic system for 3D surface scanning and automatic post mortem biopsy - PubMed
sources.claim: Virtobot is a real robotic system used in a forensic institute for 3D surface scanning and CT-guided post-mortem needle biopsy of human bodies; it samples tissue under operator planning but performs no dissection, organ evaluation, or cause-of-death determination.
sources.transferJustification: Related task = minimally invasive post-mortem tissue sampling. It is the closest robotic analogue to necropsy, but transfer fails: it acquires needle cores at pre-planned coordinates in a purpose-built imaging suite and does not open body cavities, describe lesions, select tissues adaptively, or reach a diagnosis, which is the accepted output of a veterinary postmortem.

sources.system: Scott Technology automated lamb boning / AI-enabled lamb processing system (JBS Cobram)

sources.claim: Autonomous robot lines cut and bone animal carcasses at commercial rates in purpose-built processing plants using x-ray/3D vision guidance, showing robotic carcass cutting exists but only for standardized yield cuts, not diagnostic dissection.
sources.transferJustification: Related task = robotic carcass breakdown in meat plants. Objects (ovine/bovine carcasses) and cutting tools are comparable, but the systems execute fixed anatomical yield cuts on fixtured, uniform carcasses; they perform no lesion recognition, no diagnostic sampling, and no cause-of-death determination, so performance does not carry over to necropsy.

sources.system: Tissue-Tek SmartConnect / AutoTEC a120 embedder; FinderFLEX robotic slide handling unit

sources.claim: Robotic automation in anatomic pathology handles downstream histology steps (cassette transfer, embedding, slide handling) in laboratories, i.e. only a sub-step of the postmortem workflow after tissues have been dissected and selected by a pathologist.
sources.transferJustification: Related task = histology specimen processing. It automates only tissue processing/embedding after a human has performed the necropsy and chosen the tissues; it contributes nothing to gross dissection or cause-of-death determination, so it cannot complete the instance.

sources.title: Postmortem Examinations as a Diagnostic Tool | College of Veterinary Medicine at MSU
sources.claim: A veterinary postmortem examination requires combined gross dissection and evaluation of the whole animal plus microscopic evaluation, directed by a trained pathologist who selects tissues and ancillary tests — defining the accepted output of this task.
sources.transferJustification: Not a robotic system; cited only to fix the scope and accepted output of the task (adaptive gross dissection plus lesion interpretation and diagnosis) against which robotic evidence is assessed.

tasks.label: Specialize in a particular type of treatment, such as dentistry, pathology, nutrition, surgery, microbiology, or internal medicine.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Board-certified small animal surgeon performs a referral surgical procedure (e.g., TPLO, mass excision, GDV correction, cystotomy) on an anesthetized dog in a specialty hospital operating room: clipping/draping, approach, dissection and hemostasis, repair or implant placement, layered closure, and post-op plan.

Veterinary dentist/oral surgeon works on an anesthetized dog or cat in a dental suite: full-mouth radiographs and charting, ultrasonic scaling and polishing, surgical extraction of diseased teeth with flap elevation, sectioning, alveoloplasty and suturing, plus local blocks.

Small animal internal medicine specialist runs a referral workup on a sedated or conscious patient in a specialty hospital: physical exam, abdominal ultrasound, ultrasound-guided FNA/biopsy, endoscopy or feeding-tube placement, catheter and sample handling, then diagnosis and treatment plan.

Veterinary anatomic pathologist at a diagnostic laboratory: gross necropsy of a dog, foal, or production animal on the necropsy floor — carcass positioning, dissection, organ removal and gross description, tissue collection and trimming — followed by histopathology review and a signed-out report.

Laboratory-specialty veterinarian (microbiology / clinical pathology) directing routine bench work on submitted specimens in a veterinary diagnostic lab: culture setup and streaking, incubation, plate reading, organism identification and antimicrobial susceptibility testing, and issuance of a validated report.

Equine or large-animal specialist working on-site at a barn, stable, or farm: lameness workup with flexion tests and diagnostic nerve blocks, portable radiography/ultrasound, standing sedated dental or surgical procedures, in variable footing, lighting, and animal restraint conditions.

sources.system: SRT-H (Hierarchical Surgical Robot Transformer, on dVRK-Si)
sources.title: SRT-H: A hierarchical framework for autonomous surgery via language-conditioned imitation learning | Science Robotics
sources.claim: Johns Hopkins' SRT-H autonomously executed a phase of laparoscopic cholecystectomy (clipping and cutting cystic duct and artery) on ex vivo pig gallbladders in a research lab — a sub-step of a procedure, not a whole operation on a live patient.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: human-model laparoscopic surgery on porcine tissue. It bears on veterinary soft-tissue surgery (same tissue type), but covers only one phase with the abdomen already accessed, so it does not substantiate completing a whole veterinary surgical case.

sources.title: Smart Tissue Autonomous Robot performs laparoscopic surgery on pig soft tissue without human help
sources.claim: The Smart Tissue Autonomous Robot performed laparoscopic intestinal anastomosis in live pigs without human guidance, outperforming manual suturing — still one sub-step, with access and everything else provided by the human team.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: bowel anastomosis in live pigs. Comparable tissue and precision to veterinary soft-tissue surgery, but limited to the suturing step in an anesthetized, surgically opened, fully prepared animal; no closure, hemostasis management, or case-level decision-making.

sources.system: da Vinci surgical system used in veterinary minimally invasive surgery
sources.developer: Intuitive Surgical / Cornell University Hospital for Animals
sources.title: Cornell Veterinary Podcast: Making the Most of Minimally-Invasive Surgery
sources.claim: Robotic surgery actually performed in veterinary hospitals (e.g., first live robotic gastropexy in a client-owned dog at Cornell) is da Vinci-style teleoperation by a surgeon, not autonomous operation.

sources.title: Fully-automatic robot dentist performs world's first human procedure
sources.claim: Perceptive's AI-driven robot autonomously carried out a complete crown-preparation procedure on a single human dental patient — a one-off, pre-FDA demonstration on a cooperative seated human, not veterinary extraction or oral surgery under anesthesia.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: human restorative dentistry (crown prep). Transfer to veterinary dentistry is weak: the veterinary instance is surgical extraction with flap creation and suturing, full-mouth radiographs and charting in an intubated dog or cat, with anatomy and access unlike a seated human patient.

sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated reading of human urine cultures. Same plate media, colony morphology and laboratory conditions as veterinary culture reading, so plate-handling and reading performance carries over.

sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous diagnostic ultrasound on cooperative humans. It covers only image acquisition of preset planes on a still, consenting patient; a veterinary internal-medicine workup adds restraint of an unco-operative animal, guided sampling, endoscopy and diagnosis.

tasks.label: Inspect and test horses, sheep, poultry, or other animals to detect the presence of communicable diseases.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Companion-animal clinic: dog or cat presented with cough, fever or diarrhea (or a pre-boarding/shelter intake screen). Vet restrains/handles the animal, takes temperature, auscultates, palpates lymph nodes, examines mucous membranes, collects a cephalic/jugular blood sample, fecal sample or nasal/oral swab, runs an in-house SNAP/PCR test or submits to a lab, and interprets the result for parvo, FeLV/FIV, kennel cough, giardia, etc.

Equine farm call at a boarding barn or paddock: vet examines a haltered horse (temperature, heart/lung auscultation, nasal discharge, lymph nodes, gait), draws a jugular blood sample for a Coggins/EIA test and interstate health certificate, and takes a nasopharyngeal swab or guttural pouch wash for strangles, on uneven footing with other horses nearby.

On-farm cattle herd regulatory/surveillance testing: animals run up an alley into a squeeze chute or headlocks; vet places a caudal-fold tuberculin injection and palpates the read 72 hours later, draws coccygeal or jugular blood for brucellosis/BVD/Johne's serology, checks ear-tag IDs, and inspects the herd for signs of contagious disease.

Commercial poultry flock health check in a broiler or layer house: vet walks the house observing bird distribution, posture, respiratory signs and droppings, examines and necropsies dead or culled birds, collects oropharyngeal/cloacal swabs and blood for NPIP and avian-influenza surveillance, and submits pooled samples for lab confirmation.

Ante-mortem inspection at a slaughter establishment: vet observes lots of cattle, swine or poultry at rest and in motion in the plant's holding pens, singles out suspects, takes temperature and examines them more closely for signs of communicable disease, and records dispositions.

Dairy udder-health surveillance: screening lactating cows at milking for contagious/subclinical intramammary infection by sampling each cow's milk and testing it (somatic cell count / CMT / conductivity / inflammation biomarker) to flag infected cows for follow-up culture and treatment.

sources.claim: DeLaval's Milk Cell Analysis online cell counter is integrated into VMS V300 robotic milking stalls and automatically measures somatic cell count from each cow's milk to identify subclinical mastitis.
sources.transferJustification: Same task element as the dairy instance: machine-collected milk sample plus on-board test that flags cows with intramammary infection.

sources.title: DeLaval Milk Cell Analysis (MCA) - DeLaval
sources.claim: The same DeLaval sensor is marketed as instantaneously measuring somatic cell count and identifying subclinical mastitis in individual cows.

sources.claim: Herd Navigator automatically takes milk samples through a sampler built into the milking system and analyses biomarkers (LDH) to identify mastitis with reported sensitivity above 80%, in commercial use on dairy farms.
sources.transferJustification: Automated on-farm sampling and testing of individual cows for intramammary infection is the sampling-and-testing step of the dairy surveillance instance.

sources.title: The detection of intramammary infections using online somatic cell counts - ScienceDirect
sources.claim: Peer-reviewed evaluation of the DeLaval Online Cell Counter as a sensor providing cow-level somatic cell counts at every milking for detecting intramammary infections.

sources.title: Introducing VMS Batch Milking - DeLaval
sources.claim: Robotic milking stalls autonomously prepare the udder and attach teat cups to cows that present themselves, removing the human handling step; this is the purpose-built machine environment in which the automated milk sampling and testing occurs.
sources.transferJustification: Establishes that a live cow can be handled entirely by machine in a purpose-built stall, the E1 setting assumed for the dairy instance.

sources.title: Pharm Robotics inoculates dairy cows at large farm - The Robot Report
sources.claim: Pharm Robotics' SureShot uses RFID identification and an industrial robot arm with a bumper restraint to autonomously inject dairy cows in a parlor exit lane; installed at a large commercial dairy.
sources.transferJustification: Related task (needle delivery of a fixed subcutaneous dose to a restrained cow). It shows autonomous needle work on cattle, but not venipuncture, intradermal tuberculin placement, a 72-hour palpated read, or diagnostic interpretation, so it does not carry over to herd disease testing.

sources.title: Robotics for poultry farming: Challenges and opportunities - ScienceDirect
sources.claim: Faromatics' ceiling-suspended Scout (formerly ChickenBoy) robot autonomously patrols commercial broiler houses with cameras and sensors and flags sick and dead birds and litter problems; it performs no bird handling, sampling or laboratory testing.
sources.transferJustification: Related task (automated flock health monitoring). It covers part of the visual inspection element only; without bird handling, necropsy, swabbing or confirmatory testing it cannot complete the poultry inspect-and-test instance.

sources.title: Vitestro Introduces Aletta: The First-Ever Autonomous Robotic Phlebotomy Device (ARPD)
sources.claim: Vitestro's Aletta is an autonomous robotic ... that locates a vein with AI-guided ultrasound and draws blood, validated on thousands of cooperative human patients in clinical settings.
sources.transferJustification: Related task (autonomous venipuncture). Transfer to veterinary testing fails: it requires a cooperative, still human arm positioned in the device, whereas the animal instances involve haired, moving patients of varied anatomy and also require physical examination and sample handling the device does not perform.

tasks.label: Establish or conduct quarantine or testing procedures that prevent the spread of diseases to other animals or to humans and that comply with applicable government regulations.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Companion-animal practice: a dog or cat presents with suspected contagious disease (parvovirus, canine infectious respiratory disease, ringworm, panleukopenia). The vet directs immediate isolation to the isolation ward, dons PPE, restrains the fractious/ill patient, collects the diagnostic sample (fecal swab, blood, deep pharyngeal or skin sample), runs an in-house test or packages it for the reference lab, sets the disinfection and staff-traffic protocol, and instructs the owner on home isolation and reportable-disease follow-up.

Food-animal / USDA-accredited veterinarian on a beef or dairy farm: official regulatory testing of cattle worked through a chute — caudal-fold tuberculin intradermal injection with a 72-hour palpation read, jugular or coccygeal blood draws for brucellosis/BVD/Johne's, preputial scraping for trichomoniasis — with individual ID verification (ear tags/tattoos), official test charts, CVI/VS forms, and hold orders on positives. Mud, weather, kicking animals, variable chute and handling facilities.

Equine or small-ruminant practice at a boarding barn, sale barn or backyard property: jugular blood draw for a Coggins (EIA) test and interstate health certificate before movement; or setting up and supervising a barn quarantine for a strangles or EHV-1 outbreak — designating isolation stalls, foot baths, dedicated equipment, temperature-monitoring schedules, guttural-pouch/nasal swabs on recovered animals, and coordinating release with the state veterinarian.

Institutional animal facility (animal shelter, research vivarium, zoo, or import quarantine station): veterinarian runs the incoming-animal quarantine program — intake exams and vaccination, assignment to quarantine housing, sampling for screening tests (fecal, blood, serology, sentinel/health-surveillance sampling), interpreting results, deciding release or extended isolation, and documenting compliance with USDA/state or facility regulations.

Commercial poultry or swine production veterinarian: routine surveillance and outbreak response — collecting oropharyngeal/cloacal swabs, blood for NPIP serology, or oral fluids from a house or barn; establishing movement controls, line-of-separation and zoning during an HPAI or PRRS event; overseeing depopulation/disinfection and quarantine release testing under state/USDA rules.

Establishing procedures rather than performing a specific test: writing or revising the practice/facility biosecurity, isolation and rabies-observation SOPs to match state and federal regulations, physically laying out and equipping the isolation area (barriers, signage, PPE stations, dedicated equipment, foot baths), and training staff on the protocol.

sources.title: Cut costs, improve animal welfare and reduce environmental impact with Herd Navigator - DeLaval
sources.claim: DeLaval Herd Navigator automatically draws and analyzes milk samples from individual cows during robotic/parlor milking to flag health problems (mastitis, ketosis) — an automated disease-screening sampling and analysis loop on live animals in a dairy.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated collection and analysis of a diagnostic biological sample from live cattle. It covers only the sample-and-analyze sub-step for a fixed panel of milk biomarkers; it cannot perform official regulatory tests (intradermal tuberculin, serology, PCR swabs), cannot certify results, and takes no quarantine action.

sources.date: 2024-08-21 (product page and insight article; system commercial for years)

sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated repeated blood sampling from live animals in a vivarium.
