tasks.label: Provide care to a wide range of animals or specialize in a particular species, such as horses or exotic birds.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Companion-animal preventive/wellness visit in a small-animal clinic exam room: lift and restrain a conscious dog or cat, take temperature/pulse/respiration, auscultate heart and lungs, palpate abdomen and lymph nodes, examine eyes, ears, skin and mouth, give subcutaneous vaccines and parasite preventives, trim nails, and discuss findings with the owner.

Sick or emergency patient in a clinic/animal hospital: triage and hands-on exam of a painful, fractious or collapsed dog/cat, jugular or cephalic venipuncture, IV catheter placement, positioning for radiographs/ultrasound, wound care, fluid and drug administration, and monitoring of the hospitalized animal.

Surgical or dental procedure under general anesthesia in a clinic surgical suite: induce and monitor anesthesia, clip and prep, perform spay/neuter, mass removal, laceration repair or dental scaling and extractions, close, and recover the patient.

Large-animal ambulatory call at a barn, stable, dairy or feedlot: equine lameness and dental exams, sedation, colic workup; bovine herd health with transrectal palpation/ultrasound pregnancy checks, fresh-cow exams, treatment of sick individuals and on-farm procedures, in stalls, chutes and headlocks whose layout varies site to site.

High-throughput preventive treatment of production animals in a dedicated handling facility under the veterinarian's protocol: mass injection vaccination of smolt at a fish farm/hatchery, hatchery vaccination of poultry, or programmed vaccine/reproductive-hormone injections of dairy cows as they pass through a parlor lane.

Exotic pet, avian, zoo or laboratory animal care: handling and examining a parrot, reptile, rabbit or small mammal, or an immobilized zoo species, taking samples, giving injections and treating species-specific disease in an exotics practice or zoo hospital.

sources.developer: Johns Hopkins University / Children's National Hospital
sources.title: Robot Performs First Laparoscopic Surgery without Human Help - Johns Hopkins Technology Ventures
sources.claim: STAR performed autonomous laparoscopic suturing (intestinal anastomosis) on a live anesthetized pig in a research operating room, but only that one surgical step, with human prep, port placement and fluorescent markers, under supervision.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous soft-tissue surgery on a pig. It is the closest robotic analogue to veterinary surgery, but covers a single suturing step on an already anesthetized, prepped and ported animal, not an entire veterinary operation from induction to recovery.

sources.title: Doctors Let AI Control Surgery Robot and Perform Gallbladder Removal on Its Own (Futurism)
sources.claim: SRT-H autonomously executed phases of gallbladder removal after imitation learning, but on pig cadaver/ex vivo tissue in a laboratory, not on a live veterinary patient.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous cholecystectomy phases on porcine tissue. It marks the frontier of surgical autonomy; because it works on excised/cadaver tissue in a lab rig, it does not substantiate performing a whole surgical procedure on a live veterinary patient.

sources.title: Vaccination - Maskon
sources.claim: Commercially deployed, fully automated fish vaccination machines singulate, orient and inject anesthetized smolt using machine vision at up to 40,000 fish per hour with one operator, then sort them.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: administering injectable vaccines to live animals, a core veterinary care action. The machine performs the whole injection workflow (singulate, orient, machine-vision-guided injection, sort) in a purpose-built line, matching the mass-vaccination instance.

sources.title: Control of salmon lice through optical delousing in commercial salmonid aquaculture (Aquaculture, ScienceDirect)
sources.claim: Stingray optical delousing laser nodes autonomously identify and destroy sea lice on free-swimming salmon and have been supplied commercially to Norwegian sea cages since 2014.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: delivering an antiparasitic treatment to farmed animals. It shows autonomous machine-vision treatment of animals inside a purpose-built installation, supporting the production-animal preventive-treatment instance only.

sources.title: Pharm Robotics inoculates dairy cows at large farm - The Robot Report
sources.claim: SureShot uses an RFID-triggered industrial robot arm and needleless injector to inoculate dairy cows held in a bumper restraint as they leave the milking barn; injections on live cows have been run at a large farm, while the full stack is still being refined (fully automated shots so far shown on a model cow).
sources.transferJustification: Related task: injecting vaccines/reproductive products into cattle. It shows purpose-built robotic injection of restrained livestock, but only injection - no examination, diagnosis or treatment of sick animals - and it remains a pilot/MVP.

sources.title: Revolutionizing Dairy Farming: How Robots Benefit Cows & Farmers - IEEE Spectrum
sources.claim: Lely's Astronaut A5 milking robot autonomously locates the udder of an unrestrained cow with a laser-guided arm, cleans teats, attaches cups and records health indicators; it is in commercial use on dairy farms in purpose-built milking boxes.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous manipulation of a live animal's anatomy in a purpose-built box. It is the most mature animal-contact robot in commercial use, yet it performs a fixed husbandry routine on one species and does not examine, diagnose or treat patients.

sources.title: Faromatics - EIT Food
sources.claim: The most widely commercialized livestock health robot only monitors: ChickenBoy is a ceiling-rail robot using sensors and AI to flag welfare and health risks in broiler houses; it does not handle or treat birds.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: animal health surveillance in a livestock facility. It bounds what deployed animal-health robots do - sensing and flagging - showing no hands-on examination or treatment capability transfers to veterinary care.

tasks.label: Determine the effects of drug therapies, antibiotics, or new surgical techniques by testing them on animals.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Rodent efficacy/toxicology study in a vivarium or CRO: research vet oversees and performs multi-week dosing (oral gavage, IP/SC injection) of mice or rats, daily clinical observations and body weights, interim blood sampling, then terminal necropsy and tissue collection, and interprets the drug's effects.

Rodent PK/PD or infusion study using surgically catheterized, conscious rats/mice in tethered sampling cages: timed drug dosing/infusion plus serial blood, bile or urine collection over 24-72 h, samples chilled and delivered for bioanalysis to characterize drug exposure and response.

Large-animal preclinical surgical/device study (pig, dog, sheep) in a research surgical suite: induce and maintain anesthesia, perform the novel surgical technique or implant, achieve hemostasis and closure, recover the animal, provide post-op analgesia and monitoring, then assess outcome (imaging, necropsy, histology).

Clinical trial in client-owned dogs/cats at a veterinary teaching hospital or specialty practice: screen and enroll patients, discuss consent with owners, physically examine and restrain awake animals, administer or dispense the investigational drug, draw blood and image, score adverse events, and follow up over weeks.

Food-animal field efficacy trial of an antibiotic or vaccine on commercial dairies, feedlots or swine barns: identify and enroll animals, restrain in chutes/headlocks, inject treatment or placebo, take blood/nasal/milk samples, then clinically score and record outcomes in pens or pasture over days to weeks across differing farm layouts and weather.

Aquaculture or poultry facility trial: vaccinate/medicate thousands of smolt or birds at a hatchery or research barn, run the disease challenge, and read out effects by mortality counts, lesion scoring and sampling of individual animals.

sources.system: BASi Culex NxT Automated In Vivo Sampling System (with Raturn caging)
sources.title: BASi | Culex Automated Blood Sampling Systems
sources.claim: Commercial automated in vivo sampling system that autonomously collects serial blood, bile and urine samples from awake, catheterized, freely-moving rodents in purpose-built tethered cages, used at pharmaceutical companies, universities and CROs for PK/PD studies.

sources.system: BASi Empis Automated Drug Infusion System
sources.title: BASi | Culex Automated Blood Sampling Systems
sources.claim: Companion automated dosing/infusion module that delivers scheduled drug doses to the same catheterized rodents, so that dosing plus serial sampling of a PK/PD study runs unattended.
sources.transferJustification: Same task (administering the test article and collecting the samples that determine its effects), same animals (rats/mice) and same purpose-built caging as the sampling system.

sources.title: PiDose: an open-source system for accurate and automated oral drug administration to group-housed mice (Scientific Reports)
sources.claim: Home-cage attached device that identifies group-housed mice by RFID, weighs each animal and delivers an accurate bodyweight-scaled daily drug dose in drinking water for weeks to months without experimenter handling.
sources.transferJustification: Chronic oral drug dosing of study mice is the administration step of this same task; it shows automation of dosing but not of clinical observation, sampling or necropsy.

sources.title: Robot performs first laparoscopic surgery without human help | ScienceDaily
sources.claim: Autonomous robot performed a laparoscopic intestinal anastomosis on live pigs without human guidance, but only that suturing step: the team anesthetized, positioned, placed ports and exposed the bowel, and assessed outcomes.
sources.transferJustification: Surgery on a live pig in a research surgical suite is the core act of testing a new surgical technique on animals; it substantiates autonomy for one intra-operative step only.

sources.title: Pharm Robotics inoculates dairy cows at large farm - The Robot Report
sources.claim: Industrial robot arm with needle-free injector automatically identifies dairy cows by RFID at the parlor exit, restrains them in a gate and injects pharmaceuticals; as of mid-2024 still in proof-of-concept/MVP testing at a rotary dairy rather than routine deployment.
sources.transferJustification: Injecting an identified individual cow is the administration step of a food-animal drug trial; it does not cover enrollment sampling, clinical scoring or outcome assessment.

sources.title: Vaccination - Aquaculture - Skala Maskon
sources.claim: Commercially deployed machine (85+ plants sold) that automatically anesthetizes, singularizes, orients and injects farmed salmon smolt with up to four vaccines using machine vision, at up to 40,000 fish per hour with one operator.
sources.transferJustification: Mass injection of biologics into fish is the administration step of an aquaculture vaccine/drug trial; the challenge, mortality reading and lesion scoring that determine effects remain manual.

sources.title: Vitestro's robotic blood drawing device meets trial endpoints
sources.claim: Autonomous venipuncture robot met a 95% first-stick endpoint in a human clinical trial, showing autonomous blood draw only on cooperative, immobilized human arms in a clinical setting.
sources.transferJustification: Cited as the closest analogue for trial blood sampling; it does not transfer to unsedated dogs/cats or livestock, whose jugular/cephalic veins are haired and mobile and require species-specific restraint and handling.

Administer nursing care to ill, injured, convalescent, or disabled patients. May advise patients on health maintenance and disease prevention or provide case management. Licensing or registration required.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

tasks.label: Administer medications to patients and monitor patients for reactions or side effects.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Scheduled oral med pass on a hospital inpatient unit (med-surg/telemetry): pull doses from the automated dispensing cabinet, check the order and hold parameters (e.g., hold beta-blocker if HR low), scan the patient's wristband and each barcode, position the patient, hand pills/liquids with water or give them via NG/PEG tube, confirm ingestion, document in the eMAR and watch for GI upset, sedation, hypotension or allergic reaction.

Intravenous medications on an inpatient unit: reconstitute or spike an IV piggyback, prime tubing, connect to a peripheral IV/PICC/central line, program the smart pump, or draw up and slow IV-push a drug (e.g., opioid, antiemetic, antibiotic) with saline flushes; stay with the patient during and after administration watching for infiltration, flushing, dyspnea or anaphylaxis, and stop the infusion and escalate if a reaction occurs.

Subcutaneous or intramuscular injections in a hospital, clinic or occupational/vaccination setting: sliding-scale insulin, prophylactic heparin, depot antipsychotic, or influenza/other vaccine; select and prep the site on a seated or lying patient, inject, apply a bandage, document, and observe the patient (often 15 minutes post-vaccine) for local reaction, hypoglycemia or hypersensitivity.

Infusion/oncology center: administer premedications, then a chemotherapy or biologic infusion through an implanted port or PICC, titrate rate per protocol, and monitor intensively for hypersensitivity/infusion reactions, extravasation and vital-sign changes, stopping the infusion and giving rescue drugs when a reaction occurs.

Long-term care / rehab facility med pass: 20+ residents in rooms and dayrooms, crushing tablets and mixing in applesauce for dysphagia, applying transdermal patches, instilling eye and ear drops, giving meds to residents with dementia who resist or spit them out, then charting and watching for falls, sedation or GI side effects.

Home health or hospice visit: in the patient's own home, administer an IV antibiotic through a home infusion line, give a subcutaneous injection or a controlled-substance dose, or set up and give oral meds for a patient who cannot self-manage; assess the patient before and after, teach the family, and watch for adverse effects with no other clinician present.

sources.title: Performance, Safety, and Patient Experience of an Autonomous Robotic Phlebotomy Device: A Multicenter Trial (Clinical Chemistry)
sources.claim: Vitestro's Aletta Autonomous Robotic Phlebotomy Device autonomously performs venipuncture on outpatients who place an arm in the device, in hospital outpatient phlebotomy departments, with one supervising professional per three devices; multicenter trial of 1,633 patients showed 94.5% first-stick success and 0.6% mild adverse events.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: diagnostic venipuncture. It shares the object (a seated patient's arm vein), the precision class (needle placement under ultrasound/NIR guidance) and the environment (a hospital outpatient draw room), so it substantiates the needle-into-patient element of injection/IV medication work. It does not deliver a drug, verify a medication order, or monitor the patient for drug reactions, so it does not substantiate the whole medication-administration instance.

sources.title: Vitestro raises $70m to fuel blood-drawing robot's global commercial readiness
sources.claim: The Aletta device received a CE mark in August 2024 and began commercial deployment in European healthcare settings in March 2025, confirming it is a fielded system rather than a laboratory prototype.
sources.transferJustification: Same related task as above (diagnostic blood collection); cited to establish deployment maturity and the type of facility (European hospital/laboratory outpatient blood-collection settings) in which autonomous needle work is actually done.

sources.title: Robot performs autonomous needle-less injection | Robotics and Automation Magazine
sources.claim: Cobionix's Cobi platform performed what was reported as the first autonomous robotic intramuscular ... a needle-free high-pressure jet, with the robot locating the injection site on a person's shoulder without a clinician operating it; this was a one-off laboratory demonstration in 2021, not clinical use.

sources.system: Autonomous intelligent needle-free vaccine injection robot
sources.title: China releases its first autonomous intelligent robot for needle-free vaccine injection - Global Times
sources.claim: Tongji University demonstrated an autonomous needle-free vaccine injection robot that delivers a dose to a patient's arm with dose accuracy of 0.01 mL and adjustable injection depth; the developers stated it would need one to two years of clinical trials before practical use.

sources.title: Swisslog Healthcare Partners with Diligent Robotics to Enhance Hospital Logistics
sources.claim: Diligent Robotics' Moxi operates autonomously in more than 25 US ..., but its medication role is last-mile transport of medications, lab samples and supplies through corridors and elevators to nursing units; it does not administer drugs to patients or monitor them.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: intra-hospital medication logistics in the same E2 corridors where nurses give medications. It shows that the mature hospital robots deployed today stop at delivery to the unit; the bedside acts of verifying, administering and monitoring are not part of any deployed system's envelope.

sources.system: In-home robotic medication dispensing and telecare device
sources.developer: study by Parkkari et al., Clinical Therapeutics (Evondos-type sachet dispenser)
sources.title: An In-home Advanced Robotic System to Manage Elderly Home-care Patients' Medications: A Pilot Safety and Usability Study
sources.claim: A peer-reviewed pilot of an in-home robotic medication dispenser with telecare found 97.7% on-time sachet retrieval and no missed doses across 17 nursing-home patients and 27 home-care patients; the device dispenses pre-packed sachets to patients who then self-administer, with nurses still visiting and assessing.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: scheduled dose release to a self-administering patient at home. It shares the setting (private homes) and the medications, but the machine only presents a pre-packed sachet; it performs no pre-administration clinical check, no confirmation of ingestion, no injection or IV work, and no monitoring for adverse reactions, so it does not cover the nurse's instance.

tasks.label: Maintain accurate, detailed reports and records.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

tasks.label: Monitor, record, and report symptoms or changes in patients' conditions.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Med-surg/telemetry inpatient unit: RN performs shift and focused reassessments on 4-6 assigned patients — auscultates lung/heart/bowel sounds, palpates pulses and edema, inspects IV sites, incisions and skin, checks mental status and pain, compares with prior findings, charts in the EHR flowsheet, and escalates abnormal findings to the provider by SBAR page/call.

ICU/step-down: continuous surveillance of a ventilated or hemodynamically unstable patient — reads bedside monitor/vent/pressor data, performs hourly neuro checks (pupils, GCS, motor), suctions and observes secretions, palpates for perfusion, documents q1h, and notifies the intensivist of trends and acute changes.

Emergency department: triage and serial reassessment of undifferentiated patients in bays and the waiting room — obtains vitals, inspects wounds/rashes, assesses breathing, pain and level of consciousness, watches for deterioration in a crowded noisy space, documents, and reports to the emergency physician.

Skilled nursing/long-term care or rehab: RN rounds on 20-30 residents per shift — checks skin and wounds, appetite, continence, gait/fall events, behavior and cognition changes, reviews aide-reported vitals, documents changes of condition, and calls the physician and family.

Ambulatory setting (infusion suite, dialysis, PACU, procedural recovery, clinic): RN monitors patients during and after treatment for reactions and complications — infiltration, hypotension, bleeding, nausea, airway status — repeats vitals and focused checks, documents on the flow record, and reports to the physician.

Home health/hospice visit: RN assesses a patient in their own home — listens to lungs, checks edema, wound and catheter sites, weighs the patient, reviews symptoms and medication effects with patient/family in a cluttered non-standard setting, documents on a laptop/tablet, and reports changes to the physician.

sources.title: Moxi — Diligent Robotics
sources.claim: Moxi, the most widely deployed hospital mobile manipulator in the US, is explicitly scoped to non-patient-facing logistics work (supply, lab-sample and medication runs); it does no patient assessment, monitoring or charting.
sources.transferJustification: Delivery/fetch task in the same environment (hospital ward). Cited to show the state of deployed autonomous hospital robots: they navigate wards reliably but the vendor scopes them away from any patient-facing monitoring work.

sources.title: Diligent Robotics completes 300,000 pharmacy deliveries with Moxi - The Robot Report
sources.claim: Scale of real hospital deployment of autonomous mobile manipulators as of mid-2025 — 30+ US hospitals, 300,000 pharmacy deliveries — all logistics, no patient monitoring.
sources.transferJustification: Related task (intra-hospital transport) in the identical E2 setting; establishes that autonomous ward navigation is solved while patient assessment is not attempted.

sources.title: NVIDIA, Foxconn and Taiwan Medical Centers Bring Agentic and Physical AI to 'Healthy Taiwan'
sources.claim: Nurabot, moved into clinical operations in Taiwanese hospitals by 2026, handles transport and logistics so that nurses can do direct patient care; patient assessment remains with the nurses.
sources.transferJustification: Ward logistics robot in the same hospital setting; shows the frontier of deployed 'nursing' robots stops short of monitoring and reporting patients' conditions.

sources.system: Dr. Spot (Boston Dynamics Spot with MIT/BWH payloads)
sources.developer: MIT, Brigham and Women's Hospital, Boston Dynamics
sources.title: Why Boston Dynamics Is Putting Legged Robots in Hospitals - IEEE Spectrum
sources.claim: The best-known robot for taking patient vital signs, Dr. Spot, is a clinician-operated telepresence platform: it carries contactless vital-sign sensors and an interview tablet but does not autonomously assess, chart or escalate.
sources.transferJustification: Directly on-task (vital-sign monitoring of patients in an ED triage context), but teleoperated, so under the autonomy rule it cannot support a positive judgment.

sources.system: Collaborative robotic platform for autonomous auscultation
sources.title: Development of a Collaborative Robotic Platform for Autonomous Auscultation
sources.claim: Autonomous robotic auscultation exists only as a laboratory collaborative-arm prototype that locates chest points and judges sound quality — one sensing sub-step of a nursing assessment, with no record or clinical report produced.
sources.transferJustification: Auscultation is one sub-step of the RN assessment in this task; the prototype works on prepared subjects in a lab and produces no clinical interpretation, documentation, or escalation.

sources.title: Aeolus Debuts Autonomous Dual-arm Humanoid Robot at CES2023 - Interesting Engineering
sources.claim: Deployed eldercare monitoring robots (aeo) perform autonomous night patrol and alert staff to falls or safety anomalies, but perform no clinical assessment or documentation of residents' symptoms.
sources.transferJustification: Closest deployed analogue to nurse rounding in a long-term care facility: vision-based safety surveillance with staff alerting, not the multi-modal symptom assessment, charting and provider reporting this task requires.

sources.title: New Robot Can Perform Diagnostic Blood Draws - Clinical Lab Products
sources.claim: Autonomous robot-to-patient physical contact is commercially demonstrated only for one narrow, fixture-supported procedure (venipuncture), marking the boundary of current autonomy in patient-contact work.
sources.transferJustification: Related patient-contact task (blood draw) with the arm placed in a purpose-built rest; shows that even under E1-style structuring, autonomy today covers one standardized procedure, not open-ended assessment, recording and reporting of changing conditions.

tasks.label: Provide health care, first aid, immunizations, or assistance in convalescence or rehabilitation in locations such as schools, hospitals, or industry.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Acute-care hospital inpatient shift: RN provides hands-on care at the bedside — head-to-toe assessment, vital signs, IV starts and med administration, wound/dressing changes, drain and catheter care, repositioning, and ambulating post-op patients in the room and corridor. Patients vary in size, cognition, lines and drains; conditions change hour to hour.

Routine adult immunization: cooperative adult patients at a clinic, workplace/occupational-health flu clinic, or public-health site. Verify record and consent, screen for contraindications, draw up and give IM deltoid injection, bandage, document in registry, observe for reactions.

Pediatric/school immunization session: multiple vaccines to children in a school health room or pediatric clinic — consent checks, distraction and comforting, holding or restraining a squirming child, injecting small deltoid or thigh, managing fainting or crying.

First aid / episodic acute care in a school health office or industrial occupational-health clinic: assess a laceration, sprain, burn, nosebleed, asthma attack, or eye splash; irrigate and clean, apply dressings, splint or ice, dispense OTC care, decide whether to return to class/work or refer to ER.

Convalescence and rehabilitation assistance in a rehab unit or skilled nursing facility: bed-to-chair transfers, sit-to-stand, gait training with a walker down a hallway, range-of-motion exercises, toileting and ADL assistance, fall prevention for weak or unsteady patients.

Home health / community nursing visit to a convalescent patient's private residence: vital signs, wound and ostomy care, medication set-up and injection, assessment of the home environment, patient/caregiver teaching. Layout, lighting, clutter, and pets differ at every address.

sources.title: Vitestro gains CE mark for autonomous blood drawing robot
sources.claim: Vitestro's Aletta performs autonomous venipuncture on patients (needle insertion guided by near-infrared and ultrasound imaging) and is CE-marked for clinical use in EU hospitals and labs.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: diagnostic venipuncture. It is the same class of act as vaccine administration — sterile needle insertion into a seated patient's presented arm with per-patient consumable exchange — at higher precision (vein targeting) than an IM deltoid injection. It substantiates that the physical injection procedure can be completed autonomously on real patients at clinical quality.

sources.title: Frequently Asked Questions — Vitestro
sources.claim: Aletta is commercially available and in clinical use at named hospitals and labs (OLVG, St. Antonius, Deventer, Amsterdam UMC, Odense University Hospital); it picks a fresh sterile needle-set for each puncture, and if no suitable vein is found it stops and staff decide how to proceed.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: outpatient phlebotomy. Establishes the operating environment (a hospital blood-draw department where the patient sits and presents an arm to a fixed station) and the residual human role (suitability screening, exception handling), which is the environment an automated immunization station would replicate.

sources.title: Cobi robot autonomously performs intramuscular injection without needles
sources.claim: Cobionix's Cobi robot autonomously delivered a needle-free intramuscular injection to a person without a clinician involved, but it remained a working prototype rather than a marketed or deployed product.
sources.transferJustification: Same task (immunization by intramuscular injection), but only a laboratory demonstration on a fixtured, cooperative subject; it supports the purpose-built-station case and does not substantiate completion in a general clinic.

sources.title: Robots Are Joining The Team And Elevating The Value Of Humans
sources.claim: The largest deployed hospital mobile-manipulator fleet, Diligent's Moxi, performs supply and medication fetch-and-deliver runs requested by staff through an app; it does not perform hands-on patient care.

sources.title: Foxconn deploys AI systems across Taiwan hospitals
sources.claim: Foxconn's Nurabot nursing robot, validated at Taichung Veterans General Hospital and rolling out to other Taiwanese hospitals, is scoped to transport and logistics work, freeing nurses for direct patient care rather than performing it.

sources.title: AutoPeel: Adhesion-aware Safe Peeling Trajectory Optimization for Robotic Wound Care
sources.claim: Robotic wound dressing change is still an open research problem addressed in simulation and bench trials, not a deployed clinical capability.

sources.title: Lokomat Robotic Gait Rehabilitation | UM Shore Regional Health
sources.claim: Lokomat robot-assisted gait training is widely installed in rehabilitation hospitals, but the patient must be harnessed over a treadmill and the session set up and supervised by clinical staff; the device drives the legs through a gait cycle rather than performing nursing rehabilitation assistance end to end.

tasks.label: Conduct specified laboratory tests.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Bedside capillary blood glucose check on an inpatient or nursing-home resident: nurse verifies the order and patient ID, lances a fingertip at the bedside (patient may be in bed, confused, edematous, with IV lines and dressings), applies the drop to a strip in a handheld glucometer, reads and documents the value, and acts on it (e.g., insulin dosing) within minutes.

Dipstick/waived chemistry test on a specimen handed to the nurse: urine dipstick urinalysis, urine pregnancy test, or fecal occult blood card run on a clinic counter or unit utility-room bench, with timing, visual or small-reader interpretation, quality-control logging and documentation in the chart.

Rapid infectious-disease test in a clinic, ED or occupational-health setting: nurse collects a nasal/nasopharyngeal or throat swab from a seated (sometimes pediatric, coughing, uncooperative) patient, then elutes the swab and runs a lateral-flow antigen cassette or a small point-of-care molecular analyzer and reports the result.

Point-of-care blood cartridge testing in ICU/ED/cath lab/dialysis: nurse obtains a venous or line-drawn blood sample and runs a POC chemistry/hemoglobin/coagulation test (i-STAT-type cartridge, POC INR, activated clotting time), with cartridge fill, analyzer operation, QC and result documentation.

Arterial blood gas testing in ICU/ED/PACU: nurse draws arterial blood (arterial puncture or sampling from an indwelling arterial line), expels air, mixes, and immediately runs the sample on a blood gas analyzer, with results needed within minutes for ventilator or resuscitation decisions.

Home health, school, or community nurse performing a point-of-care test at the patient's home or in the field: fingerstick glucose or INR at a kitchen table, urine dipstick on a specimen from the patient's bathroom, or rapid strep at a school clinic, with variable lighting, surfaces, pets and clutter.

sources.title: Aletta® - Vitestro
sources.claim: Vitestro's Aletta is a CE-marked autonomous robotic phlebotomy device that performs the entire venous blood draw — vein selection, needle insertion, tube changes and bandaging — with the patient's arm placed in the purpose-built device; it is in initial commercial rollout in European labs and hospitals.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: obtaining the blood specimen, which is the sample-acquisition half of a nurse-conducted blood test (glucose, chemistry, coagulation). Transfer holds because the objects (patient arm, vacuum tubes) and precision (millimetre vein cannulation) equal or exceed those of a nurse's fingerstick, and the drawn tube is directly consumable by automated analyzers.

sources.title: Vitestro's robotic blood drawing device meets trial endpoints
sources.claim: In the EU pivotal trial the Vitestro autonomous blood-drawing device reached 95% first-stick success and 0.6% hemolysis, comparable to human phlebotomists, indicating worker-quality specimen acquisition.
sources.transferJustification: Same as above: substantiates that the specimen-collection step of a nurse-conducted blood test can be done autonomously at human error rates.

sources.system: MagicNurse Intelligent Venipuncture & Blood Collection Robot
sources.developer: Beijing Magicnurse Surgical Robot Technology Co. / Zhongshan Hospital, Fudan University
sources.title: Clinical application of a fully automated blood collection robot and its assessment of blood collection quality of anticoagulant specimens
sources.claim: The MagicNurse intelligent venipuncture and blood-collection robot has been used clinically at Zhongshan Hospital, Fudan University; data from 6,255 patients showed a 94.3% puncture success rate and specimen quality suitable for anticoagulant testing, with patients seated at the fixed robot station.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: routine venous specimen collection in a hospital draw room. It substantiates the patient-contact, sample-acquisition half of nurse-conducted blood tests at clinical volume and quality; the collected anticoagulated tubes are the inputs analyzers require.

sources.developer: Hitachi High-Tech Corporation with Fujita Health University Hospital
sources.title: Hospital robots collect and deliver blood samples (Nature Portfolio)
sources.claim: Hitachi High-Tech and Fujita Health University have built and trialled an automatic fingertip blood-sampling device in which the patient rests a palm on the machine, which grips the finger, maps capillaries with near-infrared cameras, chooses a puncture point and lances it, using an automated tourniquet to obtain up to ~400 µL.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated capillary (fingerstick) sampling — the exact sample-acquisition step of a nurse's bedside glucose check — performed at a fixed station rather than at the bedside.

sources.developer: University research group (published in Scientific Reports)
sources.title: Autonomous swab robot for naso- and oropharyngeal COVID-19 screening
sources.claim: An autonomous, force-controlled swab robot station performed naso- and oropharyngeal COVID-19 swab collection on human subjects in two clinical studies, with the subject positioned at the robot station.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: patient swab specimen collection, the patient-contact step of a nurse-run rapid respiratory test; same anatomy, same swab, comparable delicacy requirements.

sources.title: The LINGCAI-II System: A Sampling Robotic System for Autonomous Oropharyngeal Swab Sampling
sources.claim: The LINGCAI-II robotic sampling workstation performs automatic oropharyngeal swab sampling and, with its internal function stations, completes the whole specimen-handling process without manual assistance; it was clinically trialled on 116 COVID-19 patients.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: end-to-end swab collection and specimen packaging at a fixed workstation, covering the collection and specimen-handling steps of a nurse-conducted rapid infectious-disease test.

sources.system: CLINITEK Novus Automated Urine Chemistry Analyzer (Sysmex UN-Series)
sources.title: CLINITEK Novus® Automated Urine Chemistry Analyzer | Sysmex America
sources.claim: The CLINITEK Novus is a fully automated walk-away urine chemistry analyzer for clinical laboratory use: specimens are loaded in racks onto a conveyor and the instrument dispenses cassettes, performs dry-pad strip chemistry, and reports results at up to 240 samples/hour.

sources.system: Total laboratory automation (Abbott, Roche, Siemens, Beckman track systems)
sources.developer: Abbott / Roche / Siemens Healthineers / Beckman Coulter
sources.title: Total Laboratory Automation Samples on Track (Clinical Laboratory News, ADLM)
sources.claim: Total laboratory automation systems integrate pre-analytics, analytics and post-analytics so that presented specimens are processed, tested and stored with minimal human intervention, and are in routine use in high-volume clinical laboratories.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: performing the analytical measurement (glucose, chemistry, coagulation, urinalysis) on a presented specimen — the assay half of the nurse's point-of-care test, delivering the same measured result the employer accepts.

sources.title: WASPLab® Automation for Microbiology | Clinical Pathology Laboratories
sources.claim: Copan's WASP/WASPLab uses robotic specimen processing — uncapping, pipetting, plating, streaking, slide preparation and ... of patient specimens including urines — and has been in clinical microbiology laboratory use since 2008.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic handling of clinical specimen containers (uncapping, aspirating, transferring) and running the test on them — the bench-side handling a nurse does when performing a dipstick or cassette test, at equal or finer precision.

sources.system: ABB robotic automated COVID-19 testing system
sources.title: ABB robots aid rapid automated testing for COVID-19 virus
sources.claim: ABB robots run Taiwan's first fully automated COVID-19 testing system, handling the repetitive sample-preparation and testing steps in a laboratory cell that previously required technicians.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: running the assay on a collected respiratory swab specimen — the analytical step of the nurse's rapid respiratory test, with the same specimen type and an accepted diagnostic output.

tasks.label: Assess the needs of individuals, families, or communities, including assessment of individuals' home or work environments, to identify potential health or safety problems.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Hospital inpatient admission / shift nursing assessment at the bedside on a med-surg or ICU unit: interview the patient and family, perform a head-to-toe physical assessment (auscultation, palpation, skin and wound inspection, edema, neuro checks), take or verify vitals, run fall-risk, skin-breakdown, nutrition, pain and psychosocial screens, inspect the immediate patient environment (bed rails, lines, call bell, clutter), then synthesize findings into documented problems and care-plan needs.

Home health or hospice RN visit to a private residence: comprehensive (e.g., OASIS) assessment of a homebound patient plus a walkthrough of the home to identify hazards - throw rugs, poor lighting, missing stair rails, bathroom transfers, space heaters, hoarding, pets, expired or duplicated medications, refrigeration and food, working smoke alarm - and assessment of caregiver capacity; conditions differ house to house and are not kept to any standard.

Public/community health nurse home visit (maternal-child home visiting, elder outreach, communicable-disease follow-up): assess family needs and coping, infant sleep environment, safe storage of chemicals and firearms, lead/mold/pest exposure, heat or utility problems, food security; conducted in varied private homes, apartments, shelters or transitional housing.

Long-term care / rehab facility RN resident assessment (MDS-driven and ongoing): interview and observe the resident, physical and functional assessment, cognition and behavior, skin and continence checks, plus a safety review of the resident's room and equipment (bed height, wheelchair fit, call light, tubing, walker, clutter) inside a facility with standard layout and equipment.

Occupational health nurse walkthrough of an employer worksite (plant floor, warehouse, office): observe tasks, postures and PPE use, review exposures, machine guarding, first-aid and eyewash provisions, ergonomic risk and injury patterns, interview workers and supervisors, and produce findings on employee health and safety needs.

sources.title: Moxi - Diligent Robotics
sources.claim: The most widely deployed autonomous US hospital robot performs fetch-and-deliver logistics, explicitly non-patient-facing work, not patient assessment.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: hospital nursing support. It is the benchmark autonomous robot working inside the same E2 hospital units where instance 0 occurs; its scope is explicitly non-patient-facing, so it does not substantiate performing a nursing assessment there.

sources.system: Dr. Spot (Boston Dynamics Spot with contactless monitoring payload)
sources.developer: MIT / Brigham and Women's Hospital / Boston Dynamics
sources.title: Robot Takes Contact-free Measurements of Patients' Vital Signs | MIT for a Better World
sources.claim: Robotic contactless vital-sign measurement in a hospital triage setting was achieved only under human remote control, and covered vitals alone rather than a nursing needs assessment.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: patient vital-sign collection, a sub-step of nursing assessment. Even this narrow sub-step required continuous teleoperation in an ED triage tent, so it cannot support a positive judgment for a whole assessment instance.

sources.title: AI Robotics, Digital Twins, and MONAI Contributions Highlight Hon Hai Foxconn's Smart Healthcare Vision at GTC Taipei 2025
sources.claim: A commercially launching hospital nursing robot's clinical scope is delivery, specimen transport, ward patrol and patient education - no assessment of patient needs or environmental hazards.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: bedside nursing support in wards and long-term care. It is the frontier deployment for nursing robots in facilities like instances 0 and 3, and its stated task list contains no patient or environment assessment.

sources.system: Autonomously navigating fall-detection robot (NIA-funded SBIR project)
sources.developer: NIA SBIR team, reported in Advances in Geriatric Medicine and Research
sources.title: Robots in Nursing Homes: Helping Nurses Detect and Prevent Falls
sources.claim: In a nursing home, an autonomously patrolling robot detects falls and fall risk but hands the evaluation to human staff via its camera; the assessment judgment remains human.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: safety-hazard (fall risk) detection in resident rooms, the closest robotic analogue to the environmental-hazard part of instances 1 and 3. The robot only raises alerts; humans perform the evaluation, so it does not complete the assessment.

sources.developer: academic groups (survey of 2021-2026 systems, incl. fully autonomous thyroid scanning)
sources.title: SAMe: A Semantic Anatomy Mapping Engine for Robotic Ultrasound
sources.claim: Autonomous robotic physical examination exists only as narrow, single-modality imaging (e.g., thyroid or carotid ultrasound) in research settings with a cooperative, positioned subject.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous hands-on examination of a patient. It marks the frontier of machine-performed physical exam - one imaging modality on a fixtured body region - which is far short of a holistic nursing needs assessment, so it does not substantiate even an E1 version of any instance.

tasks.label: Prepare patients for and assist with examinations or treatments.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Hospital inpatient unit: RN prepares a patient for a bedside procedure (lumbar puncture, central line, paracentesis, complex dressing change) — explains the procedure and verifies consent, gathers and opens supplies onto a sterile field, undresses/positions and drapes the patient (often lateral or sitting, sometimes an obese, confused, or painful patient), hands items to the physician, steadies the patient, monitors vitals and comfort, then applies dressing and repositions.

Outpatient clinic or physician office: RN rooms the patient, takes vital signs, assists the patient to undress and into a gown, positions them on the exam table (supine, lithotomy for pelvic/Pap, prone for skin lesion removal), sets out and hands instruments and specimen containers, chaperones and reassures during the exam, labels specimens, helps the patient dress and off the table.

Emergency department or urgent care: RN prepares a patient for an urgent procedure (laceration repair, splinting/reduction, Foley or NG placement, incision and drainage) — cuts away clothing, cleanses and exposes the site, opens a procedure tray, positions and physically steadies an anxious, intoxicated, or pain-limited patient, hands supplies and medications during the procedure, monitors the patient throughout.

Perioperative or procedural suite (pre-op holding, endoscopy, cath lab, interventional radiology): RN verifies identity/consent/site, gowns the patient, clips and preps skin, places IV and monitoring leads, assists transfer from stretcher to procedure table and positions/pads the patient, drapes, assists the proceduralist during the case, and monitors sedation and recovery.

Home health visit (or hospice/community setting): RN prepares a patient in their own home for an examination or treatment — clears a work surface in a cluttered room, moves furniture and pets aside, positions the patient in a home bed, recliner, or bathroom, drapes and exposes a wound or catheter site, sets up supplies from a bag, and assists the visiting clinician or performs the treatment with a family member present.

sources.title: Diligent Robotics completes 300,000 pharmacy deliveries with Moxi - The Robot Report
sources.claim: Moxi, the most widely deployed autonomous hospital mobile manipulator (25+ U.S. hospitals), performs supply and pharmacy deliveries and elevator rides; its deployed work is logistics, with no preparation of or physical contact with patients.
sources.transferJustification: Related task (hospital materials transport). Cited to show what deployed autonomous hospital robots actually do — item fetch-and-deliver in corridors — and that no deployed system undertakes patient preparation, positioning, draping, or procedural assistance.

sources.title: Performance, Safety, and Patient Experience of an Autonomous Robotic Phlebotomy Device: A Multicenter Trial | Clinical Chemistry
sources.claim: The Aletta Autonomous Robotic Phlebotomy ... autonomously performs venipuncture on outpatients in European clinical sites: the patient places their own arm in the device and presses start, the device disinfects the skin and inserts the needle under imaging guidance, while one trained professional supervises up to three devices.
sources.transferJustification: Related task (patient-contact needle procedure). This is the frontier of autonomous physical patient contact in a clinical facility, but the patient fixtures their own arm in a purpose-built cabinet and a human handles order-of-draw and supervision; it does not show gowning, positioning, draping, sterile-field setup, or assisting a clinician through an exam.

sources.title: [2409.19590] RoboNurse-VLA: Robotic Scrub Nurse System based on Vision-Language-Action Model
sources.claim: Robotic scrub-nurse systems that grasp and hand over surgical instruments remain laboratory research systems, not clinically deployed assistants.
sources.transferJustification: Related task (assisting a proceduralist by passing instruments). Cited because it covers only one fragment of the nursing prep-and-assist instance and exists only as a bench demonstration, so it cannot substantiate whole-instance completion in any clinical environment.

sources.title: A Robotic System to Anchor a Patient in a Lateral Position and Reduce Nurses' Physical Strain
sources.claim: A robot developed to hold a patient in a lateral position for bedside care is commanded by a remote nurse rather than acting autonomously, and was evaluated only in a controlled study with nurse coordination.
sources.transferJustification: Related task (positioning/holding a patient for examination or hygiene care). Directly targets the positioning fragment of this task, but is teleoperated by a remote nurse and still requires a bedside nurse, so it cannot support a positive judgment.

sources.title: A Survey of Robotic Systems for Nursing Care - Frontiers in Robotics and AI
sources.claim: Tele-nursing mobile manipulators intended for patient-side nursing tasks such as handing objects and taking vital signs are classified as teleoperated devices, remotely controlled by a human ....
sources.transferJustification: Related task (bedside nursing assistance with patients). Establishes that the patient-facing nursing robots in the literature operate under continuous human teleoperation, which the rating rules exclude from supporting positive judgments.

sources.title: Robotic-assisted dressing system accommodates different poses, body types and garments
sources.claim: Robot-assisted dressing of a person in a hospital gown remains a university laboratory research problem, demonstrated on researchers' arms rather than in patient care.
sources.transferJustification: Related task (gowning/undressing a patient, a core step of preparing patients for examination). Shows the capability exists only as a lab demonstration on healthy able-bodied subjects, far from worker-quality clinical prep.

tasks.label: Prepare rooms, sterile instruments, equipment, or supplies and ensure that stock of supplies is maintained.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Inpatient unit: prepare/turn over a patient room for an admission, transfer, or isolation case — verify bed and call light, hang IV pole and pump, set up suction canister and oxygen tubing, place monitor leads/telemetry, stock the in-room cabinet with gloves, gowns, linens and an admission kit, post isolation cart and signage. Room is occupied-adjacent, cluttered with furniture, visitors and equipment moved arbitrarily.

Bedside or treatment-room setup for a procedure (dressing change, Foley or IV insertion, central-line assist, wound irrigation, suturing): gather the correct kit and supplies, open sterile packs onto a sterile field on an overbed/Mayo table without contamination, add solutions and extra instruments with sterile technique, prime tubing, set up and test the equipment. Occurs at a hospital bedside, in a clinic treatment room, and in a small minority of cases in a patient's home.

Perioperative/procedural suite (OR, endoscopy, cath lab, L&D): prepare the procedure room for the next case — pull and check the case cart against the preference card, open sterile supplies and instrument trays onto the back table, check sterilization indicators, set up and test equipment (ESU, insufflator, scope tower, warmers), position furniture, and perform the initial instrument/sponge count with the scrub person.

Replenishment run: unit is short an item (IV pump, telemetry box, dressing supplies, a specific med) mid-shift; the nurse walks to central supply, the clean utility room or the pharmacy, retrieves the item and brings it back to the unit so care can proceed. Fixed hospital corridors, elevators, standard supply rooms.

Scheduled stock maintenance: check par levels in the unit supply room, procedure carts, isolation carts and the med room; pull replacement items from the storeroom, place them on the correct shelves/bins, rotate and check expiration dates, replace and re-lock the crash cart tray, and place restock orders in the supply system.

Clinic/ambulatory or office setting: reprocess reusable instruments between patients — transport and clean soiled instruments, ultrasonic/washer cycle, inspect, assemble and package sets in pouches or wrapped trays, run the autoclave, verify chemical/biological indicators, and shelve the sterile packs for the next day's procedures.

sources.claim: Moxi's advertised workflows include retrieving items from central supply ... and gathering supplies for patient rooms; fleet passed one million deliveries.

sources.claim: Scale of deployment: Moxi operates in 25 US hospitals with more than 1.3 million completed deliveries and thousands of autonomous elevator rides ....

sources.claim: Autonomous mobile robots from Aethon, Relay and Diligent routinely move pharmaceuticals, equipment and linens through hospital corridors.

sources.system: Omnicell XR2 Automated Central Pharmacy System
sources.title: Pharmacy Robot Increases Safety, Efficiency | Owensboro Health
sources.claim: The XR2 robotic central pharmacy system autonomously pulls, bags, seals and labels medications inside an enclosed robotic cell in a hospital pharmacy, managing inventory control.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: item-level storage, picking and inventory replenishment of small packaged healthcare consumables presented to the machine in a purpose-built enclosure — the same handling and accuracy demands as a nurse keeping par-level stock of packaged supplies.

sources.title: Automated Pharmacy Storage System - Swisslog BoxPicker
sources.claim: BoxPicker is a commercially sold, fully automated robotic storage and retrieval system that manages stock of packaged items in hospital pharmacies with barcode verification.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: maintaining stock of packaged healthcare supplies in a machine-built storeroom (put-away, tracking, retrieval) — the stock-maintenance half of the nursing task, with the work brought to the machine.

sources.developer: Hai Robotics / Equipment Depot for St. Luke's Health System
sources.title: St. Luke's Health System turns to a partnership with Equipment Depot, Inc. and Hai Robotics to streamline warehouse order fulfillment
sources.claim: A health system runs its medical-supply distribution on 28 autonomous case-handling robots that store and retrieve supply containers in a purpose-built robotic rack system feeding pick workstations.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: replenishing and maintaining stock of the same medical supplies nurses par-stock, in a purpose-built robotic storage environment; demonstrates autonomous put-away/retrieval of supply containers at production reliability.

sources.system: ORB (Operating Room Bot, Fetch mobile manipulator)
sources.title: ORB: Operating Room Bot, Automating Operating Room Logistics through Mobile Manipulation
sources.claim: ORB, an autonomous mobile manipulator, retrieved and restocked individual operating-room supply items in a mock hospital supply room with 80% retrieval and 96% restocking success.

sources.system: Autonomous instrument tray assembly system (Staubli TX2-60L arm, dual electromagnetic gripper)
sources.title: Towards Autonomous Instrument Tray Assembly for Sterile Processing Applications (arXiv:2602.01679)
sources.claim: A fully automated robotic cell ... 6-DOF industrial arm sorts and packs surgical instruments into sterile ..., the sterile-processing assembly step, validated in the lab.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: preparing sterile instruments — the identical objects (surgical instruments), the same accuracy demand (correct set composition), performed with the work presented to a fixed robot workstation.

sources.system: RIF Robotics instrument inspection and tray assembly platform
sources.developer: RIF Robotics (pilot with Wellstar Health System)
sources.title: RIF Robotics pioneers autonomous surgical tray assembly - Catalyst by Wellstar
sources.claim: A startup's AI/computer-vision robotic system for assembling and sterilizing hospital surgical instruments entered a pilot inside a hospital sterile processing department.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: preparing sterile instruments (inspection, kitting, sterilization) — same objects and sterility standard as clinic instrument reprocessing done by nurses.

sources.title: UV Robot Automates Coronavirus Disinfection, Streamlines Hospital Processes - Inside Unmanned Systems
sources.claim: Self-navigating UV-C robots autonomously disinfect an empty hospital patient room in about 10-15 minutes and are deployed for patient-room turnover, but perform only surface disinfection.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: room turnover. Cited to show the only autonomous in-room hospital system covers disinfection alone — it does not stock the room, make the bed, or set up equipment.

sources.title: Robotic scrub nurse to anticipate surgical instruments based on real-time laparoscopic video analysis
sources.claim: A research robotic scrub nurse autonomously handled about 72% of instrument anticipation and handover ... in study conditions, below clinical acceptance.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: handling surgical instruments in the OR. Cited to show the state of the art in OR instrument handling is a partial, sub-worker-quality lab capability, not sterile back-table setup.

tasks.label: Administer local, inhalation, intravenous, or other anesthetics.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Procedural/moderate sedation in a hospital or ASC: endoscopy, ED, cath lab, IR or cardioversion. RN verifies order and drug, connects syringe/pump to the patient's existing IV, gives titrated boluses or an infusion of midazolam/fentanyl/propofol/ketamine, continuously watches sedation depth, airway, SpO2 and BP, adjusts or stops dosing, and assists rescue if the patient over-sedates.

Injected local anesthetic: RN raises an intradermal lidocaine wheal or infiltrates subcutaneously before fistula cannulation in dialysis, PICC/IV insertion, port access, or infiltrates a wound field/lesion site in an ED or clinic procedure room. Requires drawing up the drug, choosing and prepping the site, aspirating, injecting small volumes, and assessing effect.

Topical/mucosal anesthetic application: EMLA/LMX cream placed over a vein or implanted port and covered with an occlusive dressing, LET gel packed into a pediatric laceration, benzocaine/lidocaine spray or gargle before endoscopy or NG tube passage, lidocaine jelly for catheterization. Done at the bedside or in a clinic exam room, timed before the procedure.

Inhaled agent administration: RN sets up and delivers 50/50 nitrous oxide-oxygen during labor or a pediatric/dental procedure, fits or coaches the patient on the demand-valve mask/mouthpiece, adjusts flow, monitors level of consciousness and side effects, and scavenges/breaks down the circuit; or assists an inhalational mask induction.

Anesthetic administration outside an institution-controlled facility: home infusion or hospice visit (topical anesthetic before port access, subcutaneous lidocaine), mobile clinic, school or occupational health site, or during interfacility transport. Layout, lighting, patient positioning and equipment vary site to site.

sources.system: Vitestro Aletta Autonomous Robotic Phlebotomy Device
sources.title: Performance, Safety, and Patient Experience of an Autonomous Robotic Phlebotomy Device: A Multicenter Trial (Clinical Chemistry)
sources.claim: Aletta, an autonomous robotic phlebotomy device using multimodal imaging, performed venipuncture on 1,633 patients in routine use at Dutch outpatient phlebotomy departments, with 94.5% first-stick success and a 0.6% mild adverse event rate; the device is CE-marked and being deployed in European clinical settings.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: diagnostic venipuncture. It shows a machine can autonomously find a vein and place a needle in a seated patient's arm at a purpose-built station in a clinical facility - the vascular-access step that precedes IV anesthetic administration. It does not deliver any drug into the patient, so it substantiates needle placement only, not administration of an anesthetic.

sources.title: The Sinking of Sedasys - Outpatient Surgery Magazine
sources.claim: The SEDASYS computer-assisted personalized sedation system received FDA premarket approval and was marketed for endoscopy units; it delivered IV 1% propofol for minimal-to-moderate sedation while integrating patient monitoring and automatically reducing dosing on signs of over-sedation, operated by a physician-led endoscopy team rather than an anesthesia professional.

sources.system: Closed-Loop Anaesthesia Delivery System (CLADS), BIS-guided automated propofol TIVA
sources.developer: PGIMER Chandigarh / Sir Ganga Ram Hospital (India)
sources.title: Evaluation of Automated Delivery of Propofol Using a Closed-Loop Anesthesia Delivery System in Patients Undergoing Thoracic Surgery: A Randomized Controlled Study (PubMed)
sources.claim: A closed-loop anesthesia delivery system ... () automatically delivered propofol TIVA by BIS feedback in a randomized controlled trial in thoracic surgery patients at a tertiary hospital, matching manual control on depth-of-anesthesia consistency while requiring zero manual infusion adjustments.

sources.system: Aisys CS2 anesthesia machine with End-tidal Control (EtC) software
sources.date: 2024-07 (Anesth Analg MASTER trial); product commercially available
sources.title: End-Tidal Control Versus Manual Control of Inhalational Anesthesia Delivery: A Randomized Controlled Noninferiority Trial
sources.claim: GE HealthCare's End-tidal Control software on the commercially sold Aisys CS2 anesthesia machine automatically adjusts fresh gas flow and vaporizer output to reach and hold a clinician-set end-tidal inhaled anesthetic concentration; in the 210-patient randomized MASTER trial it was noninferior to manual clinician control.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated delivery of a volatile inhalation anesthetic to a patient connected to the breathing circuit. It is the same physical act as administering an inhaled anesthetic agent, differing only in the agent and in the mask/circuit being attached by a human.

sources.system: Cobi (Cobionix robotic platform with needle-free jet injector)
sources.title: Cobi robot autonomously performs intramuscular injection without needles
sources.claim: Cobionix's Cobi robot performed a needle-free intramuscular injection into a human arm, using lidar/3D sensing and AI to select the injection site and a high-pressure jet to deliver the dose; reported as a first-of-its-kind single demonstration by a university spinout.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: intramuscular vaccine injection. Cited only to show the closest existing capability; it is a single unreplicated company demonstration of a deltoid jet injection, not the site-specific intradermal/subcutaneous infiltration of a local anesthetic around a cannulation site or wound, and no reliability, dosing or safety data are reported.

tasks.label: Provide or arrange for training or instruction of auxiliary personnel or students.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Preceptoring a nursing student or new-graduate RN during a clinical rotation on a hospital med-surg unit: explaining unit routines, talking through assessment findings and rationale, watching the learner perform care, giving corrective feedback, and signing off competency paperwork.

Orienting a newly hired CNA/nursing assistant or patient care tech on the unit over a shift: reviewing policies and expectations, explaining how tasks are done here, observing their work and coaching verbally as the shift proceeds.

Delivering a scheduled in-service or skills-lab session to unit staff on a new policy, medication, or piece of equipment (e.g., new IV pump or lift): presenting the material, showing how the device is used, answering questions, documenting attendance.

Arranging rather than providing training: identifying learning needs, scheduling staff into education modules or annual competencies, coordinating with the staff-development educator or vendor, tracking completion in the learning management system.

Just-in-time bedside coaching in a clinic, long-term care facility, or home-health setting: telling an aide or new tech how to do a safe transfer, glucometer check, or dressing change at the point of care, with a patient present.

tasks.label: Refer students or patients to specialized health resources or community agencies furnishing assistance.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

tasks.label: Perform physical examinations, make tentative diagnoses, and treat patients en route to hospitals or at disaster site triage centers.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Interfacility ground ambulance transport of a stable-to-moderate acuity patient (ED-to-tertiary, ICU-to-ICU): transport RN performs focused physical assessment in the moving patient compartment, monitors cardiac rhythm/vitals, manages oxygen, IV lines and drips, gives PRN medications per protocol, recognizes and responds to deterioration, and hands off at the receiving hospital.

Critical-care transport (ground or rotor/fixed-wing) of an unstable patient: RN performs ongoing exam, manages a ventilator and advanced airway, titrates vasopressors and sedation, hangs blood products, interprets monitor/point-of-care data to form a working diagnosis, and manages arrest or acute decompensation in a vibrating, noisy, cramped cabin.

Air-medical or rapid-response scene call: crew lands at a roadside crash, farm, or rural field; RN performs primary/secondary trauma survey on a patient on the ground or in a vehicle, controls hemorrhage, splints/immobilizes, establishes access, and continues treatment en route. Weather, terrain, lighting, and bystanders are as found.

Mass-casualty incident primary triage at the disaster site itself (building collapse, bus crash, active-shooter scene, tornado damage): RN moves among many casualties in rubble/debris, performs seconds-long START-type assessments, assigns triage tags, and delivers immediate life-saving interventions (airway positioning, tourniquet, chest seal) with scarce supplies.

Secondary triage and treatment at an established disaster triage center / casualty collection point / mobile field hospital tent: cots, marked treatment areas, standard supply caches, incident-command control of who enters; RN re-examines tagged patients, forms tentative diagnoses, starts IVs, dresses wounds, splints, gives medications, and prioritizes evacuation.

sources.system: DARPA Triage Challenge systems (Coordinated Robotics, DART, RoboScout, UAS-DTU, Penn PRONTO)
sources.developer: DARPA / competing university and industry teams
sources.title: DART and MSAI triumph at DARPA Triage Challenge | DARPA
sources.claim: Autonomous ground and aerial robots in the DARPA Triage Challenge performed standoff casualty localization, injury identification and vital-sign estimation on staged disaster courses (C-130 crash, night ambush) with smoke and darkness. The systems assess and prioritize casualties for human medics; they do not perform physical examination by hand or deliver treatment, and the finals are still scheduled for November 2026.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic primary triage at a mass-casualty site. It is the closest existing capability to the disaster-triage instances, but it covers only stand-off assessment, so it substantiates a sub-step rather than completion of exam + tentative diagnosis + treatment.

sources.title: Systems Competition | Event 1 | DARPA
sources.claim: The DARPA Triage Challenge Systems competition is explicitly scoped to stand-off physiological assessment to help human medical professionals prioritize casualties, i.e. detection and triage rather than hands-on treatment.
sources.transferJustification: Same related task as above (robotic field triage); cited to establish the scope limit — assessment only, no intervention — which is why it cannot substantiate the whole task.

sources.system: DARPA robotic casualty-care solicitation (no fielded system)
sources.title: DARPA launches search for robot medics to treat battlefield casualties
sources.claim: As of May 2026 DARPA was still soliciting proposals for a robot capable of assessing wounds and performing life-saving interventions on casualties at the point of need, indicating no such fielded system exists.
sources.transferJustification: Directly the related task (autonomous field casualty treatment). Cited only as context for a negative judgment: an active solicitation is an announcement of intent, not a demonstrated capability, and cannot support any positive tier.

sources.title: Sensor-guided robots could boost lifesaving combat casualty care | DARPA
sources.claim: DARPA's MASH program is still developing the autonomy software needed for robots to control hemorrhage under field conditions; the capability is a three-year research effort, not a fielded system.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous robotic hemorrhage control, a core treatment element of trauma/triage care. Cited to show it remains in development, supporting a negative judgment.

sources.system: Autonomous lightweight ultrasound robot for liver sonography
sources.developer: Tsinghua University / Beijing Tsinghua Changgung Hospital
sources.title: Beyond hospital reach: Autonomous lightweight ultrasound robot for liver sonography (arXiv 2510.08106)
sources.claim: A fully autonomous lightweight ultrasound robot was deployed in a hospital ultrasound department and autonomously acquired aorta, IVC and portal-vein views on volunteers, showing autonomy for a single imaging sub-step in a controlled clinical room, not a whole patient examination with diagnosis and treatment.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic physical/imaging examination of a patient. It transfers only partially — the patient lies still in a quiet hospital room, one organ is imaged, and no diagnosis or therapy follows — so it cannot substantiate the full task.

sources.developer: UC Santa Barbara (published in Science Translational Medicine)
sources.title: A soft robotic device for rapid and self-guided intubation | Science Translational Medicine
sources.claim: A soft robotic intubation device autonomously guided tube placement, but only in bench models and cadavers, not in live emergency patients.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic airway management, one treatment element of critical-care transport. Transfer is limited: the device is placed and operated by a clinician on a model/cadaver, so it does not substantiate autonomous treatment of a live patient.

sources.title: Portable robot for autonomous venipuncture using 3D near infrared image guidance - PMC
sources.claim: An image-guided robot autonomously detected and cannulated veins, but the evidence is early-stage in vitro and animal/in vivo model work rather than routine clinical use.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic vascular access, a treatment sub-step for transport and field nursing. Only a sub-step on a stationary arm in a lab; it cannot substantiate the whole examine–diagnose–treat instance.

sources.title: Moxi 2.0 mobile manipulator is built for AI, says Diligent Robotics - The Robot Report
sources.claim: The largest deployed clinical robot fleet in US hospitals, Moxi, performs only non-clinical fetch-and-deliver work; it does not assess or treat patients, and one health system retired its Moxi robots after less than two years.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous mobile robot work in a structured healthcare facility (E2). It shows what deployed healthcare robots actually do — logistics — and that patient assessment and treatment are outside their scope.
