roles.description: Provide advanced nursing care for patients with acute conditions such as heart attacks, respiratory distress syndrome, or shock. May care for pre- and post-operative patients or perform advanced, invasive diagnostic or therapeutic procedures.

tasks.label: Discuss illnesses and treatments with patients and family members.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

tasks.label: Diagnose acute or chronic conditions that could result in rapid physiological deterioration or life-threatening instability.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: ICU bedside: acute care NP/nurse evaluates an intubated, hemodynamically unstable patient — synthesizing monitor trends (BP, HR, SpO2, waveforms), vasopressor requirements, labs (lactate, ABG), imaging, and exam findings — and determines the diagnosis (e.g., septic shock vs. cardiogenic shock) to direct management.

Rapid response / deteriorating ward patient: called to a med-surg or telemetry patient with new tachypnea, hypotension, or altered mentation; forms a working diagnosis (e.g., pulmonary embolism, MI, sepsis, opioid-induced respiratory depression) from vitals, telemetry, history, point-of-care tests, and assessment.

Post-operative or step-down rounding: evaluates a post-op patient for complications that could destabilize them (hemorrhage, new arrhythmia, hypoxemia/atelectasis, anastomotic leak), integrating drain output, trending labs, and serial vitals into a diagnosis documented in the chart.

ED or new-admission workup: patient presents with chest pain, dyspnea, or syncope; nurse practitioner takes history, orders and interprets ECG, troponin, chest imaging, and formulates a differential and working diagnosis for an acute life-threatening condition.

Diagnosing chronic conditions that predispose to instability (heart failure, COPD, CKD, diabetes with DKA risk, cirrhosis) during admission history-taking or consult, and documenting them as active problems affecting the acute course.

tasks.label: Perform emergency medical procedures, such as basic cardiac life support (BLS), advanced cardiac life support (ACLS), and other condition-stabilizing interventions.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Code blue / in-hospital cardiac arrest at the bedside in an ICU or ED: nurse recognizes pulselessness, starts high-quality chest compressions on a bed or backboard, applies defibrillator pads, bag-mask ventilates, performs rhythm checks and defibrillation, obtains IV/IO access, pushes epinephrine and antiarrhythmics on the ACLS clock, and manages post-ROSC care as part of a code team.

Acute respiratory failure/distress on a monitored unit: nurse positions the patient, applies high-flow oxygen or a non-rebreather, suctions secretions from mouth/ETT, sets up and fits BiPAP, bag-mask ventilates a deteriorating patient, and assists intubation (cricoid pressure, suction, tube securing, ventilator hookup) while managing a combative or obtunded patient.

Shock/severe hypotension (sepsis, cardiogenic, hypovolemic) in ICU/ED: nurse establishes peripheral IV or intraosseous access on a poorly perfused patient, hangs and pressure-infuses fluid boluses, spikes and programs vasopressor drips on infusion pumps, titrates to MAP targets, and draws stat labs/blood cultures.

Post-operative or trauma emergency with active hemorrhage: nurse applies direct pressure or a tourniquet to a bleeding site or wound dehiscence, reinforces dressings, checks drains, obtains and administers blood products through a rapid infuser with two-nurse verification, and readies the patient for emergent return to OR.

Unstable arrhythmia at the bedside: nurse attaches 12-lead ECG and defibrillator pads, rapid-pushes adenosine with flush, performs synchronized cardioversion or transcutaneous pacing with sedation, administers atropine or amiodarone, and monitors capture and perfusion.

Rapid response call on a general ward for anaphylaxis, severe hypoglycemia, seizure, or opioid overdose: nurse gives IM epinephrine, IV D50 or glucagon, IV benzodiazepine, or naloxone, protects the airway, positions and pads the patient, applies oxygen and monitoring in a cluttered patient room with family present.

sources.title: LUCAS 3, v3.1 chest compression system | Stryker
sources.claim: Mechanical chest-compression devices (Stryker LUCAS 3) deliver machine-controlled compressions once a clinician positions the device on the patient, straps the patient in, and starts/pauses it; they cover only the compression sub-step of BLS and do not assess the patient, ventilate, defibrillate, or give drugs.
sources.transferJustification: Directly relevant sub-step (chest compressions during BLS/ACLS), but the device is applied, started, paused and removed by clinicians and performs no assessment, airway, defibrillation or drug tasks, so it cannot complete a whole resuscitation instance.

sources.system: AutoPulse and LUCAS mechanical chest compression devices
sources.title: Safety of mechanical chest compression devices AutoPulse and LUCAS in cardiac arrest: a randomized clinical trial for non-inferiority
sources.claim: Randomized and observational studies of AutoPulse and LUCAS in cardiac arrest show these devices are used as adjuncts within human-run resuscitation and have not shown superiority to manual compressions, i.e., machine compressions remain one component of a clinician-delivered code.
sources.transferJustification: Same task family (BLS compressions). Establishes that the only widely deployed resuscitation machine is an adjunct within a human-led code, not a substitute for the nurse's stabilizing interventions.

sources.title: Rutgers robot draws blood better than humans in first trials | The Robot Report
sources.claim: An image-guided robotic venipuncture device autonomously cannulated forearm veins in a first-in-human trial, but it is a research prototype performing elective blood draws on seated, stable volunteers, not emergency vascular access or drug administration in a decompensating patient.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: percutaneous venous access, a sub-step of IV/IO access in stabilization. It does not transfer: the trial used elective phlebotomy on cooperative, normotensive volunteers, whereas emergency access involves collapsed veins, motion, and must be followed by fluid/drug delivery.

sources.title: A robot-assisted tracheal intubation system based on a soft actuator | International Journal of Computer Assisted Radiology and Surgery
sources.claim: Autonomous robotic tracheal intubation has been demonstrated only on training manikins, not on patients, and covers one sub-step of airway stabilization.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: emergency airway management, part of respiratory stabilization. Does not transfer to real patients: manikin airways are rigid, clean, motionless and identically shaped, unlike secretion-filled, variable human airways in an emergency.

sources.title: A soft robotic device for rapid and self-guided intubation | Science Translational Medicine
sources.claim: A soft robotic self-guided intubation device achieved high success rates, but it is a hand-held tool operated by a human clinician on manikins and cadavers rather than a robot that performs the procedure on a patient by itself.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: emergency intubation. Human-held and human-operated, so it cannot substantiate autonomous completion of an airway-stabilization instance.

sources.title: Diligent Robotics completes 300,000 pharmacy deliveries with Moxi | The Robot Report
sources.claim: The mobile manipulators actually deployed at scale in US hospitals perform supply and pharmacy logistics in corridors and supply rooms; they do not perform patient-contact clinical procedures.
sources.transferJustification: Establishes the state of deployed hospital robotics (E2 setting): autonomous manipulation is limited to fetch-and-deliver logistics, with no demonstrated bedside emergency intervention.

sources.title: Hopkins robot is first to perform laparoscopic surgery without assistance from humans
sources.claim: The most advanced autonomous soft-tissue medical robot performed laparoscopic bowel anastomosis on anesthetized pigs in a research operating room; autonomy on live tissue remains preclinical and confined to a single planned surgical step.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous invasive procedure on live tissue. Does not transfer: it works on an anesthetized, immobilized animal with ports already placed and a single pre-planned suturing goal, unlike time-critical, multi-modal resuscitation of an unstable human.

tasks.label: Assess urgent and emergent health conditions, using both physiologically and technologically derived data.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: ICU/critical care bedside assessment of a critically ill patient (often intubated, sedated, on vasoactive drips): hands-on head-to-toe exam — auscultate heart/lungs/bowel, palpate pulses and abdomen, pupil and neuro checks, skin/edema/perfusion, inspect lines, drains and wounds — integrated with ventilator settings, arterial line and hemodynamic waveforms, telemetry, and lab/ABG trends to judge whether the patient is deteriorating and to escalate.

Serial shift and post-procedure reassessment on step-down/telemetry or PACU: repeated focused assessments of a post-operative or acutely ill but stable patient — vitals, level of consciousness and airway after sedation, pain, wound/dressing/drain output, telemetry rhythm review, pulse oximetry, IV site — comparing against prior findings to detect early bleeding, hypoxia, or arrhythmia.

Emergency department rapid/triage assessment of an arriving patient (walk-in or EMS) with chest pain, dyspnea, sepsis or altered mental status: obtain and interpret vitals, apply monitor/12-lead ECG and pulse oximetry, take a focused history from a distressed or uncooperative patient, do a focused physical exam, and assign acuity with point-of-care test results.

Acute deterioration event, rapid response call, or code in a hospital unit: recognize the change, perform rapid ABC assessment — responsiveness, airway patency, breathing effort and sounds, central pulse check, skin, rhythm on the monitor/defibrillator — under time pressure amid a crowded bedside team, and continuously re-assess response to interventions.

Assessment outside the fixed unit: during interfacility or intra-hospital transport in an ambulance or elevator, or on a hospital-at-home / acute-care-at-home visit in a patient's residence — assess the patient with portable monitors in cramped, variable, uncontrolled surroundings.

sources.system: Dr. Spot (MIT / Boston Dynamics / Brigham and Women's Hospital)
sources.developer: MIT, Boston Dynamics, Brigham and Women's Hospital
sources.title: Robot takes contact-free measurements of patients' vital signs | MIT News
sources.claim: Dr. Spot, a quadruped robot fitted with IR/RGB cameras, measured skin temperature, respiratory rate, pulse and SpO2 on patients in a hospital ED COVID triage tent, but it is driven and operated by clinical staff rather than acting autonomously, and it only captures a subset of vital signs — no physical exam or clinical assessment.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: contactless vital-sign acquisition in an ED triage setting, a data-gathering sub-step of urgent assessment. It is cited as a negative bound — the most clinically advanced patient-assessment robot deployment is teleoperated and covers only vitals.

sources.title: Automated Heart and Lung Auscultation in Robotic Physical Examinations
sources.claim: A robotic arm autonomously positioned a stethoscope and captured heart and lung sounds on four human subjects in a laboratory physical-examination setup, quality comparable to teleoperated capture; this is a single exam modality on cooperative seated subjects, not a whole patient assessment.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: auscultation, one component of physiologically derived data collection. Transfer is limited — same patient contact, but only one modality on healthy cooperative subjects in a lab, no integration, judgment, or acutely ill patients.

sources.system: Autonomous lightweight ultrasound robot for liver sonography
sources.developer: Tsinghua University with Beijing Tsinghua Changgung Hospital
sources.title: Beyond hospital reach: Autonomous lightweight ultrasound robot for liver sonography (arXiv:2510.08106)
sources.claim: An autonomous cable-driven ultrasound robot with an AI agent performed liver scanning on humans in the ultrasound department of a hospital, autonomously localizing target structures; capability is confined to a single scripted imaging protocol on a positioned, cooperative patient.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: acquisition of technologically derived diagnostic data by direct probe contact with a patient. It marks the frontier of autonomous patient-contact robotics — a single-organ imaging protocol, far short of an integrated urgent/emergent assessment.

sources.title: Serve Robotics to Acquire Diligent Robotics, Expanding Physical AI Platform Beyond the Sidewalk
sources.claim: Moxi, the largest deployed fleet of hospital mobile manipulators in the US, works autonomously in patient-care facilities but its accepted tasks are deliveries of medications, supplies and lab samples — it performs no patient assessment.
sources.transferJustification: Cited as a negative bound on what autonomous robots actually do in the hospital environment of this task: logistics deliveries, with no patient examination or clinical data interpretation.

sources.developer: Foxconn (Hon Hai) with NVIDIA and Kawasaki
sources.title: AI Robotics, Digital Twins, and MONAI Contributions Highlight Hon Hai Foxconn's Smart Healthcare Vision at GTC Taipei 2025
sources.claim: Nurabot, a nursing humanoid being introduced into Taiwanese hospitals, performs medication delivery, specimen transport, ward ... education — logistics and communication rather than physical assessment of acute patients.
sources.transferJustification: Cited as a negative bound: the flagship 'nursing robot' entering hospital wards handles transport and education tasks, not urgent/emergent clinical assessment.

sources.title: Automatic Vital Sign Measurement Enabled by a Semi-Autonomous Robot
sources.claim: A semi-autonomous sensing robot autonomously located measurement sites on the arms of 25 healthy adult volunteers and derived heart rate, respiratory rate, SpO2 and estimated blood pressure from PPG in under 30 seconds — a laboratory study of vital-sign capture only.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated vital-sign acquisition, the technologically derived-data sub-step of assessment. Transfer is limited to healthy seated volunteers in a lab; it provides no exam findings, trending judgment, or escalation decision.

tasks.label: Set up, operate, or monitor invasive equipment and devices, such as colostomy or tracheotomy equipment, mechanical ventilators, catheters, gastrointestinal tubes, and central lines.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: ICU/step-down bedside: insert, secure, maintain, and remove an indwelling urinary (Foley) catheter on an adult acute patient — sterile field setup, perineal prep, anatomical identification, balloon inflation, drainage bag hanging, output monitoring, and CAUTI-prevention care over the stay.

Mechanical ventilator: assemble/verify circuit, humidifier and filters, connect the patient's endotracheal or tracheostomy tube, confirm prescribed settings and alarm limits, respond to high-pressure/low-volume alarms, troubleshoot condensate, disconnections and patient-ventilator dyssynchrony during a shift.

Routine airway secretion removal on an intubated/ventilated ICU patient using a closed inline suction catheter: pre-oxygenation, catheter passes to set depth with suction applied, monitoring of SpO2/HR response, repeated as secretions accumulate over the shift.

Tracheostomy care beyond suctioning: inner cannula change/cleaning, stoma cleaning and dressing, tie changes with a second person supporting the tube, cuff pressure checks, and management of a dislodged or plugged tube.

Central venous and arterial line management: assist with sterile insertion (drape, kit, timeout), set up pressure tubing/transducer and level/zero it, perform sterile dressing and cap/tubing changes, flush/lock lumens, draw blood from the line, assess the site for infection.

GI and stoma devices: insert an NG/OG tube in a semi-cooperative patient, confirm placement, connect to low-wall suction or an enteral feeding pump, flush and check residuals; change a colostomy/ileostomy appliance, measure output, and assess peristomal skin.

sources.system: Lmeca A-1000 automatic (electric) airway suction device
sources.title: Clinical trial to verify the safety of an automatic electric airway suction system: a multicenter prospective randomized study (European Journal of Medical Research)
sources.claim: The Lmeca A-1000 automatic suction device motor-advances a suction catheter into the artificial airway and removes secretions automatically on preset intervals, depth and pressure; a multicenter randomized trial in ICU patients found it non-inferior to manual suctioning for mucosal injury and pneumonia.

sources.system: Automatic closed-suction system (investigator-initiated multicenter trial device)
sources.title: Clinical Efficacy and Safety of an Automatic Closed-Suction System in Mechanically Ventilated Patients with Pneumonia (Diagnostics)
sources.claim: A separate multicenter randomized non-inferiority trial evaluated an automatic closed-suction system performing endotracheal suctioning in mechanically ventilated ICU patients with pneumonia, reporting comparable efficacy and safety to nurse-performed suctioning.

sources.title: Vitestro Raises $70 Million in Oversubscribed Series B Financing to Advance Autonomous Robotic Phlebotomy and Commercial Readiness
sources.claim: Vitestro's Aletta is a CE-marked autonomous robotic phlebotomy device that locates a peripheral vein with imaging and inserts a needle for diagnostic blood collection at roughly manual first-stick success rates, with early hospital customers; it does not place indwelling catheters or service central lines.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous image-guided needle insertion into a peripheral vein. It is the closest demonstrated robotic vascular-access capability, but it stops at a venipuncture needle in an outpatient draw chair and does not cover catheter/guidewire placement, sterile line dressing changes, or bedside line maintenance in the ICU, so it cannot substantiate the central/arterial line instance.

sources.system: Handheld image-guided robotic vascular access device (CICC placement)
sources.developer: Herlihy, Cohn, Ebner et al. (device developer group)
sources.title: Centrally inserted central catheter placement using a novel, handheld, image-guided, robotic device: Results of initial feasibility trial in patients
sources.claim: A handheld, ultrasound image-guided robotic needle-placement device was used in a ... feasibility trial for centrally inserted central catheter (hemodialysis catheter) placement; the device is held and directed by the clinician and the rest of the Seldinger procedure remains manual.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: central venous catheter insertion. It is clinician-held and only automates needle placement, so under the autonomy rule it cannot support a positive judgment for nurse-performed central line setup and maintenance.

sources.title: AURA-CVC: Autonomous Ultrasound-guided Robotic Assistance for Central Venous Catheterization
sources.claim: AURA-CVC is an end-to-end autonomous robotic ultrasound-guided central venous catheterization pipeline, but it was validated only on a high-fidelity commercial phantom in the laboratory and covers scanning and needle placement, not full catheter placement or line care.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: central line needle insertion. Phantom-only laboratory validation of a sub-step means it cannot substantiate completion of the bedside central-line instance on patients.

sources.title: Physical artificial intelligence in nursing: Robotics
sources.claim: A 2025 nursing review of physical AI concludes that bedside nursing robotics remains largely human-operated or preprogrammed with limited autonomy and has not transferred to direct patient care.

tasks.label: Document data related to patients' care, including assessment results, interventions, medications, patient responses, or treatment changes.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

tasks.label: Administer blood and blood product transfusions or intravenous infusions, monitoring patients for adverse reactions.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: ICU/ED bedside: establish new peripheral IV access in an acutely ill adult (edematous, hypotensive, obese, or repeatedly stuck), then start the ordered fluid or antibiotic infusion — site selection, catheter insertion, securement dressing, saline flush, connecting primed tubing, barcode verification, programming the smart pump, and watching the site and patient during infusion.

Inpatient ward/step-down: hang and start a new IV medication or fluid infusion on an already-established peripheral or central line — scan patient wristband and bag, spike and prime tubing, swab and connect to needleless hub, program pump with drug library settings, assess for infusion reaction/infiltration, replace bags and clear pump alarms through the shift.

Transfusion of a unit of packed red cells, platelets, or plasma to a bleeding or anemic patient: two-nurse verification of unit against blood bank tag and patient ID band, prime blood filter set with saline, connect and start slowly, baseline and 15-minute vital signs, bedside observation for fever/chills/rash/dyspnea/hypotension through the unit, then flush, disconnect, and document; stop and manage the reaction workup if one occurs.

ICU high-risk continuous infusions via central line: titrate vasopressors, sedation, insulin, or heparin to hemodynamic and lab targets, change bags/syringes without interrupting therapy, manage multi-channel pumps and line compatibility, and detect hemodynamic reactions, extravasation, or line occlusion.

Trauma bay/code: emergency or massive transfusion — uncrossmatched units and fluids pushed through a rapid infuser or pressure bags via large-bore or intraosseous access, done simultaneously with other resuscitation, with monitoring for reactions, hypothermia, and citrate toxicity while the patient is being moved and worked on by a team.

Infusion delivered outside the standard unit: during intra-hospital transport, in a procedural/imaging area, or in a hospital-at-home program where the nurse administers IV antibiotics, fluids, or blood in the patient's own residence with variable furniture, lighting, and no institutional layout.

sources.title: Performance, Safety, and Patient Experience of an Autonomous Robotic Phlebotomy Device: A Multicenter Trial
sources.claim: The Aletta Autonomous Robotic Phlebotomy ... performs venipuncture autonomously on outpatients in clinical blood-collection settings, with one supervising professional per up to three devices, achieving a 94.5% first-stick success rate in a multicenter trial; it collects diagnostic blood samples and does not place an indwelling catheter or administer any infusion.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous venipuncture for blood draw. It shares the needle-into-vein step of IV initiation, but only on cooperative ambulatory patients who place an arm in the machine's fixture, and it ends at needle withdrawal — it never leaves a catheter, connects tubing, starts a pump, or monitors a patient for transfusion/infusion reactions.

sources.title: Vitestro raises $70m to fuel blood-drawing robot's global commercial readiness
sources.claim: Vitestro's ARPD received a CE mark in 2024 and began deployment in European healthcare settings (hospital labs and blood-collection centers) in March 2025, confirming that autonomous vascular-puncture robots are limited today to routine diagnostic phlebotomy.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated diagnostic blood collection. Establishes the deployment envelope of vascular-access robotics (supervised phlebotomy stations), which does not extend to administering infusions or blood products.

sources.title: Hyperion Surgical Announces Completion of First-in-Human Study Using Its Ivy Robotic Vascular Access Platform
sources.claim: The first robotic-assisted peripheral IV catheterization in a human was completed in October 2025 with Hyperion Surgical's Ivy, described as a semi-autonomous system that holds probe and needle for a human operator; it is a single first-in-human study and covers only catheter placement, not connecting or running an infusion.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic IV catheter placement. It is the closest system to the access step of this task, but it is clinician-held/semi-autonomous (treated as teleoperated) and stops at catheterization.

sources.title: Moxi 2.0 mobile manipulator is built for AI, says Diligent Robotics
sources.claim: The largest deployed fleet of hospital mobile-manipulation robots, Moxi, performs logistics inside hospitals — delivering medications, supplies, and lab samples — and does not perform bedside clinical procedures such as hanging or connecting infusions or monitoring patients.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous hospital material transport and manipulation. It shows the current ceiling for autonomous robots operating in hospital wards (E2) is item fetch-and-deliver, not patient-connected drug or blood administration.

sources.system: IV admixture compounding robots in a PIVAS center
sources.developer: hospital PIVAS (reported by Chinese tertiary hospital study)
sources.title: Application of information-intelligence technologies in pharmacy intravenous admixture services in a Chinese third-class a hospital
sources.claim: Hospital IV automation that handles infusion bags and vials is confined to enclosed pharmacy admixture robots that compound doses in a cleanroom, with logistics robots then transporting finished bags to the ward; administration to the patient remains manual.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic preparation of IV bags/syringes in a purpose-built enclosure. It demonstrates robotic handling of bags, spikes and luer connections at E1, but stops at the finished bag — no cited system connects a bag to a patient or observes the patient for reactions.

tasks.label: Obtain specimens or samples for laboratory work.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Routine peripheral venipuncture at the bedside on a hemodynamically stable, cooperative acute-care patient (telemetry/step-down/ED/PACU): verify patient ID against the order, apply tourniquet, select an accessible antecubital or forearm vein, insert needle, fill and invert several color-topped tubes, apply bandage, label tubes and send to the lab.

Peripheral blood draw under difficult conditions: obese, edematous, hypotensive or IV-drug-history patient with collapsed/scarred veins; confused, agitated, restrained or isolation-precaution patient; blood cultures requiring sterile prep of two separate sites; blood drawn off a freshly started IV. Requires vein hunting by palpation or ultrasound and hands-on patient management.

Blood sampling from indwelling invasive access in the ICU/PACU: aspirating a waste volume from an arterial line or central venous catheter/PICC through a closed sampling port, drawing the specimen, transferring it into vacuum tubes or an ABG syringe, and flushing the line; also direct radial artery puncture for an arterial blood gas on patients without a line.

Urine specimen collection: aspirating a sample from the sampling port of an indwelling Foley catheter, performing an in-and-out straight catheterization for a sterile specimen, or instructing/assisting a bed-bound patient with a midstream clean-catch using a bedpan or urinal, then transferring to sterile containers.

Nasal, nasopharyngeal, oropharyngeal or throat swab on a conscious, cooperative patient for MRSA admission screening, respiratory viral panel or throat culture: position the head, insert the swab to the correct depth, rotate, withdraw and place in transport medium.

Other specimens from acutely ill patients: expectorated sputum or endotracheal/tracheostomy aspirate collected with a suction catheter and sputum trap on a ventilated patient, wound or drainage culture swabs from surgical or pressure wounds, stool sample for C. difficile, and assisting with fluid aspirates.

sources.title: Autonomous Robotic Phlebotomy Shows High Success Rates in Multicenter Trial | Clinical Lab Products
sources.claim: Vitestro's Aletta autonomous robotic phlebotomy device performed diagnostic venous blood draws on 1,633 patients across three outpatient ... departments in Dutch hospitals/labs, with 94.5% first-stick success when a suitable vein was ..., 0.3% hemolysis and 0.6% mild adverse events.

sources.title: Phlebotomists - Vitestro
sources.claim: Aletta is a fixed console at which the patient positions their own arm; it locates the vein with near-infrared and Doppler ultrasound, performs the venipuncture, fills and ..., with one human supervisor overseeing up to three devices and collecting the filled tubes for lab analysis. It declines the draw when no suitable vein is found.

sources.title: Vitestro introduces autonomous robotic device for blood collection
sources.claim: Aletta received CE marking and had its first European commercial launch, with clinical validation for safety and comfort in ...; it is aimed at labs and hospitals and is not yet FDA-approved.

sources.developer: Technical University of Munich and collaborators (Franka Emika arm)
sources.title: Autonomous swab robot for naso- and oropharyngeal COVID-19 screening | Scientific Reports
sources.claim: An autonomous swab robot station (SR-NOCS) using a force-sensitive arm under impedance control and a disposable nose/throat fixation collected naso- and oropharyngeal swab specimens from 52 suspected COVID-19 patients in two clinical studies, with results fully correlating with manual sampling and minimal supervision.
sources.transferJustification: Same task (obtaining a swab specimen for laboratory PCR analysis); the subject's head is held in a purpose-built fixation while the robot inserts, rotates and withdraws the swab, so it substantiates specimen collection only with the work brought to the machine.

sources.title: New Robot Does Superior Job Sampling Blood | Rutgers University
sources.claim: A Rutgers/VascuLogic ultrasound image-guided venipuncture robot autonomously drew blood into collection tubes from 31 human participants, with 87% overall success and 97% in participants with easy-access veins, reported as comparable to or exceeding clinical standards.

sources.system: Hitachi High-Tech automated fingertip blood collection device
sources.developer: Hitachi High-Tech Corporation with Fujita Health University Hospital
sources.title: Hospital robots collect and deliver blood samples
sources.claim: At Fujita Health University Hospital, a Hitachi High-Tech automated blood collection device on which the patient rests a palm maps finger capillaries with near-infrared cameras and takes a capillary sample of up to 400 microlitres using an automated finger tourniquet; results correlated well with venous samples in healthy volunteers.
sources.transferJustification: Same task (obtaining a blood sample for laboratory analysis) but capillary rather than venous and only at a palm-rest fixture station, so it corroborates blood sampling with the work brought to the machine.

tasks.label: Manage patients' pain relief and sedation by providing pharmacologic and non-pharmacologic interventions, monitoring patients' responses, and changing care plans accordingly.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: ICU: maintaining a ventilated, fully monitored, hemodynamically stable patient at a target sedation/analgesia depth across a shift — repeatedly adjusting propofol/fentanyl/dexmedetomidine infusion rates on syringe pumps in response to sedation-scale/BIS readings, respiratory pattern and blood pressure, and documenting the response.

ICU: complicated sedation/analgesia management — agitation and delirium, daily awakening/weaning trials, pre-turn and pre-procedure bolus dosing, hypotension or over-sedation requiring a drug change, self-extubation risk, and renegotiating the plan with the intensivist and family.

Post-op floor, step-down or PACU: a PRN analgesic episode — assess and score the patient's pain, pick the ordered drug, pull the controlled substance from the automated dispensing cabinet with witness/waste, scan patient and drug, give oral tablets or draw up and IV-push through the patient's line with flush, then reassess in 30-60 minutes, document, and escalate to the provider if inadequate.

Bedside non-pharmacologic comfort measures for an acute patient in bed with lines, drains and dressings — repositioning and pillow/incision splinting, ice or heat packs, warm blankets, assisting ambulation, dimming lights, coaching breathing/distraction — then reassessing whether pain and agitation improved.

PCA pump, epidural or peripheral nerve-block infusion management on a surgical unit — programming and priming the pump, connecting it to the patient's line, independent double-check with a second nurse, teaching the patient to dose, hourly sedation/respiratory-rate/capnography checks, cassette or bag changes, and reversal (naloxone) plus provider notification if the patient over-sedates.

Bedside procedural sedation and analgesia for chest tube insertion, cardioversion, central line placement, wound packing or awake intubation — drawing up and pushing fentanyl/midazolam/ketamine, titrating extra doses to patient response, watching airway, capnography and vitals throughout, and recovering the patient afterward.

sources.developer: Hospital Foch / Universite Versailles Saint-Quentin (Le Guen, Liu, Chazot, Fischler)

sources.claim: A closed-loop controller driving propofol and remifentanil syringe pumps from a BIS monitor autonomously titrated sedation in ICU patients with multiorgan failure over roughly 18-hour periods, holding target sedation depth better than manual clinician titration (39 rate changes/hour vs 2).

sources.system: Automated total intravenous anesthesia control system
sources.title: Anesthesia Management via an Automated Control System for Propofol, Remifentanil, and Rocuronium Compared to Management by Anesthesiologists
sources.claim: Investigators of an automated propofol/remifentanil/rocuronium control system state that despite many reported automated IV anesthetic delivery systems, none is commercially available, so automated analgesic/sedative titration is not a marketed capability.
sources.transferJustification: Same drug class and control loop as nurse-managed sedation titration; establishes that automated IV analgesic/sedative delivery exists only as research prototypes rather than deployable products.

sources.title: Diligent Robotics completes 300,000 pharmacy deliveries with Moxi - The Robot Report
sources.claim: Moxi mobile manipulators are deployed in 25-30+ US hospitals and have completed over 300,000 pharmacy deliveries, but the deployed capability is transporting medications and specimens through corridors, not administering analgesia or monitoring patient response.
sources.transferJustification: Closest deployed hospital mobile-manipulation system; it covers medication logistics adjacent to this task but stops at the unit and performs no patient-contact drug administration or pain reassessment.

sources.title: Vitestro raises $70m to fuel blood-drawing robot's global commercial readiness - Medical Device Network
sources.claim: An autonomous robotic phlebotomy device is CE-marked and commercially launched in European healthcare settings, performing imaging-guided needle insertion into patients' veins with about 95% first-stick success.
sources.transferJustification: Related task (venipuncture) shows autonomous needle work on a seated patient's arm in a clinic, but it withdraws blood from a cooperative outpatient and performs no drug selection, controlled-substance verification, IV-line administration, or pain/sedation response monitoring.

sources.title: Waterloo startup performs first ever robotic intramuscular injection | Waterloo News | University of Waterloo
sources.claim: A one-off laboratory demonstration in which a robot arm autonomously located an injection site and delivered a needle-free intramuscular dose to a person; no reliability data, clinical deployment, or drug-verification and monitoring workflow.
sources.transferJustification: Related task (robotic injection) is the nearest demonstrated robotic act of giving a drug to a person, but it covers only the delivery motion on a healthy seated subject in a lab, not assessment, controlled-drug handling, or reassessment.

sources.title: Aescape Secures $83M to Scale AI-Powered Robotic Massage Technology - AlleyWatch
sources.claim: Autonomous robotic massage systems are commercially deployed at scale in fitness clubs, delivering hands-on soft-tissue work to clients lying on the machine's purpose-built table.
sources.transferJustification: Related task (robotic non-pharmacologic pain relief by massage) shows safe autonomous contact with a human body, but only with a healthy client positioned on the machine's own table; it cannot reposition, splint, blanket or ice a bedbound acute patient with lines and drains.

sources.title: Anesthesia Use for Colonoscopy Attracts New Scrutiny | HealthLeaders Media
sources.claim: The only marketed automated sedation-delivery system for procedures, Sedasys computer-assisted personalized sedation with propofol, was FDA-approved in 2013 for healthy adults with clinicians present and was withdrawn from the market in 2016.
sources.transferJustification: Related task (procedural sedation drug delivery) — the closest commercial automation of sedation titration; it is no longer available and always required clinicians for IV access, bolus judgment, airway and rescue.

instances.label: Routine post-operative surgical wound dressing change at the bedside on a med-surg or step-down unit: don sterile technique, peel off the soiled adhesive dressing without tearing fragile skin, inspect the incision for drainage/dehiscence/infection, cleanse with saline or antiseptic, apply a new sterile dressing and secure with tape, then document the wound assessment.

Emergency department or urgent-care superficial laceration: assess depth and neurovascular status, anesthetize locally, irrigate and cleanse the wound, remove debris, approximate and close with sutures, staples, skin adhesive or adhesive strips, dress the closure, and give aftercare instructions — on an awake, sometimes flinching patient.

Complex wound care on a critically ill inpatient: pressure injury, dehisced abdominal incision, or infected surgical site — measure and stage the wound, perform mechanical/sharp conservative debridement of slough, irrigate, pack tunnels or cavities with gauze, or apply and seal a negative-pressure wound therapy dressing around drains and lines.

Minor wound and skin-integrity care at the bedside: skin tears, abrasions, IV infiltration or extravasation sites, chest-tube/drain and central-line insertion site care, small partial-thickness burns — clean, apply topical agent and a small dressing, on patients with tissue-paper-thin elderly skin.

Wound care under uncontrolled bedside conditions: an agitated, confused or restrained patient, a trauma bay during active resuscitation, an isolation room in full PPE, or a patient who must be log-rolled and held by additional staff to expose a sacral or posterior wound.

sources.transferJustification: Same task (wound dressing removal); cited to establish that even the removal step alone is a laboratory research result rather than a fielded capability.

It is the closest demonstrated analogue to closing a laceration, but it covers only the suturing step on marked bowel tissue in an animal lab, not assessment, irrigation, anesthesia and dressing of a patient's skin wound.

sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous manipulation of soft biological tissue. Cited as the frontier of autonomous tissue work; it is ex vivo, fixtured, and surgical, so it does not carry over to bedside wound cleaning, packing or dressing on living patients.

instances.label: ICU: acute care nurse reviews continuous telemetry, hemodynamic, and ventilator data plus bedside observation of a critically ill adult and judges whether a change (e.g., rising heart rate, falling MAP, altered respiratory pattern) reflects an expected response to therapy or true physiological deterioration.

Post-operative/step-down unit: nurse evaluates an older adult's mental status, mobility, and pain behavior and distinguishes age-related baseline changes or dementia from new-onset delirium, hypoxia, or sepsis-related change.

ED or admission assessment of a patient with chronic illness (COPD, heart failure, ESRD): nurse separates the patient's chronic baseline findings (chronic edema, chronic hypercapnia, baseline crackles) from an acute exacerbation requiring escalation.

Pediatric or neonatal acute care: nurse interprets age-specific vital sign ranges, feeding, tone, and behavioral cues to distinguish normal developmental variation from early decompensation in an infant or child.

Rounds/handoff and chart review: nurse integrates labs, imaging, medication effects, and prior documentation to classify findings as age-appropriate or normal-for-patient versus abnormal, and communicates that determination to the team.

instances.label: ICU bedside titration of continuous IV infusions (norepinephrine, sedatives, insulin, heparin) on smart pumps: nurse reads arterial-line/monitor values, changes the pump's rate setting per titration order, re-checks response, repeats over the shift.

Adjusting mechanical ventilator or NIV settings (FiO2, PEEP, rate, pressure support) for an intubated or BiPAP patient in the ICU, per protocol/order and during weaning trials, verifying gas exchange and patient tolerance.

Adjusting supplemental oxygen delivery on a step-down/telemetry unit: turning the flowmeter or high-flow FiO2/flow settings up or down to keep SpO2 in the ordered target range for a hypoxemic patient.

Cardiac surgical ICU temporary epicardial/transvenous pacing management: checking capture and sensing thresholds on the external pulse generator, setting output at a safety margin, choosing mode/sensitivity, responding to loss of capture or failure to sense.
Executing a discrete ordered change on a temporary pacemaker box (e.g., 'increase paced rate to 90' for low cardiac output or overdrive pacing), then confirming the paced rhythm on the monitor.

Setting or changing values on other bedside assistive devices to an ordered value: enteral feeding pump rate, PCA pump dose/lockout, wound-VAC pressure, sequential compression device, forced-air warmer, chest-tube suction, patient's home CPAP.

Order, perform, or interpret the results of diagnostic tests and screening procedures based on assessment results, differential diagnoses, and knowledge about age, gender and health status of clients.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Interpreting returned diagnostic data on an ICU/ED/step-down patient: reviewing chemistry, CBC, coagulation, troponin, culture and ABG values, imaging reports and telemetry/12-lead tracings at the workstation and bedside monitor; judging them against the patient's age, baseline and current status; recognizing critical values or rhythm change and escalating to the provider with documentation. Cognitive/charting work, no manipulation of the patient.

Initiating diagnostic tests under nurse-driven protocols or standing order sets in the EHR based on the nurse's assessment (ED triage ECG and troponin for chest pain, urine hCG, sepsis-bundle lactate and blood cultures, glucose checks, stroke protocol imaging), selecting the right panel for the patient's presentation and documenting the rationale. Order entry at a computer on the unit.

Performing a 12-lead ECG or rhythm strip at the bedside on an acutely ill adult: exposing and prepping the chest, placing ten electrodes at correct anatomic landmarks (including on diaphoretic, obese, hairy or dressing-covered skin), acquiring an artifact-free tracing, and giving a preliminary interpretation (STEMI, new arrhythmia, ischemia) with immediate notification.

Obtaining a routine venous blood specimen for ordered tests from a reasonably cooperative adult inpatient at the bedside on a step-down/telemetry/ED bed: tourniquet, vein selection in the antecubital or forearm, peripheral venipuncture, filling several tubes in correct order (including blood culture bottles), bedside patient-ID labeling and dispatch to the lab.

Advanced/invasive bedside diagnostic sampling in the critically ill: radial arterial puncture or sampling from an arterial or central line for ABG/labs, difficult access in hypotensive, edematous, obese or agitated patients, running the sample on a bedside blood-gas/i-STAT analyzer, bladder scan or bedside ultrasound assessment, and assisting/performing lumbar puncture or fluid sampling.

Collecting a screening specimen for infection surveillance on admission or on suspicion: nasal/nasopharyngeal or oropharyngeal swab for MRSA, influenza, RSV or COVID on a patient in an ED or inpatient bed, correct technique and dwell, placing the swab in transport medium or running it on a rapid bedside cartridge test and reporting the result.

instances.label: Outpatient psychiatric clinic (community mental health center or med-management clinic): nurse verifies identity and prescription, does a brief pre-injection check (side effects, symptoms, consent), reconstitutes/shakes a long-acting injectable antipsychotic (e.g., paliperidone palmitate, aripiprazole lauroxil), gives a deep IM deltoid or gluteal injection to a cooperative patient, disposes of the sharp, and documents/observes briefly.

Inpatient psychiatric unit, residential/crisis stabilization or partial-hospital program: scheduled oral medication pass at a med window or bedside — identify patient by wristband, check vitals/holds, hand the cup, verify swallowing (mouth check to prevent cheeking/diversion), manage refusals and negotiate, handle PRN requests, document.

Acute agitation emergency in an ED, psychiatric unit or crisis unit: rapid IM injection (e.g., haloperidol/lorazepam/olanzapine) into a resisting or physically held, sometimes involuntarily restrained patient, coordinated with a response team, followed by post-injection monitoring for oversedation.

Community outreach/ACT team or home visit to a poorly adherent patient: travel to a private home, shelter, or group home, assess the patient in the found setting, and administer a depot injection or directly observe an oral dose, often after persuasion.

Home-based care of a stable, cooperative community patient whose scheduled oral psychotropic doses must be delivered on time day after day (the medication-administration purpose of a routine home visit), with non-taking reported back to the care team.

Substance-use treatment clinic (OTP/MAT): reconstitute and give extended-release naltrexone gluteal IM or extended-release buprenorphine subcutaneous abdominal injection; or assess for intoxication/withdrawal and administer observed oral methadone/buprenorphine dosing with verified ingestion.

sources.claim: Cobionix's Cobi robot performed what is reported as the first autonomous robotic intramuscular ..., at a kiosk-style station where the recipient registers, shows ID to a camera, and the arm-mounted system selects the site and delivers a needle-free jet injection into a bare upper arm.

Transfer is partial — the end-to-end workflow (ID check, dose retrieval, site selection, delivery, disposal) matches an injection visit, but a jet injector cannot deliver viscous depot antipsychotic suspensions.

sources.title: This robot injects vaccines with no needles — and no human help (Freethink)

sources.title: Aletta: An Update About Vitestro's Robotic Blood Draw Device

Comparable objects (needle, human arm, aseptic prep) and greater targeting precision than an IM injection, in a clinical facility — it substantiates reliable autonomous needle work on patients, though it withdraws blood rather than administering a drug.

sources.title: Vitestro's robotic blood drawing device meets trial endpoints
sources.claim: Aletta met its clinical trial primary endpoint with 95% first-stick success across 609 participants, comparable to manual phlebotomy, and is CE-marked and in routine use at hospital study sites in Europe (OLVG Amsterdam, St. Antonius Utrecht; ordered by Odense University Hospital).
sources.transferJustification: Related task: venipuncture. Provides the reliability evidence (worker-comparable success rate) for autonomous needle placement in a human arm inside a healthcare facility.

sources.title: Evondos: Automatic medication dispensing for enhanced safety and adherence
sources.claim: Evondos dispensing robots are in routine service across Nordic home-care organisations, serving tens of thousands of ... with reported adherence near 99% and double-digit reductions in home-care visits.

instances.label: Outpatient psychiatric/community mental health clinic med room: PMHNP checks the locked medication cabinet and refrigerator for long-acting injectable antipsychotics, naltrexone, buprenorphine and drug samples — verifying quantities on hand against use, checking lot/expiration dates, and flagging what must be reordered before clinic sessions.

Inpatient psychiatric unit or residential/detox facility: participation in the shift controlled-substance count and med-room stock check — verifying narcotic/benzodiazepine counts against the dispensing record, reviewing usage since last count, and identifying and resolving discrepancies before the shift is accepted.

Clinic consumables supply room: checking par levels of syringes, needles, alcohol pads, sharps containers, urine drug-screen cups, gloves and injection trays on open shelving/bins against recent use, and generating a reorder list.

Periodic (monthly/quarterly) audit of the emergency medication kit / crash cart, naloxone kits and refrigerated stock: item-by-item expiration date and package-integrity check, seal and temperature-log verification, and documentation of the audit.

Mobile/community work (ACT team, mobile crisis unit, home visits): checking the contents and condition of the clinician's medication bag and vehicle stock — injectables, sharps, naloxone, testing supplies — before and after visits in vans, patient homes and shelters.

sources.system: Omnicell XR2 Automated Central Pharmacy System
sources.title: Terrebonne General Installs Groundbreaking Technology, Omnicell XR2 Robot, in Pharmacy
sources.claim: Omnicell XR2, a robotic central pharmacy system, is installed and live in US hospital pharmacies and automates medication inventory management (storage, barcode-verified stocking, dispensing and inventory control).

sources.system: BD Rowa Vmax / BD Rowa store-and-pick robots
sources.title: BD Rowa - medication management for the hospital
sources.claim: BD Rowa robotic storage/picking systems deployed in hospital pharmacies store lot and expiry information for every medication and maintain continuously correct stock levels, i.e. they monitor use and status of pharmaceutical stock held inside the machine.

sources.system: Omnicell Controlled Substance Dispenser (automated dispensing cabinet module)
sources.title: Pharmacy automated dispensing system - BTM - OMNICELL
sources.claim: Omnicell's automated unit-dose narcotics dispensing hardware, installed in nursing-unit automated dispensing cabinets, dispenses individual controlled-substance doses and removes the need for manual nurse countbacks.

sources.title: Automated Dispensing Cabinet Functionality Expansion to Reduce Controlled Substance Inventory Discrepancies
sources.claim: Automated dispensing cabinets in hospitals maintain a machine-held virtual perpetual inventory of controlled substances from every transaction and automatically surface count discrepancies for investigation.

sources.title: Harmons Deploys Simbe's Tally Inventory Robot In Stores Following Pilot Success
sources.claim: Simbe's Tally autonomous shelf-scanning robot is deployed across 17 Harmons grocery stores, traversing aisles by itself several times a day to capture shelf-level product availability, placement and pricing data used for replenishment.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: shelf inventory auditing in a retail store. It transfers to auditing par levels of packaged clinical consumables on labeled shelving in a clinic supply room — same object class (boxed/bagged packaged goods on fixed shelving), same required output (stock level and gap/reorder reporting), and the same class of institution-controlled indoor facility.

sources.title: RAIN RFID-Enabled Tally Robot Automates Grocery Store Inventory
sources.claim: The RFID-enabled Tally 3.0 monitors inventory levels and expiration dates ... goods on store shelves, deployed at grocery locations.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated stock-level and expiration monitoring of tagged packaged goods on shelves; transfers to monitoring status (quantity plus dating) of tagged clinical consumables on supply-room shelving, comparable object size and labeling.

sources.title: How Diligent's Robots Are Making a Difference in Texas Hospitals
sources.claim: Diligent Robotics' Moxi mobile manipulator operates autonomously in Texas hospitals, navigating corridors and picking supplies out of hospital supply closets for delivery.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous mobile manipulation inside hospital supply closets. It shows a robot can reach, identify and handle clinical consumables in an as-found healthcare supply room, supporting the environment (not the counting logic) for supply-room stock monitoring.

tasks.label: Treat patients for routine physical health problems.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Outpatient community mental health clinic or integrated behavioral health practice: during a psych visit the patient reports a routine physical complaint (sore throat, cough, UTI symptoms, headache, rash, GI upset). The PMHNP takes a history, performs a focused exam (temperature/BP, throat and ear inspection, lung auscultation, abdominal palpation, skin inspection), forms a diagnosis, and prescribes or advises OTC treatment with follow-up instructions.

Ongoing management of routine chronic physical comorbidities in psychiatric patients (hypertension, hyperlipidemia, type 2 diabetes, obesity, constipation, smoking-related complaints), including antipsychotic metabolic monitoring: measure weight/waist/BP, review lab results, palpate/inspect as needed, adjust or start medication, counsel the patient, and document.

Inpatient psychiatric unit or residential/detox facility: bedside evaluation and treatment of a routine physical problem (minor abrasion or superficial self-harm wound, constipation, dental pain, cellulitis, fall bruise, alcohol-withdrawal vitals), often with a guarded, agitated, or uncooperative patient in a ward room with limited equipment; includes hands-on wound cleaning/dressing and ordering or giving medication.

Hands-on preventive or procedural treatment in the clinic: administering an intramuscular or subcutaneous injection (influenza/COVID vaccine, B12, IM ceftriaxone), performing a point-of-care test (rapid strep, urine dipstick, fingerstick glucose) and acting on the result, or cleaning and dressing a minor wound, including patient identification, consent, aftercare observation, and documentation.

In-office venous blood specimen collection performed by the PMHNP to guide treatment of the physical problem (CBC/CMP, lipids, A1c, thyroid, drug levels): seat the patient, apply tourniquet, select and puncture a vein, fill tubes, label, and apply dressing.

Community or home-based setting: assertive community treatment home visit, group home, homeless shelter, or jail/holding clinic. The PMHNP evaluates and treats a routine physical complaint using portable equipment in a room taken as found (variable lighting, furniture, clutter, other people present), then dispenses or prescribes treatment.

sources.title: Vitestro raises $70m to fuel blood-drawing robot's global commercial readiness - Medical Device Network
sources.claim: Vitestro's Autonomous Robotic Phlebotomy Device performs venipuncture autonomously, holds an EU CE mark, and has been deployed commercially in European laboratory and hospital blood-collection settings since March 2025.
sources.transferJustification: Venipuncture for lab specimens is the in-office blood-draw instance of this task; the device performs the same needle procedure on the same patient population in a clinic/lab room, so performance carries over to instance 5 only, not to examination or treatment.

sources.title: Vitestro's robotic blood drawing device meets trial endpoints
sources.claim: In a multicenter clinical trial the autonomous phlebotomy device achieved first-stick success comparable to human phlebotomists with low complication rates, indicating worker-quality performance for venipuncture.
sources.transferJustification: Same transfer as above: quantifies that autonomous venipuncture reaches human-comparable quality, supporting only the specimen-collection instance.

sources.title: Cobi robot autonomously performs needle-less vaccinations - New Atlas
sources.claim: The Cobi robot demonstrated an autonomous needle-free intramuscular injection, but only as a laboratory prototype demonstration that its developers said was years from general use; there is no evidence of a deployed autonomous injection service.
sources.transferJustification: Directly relevant to the injection portion of instance 4, but it is a single prototype demonstration of one needle-free jet injection, not an accepted-quality clinical procedure with consent, site prep and aftercare.

sources.system: Fully autonomous robotic ultrasound system for thyroid scanning
sources.title: A fully autonomous robotic ultrasound system for thyroid scanning | Nature Communications
sources.claim: Fully autonomous contact-based clinical examination by a robot exists only at research level: an autonomous robotic ultrasound system scanned thyroid regions of human participants in a laboratory study.
sources.transferJustification: Closest related task to the physical-examination component: autonomous, force-controlled contact with a patient's body. It covers one imaging modality on a cooperative participant in a lab and does not extend to a diagnose-and-treat encounter.

sources.title: Towards Autonomous Tape Handling for Robotic Wound Redressing
sources.claim: Autonomous robotic wound care remains a research problem; published work addresses only isolated steps such as removing adhesive tape, not a complete dressing change on a patient.
sources.transferJustification: Directly addresses the wound-care element of instances 3 and 4 and shows only sub-step capability in a laboratory.

sources.developer: Foxconn with Kawasaki Heavy Industries and Nvidia
sources.title: Could AI nursing robots help healthcare staffing shortages? | CNN Business
sources.claim: Humanoid nursing robots piloted in hospitals perform logistics and guidance tasks rather than examining or treating patients.
sources.transferJustification: Shows the state of patient-facing hospital robots in a structured facility (E2): delivery and escort, with clinical assessment and treatment left to nurses.

sources.title: VSee Unveils World's First Autonomous Telehealth AI Robot at HIMSS 2026
sources.claim: The newest 'autonomous' hospital clinical robot is a telepresence platform: autonomy covers navigation to the bedside while a remote human clinician performs the clinical encounter.
sources.transferJustification: Relevant because it is the closest commercial system for bedside clinical encounters; the clinical assessment and treatment are performed by a remote human, so it cannot support a positive judgment.

roles.description: Provide specialized nursing care for patients in critical or coronary care units.

tasks.label: Evaluate patients' vital signs or laboratory data to determine emergency intervention needs.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

tasks.label: Monitor patients for changes in status and indications of conditions such as sepsis or shock and institute appropriate interventions.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: ICU patient in shock on vasopressors (post-cardiac-surgery or septic): nurse continuously watches arterial line/MAP, CVP, cardiac output, rhythm, urine output, chest tube output and skin perfusion; on a pressure drop she checks the patient and lines for artifact or bleeding, gives a fluid bolus, titrates norepinephrine per protocol, draws a lactate/ABG and notifies the intensivist.

New deterioration suggesting sepsis in a less acute ICU/step-down patient: nurse notices fever, tachycardia, hypotension, new confusion or decreased urine output during rounds; escalates, obtains blood cultures and lactate, starts broad-spectrum antibiotics and a 30 mL/kg crystalloid bolus, reassesses perfusion and documents the bundle.

Routine hourly/shift surveillance in the ICU: head-to-toe and neuro assessments, hands-on checks (pulses, capillary refill, skin, lung sounds, abdomen), vital-sign and I&O trending, alarm parameter setting, drain/line/ventilator checks; small interventions such as repositioning, oxygen adjustment, suctioning, and notifying the provider on subtle change.

Abrupt decompensation or arrest (arrhythmia, respiratory failure, massive bleed): nurse recognizes the change, calls rapid response/code, starts bag-mask ventilation or compressions, applies defibrillator pads, draws up and pushes emergency drugs, assists with intubation or emergent line placement.

Protocol-driven titration of a single support therapy against a continuously monitored variable in a supported but diagnostically stable ICU patient over hours: vasopressor infusion held to a physician-set MAP target, or ventilator FiO2/PEEP/minute ventilation adjusted to SpO2/etCO2 targets, with lines, pump and ventilator already in place.

sources.system: Closed-loop vasopressor (CLV) controller (Rinehart/Joosten group; Chemyx syringe pump driven from an EV-1000 monitor)
sources.developer: Desebbe, Rinehart, Cannesson, Joosten et al. (academic; Sironis-related controller)
sources.title: Control of Postoperative Hypotension Using a Closed-Loop System for Norepinephrine Infusion in Patients After Cardiac Surgery: A Randomized Trial
sources.claim: A closed-loop vasopressor controller autonomously titrated norepinephrine infusion in patients in the ICU after cardiac surgery, holding MAP in a set target band with far less hypotension than manual clinician titration.
sources.transferJustification: Same narrow task element: detecting a hemodynamic change (falling MAP) in a monitored ICU patient and instituting the protocol intervention (vasopressor titration); the machine acts on the physical world by driving the infusion pump.

sources.title: Tight control of mean arterial pressure using a closed loop system for norepinephrine infusion after high-risk abdominal surgery: a randomized controlled trial (PubMed)
sources.claim: In a second randomized ICU trial, the closed-loop norepinephrine system maintained a physician-set MAP target better than manual titration by clinicians.
sources.transferJustification: Same narrow element of the task (recognize hypotension, institute vasopressor intervention) in the ICU setting, with quality benchmarked against clinician manual titration.

sources.title: Effect of Automated Closed-Loop Ventilation Versus Conventional Ventilation on Duration and Quality of Ventilation (ACTiVE), ClinicalTrials.gov NCT04593810
sources.claim: A fully automated closed-loop ventilation mode on commercial ICU ventilators adjusts ventilation and oxygenation settings to physician-set physiological targets without step-by-step clinician input.
sources.transferJustification: Related task element: continuous monitoring of a critically ill patient's oxygenation/ventilation status and automatic institution of the corresponding support change (FiO2, PEEP, minute ventilation), the ventilator-side analogue of protocolized nurse titration.

sources.title: INTELLiVENT-ASV Intelligent ventilation mode | Hamilton Medical
sources.claim: The automated closed-loop ventilation mode is used as a routine ventilation mode in real ICUs, indicating deployment rather than laboratory demonstration only.
sources.transferJustification: Deployment evidence for the same closed-loop titration element described above; not evidence for patient assessment or other nursing interventions.

sources.title: Moxi, healthcare robot created in Austin, completes 500k deliveries
sources.claim: The most widely deployed US hospital robot performs logistics (supplies, medications, lab specimens) on hospital floors; it does no patient assessment or bedside clinical intervention.
sources.transferJustification: Cited to bound capability: the most mature deployed hospital robot handles transport tasks only, so it cannot substantiate assessment-plus-intervention instances.

sources.developer: Foxconn with NVIDIA / Kawasaki (piloted at Taichung Veterans General Hospital)
sources.title: Could AI nursing robots help healthcare staffing shortages? | CNN Business
sources.claim: A piloted hospital nursing robot in a Taiwanese ward performs medication delivery, ward patrol and patient guidance, not hands-on patient assessment or resuscitation.
sources.transferJustification: Cited to bound capability of current ward robots: delivery and guidance only, no bedside monitoring-and-intervention loop.

sources.developer: UC San Diego (Yip lab) et al.
sources.title: Humanoids in Hospitals: A Technical Study of Humanoid Robot Surrogates for Dexterous Medical Interventions
sources.claim: Humanoid robots performing physical examinations and emergency interventions have only been shown under human teleoperation in simulated settings.
sources.transferJustification: Directly covers bedside exam and emergency intervention, but only teleoperated and in simulation, so it cannot support a positive judgment.

sources.title: Performance, Safety, and Patient Experience of an Autonomous Robotic Phlebotomy Device: A Multicenter Trial
sources.claim: An autonomous robotic phlebotomy device performs venipuncture on cooperative outpatients under human supervision in hospital blood-draw departments.
sources.transferJustification: Covers one sub-step of a sepsis bundle (obtaining blood) in seated, cooperative outpatients; it does not transfer to recognizing deterioration or delivering the rest of the bundle at an ICU bedside.

tasks.label: Administer medications intravenously, by injection, orally, through gastric tubes, or by other methods.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: ICU bedside: managing and titrating running continuous IV infusions (norepinephrine, propofol/fentanyl sedation, insulin, heparin) to a monitored target - adjusting pump rates to the patient's hemodynamics/sedation level over the shift and keeping the drug flowing.

ICU bedside: intermittent IV doses - pulling the vial/bag from the automated dispensing cabinet, scanning patient and drug, reconstituting or drawing up the dose, scrubbing the needleless hub of a central or peripheral line, giving an IV push over 2-5 min or spiking/priming and hanging a piggyback, flushing, and watching the patient for reaction.

Awake, extubated ICU/step-down patient: oral medications - several tablets (some crushed in applesauce) and liquids given by mouth with water, assessing swallow and aspiration risk, confirming ingestion.

Intubated/sedated patient with NG/OG/PEG tube: crushing and dissolving tablets, verifying tube placement, checking gastric residual, flushing before/between/after each drug, delivering via ENFit syringe into the tube.

Subcutaneous or intramuscular injection to a patient lying in an ICU bed (SC heparin/enoxaparin, sliding-scale insulin, IM antiemetic): site selection on abdomen/arm/thigh amid lines, dressings and edema, injection and sharps disposal.

Code/crisis: rapid administration of resuscitation and emergency drugs (epinephrine, amiodarone, push-dose pressors, RSI agents) from the crash cart on verbal orders, in a crowded room while chest compressions and other procedures are underway.

sources.system: Closed-loop vasopressor (CLV) controller driving a norepinephrine syringe pump
sources.title: Control of Postoperative Hypotension Using a Closed-Loop System for Norepinephrine Infusion in Patients After Cardiac Surgery: A Randomized Trial - PMC
sources.claim: A closed-loop vasopressor controller autonomously titrated a norepinephrine infusion in critically ill patients in an ICU after cardiac surgery, maintaining arterial pressure better than nurse-performed manual titration.

sources.title: Tight control of mean arterial pressure using a closed loop system for norepinephrine infusion after high-risk abdominal surgery: a randomized controlled trial - PMC
sources.claim: A second randomized trial in ICU patients after high-risk abdominal surgery showed closed-loop control of norepinephrine infusion held the ordered mean-arterial-pressure target better than manual titration by ICU nurses.

sources.system: BIS-guided dual closed-loop propofol/remifentanil sedation controller
sources.developer: Le Guen / Fischler et al. (Hopital Foch)
sources.title: Automated sedation outperforms manual administration of propofol and remifentanil in critically ill patients with deep sedation: a randomized phase II trial | Intensive Care Medicine
sources.claim: A dual closed-loop controller automatically administered and titrated IV propofol and remifentanil for sedation of critically ill ICU patients with multiorgan failure, outperforming manual administration.

sources.title: First ever robotic intramuscular injection - Hospital News
sources.claim: A robot autonomously performed an intramuscular injection (needle-free jet) into a person's arm, identifying the site itself and delivering the dose without human involvement.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: vaccine-type intramuscular injection. It is the same physical act as a nurse's injection (locate site on a presented limb, deliver a drug dose into tissue), but jet-delivered and shown only once, so it supports only a fixtured, purpose-built presentation.

sources.title: Vitestro Achieves CE Marking for Autonomous Blood Drawing Device
sources.claim: A CE-marked autonomous device inserts a needle into a patient's vein and completes a blood draw with the arm placed in the device's cradle; it has been used in over 10,000 patients and is being deployed in ... and labs.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: venipuncture. Closest patient-contacting needle robotics in routine use - autonomous vessel finding and needle placement with the arm fixtured in the machine - but it withdraws blood at a draw station and does not deliver drugs, verify orders, or work on lines of critically ill patients.

sources.title: World's First Robot with Closed System Transfer Device to be Introduced by Equashield to Further Protect Pharmacy Staff during Hazardous Drug Compounding
sources.claim: Commercial compounding robots autonomously prepare IV doses (drawing drug from vials into syringes and bags) inside an enclosed cabinet-sized cell in hospital pharmacies; they never contact a patient or an indwelling line.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: sterile IV compounding, the preparation step upstream of the nurse's administration. It shows vial/syringe handling is automated inside a fenced pharmacy cell, but no such robot connects a syringe to a patient's vascular access or gives the dose.

sources.system: Moxi; Nurabot; Changi General Hospital robot fleet
sources.title: Could AI nursing robots help healthcare staffing shortages? | CNN Business
sources.claim: Hospital service robots deployed at scale carry medicines and supplies through wards to staff; patient-facing clinical acts are not part of what they do.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: medication transport. Bounds deployed hospital robot capability - the robot brings the drug to the unit, and a nurse performs the administration.

sources.system: Moxi and other hospital assistant robots
sources.title: This Humanoid AI Robot Is Being Tested in Hospitals—Plus 7 More Transforming Healthcare | Nurse.Org
sources.claim: Hospital humanoid/assistant robots under test are restricted to non-patient-facing work such as delivering specimens, supplies and linens.
sources.transferJustification: Bounding evidence: shows the deployed envelope for hospital robots excludes patient-facing medication administration.
