tasks.label: Conduct pulmonary assessments to identify abnormal respiratory patterns or breathing sounds that indicate problems.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Scheduled shift/hourly pulmonary assessment on an intubated, mechanically ventilated ICU patient: inspect chest rise and symmetry, work of breathing and ventilator synchrony; auscultate anterior and lateral fields (and posterior fields when the patient is turned) around ETT, lines, drains, dressings and monitoring leads; correlate diminished sounds, crackles, wheezes or secretions with vent waveforms, SpO2/ETCO2 and ABGs; document and report findings.

Scheduled/serial pulmonary assessment on a non-intubated critical or coronary care patient (heart failure, COPD exacerbation, post-cardiac-surgery, sepsis, high-flow or BiPAP): count and characterize rate, depth, rhythm and effort, note accessory-muscle use and speech in phrases; sit the patient forward or roll them to auscultate posterior bases; assess cough and sputum; identify crackles, wheeze or absent bases and act on them.

Rapid focused pulmonary assessment during acute deterioration (sudden desaturation, dyspnea, ventilator high-pressure alarm, post-op bleed, code/rapid-response): within seconds distinguish unilateral absent breath sounds (pneumothorax, mainstem intubation, mucus plug), bronchospastic wheeze, stridor, gurgling secretions, and abnormal patterns (Cheyne-Stokes, Kussmaul, paradoxical, agonal), amid alarms, a crowded bedside and simultaneous interventions.

Focused post-procedure or post-positioning verification check: confirm bilateral, equal breath sounds and adequate pattern after intubation or tube repositioning, extubation, chest tube insertion or removal, central line placement, suctioning, bronchoscopy, proning/supination, or return from transport; escalate immediately if asymmetric or absent.

Pulmonary assessment away from the ICU bedside: during intra-hospital transport to CT/OR/cath lab, in an ED resuscitation bay, PACU, or on an interfacility ground/air critical-care transport, with high ambient noise, cramped access, the patient covered by blankets and straps, and only a portable monitor and ventilator available.

sources.system: Autonomous robotic auscultation platform (Bayesian-optimization stethoscope placement)
sources.developer: Yifan Zhu, Alexander Smith, Kris Hauser (Univ. of Illinois Urbana-Champaign / Duke)
sources.title: Automated Heart and Lung Auscultation in Robotic Physical Examinations (arXiv:2201.09511 / IEEE RA-L)
sources.claim: First implementation of autonomous robotic ...: a robot arm autonomously selects and reaches auscultation points on seated human subjects and captures sounds; validated on 4 healthy subjects in a laboratory, with no automated identification of abnormal breath sounds or respiratory patterns and no patient-care deployment.
sources.transferJustification: Same task's core physical sub-step (placing a stethoscope on the chest and capturing lung sounds), but it stops at sound acquisition on cooperative healthy volunteers in a lab; it does not produce the nurse's clinical output of identifying abnormal breath sounds or respiratory patterns, and has not been shown on critically ill patients.

sources.system: Collaborative robotic platform for autonomous auscultation
sources.developer: D. Lopes, L. Coelho, M. F. Silva (ISEP / INESC TEC, Portugal)
sources.title: Development of a Collaborative Robotic Platform for Autonomous Auscultation (Applied Sciences 13(3):1604)
sources.claim: Collaborative robot arm with 3D vision that autonomously locates auscultation points and places a stethoscope on the skin; evaluated performing a simulated pulmonary auscultation on six volunteers in a laboratory, reporting correct point identification and comfortable positioning, but not clinical interpretation of lung sounds.

sources.system: Automated robotic platform for remote auscultation
sources.title: Toward Fully Automated Robotic Platform for Remote Auscultation (arXiv:2201.05272)
sources.claim: Automated robotic platform for remote ... using a 6-DOF cooperative arm and LiDAR camera to estimate stethoscope landing positions from body-surface landmarks with force-limited contact; results reported are preliminary and focused on cardiac landing-point estimation, not on completing a pulmonary assessment.
sources.transferJustification: Related task (robotic placement of a stethoscope for cardiac auscultation) shares the object and precision of chest auscultation, but the reported capability is landing-point estimation and contact control, not identification of abnormal breath sounds or breathing patterns.

sources.title: Autonomous Robotic Point-of-Care Ultrasound Imaging for Monitoring of COVID-19-Induced Pulmonary Diseases (Frontiers in Robotics and AI)
sources.claim: Robotic chest examination that has actually been used on real patients with respiratory pathology in hospital settings (COVID-19 cabin hospitals/ICUs) is tele-echography: a remote physician drives the probe, so the clinical assessment is produced by a human operator, not autonomously by the machine.
sources.transferJustification: Related task (robotic acquisition of chest data on hospitalized respiratory patients); cited to show that the only patient-facing chest-examination robots in real hospital use are teleoperated, so they cannot support a positive autonomy judgment.

sources.system: Autonomous lightweight ultrasound robot for liver sonography
sources.developer: Tsinghua University / Beijing Tsinghua Changgung Hospital collaboration
sources.title: Beyond hospital reach: Autonomous lightweight ultrasound robot for liver sonography (arXiv:2510.08106)
sources.claim: The current frontier of autonomous contact examination of a human torso in a real hospital is autonomous ultrasound scanning of cooperative subjects in an ultrasound department; the robot acquires standard imaging planes for physician interpretation rather than delivering a bedside clinical assessment of a critically ill patient.
sources.transferJustification: Related task (autonomous placement of a hand-held sensor on a patient's trunk in a hospital); shows autonomous torso contact is feasible for imaging acquisition on cooperative outpatients, but the output is images for a radiologist, not identification of abnormal breathing sounds or patterns in critical care.

sources.developer: Kawasaki Heavy Industries with Foxconn (NVIDIA AI stack), piloted at Taichung Veterans General Hospital
sources.title: Kawasaki Develops Nurse Assistant Robot with Foxconn
sources.claim: Nursing robots actually piloted in hospital wards are confined to logistics and guidance tasks; patient assessment and clinical judgment remain with nurses.
sources.transferJustification: Cited as the state of deployed hospital nursing robotics: no assessment or auscultation function, confirming the absence of a deployed system able to perform pulmonary assessment in an ICU.

tasks.label: Assess patients' pain levels or sedation requirements.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Alert, communicative ICU patient (e.g., post-op cardiac, extubated, or awaiting extubation): nurse goes to the bedside on a q1-4h schedule, elicits a 0-10 numeric rating plus location/quality/radiation, inspects incision or line sites (often lifting dressings, light palpation), correlates with HR/BP/RR and grimacing, judges whether the current analgesic regimen is adequate, and documents the score and plan in the EHR.

Intubated, mechanically ventilated, sedated patient: nurse scores pain with a behavioral tool (CPOT/BPS) — facial expression, body movement, ventilator compliance, and muscle tension elicited by passive flexion/extension of the arm — and scores sedation depth with RASS/SAS, escalating from observation to voice to physical stimulation (shoulder shake, sternal rub) as needed, then judges whether sedation is at the ordered target and whether analgesia should precede sedation titration.

Procedural and turning-related pain: nurse assesses pain before, during, and after painful interventions (repositioning, dressing/wound care, chest tube or line removal, suctioning, mobilization), watching guarding, grimacing, hemodynamic and ventilator responses in real time, deciding whether to pre-medicate, pause, or bolus.

Confounded/complex patient in whom standard scales are unreliable: delirium, dementia, severe TBI or post-arrest neuro injury, deep sedation with neuromuscular blockade, or a hemodynamically unstable patient; the nurse must infer discomfort from physiologic trends, ventilator dyssynchrony, pupillary/BIS or other adjunct data, family/baseline input, and a targeted physical check for pain sources (bladder distension, positioning, ischemic limb).

Synthesis and communication of sedation/analgesia requirements at rounds or handoff: reviewing 12-24h score trends, drip rates, tolerance/withdrawal signs, and daily sedation-interruption/awakening-trial results, then recommending a target and titration change to the intensivist and receiving/verifying new orders.

sources.title: Diligent Robotics Unveils Moxi 2.0, Advancing The Largest Fleet of Deployed AI-Powered Mobile Manipulation Robots
sources.claim: Moxi is the largest deployed fleet of autonomous mobile manipulation robots in US hospitals, but its work is non-clinical fetch-and-deliver logistics (medications, lab samples, supplies); it performs no patient assessment or patient contact.
sources.transferJustification: Cited to mark the deployed frontier of hospital robotics, not to substantiate the task: Moxi never touches or evaluates a patient, so nothing transfers to eliciting and scoring pain/sedation responses.

sources.developer: Foxconn with NVIDIA / Taichung Veterans General Hospital
sources.title: Could AI nursing robots help healthcare staffing shortages? | CNN Business
sources.claim: Nurabot, an autonomous AI nursing robot piloted in a Taiwanese hospital, is scoped to delivery and patient guidance tasks rather than clinical patient assessment.
sources.transferJustification: Cited as the closest 'nursing robot' deployment; its demonstrated tasks are transport and wayfinding, which do not transfer to bedside pain scoring or sedation-depth stimulation and judgment.

sources.system: Smart patient-care robot (2D LiDAR + enhanced D* Lite)

instances.label: Arterial blood sampling in an ICU bed: nurse draws from an indwelling radial/femoral arterial line (waste volume, ABG syringe plus vacutainer tubes, flush, re-zero transducer, keep the stopcock sterile) or, when no line exists, performs a radial artery puncture on a hypotensive, often edematous patient; specimen labeled at bedside and run STAT.

Blood sampling from a central venous catheter, PICC or dialysis catheter in an ICU bed: pausing infusions, discarding waste, filling multiple tube types in order of draw (chemistry, CBC, coags, lactate), inoculating blood-culture bottles with sterile technique, then flushing/locking the line and labeling tubes at the bedside.

Peripheral venipuncture on a supine ICU or step-down patient with no usable line: tourniquet, vein selection in an edematous or vasoconstricted arm, needle stick, filling several labeled vacuum tubes, mixing them, applying a dressing.

Urine specimen: sterile aspiration from the sampling port of an indwelling Foley catheter (or straight-cath / clean-catch collection in an awake patient), transfer into a sterile cup or transport tube, and labeling, for urinalysis and culture.

Respiratory specimen: tracheal aspirate from an intubated, ventilated patient using a suction catheter and sputum trap (or an expectorated sputum sample, or a naso-/oropharyngeal swab for a viral panel), with pre-oxygenation and monitoring of patient tolerance.

Other body specimens: wound and drain-fluid cultures, stool sample for C. difficile, rectal/nares surveillance swabs, CSF drawn from an external ventricular drain, pleural or peritoneal fluid handed off during a bedside procedure, each placed in the correct container and labeled.

sources.title: Performance, Safety, and Patient Experience of an Autonomous Robotic Phlebotomy Device: A Multicenter Trial (Clinical Chemistry)
sources.claim: Vitestro's Aletta autonomous robotic phlebotomy device performed venipunctures autonomously on 1633 outpatients in Dutch hospital phlebotomy departments with a 94.5% first-stick success rate, including 92.7% in patients with difficult venous ....
sources.transferJustification: Related task: routine diagnostic venipuncture in an outpatient phlebotomy department rather than ICU specimen collection. It transfers to the peripheral-venipuncture instance (same act, same needle/tube hardware, same accepted output of filled labeled tubes), but only with the patient seated and the arm fixtured in the device; it does not address line draws, catheters or airway specimens.

tasks.label: Set up and monitor medical equipment and devices such as cardiac monitors, mechanical ventilators and alarms, oxygen delivery devices, transducers, or pressure lines.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: ICU/CCU admission or transfer: nurse applies 5-lead ECG electrodes to a patient's prepped chest skin (peeling adhesive backing, siting to anatomical landmarks, snapping lead wires), places an SpO2 probe on a finger/ear, wraps an NIBP cuff, routes cables clear of lines, then verifies waveforms and sets patient-specific alarm limits on the bedside cardiac monitor.

Oxygen delivery device set-up or escalation at the bedside: selecting and fitting a nasal cannula, simple/non-rebreather mask, high-flow nasal cannula (attaching heated circuit, water bottle/sterile water bag, cannula sized to nares) or NIV mask, connecting to a flowmeter or blender, setting flow/FiO2, checking seal and skin, and confirming SpO2 response on a often restless, sometimes agitated or obese patient.

Mechanical ventilator set-up/verification for an intubated patient: assembling the circuit with humidifier or HME, inline suction catheter and filters, performing the machine self-test/leak check, connecting to the endotracheal or tracheostomy tube without dislodging it, supporting the tubing, confirming prescribed mode/settings and setting alarm limits.

Invasive hemodynamic pressure line set-up: spiking a heparinized/normal saline bag into a pressure infuser, priming a disposable transducer kit and pressure tubing without air bubbles, connecting to an arterial or central venous catheter using aseptic technique, mounting and leveling the transducer to the phlebostatic axis, zeroing to atmosphere, running a square-wave test, and confirming waveform quality.

Continuous monitoring and troubleshooting across a shift: watching monitor waveforms and vent graphics, responding to alarms (artifact, lead-off, damped arterial trace, high peak pressure, desaturation), physically re-siting electrodes or probes, re-zeroing and re-leveling transducers after repositioning, suctioning or re-securing circuits, adjusting FiO2/flow, retitrating alarm limits, and escalating to the intensivist.

sources.title: Swisslog Healthcare Partners with Diligent Robotics to Enhance Hospital Logistics – Ortho Spine News
sources.claim: The most widely deployed autonomous hospital robot fleet (Moxi, 25+ US hospitals) performs logistics — delivering medications, supplies and lab specimens — and is described as handling non-patient-facing tasks; it does not set up or attach monitoring, ventilation or oxygen equipment to patients.
sources.transferJustification: Cited to establish the ceiling of currently deployed autonomous hospital-floor robotics: mobile manipulation limited to transport and supply picking in corridors and supply rooms, with no bedside device set-up or patient attachment, so it cannot substantiate this task at any tier.

sources.title: Autonomous Robotic Phlebotomy Shows High Success Rates in Multicenter Trial | Clinical Lab Products
sources.claim: Autonomous patient-contact robotics does exist in structured clinical settings, but only for a narrow, heavily fixtured procedure: Vitestro's Aletta device performs venous blood draws autonomously on patients in outpatient phlebotomy departments in a multicenter trial.
sources.transferJustification: Related task = venipuncture. It shows autonomy on a cooperative seated patient whose arm is fixtured in a dedicated armrest, using one instrument on one target. It does not transfer to ICU device set-up, which requires handling adhesive electrodes, deformable tubing/circuits, connectors, saline bags and masks on a supine, lined, often agitated patient, so it supports no positive judgment here.

sources.title: Frontiers | Telerobotic Operation of Intensive Care Unit Ventilators
sources.claim: Robotic operation of ICU ventilators has been prototyped only as teleoperation: a Cartesian robot presses the ventilator touchscreen under remote human control from outside the room, tested on a ventilated mannequin.
sources.transferJustification: Directly related task (operating ICU ventilator controls), but it is continuously teleoperated and only adjusts an already-connected machine's touchscreen; it cannot support a positive judgment for setting up or monitoring the device.

sources.developer: Tsinghua University / Beijing Tsinghua Changgung Hospital team (arXiv 2510.08106)
sources.title: Beyond hospital reach: Autonomous lightweight ultrasound robot for liver sonography
sources.claim: Autonomous force-controlled placement of a handheld sensor on a patient's torso has been demonstrated in a hospital department (autonomous liver ultrasound scanning at Beijing Tsinghua Changgung Hospital), but only for imaging, not for attaching or assembling clinical equipment.
sources.transferJustification: Related task = placing a probe against a patient's skin with force control. It is the closest patient-contact analog to placing electrodes/probes, but it involves a single rigid tool on an exposed abdomen with no adhesive handling, cable/tubing routing, connector mating, priming, or alarm configuration, so it does not substantiate completing any instance of this task.

sources.title: Feasibility study on full closed-loop control ventilation (IntelliVent-ASV) in ICU patients with acute respiratory failure - PubMed
sources.claim: Commercial closed-loop ventilation automates titration of ventilator parameters once the patient is already connected, but is a self-adjusting device rather than a system that sets up circuits, attaches devices to patients, or performs the nurse's bedside alarm troubleshooting.
sources.transferJustification: Related capability = automated adjustment of ventilator settings from measured SpO2/EtCO2. It covers only in-machine parameter titration on an already-connected patient and still raises alarms requiring bedside human assessment, so it cannot complete the whole monitoring instance.

tasks.label: Administer blood and blood products, monitoring patients for signs and symptoms related to transfusion reactions.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Routine packed red blood cell transfusion for a hemodynamically stable ICU patient: bedside two-person verification of unit/patient armband/blood bank tag, baseline vital signs, spiking the unit with filtered Y-tubing, priming with saline, connecting to an existing central or peripheral line, programming the pump, remaining at bedside for the first 15 minutes, rechecking vitals per protocol, flushing and documenting at completion.

Administration of non-RBC products — platelets, fresh frozen plasma, cryoprecipitate, albumin, factor concentrates — often several in sequence on a patient already running multiple drips, requiring line/lumen compatibility checks, appropriate filters and rates, and observation for reactions.

Massive transfusion during active hemorrhage (trauma, GI bleed, post-cardiac-surgery bleeding): receiving coolers, running multiple units through a rapid infuser/blood warmer in quick succession while the team works around the bed, watching for hypothermia, citrate-induced hypocalcemia, and circulatory overload amid alarms and interruptions.

Suspected transfusion reaction: recognizing fever/rigors, hypotension, dyspnea, urticaria, or hemoglobinuria; stopping the transfusion, disconnecting tubing and maintaining the line with saline, reassessing airway and vitals, notifying the provider, giving antihistamine/steroid/epinephrine or vasopressors, rechecking clerical identification, and returning the bag and post-reaction blood/urine specimens to the blood bank with documentation.

Transfusion in a device-encumbered or access-difficult patient: prone-positioned ARDS patient, ECMO or CRRT circuit, dialysis catheter or PICC, contact-isolation room, agitated or restrained patient, or small-volume aliquots given by syringe pump to a pediatric/neonatal or fluid-restricted patient.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Routine ordered lab work on a comparatively stable ICU/step-down patient with accessible arm veins: nurse selects a vein, applies tourniquet, performs peripheral venipuncture, fills and inverts several vacuum tubes, withdraws needle and bandages, then labels specimens at bedside.

Vascular access and line sampling in unstable or difficult patients: placing a peripheral IV in an edematous, hypotensive or coagulopathic patient, drawing an arterial blood gas or sampling from an arterial/central line with waste and flush steps, drawing blood cultures with sterile technique, at the bedside amid pumps, ventilator tubing and family presence.

Airway and pulmonary therapeutic procedures on a ventilated patient: open or closed endotracheal/tracheostomy suctioning titrated to secretions and desaturation, oral care, cuff pressure checks, assisting with intubation/extubation, chest tube and drainage system management, proning/repositioning.

High-risk medication and infusion procedures: spiking, priming and hanging vasoactive, sedative and electrolyte infusions, programming smart pumps, titrating drips to MAP/sedation targets, giving IV push meds through multi-lumen lines, checking and administering blood products with two-nurse verification.

Wound, drain, line-site and tube procedures: sterile central line and arterial line dressing changes, surgical wound and pressure-injury dressing changes with packing, drain stripping and emptying, indwelling urinary catheter insertion, NG/OG tube insertion with placement verification and enteral feeding setup.

Bedside diagnostic procedures: obtaining a 12-lead ECG (electrode placement on a supine, lined patient), leveling/zeroing hemodynamic transducers and running cardiac output measurements, point-of-care glucose and blood gas sampling and analysis, collecting sputum/tracheal aspirate, urine and wound culture specimens.

sources.title: Aletta® - Vitestro
sources.claim: Vitestro's Aletta is a CE-marked robotic device that performs the complete venous blood draw autonomously — tourniquet, imaging-based vein selection, needle insertion, tube changing and inversion, bandaging — at a fixed workstation where the patient positions an arm in the device, supervised by one staff member per up to three devices.
sources.transferJustification: Directly a therapeutic/diagnostic bedside-type procedure (venipuncture for ordered labs) that critical care nurses perform.

sources.transferJustification: Establishes worker-comparable reliability (first-stick success comparable to manual 93-97%) for autonomous venipuncture, the routine blood-sampling procedure in this task.

tasks.label: Assist physicians with procedures such as bronchoscopy, endoscopy, endotracheal intubation, or elective cardioversion.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Urgent/emergent endotracheal intubation at the ICU bedside of a deteriorating patient: nurse assembles and checks airway cart (laryngoscope/video scope, tubes, stylet, bougie, bag-valve-mask, suction), preoxygenates and positions the patient, draws up and pushes induction and paralytic agents per physician order, hands equipment in sequence, applies external laryngeal manipulation and suction of vomitus/secretions, watches monitor and calls out vitals/desaturation, inflates cuff, secures tube, connects capnography and ventilator, and arranges confirmatory imaging.

Bedside flexible bronchoscopy in an intubated ICU patient (bronchoalveolar lavage, secretion clearance, or airway inspection): nurse sets up scope tower, light source, swivel adapter and suction, prepares saline aliquots and lidocaine, titrates sedation/analgesia per protocol, feeds and receives lavage syringes, labels and dispatches specimens, monitors SpO2/hemodynamics and manages desaturation or arrhythmia during the procedure, then reassesses the patient afterward.

Elective/urgent synchronized cardioversion for atrial fibrillation or flutter in a coronary/critical care unit: nurse verifies consent, NPO status and anticoagulation, applies defibrillation pads in correct anterior-posterior/anterolateral position on a possibly diaphoretic or hairy chest, sets the defibrillator to synchronized mode with adequate R-wave sensing, administers and monitors procedural sedation with airway equipment ready, delivers/charges shock at the physician's direction, and monitors rhythm, airway and vitals through recovery.

Bedside upper GI endoscopy in an ICU patient with a GI bleed: nurse positions the patient in left lateral decubitus, places bite block and protects the airway, manages suction of blood and secretions, hands and manages accessories (clips, injection needles, banding devices), assists with irrigation and specimen handling, gives and titrates sedation, restrains or calms an agitated patient, and monitors hemodynamics during active bleeding.

Assisting with other bedside invasive procedures in the ICU (central venous or arterial line, chest tube, lumbar puncture, percutaneous tracheostomy, PEG): nurse performs time-out, opens and arranges the sterile kit, gowns/gloves the physician, maintains the sterile field, hands syringes, flushes, sutures and dressings, holds and positions the patient (e.g., curled for LP, Trendelenburg for IJ line), administers local/sedating drugs, monitors the patient, and applies the final dressing and documentation.

tasks.label: Identify malfunctioning equipment or devices.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Monitoring artifact/alarm triage at the ICU bedside: a cardiac monitor, arterial line or pulse oximeter shows a suspect waveform or alarms; the nurse inspects electrodes on the patient's skin, cables, transducer and probe, re-levels/flushes or swaps a component, and decides whether the fault is a failing device/cable or a real patient change, within minutes and while care continues.

Ventilator/respiratory equipment alarm on an intubated patient: high peak pressure, low tidal volume, or circuit-disconnect alarm; the nurse traces the circuit, checks connections, condensate, kinks, filters, humidifier, O2/air supply and the machine's self-test, and determines whether the ventilator or circuit is malfunctioning versus a patient cause, escalating to RT/biomed and swapping the unit if needed.

Infusion or syringe pump fault: occlusion, air-in-line, downstream-pressure or door/keypad errors, or a vasoactive drip not delivering; the nurse traces the tubing through pumps, clamps and stopcocks, checks the IV site, tests the channel, concludes the pump itself is defective, tags it out and swaps in a replacement quickly.

Scheduled pre-use and shift-start equipment checks in the unit: crash-cart/defibrillator daily check, wall and portable suction, manual resuscitation bag, backup oxygen, bed and bed-alarm function, telemetry/pump batteries and spare devices; the nurse runs the function tests, identifies units that fail, and flags them for biomedical engineering.

Specialty life-support/therapy devices: CRRT machine, intra-aortic balloon pump, ECMO circuit, targeted temperature-management unit, VAD controller or feeding pump throws an error code or alarm; the nurse inspects circuit, sensors and connections and determines whether it signals a device malfunction (clotted filter, air detected, sensor/pump failure) or patient physiology, while therapy continues.

sources.transferJustification: Establishes the actual functional scope of autonomous robots deployed in US hospital wards/ICUs: item transport, not inspection or troubleshooting of patient-connected devices, so it cannot substantiate completion of this task at E2.

sources.title: Could AI nursing robots help healthcare staffing shortages? | CNN Business

sources.title: Quadruped robot boosts safety and maintenance at aging cement plant

sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous fault detection on machinery in a structured facility. Transfer to ICU work is limited — the checkpoints are pre-mapped fixed plant machinery inspected by remote sensing, with no handling of patient-attached tubing, cables or probes and no clinical artifact-versus-patient judgment.

sources.title: MATT the Smart Device Test Automation Robot | Adapta Robotics
sources.claim: MATT is a commercial robotic test-automation system that physically presses buttons and touchscreens on fixtured devices — including medical devices — verifies displayed/functional response against references with AI computer vision, and runs continuous unattended test cycles, replacing manual QA checking of whether a device functions correctly.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic functional testing of fixtured electronic/medical devices to determine whether they work correctly. This is the E1 counterfactual form of a pre-use equipment check — the device is brought to the machine, the robot exercises its controls and verifies its response, flagging failing units.

instances.label: Routine post-mortem care in an ICU room after an expected death: nurse verifies death and time, removes ET tube, IV lines, arterial/central lines, urinary catheter and drains (peeling adhesive tape and dressings off fragile skin), dresses or plugs leaking sites, cleans blood and body fluids from the body, closes eyes and mouth, positions the body supine with a pillow, replaces the gown and linens, applies wrist/toe ID tags, wraps in a shroud or zips into a body bag, and helps transfer the body to a mortuary cart.

Post-mortem care with family at the bedside: nurse removes equipment and tidies the room enough for viewing, gently washes the face and hands and combs hair, arranges the body and covers to look peaceful, supports and answers questions from grieving relatives, gives them private time, collects and inventories personal belongings and returns them, then completes bagging/tagging after the family leaves.

Medical examiner / coroner case (unexpected death, trauma, suspected homicide or death within 24 h of admission): all lines, tubes and devices are left in place and secured, restraints and clothing preserved, hands sometimes bagged, no washing of the body, careful chain-of-custody documentation and belongings handling, body tagged and bagged intact for the ME.

Post-mortem care with religious or cultural requirements: family members or a religious representative participate in or perform the washing and positioning, specific rituals and orientation of the body, restrictions on who may touch the body or on removal of items, tight timelines for release; nurse coordinates, assists and adapts the standard procedure.

Complex body condition: bariatric or contaminated/infectious (isolation precautions, sealed double bagging, PPE), or after prolonged CPR with extensive blood, emesis and fluid soiling, open chest/wounds, multiple devices and lines, sometimes with organ/tissue-donation coordination requiring the body and lines kept in a specified state; requires multi-person lifting and repositioning.

sources.title: RABBIT: A Robot-Assisted Bed Bathing System with Multimodal Perception and Integrated Compliance
sources.claim: The closest robotic capability to body washing is a Cornell lab system, RABBIT, which autonomously washes, rinses and dries skin, but its demonstrated scope is a single limb (e.g., a forearm) of a cooperative living participant in a lab study, not full-body post-mortem care with device removal, shrouding and tagging.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: bed bathing a human body. It is the nearest demonstrated robotic contact-with-body hygiene skill, but it covers only one limb of a cooperative person under lab conditions and does not transfer to whole-body post-mortem care, which additionally requires removing taped tubes and catheters, dressing sites, repositioning a dead weight body, shrouding, tagging and family interaction.

sources.developer: Georgia Tech / Stanford (Erickson, Kapusta, Liu, Kemp et al.)
sources.title: Personalized collaborative plans for robot-assisted dressing via optimization and simulation (Autonomous Robots)
sources.claim: Robot-assisted dressing research (nearest analogue to gowning/shrouding a body) has only reached lab-scale assistance with sliding a hospital gown onto the arms of seated, cooperative participants.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robot-assisted dressing, analogous to gowning/shrouding in post-mortem care. It falls far short: the recipient is alive, seated and actively cooperating, only sleeves are handled, and no manipulation of a limp, heavy body, linens or a body bag was demonstrated.

sources.developer: Diligent Robotics (acquired by Serve Robotics, announced 2026-01)
sources.title: Serve Robotics to Acquire Diligent Robotics, Expanding Physical AI Platform Beyond the Sidewalk
sources.claim: The largest real-world hospital mobile-manipulation deployment, Moxi, performs autonomous point-to-point delivery of supplies, medications and lab specimens in hospital corridors; it does no bedside patient or decedent body care.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous mobile manipulation inside hospitals (the same E2 setting as post-mortem care). It establishes what deployed hospital robots actually do — fetch-and-deliver logistics — and does not substantiate any physical care of a decedent's body.

sources.system: Hydraulic cadaver lifts, concealed cadaver transport carts, Body Scoop rail transfer
sources.developer: Mopec / Spire Integrated Solutions / American Mortuary Coolers and similar vendors
sources.title: Morgue & Autopsy Equipment | Cadaver Lifters - Spire Integrated Solutions
sources.claim: Equipment used to move and lift deceased bodies in hospitals and mortuaries is human-operated mechanical/hydraulic apparatus (cadaver lifts, concealed transport carts, body scoops on rail systems), not autonomous robotic systems, and it covers only the transport step rather than post-mortem care.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: moving a deceased body. These are operator-driven lifting aids, not machines acting under machine control, so they cannot support a positive robotic judgment for any part of post-mortem care.

tasks.label: Ensure that equipment or devices are properly stored after use.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: After bedside use in an ICU room, small portable devices (glucometer, bladder scanner, vascular Doppler, tympanic thermometer, portable 12-lead EKG, transport monitor) are unplugged/undocked, wiped with hospital disinfectant per contact time, cords coiled, and returned to their labelled charging cradle or shelf in the unit alcove/clean utility room, with low-battery or broken items flagged.

Large mobile equipment no longer needed (extra IV/syringe pumps, feeding pump, portable ultrasound, warming unit, ventilator or CRRT machine, chair scale, patient lift) is disconnected from patient and power, wiped or bagged, tagged clean or soiled, wheeled out of a crowded ICU room past lines and visitors, and parked in the unit equipment storage room or soiled-hold/equipment-pool pickup area.

Leftover unopened supplies from a procedure or kit (dressings, tubing sets, syringes, spare cables and transducers, suction tubing) are gathered from the bedside table and room bins and put back in their correct bins/shelves in the unit supply room or returned to the automated dispensing cabinet, with charges/credits handled.

After a code or bedside procedure (intubation, central line, chest tube), the shared cart or kit (crash cart, difficult-airway box, procedure cart, defibrillator, bedside ultrasound) is restocked to the par list, closed and re-sealed with a numbered lock, logged as ready, and returned to its designated parking spot and power outlet on the unit.

End-of-shift or room-turnover sweep at an occupied bed space: verifying everything is stowed as policy requires — monitor cables hung, suction canister capped and stowed, pumps plugged in and poles positioned, defibrillator pads and transport bag replaced, drawers closed — and correcting whatever is out of place around the patient, family members and running lines.

sources.title: Introducing Vulcan: Amazon's first robot with a sense of touch
sources.claim: Amazon's Vulcan robot autonomously stows individual items into designated fabric storage pods (and picks from them) in working fulfillment centers in Spokane and Hamburg, handling ~75% of item types at speeds comparable to employees, and calls a human when it cannot handle an item.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: warehouse stowing. Storing a used device or supply means placing a varied, unfixtured object into its designated storage slot; Vulcan does exactly this for heterogeneous items at human speed, but only in a purpose-built cell where the storage pod is presented to it.

sources.title: Atlas Workflow Automation Vehicle for Washers | STERIS
sources.claim: STERIS's ATLAS Workflow Automation Vehicle is a commercial sterile-processing system that loads and unloads racks of used surgical instruments (up to 160 lb) into washer/disinfectors unattended, queues loads, and delivers them onward to prep-and-pack.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: post-use handling of contaminated medical equipment. It shows heavy used hospital equipment moved, cleaned and racked without staff, but only inside a purpose-built SPD automation path where loads are presented on standard racks at fixed stations.

sources.title: ORB: Operating Room Bot, Automating Operating Room Logistics through Mobile Manipulation
sources.claim: ORB, an autonomous mobile manipulator for operating-room logistics, achieved a 96% success rate at restocking (grabbing OR items from a cart and placing them onto storage shelves) and 80% at retrieval, evaluated in an environment simulating a hospital supply room with ....
sources.transferJustification: Related task: restocking hospital supplies. Putting hospital items back onto their storage shelves is the same act; the demonstration used a mocked-up supply room with a small fixed item set, so it evidences the structured case only.

sources.title: Towards Autonomous Instrument Tray Assembly for Sterile Processing Applications
sources.claim: A fully automated robotic cell (Staubli TX2-60L arm with dual electromagnetic gripper and vision) sorts surgical instruments and packs them into their designated positions in sterile trays using 3D-printed dividers and holders, with fewer tool-to-tool collisions than human-assembled trays.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: returning reusable medical devices to their proper stowed position after use. Instruments are comparable objects (small, metallic, varied shapes) and the acceptance criterion (right item in the right holder) matches; it works only in a fixtured cell with items presented to the arm.

sources.title: How Diligent's Robots Are Making a Difference in Texas Hospitals - IEEE Spectrum
sources.claim: Diligent Robotics' Moxi is the deployed state of the art for hospital mobile manipulation: it autonomously picks supplies out of supply closets ... delivers them to patient rooms, with over a million deliveries across 25+ US hospitals; its workflows are fetch-and-deliver, not collecting, cleaning and stowing used equipment at the bedside.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: hospital supply logistics. It establishes what autonomous manipulation is actually fielded in real hospital corridors and supply rooms (fetching and delivering), which bounds the E2 judgment for stowing used equipment.

sources.title: Automated Pharmacy Storage System - Swisslog BoxPicker
sources.claim: Swisslog Healthcare's BoxPicker is a commercial robotic storage-and-retrieval system installed in hospital pharmacies that fully automates medication storage and ...; its PillPick system likewise automates storing, dispensing and returning unit-dose medications.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: putting hospital items away in their correct storage location and returning unused stock. The machine performs put-away and return-to-stock reliably, but only for items handed to it at its purpose-built loading station.

sources.developer: KTH Royal Institute of Technology / University of Padova / Animum AB
sources.title: From Pixels to Shelf: An Integrated Robotic System for Autonomous Supermarket Stocking with a Mobile Manipulator
sources.claim: An integrated mobile-manipulator shelf-stocking system achieved over 98% success across more than 700 pick-and-place stocking events with autonomous docking and charging, in laboratory experiments replicating supermarket conditions; the authors state current autonomous performance remains inferior to human workers.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: shelf stocking. Placing supplies back onto their designated shelf positions is the same manipulation; validation was in a replica environment and explicitly below human productivity, so it supports only the structured case.

roles.description: Direct nursing staff in the provision of patient care in a clinical practice setting, such as a hospital, hospice, clinic, or home. Ensure adherence to established clinical policies, protocols, regulations, and standards.

tasks.label: Provide specialized direct and indirect care to inpatients and outpatients within a designated specialty, such as obstetrics, neurology, oncology, or neonatal care.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Inpatient bedside consult in the CNS's specialty (e.g., oncology, neuro, critical care): advanced assessment of a complex patient — auscultation, palpation, neuro checks, inspection of lines, drains, wounds and pumps — synthesizing with the chart, adjusting the plan of care with the team, and teaching the patient/family at the bedside on an occupied acute-care unit.

Hands-on specialty intervention at the bedside: complex wound/ostomy dressing change, tracheostomy or central-line dressing care, difficult IV/PICC access, drain management, or NICU care of a fragile infant (positioning, feeding, skin care) — performed on a live patient who moves, is in pain, and whose anatomy varies.

Outpatient specialty clinic visit (heart failure, diabetes, oncology survivorship, wound clinic): rooming and vitals, focused physical exam, medication titration, injections or infusion oversight, device/self-care teaching, and documentation, in a clinic exam room.

Indirect care on the unit: rounding with staff nurses, demonstrating and validating a technique at the bedside (e.g., correct dressing or device use), troubleshooting equipment on a patient, auditing protocol adherence, and coaching staff during an actual patient encounter.

Home, hospice, or community specialty visit: assessment and hands-on care of a patient in a private residence or long-term-care room with variable layout, pets, clutter, and family present; equipment and supplies as found.

sources.developer: Foxconn (Hon Hai) with Kawasaki Heavy Industries and NVIDIA
sources.title: Could AI nursing robots help healthcare staffing shortages? | CNN Business
sources.claim: Nurabot, the most advanced fielded hospital 'nursing' humanoid, works autonomously on wards but its scope is medication/specimen delivery and patient wayfinding — not clinical assessment or hands-on specialty care.
sources.transferJustification: Closest fielded 'nursing robot' to the CNS task and it operates in the same E2 hospital ward; its demonstrated scope is logistics and wayfinding, so it substantiates no part of specialized direct patient care.

sources.title: Diligent Robotics hits 1M picks with Moxi robot in healthcare settings - The Robot Report
sources.claim: Moxi, the largest deployed fleet of hospital mobile manipulators in the US, performs autonomous fetch-and-deliver logistics in hospital corridors; it does not perform patient-contact clinical tasks.
sources.transferJustification: Related task (hospital material transport) in the same E2 setting; it establishes what autonomous hospital robots can reliably do today and shows the gap to advanced-practice patient assessment and intervention.

sources.title: Performance, Safety, and Patient Experience of an Autonomous Robotic Phlebotomy Device: A Multicenter Trial | Clinical Chemistry
sources.claim: The frontier of autonomous physical patient contact is a single narrow procedure: robotic venipuncture, evaluated in outpatient phlebotomy departments with the patient's arm fixtured in the device; it is investigational and covers only blood collection, not a nursing visit.
sources.transferJustification: Venipuncture is one hands-on sub-step of nursing care with comparable patient contact; even here autonomy requires a dedicated fixturing device and covers only the needle stick, so it cannot carry a whole CNS assessment-plus-intervention encounter.

sources.system: FARUS fully autonomous robotic ultrasound system
sources.developer: Su et al. (academic, published in Nature Communications)
sources.title: A fully autonomous robotic ultrasound system for thyroid scanning | Nature Communications
sources.claim: Autonomous robotic ultrasound of a body region has been shown on volunteers in a laboratory/research setting, indicating that even a single specialty diagnostic scan is at research maturity.
sources.transferJustification: Related task (a specialty bedside diagnostic procedure on a live patient); it shows autonomous patient-contact procedures exist only as single-organ research demos, not as a substitute for a specialist nurse's examination.

sources.title: AutoPeel: Adhesion-aware Safe Peeling Trajectory Optimization for Robotic Wound Care
sources.claim: Robotic wound dressing removal — a core CNS hands-on intervention — exists only as laboratory work on foam phantoms with a research manipulator.
sources.transferJustification: Directly related to the wound/ostomy care sub-step of specialty nursing; performance is limited to removing a dressing from a phantom in a lab, far short of a complete dressing change on a patient.

tasks.label: Observe, interview, and assess patients to identify care needs.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Inpatient bedside assessment on a hospital medical-surgical or ICU unit: the CNS reviews the chart and monitor data, greets and interviews the patient about symptoms, observes appearance, breathing, mentation and behavior, performs a focused hands-on exam (auscultating lungs/heart/bowel, palpating abdomen and extremities, checking skin, IV sites, lines and drains, edema, capillary refill), and synthesizes findings into identified care needs and a plan communicated to staff.

Specialty consult assessment at the bedside (wound/ostomy, pain, diabetes, stroke, palliative): CNS uncovers and inspects a wound or stoma, measures and probes the wound bed, palpates periwound tissue, assesses drainage, odor and pain response, interviews the patient about self-care and symptoms, and documents specific care needs and product/protocol recommendations.

Outpatient or specialty clinic assessment in an exam room: patient arrives for a scheduled visit; CNS interviews about interval history and medications, takes or verifies vitals, performs a focused physical exam (auscultation, palpation, inspection of feet/skin/injection sites), assesses self-management and education needs, and identifies care needs.

Assessment of a patient who cannot reliably self-report — sedated/ventilated, delirious, dementia, aphasic, or nonverbal pediatric — in a hospital or long-term care unit: care needs must be inferred from behavioral observation (grimacing, restlessness, guarding), physiological signs, hands-on exam, and interview of family and bedside staff.

Home or hospice visit assessment: CNS enters a private residence of unknown layout, observes the living environment and caregiver situation, interviews patient and family, and examines the patient in a bed, recliner or wheelchair (lung sounds, edema, skin/wound checks, functional status) to identify care needs.

Assessment during unit rounds: CNS walks the unit, briefly observes multiple patients and their monitors/equipment, speaks with patients and bedside nurses, and spots emerging needs (deterioration, fall or pressure-injury risk, restraint or delirium concerns) requiring intervention.

sources.system: Teleoperated Unitree G1 humanoid surrogate (UCSD 'Humanoids in Hospitals')
sources.developer: UC San Diego (Atar, Liang, Joyce, Richter, Yip et al.) with UCSD Health clinicians
sources.title: Humanoids in Hospitals: A Technical Study of Humanoid Robot Surrogates for Dexterous Medical Interventions
sources.claim: A Unitree G1 humanoid was made to perform physical-examination actions such as auscultation and abdominal palpation, but only under full teleoperation and in a simulated (mannequin/lab) hospital setting.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robot-performed physical examination manoeuvres (auscultation, palpation) that are the hands-on core of a nursing assessment; it shows the frontier is human-in-the-loop teleoperation on simulators, not autonomous patient assessment.

sources.system: Dr. Spot (Boston Dynamics Spot with contactless vital-sign payload)
sources.developer: MIT / Brigham and Women's Hospital / Boston Dynamics
sources.title: Brigham and Women's Hospital, MIT use Spot to measure patient vitals
sources.claim: Spot carrying contactless vital-sign sensors and a tablet was used at a hospital COVID triage tent to measure vitals and let clinicians question patients remotely; the robot was driven by a human with a handheld controller.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: remote vital-sign measurement and patient questioning, the observation/interview components of assessment; the robot is a teleoperated conduit for a clinician rather than an autonomous assessor.

sources.title: Diligent Robotics Unveils Moxi 2.0, Advancing The Largest Fleet of Deployed AI-Powered Mobile Manipulation Robots
sources.claim: The largest deployed fleet of autonomous mobile manipulators in US hospitals performs only logistics work — delivering medications and lab samples — and no patient assessment.
sources.transferJustification: Defines the state of autonomous robot work inside E2 hospital wards: navigation and item transport only, establishing that no deployed hospital robot conducts patient observation, interview or examination.

sources.system: Fully autonomous robotic ultrasound system for thyroid scanning
sources.title: A fully autonomous robotic ultrasound system for thyroid scanning
sources.claim: A fully autonomous robotic ultrasound ... scanned the thyroid of seated human participants with quality close to clinician scans, in a laboratory/clinical research setup with the subject positioned for the machine.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous, force-controlled contact examination of a human body region — the closest autonomous analogue of a hands-on assessment step — but limited to one instrumented modality on a positioned volunteer, with no interview, observation or care-need synthesis.

sources.developer: Townsville Hospital and Health Service / James Cook University / QUT
sources.title: Health Promotion, Health Literacy and Vaccine Hesitancy: The Role of Humanoid Robots
sources.claim: A humanoid social robot trialled in a hospital delivered health promotion and information from a fixed spot in the entrance corridor; its role was public-facing education, not patient assessment.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robot-conducted health conversations/surveys with patients, the interview component; it shows only scripted public health-literacy interaction in a corridor, far short of a clinical assessment interview yielding identified care needs.

tasks.label: Provide direct care by performing comprehensive health assessments, developing differential diagnoses, conducting specialized tests, or prescribing medications or treatments.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Inpatient bedside comprehensive health assessment on a hospital unit (med-surg, ICU, oncology, peds): interview an ill, sometimes confused or lined/tubed patient, take a history, perform a head-to-toe exam (auscultate heart/lungs/bowel sounds, palpate abdomen, assess skin, edema, neuro status, pain), synthesize with labs and monitor data into a differential, and enter orders or recommendations in the EHR.

Outpatient specialty clinic visit (diabetes, heart failure, wound/ostomy, oncology, psych-mental health): 20-40 minute encounter with an ambulatory patient — interview, focused physical exam, order and interpret labs/diagnostics, then prescribe or titrate medications and write the treatment plan under the state's prescriptive authority.

Performing a specialized hands-on test or treatment at the bedside or in clinic: sharp/conservative wound debridement and dressing change on a pressure or diabetic ulcer, ostomy/stoma assessment and pouching, EKG lead placement, spirometry coaching, urinary catheter or ultrasound-guided PIV placement, tracheostomy care — on patients of varying body habitus, mobility and cooperation.

Routine diagnostic venous blood specimen collection performed as part of direct care at a hospital draw station or bedside on a cooperative adult with usable antecubital veins, filling labeled tubes in draw order for the ordered panel.

Home or hospice visit: assess a patient in their own residence (cluttered rooms, poor lighting, patient in a recliner or bed, pets and family present), perform a symptom-focused physical assessment, review a pill box, adjust the medication regimen and teach the caregiver.

Rapid-response or acute-deterioration consult: urgent bedside evaluation of an unstable patient (sepsis, respiratory distress, arrhythmia, post-op bleed), rapid focused exam and vital-sign synthesis, formulation of a working differential, and immediate initiation of treatment (oxygen, fluids, drugs) within minutes.

sources.title: Performance, Safety, and Patient Experience of an Autonomous Robotic Phlebotomy Device: A Multicenter Trial | Clinical Chemistry
sources.claim: Vitestro's Aletta Autonomous Robotic Phlebotomy Device autonomously performs diagnostic venipuncture on patients in hospital outpatient phlebotomy departments, with one human professional supervising up to three devices; evaluated in a 1,633-patient multicenter trial at Dutch hospitals.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: diagnostic blood specimen collection. This is one of the 'specialized tests' a clinical nurse specialist conducts in direct care; same patient contact, same needle-in-vein precision, same hospital setting.

sources.title: Aletta® - Vitestro
sources.claim: The Aletta device performs the complete blood-draw workflow end to end, from tourniquet placement through bandaging, and is marketed for busy blood-draw centers.
sources.transferJustification: Establishes whole-task (not sub-step) completion of the venipuncture instance, including preparation and closure steps a nurse would perform.

sources.title: Vitestro gains CE mark for autonomous blood drawing robot - Medical Device Network
sources.claim: Aletta received a CE mark in 2024, the first for an autonomous blood-drawing device, with limited market release at selected hospitals; trial reported 95% first-stick success comparable to ....
sources.transferJustification: Confirms regulatory clearance and real hospital deployment rather than a laboratory demonstration, supporting the worker-quality standard for the venipuncture instance.

sources.developer: University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign (Zhu, Smith, Hauser)
sources.title: Automated Heart and Lung Auscultation in Robotic Physical Examinations — University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign
sources.claim: Autonomous robotic auscultation of heart ... has been demonstrated only in a laboratory study on four human subjects; it captures sounds but does not perform a full physical assessment, differential diagnosis, or treatment decision.
sources.transferJustification: Directly relevant sub-step of the comprehensive physical assessment instances; cited to show that only an isolated component, in a lab, has been automated.
