roles.title: Nurse Anesthetists
aliases: Staff Certified Registered Nurse Anesthetist (Staff CRNA)
roles.description: Administer anesthesia, monitor patient's vital signs, and oversee patient recovery from anesthesia. May assist anesthesiologists, surgeons, other physicians, or dentists. Must be registered nurses who have specialized graduate education.

tasks.label: Manage patients' airway or pulmonary status, using techniques such as endotracheal intubation, mechanical ventilation, pharmacological support, respiratory therapy, and extubation.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Routine general anesthesia for an elective adult case (ASA I–II) in a hospital OR or ambulatory surgery center: preoxygenate by mask, induce, mask-ventilate, perform direct or video laryngoscopy and endotracheal intubation, confirm placement by capnography/auscultation, secure tube, set and titrate mechanical ventilation for the case, suction, reverse neuromuscular blockade, and extubate at emergence with airway rescue if needed.

Short elective case managed with a supraglottic airway (LMA): insert and seat the LMA, verify seal and ventilation, maintain spontaneous or pressure-support ventilation with pharmacologic support, adjust head/jaw position for obstruction, then remove the device at emergence and support the airway in transport to PACU.

Monitored anesthesia care / sedation or regional case without an artificial airway: apply supplemental oxygen, monitor capnography and saturation, perform chin lift, jaw thrust or nasal/oral airway insertion for obstruction or apnea, titrate sedatives, and rescue with mask ventilation or conversion to a definitive airway if respiration deteriorates.

High-risk or difficult airway case: morbidly obese or OSA patient, rapid sequence induction with cricoid pressure for a full stomach, awake flexible-scope intubation, trauma or unanticipated difficult laryngoscopy requiring bougie/videolaryngoscope/supraglottic rescue, or double-lumen tube placement with one-lung ventilation for thoracic surgery, in a hospital OR.

Pediatric, obstetric, or out-of-OR anesthetizing location (endoscopy suite, cath lab, radiology, labor and delivery): size-appropriate airway equipment, limited space and remote monitoring, rapid desaturation risk, emergency conversion of neuraxial block to general anesthesia with intubation, and extubation in a non-OR setting.

Perioperative ventilated-patient and PACU/ICU airway work: receive or transport an already-intubated patient with hand or transport ventilation, verify tube position and connect/set the ventilator, suction secretions, deliver bronchodilator or other respiratory therapy through the circuit, wean and extubate, or respond to a post-extubation airway emergency with reintubation.

sources.title: First robotic tracheal intubations in humans using the Kepler intubation system - ScienceDirect
sources.claim: The only robotic intubations reported in living patients (Kepler Intubation System, McGill) were performed by an operator driving a robot-mounted videolaryngoscope from a joystick workstation, i.e. teleoperation, with a 91% success rate in a small feasibility series.
sources.transferJustification: Same task (endotracheal intubation of an anesthetized patient); establishes that in-human robotic intubation is teleoperated and only at feasibility stage.

sources.title: The Kepler Intubation System (Anesthesia & Analgesia)
sources.claim: The Kepler system's architecture is explicitly a remote joystick console driving a robotic arm holding a videolaryngoscope, confirming human-in-the-loop control rather than autonomous airway management.
sources.transferJustification: Same task; documents the control mode (teleoperation) of the leading robotic intubation platform.

sources.developer: University research group (Int J Comput Assist Radiol Surg)
sources.title: A robot-assisted tracheal intubation system based on a soft actuator
sources.claim: Fully autonomous robotic tracheal intubation has been demonstrated only on training manikins (synthetic, fixtured airways), not on living patients, and only for tube insertion rather than whole-case airway management.

sources.developer: ETH Zurich / University Hospital Zurich (Biro et al.)
sources.title: Scope of artificial intelligence in airway management (Indian Journal of Anaesthesia)
sources.claim: An earlier automated robotic endoscope (REALITI, ETH Zurich/UZH) also achieved automated tracheal intubation only in an airway manikin as a proof of concept.

sources.title: Spiro Robotics Wins FDA Clearance for Spiro-VISTA
sources.claim: The only FDA-cleared 'robotic' intubation product is a handheld device that a clinician holds and steers as an aid to tube placement; it does not perform airway management on its own.

sources.system: Soft Robot Intubation System (SRIS), everting vine robot
sources.title: A soft robotic device for rapid and self-guided intubation | Science Translational Medicine
sources.claim: A self-guiding soft robotic intubation device has succeeded only in manikins and cadavers and is inserted and operated by a human user, so it does not replace the clinician performing the intubation.

sources.title: Closed–Loop ventilation using sidestream versus mainstream capnography for automated adjustments of minute ventilation—A randomized clinical trial in cardiac surgery patients
sources.claim: Closed-loop ventilators (INTELLiVENT-ASV) do autonomously titrate ventilation in real patients in ICUs and after cardiac surgery, but they only adjust settings on an airway a clinician has already established and cannot intubate, suction, or extubate.
sources.transferJustification: Related sub-task (mechanical ventilation titration) within this task; cited to show automation exists for one component only, not for airway instrumentation or extubation.

tasks.label: Respond to emergency situations by providing airway management, administering emergency fluids or drugs, or using basic or advanced cardiac life support techniques.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Intraoperative airway emergency during general anesthesia in a hospital OR: laryngospasm, difficult mask ventilation, bronchospasm or aspiration with rapid desaturation. CRNA repositions the head, applies jaw thrust and two-hand mask ventilation, deepens anesthesia or pushes succinylcholine, suctions, and intubates or places a rescue supraglottic device while the surgical team continues working.

Intraoperative hemodynamic or allergic crisis: sudden severe hypotension from hemorrhage, high spinal, or anaphylaxis, or an acute arrhythmia. CRNA diagnoses the cause, pushes vasopressors/epinephrine, opens fluids and pressure-infuses blood products through IV access, adjusts anesthetic depth, calls for help and documents.

Full cardiac arrest / ACLS code in the OR, PACU, or on a hospital ward or procedure area: chest compressions, rhythm interpretation and defibrillation, timed epinephrine and antiarrhythmics, airway control with bag-mask then endotracheal tube, and treatment of reversible causes with a code team.

Post-anesthesia emergency in PACU or during transport: opioid-induced respiratory depression, airway obstruction, negative-pressure pulmonary edema, or residual paralysis in a semi-awake, moving patient. CRNA applies chin lift/oral airway and bag-mask ventilation, gives reversal agents (naloxone, sugammadex), and may reintubate.

Emergency at a remote anesthetizing location or in obstetrics: endoscopy suite, cath lab, MRI, labor and delivery, ambulatory surgery center or office/dental setting, with limited equipment and delayed help. Includes local anesthetic systemic toxicity, high spinal with apnea, maternal hemorrhage, or neonatal resuscitation.

sources.developer: UC Santa Barbara (Haggerty et al., Science Translational Medicine)
sources.title: UCSB-designed soft robot intubation device could save lives | The Current
sources.claim: A soft robotic intubation system (SRIS) that everts into the airway was tested in mannequins and cadavers, achieving high success rates, but it is inserted and operated by a human user and has not been used autonomously in live emergency patients.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: emergency endotracheal intubation, the core of airway management in this task. It does not transfer because the device is human-guided and was evaluated on cadavers/mannequins, not on live patients in crisis.

sources.title: First robotic tracheal intubations in humans using the Kepler intubation system - British Journal of Anaesthesia
sources.claim: The Kepler Intubation System performed the first robotic tracheal intubations in humans, but it is a remote joystick-controlled (teleoperated) system used in 12 elective OR patients in a pilot study.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: tracheal intubation in the OR. Teleoperated control means it cannot support a positive judgment, and it addresses only one step of emergency response.

sources.title: Automated closed-loop versus manually controlled norepinephrine infusion in patients undergoing intermediate- to high-risk abdominal surgery: a randomised controlled trial
sources.claim: A closed-loop vasopressor (CLV) controller autonomously titrated a norepinephrine infusion to correct hypotension in patients undergoing abdominal surgery in the operating room, reducing hypotensive episodes versus manual control.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: administering emergency vasopressor drugs intraoperatively. Transfer is partial only: the system titrates one drug via pre-placed arterial line and pump under clinician supervision, and performs no diagnosis, bolus drug push, fluid handling, or airway care.

sources.title: LUCAS 3, v3.1 chest compression system | Stryker
sources.claim: The LUCAS 3 mechanical chest compression system delivers automated, guideline-consistent compressions in hospitals and prehospital care, but a clinician must position the patient, apply the device and run the rest of the resuscitation.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: chest compressions within ACLS. It covers only that sub-step; device application, rhythm analysis, defibrillation, drugs and airway remain human work.

sources.system: Humanoid robots in the operating room (staged framework)
sources.developer: Authors of perioperative humanoid-robot perspective (reported by News-Medical)
sources.title: Humanoid robots could take on low-risk operating room tasks before assisting surgical teams
sources.claim: A 2026 perspective on humanoid robots in operating rooms proposes starting with logistics and low-risk perioperative tasks, stating that autonomous clinical use is premature and requires validation and human oversight.
sources.transferJustification: Directly characterizes the state of general-purpose robots in the OR, the setting of most instances, confirming no fielded system performs hands-on clinical crisis care.

tasks.label: Monitor patients' responses, including skin color, pupil dilation, pulse, heart rate, blood pressure, respiration, ventilation, or urine output, using invasive and noninvasive techniques.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Routine elective general anesthesia, adult ASA I–III, hospital OR or ambulatory surgery center: continuous vigilance over ECG, NIBP, SpO2, capnography and ventilator parameters, temperature; periodic hands-on checks of skin color, pupils and chest rise; re-siting probes, re-zeroing transducers and resolving artifacts; reacting to surgical events.

Routine minimal-to-moderate sedation/MAC for a healthy adult (ASA I–II) during screening colonoscopy/EGD or a minor procedure in an endoscopy suite: noninvasive monitoring of pulse, heart rate, blood pressure, oximetry, capnography/respiration and patient responsiveness.

Sedation/MAC or regional anesthesia in higher-risk or out-of-OR settings (cath lab, IR, MRI, ophthalmology, dental/office-based surgery, elderly or comorbid patients): deep sedation with unsecured airway, restricted physical access to the patient, block-level and responsiveness checks.

High-acuity invasive case (cardiac, major vascular, trauma, transplant): arterial line and CVP/PA waveform interpretation, TEE/cerebral oximetry, serial arterial blood gas draws, hourly urine output, rapid hemodynamic swings requiring immediate recognition and response.

Obstetric and pediatric anesthesia: awake laboring mother after epidural (frequent BP cycles, block level by cold/pinprick, watching for high block or hypotension), or a crying, moving child at mask induction where probes and cuff must be kept on and color and respiration watched directly.

Emergence, PACU recovery and intra-hospital transport: assessing return of protective reflexes, airway patency, skin color, pupils, responsiveness, residual neuromuscular blockade and urine output with portable or hand-cycled monitoring, then handoff.

sources.system: SEDASYS Computer-Assisted Personalized Sedation System (Ethicon Endo-Surgery / J&J)
sources.title: The debate for nonanesthesiologist-administered propofol sedation in endoscopy rages on: who will be the "King of Prop?"
sources.claim: SEDASYS, a computer-assisted personalized sedation system, integrated continuous noninvasive monitoring of oximetry, capnography, ECG and noninvasive blood pressure with ... automated responsiveness monitor that probed the patient with auditory and tactile stimuli.

sources.title: SEDASYS Propofol Sedation System Gets FDA Nod
sources.claim: The FDA-approved SEDASYS system automatically detected physiologic deterioration (desaturation, low respiratory rate/apnea) and responded without human input by reducing or stopping propofol, increasing oxygen and prompting the patient to breathe.

sources.title: FDA Grants Premarket Approval (PMA) For The SEDASYS System For Healthy Patients Undergoing Sedation During Routine Colonoscopy And EGD Procedures
sources.claim: SEDASYS received FDA premarket approval for minimal-to-moderate sedation of healthy patients in routine colonoscopy/EGD, and was sold only to facilities where an anesthesia ... remained available, i.e. the machine's monitoring was accepted only for a narrow low-risk population.

sources.title: The Sinking of Sedasys — Outpatient Surgery Magazine
sources.claim: SEDASYS was commercially launched in US endoscopy suites in 2014 and then withdrawn in 2016 after limited adoption; it remains the only machine deployed in place of a clinician for monitoring routine sedation.

sources.system: Closed-loop anesthetic delivery (CLAD) system, physiology-based control in nonhuman primates
sources.developer: MIT / Massachusetts General Hospital research group
sources.title: Closed-loop control of anesthetic state in nonhuman primates
sources.claim: Closed-loop anesthesia delivery systems that continuously monitor physiology and titrate drugs have not been approved for human testing in the ..., and ASA standards require a qualified anesthesia provider present and continually monitoring throughout surgery.
sources.transferJustification: Closed-loop anesthetic control is the nearest automated analogue of intraoperative monitoring: it requires continuous machine monitoring of the patient's state. Its restriction to animals in the US bounds what machine monitoring can do for general anesthesia.

sources.title: Evaluation of Automated Delivery of Propofol Using a Closed-Loop Anesthesia Delivery System in Patients Undergoing Thoracic Surgery: A Randomized Controlled Study
sources.claim: Closed-loop anesthesia delivery systems (CLADS) have been run autonomously in human operating rooms in randomized trials, but they monitor and control only depth of hypnosis via BIS with propofol infusion, under an anesthesiologist who performs all other monitoring.
sources.transferJustification: Automated drug titration depends on continuous automated monitoring of the anesthetized patient, so it is the closest demonstrated machine substitute for intraoperative vigilance; its single-signal scope shows the gap to the full monitoring task.

sources.title: Accuryn Achieves Product Commercialization and Compliance Success
sources.claim: Automated urine-output monitoring exists as an FDA-cleared, hospital-deployed device measuring urine output, intra-abdominal pressure and core temperature continuously in critical care and cardiac surgery patients.
sources.transferJustification: Automates one listed modality (urine output) of the monitoring task in the same hospital settings, but is a fixed catheter-based instrument that a clinician must place and interpret alongside the other parameters.

sources.system: Dr. Spot (Boston Dynamics Spot with contactless vital-sign sensors)
sources.developer: MIT / Brigham and Women's Hospital / Boston Dynamics
sources.title: Boston Dynamics Robo-Dog Could Soon Monitor Patient Vitals
sources.claim: The best-known mobile robot demonstration of patient vital-sign monitoring (MIT/Brigham and Women's 'Dr. Spot') was operator-controlled triage-grade contactless measurement in ED tents, not autonomous clinical monitoring.
sources.transferJustification: Directly a patient vital-sign monitoring robot, but teleoperated and limited to triage-level contactless measurements, so it cannot support a positive judgment for anesthesia monitoring.

sources.developer: Foxconn with NVIDIA and Kawasaki, at Taichung Veterans General Hospital
sources.title: Foxconn Taps NVIDIA to Accelerate Physical and Digital Robotics for Global Healthcare Industry
sources.claim: Hospital robots actually deployed on wards in 2025 (Nurabot) perform logistics and patrol duties supporting nurses, not physiologic patient monitoring.
sources.transferJustification: Shows the state of autonomous robots deployed inside structured hospital facilities: delivery and patrol work, not hands-on physiologic monitoring of anesthetized patients.

tasks.label: Select, order, or administer anesthetics, adjuvant drugs, accessory drugs, fluids or blood products as necessary.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Routine elective general anesthesia for a healthy/stable adult in a hospital OR or ambulatory surgery center (hernia, arthroscopy, lap chole): select and push IV induction agents (propofol + opioid +/- neuromuscular blocker), titrate maintenance (TIVA infusions or volatile agent) to depth of anesthesia, give standard adjuncts (antibiotic, antiemetic, occasional pressor bolus), run maintenance crystalloid, and dose reversal at emergence.

Monitored anesthesia care / procedural sedation for a low-risk adult in a GI endoscopy suite, ophthalmic ASC, or minor-procedure room: select and titrate propofol (with or without a small opioid/benzodiazepine dose) through a peripheral IV to patient response, reducing or stopping drug for oversedation or hypotension.

Neuraxial or regional anesthesia: labor epidural on a labor-and-delivery unit, spinal for cesarean or joint replacement, or ultrasound-guided peripheral nerve block; select local anesthetic and adjuvants, position and prep the patient, place needle/catheter and inject, set the epidural infusion, then treat resulting hypotension with pressors and fluid.

High-acuity or complex case (ASA III-IV, major abdominal/vascular/cardiac, trauma, obstetric hemorrhage) in a hospital OR: vasoactive and inotrope infusions, goal-directed fluid boluses, checking and transfusing packed cells/plasma/platelets on a rapid infuser, coagulation agents and emergency drugs, with the drug plan changing minute to minute in response to surgical events.

Peri-anesthetic adjunct and accessory drug administration away from the anesthetic itself: premedication/anxiolytic in the preop holding bay, prophylactic antibiotic timing, rescue analgesic or antiemetic in PACU, drugs given during transport - locate the patient, verify identity, draw up and give the drug.

Anesthesia at an off-site or office-based location (dental or plastic-surgery office, imaging suite, cath lab, remote hospital location) with nonstandard rooms, limited equipment and often a shared airway; select and titrate sedative/anesthetic and adjuvant drugs improvised to the setting.

sources.developer: University of Fukui / Nagata, Shigemi et al.
sources.title: Safety and efficacy of an automated anesthesia delivery system for total intravenous anesthesia with propofol, remifentanil, and rocuronium: a non-inferiority randomized controlled trial versus manually controlled anesthesia
sources.claim: A closed-loop automated anesthesia control system administered propofol, remifentanil and rocuronium for total intravenous anesthesia in surgical patients, with anesthetic adequacy non-inferior to anesthesiologist-controlled manual administration.

sources.system: McSleepy closed-loop TIVA drug delivery system
sources.title: Evaluation of a novel closed-loop total intravenous anaesthesia drug delivery system: a randomized controlled trial
sources.claim: In a 186-patient randomized controlled trial in an operating room, a closed-loop anesthesia drug delivery system automatically administered the hypnotic, opioid and muscle relaxant, versus manual administration by clinicians.

sources.title: A technical description of a novel pharmacological anesthesia robot
sources.claim: The peer-reviewed technical description of McSleepy calls it a pharmacological anesthesia robot and states it controls all three drug components across the whole anesthetic, from induction through emergence.

sources.system: ACTIVA (Automatic Control of Total Intravenous Anesthesia)
sources.developer: University of Brescia / Italian collaborating hospitals
sources.title: Clinical Performance of a Bispectral Index Controlled Closed-Loop Administration System for Simultaneous Administration of Propofol and Remifentanil
sources.claim: A BIS-controlled closed-loop system autonomously co-administered propofol and remifentanil in surgical patients from induction until the end of surgery, maintaining adequate anesthesia 75-94% of the time.

sources.title: Closed-loop systems for automated hypnotic drug delivery during general anaesthesia: a systematic review and meta-analysis
sources.claim: Pooled randomized-trial evidence across 17 trials and 1898 patients shows closed-loop hypnotic delivery controls anesthetic depth at least as safely as manual clinician titration.

sources.title: Sedasys Computer-Assisted System for GI Propofol Sedation Approved by FDA
sources.claim: The SEDASYS computer-assisted personalized sedation system received FDA premarket approval to intravenously administer propofol for minimal-to-moderate sedation during ... without an anesthesia professional delivering the drug.

sources.title: Johnson & Johnson To Stop Selling Sedasys System
sources.claim: SEDASYS was sold and used clinically in US endoscopy suites for healthy adults undergoing routine colonoscopy/EGD; it metered propofol into the patient's vein and automatically slowed or stopped the infusion on signs of oversedation, before J&J exited the product in 2016.

sources.title: GE Healthcare Receives FDA Approval of End-tidal Control Software for General Anesthesia Delivery
sources.claim: FDA premarket approval of End-tidal Control makes automated closed-loop delivery of inhaled anesthetic agent and oxygen to clinician-set targets commercially available on US anesthesia machines.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: maintenance-phase administration of the volatile anesthetic, the most common US general-anesthesia maintenance technique. Same patient, same drug-delivery act as closed-loop IV titration, in the same operating room, with the machine holding the target autonomously.

sources.developer: Erasme Hospital Brussels / UC Irvine (Joosten, Rinehart, Cannesson)
sources.title: Automated closed-loop versus manually controlled norepinephrine infusion in patients undergoing intermediate- to high-risk abdominal surgery: a randomised controlled trial
sources.claim: A closed-loop controller automatically titrated a norepinephrine infusion to correct intraoperative hypotension in a randomized trial of abdominal surgery patients, showing one accessory-drug channel is automatable but only that single variable.

sources.title: Technical communication: First robotic ultrasound-guided nerve blocks in humans using the Magellan system
sources.claim: The only robotic system shown performing nerve-block needle placement and local anesthetic injection in humans is joystick-driven by the clinician, i.e. teleoperated rather than autonomous.

sources.title: Vitestro launches new website and first public video of Aletta Autonomous Robotic Phlebotomy Device
sources.claim: A CE-marked autonomous robot performs needle insertion into a patient's vein in routine clinical practice, but only to collect diagnostic blood samples - it does not select, prepare or administer drugs.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous venous needle placement in a human clinical facility. It substantiates autonomous needle-in-vein work at E2, but performs blood collection only, so it does not carry over to selecting and administering anesthetic or adjuvant drugs.

sources.title: New Automated Robot System in Renown Health
sources.claim: Robotic IV automation systems select vials and autonomously prepare labeled syringes and IV bags to clinical standards inside an enclosed purpose-built cabinet in hospital pharmacies.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: drug selection and preparation (drawing up syringes/admixtures), the preparatory half of this task. Same drugs and precision, performed autonomously inside a purpose-built enclosure, supporting the E1 premise that drugs can be presented preloaded to a closed-loop delivery system.

tasks.label: Select, prepare, or use equipment, monitors, supplies, or drugs for the administration of anesthetics.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Routine hospital OR / ASC case: at the anesthesia cart, pull vials and ampoules from the automated dispensing cabinet and draw up, dilute and label the standard drug set (propofol, lidocaine, fentanyl/midazolam, rocuronium or succinylcholine, phenylephrine/ephedrine, ondansetron, antibiotic), checking concentrations and expiry.

Pre-case anesthesia workstation setup and machine check in the OR: connect gas supply and breathing circuit/bag, run leak and self-test, check CO2 absorbent and vaporizer levels, verify suction and backup oxygen, and lay out airway supplies (videolaryngoscope, ETTs/LMAs in several sizes, stylet, oral airway, tape), monitor cables and warming device.

Start of case in the OR: apply ECG leads, NIBP cuff, pulse oximeter, temperature probe and depth-of-anesthesia sensor to the specific patient, place or check the peripheral IV, spike and connect fluids, and load/program infusion pumps and lines before induction.

Stable maintenance phase of a routine total-intravenous general anesthetic: continuously titrate the hypnotic infusion against depth-of-anesthesia (BIS) monitoring to hold the patient in the target range for the duration of the case.

Dynamic intraoperative use of the full equipment and drug set: adjust vaporizer and ventilator settings, bolus vasopressors for hypotension, redose opioid/relaxant, manage fluids and blood products, swap or troubleshoot failing equipment, and respond to alarms and surgical events.

Specialized/regional setup: prepare and use an epidural or spinal tray in labor and delivery, an ultrasound machine and nerve-block tray, an arterial or central line kit, transducers, or cell saver for a specific patient and procedure.

Off-site, office-based or urgent work: set up a portable anesthesia machine, monitors and drugs for a dental or plastic-surgery office, GI endoscopy suite or MRI, or rapidly assemble equipment and drugs for an emergent case including difficult-airway and malignant-hyperthermia carts.

sources.title: New Automated Robot System in Renown Health
sources.claim: ARxIUM's RIVA robotic IV automation system autonomously compounds patient doses into labeled syringes and IV bags inside an enclosed ISO Class 5 cell in a hospital pharmacy after technicians load vials, syringes and bags; deployed at Renown Health.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: sterile drug preparation. The nurse anesthetist's drawing-up of syringes handles the same objects (vials, ampoules, syringes, labels) at the same dose precision; RIVA does this with gravimetric and barcode verification, but only inside a loaded, enclosed machine cell.

sources.title: ARxIUM Celebrates Major RIVA Milestone | The National Law Review
sources.claim: RIVA's installed base has compounded more than 19 million doses in USP <797> compliant hospital pharmacy environments, indicating sustained production-grade reliability.
sources.transferJustification: Same related task (sterile syringe preparation); establishes the error/reliability record at scale for machine-prepared syringes of the kind used in the OR.

sources.title: Ballad Health expands patient safety with new robotic pharmacy technology
sources.claim: Three Omnicell IVX Station compounding ... installed in Ballad Health's central fill pharmacy pre-fill syringes, explicitly to supply medications for urgent situations such as the ....
sources.transferJustification: Related task: preparation of ready-to-administer syringes destined for anesthesia/OR use; identical output object (labeled filled syringe) to what the CRNA prepares, produced inside a purpose-built compounding enclosure.

sources.system: BIS-guided closed-loop hypnotic delivery systems (pooled across 17 randomised trials)
sources.developer: multiple academic groups (systematic review published in British Journal of Anaesthesia)
sources.title: Closed-loop systems for automated hypnotic drug delivery during general anaesthesia: a systematic review and meta-analysis
sources.claim: Closed-loop hypnotic delivery systems automatically adjust propofol infusion rates from continuous BIS feedback during general anesthesia; a 2026 systematic review pooled 17 randomised trials with 1898 surgical patients comparing them with clinician-directed manual control.

sources.developer: G.D. Puri / PGIMER, evaluated at Sir Ganga Ram Hospital
sources.title: Performance Analysis of Hermetic Closed-loop Anesthesia Delivery System (NCT05967403)
sources.claim: The CLADS closed-loop anesthesia delivery system is a computer-controlled device that delivers propofol TIVA to patients through an automated infusion pump using BIS feedback and a PID controller, updating delivery every 30 seconds during maintenance, under clinical study in a hospital operating room.

sources.title: Vitestro Unveils Aletta: The World's First Autonomous Robotic Phlebotomy Device (ARPD)
sources.claim: Vitestro's Aletta performs autonomous ultrasound/AI-guided venipuncture for diagnostic blood collection and is CE-marked with initial commercial launch in Europe; it collects blood but does not place IV catheters, connect infusion pumps or apply patient monitors.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: needle insertion into a peripheral vein with the arm placed in a device fixture. It bounds what is automated today for vascular access; it does not cover IV cannula placement, line/pump connection or monitor application.

sources.title: Hyperion Surgical Announces Completion of First-in-Human Study Using Its Ivy Robotic Vascular Access Platform
sources.claim: Hyperion Surgical reported the first-in-human robotic-assisted IV catheterization with its Ivy platform in October 2025, a feasibility study performed by a clinical team rather than autonomous routine practice.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: peripheral IV placement, part of pre-induction line setup. Cited to bound capability: first-in-human and operator-directed, so it cannot support a positive judgment.

sources.title: Swisslog Healthcare Partners with Diligent Robotics to Enhance Hospital Logistics
sources.claim: Moxi, the largest deployed fleet of hospital mobile manipulators, autonomously fetches and delivers supplies and pharmacy items along hospital corridors in more than 25 US ...; its work is transport, not clinical equipment setup or drug preparation.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: hospital supply logistics. Shows the state of deployed in-facility mobile manipulation (fetch and deliver in corridors), which does not extend to assembling or checking an anesthesia workstation.

sources.title: An original design of remote robot-assisted intubation system | Scientific Reports
sources.claim: The Kepler Intubation System performed robotic tracheal intubation in patients, but it is a joystick-directed research device rather than an autonomous or deployed system.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: use of airway equipment (laryngoscope, tube) that the CRNA prepares and uses. Cited as a bound: teleoperated and research-only, so it supports no positive judgment.

tasks.label: Assess patients' medical histories to predict anesthesia response.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

tasks.label: Perform or manage regional anesthetic techniques, such as local, spinal, epidural, caudal, nerve blocks and intravenous blocks.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Spinal (subarachnoid) anesthesia in a hospital OR or pre-op holding area for orthopedic, urologic or cesarean surgery: position the awake patient sitting or lateral, palpate/ultrasound the interspace, sterile prep and drape, raise a skin wheal, advance the spinal needle to free CSF flow, inject the local anesthetic-opioid mix, lay the patient down, then check block level and treat hypotension.

Labor epidural on a labor-and-delivery unit: consent and position a moving, contracting patient, sterile prep, loss-of-resistance to identify the epidural space, thread and secure the catheter, give a test dose and loading dose, start the infusion, and troubleshoot one-sided or inadequate block.

Ultrasound-guided peripheral nerve block (interscalene, supraclavicular, adductor canal, popliteal, TAP, erector spinae) in a block bay of a hospital or ambulatory surgery center: light sedation and monitors, scan and identify the target, in-plane needle advance around vessels and nerves, incremental injection with aspiration and hydrodissection, sometimes a perineural catheter.

Local anesthetic infiltration and intravenous regional (Bier block) work: skin wheals before IV or arterial line placement and before neuraxial needles, field infiltration at the surgical site, or a Bier block with distal IV, Esmarch exsanguination, double tourniquet, slow lidocaine injection and staged tourniquet release with LAST vigilance.

Managing an established regional technique during a case or on the floor: assessing sensory/motor level by pinprick or cold, giving epidural top-ups or catheter boluses, adjusting infusion pumps, treating hypotension/bradycardia or high block, and converting to general anesthesia when a block fails.

Caudal or other pediatric/specialty block, typically performed on an anesthetized child in the OR: position laterally, palpate the sacral hiatus or scan it, single-shot caudal injection with aspiration and test dosing, or an awake infant spinal in a tightly held infant.

sources.developer: Oceanic Medical Products / McGill University (Hemmerling group)
sources.title: Artificial Intelligence-Supported Ultrasonography in Anesthesiology: Evaluation of a Patient in the Operating Theatre
sources.claim: The Magellan system is the only robot reported to have performed ultrasound-guided nerve blocks in human patients, and it is a joystick-driven, remotely controlled (teleoperated) arm holding the block needle, not an autonomous system; it remains a research device rather than routine clinical equipment.
sources.transferJustification: Directly on task (ultrasound-guided peripheral nerve blocks in humans), but teleoperated, so it cannot support a positive judgment.

sources.system: Focalist handheld robotic needle placement system
sources.title: Mendaera announces first procedures with Focalist handheld robotic system
sources.claim: Mendaera's Focalist, FDA-cleared in July 2025 for ultrasound-guided instrument/needle placement and first used clinically in September 2025 for kidney access during PCNL at Mayo Clinic Arizona, is a provider-held, provider-guided handheld robot: the clinician holds it against the patient and taps the target, and the device computes and executes the needle trajectory.
sources.transferJustification: Closest cleared robotic system for ultrasound-guided percutaneous needle placement; it is human-held and human-triggered and performs only the needle-advance step, so it does not autonomously complete a regional anesthetic.

sources.system: Autonomous spinal robotic system for transforaminal lumbar epidural injections
sources.developer: Johns Hopkins University (Margalit, Phalen, Taylor, Armand, Jain et al.)
sources.title: Autonomous Spinal Robotic System for Transforaminal Lumbar Epidural Injections: A Proof of Concept of Study
sources.claim: The most advanced 'autonomous' spinal injection robot reported is a Johns Hopkins markerless system evaluated only in a lumbar spine phantom, with mean needle-tip deviation of about 11 mm — no human or in-vivo use and precision far short of neuraxial anesthesia requirements.
sources.transferJustification: Related task (image-guided epidural injection). It is a bench phantom proof of concept, not a patient procedure, so it cannot substantiate completion of an epidural or spinal anesthetic on a person.

sources.system: Autonomous robotic US-guided regional anesthesia pipeline (nerve localization and needle guidance)
sources.developer: AIIMS New Delhi / IIIT Hyderabad (Tyagi et al.)
sources.title: Nerve Block Target Localization and Needle Guidance for Autonomous Robotic Ultrasound Guided Regional Anesthesia
sources.claim: Work toward autonomous robotic ultrasound-guided regional anesthesia remains at the perception/algorithm stage: nerve segmentation, needle-tip localization and target definition from patient ultrasound datasets, with no robot performing blocks on patients.
sources.transferJustification: Same task domain (nerve blocks), but the contribution is imaging software for a future robot; no robotic needle placement in patients is demonstrated.

sources.title: Performance, Safety, and Patient Experience of an Autonomous Robotic Phlebotomy Device: A Multicenter Trial
sources.claim: The only autonomous needle-in-patient robot in clinical use is Vitestro's Aletta phlebotomy device, CE-marked and deployed in European hospitals for routine diagnostic blood draws from superficial arm veins, with a 94.5% first-stick rate in a multicenter trial; it does not inject drugs, place catheters, or approach nerves or the neuraxis.
sources.transferJustification: Related task (autonomous venipuncture in a clinical facility). Transfer fails for this task: it targets superficial arm veins for blood withdrawal, and does not perform sterile local infiltration, tourniquet/exsanguination management, drug injection, or deep ultrasound-guided perineural or neuraxial needle placement.
