tasks.label: Prepare prescribed solutions and administer local, intravenous, spinal, or other anesthetics, following specified methods and procedures.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Hospital OR, general anesthesia: at the anesthesia cart the CRNA draws up and labels propofol, opioid and neuromuscular blocker from vials/ampoules, checks IV access (often placing the IV), then administers the induction bolus by IV push and maintains anesthesia (volatile or TIVA infusion), titrating boluses to the patient's hemodynamic and depth responses through the case.

Neuraxial anesthesia (spinal or epidural) for cesarean section, joint replacement or urology: patient positioned sitting/lateral, sterile prep, local skin wheal, prepared hyperbaric bupivacaine/opioid mixture drawn from ampoules, needle advanced by palpated landmarks or ultrasound to CSF/epidural space, injection or catheter dosing, then level checked and managed.

Regional block bay or OR: ultrasound-guided peripheral nerve block (interscalene, adductor canal, TAP) — dilute the ropivacaine/bupivacaine mixture with adjuncts, scan, insert block needle, inject in aliquots with aspiration; also plain local anesthetic infiltration for arterial/central lines.

Ambulatory surgery center, endoscopy suite or off-site location (cath lab, MRI, L&D): place the peripheral IV, draw up midazolam/fentanyl/propofol/ketamine, deliver MAC sedation by titrated bolus or infusion while supporting the airway, on a fast, high-turnover schedule with varied patient comorbidity.

Case setup/turnover: preparing the prescribed solutions themselves — drawing up and labeling the case's syringes, diluting vasopressors (phenylephrine, epinephrine) and oxytocin to protocol concentrations, and mixing infusion bags (epidural bupivacaine/fentanyl, remifentanil) so a correctly compounded, labeled, ready-to-administer set is available for the case.

sources.title: Ballad unveils new robotic compounding pharmacy technology
sources.claim: Omnicell IVX Station robotic compounders are installed and running in a health system's central-fill pharmacy, autonomously pre-filling syringes including doses used in the operating room.
sources.transferJustification: Same physical act as the preparation half of this task: aseptically transferring drug from vials into labeled syringes/bags at prescribed concentrations.

sources.title: New Automated Robot System in Renown Health
sources.claim: ARxIUM's RIVA is a fully automated IV compounding robot preparing syringes and IV bags, newly placed in a US hospital pharmacy.
sources.transferJustification: Covers preparing prescribed injectable solutions (dilutions, syringes, bags) — the preparation instance of this task.

sources.title: Syringe, IV Bag Compounding/Filling Systems Fulfill 'Mission': Part II
sources.claim: The RIVA robot works inside its own enclosed ISO Class 5 chamber where consumables are loaded and a six-axis arm moves them — a purpose-built machine enclosure, not an open human workspace.
sources.transferJustification: Establishes the environment class (enclosed, fixtured, purpose-built cell) in which the compounding robots operate.

sources.title: Technical communication: First robotic ultrasound-guided nerve blocks in humans using the Magellan system
sources.claim: The only robotic system reported to perform ultrasound-guided nerve blocks in humans, Magellan, is joystick-driven from a remote control centre, i.e. teleoperated, in a 13-patient pilot.

sources.title: Autonomous Spinal Robotic System for Transforaminal Lumbar Epidural Injections: A Proof of Concept of Study
sources.claim: Autonomous robotic needle placement for lumbar epidural/transforaminal injection has only been shown as a proof of concept in a phantom model, not in patients.

sources.title: Evaluation of a novel closed-loop total intravenous anaesthesia drug delivery system: a randomized controlled trial
sources.claim: Closed-loop anesthesia delivery (McSleepy) can automatically administer propofol, remifentanil and rocuronium through infusion pumps in randomized trials, but it is a supervised research drug-delivery controller: an anesthetist prepares and loads the drugs, secures IV access and manages the airway.

sources.title: Johnson & Johnson To Stop Selling Sedasys System
sources.claim: SEDASYS, the only FDA-approved computer-assisted sedation system, was limited to minimal-to-moderate propofol sedation in healthy adults for routine endoscopy, required an endoscopist/nurse team, and was withdrawn from the market in 2016.

sources.title: Waterloo startup performs first ever robotic intramuscular injection
sources.claim: An autonomous mobile robot performed a needle-free intramuscular injection on a person in a company demonstration; it does not compound drugs, gain vascular access, or titrate anesthetics.
sources.transferJustification: Nearest autonomous robotic drug-administration demo; cited to show the frontier is a fixed-dose IM jet injection, not preparation plus titrated IV/neuraxial anesthesia.

tasks.label: Perform pre-anesthetic screenings, including physical evaluations and patient interviews, and document results.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Day-of-surgery pre-anesthetic evaluation in a hospital pre-op holding bay: CRNA reviews the chart/labs, interviews the patient about history, medications, allergies, prior anesthesia and NPO status, then performs a focused physical — airway exam (mouth opening, Mallampati, thyromental distance, neck range of motion, dentition/loose teeth, beard), auscultation of heart and lungs, inspection of IV/vein access — formulates ASA class and anesthetic plan, discusses risks/consent, and documents in the EHR anesthesia record. Patient is gowned on a stretcher behind a curtain, family present, noise and time pressure.

Ambulatory surgery center / endoscopy center pre-op screening of mostly ASA I–II adults: brief phone or portal pre-screen plus a short day-of interview and focused airway/cardiopulmonary exam in a pre-op bay, sleep-apnea and difficult-airway screening, weight/BMI and vitals check, quick documentation on a standardized short form. High volume, rapid turnover.

Pre-anesthesia testing clinic visit days before surgery for a complex patient (morbid obesity, poorly controlled diabetes, cardiac stents, COPD, on anticoagulants): full history and physical in an exam room, functional capacity assessment, review of consultant notes and prior anesthetic records, ordering/interpreting labs, EKG or echo, medication instructions, and a detailed dictated/typed pre-anesthesia evaluation note.

Urgent or emergent screening in the ED, ICU, or labor and delivery: rapid focused assessment of an uncooperative, obtunded, intoxicated, in-pain, or laboring patient — airway and aspiration-risk assessment, cervical collar or trauma constraints, history obtained from family or paramedics, exam performed around monitors, lines and a moving bed, abbreviated documentation under severe time pressure.

Off-site / office-based anesthesia (dental or oral surgery office, plastic surgery suite, imaging suite), including pediatric or special-needs patients: screening performed in a dental chair or small procedure room with limited equipment, parent or caregiver interview, airway and behavioral assessment, documentation on the practice's own form.

sources.system: Automated robotic platform for remote auscultation (Tsumura et al., AIST)
sources.developer: National Institute of Advanced Industrial Science and Technology (AIST), Japan
sources.title: Toward Fully Automated Robotic Platform for Remote Auscultation (arXiv:2201.05272)
sources.claim: A research robotic platform performs autonomous stethoscope placement for auscultation using a cooperative arm, LiDAR camera and passive force mechanism — a single sub-step of a physical exam, demonstrated in a laboratory on subjects/phantoms, not a whole clinical screening.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic chest auscultation. It covers only one component of the pre-anesthetic physical evaluation (heart/lung listening) and does not address the airway exam, interview, clinical judgment, or documentation, so it cannot substantiate completion of the whole instance.

sources.system: Collaborative robotic platform for autonomous auscultation (Lopes et al.)
sources.title: Design and Development of Hugging Mechanism for Capturing Chest and Back Auscultatory Sounds (Applied Sciences)
sources.claim: A second research system autonomously locates and reaches auscultation points on the body with a UR3e arm and RGB-D camera, tested on six subjects — again only the auscultation sub-step, at research maturity.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic auscultation on human subjects. Transfers only to the chest-listening portion of a pre-anesthetic physical exam; no evidence of airway assessment, history taking with clinical judgment, or charting.

sources.developer: UC San Diego (Yip lab) with UCSD Health clinicians
sources.title: Humanoids in Hospitals: A Technical Study of Humanoid Surrogates for Dexterous Medical Interventions
sources.claim: The most advanced demonstration of a general-purpose robot performing clinical physical-exam and airway tasks (stethoscope, laryngoscope, bag-valve-mask, ultrasound) used a humanoid under bi-manual human teleoperation, not autonomy.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robot-performed physical examination and airway manipulation. It is the closest analogue to a pre-anesthetic physical evaluation, but because it is continuously teleoperated it cannot support a positive judgment at any tier.

sources.system: Dr. Spot (Boston Dynamics Spot with contactless vital-sign camera suite)
sources.developer: MIT, Brigham and Women's Hospital, Boston Dynamics
sources.title: Mobile Robotic Platform for Contactless Vital Sign Monitoring (PMC9096356)
sources.claim: A quadruped fitted with cameras and a tablet was used in hospital triage to take contactless vital signs and enable clinician-patient interviews, but the robot was teleoperated by clinical staff and the interview and assessment were done by the human clinician through the robot.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robot-mediated patient triage interview and vital-sign capture in a hospital. It is teleoperated telepresence — the clinician performs the assessment — so it does not substantiate autonomous completion of a pre-anesthetic screening.

sources.title: Serve Robotics to Acquire Diligent Robotics, Expanding Physical AI Platform Beyond the Sidewalk
sources.claim: The largest commercial autonomous mobile-manipulator deployment inside US hospitals performs supply and pharmacy deliveries only; no deployed hospital robot performs patient assessment or examination.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous hospital mobile manipulation. It establishes the ceiling of deployed hospital robot capability — item transport in corridors — which does not transfer to interviewing patients or performing an airway and cardiopulmonary examination.

tasks.label: Calibrate and test anesthesia equipment.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Start-of-day full pre-anesthesia checkout in a hospital OR: verify auxiliary O2 cylinder and self-inflating manual ventilation device, confirm wall suction clears an airway, confirm pipeline pressures and AC power, verify/fill vaporizers, inspect and connect the breathing circuit and CO2 absorbent, run the machine's leak/compliance/ventilator test, verify monitors, alarms and scavenging, then document readiness before the first patient.

Between-case abbreviated check in the same OR (several times per day): change breathing circuit/filter and reservoir bag, re-run the circuit leak and compliance test, confirm vaporizer level and agent/gas analyzer readings, re-check suction and airway/monitoring equipment, confirm alarms reset, all under turnover time pressure.

Machine electronic system test and sensor calibration on a workstation already set up and connected (circuit parked on the test port from the prior evening or after the machine is moved): initiate/complete the leak, compliance, flow-sensor and O2-sensor calibration sequence and record a pass/fail result.

Checkout at an off-site anesthetizing location (endoscopy suite, cath lab, MRI, dental or office-based surgery): compact/portable anesthesia machine or O2 cylinder plus portable monitors and suction; check tank pressures and regulator, connect and leak-test the circuit, verify monitor function and battery, confirm emergency airway and backup ventilation gear in a cramped, non-OR room.

Testing and troubleshooting ancillary anesthesia equipment or a failed check: swap out a machine that fails its leak test and re-test the replacement, test infusion/syringe pumps, fluid warmer, video laryngoscope, nerve stimulator or ultrasound, zero transducers, and coordinate with biomedical engineering.

sources.system: Dräger Atlan A300/A350 anesthesia workstation (automatic self-test / Auto On)
sources.title: Patient Safety in the Operating Room – Dräger Atlan
sources.claim: The Dräger Atlan anesthesia workstation runs an automatic self-test that covers leakage, compliance and flow-sensor calibration, and can be scheduled to power the machine on and run the test in the operating room with no one present.

sources.system: Dräger Auto-On / Self-Test Tracker (Atlan family, Perseus A500)
sources.title: Auto-On & Self-Test Tracker | Dräger
sources.claim: Dräger's timer-controlled fully automatic self-test on Atlan and Perseus A500 machines calibrates all sensors, performs an O2 real-gas test and detects breathing-tube exchange, but requires a human to have completed a manual preparation checklist beforehand.

sources.title: Perseus A500 | Draeger
sources.claim: The Perseus A500 anesthesia workstation performs a timer-based, fully automatic self-test that readies the machine before clinicians arrive in the operating room; results are visible centrally via the Self-Test Tracker dashboard.

sources.system: ASA/AACR 2008 Recommendations for Pre-Anesthesia Checkout (task-scope reference, not a robotic system)
sources.title: New Guidelines Available for Pre-Anesthesia Checkout – Anesthesia Patient Safety Foundation
sources.claim: The recognized scope of the pre-anesthesia checkout is 15 items daily (8 before each case), including provider-performed items such as verifying the auxiliary oxygen cylinder and manual ventilation (Ambu) bag and verifying that patient suction is adequate to clear the airway.
sources.transferJustification: Defines the accepted output of the checkout instances; used to show which items the machine self-test cannot cover.

sources.title: Anesthesia Machine Checkout | Anesthesia Equipment Simplified | AccessAnesthesiology
sources.claim: Anesthesia reference texts note that machines' built-in automated checkouts cover only some required checks, leaving user-performed tests (e.g., low-pressure leak test) that vary by machine model.

sources.system: Humanoid robots for operating room support (perspective/roadmap)
sources.developer: academic surgical robotics groups (review in surgical literature)
sources.title: Humanoid robots could take on low-risk operating room tasks before assisting surgical teams
sources.claim: As of July 2026, general-purpose humanoid robots in operating rooms remain prospective: proposed roles (supplies, equipment handling, room turnover) would begin as teleoperated or closely supervised low-risk ..., with autonomous clinical use considered premature.
sources.transferJustification: Nearest robotic capability for manipulating equipment inside an OR; shows no autonomous system handles OR equipment preparation today.

tasks.label: Evaluate patients' post-surgical or post-anesthesia responses, taking appropriate corrective actions or requesting consultation if complications occur.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: End-of-case emergence in the OR: CRNA assesses return of spontaneous ventilation, train-of-four reversal, airway reflexes and responsiveness; suctions the oropharynx, extubates, applies mask oxygen, treats cough/laryngospasm/desaturation with jaw thrust or positive-pressure ventilation, and boluses IV analgesic or antihypertensive before transport.

Routine PACU bedside evaluation of an adult after general anesthesia: level of consciousness, airway patency and respiratory rate, SpO2, BP/HR, temperature/shivering, pain score, nausea, dressing/drain/bleeding check; corrective actions include titrated IV opioid or antiemetic, oxygen adjustment, warming, repositioning, and rechecking against discharge criteria.

Recovery after neuraxial/regional block or MAC sedation at a hospital or ambulatory surgery center: test sensory/motor block level and regression, watch for oversedation or high spinal, treat hypotension/bradycardia with fluids and vasopressor, support the airway if respirations depress, and verify block resolution or discharge readiness.

Acute post-anesthesia complication requiring rescue: post-extubation laryngospasm, opioid-induced apnea, hemorrhage with hypotension, anaphylaxis, malignant hyperthermia or emergence delirium. Requires immediate hands-on airway management (bag-mask, reintubation), emergency drugs (sugammadex, naloxone, epinephrine, dantrolene), and calling the anesthesiologist or surgeon for consultation.

Office-based, dental or endoscopy-suite recovery with minimal staff and equipment: CRNA evaluates emergence, PONV, hypotension and delayed awakening, applies Aldrete/discharge criteria for same-day release, treats problems at the bedside, and escalates or arranges transfer if needed.

Post-operative rounding on admitted patients (ward/ICU) or next-day follow-up: bedside exam for residual block, post-dural-puncture headache, sore throat, nerve injury, delayed emergence or persistent nausea; orders or administers treatment, requests consultation, documents findings.

sources.title: Diligent Robotics Unveils Moxi 2.0, Advancing The Largest Fleet of Deployed AI-Powered Mobile Manipulation Robots
sources.claim: The largest deployed US hospital robot fleet performs logistics (medication and specimen delivery), not bedside clinical evaluation or treatment of patients.
sources.transferJustification: Related task (hospital nursing support): establishes that the demonstrated scope of autonomous mobile manipulators in structured hospital settings is item transport, with no patient assessment or corrective clinical intervention, so capability does not transfer to post-anesthesia evaluation.

sources.title: Could AI nursing robots help healthcare staffing shortages? | CNN Business
sources.claim: An AI nursing robot piloted in hospitals is limited to delivery and patient guidance tasks, not clinical assessment or intervention.
sources.transferJustification: Related task (ward nursing support): shows the current frontier of hospital humanoid deployment is transport and wayfinding, not physical patient examination or post-anesthesia rescue, so capability does not carry over.

sources.title: Automated closed-loop versus standard manual oxygen administration after major abdominal or thoracic surgery: an international multicentre randomised controlled study
sources.claim: Automated closed-loop oxygen titration adjusts a single variable (O2 flow to an SpO2 target) in the recovery room after major surgery, without assessing consciousness, airway, pain or the surgical site.
sources.transferJustification: Related task (post-operative oxygen management): the closest automated 'corrective action' after anesthesia, but a single-parameter flow controller supervised by clinicians that performs none of the multi-system evaluation or manual interventions this task requires.

sources.developer: Joosten, Rinehart, Cannesson et al. (research system)
sources.title: Automated closed-loop versus manually controlled norepinephrine infusion in patients undergoing intermediate- to high-risk abdominal surgery: a randomised controlled trial
sources.claim: Closed-loop vasopressor infusion can autonomously maintain blood pressure during surgery, but only as a supervised single-variable controller with anesthesia providers present.
sources.transferJustification: Related task (intraoperative haemodynamic management): demonstrates automated drug titration to an arterial-pressure target, but not the bedside evaluation, airway handling, or escalation decisions that define evaluation of post-anesthesia responses.

sources.system: Anesthesia airway management robot (snake-arm mask ventilation prototype)
sources.developer: Academic research group, published in Sensors
sources.title: Development of a Novel Anesthesia Airway Management Robot
sources.claim: Robotic mask ventilation / airway management remains an early laboratory prototype tested on a mock person, not a clinically usable autonomous rescue system.
sources.transferJustification: Related task (mask ventilation): the manual rescue manoeuvre most needed when post-anesthesia respiratory complications occur; demonstrated only on a manikin with unclear autonomy, so it cannot substantiate completion.

tasks.label: Administer post-anesthesia medications or fluids to support patients' cardiovascular systems.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Hospital PACU after general anesthesia: patient becomes hypotensive on the NIBP cuff; CRNA assesses, selects and draws up (or uses a prefilled syringe of) ephedrine or phenylephrine, swabs the IV port, pushes the bolus through the existing peripheral line, flushes, rechecks pressure and repeats as needed.

Post-cardiac or major-surgery patient in ICU/PACU with an arterial line and a norepinephrine (or nicardipine) infusion already running on a pump; the CRNA titrates the rate up and down to hold MAP in a target band during emergence, transport and handoff.

IV fluid support in PACU: spiking and hanging a crystalloid bag or programming the pump, giving 250-500 mL boluses for post-anesthetic hypovolemia/hypotension, then continuing maintenance fluids until discharge criteria are met.

Ambulatory surgery center or hospital PACU: post-op blood pressure out of range (hypertension or persistent hypotension) treated with a titratable vasoactive agent by infusion until pressure is controlled, with cuff monitoring only.

Ambulatory/office-based recovery: bradycardia, tachycardia or other cardiovascular disturbance treated with IV push agents (glycopyrrolate, atropine, esmolol, labetalol, hydralazine) chosen case by case, often through a saline lock with intermittent cuff monitoring and no invasive line.

Unstable post-op patient: hemorrhage or severe hemodynamic instability requiring rapid crystalloid/colloid and blood product resuscitation, multiple vasoactive agents, possibly placing additional IV access, while coordinating with surgeon and ICU team.

sources.developer: Academic group (Joosten, Rinehart, Cannesson et al.), Sauvegarde Clinic, Lyon
sources.title: Control of Postoperative Hypotension Using a Closed-Loop System for Norepinephrine Infusion in Patients After Cardiac Surgery: A Randomized Trial
sources.claim: A closed-loop vasopressor (CLV) controller autonomously drove the norepinephrine infusion pump for patients recovering in a cardiac-surgery ICU (i.e., post-anesthesia), holding MAP 65-75 mmHg with far less hypotension than nurse-controlled manual titration over a 2-hour study period.

sources.title: Automated closed-loop versus manually controlled norepinephrine infusion in patients undergoing intermediate- to high-risk abdominal surgery: a randomised controlled trial
sources.claim: Randomized trial in which a closed-loop controller automatically adjusted a norepinephrine infusion during general anesthesia, reducing hypotension compared with manual clinician titration.

sources.system: Closed-loop goal-directed fluid therapy system (Sironis/UCI-derived controller)
sources.developer: Lilot et al. / academic group (Lyon, UCI)
sources.title: Comparison of cardiac output optimization with an automated closed-loop goal-directed fluid therapy versus non standardized manual fluid administration during elective abdominal surgery
sources.claim: A closed-loop goal-directed fluid therapy system linked to a cardiac output monitor automatically delivered colloid fluid boluses to surgical patients in a randomized controlled trial.

sources.title: Implementation of closed-loop-assisted intra-operative goal-directed fluid therapy during major abdominal surgery: A case-control study with propensity matching
sources.claim: In routine implementation for 104 major abdominal surgery patients, the closed-loop system itself delivered both the maintenance crystalloid infusion and additional 100 mL hemodynamic boluses through the infusion pumps.

sources.title: Multicenter trial of automated nitroprusside infusion for postoperative hypertension
sources.claim: Multicenter clinical trial in which post-cardiotomy hypertensive patients had their intravenous sodium nitroprusside infusion titrated by an automated closed-loop system rather than by clinicians.

sources.title: New Automated Robot System in Renown Health
sources.claim: A robotic IV compounding system in routine hospital pharmacy use autonomously prepares IV syringes and bags from vials inside an enclosed ISO Class 5 cell.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: medication preparation rather than administration. It shows the vial-handling/syringe-filling manipulation of drug preparation is machine-doable only inside a purpose-built enclosed cell, supporting an E1 (work-brought-to-machine) judgment for instances whose preparation step must be automated.

sources.title: Monitoring Inputs, Control Architectures, and Failure Modes in Closed-Loop Vasopressor Systems: A Comprehensive Review
sources.claim: As of 2026, closed-loop vasopressor systems that couple real-time blood pressure monitoring to automated drug dosing are described as operating in perioperative and critical care settings under clinician supervision.

sources.title: Control of mean arterial pressure using a closed-loop system for norepinephrine infusion in severe brain injury patients: the COMAT randomized controlled trial
sources.claim: Randomized controlled trial (COMAT) of a closed-loop vasopressor system maintaining mean arterial pressure by automated norepinephrine infusion in severe brain injury patients in intensive care.

tasks.label: Select and prescribe post-anesthesia medications or treatments to patients.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

tasks.label: Perform or evaluate the results of diagnostic tests, such as radiographs (x-rays) and electrocardiograms (EKGs).

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

tasks.label: Select, order, or administer pre-anesthetic medications.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Routine adult in a hospital/ASC pre-op holding bay: CRNA reviews chart, selects and gives an IV anxiolytic/analgesic premedication (e.g., midazolam 1-2 mg ± fentanyl) through the IV already placed by the pre-op nurse, then watches sedation level, respiration and SpO2 before transport to the OR. Healthy, cooperative ASA I-II patient, standing protocol dose.

Protocolized IV adjuncts before induction: prophylactic antibiotic (e.g., cefazolin 2 g), antiemetic (ondansetron/dexamethasone), H2 blocker or nonparticulate antacid, drawn up or spiked and given through the existing IV in holding or on OR arrival, with weight/renal dose check and timing relative to incision. Fixed dose, minimal titration.

Oral/multimodal pre-op medication in the pre-op bay: acetaminophen, gabapentin/pregabalin, celecoxib, or an oral antacid handed to an alert adult with a sip of water, after confirming identity, allergies and NPO status, and confirming the patient swallows the doses.

Pediatric or cognitively impaired/highly anxious patient: oral midazolam syrup in juice or intranasal midazolam/dexmedetomidine atomized into the nostrils of a frightened, squirming child with a parent at the bedside; requires coaxing, weight-based dosing, restraint-free technique and close observation for over-sedation.

High-risk or complex case: frail elderly, morbid obesity/OSA, obstetric, trauma/ICU or awake fiberoptic intubation prep. CRNA decides whether to withhold or reduce premedication, orders and gives drugs such as glycopyrrolate, a titrated dexmedetomidine infusion, or aspiration prophylaxis, and stays with the patient managing airway/hemodynamic risk.

sources.title: American Society of Anesthesiologists (ASA) offers recommendations for using SEDASYS
sources.claim: SEDASYS, a computer-assisted personalized sedation system, received FDA premarket approval and was sold commercially for machine-controlled delivery of IV propofol to healthy adults during endoscopy, i.e. an automated device delivering a sedative drug into a patient's IV line in a clinical facility.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: procedural sedation drug delivery. It is the same route (IV line), same drug class (sedative-hypnotic), same patient population and same institutional setting as administering a pre-anesthetic sedative, and the machine performs the dose delivery and monitoring that a CRNA would perform.

sources.title: Recent Advances in Endoscopy Sedation: The Anesthesiologist's Perspective
sources.claim: The SEDASYS device automatically maintains, reduces or discontinues the propofol infusion based on capnography and an ...; the clinician sets the initial infusion rate, so dose escalation remains human-controlled.
sources.transferJustification: Same related task as above (procedural sedation); documents the degree of machine control over drug administration and its limits.

sources.developer: Japanese academic group (Journal of Anesthesia, non-inferiority RCT)
sources.title: Safety and efficacy of an automated anesthesia delivery system for total intravenous anesthesia with propofol, remifentanil, and rocuronium: a non-inferiority randomized controlled trial versus manually controlled anesthesia
sources.claim: An automated closed-loop anesthesia delivery system controlling propofol, remifentanil and rocuronium was tested in a randomized controlled trial against anesthesiologists and was non-inferior for keeping patients in the target range, showing a machine can compute and deliver IV sedative/opioid doses to real patients in an operating room.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated administration of IV anesthetic and opioid drugs during anesthesia. Same route, same drug classes (benzodiazepine/opioid-type CNS depressants), same patients and same institution as pre-anesthetic IV medication, with machine-selected doses derived from monitored variables.

sources.title: Performance, Safety, and Patient Experience of an Autonomous Robotic Phlebotomy Device: A Multicenter Trial (Clinical Chemistry)
sources.claim: An autonomous robotic phlebotomy device performed venipuncture on 1633 patients in Dutch outpatient phlebotomy departments with a 94.5% first-stick success rate and 0.6% mild adverse events; the device is CE marked and commercially launched.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous needle placement in a patient's vein at a dedicated draw station inside a healthcare facility. It shows machines can safely perform needle-based vascular procedures on unrestrained patients at human-comparable success rates, supporting the patient-contact portion of IV medication administration; it does not itself select or deliver drugs.

sources.title: Cobi robot autonomously performs intramuscular injection without needles
sources.claim: An autonomous robotic platform performed an intramuscular injection on a person using needle-free injection technology without a healthcare professional involved, in a laboratory demonstration.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous intramuscular drug injection into a human. Comparable act to giving an IM pre-anesthetic medication, though demonstrated only once in a lab and with a needle-free device.

sources.title: Automated Medication Platform With Video Observation and Facial Recognition to Improve Adherence to Antiretroviral Therapy (NCT05454514 protocol)
sources.claim: HiDO is an automated medication platform that dispenses prescribed oral doses to an identified patient at set times and uses facial recognition and a front-facing camera to validate that the dose was taken; it has been used as the study device in NIH-funded clinical trials.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated dispensing of prescribed oral doses to a verified individual with observed ingestion. This is the physical core of administering an oral premedication (right patient, right pills, confirmed swallowed), with the drugs pre-loaded into the machine.

tasks.label: Insert peripheral or central intravenous catheters.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Pre-op holding area or ambulatory surgery center: cooperative adult with visible/palpable forearm or hand veins. CRNA applies tourniquet, preps skin, places an 18-20 g catheter over-the-needle, advances the cannula, withdraws the needle, secures with transparent dressing, connects and flushes IV tubing, confirms free flow.

Pre-op bay: adult whose veins are harder but still locatable - obese, elderly with fragile/rolling veins, mildly dehydrated, anxious - CRNA uses a vein-visualization aid or ultrasound, may need a second site, then places and secures a standard 18-20 g catheter.

Severe difficult venous access: no visible or palpable veins (edema, chemotherapy-sclerosed veins, IV drug use, ESRD, cachexia). CRNA performs ultrasound-guided cannulation of a deep basilic/brachial vein with a long catheter, often after other clinicians have failed.

Intraoperative: anesthetized, draped patient on the OR table, arms tucked or on an armboard under a warming blanket. CRNA places an additional or large-bore (16-14 g) IV mid-case for volume/blood administration, secures it and connects it to a running infusion, under time pressure next to the sterile field.

Pediatric case: infant or child, usually cannulated after inhalational mask induction, 22-24 g catheter in a hand, foot, or scalp vein; tiny mobile vessels with a small margin for through-puncture; must be secured to survive the case.

Central venous catheter placement (internal jugular or subclavian) for a major/cardiac case or poor peripheral access: full sterile barrier, ultrasound-guided puncture, Seldinger guidewire, dilator, multi-lumen catheter, aspirate/flush all lumens, suture and dress, confirm tip position.

sources.title: Vitestro Publishes Breakthrough Study on Autonomous Robotic Blood Collection System
sources.claim: Peer-reviewed multicenter trial of Vitestro's Aletta autonomous robotic phlebotomy device: 1,633 patients in three outpatient phlebotomy departments, 94.5% first-stick success when a suitable vein was ..., including 97.4% in obese and 92.7% in self-reported difficult-access patients; adverse event rate 0.6%, all mild.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: diagnostic peripheral venipuncture. Same target (superficial arm vein of an adult), same guidance (Doppler ultrasound plus near-infrared), same sub-millimeter needle-tip precision and same institutional setting; peripheral IV placement adds advancing a cannula over the needle, a step demonstrated robotically in humans by Hyperion's Ivy.

sources.title: Aletta - Vitestro
sources.claim: Aletta executes the complete venipuncture procedure autonomously - tourniquet, vein selection, needle insertion, tube filling, needle withdrawal, bandage - with one human supervisor overseeing up to three devices.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: peripheral venipuncture on adults. Establishes that the ancillary steps of vascular access (tourniquet, site handling, sharps handling, dressing) are done by the machine without human hands - the part of IV placement beyond needle targeting.

sources.title: Hyperion Surgical Announces Completion of First-in-Human Study Using Its Ivy Robotic Vascular Access Platform, Achieving World's First Robotic-Assisted IV Catheterization
sources.claim: Hyperion Surgical completed a first-in-human study of the Ivy robotic vascular access platform, the first robotic-assisted peripheral IV catheterization; the robot holds the ultrasound probe and needle and places the catheter itself with AI vessel recognition and no user contact. Not yet FDA-submitted or commercialized.

sources.title: Aletta: A new blood draw experience - Vitestro (Patients)
sources.claim: Aletta is used as a fixed station: a staff member loads the tube cartridge, the patient sits down, presses start and places their arm in the device as instructed, after which the robot proceeds using near-infrared and ultrasound vein finding.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: peripheral venipuncture. Cited to characterise the environment the system needs - the patient is brought to the machine and the arm is fixtured in the device's cradle, i.e. a purpose-built station rather than bedside work.

sources.title: AURA-CVC: Autonomous Ultrasound-guided Robotic Assistance for Central Venous Catheterization
sources.claim: AURA-CVC, an end-to-end autonomous ultrasound-guided robotic central venous catheterization pipeline, achieved 10/10 first-attempt needle placements, but only on a high-fidelity commercial phantom - no animal or human use.

sources.title: AI-Enabled, Ultrasound-Guided Handheld Robotic Device for Femoral Vascular Access
sources.claim: AI-GUIDE is a hand-held, clinician-held device that robotically punctures a deep vessel and deploys a guidewire for Seldinger catheter insertion; evidence is from tissue-mimicking phantoms and live porcine femoral access, not human central line placement.

sources.title: Automated Phlebotomy Firm Vitestro Eyes 2027 Commercial Launch of Robotic Blood Draw Device
sources.claim: As of April 2026 Vitestro's device holds a CE mark and units have been placed in hospitals in the Netherlands and ..., so far within clinical trials, with European commercial launch targeted for 2027 and a US de novo submission planned.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: peripheral venipuncture. Cited for the maturity and deployment status of the decisive system.

tasks.label: Insert arterial catheters or perform arterial punctures to obtain arterial blood samples.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Routine radial arterial line placement in an adult surgical patient in a hospital OR, usually after induction: position and extend the wrist, palpate or use ultrasound, prep and drape, cannulate the radial artery with a 20G catheter (often Seldinger/integral-wire), confirm pulsatile flow, connect and flush the transducer tubing, secure with dressing/suture, and zero the line.

Difficult adult arterial access in the OR/ICU: obese, edematous, hypotensive/vasopressor-dependent, vasculopathic or previously cannulated patients; requires ultrasound guidance, repositioning, repeated attempts, sometimes switching sites (contralateral radial, brachial, dorsalis pedis, axillary) and managing hematoma or vasospasm.

Awake pre-induction arterial line in a high-risk cardiac, trauma or obstetric patient: coach and reassure the patient, infiltrate local anesthetic, cannulate while the patient may move, then place femoral or larger-bore lines in unstable cases, all under time pressure before induction.

Pediatric or neonatal arterial cannulation in the OR: 22-24G catheter into a 1-2 mm radial or femoral artery of an anesthetized infant/child, ultrasound or transillumination guided, with very low tolerance for repeated punctures.

Percutaneous arterial puncture for a blood gas sample (no indwelling line): assess collateral flow, palpate/ultrasound the radial or femoral artery, puncture with a heparinized ABG syringe, allow passive fill, withdraw, hold firm compression for several minutes, expel air, mix and deliver the sample to the analyzer promptly (OR, PACU or ICU).

sources.system: Autonomous femoral cannulation robot (Zevallos et al., CMU Robotics Institute / Univ. of Pittsburgh)
sources.developer: Carnegie Mellon University Robotics Institute with University of Pittsburgh Critical Care
sources.title: Automatic Cannulation of Femoral Vessels in a Porcine Shock Model (arXiv 2506.14467)
sources.claim: CMU/Pitt research robot (UR3e arm with ultrasound probe, force sensor and needle actuator) autonomously scanned and punctured femoral vessels, including arteries, in two live anesthetized pigs in hemorrhagic shock; a human marked the scan region and inserted the guidewire, and only 3 of 6 (trial 1) and 1 of 2 (trial 2) insertion attempts succeeded.
sources.transferJustification: Closest analogue to arterial catheter insertion: ultrasound-guided arterial puncture with guidewire placement in a live anesthetized subject. It does not transfer to worker quality because roughly half of attempts failed, the operator seeded the scan region and inserted the guidewire, the target was a large femoral artery rather than a 2-3 mm radial artery, and no catheter securing/transducer setup was performed.

sources.title: Performance, Safety, and Patient Experience of an Autonomous Robotic Phlebotomy Device: A Multicenter Trial (Clinical Chemistry)
sources.claim: Vitestro's Aletta Autonomous Robotic Phlebotomy Device performs venous blood draws autonomously on seated outpatients who place an arm into the machine, with one supervisor overseeing up to three devices; a multicenter trial of 1633 patients reported 94.5% first-stick success and 0.6% mild adverse events.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous needle insertion into a superficial forearm vein of a cooperative seated patient with an arm fixtured in the device. It does not transfer to arterial puncture or arterial catheterization: the device targets low-pressure superficial veins only (it excludes patients in whom no suitable vein is found), does not cannulate arteries, does not thread and secure an indwelling arterial catheter or connect a transducer, and does not provide the several minutes of arterial compression hemostasis the task requires.

sources.title: AURA-CVC: Autonomous Ultrasound-guided Robotic Assistance for Central Venous Catheterization (IJCARS)
sources.claim: AURA-CVC, an end-to-end robotic ultrasound pipeline for central venous catheterization, achieved 10/10 first-attempt needle placements, but only on a high-fidelity commercial phantom and with operator feedback during the needle-guidance step; the authors state full autonomy remains challenging.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: ultrasound-guided vascular puncture and catheterization. Evidence is phantom-only with operator feedback, so it cannot substantiate completing catheterization of a live patient's artery at worker quality in any environment.

sources.title: AI-Enabled, Ultrasound-Guided Handheld Robotic Device for Femoral Vascular Access (PMC)
sources.claim: AI-GUIDE is a handheld robotic device for femoral vascular access that a human user positions and operates; it robotically punctures the vessel and advances a preloaded guidewire, validated in phantoms and live pigs, not autonomously in patients.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: percutaneous vascular access with guidewire placement. It is user-held and user-directed rather than autonomous, so it cannot support a positive judgment for unattended completion of arterial cannulation.

tasks.label: Discharge patients from post-anesthesia care.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

tasks.label: Read current literature, talk with colleagues, and participate in professional organizations or conferences to keep abreast of developments in nursing.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

tasks.label: Request anesthesia equipment repairs, adjustments, or safety tests.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

tasks.label: Instruct nurses, residents, interns, students, or other staff on topics such as anesthetic techniques, pain management and emergency responses.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Informal point-of-care teaching of a student registered nurse anesthetist or anesthesia resident during a live OR case: the CRNA explains and talks through induction sequence, airway assessment, laryngoscopy technique, and drug dosing rationale while the trainee performs or observes, giving verbal correction and feedback.

Instructing PACU or floor nurses on post-operative pain management: explaining PCA pump programming, epidural/regional block care, opioid titration limits, and warning signs of respiratory depression, typically at a bedside handoff or a short unit in-service.

Delivering a formal didactic lecture or grand-rounds/in-service presentation in a hospital conference room or nursing school classroom on topics such as regional anesthesia pharmacology or difficult-airway algorithms, with slides and Q&A.

Leading or co-leading a simulation-lab session or mock emergency drill (malignant hyperthermia, local anesthetic systemic toxicity, code blue) with manikins, then conducting the structured debrief and feedback with students and staff.
Ad hoc instruction to OR staff, surgical techs, or new hires during pre-op huddles or orientation on emergency-response roles, crash-cart and MH-cart contents, and escalation procedures.

tasks.label: Disassemble and clean anesthesia equipment.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Hospital OR between-case turnover: after emergence, the CRNA strips the used single-patient breathing circuit, mask, HME/filter, gas sampling line and suction tubing off the anesthesia machine, discards them in the right waste stream, wipes the machine front panel, vaporizer knobs, monitor screen, BP cuff/cables, cart drawers and drug tray with hospital disinfectant wipes, and hangs a fresh circuit — all within a ~10-15 minute turnover alongside OR staff cleaning the room.

End-of-case/end-of-day handling of reusable items: separate laryngoscope blade from handle, break down video laryngoscope, LMAs, reusable bag/circuit, oral airways and stylets, wipe gross soil at point of use, place items in a covered biohazard bin, and deliver to the sterile processing decontamination window for washer-disinfector reprocessing.

Ambulatory surgery center, endoscopy suite, or office-based (dental/plastics) anesthesia where the CRNA does all of it alone: strip and clean the portable anesthesia machine or sedation setup, empty and change suction canisters, clean scavenging tubing, wipe portable monitors and their cables, and restock between quick back-to-back cases.

Machine-level disassembly and cleaning: remove and replace the CO2 absorbent canister, drain and clean water traps and condensate collectors, remove and clean/replace the bellows assembly, ventilator flow sensors and the removable breathing-system block, then reassemble and run the machine self-test and leak check before the next case.

After a grossly contaminated or infectious case: blood, secretions or vomitus on the laryngoscope, mask, circuit and machine surfaces; immediate point-of-use enzymatic pre-treatment, careful disassembly under PPE, double-bagged transport, and an extended contact-time wipe-down of the machine, cart, and cables per isolation protocol.

Off-site/austere practice: military field or forward surgical unit, mobile dental/surgical van, disaster or mission setting — the CRNA breaks down a portable draw-over or transport anesthesia machine and cleans components with limited water, improvised space and no sterile processing department.

sources.title: Bryan Health Uses New Robotic Technology to Clean and Sterilize Surgical Instruments
sources.claim: The most advanced deployed sterile-processing robot in a US hospital, STERIS's ATLAS Workflow Automation Vehicle, only transports racks of instruments to washers; technicians still hand-clean and break down the instruments themselves.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: hospital reprocessing of reusable medical devices, the destination of anesthesia equipment cleaning. It shows the deployed robot's role is rack logistics, not disassembly or cleaning of devices.

sources.developer: RIF Robotics (pilot with Wellstar Windy Hill Hospital)
sources.title: RIF Robotics pioneers autonomous surgical tray assembly - Catalyst by Wellstar
sources.claim: A robotic arm piloted in a hospital sterile processing department autonomously assembled a minor surgical tray from clean instruments; disassembly, decontamination and inspection remained human work.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic handling of surgical instruments inside a hospital SPD (E2). It is the closest demonstrated manipulation of medical devices, but covers picking and placing clean rigid instruments, not detaching tubing or cleaning equipment.

sources.developer: Georgia Tech / University of Louisville authors (Sankaranarayanan et al.)
sources.title: Towards Autonomous Instrument Tray Assembly for Sterile Processing Applications
sources.claim: Research systems can sort and pack surgical instruments into trays automatically, but the demonstrated scope is the clean assembly stage in a laboratory, not decontamination or device disassembly.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic handling of surgical instruments for reprocessing. Included to show that even in research, automation stops at sorting/packing rigid instruments and does not address disassembling or cleaning anesthesia devices.

sources.system: Husky-based autonomous wiping and UV-C disinfection robot
sources.developer: academic research team (published in Robotics, MDPI)
sources.title: Transforming hospital sanitation: Autonomous robots for wiping and UV-C disinfection
sources.claim: A research mobile manipulator can autonomously navigate hospital-like spaces and physically wipe surfaces before UV-C treatment, but it addresses flat high-touch surfaces, not stripping and reprocessing medical equipment.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic surface disinfection in a healthcare facility, the wipe-down half of this task. It is a laboratory/pilot demonstration on plain surfaces and does not handle machine panels, cables or removable anesthesia components.

sources.title: Why Bond Analysts Should Be Watching Hospitals' Infection-Fighting Robots
sources.claim: Deployed hospital UV disinfection units such as Xenex LightStrike are human-positioned emitters used after manual cleaning; they neither manipulate nor disassemble equipment.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: terminal room disinfection in ORs. Cited to establish that the widely deployed hospital 'cleaning robots' are adjunct emitters requiring prior manual cleaning, so they cannot substitute for equipment breakdown and wipe-down.

sources.title: Somatic - Autonomous Bathroom Cleaning Robots
sources.claim: Commercially deployed autonomous cleaning robots in hospitals and airports clean restroom fixtures, floors and trash — structured, robust surfaces — with no capability for delicate medical device disassembly.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous spray-and-wipe cleaning inside institutional (E2) facilities. It shows the state of deployed cleaning manipulation is rugged fixtures, not electronics, vaporizers, cables or breathing-circuit connectors.

sources.title: What is a Medical Washer-Disinfector? Learn More
sources.claim: Reusable anesthesia items (breathing circuits, masks, laryngoscope blades, LMAs) are cleaned in medical washer-disinfectors, machines that require humans to disassemble the devices and load them into racks first.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated cleaning of anesthesia accessories. The machine performs only the wash cycle on pre-disassembled, human-loaded items, so it cannot complete the disassemble-and-clean instance on its own.

roles.title: Nurse Midwives
roles.description: Diagnose and coordinate all aspects of the birthing process, either independently or as part of a healthcare team. May provide well-woman gynecological care. Must have specialized, graduate nursing education.

tasks.label: Provide prenatal, intrapartum, postpartum, or newborn care to patients.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Routine prenatal visit in an outpatient OB/midwifery clinic: take history, check BP/weight, palpate the abdomen (Leopold's maneuvers), measure fundal height, auscultate fetal heart tones with a Doppler, sometimes perform a pelvic/cervical exam or bedside ultrasound, and counsel the patient on nutrition, warning signs, and birth planning.

Intrapartum labor management in a hospital labor-and-delivery unit: serial cervical exams, interpretation of continuous or intermittent fetal monitoring, position changes and hands-on comfort measures, coaching pushing, supporting the perineum and controlling delivery of the head and shoulders, managing nuchal cord and shoulder dystocia maneuvers.

Immediate third/fourth-stage postpartum care in the delivery room: controlled cord traction and delivery of the placenta, inspection of the placenta and birth canal, fundal massage, administration of uterotonics, suturing perineal or vaginal lacerations, and recognizing and managing postpartum hemorrhage.

Immediate newborn care at the birth: drying and stimulating, skin-to-skin placement, Apgar scoring, cord clamping and cutting, bulb suction, initiating positive-pressure ventilation for a non-vigorous newborn, and performing the newborn head-to-toe physical exam and first latch assistance.

Postpartum inpatient rounds or an outpatient postpartum visit: palpate the fundus, assess lochia and perineal or cesarean incision healing, hands-on breastfeeding/latch assistance, screen for depression, examine and counsel on contraception.

Out-of-hospital birth care at a freestanding birth center or in the patient's home: same intrapartum, postpartum and newborn care but with variable layout, limited equipment brought in a kit, family and pets present, and no institutional control of the setting.

sources.title: Mama Anne robot gives birth to train midwifery students at York St John | Fox News
sources.claim: The closest thing to a 'midwifery robot' in real use is a robotic childbirth manikin that plays the role of the patient for student training; it does not provide care to anyone.
sources.transferJustification: Negative/context evidence: the robot is the simulated patient, not the care provider, so it substantiates no completion of midwifery care.

sources.title: Vitestro's robotic blood drawing device meets trial endpoints
sources.claim: Autonomous robotic venipuncture on real human patients has reached clinical-trial performance comparable to human phlebotomists, showing the frontier of autonomous hands-on procedures on human bodies is a single narrow, fixtured sub-step (an immobilized arm), not a multi-step clinical encounter.
sources.transferJustification: Related task = venipuncture. It does NOT transfer to this task: it is one fixtured needle insertion into a restrained forearm, whereas prenatal/intrapartum care requires whole-body palpation, internal exams, delivery maneuvers and clinical judgement on a moving, unrestrained patient.

sources.title: Robot Performs First Laparoscopic Surgery without Human Help - Johns Hopkins Technology Ventures
sources.claim: The most advanced autonomous soft-tissue robotic suturing works only on exposed, marked bowel in an anesthetized animal under surgeon supervision, with the routine selected by the operating surgeon.
sources.transferJustification: Related task = autonomous soft-tissue suturing, relevant to perineal laceration repair. It does not transfer: STAR was demonstrated only in anesthetized pigs on surgically exposed, fluorescently marked bowel, not on an awake postpartum patient's perineum, and it does not perform the surrounding assessment or hemorrhage management.

sources.title: Humanoid Robots in Healthcare [2026] - RoboZaps
sources.claim: Robots actually deployed in US hospitals perform logistics and telepresence — fetching supplies, delivering medications, transporting ... — not hands-on clinical care.
sources.transferJustification: Negative/context evidence establishing that deployed hospital robots handle materials in corridors rather than performing patient assessment or delivery care.

sources.system: auto-RUSS autonomous robotic ultrasound scanning system
sources.title: Autonomous robotic ultrasound scanning system: a key to enhancing image analysis reproducibility and observer consistency in ultrasound imaging - PMC
sources.claim: Autonomous robotic ultrasound scanning systems exist as research prototypes using a force-controlled 7-DoF arm with visual servoing, i.e. image acquisition only, evaluated against physicians for image reproducibility.
sources.transferJustification: Related task = probe placement for sonography, a possible sub-step of a prenatal visit. It does not transfer to the whole instance, which additionally requires palpation, fundal height measurement, pelvic exam, interpretation and counseling.

tasks.label: Monitor fetal development by listening to fetal heartbeat, taking external uterine measurements, identifying fetal position, or estimating fetal size and weight.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Routine third-trimester prenatal visit in a midwifery clinic/office exam room: the woman lies supine on an exam table, the midwife performs Leopold's maneuvers to determine fetal lie/presentation, measures fundal height with a tape, estimates fetal size and weight by palpation, then locates and counts the fetal heart rate with a handheld Doppler and documents/discusses findings.

Mid-pregnancy (16-28 week) prenatal visit in a clinic exam room: fundal height measured with a tape from symphysis to fundus and fetal heart tones located with a handheld Doppler on a smaller, mobile fetus whose position is not yet fixed; result plotted against gestational age.

Intrapartum monitoring in a hospital labor room or freestanding birth center: intermittent auscultation of the fetal heart with a Doppler through and between contractions while the laboring woman moves, changes position, or is in a tub, plus palpation to confirm fetal position/descent and placement or repositioning of external fetal monitor transducers.

Point-of-care obstetric ultrasound in the clinic to confirm fetal presentation at or near term or to estimate fetal weight/growth (BPD, HC, AC, FL biometry), performed by the midwife with a cart or handheld ultrasound on a patient on an exam table.

Home-birth practice: prenatal or labor assessment in the client's own home - palpation, fundal height, and Doppler auscultation with the client on her own bed, couch, or floor mat, variable lighting and furniture, family and pets present, no standard equipment or layout.

sources.developer: AdEchoTech / UiT The Arctic University of Norway, Finnmark Hospital
sources.title: Introduction of robot-assisted obstetric ultrasound in rural Northern Norway (Acta Obstetricia et Gynecologica Scandinavica)
sources.claim: The only obstetric ultrasound robot in clinical use for fetal biometry and biophysical assessment is remotely controlled by an obstetrician - teleoperated, not autonomous - studied on 46 pregnant women in rural Norway.

sources.title: Robotic Tele-Ultrasound: How Norway Is Bringing Prenatal Care Closer to Pregnant Women
sources.claim: In the deployed Norwegian tele-robotic prenatal ultrasound service a local midwife or health professional must be present with the patient while the remote physician drives the probe in real time; no part of the exam is autonomous.

sources.system: Obstetric cobotic ultrasound platforms (Arbeille et al. and successors)
sources.title: Cobotic Ultrasound Systems in Obstetric Assessment: A Scoping Review (Sonography)
sources.claim: A 2025 scoping review of cobotic ultrasound systems in obstetric assessment describes obstetric robotic platforms (fetal presentation, biometry, anatomy) as operating under direct expert human control rather than autonomously.

sources.title: Towards Standardized Acquisition with a Dual-probe Ultrasound Robot for Fetal Imaging
sources.claim: The leading research robot purpose-built for fetal ultrasound acquisition had only been tested in vivo on non-pregnant volunteers for general abdominal scans; it was not yet approved for use on pregnant participants and does not deliver a clinical fetal assessment.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic abdominal ultrasound acquisition. This is the closest system explicitly aimed at fetal imaging, and it shows the fetal application has not been performed on pregnant patients, so it cannot substantiate completion of fetal monitoring at any tier.

sources.system: Autonomous lightweight ultrasound robot for liver sonography (6-DOF cable-driven robot + AI agent)
sources.developer: Tsinghua University / Beijing Tsinghua Changgung Hospital
sources.title: Beyond hospital reach: Autonomous lightweight ultrasound robot for liver sonography (arXiv:2510.08106)
sources.claim: A lightweight abdomen-mounted robot autonomously acquires expert-level standard liver ultrasound planes ... detects pathology in patients, demonstrated in a hospital ultrasound department and in field settings.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous abdominal sonography on human patients - the strongest autonomous analogue. However, its targets are static adult organs; it does not demonstrate locating a mobile fetus, fetal heart auscultation, presentation determination, fundal-height measurement, or biometry-based fetal weight estimation on a pregnant abdomen, so it does not transfer to this task.

sources.system: Fully autonomous robotic ultrasound system for thyroid scanning (UR3 arm, reinforcement learning, force feedback)
sources.developer: Tsinghua University / Carleton University et al.
sources.title: A fully autonomous robotic ultrasound system for thyroid scanning (Nature Communications)
sources.claim: A fully autonomous robotic ultrasound ... scans the thyroid without human assistance and identifies nodules, achieving image quality on human participants close to clinician-acquired scans.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous ultrasound scanning of a superficial organ on cooperative human subjects. It shows autonomy is achievable for a static, predictably located target in a controlled exam room, but establishes nothing about fetal position determination, fetal heart tones, or fetal weight estimation in pregnancy.

tasks.label: Document patients' health histories, symptoms, physical conditions, or other diagnostic information.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

tasks.label: Provide patients with direct family planning services, such as inserting intrauterine devices, dispensing oral contraceptives, and fitting cervical barriers, including cervical caps or diaphragms.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: IUD insertion in a clinic exam room: patient in lithotomy position, bimanual exam to assess uterine position, speculum placement, cervix cleansed, tenaculum applied, uterus sounded, IUD deployed at the fundus with the manufacturer's inserter, strings trimmed; must manage cervical stenosis, vasovagal reaction and avoid perforation.

Follow-up/removal visit: speculum exam and string check after insertion, or IUD removal by grasping strings with ring forceps and applying steady traction; occasionally strings not visible, requiring retrieval instruments or ultrasound.

Dispensing oral contraceptives (or ring/patch) at a clinic or health-department visit: confirming eligibility, then physically providing packs/starter supplies from clinic stock or a dispensary to the patient with usage instructions and a supply for continuation.

Contraceptive injection or subdermal implant service in the clinic: drawing/administering depot medroxyprogesterone acetate IM or SC, or placing/removing an etonogestrel implant in the upper arm using local anesthetic, sterile field and trocar.

Fitting a cervical barrier: pelvic exam to size a diaphragm or cervical cap, trial insertion and check of fit over the cervix, removal, and hands-on teaching of the patient's own insertion/removal with spermicide.

sources.title: MedAvail's SpotRx Pharmacy and Cigna Medical Group Partner to Help Improve Medication Access in Phoenix
sources.claim: MedAvail's MedCenter is a robotic dispensing platform deployed inside medical clinics that fills and releases prescriptions to patients on site, with a remote pharmacist available by video.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated in-clinic prescription dispensing. It transfers to 'dispensing oral contraceptives' because the object handled is the same (a sealed retail pack of oral medication), the precision demanded is package selection and release rather than manipulation, and the environment is the same clinic in which the midwife dispenses.

sources.title: Cape Cod Healthcare Launches InstyMeds at Cape Cod Hospital – The First Fully Automated Prescription Drug Dispenser in the Northeast
sources.claim: InstyMeds automated dispensers are installed in US emergency departments, urgent care centers and student health clinics and hand pre-packaged prescription medications directly to patients after prescriber and pharmacist verification.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: point-of-care dispensing of pre-packaged prescription drugs to patients in a health facility. Same object class (unit-of-use oral medication packs), same accuracy requirement (right drug to the right patient), and the same institutional clinic setting as midwife dispensing.

sources.system: ScriptPro SP 200 Robotic Prescription Dispensing System
sources.title: ScriptPro Robotic Prescription Dispensing Systems
sources.claim: ScriptPro robotic prescription dispensing systems are long-standing commercial installations in health-system and retail pharmacies, autonomously selecting, counting, filling and labeling oral solid prescriptions with stated 99.70% counting accuracy.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic prescription fulfillment. Oral contraceptives are ordinary oral solid/blister products handled by these machines, and the reliability figure documents worker-comparable error rates for the medication-provision step of the midwife's dispensing instance.

sources.title: Cobi robot autonomously performs intramuscular injection without needles
sources.claim: Cobionix's Cobi robot performed an autonomous needle-free intramuscular injection on a human in a university laboratory demonstration; it remains a research prototype rather than a cleared, deployed clinical device.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous injection into a patient's arm. It is the nearest analogue to a contraceptive injection, but it is a one-off needle-free jet demonstration, not a validated delivery of a viscous DMPA suspension, and gives no basis for implant trocar placement.

sources.system: Robot-assisted gynecologic surgery platforms (da Vinci and emerging systems)
sources.title: Future of robot-assisted surgery in gynecology: technological innovation, challenges, and interdisciplinary integration
sources.claim: Robotic platforms used in gynecology (da Vinci-class and emerging systems) are master-slave teleoperated instruments driven continuously by a surgeon at a console; no autonomous transcervical or intrauterine device-placement system is reported.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic instrument work in the female pelvis. It bounds the state of the art: these systems are surgeon-teleoperated, so they cannot support an autonomous judgment for speculum/tenaculum/IUD-inserter work.

tasks.label: Initiate emergency interventions to stabilize patients.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Postpartum hemorrhage in a hospital labor-and-delivery room: midwife recognizes excessive bleeding within minutes of birth, performs vigorous fundal massage and bimanual uterine compression, calls for help, establishes/uses IV access, administers uterotonics (oxytocin infusion, IM methylergonovine, misoprostol, tranexamic acid), expresses clots, inspects and may repair lacerations, monitors vitals until the patient is stable.

Newborn who does not breathe at a hospital birth: midwife dries and stimulates the infant, positions the airway, suctions if needed, starts positive-pressure bag-mask ventilation within the first minute, applies pulse oximetry, adjusts ventilation, initiates chest compressions if heart rate remains low, and calls the neonatal team.

Acute intrapartum emergency at a hospital birth requiring immediate hands-on maneuvers: shoulder dystocia (McRoberts positioning, suprapubic pressure, Rubin/Woods rotation, delivery of the posterior arm) or cord prolapse (manual elevation of the presenting part, knee-chest positioning) while summoning the obstetric team.

Maternal medical emergency on the hospital unit: eclamptic seizure, severe-range hypertension, anaphylaxis, or amniotic-fluid-embolism collapse — protect airway and position the patient, apply oxygen and monitors, give IV magnesium sulfate/labetalol/epinephrine, start fluids, begin CPR and activate the code team as needed.

Emergency at an out-of-hospital birth (client's home or freestanding birth center): limited equipment, variable layout and lighting; midwife performs neonatal PPV or hemorrhage control with portable supplies, administers medications, calls 911, and stabilizes the mother or newborn for ambulance transfer.

Emergency during office gynecologic or prenatal care in a clinic exam room: vasovagal syncope or severe cramping after IUD insertion, heavy vaginal bleeding from miscarriage, or allergic reaction — position the patient, take vitals, apply pressure/remove device, give IV fluids or epinephrine, and arrange emergency transfer.

sources.title: Diligent Robotics completes 300,000 pharmacy deliveries with Moxi - The Robot Report
sources.claim: The most widely deployed hospital mobile manipulator fleet performs point-to-point logistics (medications, lab samples, supplies) in hospitals; it does not perform hands-on clinical or emergency interventions on patients.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous in-hospital delivery. It establishes the state of deployed hospital robotics — navigation and item transport in an E2 facility — and shows the deployed frontier stops short of touching patients, so it cannot substantiate emergency stabilization.

sources.developer: AIST / CNRS-AIST JRL with Kawasaki Heavy Industries
sources.title: Humanoid Robot RHP Friends: Seamless Combination of Autonomous and Teleoperated Tasks in a Nursing Context (arXiv:2412.20770)
sources.claim: State-of-the-art humanoid research platforms aimed at nursing care combine limited autonomy with human teleoperation for patient-adjacent tasks; dexterous care actions rely on remote operators rather than autonomous execution.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: humanoid assistance in a nursing context. It is the closest robotic work to hands-on patient care; because the patient-facing manipulation is teleoperated and demonstrated only in staged settings, it cannot substantiate autonomous emergency stabilization.

sources.title: Rutgers robot draws blood better than humans in first trials - The Robot Report
sources.claim: Autonomous medical robots that touch patients are confined to single, narrowly scoped procedures such as needle insertion for blood draw, evaluated in early first-in-human studies rather than deployed emergency care.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous venipuncture, a sub-step resembling emergency IV access. It does not transfer: obtaining vascular access on a still, presented arm is one step of a multi-action emergency response involving assessment, positioning, drug choice, and manual obstetric maneuvers.

sources.title: Effectiveness of a Brief Educational Video on the Correct Placement of Automated Chest Compression Devices: A Prospective Study
sources.claim: Mechanical chest-compression machines deliver one resuscitation sub-step only after a clinician recognizes arrest and correctly positions the device on the patient; placement accuracy is itself a trained human skill.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: mechanical CPR during cardiac arrest. It is an automated actuator, not a robot that senses, decides, and acts: a human must diagnose the emergency and mount the device, so it cannot complete an emergency-stabilization instance.

instances.label: Routine prenatal visit in a clinic exam room: midwife takes BP, pulse, weight, checks lower-extremity edema and deep tendon reflexes if indicated, measures fundal height, performs Leopold's maneuvers to determine fetal lie, and auscultates fetal heart tones on a clothed/partially draped pregnant patient who moves, talks, and asks questions.

Well-woman gynecologic visit in an office exam room: vital signs, clinical breast exam (systematic palpation of both breasts, axillae, nipple assessment), speculum insertion with visualization of the cervix and Pap/STI specimen collection, then bimanual pelvic exam palpating uterus and adnexa on a patient in lithotomy position, with verbal coaching for comfort and consent throughout.

Intrapartum assessment on a hospital labor unit: maternal vitals, sterile-gloved digital cervical exam to assess dilation, effacement, station, membrane status and fetal position, repeated between contractions on a laboring patient who is moving, in pain, and may be in bed, on a ball, or in a tub.

Postpartum maternal exam (hospital room or clinic): vitals, palpation of uterine fundus for tone and position, inspection/palpation of perineal laceration repair or cesarean incision, breast exam for engorgement, mastitis or nipple trauma, lochia assessment, often with a newborn present and the patient partly undressed in bed.

Urgent triage assessment for suspected hypertensive disorder of pregnancy in an obstetric triage bay: repeat blood pressures with correct cuff size and positioning, pulse and respirations, deep tendon reflex and clonus testing, facial/hand edema and right-upper-quadrant tenderness palpation, with rapid interpretation feeding an immediate treatment decision.

Home visit or freestanding birth-center exam by a home-birth/community midwife: vitals, abdominal palpation, fetal heart tones and cervical or perineal exam performed on a bed, sofa, or birth pool in the client's own house, with varied lighting, furniture, pets, family members present, and no institutional control of the space.

sources.system: IRIS (robotIc Radial palpatIon mechaniSm), Bristol Robotics Laboratory / University of Bristol
sources.developer: University of Bristol / Bristol Robotics Laboratory
sources.title: New robot could help diagnose breast cancer early
sources.claim: IRIS, a 3D-printed radial palpation manipulator for clinical breast examination, is a laboratory prototype validated only on a silicone breast phantom and its digital twin, not on patients; it does not perform a complete clinical breast exam with diagnostic judgment.
sources.transferJustification: Directly related to the breast-examination component of this task; cited to show the closest robotic palpation work remains a bench prototype on phantoms, so it cannot substantiate completion on patients in any environment.

sources.system: Agile mobile robotic platform for contactless vital-signs monitoring (Boston Dynamics Spot)
sources.developer: MIT, Boston Dynamics, Brigham and Women's Hospital
sources.title: Dog-like robot measures patients' vital signs remotely – Physics World
sources.claim: A Boston Dynamics Spot platform instrumented by MIT/Brigham and Women's measured four vital signs contactlessly on healthy volunteers at 2 m; the team stated a fully autonomous version was still future work, so the demonstration was human-operated and covers only a subset of vital signs.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic vital-sign acquisition, the least demanding component of this exam task. Cited as a negative bound: even this narrow contactless subset was operator-driven on healthy volunteers, not autonomous clinical measurement.

sources.developer: Su et al., published in Nature Communications
sources.title: A fully autonomous robotic ultrasound system for thyroid scanning | Nature Communications
sources.claim: FARUS autonomously performed thyroid ultrasound scans on 70 human volunteers with force-controlled probe contact, showing autonomous, safe robot contact with a person's body is possible in a controlled research/clinical room, but limited to one imaging modality on a supine, still subject.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous robot-to-patient contact scanning. Transfer is limited — it acquires images of an exposed, immobile neck; it does not take vital signs, elicit reflexes, palpate breasts, insert a speculum, or perform bimanual/digital pelvic examination.

sources.title: Medical Robotics for Ultrasound Imaging: Current Systems and Future Trends | Current Robotics Reports
sources.claim: The only commercially available robotic ultrasound systems for patient examination are teleoperated (MGIUS-R3, MELODY), i.e. a remote clinician drives the probe, so commercial robotic patient-examination hardware is not autonomous.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robot-mediated physical examination of patients. Cited as a negative bound — the commercially deployed systems in this space require continuous human teleoperation, which does not satisfy the limited-intervention standard.
