tasks.label: Provide primary health care, including pregnancy and childbirth, to women.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Routine scheduled prenatal visit in a midwifery clinic or hospital outpatient office: greet and interview the pregnant patient, take/verify vitals and weight, palpate the abdomen (Leopold's maneuvers), measure fundal height with a tape, auscultate fetal heart tones with a handheld Doppler, check for edema, review labs/ultrasounds, order tests, counsel on nutrition, warning signs and birth planning, and document an assessment and plan.

Managing labor and attending a spontaneous vaginal birth on a hospital labor and delivery unit: serial cervical exams, membrane status assessment, interpreting continuous or intermittent fetal heart monitoring, hands-on support and position changes, controlling the delivery of the head and shoulders, catching the newborn, clamping and cutting the cord, delivering the placenta, and repairing a first- or second-degree perineal laceration with sutures.

Well-woman gynecologic primary care visit in a clinic exam room: history and counseling, clinical breast exam, speculum insertion with visualization of the cervix, Pap/HPV specimen collection, STI swabs, bimanual pelvic exam, and contraception provision including IUD insertion or contraceptive implant placement in the arm.

Postpartum and newborn care: immediate postpartum assessment on the unit (fundal massage, lochia and perineum check, vital signs), breastfeeding/latch assistance, newborn physical assessment, and the 1-2 week and 6-week postpartum office visits including incision or perineal healing checks and depression screening.

Urgent or emergent intrapartum/postpartum management in the hospital: shoulder dystocia maneuvers (McRoberts, suprapubic pressure, Woods screw), manual management of postpartum hemorrhage with uterine massage/bimanual compression and medication administration, cord prolapse elevation, neonatal resuscitation with bag-mask ventilation, and escalation/handoff to obstetric or neonatal teams.

Out-of-hospital birth attended at a client's private home or a freestanding birth center taken as found: arriving with portable equipment, setting up in an unstandardized room, monitoring labor with a handheld Doppler, attending the birth on a bed/floor/tub, managing third stage, suturing if needed, and performing newborn and maternal assessments before departure.

sources.system: Autonomous lightweight ultrasound robot for liver sonography
sources.developer: Tsinghua University / Beijing Tsinghua Changgung Hospital collaboration
sources.title: Beyond hospital reach: Autonomous lightweight ultrasound robot for liver sonography (arXiv 2510.08106)
sources.claim: An autonomous lightweight robotic ultrasound system performed liver sonography on humans and was deployed in a hospital ultrasound department to test autonomous scanning in a clinical setting. This is at most one imaging sub-step of a prenatal visit, not the whole encounter.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: abdominal ultrasound probe placement on a human torso. It is the closest robotic analogue to the abdominal palpation/Doppler component of a prenatal exam, but it delivers only images and does not perform the interview, assessment, counseling, or plan that constitute the visit.

sources.system: Robotic fetal ultrasonography platform with DNN scan-motion generation
sources.developer: Japanese university research group (Advanced Robotics, Vol 38 No 3)
sources.title: Autonomous scanning motion generation adapted to individual differences in abdominal shape for robotic fetal ultrasound
sources.claim: Research robotic fetal ultrasound platforms generate autonomous scanning motions over the pregnant abdomen, but remain laboratory/volunteer research systems automating only the imaging protocol.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated fetal ultrasound acquisition. Directly relevant to prenatal assessment of the fetus, but it covers only image acquisition on a cooperative supine abdomen and does not perform fundal height measurement, Doppler auscultation, examination, diagnosis or counseling.

sources.system: SRT-H (Surgical Robot Transformer-Hierarchy), successor to STAR
sources.title: Doctors Let AI Control Surgery Robot and Perform Gallbladder Removal on Its Own
sources.claim: The SRT-H surgical robot autonomously performed gallbladder removal steps on pig cadavers in a laboratory, the current frontier of autonomous soft-tissue surgical manipulation; no comparable system performs perineal laceration repair on a live human.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous soft-tissue dissection and suturing. It bounds what autonomous robots can do with deformable human-like tissue; performance does not carry over to intrapartum perineal repair, which occurs on a live, moving, bleeding patient in an unfixtured field.

sources.system: Teleoperated humanoid surgical surrogates (e.g., Unitree G1-class platforms)
sources.developer: Academic surgical/robotics teams reported in medical press
sources.title: Surgeons use teleoperated humanoid robots to perform live surgery—a world first
sources.claim: Humanoid robots used in live surgery in 2026 were remotely operated by surgeons, not autonomous, so they cannot substantiate autonomous completion of clinical care tasks.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: humanoid robot performing bedside/operative clinical manipulation. Cited to show that the most dexterous clinical humanoid demonstrations as of mid-2026 remain continuously teleoperated, which under the autonomy rule cannot support a positive judgment.

instances.label: Bedside clinical precepting on a hospital labor-and-delivery unit: the CNM supervises a student nurse midwife or OB resident managing a laboring patient, explaining fetal heart tracing interpretation, labor progress, and delivery technique, coaching the learner through the delivery and giving feedback afterward.

Didactic instruction — classroom lecture, seminar, or web conference for student nurse midwives or medical students on the physiology and stages of labor, mechanisms of birth, third-stage management, and evidence-based practice, including slides, Q&A, and assigned readings.

Case-based teaching and debriefing away from the patient: rounds discussion, chart and partograph review, post-delivery debriefs, feedback on clinical reasoning and documentation, and competency evaluation meetings with the learner.

Simulation-lab teaching in a nursing/medical school skills center: demonstrating and drilling cardinal movements, shoulder dystocia maneuvers, and postpartum hemorrhage response on birthing manikins, then critiquing the learner's performance.

Teaching hands-on assessment skills in an outpatient birth center or prenatal clinic: showing a student how to perform Leopold maneuvers, fundal height measurement, and cervical examination on a consenting patient, correcting hand placement and technique.

tasks.label: Manage newborn care during the first weeks of life.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Hospital or birth-center postpartum unit, first 24-72 hours after birth: the midwife performs the full newborn assessment on a squirming, undressed infant - auscultates heart and lungs, palpates abdomen and fontanelles, checks hips (Ortolani/Barlow), reflexes, clavicles, cord stump, skin/jaundice, measures weight, length and head circumference, interprets findings, counsels the parents, documents, and judges discharge readiness.

Clinic/office newborn follow-up at day 3-5 and again at 1-2 weeks: undress and weigh the baby on an infant scale, assess weight trajectory, hydration, jaundice, cord and circumcision healing, repeat head-to-toe exam, review feeding and output history with the parents, order/interpret bilirubin or repeat screens, give anticipatory guidance and a care plan.

Home visit by a home-birth or birth-center midwife at 24-48 hours and day 3-5: newborn exam done on a bed or sofa in a family's home with pets, siblings, clutter and variable lighting; portable scale; heel-stick blood-spot newborn screening onto a filter card; observation of a feed; safe-sleep and cord-care teaching; decision on whether the baby needs escalation.

Hands-on feeding/lactation management: positioning and latching a fussy or sleepy newborn at the breast, correcting the latch by hand, assessing suck and milk transfer (pre/post weights), inspecting oral anatomy for tongue-tie, teaching hand expression, syringe/finger feeding or supplementation, coaching a distressed mother in real time.

Newborn procedures and screening in a facility: heel-stick metabolic blood-spot collection on a filter card, transcutaneous or serum bilirubin, pulse-oximetry CCHD screen, vitamin K and hepatitis B injection, hearing-screen setup, weighing and swaddling, with comfort measures for the infant and parental consent/explanation.

Recognizing and escalating a sick newborn: infant with >10% weight loss, poor feeding, lethargy, rising bilirubin or respiratory distress; re-examine the baby, take vitals, arrange phototherapy, home nursing or transfer, hand off to pediatrics or the emergency department, and coordinate follow-up with the family.

sources.title: Vitestro Publishes Landmark Peer-Reviewed Multicenter Clinical Study of Autonomous Robotic Phlebotomy in Clinical Chemistry
sources.claim: Vitestro's Aletta performs fully autonomous venous blood draws on adult outpatients in hospital phlebotomy departments with a 94.5% first-stick success rate across 1,633 patients - the closest existing autonomous system to any blood-collection sub-step of newborn care, but validated only on adult arms, not neonatal heel sticks.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: diagnostic blood collection. Cited to test transfer to the neonatal heel stick in this task; transfer fails - the device targets adult antecubital veins with the cooperative adult arm fixtured in a purpose-built draw station, not a capillary heel stick on a moving newborn, and no neonatal validation is reported.

sources.system: Unitree G1 humanoid bimanual teleoperation system for medical procedures
sources.developer: Humanoids in Hospitals research team (Johns Hopkins-affiliated)
sources.title: Humanoids in Hospitals: A Technical Study of Humanoid Robot Surrogates for Dexterous Medical Interventions
sources.claim: A state-of-the-art attempt to have a humanoid robot perform clinical tasks including physical examinations and precision needle procedures worked only through bimanual teleoperation by a human operator, with reported limits in force output and sensor sensitivity.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: hands-on physical examination and needle procedures on adult patients/manikins. It is the nearest evidence for robotic physical assessment; because it is entirely teleoperated it cannot support a positive judgment for autonomous newborn examination.

sources.title: Diligent Robotics completes 300,000 pharmacy deliveries with Moxi - The Robot Report
sources.claim: The robots actually deployed at scale in US hospitals - Diligent Robotics' Moxi - perform autonomous fetch-and-deliver logistics (supplies, pharmacy items, lab samples), not hands-on patient assessment or care of infants.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous mobile manipulation inside hospitals (E2). Establishes that deployed hospital robots handle inanimate supplies only; this does not transfer to examining, handling or treating a newborn, which requires contact-safe manipulation of a fragile human plus clinical judgment.

sources.system: RP-7 robot-assisted telemedicine in the NICU
sources.developer: Children's Hospital Los Angeles / InTouch Health platform
sources.title: "Tele-Rounding": Robots in the Neonatal Intensive Care Unit | Children's Hospital Los Angeles
sources.claim: In neonatal care specifically, the demonstrated robotic role is telepresence: a mobile telemedicine robot lets a remote neonatologist round on infants and direct daily care, while all physical examination and handling of the newborn is done by human staff at the bedside.
sources.transferJustification: Same task domain (managing newborn care in the first days of life). The robot is a remotely driven telepresence platform with no manipulation capability, so the physical newborn assessment remains entirely human.

May order, perform, or interpret diagnostic tests such as lab work and x rays. May prescribe medication. Must be registered nurses who have specialized graduate education.

tasks.label: Diagnose or treat complex, unstable, comorbid, episodic, or emergency conditions in collaboration with other health care providers as necessary.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Acute-care NP in a hospital ICU or step-down unit evaluates a deteriorating patient (sepsis, respiratory failure, post-op instability): bedside physical exam, synthesis of monitor data, labs and imaging, ordering and performing invasive procedures (arterial/central line, chest tube, airway support), titrating vasopressors, and discussing the plan with the intensivist.

Emergency department or urgent care NP works up an undifferentiated acute presentation (chest pain, abdominal pain, laceration, possible fracture): history and hands-on physical exam, point-of-care ultrasound, ordering labs/imaging, bedside procedures such as suturing, splinting or joint reduction, and disposition decided with the attending physician.

Primary care or specialty clinic NP sees a comorbid patient (e.g., heart failure plus diabetes plus CKD) with an acute exacerbation: focused exam (auscultation, edema, wound/foot check), medication titration, in-office tests, deciding between treat-in-clinic and ED transfer, and coordinating with the collaborating physician and specialists.

Hospitalist/rapid-response NP called to a med-surg floor for acute deterioration (hypotension, chest pain, altered mental status, arrest): rapid bedside assessment, hands-on airway/circulation support, ACLS participation with the code team, immediate orders and transfer to higher level of care.

NP covering a skilled nursing or long-term care facility responds to an acute change in condition in a frail resident (fall with possible fracture, delirium, aspiration pneumonia): on-site assessment with limited equipment, wound or catheter care, orders for treat-in-place, and negotiation with family and the attending about hospital transfer.

Home-based primary care NP visits a homebound complex patient for an episodic exacerbation (COPD flare, infected pressure ulcer, uncontrolled pain): assessment in a cluttered private residence with a portable kit, wound debridement/dressing, medication changes, and phone coordination with the physician and hospice/home-health team.

sources.title: Performance, Safety, and Patient Experience of an Autonomous Robotic Phlebotomy Device: A Multicenter Trial | Clinical Chemistry
sources.claim: An autonomous robotic phlebotomy device performed venipuncture on patients in a multicenter trial, but it is limited to a single narrow procedure (blood draw) and screens out patients without a suitable vein; it performs no assessment, diagnosis, or treatment of unstable conditions.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: peripheral blood draw/IV access, a sub-step NPs sometimes perform. It shows the current ceiling of autonomous patient-contact robotics in a clinical facility (one fixtured, seated-patient procedure), far short of examining, diagnosing and treating an unstable comorbid patient.

sources.system: Autonomous lightweight ultrasound robot for liver sonography
sources.developer: Tsinghua University / Beijing Tsinghua Changgung Hospital collaboration
sources.title: Beyond hospital reach: Autonomous lightweight ultrasound robot for liver sonography (arXiv)
sources.claim: A fully autonomous ultrasound robot performed liver scanning on humans in a hospital ultrasound department, demonstrating autonomous probe placement and image acquisition, but only for an imaging sub-step on a cooperative, positioned patient.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: diagnostic imaging acquisition, one input NPs use. Transfer is partial only: the robot acquires images on a still, supine, consenting patient and does not conduct a physical exam, integrate history, or deliver treatment.

sources.system: Robot-assisted medical ultrasound imaging systems (survey of field)
sources.title: Review of robot-assisted medical ultrasound imaging systems: Technology and clinical applications - ScienceDirect
sources.claim: Reviews of robotic medical ultrasound state that fully autonomous systems cannot yet independently complete common scan-and-diagnose workflows and raise safety concerns, indicating no autonomous robot performs clinical diagnostic workups.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic diagnostic examination. Establishes that even the narrow imaging portion of a clinical workup is not autonomously completed at clinical standard, so the broader diagnose-and-treat task is not substantiated.

sources.title: Humanoid Robots in Healthcare [2026] - RoboZaps Blog
sources.claim: Robots actually deployed in US hospitals are logistics platforms: Moxi autonomously moves supplies, specimens and medications on hospital floors and does not perform patient assessment or treatment.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: in-hospital material transport. Cited to characterize the actual state of autonomous hospital robotics (non-patient-facing logistics), supporting a negative judgment on autonomous diagnosis or treatment of unstable patients.

sources.developer: academic team reported in Science Translational Medicine
sources.title: A soft robotic device for rapid and self-guided intubation | Science Translational Medicine
sources.claim: A self-guided soft robotic intubation device achieved high success in mannequin and cadaver testing, but it is operated by a human user and has not been shown to autonomously manage an emergency airway in patients.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: emergency airway management, a treatment step in unstable-patient care. It does not transfer: the device is hand-held and human-directed, tested on mannequins/cadavers, so it cannot substantiate autonomous emergency treatment.

tasks.label: Diagnose or treat acute health care problems, such as illnesses, infections, or injuries.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Adult acute illness visit in a primary care or urgent care clinic exam room: NP takes the history, performs a focused hands-on exam (vitals, otoscopy, oropharynx, lung and heart auscultation, abdominal palpation, node/skin inspection), obtains a rapid strep/flu/COVID swab or urine dip, interprets the result, forms a diagnosis, prescribes antibiotics/antivirals or symptomatic therapy, and counsels the patient. Patients vary in age, cooperation, language, and comorbidity.

Pediatric acute visit in a clinic: febrile infant or young child with ear pain, cough, sore throat, or rash; NP must restrain/soothe a squirming, crying child to perform otoscopy, throat exam and auscultation, judge hydration and toxicity, do weight-based dosing, and may give in-office treatment (nebulizer, antipyretic, cerumen removal) plus parent instructions.

Minor acute injury procedure in urgent care or ED procedure room: assess a laceration, abscess, foreign body, or extremity injury; obtain consent; inject local anesthetic; irrigate and explore the wound; close with sutures, staples, or adhesive; incise and drain an abscess; reduce and splint a sprain or simple fracture; dress the wound and give aftercare and tetanus prophylaxis.

Acute presentation in a hospital ED or inpatient unit: chest pain, abdominal pain, dyspnea, or suspected sepsis; NP performs bedside exam, orders and interprets labs, ECG, and imaging, places IV access or performs bedside procedures, initiates fluids/medications, reassesses, and decides disposition, often under time pressure with an unstable patient.

Acute problem evaluated at the bedside in a nursing-home resident's room or the patient's own home (home-based primary care / house call): fall injury, cellulitis, suspected UTI, COPD exacerbation; cluttered or variable room layout, frail patient in bed or chair, limited portable equipment, exam and on-the-spot treatment or transfer decision.

Virtual/telehealth acute visit: history taken by video, visual inspection of a rash or throat through the camera, no hands-on examination; NP reaches a diagnosis, e-prescribes, and arranges follow-up.

sources.title: Performance, Safety, and Patient Experience of an Autonomous Robotic Phlebotomy Device: A Multicenter Trial (Clinical Chemistry)
sources.claim: Vitestro's autonomous robotic phlebotomy device draws venous blood from patients in outpatient blood-collection centers with a 94.5% first-stick success rate, but it performs only one sub-step of a diagnostic workup (specimen collection) and does no examination, diagnosis, or treatment.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: venipuncture for laboratory testing, a component of the acute workup in instances 1 and 4. It substantiates autonomous needle placement on a fixtured arm in a structured facility, but not history-taking, physical examination, diagnostic reasoning, prescribing, or wound/injury treatment, so it cannot carry a whole-instance judgment.

sources.developer: Lifeline Robotics (University of Southern Denmark spin-out)
sources.title: Throat swabbing robot developed for COVID-19 testing by Danish startup
sources.claim: Lifeline Robotics built an autonomous throat-swabbing robot using two UR3 arms and machine vision that collects an oropharyngeal specimen from a seated person and caps the sample jar, demonstrating autonomous instrument contact inside a patient's mouth in a fixed test booth.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: point-of-care specimen collection during an acute respiratory illness visit (instances 1 and 2). It shows autonomous contact with a cooperative adult's oropharynx in a purpose-built booth, but no interpretation, diagnosis, or treatment, and no capability with uncooperative children.

sources.developer: Tsinghua University / Beijing Tsinghua Changgung Hospital
sources.title: Beyond hospital reach: Autonomous lightweight ultrasound robot for liver sonography
sources.claim: A 588-gram autonomous cable-driven ultrasound robot with an AI agent acquired standard liver imaging planes and detected pathology on real patients in a hospital ultrasound department, showing autonomous acquisition of one diagnostic imaging modality only.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: bedside diagnostic imaging during an acute abdominal complaint (instances 4 and 5). It substantiates autonomous probe placement on a supine cooperative patient, but covers only image acquisition of one organ, not the encounter's history, exam, decision, or treatment.

sources.title: Robot performs first laparoscopic surgery without human help (ScienceDaily / Johns Hopkins)
sources.claim: The Smart Tissue Autonomous Robot performed laparoscopic intestinal anastomosis suturing on live pigs without human guidance, the leading demonstration of autonomous soft-tissue suturing; it operated on anesthetized, fixtured animals in a research operating room, not on human wounds in a clinic.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: suturing soft tissue, the core motor step of laceration repair (instance 3). Transfer is limited: it is an in-vivo animal study on exposed, immobilized bowel under a surgeon's supervision, with no wound assessment, anesthesia, irrigation, exploration, or dressing, so it does not substantiate completing a laceration-repair encounter.

sources.title: Perceptive Completes World's First Fully Automated Dental Procedure on a Human Using AI-Driven Robotic System
sources.claim: Perceptive reported a single fully automated robotic crown-preparation procedure on a human dental patient in a dental chair; the result is a company claim without peer-reviewed publication, and it covers one planned restorative procedure on a rigid tooth, not acute illness or injury care.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: an automated clinical procedure on a seated human patient (closest analogue to instance 3). Transfer fails: the workpiece is a rigid tooth held in a purpose-built mouthpiece under a pre-planned scan, unlike bleeding, mobile soft tissue requiring anesthesia, exploration, and judgment; autonomy is also unverified.

sources.system: Humanoid robots for laparoscopic surgical tasks (in vivo feasibility study)
sources.title: In vivo feasibility study of humanoid robots in surgery (Nature)
sources.claim: The most recent in-vivo evaluation of humanoid robots performing clinical manipulation tasks required teleoperation, indicating that general-purpose robotic performance of hands-on clinical procedures is not yet autonomous.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: dexterous clinical manipulation on a live subject. Cited only as a negative indicator: state-of-the-art general-purpose robots in clinical procedures remain teleoperated, so they cannot support a positive judgment for any instance.

instances.label: Office/urgent-care visit for acute minor illness (sore throat, URI, sinusitis, suspected UTI): NP takes history, performs focused exam (vitals, otoscopy, pharynx, cervical nodes, lung auscultation, abdominal/CVA palpation), collects or orders point-of-care test (rapid strep swab, urine dip/culture), then prescribes antibiotics/symptomatic therapy, gives patient instructions, or refers if red flags appear.

Chronic primary care condition follow-up, most commonly hypertension: NP re-measures blood pressure (repeat cuff, sometimes manual), performs cardiovascular/edema exam, reviews home readings and labs, titrates medication and writes prescriptions, orders labs/EKG, counsels, and refers to cardiology or nephrology when uncontrolled.

Walk-in retail/urgent care or clinic visit needing on-the-spot treatment: headache evaluation with neuro exam and IM ketorolac or triptan injection, nebulizer treatment for wheeze, IM ceftriaxone, ear lavage; NP must also decide and arrange emergency referral (e.g., thunderclap headache, hypertensive emergency).

Dermatologic complaint: NP inspects and palpates lesion/rash with good lighting (sometimes dermatoscope), often performs an in-office procedure — cryotherapy of a wart or seborrheic keratosis, incision and drainage of an abscess, shave biopsy, intralesional steroid — or prescribes topical/oral therapy and refers suspicious lesions to dermatology.

Virtual/telehealth visit from the NP's clinic workstation for URI, UTI, rash photo, or hypertension refill: history by video, review of patient-reported vitals and images, e-prescribing, and referral arrangement with no hands-on exam.

House-call, home-health, or long-term-care visit: NP travels to a patient's residence or facility room, examines the patient in a cluttered, uncontrolled space (bed or armchair), manages hypertension, UTI, skin breakdown or URI with portable equipment, and treats, prescribes, or arranges transfer/referral.

sources.system: SR-NOCS autonomous swab robot (Franka Emika arm, impedance control)
sources.developer: Technical University of Munich / collaborators (published in Scientific Reports)
sources.title: Autonomous swab robot for naso- and oropharyngeal COVID-19 screening | Scientific Reports
sources.claim: A force-controlled autonomous robot station performed combined naso-/oropharyngeal swabbing on patients in two clinical studies, matching manual sampling results — an autonomous specimen-collection sub-step of an acute-illness visit, not diagnosis, treatment, or referral.
sources.transferJustification: Related task = point-of-care specimen collection during a URI visit. It shows a robot can safely contact a patient's airway autonomously, but covers only one sub-step; it performs no history-taking, no diagnosis, no prescribing, and no referral decision.

sources.title: Robot performs autonomous needle-less injection | Robotics and Automation
sources.claim: An autonomous robotic platform delivered a needle-free intramuscular injection to a person without a healthcare professional involved — an autonomous drug-administration sub-step relevant to in-office injections.
sources.transferJustification: Related task = administering an IM injection in clinic. It substantiates only the injection motion in a single controlled demonstration; there is no evidence of evaluating the patient, choosing the drug, or handling the rest of the encounter.

sources.title: Beyond hospital reach: Autonomous lightweight ultrasound robot for liver sonography (arXiv:2510.08106)
sources.claim: A wearable autonomous ultrasound robot acquired standard liver imaging planes and detected pathology in patients, first deployed in a hospital ultrasound department — autonomous diagnostic imaging on human subjects, still only an imaging sub-step.
sources.transferJustification: Related task = performing a diagnostic exam on a patient in a clinical facility. It shows autonomous, force-safe contact with patients, but is confined to imaging one organ and produces no treatment plan, prescription, or referral.

sources.developer: Synyi AI with Almoosa Health Group (Al-Ahsa, Saudi Arabia)
sources.title: World's first AI medical clinic opens in Saudi Arabia with Dr Hua system | Business Standard
sources.claim: The most advanced 'autonomous' primary-care diagnosis-and-prescribing deployment reported is a screen-based AI system with no physical embodiment, and its plans are reviewed by human physicians before action.
sources.transferJustification: Directly on-task (diagnose and treat primary-care complaints), but it is software on a screen, not a physically embodied machine, and human clinicians verify every plan — so it cannot support a positive robotic judgment.

tasks.label: Perform routine or annual physical examinations.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Adult annual/routine physical in an outpatient primary-care clinic exam room: NP reviews history and vitals, then performs a hands-on head-to-toe exam — HEENT inspection, otoscopy/ophthalmoscopy, thyroid and lymph node palpation, cardiac and pulmonary auscultation, abdominal palpation, extremity/pulse/edema check, skin survey, neuro screen — then counsels the patient and orders labs/screenings and documents findings.

Well-child/well-adolescent visit in a pediatric clinic: length/height, weight, head circumference, developmental and behavioral screening, hands-on exam of a squirming or crying infant or a shy child (otoscopy, red reflex, heart/lung auscultation, hip and abdominal exam, scoliosis check), plus caregiver counseling and immunization orders.

Adult women's health annual exam in a clinic or women's health center: clinical breast exam, pelvic/bimanual exam and speculum insertion with Pap/HPV sample collection, plus the general physical exam and contraception/screening counseling.

Sports pre-participation, pre-employment, DOT, or school physical performed in an occupational health clinic, retail/urgent-care clinic, or a school gym set up as a mass-screening station: vision and hearing screen, vitals, brief cardiopulmonary auscultation, musculoskeletal and range-of-motion exam, hernia check, and completion of a clearance form.

Annual/periodic physical of a nursing home or assisted-living resident at the bedside or in the facility clinic: often frail, contracted, hard-of-hearing, or cognitively impaired patient who must be repositioned or examined in bed or a wheelchair; skin/pressure-area inspection, chest and abdominal exam, edema, functional and cognitive assessment.

Home-based annual physical / Medicare annual wellness visit conducted as a house call in the patient's residence: exam performed on a sofa, kitchen chair, or bed in a cluttered, variable home with pets and family present; portable equipment carried in, plus home-safety and functional assessment.

sources.system: Teleoperated humanoid surrogate (Unitree/bimanual humanoid teleoperation system, UCSD ARCLab)
sources.developer: UC San Diego (ARCLab) with UCSD School of Medicine
sources.title: Humanoids in Hospitals: A Technical Study of Humanoid Robot Surrogates for Dexterous Medical Interventions
sources.claim: The most advanced demonstration of a humanoid robot performing physical-examination maneuvers on patients/manikins (auscultation, abdominal palpation, ultrasound-guided injection) was achieved only through bimanual teleoperation by a human operator, in a lab/simulation setting.
sources.transferJustification: Directly covers components of a routine physical exam (auscultation, abdominal palpation). It shows the state of the art for robot hands-on patient examination is human-in-the-loop teleoperation, not autonomous completion of an exam.

sources.system: Automated robotic auscultation platform (6-DOF cooperative arm with LiDAR/camera)
sources.developer: Ryosuke Tsumura et al. (Waseda University / AIST, Japan)
sources.title: Toward Fully Automated Robotic Platform for Remote Auscultation
sources.claim: Autonomous robotic auscultation exists only as a research prototype that places a stethoscope on a chest to capture heart/lung sounds; it performs one sub-step of an exam, not a complete physical examination, and is evaluated on subjects/phantoms in a laboratory.
sources.transferJustification: Robotic auscultation is one hands-on component of the routine physical exam; the evidence shows only single-sensor placement on a cooperative, still subject is automated, with no history-taking, multi-system exam, or clinical judgment.

sources.system: Lucid Robotic System (NeuralBot / NovaGuide Intelligent Ultrasound)
sources.title: Houston Methodist is first in United States to use robotic ultrasound technology to noninvasively evaluate brain blood flow
sources.claim: The most capable autonomous patient-contact robot in routine hospital use is a single-purpose ultrasound device that finds and insonates cerebral vessels; it performs one measurement, not a general physical examination.
sources.transferJustification: Closest deployed example of an autonomous robot making physical contact with a patient for a diagnostic measurement; it delimits current capability to a single fixed protocol on a still, positioned patient, far short of a whole annual physical exam.

sources.title: Serve Robotics to Acquire Diligent Robotics, Expanding Physical AI Platform Beyond the Sidewalk
sources.claim: The largest deployed fleet of autonomous mobile manipulation robots in US hospitals performs logistics (delivering medications, lab samples, supplies) and does not examine patients.
sources.transferJustification: Shows what autonomous robots actually do in the structured healthcare facilities where these task instances occur: item transport, with clinical patient assessment explicitly left to human staff.

sources.title: Forward Falls Flat: Healthcare Kiosks Take Another Hit
sources.claim: The only commercial attempt at an automated, self-service physical check-up station in the US (an AI kiosk that measured biometrics and ran screenings without a clinician) ceased operations in November 2024, and it never performed a clinician-grade hands-on physical examination.
sources.transferJustification: Directly targeted the automated check-up market; its closure and its limitation to self-service biometrics/lab screens show no fielded machine completes a routine physical examination even in a purpose-built booth.

tasks.label: Perform primary care procedures such as suturing, splinting, administering immunizations, taking cultures, and debriding wounds.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Routine immunization of a cooperative adult/adolescent in a primary care or retail clinic exam room: verify order and vaccine, draw up or take prefilled syringe, position patient, landmark and clean the deltoid, give the IM/SC injection, dispose of the sharp, bandage, observe for reaction.

Well-child immunizations for an infant or young child: 2-4 injections into the vastus lateralis/deltoid at one visit, with a squirming, crying, parent-held child, distraction technique, and rapid sequential injections.

Specimen collection for testing/culture on a seated patient: throat or nasopharyngeal swab for strep/flu/COVID culture or rapid test, or drawing venous blood into culture/lab tubes, then labeling and sending the specimen.

Repair of a simple laceration in a clinic/urgent-care procedure room: assess and explore the wound, infiltrate local anesthetic, irrigate and clean, close with interrupted sutures at appropriate tension, dress the wound.

Splinting/immobilization of a sprain or simple fracture: assess neurovascular status, position the limb, apply padding and a fiberglass/prefabricated splint or buddy tape, mold and wrap, check fit and circulation.

Other minor office procedures on tissue: sharp/mechanical debridement of a chronic diabetic foot or pressure ulcer, abscess incision and drainage, skin lesion shave/punch biopsy, wound or cervical/vaginal swab cultures, and intra-articular or trigger-point injections.

sources.title: Performance, Safety, and Patient Experience of an Autonomous Robotic Phlebotomy Device: A Multicenter Trial
sources.claim: Vitestro's Aletta Autonomous Robotic Phlebotomy Device performed venipuncture autonomously on 1633 routine outpatients across three Dutch hospital phlebotomy departments, with 94.5% first-stick success and 0.6% mild adverse events; the patient places their arm into the device, which disinfects skin, images the vein, inserts the needle, fills tubes and applies a bandage, one professional supervising up to three devices.
sources.transferJustification: Venous blood draw for cultures/labs is itself part of the 'taking cultures' instance; for immunization it is a related task involving the same objects (needle, adult arm, skin prep, bandage) at higher precision (sub-millimetre vein targeting) on ordinary clinic patients, so the needle-in-arm act transfers to intramuscular injection at a fixtured station.

sources.title: Vitestro raises $70m to fuel blood-drawing robot's global commercial readiness
sources.claim: The Vitestro blood-drawing robot holds an EU CE mark and has been placed in hospitals in the Netherlands and ..., i.e. it is a real fielded device rather than a laboratory prototype.
sources.transferJustification: Same transfer as above: establishes that autonomous needle procedures on human arms are performed in real healthcare settings, not only in research demos.

sources.title: Waterloo startup performs first ever robotic intramuscular injection
sources.claim: Cobionix's Cobi platform autonomously located an injection site on a human volunteer and delivered an intramuscular dose using a needle-free jet injector, described by the developer as fully autonomous.

sources.title: InjectMeAI—Software Module of an Autonomous Injection Humanoid
sources.claim: An autonomous humanoid injection module detected the deltoid injection site and drove the arm to it, but achieved only about 80% success, showing that autonomous IM injection targeting is feasible yet not yet at clinician reliability outside a fixtured station.

sources.title: Autonomous swab robot for naso- and oropharyngeal COVID-19 screening
sources.claim: The SR-NOCS autonomous swab robot station took naso- and oropharyngeal swabs from human subjects with a force-controlled arm, a disposable nose/throat fixation device and voice guidance, in two clinical studies (a European hospital during lockdown and later a public testing site).

sources.title: Autonomous Swab Robot for Naso- and Oropharyngeal COVID-19 Screening (ResearchGate record)
sources.claim: In clinical studies of the autonomous swab robot, 52 suspected COVID-19 patients were sampled and the robot-collected specimens agreed completely with manually collected specimens, indicating specimen quality equal to a clinician's.

sources.title: Robot performs first laparoscopic surgery without human help
sources.claim: The Smart Tissue Autonomous Robot autonomously sutured an intestinal anastomosis in live pigs under laparoscopy, the strongest demonstration of autonomous suturing of living tissue; it required an operating-room setup, human-placed fluorescent markers and general anesthesia, and does not perform anesthesia, irrigation or skin closure.
sources.transferJustification: Autonomous suturing of living soft tissue is the closest published analogue to laceration repair, but it is intracorporeal bowel anastomosis in anesthetized animals with human-placed markers, so it does not cover the whole office laceration-repair instance.

sources.system: DLR MIRO with MICA / ERBEJET waterjet debridement system
sources.developer: German Aerospace Center (DLR) and University of Freiburg
sources.title: Robotic waterjet wound debridement – Workflow adaption for clinical application and systematic evaluation of a novel technology
sources.claim: A DLR MIRO robot with a waterjet instrument autonomously planned and executed wound debridement paths, but the systematic evaluation was performed on tissue models in the laboratory rather than on patients' chronic wounds.

tasks.label: Evaluate hearing and balance disorders to determine diagnoses and courses of treatment.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Private-practice/retail audiology clinic, adult diagnostic hearing evaluation: audiologist reviews case history, otoscopy findings, pure-tone air/bone thresholds, speech recognition scores and tympanometry/reflexes, classifies the loss (e.g., bilateral symmetric sensorineural presbycusis vs. conductive component), rules out red flags, and decides the course of treatment (amplification candidacy, medical referral, monitoring) and explains it to the patient.

Pediatric evaluation in a children's hospital or school audiology program: audiologist interprets behavioral (VRA/CPA) or ABR/OAE and middle-ear results in a child with limited cooperation, weighs cross-check consistency and developmental/speech-language history, determines degree/type/configuration of loss, and sets the plan (repeat testing, ENT referral for effusion, amplification, early-intervention referral).

Hospital/ENT clinic complex adult case: asymmetric or sudden sensorineural loss, tinnitus, or retrocochlear concern; audiologist integrates audiometric, ABR, OAE and reflex-decay findings with medical history and imaging status to form a differential diagnosis and recommend urgent otologic referral, further testing, or cochlear implant candidacy evaluation.

Vestibular/balance clinic evaluation: audiologist interprets VNG/caloric, vHIT, rotary chair, VEMP and positional testing results together with symptom history to distinguish BPPV, unilateral vestibular hypofunction, Meniere's disease or central involvement, and determines treatment course (canalith repositioning, vestibular rehab referral, neurology/ENT referral).

Follow-up, monitoring and program contexts: ototoxicity or noise-exposure serial monitoring, occupational hearing-conservation threshold-shift review, post-fitting or cochlear-implant progress review, or remote/tele-audiology record review; audiologist compares results over time, decides whether status has changed and revises the treatment or referral plan.

tasks.label: Fit, dispense, and repair assistive devices, such as hearing aids.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Initial hearing aid fitting/verification appointment in an audiology clinic or ENT office: otoscopy, selecting and attaching the correct dome/receiver-wire length or earmold, placing the BTE/RIC device on the patient's ear, inserting a probe-tube microphone into the ear canal for real-ear measurement, adjusting physical fit for comfort and retention, checking for feedback/slit leak, and hands-on demonstration of insertion/removal to the patient.

In-clinic repair/service of a patient's hearing aid at the bench: inspecting a wax-clogged or dead device, cleaning the shell/ports, replacing wax guards, domes, receivers, tubing, filters or battery doors, retubing or buffing/modifying an earmold shell with a grinder, and verifying output in a test box or with a listening tube before returning it to the patient.

Taking ear impressions in the clinic for a custom earmold or in-the-ear device: otoscopic inspection, placing an otoblock at the correct depth in the ear canal, injecting silicone impression material into canal and concha, waiting for cure, removing the impression along the canal curvature, re-inspecting the canal, and evaluating the impression for acceptability.

Follow-up dispensing/adjustment visits in the clinic: checking physical fit and comfort of an already-dispensed aid, swapping dome or tubing size, shortening/replacing a receiver wire, re-instructing an older patient with limited dexterity on insertion, cleaning the device, and confirming retention and absence of feedback.

Fitting, dispensing, or servicing devices outside the clinic: bedside in a nursing-home resident's room or hospital ward, in a school classroom (FM/DM systems and earmolds for children), or on a home visit — cluttered, variable settings with uncooperative, moving or frail patients and no clinic equipment at hand.

sources.title: First Study in Men Evaluating a Surgical Robotic Tool Providing Autonomous Inner Ear Access for Cochlear Implantation - PubMed
sources.claim: The only robots demonstrated performing autonomous, precise work at the human ear are otologic surgical robots (HEARO) that drill an access tunnel to the cochlea in an operating room with the patient's head rigidly fixed; they do not fit, dispense, or service wearable hearing devices.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic drilling for cochlear implant access. It is the closest robotic work at the ear, but it operates on an anesthetized, head-fixated surgical patient under surgeon supervision and image guidance, and involves no handling of hearing aids, earmolds, domes, probe tubes or impression material, so performance does not carry over to fitting, dispensing or repairing assistive devices.

sources.title: UR5 handles tiny hearing aid components with precision | Universal Robots case story
sources.claim: Robotic automation in the hearing-aid industry is confined to fenced/fixtured factory cells handling new components (e.g., a UR5 removing tiny moulded parts inside an injection-moulding machine at Oticon), not to clinical fitting or repair of patients' devices.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: manufacturing pick-and-place of hearing aid components. Objects are comparable in size, but the robot performs a fixed, fixtured pick from a mould of identical new parts; it does not diagnose faults, disassemble wax-contaminated used devices, replace receivers/tubing, or verify a repaired aid, so it does not substantiate completion of clinical repair even at E1.

sources.title: Flexible Automation | Isthmus Engineering & Manufacturing
sources.claim: Hearing-aid-related robotic packaging work is likewise purpose-built line automation (delta robots placing hearing aid batteries into packaging), unrelated to patient-side dispensing.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: high-speed packaging of hearing aid accessories in a fenced cell. It shows only rigid pick-and-place of uniform parts and has no patient contact or device servicing content, so it does not transfer to fitting, dispensing or repairing devices on patients.

sources.developer: Academic research group (published in J. Clin. Med.)
sources.title: A Novel Ear Impression-Taking Method Using Structured Light Imaging and Machine Learning: A Pilot Proof of Concept Study
sources.claim: Ear impression capture remains a clinician-performed manual procedure; even non-contact alternatives are only research prototypes, and no robotic system takes ear impressions.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: capturing ear canal geometry for custom earmolds. The prototype is a non-robotic imaging device with partial ear-canal matching only, confirming that no embodied system performs the impression instance autonomously.

sources.title: New technology enables fully-remote hearing aid fittings | Sonova International
sources.claim: Automation of hearing aid fitting that has reached deployment is software-based teleaudiology/remote fine-tuning, in which the patient performs all physical handling of the device; no robotic system performs the physical fitting steps.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: remote hearing aid programming. It is software-only (no embodied machine acts on the ear or device), so it cannot support any positive robotic judgment; it is cited to show the fitting instance's physical steps remain human-performed.

tasks.label: Administer hearing tests and examine patients to collect information on type and degree of impairment, using specialized instruments and electronic equipment.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Comprehensive diagnostic audiologic evaluation of a cooperative adult in a clinic sound-treated booth: case history, otoscopic inspection of both ear canals and drums, seating and instructing the patient, placing supra-aural or insert earphones and a bone oscillator, running air- and bone-conduction pure tones with clinical masking decisions, speech reception and word-recognition testing scored live, and recording the audiogram.

Immittance and otoacoustic emission testing as part of a workup in the clinic: selecting an eartip, inserting the probe into the ear canal to obtain a hermetic seal while the patient sits still, running tympanometry, ipsi/contra acoustic reflexes and DPOAE/TEOAE, reseating the probe when a seal or noise problem occurs, and judging validity of the tracings.

Pediatric behavioral evaluation in a clinic booth: visual reinforcement or conditioned play audiometry with an infant or toddler on a caregiver's lap or at a small table, coaxing the child to keep insert earphones or a headband on, conditioning the child, reading head-turn or play responses, and interleaving OAE/tympanometry between bouts of squirming and crying.

Electrophysiologic and vestibular testing in a clinic or hospital suite: abrading and prepping skin, applying electrodes at vertex, mastoids and forehead, checking impedances, placing insert earphones (often on a sleeping or sedated infant), running ABR/ASSR or ECochG, or fitting VNG goggles and performing positional and caloric irrigations, then judging waveform/trace quality.

Bedside or nursery testing with portable equipment: newborn hearing screening (AABR/OAE) on a swaddled infant in a hospital nursery or postpartum room, or diagnostic/screening testing at an inpatient bedside or nursing-home room, working around bedding, tubing, ambient noise and patients who cannot be repositioned to a standard chair.

Off-site screening programs: occupational hearing conservation testing in a mobile audiometric van or plant multi-station booth, school screening in a classroom or gym, or community health-fair screening — otoscopy, transducer placement and screening audiometry/tympanometry on a rapid throughput schedule in a borrowed space.

sources.title: A robot to assist in transcranial magnetic stimulation (TMS / rTMS) — TMS-Robot Features
sources.claim: Axilum Robotics TMS-Robot is a commercial, CE-marked robot that automatically positions a stimulation coil against a seated patient's head under neuronavigation and compensates for head movement — the closest demonstrated robotic capability to placing a transducer on a patient's head in a clinic, but it performs no ear inspection, no ear-canal insertion and no hearing-test administration.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic placement of a transducer against a human head in a clinic. It shows contact positioning on a head is feasible, but audiometric work additionally requires otoscopic assessment, ear-canal probe insertion with a hermetic seal, patient instruction and adaptive behavioral response scoring, none of which this system does; it therefore does not substantiate completion of any instance.

sources.developer: Lifeline Robotics / University of Southern Denmark
sources.title: Throat swabbing robot developed for COVID-19 testing by Danish startup
sources.claim: An autonomous throat-swabbing robot has taken oropharyngeal samples from humans, showing that instrument insertion into a human orifice has been demonstrated robotically — but only as a startup demonstration in the mouth, not ear-canal probe placement or hearing testing.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous insertion of an instrument into a human orifice. Ear-canal work needs otoscopic judgment, a sealed probe fit in a narrow, sensitive, curved canal, and full test administration; a demo-stage oropharyngeal swab does not carry over to completing an audiologic evaluation.

sources.developer: NCHAM (National Center for Hearing Assessment and Management), Utah State University
sources.title: Tele-Audiology Equipment, Technology, and Privacy — Timely Diagnosis and Follow-up: A Resource Guide Supporting Tele-Audiology
sources.claim: In tele-audiology — the most automated remote delivery model in current practice — a human technician physically prepares the patient, performs otoscopy and places the electrodes at the patient site while the audiologist only drives the software remotely; no robot performs the physical portion.
sources.transferJustification: Same task, remote-delivery variant: it documents that the physical acts of this task (otoscopy, electrode and transducer placement on the patient) still require an on-site human, supporting a negative judgment rather than a positive one.

sources.system: TympaHealth all-in-one ear and hearing assessment system
sources.title: Bringing ear clinics to the community — Team Consulting
sources.claim: The leading all-in-one ear-and-hearing assessment platform (video otoscopy, hearing test, microsuction wax removal) is a hand-held smartphone-based device operated by trained human staff; the automation is AI image guidance, not a robot that handles the patient's ear.
sources.transferJustification: Same task domain (ear examination plus hearing test). It shows the state of the art in packaging this task is a human-held instrument, i.e., no robotic system performs the ear examination or transducer placement.

sources.title: GSI AMTAS: Automated Hearing Assessment — AudiologyOnline
sources.claim: Automated audiometry (e.g., GSI AMTAS) can run a threshold test without clinician supervision, but it is software in kiosk mode: a human still sets the patient up with headphones and bone oscillator, and the system is not a physically embodied machine acting on the patient.
sources.transferJustification: Same task's test-presentation sub-step. It is software plus headphones, not a robotic system, and it still depends on a person to place the transducers on the patient, so under the rules it cannot support a positive judgment at any environment tier.

tasks.label: Examine and clean patients' ear canals.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Routine otoscopic examination of a cooperative adult in an audiology clinic exam room before audiometry, immittance testing, or a hearing-aid fitting: pull the pinna, insert a speculum/video otoscope a few millimeters into the canal, inspect canal skin and tympanic membrane, judge whether the view is clear and the ear healthy, and document findings.

Removal of partially occluding, soft-to-moderate cerumen in a cooperative adult in the clinic, using curette, loop, or microsuction under headlight/loupe or microscope, working within millimeters of a sensitive canal wall and the eardrum, then re-examining to confirm a clear canal.

Removal of hard, impacted cerumen in an older adult or long-time hearing-aid wearer with a narrow or tortuous canal: pre-examination to rule out perforation/otitis, softening drops, warm-water irrigation and/or extended microsuction over several passes, monitoring for pain, bleeding, or vertigo, and post-procedure otoscopy.

Examination and wax/debris clearing in a young or uncooperative pediatric patient in a clinic or school hearing-screening room: small moving head, tiny canal, sometimes tympanostomy tubes or drainage, requiring parental holding, coaxing, and quick, gentle work.

Exam and cleaning performed away from the clinic during a mobile/home visit to a homebound patient: patient seated in an armchair or bed, portable otoscope and suction/curette kit, variable lighting, furniture, and improvised positioning.

sources.title: OtoSet by SafKan Health Introduces the First Automated & FDA Cleared Ear Cleaning Device to Manage Earwax Buildup
sources.claim: OtoSet is an FDA-cleared, commercially deployed ear-cleaning system used in hearing-care clinics that runs a machine-controlled irrigation and micro-suction cycle; a clinician places the headset and ear tips on the patient and performs the otoscopic examination and clinical judgment before and after, so the device neither examines the canal nor positions itself.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: powered cerumen removal. It covers only the irrigation/suction sub-step; the device is applied by a clinician and provides no otoscopic examination, no screening for contraindications, and no verification of a clear canal, so it cannot substantiate whole-instance completion.

sources.developer: CASCINATION AG / MED-EL (clinical study by Topsakal et al., Antwerp)
sources.title: First Study in Men Evaluating a Surgical Robotic Tool Providing Autonomous Inner Ear Access for Cochlear Implantation
sources.claim: The most capable autonomous ear robot in clinical use, HEARO, drills a keyhole trajectory to the inner ear for cochlear implantation in an operating room with the anesthetized patient's head clamped, mastoid fiducial screws, and CBCT-based surgeon planning; it does not examine or clean ear canals.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic otologic surgery on the temporal bone. Performance does not carry over: the target is bone behind the canal, the patient is anesthetized with the head clamped and registered to CT, and no otoscopic assessment or cerumen clearance of an awake patient's canal is demonstrated.

sources.title: Robot-Assisted Middle Ear Endoscopic Surgery: Preliminary Results on 37 Patients
sources.claim: RobOtol, the otologic robot used clinically for middle-ear and cochlear-implant procedures in 37 patients, is continuously teleoperated by the surgeon in the operating room rather than autonomous.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: instrument manipulation inside the human ear. It is disqualifying rather than supporting: the state of the art for in-ear robotic manipulation remains continuous surgeon teleoperation, which cannot support autonomous examination or cleaning.

sources.system: SR-NOCS autonomous swab robot (Cartesian impedance-controlled arm)
sources.developer: University of Southern Denmark / Lifeline Robotics
sources.title: Autonomous swab robot for naso- and oropharyngeal COVID-19 screening
sources.claim: SR-NOCS is an autonomous, force-controlled robot station that inserts swabs into the nose and throat of awake seated subjects, validated on 52 patients in two clinical studies; it is the nearest demonstrated autonomous insertion of an instrument into a human body orifice.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous instrument insertion into a body orifice of an awake patient. Transfer fails: the swab enters a wide open mouth or nostril for a sampling stroke with no diagnostic interpretation, whereas ear-canal work needs visual diagnosis and sub-millimetre curette/suction control in a curved 7 mm canal ending at a fragile eardrum.

sources.developer: Research group publishing in Nature Communications (Zhao et al.)
sources.title: Interaction-aware dexterous robot for minimally invasive transcanal inner ear interventions
sources.claim: The most advanced transcanal ear robot reported, a dual-segment continuum robot with endoscopy and a force-sensing microneedle, has been validated only on cadavers and in vivo ..., not on awake clinic patients.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic navigation through the external auditory canal. It shows the frontier is cadaver/animal research aimed at round-window access, with no demonstration of examining or clearing cerumen from a conscious patient's canal.

tasks.label: Plan and conduct treatment programs for patients' hearing or balance problems, consulting with educators, physicians, nurses, psychologists, speech-language pathologists, and other health care personnel, as necessary.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Adult amplification treatment program in an outpatient audiology clinic (private practice or hospital ENT clinic): audiologist plans the rehabilitative plan after diagnostic results, selects and programs hearing aids, takes ear impressions or selects domes, physically places devices and probe-mic tubes for real-ear verification, counsels the patient, sends/receives notes with the referring physician, and adjusts over follow-up visits until the patient accepts the outcome.

Aural rehabilitation program for a cochlear implant or complex hearing-loss patient at a hospital/medical center: audiologist plans post-activation mapping schedule, performs processor programming and coil placement, runs auditory/speech-perception training sessions, and coordinates with the implant surgeon, speech-language pathologist, and psychologist over months.

Pediatric/educational audiology: audiologist plans and carries out a hearing-management program for a school-age child in a school building or pediatric clinic \and remote-microphone/DM systems, verification of the child's hearing devices, listening-skill training, classroom acoustic recommendations, and consultation with teachers, SLPs, school nurses, and parents at IEP meetings.

Tinnitus/hyperacusis or hearing-conservation management program in a private practice: plan of sound therapy and counseling, fitting and programming of sound generators or combination devices in the ear, structured counseling sessions over several visits, and coordination with the patient's physician or psychologist.

Balance/vestibular treatment program in a hospital or balance clinic: audiologist plans treatment after vestibular testing, physically performs canalith repositioning maneuvers (guiding the patient's head and trunk through the Epley/BBQ-roll sequences), prescribes and demonstrates habituation/gaze-stabilization exercises, and coordinates with the neurologist, ENT, or physical therapist.

Treatment program delivered outside a clinic: home visit to a homebound or memory-care patient (mobile audiology) to fit, insert, and troubleshoot hearing devices, train the caregiver, and coordinate with visiting nurses and family in a cluttered, non-standardized living space.

sources.developer: Collin (RobOtol), CAScination/HEARO and others (review by Du et al.)
sources.title: Robotic Systems for Cochlear Implant Surgeries: A Review of Robotic Design and Clinical Outcomes
sources.claim: Best-available otologic robots (RobOtol, HEARO-type systems) are surgeon-controlled assistive platforms for cochlear-implant electrode insertion in an operating room; the review states they remain assistive rather than autonomous. They do not plan or deliver an audiologist's treatment program.
sources.transferJustification: Closest robotic capability acting on the ear in a clinical setting; cited to show that even in a purpose-built OR the robot performs one surgeon-directed sub-step, so it cannot substantiate autonomous planning and delivery of an audiologic treatment program.

sources.system: Affective robot assistant based on Pepper humanoid robot
sources.developer: Research group (International Journal of Social Robotics study)
sources.title: Experience with an Affective Robot Assistant for Children with Hearing Disabilities
sources.claim: A Pepper humanoid social robot was used in a clinical audiology setting with 16 children with hearing aids/cochlear implants, as an engagement and emotion-recognition assistant during gamified audiometry tests and rehabilitation activities; it does not fit devices, perform maneuvers, or manage a treatment program.
sources.transferJustification: Related task (pediatric audiometry/rehabilitation engagement) in the same clinical environment; cited because it is the closest robotic presence in audiologic care, yet it performs no hands-on treatment step and is a research demonstration, so it cannot substantiate completion of this task.

sources.title: Holy Name is 1st hospital to use hunova, innovative technology that helps restore balance
sources.claim: Robotic balance-rehabilitation platforms such as hunova are deployed in hospital rehabilitation departments for assessment and balance training, but they are clinician-programmed exercise devices for lower-limb/trunk sensorimotor rehab, not systems that diagnose the vestibular problem, plan the program, perform repositioning maneuvers, or consult with the care team.
sources.transferJustification: Related task (balance rehabilitation exercise delivery) in a structured hospital facility; cited to test whether the balance-treatment instance could be covered, but the device only executes clinician-prescribed exercise protocols on a patient who is set up and supervised by staff, so it does not complete the instance.

tasks.label: Measure noise levels in workplaces and conduct hearing conservation programs in industry, military, schools, and communities.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Area noise survey of a manufacturing/processing plant: walking the production floor during operations with a calibrated Type 2 sound level meter (plus octave-band analysis), taking readings at machines and worker stations, sketching a noise map, flagging areas above 85 dBA for hearing-protection posting, and writing the survey report.

Personal noise dosimetry: at shift start, clipping dosimeters/microphones to the collars of selected workers in a plant, briefing them, verifying calibration, retrieving units at shift end, downloading and interpreting full-shift TWA data.

Baseline/annual audiometric testing of employees on site in a mobile hearing van or plant sound booth: brief history, otoscopic inspection of ear canals, seating and placing supra-aural or insert earphones on each worker, running the pure-tone test, checking validity, and counseling workers whose thresholds shifted.

Hearing protector work: selecting appropriate earplugs/muffs for a worker and noise level, demonstrating and checking insertion in the worker's ears, running an individual fit test (e.g., field attenuation estimation) and retraining until an adequate personal attenuation rating is achieved; group training sessions on the hearing conservation program.

School/institutional program: pure-tone hearing screening of students in a school health room or gym (placing headphones on children, coaching responses, otoscopy on referrals), plus spot noise checks in shop classes, band rooms, and cafeterias, and teacher/student education.

Field/community and military noise measurement: measuring noise at outdoor or semi-outdoor sites such as a flight line, firing range, shipboard space, construction area, or community property line, including choosing measurement positions and documenting exposures for the hearing conservation program.

sources.date: 2021-03 (trial), updated case study 2024-04; ANYmal X Ex-zone deployment 2024-07
sources.title: Automation and digitalization with ANYmal: the case at BASF
sources.claim: ANYbotics' ANYmal quadruped autonomously runs inspection missions inside BASF's operating Ludwigshafen chemical plant, using a pan-tilt payload to take acoustic (as well as visual and thermal) measurements of equipment at defined inspection points and analyzing the data, returning to its dock without human intervention.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic acoustic condition-monitoring rounds. It carries over to a plant noise survey because the robot autonomously traverses the same environment (an operating industrial facility with stairs, walkways and running machinery), positions an acoustic sensor at specified measurement points, and logs/analyzes the readings — the same physical acts as a walk-around sound-level survey, differing mainly in sensor calibration and reporting software.

sources.title: Robot dogs revolutionize industrial maintenance | Siemens
sources.claim: ANYmal collects data from hundreds of inspection ... on its own and its acoustic sensors measure audible as well as ultrasonic frequencies, with captured data integrated and interpreted automatically for facility operators.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous acoustic/thermal inspection rounds. Shows the acoustic payload covers the audible band used for occupational noise measurement and that route execution and data capture at many defined points are autonomous, which is what a plant noise survey requires.

sources.system: Boston Dynamics Spot with Fluke SV600 acoustic imager
sources.title: Fluke Process Instruments SV600 Fixed Acoustic Imager now fully integrated with Boston Dynamics' Spot robot
sources.claim: Fluke's SV600 acoustic imager is integrated as a payload on Boston Dynamics' Spot, letting industrial maintenance teams capture acoustic inspection data in plants where sending people is undesirable; Spot performs route-based industrial inspections.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic acoustic imaging inspection. Supports (but does not by itself establish, since triggering appears operator-initiated) the availability of commercial acoustic-measurement payloads on legged robots working in industrial facilities.

sources.system: Boston Dynamics Spot with Trimble X7 / FieldLink
sources.title: Trimble Releases Turnkey Autonomous Robotic Scanning Solution
sources.claim: Trimble sells a turnkey solution pairing Spot with the X7 3D laser scanner for autonomous data-capture missions on active construction sites, i.e. route-following sensor data collection in an as-found outdoor/unstructured setting.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous instrument-carrying survey rounds on a jobsite. Shows legged robots can autonomously repeat measurement routes outside controlled plants, relevant to field noise measurement, though the demonstrated payload is a laser scanner rather than a sound level meter.
