roles.title: Anesthesiologists
aliases: DO Physician (Doctor of Osteopathic Medicine Physician)
roles.description: Administer anesthetics and analgesics for pain management prior to, during, or after surgery.

tasks.label: Examine patient, obtain medical history, and use diagnostic tests to determine risk during surgical, obstetrical, and other medical procedures.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Day-of-surgery preanesthesia evaluation in the hospital/ASC preoperative holding area of a healthy or mildly ill adult (ASA 1-2) for an elective case: review chart, labs and ECG, interview the patient about history, medications, allergies, fasting and prior anesthesia, perform a focused exam (airway/Mallampati, dentition, heart and lung auscultation, IV sites), then assign ASA class, judge risk and set the anesthetic plan.

Day-of-surgery or same-week evaluation of a medically complex adult (ASA 3-4: coronary disease, heart failure, COPD, morbid obesity with OSA, dialysis, frailty): detailed history often from an unreliable or poorly documented patient, focused cardiopulmonary and airway exam, interpretation of ECG, echo, stress test and labs, decision on further testing or postponement, and documented risk stratification.

Preanesthesia testing clinic visit days to weeks before surgery: comprehensive history and physical, ordering and interpreting diagnostic tests (labs, ECG, imaging, pulmonary function), consulting specialists, medication optimization, and a written risk assessment used to schedule and plan the anesthetic.

Obstetric evaluation on labor and delivery before epidural or cesarean: history taken from a laboring, uncomfortable and sometimes distressed patient under time pressure, airway and lumbar spine/back exam, review of platelet count/coags and fetal status, and rapid risk judgment for neuraxial versus general anesthesia.

Urgent/emergent evaluation in the emergency department, trauma bay or ICU: patient may be altered, sedated, intubated or uncooperative; history pieced together from records, EMS and family; rapid airway, volume-status and hemodynamic assessment plus point-of-care labs and imaging to judge anesthetic risk within minutes.

Evaluation for non-operating-room or pediatric anesthesia (endoscopy suite, cath lab, MRI, dental or office-based surgery): brief screening evaluation, often of a child accompanied by a parent or of an outpatient with sleep apnea, including recent-URI and NPO assessment, airway exam of a possibly uncooperative patient, and a sedation-risk decision.

sources.system: Autonomous robotic auscultation system (Zhu, Smith & Hauser)
sources.title: Automated Heart and Lung Auscultation in Robotic Physical Examinations | IEEE Journals & Magazine | IEEE Xplore
sources.claim: A robot arm autonomously selects auscultation locations and acquires diagnostic-quality heart and lung sounds on human subjects, but only as a laboratory demonstration on a few healthy volunteers; it performs no history taking, airway exam, or risk determination.
sources.transferJustification: Auscultation is one physical sub-step of the anesthesiologist's preoperative exam; it marks the frontier of autonomous robotic physical examination, covering only sound acquisition on healthy volunteers, not the whole evaluation or the risk judgment.

sources.developer: Technical University of Munich (Berlet et al.)
sources.title: Toward telemedical diagnostics—clinical evaluation of a robotic examination system for emergency patients
sources.claim: A robotic telemedical examination cabin with robotic arms was clinically evaluated on emergency patients, but the examination (auscultation, percussion, palpation) is performed by a physician teleoperating the arms from a remote cockpit.
sources.transferJustification: This is the closest system to a robot performing a whole clinical patient examination in a hospital, and it is human-controlled throughout, so it cannot support an autonomous judgment for the examination component of this task.

sources.system: Unitree G1 humanoid clinical teleoperation system
sources.developer: UC San Diego ARCLab / UC San Diego Health
sources.title: Humanoids in Hospitals: A Technical Study of Humanoid Surrogates for Dexterous Medical Interventions
sources.claim: A humanoid robot was evaluated on hospital clinical tasks including physical examination (auscultation, abdominal palpation), ultrasound and airway procedures, entirely under bimanual teleoperation by a human operator.
sources.transferJustification: Humanoid physical examination of patients is the nearest analogue to the exam component of preanesthetic assessment; the study establishes that such exams currently require continuous teleoperation.

sources.system: Fully autonomous robotic ultrasound system for thyroid scanning
sources.developer: Su et al., Nature Communications (Chinese university consortium)
sources.title: A fully autonomous robotic ultrasound system for thyroid scanning - PubMed
sources.claim: A fully autonomous robotic ultrasound ... scans the thyroid region of human subjects without human assistance, showing autonomy is achievable only for a narrowly scoped imaging exam of one body region.
sources.transferJustification: Diagnostic image acquisition is a related physical clinical task; it shows autonomy exists for tightly scoped single-organ imaging, not for a multi-part physical examination combined with history taking and anesthetic risk determination.

sources.title: Performance, Safety, and Patient Experience of an Autonomous Robotic Phlebotomy Device: A Multicenter Trial
sources.claim: An autonomous robotic phlebotomy device performs venipuncture on patients in outpatient blood-draw departments with one supervising staff member per three devices, i.e. autonomy for a single narrowly scoped specimen-collection step.
sources.transferJustification: Blood sampling supports the 'use diagnostic tests' element of the task; it demonstrates that today's autonomous clinical robots handle one bounded physical procedure and produce no clinical history, examination findings, or risk stratification.

sources.title: Towards expert-level autonomous carotid ultrasonography with large-scale learning-based robotic system - PubMed
sources.claim: A learning-based robot performs autonomous carotid ultrasound at reported expert level, again a single-region imaging workflow rather than a clinical patient evaluation.
sources.transferJustification: Autonomous acquisition of a diagnostic study in a clinical room is the related task; it bounds current autonomy to protocolized imaging of one anatomic region and does not extend to bedside history, airway exam, and anesthetic risk assignment.

tasks.label: Administer anesthetic or sedation during medical procedures, using local, intravenous, spinal, or caudal methods.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Elective surgery in a hospital OR or ambulatory surgery center, adult ASA I-III patient with an IV already sited: anesthesiologist gives the IV induction bolus (hypnotic, opioid, neuromuscular blocker) and then titrates IV/infused anesthetic through the case to depth-of-anesthesia and hemodynamic targets until emergence.

Routine procedural sedation/MAC for a healthy adult (screening colonoscopy or EGD in an endoscopy suite, dental/oral-surgery or minor office procedure): IV in place, titrated propofol or midazolam/opioid sedation to a comfortable, cooperative, spontaneously breathing patient for 15-45 minutes.

Neuraxial anesthesia: spinal for cesarean delivery or joint arthroplasty, labor epidural on the L&D unit, or pediatric caudal block — palpate/ultrasound landmarks, position the patient, advance a needle to the intrathecal or epidural/caudal space, confirm placement, and inject local anesthetic.

Local infiltration and ultrasound-guided peripheral nerve blocks (interscalene, adductor canal, TAP, axillary) done in a block bay or OR on an awake or lightly sedated patient: scan, identify nerve and vessels, advance needle millimetres from the nerve, aspirate, and inject in divided doses.

High-risk, emergent, or uncooperative cases: trauma/emergency rapid-sequence induction in an unstable patient, ASA IV cardiac or cath-lab/IR sedation in a frail elderly patient, or inhalational/IV induction in a struggling child with difficult venous access — dosing improvised moment to moment around hemodynamic collapse or patient movement.

sources.system: Automated anesthesia control system (University of Fukui / Japanese closed-loop TIVA system)
sources.developer: University of Fukui Hospital, Department of Anesthesiology and Reanimatology (Nagata, Shigemi et al.)
sources.title: Safety and efficacy of an automated anesthesia delivery system for total intravenous anesthesia with propofol, remifentanil, and rocuronium: a non-inferiority randomized controlled trial versus manually controlled anesthesia
sources.claim: A closed-loop automated anesthesia delivery system administered propofol, remifentanil and rocuronium for total intravenous anesthesia in real operating rooms and was non-inferior to anesthesiologists at keeping patients adequately anesthetized, with no difference in adverse events.

sources.title: Closed-loop systems for automated hypnotic drug delivery during general anaesthesia: a systematic review and meta-analysis (British Journal of Anaesthesia)
sources.claim: Pooled randomized evidence through 2026 shows closed-loop machines controlling hypnotic infusion during general anesthesia outperform clinician-directed titration for control of anesthetic depth.

sources.developer: PGIMER Chandigarh (G.D. Puri et al.), India
sources.title: A Multicenter Evaluation of a Closed-Loop Anesthesia Delivery System: A Randomized Controlled Trial
sources.claim: A patented closed-loop anesthesia delivery system automatically titrated propofol during both induction and maintenance of general anesthesia for adults undergoing major surgery in a six-site randomized trial in hospital operating rooms.

sources.title: A technical description of a novel pharmacological anesthesia robot (Journal of Clinical Monitoring and Computing)
sources.claim: McSleepy, described in the peer-reviewed literature as a pharmacological anesthesia robot, closed-loop controls hypnosis, analgesia and neuromuscular blockade across induction, maintenance and emergence of general anesthesia.

sources.title: FDA Grants Premarket Approval (PMA) For The SEDASYS System For Healthy Patients Undergoing Sedation During Routine Colonoscopy And EGD Procedures
sources.claim: The SEDASYS computer-assisted personalized sedation machine received FDA premarket approval to deliver IV propofol itself for initiation and maintenance of minimal-to-moderate ... in healthy adults during colonoscopy and EGD, i.e. in place of an anesthesia professional.

sources.developer: Ethicon Endo-Surgery / Johnson & Johnson (Pambianco et al.)
sources.title: Computer-assisted personalized sedation for upper endoscopy and colonoscopy: a comparative, multicenter randomized study
sources.claim: In a multicenter randomized trial in endoscopy units, machine-delivered computer-assisted personalized sedation produced sedation comparable to standard clinician sedation with higher patient and clinician satisfaction.

sources.title: Johnson & Johnson bails on Sedasys anesthesia device - MassDevice
sources.claim: The SEDASYS sedation machine was marketed only briefly and withdrawn in 2016 for commercial reasons, so no approved automated sedation machine is currently sold in the US.

sources.title: Technical communication: First robotic ultrasound-guided nerve blocks in humans using the Magellan system
sources.claim: The only reported robotic ultrasound-guided nerve blocks in humans were performed with a joystick-driven robotic arm under continuous physician control, not autonomously.
sources.transferJustification: Related task (regional/neuraxial needle placement with injection of local anesthetic); shows the state of the art for robotic block placement is teleoperated, so it cannot support autonomous completion.

sources.developer: Johns Hopkins University (Margalit, Phalen, Taylor, Armand, Jain et al.)
sources.title: Autonomous Spinal Robotic System for Transforaminal Lumbar Epidural Injections: A Proof of Concept of Study
sources.claim: Autonomous robotic placement of spinal (transforaminal epidural) injections has been demonstrated only in a lumbar spine phantom, not in living patients.
sources.transferJustification: Closest robotic analogue to caudal/epidural anesthetic injection; phantom-only performance cannot substantiate needle placement in a live patient at clinician quality.

sources.system: Automated venipuncture device (Rutgers/VascuLogic-type portable venipuncture robot)
sources.developer: Rutgers University / Mount Sinai collaborators (Leipheimer, Balter, Yarmush et al.)
sources.title: First-in-human evaluation of a hand-held automated venipuncture device for rapid venous blood draws
sources.claim: An autonomous image-guided venipuncture robot has been tested first-in-human for blood draws with 87% overall success, but remains a research prototype rather than a deployed clinical device.
sources.transferJustification: Related task (establishing the intravenous route). Shows automated needle-into-vein access in humans exists only as a prototype, so the IV route itself is normally established by nursing staff before the drug-administration instance begins.

tasks.label: Record type and amount of anesthesia and patient condition throughout procedure.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

tasks.label: Monitor patient before, during, and after anesthesia and counteract adverse reactions or complications.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Hospital OR, routine elective general anesthesia (ASA I–II, e.g., laparoscopic cholecystectomy, joint replacement): continuous vigilance over ECG, BP, SpO2, capnography, airway pressures, anesthetic depth and neuromuscular block; recognizing and treating intraoperative hypotension, hypertension, tachycardia, light anesthesia, bronchospasm, hypoxemia, circuit/tube problems by adjusting the machine, giving bolus drugs/vasopressors, repositioning the airway.

Monitored anesthesia care / procedural sedation in an endoscopy suite, cath lab, interventional radiology, or eye/office surgical suite: titrating sedation while watching ventilation and oxygenation, and rescuing the patient from apnea, airway obstruction or desaturation with chin lift/jaw thrust, oral airway, mask ventilation, and occasionally converting to general anesthesia.

High-risk or complex case (cardiac, major vascular, trauma, transplant, pediatric, ASA III–IV) in a hospital OR: invasive monitoring including arterial line/TEE, managing hemorrhage, arrhythmias, vasoactive infusions, transfusion, and rare crises such as anaphylaxis, malignant hyperthermia or cardiac arrest with ACLS.

Emergence, extubation and immediate post-anesthesia recovery in OR and PACU: assessing reversal of neuromuscular block, deciding on and performing extubation, handoff, then monitoring for hypoventilation, airway obstruction, hypoxemia, hypotension, pain, PONV, shivering, delirium, and treating them (drugs, oxygen, airway maneuvers, occasional reintubation).

Preoperative and induction period in the preop holding area and OR: reviewing history, applying monitors, obtaining baseline vitals, preoxygenating, watching the patient through IV or inhalational induction and intubation, and treating induction hypotension, bradycardia, laryngospasm or difficult airway events.

Labor and delivery unit, obstetric neuraxial anesthesia: monitoring maternal blood pressure and block level after epidural/spinal dosing and during cesarean delivery, treating hypotension with vasopressors and fluids, managing high block, local anesthetic toxicity, nausea, and fetal heart-rate consequences.

sources.developer: G.D. Puri / PGIMER Chandigarh (multicenter Indian trials)
sources.title: Evaluation of Automated Delivery of Propofol Using a Closed-Loop Anesthesia Delivery System in Patients Undergoing Thoracic Surgery: A Randomized Controlled Study - PubMed
sources.claim: Bispectral-index-guided closed-loop anesthesia delivery systems autonomously titrate propofol infusion during surgery in hospital operating rooms, but control only depth of hypnosis (one sub-step of intraoperative management) while an anesthesiologist remains present and responsible for everything else.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated titration of anesthetic depth. It bears on this task because titrating drug in response to monitored signals is one of the countermeasures an anesthesiologist applies, but it covers only hypnotic depth, not the broader monitoring and rescue repertoire.

sources.developer: Joosten/Rinehart et al. (Erasme Hospital, UC Irvine)
sources.title: Automated closed-loop versus manually controlled norepinephrine infusion in patients undergoing intermediate- to high-risk abdominal surgery: a randomised controlled trial - ScienceDirect
sources.claim: A closed-loop vasopressor controller autonomously titrated a norepinephrine infusion to correct intraoperative hypotension in patients undergoing abdominal surgery in the operating room, outperforming manual titration on time in target MAP range.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated treatment of one adverse reaction (hypotension). It transfers only partially: it counteracts a single, well-instrumented complication in the same OR setting, but does not perform the general vigilance or other rescues the task requires.

sources.title: Johnson & Johnson To Stop Selling Sedasys System - Anesthesia Experts
sources.claim: The only US-marketed automated sedation device, SEDASYS, was FDA-approved for mild-to-moderate propofol sedation in healthy adults for endoscopy only, required an anesthesia professional to be available, and was withdrawn from the market by Johnson & Johnson in 2016.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated procedural sedation with automatic drug reduction on signs of oversedation. It is the closest commercial analogue to the MAC instance, but it was restricted to healthy adults for endoscopy, could not perform airway rescue, and is no longer marketed.

sources.title: SEDASYS(®), airway, oxygenation, and ventilation: anticipating and managing the challenges - PubMed
sources.claim: SEDASYS's FDA approval was explicitly limited to mild-to-moderate sedation for colonoscopy and EGD, and the airway, oxygenation and ventilation challenges it creates must be anticipated and managed by clinicians.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated sedation delivery. Shows the device offloads drug titration but leaves airway rescue — the decisive physical countermeasure in the sedation instance — to human clinicians.

sources.title: Feasibility study on full closed-loop control ventilation (IntelliVent-ASV™) in ICU patients with acute respiratory failure - PubMed
sources.claim: A commercially available full closed-loop ventilation mode automatically adjusts ventilation and oxygenation settings (including FiO2 and PEEP) to targets in ICU and post-cardiac-surgery patients, i.e., one automated countermeasure for hypoxemia/hypercapnia, under clinician supervision.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated ventilator management. Ventilator adjustment is one countermeasure used during and after anesthesia, but the device does not monitor the patient globally, examine the airway, or administer drugs.

sources.title: Artificial Intelligence in Anesthesia: Enhancing Precision, Safety, and Global Access Through Data-Driven Systems (J. Clin. Med.)
sources.claim: Contemporary reviews of AI and closed-loop anesthesia state that these systems augment rather than replace clinicians and that human supervision remains essential; no fully autonomous perioperative monitoring-and-rescue system exists in practice.
sources.transferJustification: State-of-the-field review used as negative evidence: it establishes that the automated systems cited above are supervised adjuncts covering single variables, not whole-task substitutes.

sources.title: Closed-Loop Anesthesia: Advances in Automated Drug Delivery and Perioperative Monitoring - PMC
sources.claim: A 2026 review of closed-loop anesthesia concludes that even with combined control of anesthetics, fluids and blood pressure drugs, human supervision remains essential for ... anesthesia care.
sources.transferJustification: Negative evidence current to the rating date: confirms that no deployed system performs autonomous whole-task perioperative monitoring and complication management.

sources.transferJustification: Related task: securing the airway, the key rescue maneuver when anesthesia causes apnea or obstruction. Evidence is preclinical/prototype, so it cannot substantiate worker-quality completion of airway rescue in patients.

tasks.label: Position patient on operating table to maximize patient comfort and surgical accessibility.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Supine positioning for routine general/laparoscopic surgery under general anesthesia: patient scoots onto the OR table or is slide-board transferred, arms abducted <90 degrees on padded arm boards or tucked at the sides with a draw sheet, head on a foam donut with eyes taped, heels and elbows padded, safety strap over thighs, table height/tilt set for surgical access after induction.

Lithotomy and/or steep Trendelenburg for gynecologic, urologic, colorectal or robotic-assisted surgery: legs lifted simultaneously into candy-cane or boot stirrups with hips/knees flexed and peroneal nerve protected, anti-slide gel pad or shoulder supports placed, arms tucked, then steep head-down tilt with re-verification of ETT position and pressure points.

Lateral decubitus positioning for thoracic, hip or renal surgery: team log-roll of the anesthetized patient onto the side while the anesthesiologist controls head/airway, axillary roll placed, beanbag or hip positioners, dependent arm on arm board and non-dependent arm on padded support, head/neck kept in axial alignment, table flexed/kidney rest raised.

Prone positioning for spine or posterior fossa surgery: coordinated log-roll from stretcher onto Wilson frame/Jackson table with the anesthesiologist protecting the airway and lines, chest rolls or bolsters placed, face in prone headrest with repeated eye and pressure checks, arms tucked or 'superman' with shoulders <90 degrees, breasts/genitalia and abdomen freed.

Sitting/beach-chair, semi-Fowler or ramped positioning: shoulder or craniotomy beach-chair setup with head holder and body straps, or ramped 'ear-to-sternal-notch' positioning of an obese or difficult-airway patient before induction, with blankets/ramp devices built up and arms supported to prevent slide.

Positioning an awake patient for neuraxial anesthesia and then on the table: coaching and physically supporting a laboring, frail or arthritic patient into sitting-flexed or lateral position for spinal/epidural, then settling them supine on the OR table with left uterine displacement wedge or limb supports.

sources.title: AI Robots Could Ease Japan's Elderly Care Crisis by 2030
sources.claim: AIREC, a 150-kg AI-driven humanoid, was shown in a Tokyo lab rolling a supine person onto their side (a bed-repositioning maneuver) — the closest robotic analog to arranging an unconscious adult's body; it remains a laboratory demonstration with a cooperative, non-anesthetized subject and no padding, airway or pressure-point management.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: repositioning a person lying on a bed. It is the nearest demonstrated robotic manipulation of a whole human body, so it bounds what is possible for turning/log-rolling an anesthetized surgical patient; it falls short because the subject is healthy and cooperative, the setting is a lab bed, and no padding, line/airway protection or nerve-injury checks are performed.

sources.title: Japan tests AIREC robot to roll patients, easing caregiving challenges
sources.claim: The same AIREC system is explicitly pre-commercial: its developers estimate readiness for nursing or medical facilities only around 2030, so no deployed robot performs whole-body patient handling today.
sources.transferJustification: Same related task (bed repositioning of a person); cited to date the maturity of the frontier system rather than to substantiate completion.

sources.title: Medicaroid Launches the SOT-100 Vercia, Operating Table with the Function to Move Patients Widely
sources.claim: The SOT-100 Vercia robotic operating table, commercially sold in Japan since 2017, moves the tabletop (with the patient already lying on it) between stored positions such as the anesthesia, surgical and fluoroscopy positions; the motions are commanded by staff at a control panel and the system does not transfer, arrange or pad the patient's body.
sources.transferJustification: Directly related: machine-controlled patient positioning in an operating room. It shows that the only machine-controlled 'positioning' in ORs is operator-commanded tabletop motion of a patient humans have already placed and secured, not the body arrangement, padding and transfer the anesthesiologist performs.

sources.title: CIVCO Announces FDA 510(k) Clearance of Protura Robotic Patient Positioning System Integration with Varian Clinac iX and Trilogy Linacs
sources.claim: Protura is an FDA-cleared, clinically installed robotic patient positioning system that applies six-degree-of-freedom couch corrections with sub-millimeter accuracy; it repositions a patient who has already been placed and immobilized on the couch by therapists and does not manipulate limbs or place padding.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: positioning a patient on a treatment couch in a purpose-built radiotherapy vault. Same object (a human on a table) and higher geometric precision, but the robot only moves a couch top holding an already-immobilized, conscious patient, so it cannot substantiate transferring, log-rolling, limb-arranging or padding an anesthetized surgical patient.

sources.system: Intelligent fracture reduction robot system (UR16e arm + NDI Polaris navigation)
sources.developer: Beijing Jishuitan Hospital / Beijing Rossum Robotics
sources.title: Robot-assisted closed reduction of femoral shaft fractures: a prospective controlled study
sources.claim: In the most autonomous robotic OR procedure reported to date — an intelligent fracture-reduction robot that automatically executes a planned reduction path on anesthetized patients — the patient is still positioned on the operating table by the clinical team before the robot acts, and the robot manipulates only bone fragments via pins.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic manipulation of an anesthetized patient's limb segments in a real operating room. It is the closest in-OR robotic handling of a patient's body, yet the whole-body positioning on the table remains a human task, showing the anesthesiologist's positioning task is not performed by any fielded system.

sources.title: Humanoid Robot RHP Friends: Seamless Combination of Autonomous and Teleoperated Tasks in a Nursing Context
sources.claim: Humanoid robots developed for physical nursing assistance combine limited autonomy with teleoperation for the human-contact portions of care tasks, indicating that robot handling of human bodies is not yet autonomous.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: physical nursing assistance involving contact with a person. Shows that state-of-the-art humanoids performing patient-contact care rely on teleoperation, which cannot support a positive judgment for autonomous patient positioning.

tasks.label: Provide and maintain life support and airway management and help prepare patients for emergency surgery.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Emergency rapid-sequence induction and tracheal intubation in the OR or pre-op holding area: unstable, full-stomach patient for urgent surgery; anesthesiologist preoxygenates, applies monitors, gives induction and paralytic drugs, performs laryngoscopy and tube placement, confirms with capnography, secures the tube and sets up mechanical ventilation.

Trauma-bay / ED resuscitation before emergency laparotomy or craniotomy: airway secured amid blood, vomit, cervical collar and a crowded team; large-bore IV/IO access, blood product and fluid resuscitation, ventilation and vasopressor support while the patient is readied for the OR.

Stabilizing and transporting a critically ill patient (ICU or ED) to the OR for emergency surgery: placing arterial/central lines and monitors, starting and titrating vasopressor and sedation infusions, hand-ventilating or transport-ventilating, moving the bed through corridors and elevators, handing over in the OR.

Code blue / cardiac arrest response elsewhere in the hospital (ward room, radiology suite, endoscopy): bag-mask ventilation, intubation during ongoing chest compressions, drug administration and ACLS participation in a cramped, cluttered space around the patient's bed.

Difficult or failed airway rescue: distorted anatomy (airway tumor, facial trauma, morbid obesity, angioedema); escalation through video laryngoscopy, supraglottic airway, awake flexible-scope intubation, or emergency front-of-neck access (cricothyrotomy) with the surgical team standing by.

sources.title: Evaluation of a Novel, Image-Guided Robotic Intubation Platform for Difficult Airways: A Prospective Observational Study — Anesthesia & Analgesia
sources.claim: Spiro-VISTA, the most advanced clinical airway robot, is a handheld device whose steerable intubation scope is driven by a clinician with a joystick; it assists a human intubator rather than performing intubation on its own.
sources.transferJustification: Directly the airway-management step of this task; shows the state of the art in clinical airway robotics is operator-driven, not autonomous.

sources.developer: UC Santa Barbara (Hawkes lab) / Stanford collaborators
sources.title: UCSB-designed soft robot intubation device could save lives — The Current, UC Santa Barbara
sources.claim: The UCSB soft robotic intubation system self-navigates a tube into the trachea, but it is a hand-held device inserted and operated by a human user, and testing was in manikins and cadavers, not live emergency patients.
sources.transferJustification: Same procedure (endotracheal intubation), but the robotic element is a self-guiding tube tip used by a human provider; no system autonomously manages a patient's airway end to end.

sources.title: The Kepler Intubation System — Anesthesia & Analgesia
sources.claim: The Kepler Intubation System, the first robotic intubation system tested in patients, was joystick-controlled by an anesthesiologist; its 'semiautomated' mode merely replayed a previously recorded human maneuver.
sources.transferJustification: Directly the intubation step; demonstrates that in-patient robotic intubation has been teleoperated or scripted replay, which cannot support a positive autonomy judgment.

sources.title: Performance, Safety, and Patient Experience of an Autonomous Robotic Phlebotomy Device: A Multicenter Trial — Clinical Chemistry
sources.claim: An autonomous robotic phlebotomy device performs needle insertion and blood collection without a human operator and is CE-marked and deployed in European hospitals, but only on cooperative seated patients presenting an arm at a fixed draw station.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: percutaneous vascular access, a sub-step of preparing a patient. Transfer fails here — the device works on a still, cooperative, positioned arm in an outpatient draw booth, not on a hypotensive, moving emergency patient, and it neither manages an airway nor titrates therapy.

sources.date: 2013 (ARDS study); commercially in ICU use through 2026
sources.title: Comparison of an entirely automated ventilation mode, Intellivent-ASV, with conventional ventilation in ARDS patients: a 48-hour study — PMC
sources.claim: Fully closed-loop ventilation modes automatically adjust ventilator settings for already-intubated ICU patients, showing that maintenance of mechanical ventilation can be machine-controlled once a human has established the airway and connected the circuit.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: maintaining ventilatory life support. It automates one sub-step (gas delivery settings) on an already-secured airway; it cannot intubate, suction, resuscitate, place lines, or move the patient.

sources.title: Evaluation of Automated Delivery of Propofol Using a Closed-Loop Anesthesia Delivery System in Patients Undergoing Thoracic Surgery: A Randomized Controlled Study — ScienceDirect
sources.claim: Closed-loop anesthesia delivery systems can titrate intravenous anesthetic automatically during surgery under anesthesiologist supervision, automating drug dosing but no other part of perioperative management.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated titration of anesthetic drugs, a sub-step of life support. It runs through pre-placed IV lines in an elective OR with a clinician present, and performs no physical airway or resuscitation actions.

sources.system: Autonomous mobile robot-assisted tracheal intubation system
sources.title: Preoperative positioning of robot-assisted tracheal intubation system in intensive care unit — Journal of Robotic Surgery
sources.claim: Research on mobile intubation robots has so far addressed only autonomous navigation and pre-procedure positioning of the robot at the bedside; the intubation itself remains robot-assisted under human control.
sources.transferJustification: Directly related to bedside airway management, but the autonomous component is only driving to and aligning at the bed, not securing an airway or supporting a patient.

instances.label: Preoperative evaluation (pre-anesthesia clinic or day-of-surgery holding area): the anesthesiologist reviews the chart, prior notes, labs, ECG, echo and imaging reports, interviews the patient, and performs a focused airway/cardiopulmonary assessment to identify or confirm illnesses bearing on anesthesia — undiagnosed obstructive sleep apnea, aortic stenosis, poorly controlled diabetes, anemia, difficult airway anatomy — and assigns an ASA physical status. Output is a documented diagnostic assessment and plan.

Intraoperative diagnosis of an acute deterioration in a hospital OR: the anesthesiologist interprets monitor waveforms (ECG, pulse oximetry, capnography, arterial line), point-of-care labs/ABG, and sometimes TEE or ultrasound to determine the cause of hypotension, hypoxemia, rising end-tidal CO2 or rash — distinguishing e.g. anaphylaxis from bronchospasm, hypovolemia from tamponade, malignant hyperthermia from sepsis — under time pressure.

Postoperative/PACU diagnostic assessment: evaluating delayed emergence, residual neuromuscular blockade, opioid-induced respiratory depression, postoperative myocardial injury, or nerve-block complications using bedside examination, twitch monitoring, ECG, troponin and other labs, and radiology reports.

ICU or critical-care consultation by an anesthesiologist-intensivist: synthesizing exam findings, ventilator data, cultures, labs, and imaging reports to diagnose sepsis, ARDS, shock subtype, or acute kidney injury in an admitted patient.

Chronic pain clinic consultation: diagnosing the source of pain (lumbar radiculopathy, facet arthropathy, CRPS, neuropathy) from history, focused neuromusculoskeletal examination, MRI/EMG reports, and results of diagnostic nerve blocks.

Obstetric anesthesia on labor and delivery: diagnosing conditions such as post-dural-puncture headache, high/total spinal, local anesthetic systemic toxicity, or complications of preeclampsia/HELLP, using bedside examination, vital-sign trends, and laboratory reports.

tasks.label: Teach anesthesiology principles to residents.

tasks.label: Conduct medical research to aid in controlling and curing disease, to investigate new medications, and to develop and test new medical techniques.

instances.label: Academic anesthesiologist runs an IRB-approved randomized trial in the OR/PACU: screens and consents a surgical patient, administers the investigational anesthetic/analgesic or comparator per randomization while managing the anesthetic, draws timed blood samples for pharmacokinetics, records hemodynamic and recovery outcomes, and adjudicates adverse events.

Desk-based scholarship in an academic office: writing the study protocol and IRB/FDA submissions, extracting and statistically analyzing registry or EHR/perioperative-database data, preparing manuscripts, grant applications and review responses.

Wet-bench / translational work in a university research lab: culturing cells or neurons, running ELISA/western/qPCR assays and dose-response screens on candidate analgesic or anesthetic compounds, processing and banking trial-derived blood and tissue specimens.

Preclinical animal study in a vivarium or animal OR: anesthetizing rodents or swine, dosing a new agent, instrumenting and monitoring physiology, performing behavioral nociception or injury-model procedures, collecting blood and terminal tissue samples.

Bench/simulation validation of a new technique or device (e.g., a videolaryngoscope, airway adjunct, or ultrasound-guided block approach) on mannequins, task trainers or cadavers: setting up test conditions, measuring performance across operators, and iterating the design before first-in-human use.

sources.system: Maholo LabDroid + batch Bayesian optimization (Robotic Biology Institute / RIKEN, Kanda et al.)
sources.developer: Robotic Biology Institute / RIKEN / Kyoto University collaboration
sources.title: Robotic Search for Optimal Cell Culture in Regenerative Medicine (preprint of eLife 2022 paper)
sources.claim: A dual-arm humanoid lab robot (Maholo LabDroid) coupled to a batch Bayesian optimizer autonomously executed and iterated a biomedical cell-culture experiment campaign, discovering improved iPSC-to-RPE differentiation conditions — an end-to-end autonomous wet-bench research loop in a fixtured robot station.

sources.title: A mobile robotic chemist | Nature
sources.claim: A free-roaming mobile manipulator autonomously ran a multi-day experimental research campaign using human-scale instruments in a standard university chemistry laboratory, selecting its own next experiments.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous experimental campaigns in a human research laboratory. It shows a robot can occupy a human lab and operate its instruments, but the chemistry formulation/photocatalysis workflow does not establish sterile mammalian cell culture or biological assay work, so transfer to biomedical benchwork in an unmodified human lab is only partial.

sources.system: Ginkgo Cloud Lab / Reconfigurable Automation Carts (RACs)
sources.title: Ginkgo Bioworks Launches Ginkgo Cloud Lab | Contract Pharma
sources.claim: Commercially operating autonomous laboratory infrastructure built on robotic-arm automation carts performs researchers' benchwork, with the workflow arranged around the machines rather than around people.

sources.title: Robot performs first laparoscopic surgery without human help | ScienceDaily
sources.claim: An autonomous surgical robot performed laparoscopic intestinal anastomosis in live pigs without human guidance, i.e., a single procedural step of a preclinical animal experiment.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: performing an experimental surgical procedure on a research animal. It substantiates only the intraoperative manipulation step, not the surrounding study conduct (anesthesia management, dosing, monitoring, sampling, endpoint analysis) that the anesthesiologist-researcher performs.

sources.system: Automated image-guided rodent tail-vein cannulation robot
sources.title: Design and Evaluation of a Robotic Device for Automated Tail Vein Cannulations in Rodent Models
sources.claim: An image-guided robotic device automatically cannulates rodent tail veins for preclinical blood sampling and drug delivery, with the animal held on a dedicated platform.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: obtaining venous access in laboratory rodents for dosing and sampling. It covers one manipulation step of a preclinical study, not the whole experiment.

sources.developer: Rutgers University / Vasculogic (Leipheimer, Balter et al.)
sources.title: First-in-human evaluation of a hand-held automated venipuncture device for rapid venous blood draws | TECHNOLOGY
sources.claim: A hand-held robotic venipuncture device guided by ultrasound achieved 87% cannulation success in a first-in-human study, but is held and positioned by a clinician rather than operating as a standalone autonomous phlebotomist.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: drawing timed research blood samples from trial participants. Cited only to show that even this sub-step remains clinician-held and semi-autonomous, so it cannot support a positive judgment.

sources.title: Robot performs first realistic surgery without human help | Hub (Johns Hopkins)
sources.claim: An AI-driven surgical robot autonomously executed all steps of a cholecystectomy on ex vivo porcine tissue in a laboratory, illustrating that autonomous procedural robots are currently the subject of technique research rather than the experimenter conducting it.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: executing a medical procedure autonomously in a lab setting. Relevant because technique-development research tests such systems; it does not show a robot designing, running and evaluating the validation study itself.

roles.title: Cardiologists
aliases: DO Physician (Doctor of Osteopathic Medicine Physician)
roles.description: Diagnose, treat, manage, and prevent diseases or conditions of the cardiovascular system. May further subspecialize in interventional procedures (e.g., balloon angioplasty and stent placement), echocardiography, or electrophysiology.

tasks.label: Administer emergency cardiac care for life-threatening heart problems, such as cardiac arrest and heart attack.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Emergency primary PCI for acute STEMI: patient arrives via ED/EMS activation, cardiologist scrubs in at the cath lab table, obtains radial or femoral arterial access, engages the guiding catheter, crosses the thrombotic occlusion with a wire, aspirates/balloons and stents the culprit vessel, manages no-reflow, dissection, or arrest on the table, and achieves TIMI-3 flow within door-to-balloon time.

In-hospital cardiac arrest (code blue) on a ward, CCU, or ED bay: cardiologist runs ACLS — confirms pulselessness, directs/performs chest compressions, applies pads and defibrillates VF/VT, gives IV epinephrine/amiodarone, supports the airway, uses bedside ultrasound to find reversible causes (tamponade, PE), and delivers post-ROSC care.

Cardiogenic shock / acute decompensation at the bedside in CCU or cath lab: hands-on exam, emergent placement of mechanical circulatory support (IABP or Impella) via arterial access, right-heart catheter placement, vasopressor and inotrope titration, escalation to ECMO cannulation with the shock team.

Urgent bedside cardiac procedures in CCU/ED for unstable patients: emergency synchronized cardioversion, transcutaneous/emergent transvenous pacemaker insertion via central venous access for complete heart block or asystole, or pericardiocentesis under echo guidance for tamponade.

Cardiologist responds to a collapse outside a treatment room — outpatient clinic waiting area, hospital lobby, or a public/community setting — starting BLS, applying an AED, and running the resuscitation with improvised equipment until EMS or the code team arrives and transport is arranged.

sources.title: Robotic Assisted Percutaneous Coronary Intervention: Hype or Hope? | Journal of the American Heart Association
sources.claim: Commercial robotic PCI platforms (CorPath 200/GRX) are remote-controlled by the interventional cardiologist; arterial access, diagnostic angiography, and guide catheter engagement remain manual bedside tasks performed by the physician.
sources.transferJustification: Directly relevant to the emergency PCI instance: shows the robotic platform performs only wire/balloon/stent manipulation under continuous human joystick control, with the access and catheter-engagement steps done by hand.

sources.title: Robotic Assisted Percutaneous Coronary Intervention: Hype or Hope? | Journal of the American Heart Association
sources.claim: In the largest clinical robotic-PCI experience (CORA-PCI), STEMI cases requiring primary PCI were explicitly excluded, and 18.5% of attempted robotic cases needed partial or full manual conversion.

sources.title: Robocath R-One Results From European Multicenter R-EVOLUTION Study Presented - Cardiac Interventions Today
sources.claim: The second commercial robotic PCI system, R-One, is likewise driven by a physician using joysticks at a control station to move guidewires, balloons and stents.

sources.title: Latest Developments in Robotic Percutaneous Coronary Interventions | Interventional Cardiology Review
sources.claim: Current-generation robotic PCI still requires a scrubbed human bedside operator to load and exchange wires and devices, and the platforms cannot use over-the-wire, atherectomy, or multiple simultaneous devices.

sources.title: Robotic catheter brings autonomous navigation into human body - The Robot Report
sources.claim: The most advanced autonomous intracardiac navigation demonstration steered a catheter to a leaking valve inside a live pig's beating heart, but the therapeutic deployment step was still joystick-controlled by a surgeon, and the work remains a laboratory animal study.
sources.transferJustification: Closest autonomous cardiac-catheter capability. It covers only intracardiac navigation to a fixed anatomical target in an anesthetized animal under elective conditions; it does not perform vascular access, thrombus crossing, stenting, or any resuscitation, so it cannot substantiate completion of emergency cardiac care.

sources.title: Robot performs first realistic surgery without human help – Johns Hopkins Malone Center
sources.claim: The frontier autonomous surgical system performed a multi-step gallbladder dissection, but on pig cadaver tissue in a laboratory setup rather than on live human patients.
sources.transferJustification: Cited as the frontier of surgical autonomy. It is an elective soft-tissue dissection on ex vivo tissue with a pre-set laparoscopic field, with no time pressure, no patient instability, and no cardiac procedures; it does not transfer to time-critical emergency cardiac care on live patients.

sources.title: LUCAS device - Wikipedia
sources.claim: Mechanical chest-compression machines automate only the compression component of resuscitation and must be positioned on the patient by clinicians, who continue to perform rhythm analysis, defibrillation, drug delivery and airway management.
sources.transferJustification: Relevant to the cardiac-arrest instances: it is the only widely deployed machine that acts physically during resuscitation, but it executes a single scripted sub-step after human application and cannot diagnose, defibrillate, medicate, or manage post-ROSC care.

tasks.label: Calculate valve areas from blood flow velocity measurements.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Echo lab reading room: cardiologist reviews an acquired transthoracic echo study and computes aortic valve area by the continuity equation from LVOT diameter, LVOT velocity-time integral, and aortic jet VTI/peak velocity, then records the value in the interpretation report.

Mitral stenosis assessment: cardiologist derives mitral valve area from Doppler tracings using pressure half-time (and cross-checks against planimetry or the continuity method) in a patient with rheumatic mitral stenosis, adjudicating discordance among methods.

Cardiac catheterization lab: cardiologist calculates valve area from invasively measured transvalvular gradient and cardiac output (Gorlin/Hakki) when Doppler data are discordant or nondiagnostic, integrating simultaneous pressure and thermodilution/Fick flow data.

Structural heart/TAVR or intraoperative TEE setting: cardiologist computes valve area and dimensionless index from TEE Doppler measurements for procedural planning or immediate post-deployment assessment, often under time pressure in the procedure room.

Prosthetic valve follow-up: cardiologist computes effective orifice area and dimensionless velocity index from Doppler velocities to distinguish prosthesis-patient mismatch from prosthetic stenosis, comparing to reference values for valve type and size.

tasks.label: Conduct electrocardiogram (EKG), phonocardiogram, echocardiogram, or other cardiovascular tests to record patients' cardiac activity, using specialized electronic test equipment, recording devices, or laboratory instruments.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Resting 12-lead ECG in an outpatient cardiology clinic exam room: prep skin, palpate intercostal landmarks, apply ten electrodes, connect leads, coach the patient to lie still, acquire and check the tracing for artifact or lead reversal, then remove electrodes.

Comprehensive transthoracic echocardiogram in a hospital/clinic echo lab: patient in left lateral decubitus on a scanning bed, parasternal, apical, subcostal and suprasternal windows, 2D/M-mode, color and spectral Doppler, on-cart measurements, breath-hold coaching, adapting to poor acoustic windows and varied body habitus.

Focused/limited bedside echo (POCUS) on an inpatient in a ward or ICU: handheld or cart device at the bedside among lines, drains and monitors; obtain a few standard views to assess LV function, pericardial effusion and IVC, on a patient who may be supine, obese or uncooperative.

Exercise treadmill stress test (or stress echo/pharmacologic stress) in a stress lab: electrode and blood-pressure hookup, baseline ECG, continuous rhythm and symptom monitoring during exercise, immediate post-exercise image or ECG capture, readiness to stop the test and respond to ischemia or arrhythmia.

Transesophageal echocardiogram in an echo/procedure suite or operating room: sedated patient, topical airway anesthesia, insert and advance the TEE probe, rotate/flex to obtain the full multi-plane study with Doppler, withdraw probe and monitor recovery.

Ambulatory monitor hookup and adjunct cardiovascular tests: apply Holter, event recorder or adhesive ECG patch and instruct the patient; or perform adjunct bedside tests such as an agitated-saline shunt bubble study, ankle-brachial index or tilt-table recording in a clinic or hospital lab.

sources.title: Towards expert-level autonomous carotid ultrasonography with large-scale learning-based robotic system - PubMed
sources.claim: UltraBot is a fully autonomous robotic ... that performs carotid artery ultrasound examinations on human volunteers, including probe servoing, biometric measurement and plaque screening, with over 90% success and expert-level accuracy in clinical-oriented validation.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous vascular (carotid) ultrasound rather than cardiac. It shows autonomous probe placement and servoing on live humans in a clinical facility, but carotid vessels are superficial with fixed anatomy, whereas echocardiography requires intercostal acoustic windows, patient repositioning and Doppler measurement, so it does not substantiate completing an echocardiogram.

sources.developer: Tsinghua University / Beijing Tsinghua Changgung Hospital
sources.title: [2510.08106] Beyond hospital reach: Autonomous lightweight ultrasound robot for liver sonography
sources.claim: A lightweight autonomous ultrasound robot deployed in the ultrasound department ... autonomously acquired expert-level standard liver ultrasound planes (including aorta, IVC and portal vein planes) and detected pathology in real patients.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: abdominal (liver) sonography, not cardiac. It shows autonomous probe manipulation on breathing patients inside a hospital imaging department, but abdominal windows are broad and static compared with the intercostal, motion-gated views and Doppler measurements an echocardiogram requires, so transfer to echocardiography is not established.

tasks.label: Conduct research to develop or test medications, treatments, or procedures that prevent or control disease or injury.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Site-investigator study visit in a multicenter cardiovascular drug trial: screening a patient in the hospital research clinic, obtaining informed consent, targeted history and cardiac exam, ECG, protocol blood draws, dispensing or administering the investigational agent, and assessing eligibility and adverse events.

Desk-based research work: writing the protocol and IRB/FDA submissions, defining endpoints, adjudicating events, cleaning and statistically analyzing trial data, DSMB/steering committee participation, and writing grants and manuscripts in the office.

Protocol-mandated invasive procedure in an interventional or device trial: implanting an investigational stent, occluder or lead in the cath lab/EP lab with protocol-specified intracoronary imaging (IVUS/OCT), pressure-wire measurements, and per-protocol handling of complications.

Research imaging and physiologic testing per core-lab protocol: acquiring or supervising a study echocardiogram with extra research views and strain, exercise or dobutamine stress testing, and measurement/QC of images in the hospital echo lab.

Translational bench work on cells and tissue: running compound screens, cardiomyocyte or endothelial cell assays, ELISA/biomarker plates and PCR in an academic laboratory, iterating on results to test candidate drug effects.

Animal-model experiments: rodent or large-animal surgery (coronary ligation, aortic banding), catheter-based hemodynamics and telemetry implantation, dosing and terminal tissue harvest in a vivarium or animal OR.

sources.system: Vitestro Aletta ARPD (autonomous robotic phlebotomy device)
sources.title: Performance, Safety, and Patient Experience of an Autonomous Robotic Phlebotomy Device: A Multicenter Trial (Clinical Chemistry)
sources.claim: Vitestro's Autonomous Robotic Phlebotomy Device performed venipuncture autonomously on 1,633 outpatients in Dutch hospital phlebotomy departments with 94.5% first-stick success and 0.6% mild adverse events; it performs the draw only, not consent, examination or adverse-event judgment.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: routine diagnostic phlebotomy. Protocol blood sampling at a research visit involves the same objects (vacutainers, antecubital veins) and precision, so capability transfers to that sub-step only, not to consent, exam or protocol judgment.

sources.title: Vitestro unveils Aletta robotic phlebotomy device – CAP TODAY
sources.claim: The ARPD is CE-marked and marketed for autonomous end-to-end blood collection in ordinary hospital blood-collection rooms, i.e. a structured human clinical facility rather than a fenced machine cell.
sources.transferJustification: Same as above: establishes commercial maturity and clinical-facility setting of the phlebotomy sub-step of a research study visit.

sources.title: ROB-OSTIAL Study Protocol (ClinicalTrials.gov posted document)
sources.claim: The only clinically used cardiac catheterization robot, CorPath GRX, is a remote master-slave system in which the interventionalist manipulates wires and devices from a console throughout the case: teleoperation, not autonomous completion of a trial procedure.

sources.title: Robotic catheter brings autonomous navigation into human body (The Robot Report)
sources.claim: Autonomous intracardiac catheter navigation has been shown only as a sub-step in animals: a robotic catheter autonomously navigated to a leaky valve inside a beating pig heart, without performing a complete human trial procedure.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: intracardiac device navigation, the core motion of an investigational-device trial procedure. It shows only autonomous navigation in an animal, not implantation, protocol imaging and complication handling in patients.

sources.title: Current Status and Pending Developments of Robotic Tele-Echocardiography (JACC: Cardiovascular Imaging)
sources.claim: A 2025 JACC: Cardiovascular Imaging review of robotic echocardiography describes clinical systems as tele-operated by a remote sonographer or cardiologist and treats autonomous robot-acquired echocardiography as not yet established.

sources.system: Autonomous ultrasound scanning robotic system for cardiac imaging
sources.title: Autonomous ultrasound scanning robotic system based on human posture recognition and image servo control: an application for cardiac imaging (Frontiers in Robotics and AI)
sources.claim: Autonomous robotic cardiac ultrasound exists only as a laboratory prototype using posture recognition and force/image servo control, not as a system producing protocol-grade research echocardiograms.

sources.developer: Universities of Manchester, Aberystwyth and Cambridge
sources.title: Cheaper faster drug development validated by the repositioning of drugs against neglected tropical diseases (Journal of the Royal Society Interface)
sources.claim: The Robot Scientist 'Eve' autonomously ran closed-loop drug-discovery cycles — library screening, hit confirmation and lead generation — in a purpose-built automated screening laboratory, yielding a published repositioning finding against malaria targets.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated compound screening to test candidate medications. Same objects (microplates, cell assays, liquid handling) and closed-loop experimental logic as a cardiologist's translational bench screening work.

sources.developer: academic group, published in Scientific Reports
sources.title: Development of the autonomous lab system to support biotechnology research (Scientific Reports)
sources.claim: An autonomous laboratory system combining robotics and AI executed biotechnology experiments and formulated hypotheses without step-by-step human control, operating in a machine-configured lab cell.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated wet-lab biological experimentation. Same plate and liquid-handling objects and precision as cardiovascular cell-assay bench work, in a laboratory laid out around the robot.

sources.title: Pioneering AI Drug Discovery (Recursion)
sources.claim: Recursion operates a commercial automated wet lab where robotics and computer vision execute millions of cell experiments weekly to test drug candidates, showing industrial-scale robotic execution of screening research in a purpose-built facility.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: high-throughput cell-based compound testing, the same class of experiment (plates, cell culture, imaging readouts) as translational cardiovascular bench screening.

tasks.label: Diagnose cardiovascular conditions, using cardiac catheterization.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Elective diagnostic left heart catheterization / coronary angiography via radial access in a hospital cath lab: sterile prep, ultrasound- or palpation-guided arterial puncture and sheath placement, advancing diagnostic catheters to the aortic root, selective cannulation of left and right coronary ostia, hand/power contrast injections in multiple views, aortic and LV pressure recording, interpretation of stenosis severity on the spot, catheter/sheath removal and hemostasis.

Diagnostic angiography in difficult anatomy: obese patient or peripheral arterial disease requiring femoral access, tortuous/calcified subclavian or iliac vessels, prior CABG requiring selective engagement of saphenous vein and internal mammary grafts with specialty catheters, plus LV angiography — performed in the same hospital cath lab with variable catheter exchanges and troubleshooting.

Right heart catheterization (often combined with left heart cath) for hemodynamic diagnosis: venous access, floating a balloon-tipped Swan-Ganz catheter through RA/RV to pulmonary artery and wedge position, recording pressure waveforms, oximetry sampling for shunt runs, thermodilution/Fick cardiac output, and interpreting the data for pulmonary hypertension, valve disease, shunt, or transplant workup.

Adjunctive invasive physiology and intracoronary imaging during a diagnostic cath: advancing a pressure wire across an intermediate lesion for FFR/iFR with hyperemic agent, or IVUS/OCT pullback to assess plaque and lumen area, then integrating the numbers with the angiogram to decide lesion significance.

Emergent/urgent catheterization in an unstable patient (STEMI activation, cardiogenic shock, resuscitated arrest, often off-hours): rapid access with the patient moving, intubated, or on pressors/mechanical support, expedited angiography of both coronaries to identify the culprit lesion, with hemodynamic monitoring and constant adaptation to the patient's condition.

sources.title: Robotically performed diagnostic coronary angiography — Catheterization and Cardiovascular Interventions
sources.claim: Robotic diagnostic coronary angiography has been done clinically with the CorPath GRX, but vascular access and initial catheter advancement were manual and all robotic catheter motions were commanded by the physician from a console (teleoperation).
sources.transferJustification: Directly the task: diagnostic coronary angiography in a hospital cath lab; cited to establish that the only clinical robotic pathway is physician-commanded teleoperation, not autonomous.

sources.title: The ROB-OSTIAL Study protocol (ClinicalTrials.gov NCT05634538)
sources.claim: The CorPath GRX system's intended use is explicitly remote (master-slave) manipulation of guidewires, devices, and guide catheters by the operator, confirming there is no autonomous mode.
sources.transferJustification: Same device family used for diagnostic angiography; establishes autonomy status of the leading commercial cath-lab robot.

sources.system: Clinical robotic catheter platforms (CorPath GRX, R-One, Stereotaxis, etc.)
sources.developer: multiple (review by Tavallaei et al., Houston Methodist DeBakey Cardiovascular Journal)
sources.title: Robotic Systems in Cardiovascular Interventions: Evolving Platforms and the Path Forward
sources.claim: A 2025 review of 19 clinical cardiovascular robotic catheter platforms states that existing systems sit at the lowest autonomy levels (robot assistance / task-level assistance), with full procedural automation not achieved.
sources.transferJustification: Survey of the exact device class used for cardiac catheterization; substantiates that no clinically available cath-lab robot performs the procedure autonomously.

sources.system: Autonomous haptic-vision robotic catheter (Dupont Lab, Boston Children's Hospital)
sources.developer: Boston Children's Hospital / Harvard Medical School
sources.title: Advanced Robotics for the Next-Generation of Cardiac Interventions (Micromachines review)
sources.claim: Genuinely autonomous intracardiac catheter navigation has been demonstrated only as a narrow sub-step (wall-following from a surgical apical port to a paravalvular leak) in anesthetized pigs, not as a diagnostic catheterization from access to interpretation.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous intracardiac catheter navigation. Cited as the strongest autonomous cardiac catheter result; it covers only navigation to a target in an animal, without percutaneous arterial access, selective coronary cannulation, contrast angiography, or diagnosis.

sources.system: AURA-CVC autonomous ultrasound-guided robotic vascular access pipeline
sources.developer: academic (published in Int. J. Computer Assisted Radiology and Surgery)
sources.title: AURA-CVC: Autonomous Ultrasound-guided Robotic Assistance for Central Venous Catheterization
sources.claim: Autonomous ultrasound-guided vascular needle placement — the access sub-step of catheterization — has been demonstrated only on a commercial phantom, with operator feedback in the loop.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic vascular access, the first sub-step of cardiac catheterization. Shows autonomy exists only for needle puncture on phantoms, not for the whole diagnostic catheterization in patients.

tasks.label: Inject contrast media into patients' blood vessels.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Diagnostic selective coronary angiography in a hospital cardiac cath lab: with a diagnostic catheter engaged in the left/right coronary ostium, the cardiologist makes repeated hand injections of iodinated contrast through a manifold or injector controller, modulating force/volume in real time while watching fluoroscopy and the pressure waveform for damping or ventricularization, timed to cine acquisition, under sterile drapes.

Programmed high-flow power-injector runs during diagnostic catheterization or structural work: left ventriculogram, aortogram/aortic root angiogram (e.g., during TAVR), or pulmonary angiogram. Injector tubing is connected to a pigtail catheter, rate/volume/pressure limit are set (e.g., 30 mL at 12 mL/s), the run is triggered with cine.

Contrast injections during PCI or structural intervention through a guide catheter: many small injections interleaved with guidewire, balloon and stent manipulation, often in urgent/STEMI cases, with deliberate contrast minimization in CKD patients and constant judgment about vessel opacification, no-reflow, dissection or perforation.

Venous and peripheral contrast runs in the lab: upper-extremity/subclavian venography through a peripheral IV during pacemaker or ICD implantation, or peripheral/renal/graft angiographic runs during endovascular work, through a catheter or IV in the sterile field.

Intravenous contrast bolus in an imaging suite: iodinated contrast for coronary CT angiography (biphasic bolus plus saline chaser, bolus tracking) or an ultrasound contrast agent given through a pre-placed peripheral IV for contrast echocardiography, ordered/supervised by the cardiologist.

sources.system: Nemoto Press Duo Elite closed-circuit dual-port injector with foot-pedal 'Trace Shot'
sources.developer: Nemoto Kyorindo (clinical study, University of Pennsylvania)
sources.title: Closed-Circuit Dual-Port Injector System for Fully Automated Contrast Delivery in Diagnostic Cerebral Angiography
sources.claim: A closed-circuit dual-port power injector (Nemoto Press Duo Elite) delivered every contrast injection of diagnostic cerebral angiography - both small navigation 'puffs' for vessel selection and full pre-programmed diagnostic runs at vessel-specific flow rates and volumes - with the machine executing the preset rate/volume/pressure after an operator trigger; 19 consecutive patients, all diagnostically adequate, no complications, eliminating manual tableside contrast handling.
sources.transferJustification: Cerebral rather than coronary angiography, but the act is identical: machine-controlled delivery of iodinated contrast through a selectively placed intra-arterial catheter in a hospital angiography lab, at comparable volumes (1-15 mL), rates (2-10 mL/s) and pressure limits, judged by the same diagnostic-image standard.

sources.title: Early clinical experiences with a novel contrast volume reduction system during invasive coronary angiography (PMC)
sources.claim: The ACIST CVi automated contrast injector is used routinely for invasive coronary angiography and PCI, delivering contrast at operator-set flow rate, volume, pressure limit and rise time with built-in air-column detection; clinical series report contrast volume savings without loss ....

sources.title: MEDRAD Mark 7 Arterion Injection System | Radiology US (Bayer)
sources.claim: Bayer's Medrad Mark 7 Arterion is a commercially deployed angiographic injection system that mechanically administers intravascular contrast media and flushing agents during angiographic procedures in cath labs, IR suites and hybrid ORs, executing programmed injections.

sources.title: Bayer Receives FDA Clearance for CT Injection System | Imaging Technology News
sources.claim: Bayer's Medrad Centargo CT injection system, FDA 510(k)-cleared in November 2024 and launched in 49 markets, automates contrast administration for CT/CT angiography: the snap-in patient line auto-primes and the machine delivers the programmed multi-phase intravenous bolus for successive patients.
sources.transferJustification: Covers the intravenous-contrast instance: the same act of driving contrast media into a patient's blood vessel, here through a peripheral IV for CT angiography, with machine-controlled rate, volume and pressure.

sources.system: CorPath / CorPath GRX robotic PCI platform
sources.title: Demonstration of the Safety and Feasibility of Robotically Assisted Percutaneous Coronary Intervention in Complex Coronary Lesions (CORA-PCI Study)
sources.claim: In robotic-assisted PCI with the CorPath system the robot manipulates guidewires and devices while contrast injection remains a human, tableside task; the seated operator controls fluoroscopy pedals and the bedside team performs the contrast injections.

sources.title: Robotic-assisted percutaneous coronary intervention: current evidence and future directions (Frontiers in Cardiovascular Medicine)
sources.claim: A 2026 review of robotic-assisted PCI confirms that vascular access, coronary ostium engagement and catheter/fluid-path handling are still done manually by a scrubbed bedside operator; the robot only takes over guidewire and device control after the catheter is connected.

tasks.label: Monitor patients' conditions and progress, and reevaluate treatments, as necessary.
