tasks.label: Observe ultrasound display screen, and listen to signals to record vascular information, such as blood pressure, limb volume changes, oxygen saturation, and cerebral circulation.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Non-invasive lower-extremity arterial physiologic study in a cardiology office or hospital vascular lab: cuffs at thigh/calf/ankle plus digits, resting and post-exercise segmental blood pressures, ABI/TBI, pulse-volume-recording (limb volume change) waveforms and digit PPG/oxygen saturation; cardiologist/lab watches the tracings and Doppler audio and records the values into the study.

Carotid/vertebral duplex in an accredited vascular lab: operator watches the B-mode/color screen and listens to the spectral Doppler signal while angling the probe through CCA/ICA/ECA/vertebral bilaterally, freezing and recording peak systolic and end-diastolic velocities, plaque and intima-media findings for stenosis grading (cerebral circulation).

Lower-extremity venous duplex in the lab or at the bedside: serial transverse compressions from common femoral to popliteal/calf, watching lumen coaptation on screen, listening to phasic/augmented Doppler signals, recording images and waveforms to rule out DVT (or reflux timing for venous insufficiency).

Peripheral or visceral arterial duplex imaging in the lab: bypass graft/stent surveillance, aorto-iliac or renal/mesenteric duplex, AAA diameter surveillance, or dialysis-access flow study — screen observation plus spectral Doppler audio to record velocities, waveform morphology and diameters at defined sites.

Transcranial Doppler / cerebral circulation study: insonating temporal windows to record middle cerebral artery blood-flow velocities — agitated-saline bubble study for right-to-left shunt in the clinic, or vasospasm/emboli monitoring at the ICU bedside after subarachnoid hemorrhage.

Ad hoc periprocedural or critical-care vascular signal check: post-catheterization femoral/radial access-site duplex, continuous-wave Doppler over a pulseless limb, or pulse-oximetry/Barbeau patency check on a draped, monitored, often uncooperative patient in a cath lab, ED or ICU bay.

sources.title: Fully Automated Transcranial Doppler Ultrasound for Middle Cerebral Artery Insonation
sources.claim: NovaGuide is a five-degree-of-freedom autonomous robotic transcranial Doppler system that itself finds the acoustic window and optimizes ... cerebral blood flow velocity signal, i.e. it performs the probe search and signal optimization a human operator would do while watching the screen.

sources.title: Safety and efficacy of a novel robotic transcranial doppler system in subarachnoid hemorrhage (Scientific Reports)
sources.claim: Robotic TCD (NovaGuide) is used as the routine acquisition method in a hospital neuro unit, recording middle cerebral artery velocities in subarachnoid hemorrhage patients at the bedside; staff drape the insonators, place registration dots and position the head cradle, then the robot acquires.

sources.title: Robot-Assisted Transcranial Doppler Versus Transthoracic Echocardiography for Right to Left Shunt Detection (Stroke)
sources.claim: Robot-assisted TCD was evaluated against transthoracic echocardiography for right-to-left shunt detection in a prospective multicenter device trial at six clinical sites, and detected shunts about three times more often than standard of care; the device is FDA-cleared.

sources.title: Towards expert-level autonomous carotid ultrasonography with large-scale learning-based robotic system (Nature Communications)
sources.claim: UltraBot, a learning-based autonomous carotid ultrasound robot, performed autonomous carotid examinations on 41 previously unseen volunteers in clinical environments with over 90% success and expert-level accuracy.

sources.title: Towards expert-level autonomous carotid ultrasonography with large-scale learning-based robotic system (Nature Communications), Fig. 6
sources.claim: UltraBot's end-to-end autonomous carotid exam includes acquiring the images, performing biometric measurements, plaque segmentation and ..., and producing a report containing peak systolic velocity, end-diastolic velocity and resistive index — the same recorded vascular information a sonographer/cardiologist logs.

sources.system: Automatic robotic Doppler sonography system (Osburg et al., 7-DoF manipulator with 3D US probe)
sources.title: Automatic robotic doppler sonography of leg arteries (International Journal of Computer Assisted Radiology and Surgery)
sources.claim: A 7-DoF robotic arm with force-compliant control and Doppler-based visual servoing autonomously scanned and tracked the femoral artery of seven ... over a 20 cm segment, keeping the vessel properly visualized during the scan.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous Doppler ultrasound tracking of a limb artery. It transfers to peripheral/graft/access duplex recording because it is the same object (a limb artery), the same modality and precision (probe normal-alignment and Doppler signal maintenance), on live human subjects lying on a scanning table.

sources.system: KMP-based robotic ultrasound system for DVT examination
sources.developer: Technical University of Munich / academic group
sources.title: Imitation Learning for Robotic Assisted Ultrasound Examination of Deep Venous Thrombosis using Kernelized Movement Primitives (arXiv)
sources.claim: A robotic ultrasound system using kernelized movement primitives reproduced expert probe trajectories and compression force profiles for deep venous thrombosis examination, tested on human volunteers' limbs.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic venous compression scanning. It transfers to the venous duplex instance because the assessed object (a compressible deep vein), the required force-controlled probe compression and the image-quality criterion are the same as in a DVT rule-out study; the demonstration was on live volunteers.

sources.system: Viasonix Falcon Xpress vascular diagnostic system
sources.title: Falcon Xpress | Image Monitoring USA
sources.claim: A commercially marketed US vascular-lab system performs segmental arterial testing with an automatic multi-hose cuff selector that controls cuff inflation and deflation without ..., running ABI, TBI, segmental pressures, PVR and post-exercise protocols once the operator has fitted the cuffs.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated segmental pressure and pulse-volume-recording acquisition. It is the same recorded quantities named in this task (blood pressure, limb volume changes) and the machine physically inflates/deflates the cuffs and captures the waveforms once the limbs are presented in the cuffs.

sources.system: MESI mTABLET ABI / MESI ABPI MD
sources.title: Measure Ankle Brachial-Index with MESI mTABLET ABI
sources.claim: A fully automated multi-cuff ABI system completes the ankle-brachial index measurement in one minute after the user places the cuffs, using plethysmography sensors that detect limb volume changes and producing the waveform report.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated ankle-brachial index and plethysmographic waveform acquisition. It produces exactly the vascular information this task records (limb blood pressures and volume-change waveforms) with no operator observation of the tracings required beyond cuff placement.

sources.system: Autonomous lightweight cable-driven ultrasound robot (588 g) with AI agent
sources.developer: Tsinghua University / Beijing Tsinghua Changgung Hospital
sources.title: Beyond hospital reach: Autonomous lightweight ultrasound robot for liver sonography (arXiv 2510.08106)
sources.claim: An autonomous lightweight ultrasound robot was deployed in a hospital ultrasound department and autonomously localized the abdominal aorta, IVC and portal vein imaging planes on volunteers who were breathing freely, starting from randomized initial planes.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous acquisition of abdominal vascular planes (aorta, IVC, portal vein). It transfers to abdominal vascular duplex recording because the targets are the same vessels and the robot must find and hold the standard plane on a freely breathing patient, as required to record aortic diameter or visceral flow.

tasks.label: Obtain and record patient information, including patient identification, medical history, and examination results.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: New-patient outpatient cardiology consult: verify patient identity and demographics, interview the patient about chest pain/dyspnea/palpitations, elicit cardiac risk factors, medication list, prior interventions, family and social history; review outside records; dictate or type the history and findings into the EHR note.

Established-patient follow-up in clinic: confirm identifiers, obtain interval history (symptoms, medication adherence, device checks), incorporate vitals and exam findings reported/observed, and record an updated note and problem/medication list in the EHR.

Inpatient or ED cardiology consultation: obtain history from the patient, family, nurse, or referring team (sometimes with a poor historian or via interpreter), collate chart data (labs, telemetry, ECG), and write/dictate the consult note in the hospital record.

Pre-procedure intake in the cath/EP lab or pre-op area: confirm patient identification and site, allergies, anticoagulation and renal history, prior stents/devices, and record the pre-procedure history and verification into the procedural record.

Reading and recording diagnostic examination results: entering/attesting echo, stress test, Holter, or device interrogation findings into the patient record, and telehealth visits where history is obtained by video and documented.

tasks.label: Operate diagnostic imaging equipment to produce contrast-enhanced radiographs of heart and cardiovascular system.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Elective diagnostic coronary angiography in a hospital cardiac catheterization laboratory: sterile prep, radial or femoral arterial access, advance and exchange diagnostic catheters over a wire, selectively engage left and right coronary ostia, hand- or power-inject iodinated contrast while stepping on fluoroscopy/cine, pan and angulate the C-arm through multiple standard projections, judge image adequacy and repeat runs, manage catheter-induced pressure damping/ectopy, then remove sheath and achieve hemostasis.

Additional contrast runs during the same catheterization: pigtail catheter into the left ventricle for a power-injected ventriculogram (RAO/LAO), aortic root angiography, saphenous-vein/LIMA graft angiography in post-CABG patients, or selective renal/iliac runs — each requiring catheter selection, ostial engagement, injector programming and gated cine acquisition.

Emergent angiography for STEMI or hemodynamically unstable patient, often off-hours: rapid access in a moving, sometimes intubated or agitated patient, limited number of contrast runs to identify the culprit vessel quickly, imaging performed alongside pressors, IABP/Impella lines and ongoing resuscitation, with contrast volume minimized in renal impairment.

Contrast imaging embedded in structural or electrophysiology procedures in a hybrid lab: aortic root angiography for valve positioning during TAVR, balloon-occlusion coronary sinus venography for CRT lead placement, pulmonary vein or left atrial appendage angiography during ablation/occluder cases — contrast timed to device manipulation and hemodynamics.

Coronary CT angiography acquisition in the hospital/outpatient CT suite under cardiologist supervision: heart-rate control with beta blockers and sublingual nitroglycerin, IV placement and power-injector connection, patient positioning and ECG gating setup, breath-hold coaching, bolus-tracking triggered contrast-enhanced acquisition, immediate review for motion/contrast timing and decision to rescan.

sources.title: The ROB-OSTIAL Study protocol (NCT05634538)
sources.claim: CorPath GRX, the FDA-cleared robotic PCI platform, is a remote-manipulation (teleoperated) system: the physician drives guidewires, catheters and devices from a shielded control console; it does not obtain vascular access, select/engage diagnostic catheters or run contrast injections autonomously.
sources.transferJustification: Same environment (cath lab) and same instruments as contrast angiography; cited to show the state of the art in cath-lab robotics is physician-in-the-loop teleoperation, not autonomous imaging acquisition.

sources.date: 2023-05 (launch); first-in-human of next-gen platform completed enrollment 2026-05
sources.title: Robocath launches new robotic platform R-One+ (PCRonline press release)
sources.claim: Robocath's R-One+ commercial cath-lab robot likewise requires the interventional cardiologist to control every device motion from a command unit; it is an assistance platform, not an autonomous operator.
sources.transferJustification: Coronary angioplasty uses the same guide catheters, wires and contrast angiography as diagnostic coronary imaging; shows commercial cardiac robots remain fully human-driven.

sources.system: Autonomous robotic catheter with haptic vision (Fagogenis et al.)
sources.developer: Boston Children's Hospital / Harvard Medical School (Pierre Dupont lab)
sources.title: Autonomous robotic intracardiac catheter navigation using haptic vision | Science Robotics
sources.claim: The only demonstrated autonomous intracardiac catheter navigation is a research prototype using haptic vision, shown in animal (in vivo porcine) experiments for wall-following navigation to a valve — not contrast angiography, not in patients, and not a deployed clinical workflow.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: intravascular/intracardiac catheter navigation, a prerequisite step for producing contrast angiograms. Cited as the ceiling of demonstrated autonomy; it stops short of contrast injection, C-arm operation and image adequacy judgment in humans.

sources.system: Autonomous soft robotic guidewire navigation via imitation learning
sources.title: Autonomous Soft Robotic Guidewire Navigation via Imitation Learning (arXiv:2510.09497)
sources.claim: Autonomous endovascular guidewire navigation remains at the phantom/benchtop research stage with sub-clinical reliability (e.g., 83% success reaching a target in unseen vascular geometries).
sources.transferJustification: Related task: guidewire/catheter navigation in vasculature, the core physical skill behind selective contrast angiography; the reported success rate and phantom setting show worker-quality completion is not yet achieved even in a purpose-built setup.

sources.title: Performance, Safety, and Patient Experience of an Autonomous Robotic Phlebotomy Device: A Multicenter Trial | Clinical Chemistry
sources.claim: Autonomous vascular access robotics that is actually commercial is limited to peripheral venous blood draws under staff supervision, with an overall success rate below expert clinical standards; nothing comparable exists for arterial access or selective coronary catheterization.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: percutaneous vascular needle access, a prerequisite for both IV contrast and arterial catheterization. It substantiates only superficial venous puncture in a supervised draw station, not arterial sheath insertion or contrast angiography.

sources.system: SOMATOM CT with FAST 3D Camera and FAST Bolus
sources.title: Use of a 3D camera for automated patient positioning for chest-abdomen-pelvis CT scans (ScienceDirect)
sources.claim: Modern CT scanners automate sub-steps of contrast-enhanced cardiac acquisition (3D-camera patient positioning, bolus tracking to trigger the scan), but the patient transfer, IV placement, injector connection, breath-hold coaching and protocol supervision remain human tasks performed by technologists and the supervising cardiologist.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated patient positioning for CT acquisition. It covers only one sub-step of the cardiac CTA instance and therefore cannot substantiate whole-instance completion.

tasks.label: Order medical tests, such as echocardiograms, electrocardiograms, and angiograms.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

tasks.label: Perform minimally invasive surgical procedures, such as implanting pacemakers and defibrillators.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Diagnostic left/right heart catheterization and coronary angiography in a hospital cath lab: radial or femoral arterial access under ultrasound, sheath placement, advancing and torquing diagnostic catheters to selectively engage coronary ostia under fluoroscopy, contrast injections, pressure measurement, sheath removal and hemostasis in a sedated, moving, anticoagulated patient.

Percutaneous coronary intervention with stenting (often ad hoc after angiography): guide catheter engagement, crossing a stenosis with a 0.014-inch guidewire, balloon predilatation, stent positioning and deployment, post-dilatation, imaging (IVUS/OCT/FFR) confirmation, and management of complications such as dissection, no-reflow, or perforation.

Transvenous device implantation (single/dual-chamber pacemaker, ICD, or CRT) in an EP lab or hybrid room: local anesthesia, skin incision and prepectoral pocket creation, axillary/subclavian or cephalic venous access, fluoroscopically guided active-fixation lead placement with sensing/threshold testing, defibrillation testing when indicated, generator connection, pocket closure with layered suturing.

Catheter ablation of arrhythmia (AF pulmonary vein isolation, SVT, atrial flutter) in an EP lab: multiple femoral venous sticks, transseptal puncture, electroanatomic mapping, catheter contact and stability control against a beating heart, delivery of RF/cryo/pulsed-field energy, and confirmation of block.

Small implantable device or simplified procedure: implantable loop recorder insertion in a clinic procedure room, leadless pacemaker (femoral venous delivery and tine fixation in the RV), or subcutaneous ICD tunneling and pocket, plus temporary pacing wire placement at the bedside/lab.

Structural intervention in a hybrid cath lab by an interventional cardiologist: TAVR, left atrial appendage occlusion, or PFO/ASD closure, with large-bore access, echo/fluoro co-registration, device positioning and deployment, and vascular closure.

sources.title: Robotic PCI confirmed to be both safe and effective in new comprehensive analysis
sources.claim: Corindus CorPath GRX, the FDA-cleared robotic PCI platform used in the PRECISION and PRECISION GRX registries (nearly 1,900 procedures in cath labs), is operated by the interventional cardiologist from a cockpit/control room via joysticks, and still requires a tableside team for device exchanges and manual assistance - i.e., it is teleoperated and cannot complete a PCI autonomously.

sources.system: Stereotaxis Genesis / GenesisX Robotic Magnetic Navigation
sources.title: Robotics in EP and Cath Labs | DAIC
sources.claim: Stereotaxis robotic magnetic navigation (Niobe, Genesis, GenesisX, FDA-cleared Nov 2025), deployed in cath and EP labs for catheter ablation, is physician-controlled: the interventionalist drives the catheter from a computer cockpit; no autonomous ablation is described.

sources.title: Robocath Launches New Robotic Platform R-One+ | Cath Lab Digest
sources.claim: Robocath's R-One+ robotic angioplasty platform, commercially installed in European and Chinese hospitals, is a remote-control system: the cardiologist manipulates guidewires and stents through a control unit in the cath lab or ....

sources.title: Towards autonomous robot-assisted transcatheter heart valve implantation: in vivo teleoperation and phantom validation of AI-guided positioning
sources.claim: The most advanced published attempt at autonomy in a transcatheter cardiac implant procedure (Caranx Medical robot-assisted TAVI) achieved only teleoperated instrument control and valve deployment in live animals; supervised-autonomy positioning was shown only on bench phantoms, not in a patient.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: transcatheter valve implantation, the closest published analogue to catheter-based implant work by cardiologists. It shows the autonomy frontier for this task family stops at teleoperation in vivo, so it cannot support a positive judgment for pacemaker/PCI work.

sources.title: SRT-H: A hierarchical framework for autonomous surgery via language-conditioned imitation learning | Science Robotics
sources.claim: The state of the art in autonomous soft-tissue surgery, Johns Hopkins' SRT-H, operated fully autonomously only on ex vivo pig gallbladders in a laboratory, completing a phase of cholecystectomy rather than a whole procedure on a living patient.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: laparoscopic gallbladder dissection. Cited as the frontier of autonomous surgical manipulation; it involves ex vivo tissue in a lab bench setup, not living cardiovascular anatomy under fluoroscopy, so capability does not transfer to catheter or device implant procedures.

sources.developer: Boston Children's Hospital / Harvard Medical School (Pierre Dupont lab)
sources.title: Robotic catheter brings autonomous navigation into the human body - The Robot Report
sources.claim: The first autonomous in-body navigation demonstration (Boston Children's Hospital concentric-tube catheter) autonomously drove a catheter to a leaky valve in a live pig, but only the navigation sub-step was autonomous; the surgeon still performed the therapeutic deployment.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: intracardiac catheter navigation in a beating heart, a sub-step of ablation and structural procedures. It is autonomous but covers navigation only, in an animal research setting, so it does not substantiate whole-procedure completion.

tasks.label: Perform vascular procedures, such as balloon angioplasty and stents.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Elective or ad hoc single-vessel coronary PCI for stable angina/NSTEMI in a hospital cardiac cath lab: radial arterial access, diagnostic angiography, engage the coronary ostium with a guide catheter, cross the lesion with a 0.014" wire, predilate with a balloon, size and deploy a drug-eluting stent, post-dilate, confirm result, remove sheath and achieve hemostasis, with a scrub and circulating team present.

Primary PCI for acute STEMI, often off-hours: unstable, moving, sometimes intubated or arresting patient; rapid femoral/radial access, culprit identification amid thrombus, aspiration or direct stenting, management of no-reflow, arrhythmia and hypotension, occasional temporary pacer or mechanical support, under door-to-balloon time pressure.

Complex/high-risk coronary PCI: chronic total occlusion with antegrade/retrograde wiring and microcatheters, heavily calcified lesions requiring rotational/orbital atherectomy or intravascular lithotripsy, left main or bifurcation two-stent strategies, IVUS/OCT guidance and Impella/IABP hemodynamic support, in a hospital cath lab.

Peripheral arterial intervention in a hospital cath lab or office-based lab: iliac, superficial femoral, popliteal or below-the-knee angioplasty, drug-coated balloon, atherectomy and self-expanding stent placement (or carotid/renal stenting with embolic protection), including contralateral or antegrade access and closure device deployment.

Diagnostic catheterization with physiologic assessment where intervention may or may not follow: arterial access, selective coronary/graft engagement and multi-view angiography, FFR/iFR pressure wire or intravascular imaging, decision to defer, treat with balloon only, or refer to surgery; sheath removal and hemostasis.

Intraprocedural complication management and bailout during a vascular procedure: coronary perforation requiring covered stent or coil embolization, dissection propagation, guidewire fracture or device entrapment, access-site bleeding/pseudoaneurysm, abrupt closure with hemodynamic collapse, in the same cath lab under extreme time pressure.

sources.title: Robotic-Assisted Percutaneous Coronary Intervention: Final Results of the PRECISION and PRECISION GRX Studies
sources.claim: CorPath GRX/CorPath 200 robotic PCI is a physician-directed, console-controlled (teleoperated) system; in the largest prospective registries about 10% of cases still needed unplanned manual assistance or conversion to manual PCI (technical success = clinical success without conversion).

sources.system: CorPath GRX (Cleveland Clinic robotic PCI program)
sources.title: Robotic Percutaneous Coronary Intervention: The Good, the Bad, and What is to Come
sources.claim: All commercially available robotic PCI platforms require the human operator to manually obtain vascular ... before the robot is used; the operator then drives every device movement from a shielded console.

sources.title: Robocath's R-One+ Robotic Platform Launched for PCI Procedures
sources.claim: Robocath's R-One+ commercial robotic angioplasty platform is operated by the interventional cardiologist through a control unit in the cath lab or ..., i.e. continuous human control of guidewire, balloon and stent motion.

sources.title: Robocath launches first-in-human study of next-gen robot for coronary artery disease
sources.claim: As of 2026 the fielded vascular-intervention robots remain teleoperated platforms; Robocath's R-One is in clinical use in Europe, Africa and China and its next-generation system only began first-in-human study in 2026.

sources.title: Siemens Healthineers is cutting back on surgical robotics program
sources.claim: Siemens Healthineers discontinued its Corindus cardiovascular robotics platform for cardiology procedures, indicating that even teleoperated robotic PCI has not been sustained as a mainstream capability in US cath labs.

sources.system: Autonomous concentric-tube robotic catheter (Fagogenis et al., Science Robotics)
sources.developer: Boston Children's Hospital / Harvard Medical School
sources.title: Surgeons Use Self-Navigating Robot to Find Leaky Valve in Pig Hearts
sources.claim: The strongest in vivo demonstration of autonomy inside the heart is a concentric-tube catheter that autonomously navigated to a leaking prosthetic valve in live pigs; a human operator still performed the therapeutic step.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous intracardiac catheter navigation. Cited to bound the state of autonomy — it covers navigation only, in an animal model, with the clinician performing the therapy, so it does not transfer to completing angioplasty and stenting.

sources.title: Autonomous Soft Robotic Guidewire Navigation via Imitation Learning
sources.claim: Autonomous endovascular guidewire navigation remains a laboratory capability validated in phantom vasculature with sub-clinical reliability (83% success reaching a target in unseen geometries).
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous guidewire navigation to a vascular target. Cited to show that even the navigation sub-step of angioplasty is only phantom-validated at reliability far below worker quality, and no autonomous system deploys balloons or stents.

sources.title: Advancements and challenges in autonomous endovascular interventional robotics: A comprehensive review
sources.claim: A 2025 comprehensive review of autonomous endovascular interventional robotics finds the field still constrained by imaging, physician dependence and device manipulation limits, i.e. autonomy is not established in clinical practice.

roles.title: Dermatologists
aliases: DO Physician (Doctor of Osteopathic Medicine Physician)
roles.description: Diagnose and treat diseases relating to the skin, hair, and nails. May perform both medical and dermatological surgery functions.

tasks.label: Conduct complete skin examinations.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Routine annual total-body skin cancer screening of an adult in a dermatology clinic exam room: gowned patient, dermatologist inspects head-to-toe (scalp with hair parted, ears, face, lips, trunk, axillae, buttocks/genital area, between toes, nails), applies a contact dermatoscope to atypical lesions, palpates lesions and lymph nodes, then documents findings and disposition (reassure, monitor, biopsy).

Complete skin exam of a high-risk patient (dysplastic nevus syndrome, prior melanoma, transplant recipient) with dozens to hundreds of nevi: exam combined with mole-mapping/total-body photography comparison and sequential digital dermoscopy, deciding which changed lesions warrant biopsy and marking them.

Complete skin exam of a patient presenting with a rash or generalized inflammatory dermatosis: assess morphology, distribution, scale and induration by palpation, check Nikolsky sign/diascopy, examine mucous membranes, nails, scalp, and formulate a differential diagnosis during the exam.

Pediatric complete skin exam in the clinic: infant or squirming toddler held by a parent, exam sequence improvised around the child's cooperation; birthmarks, hemangiomas, atopic dermatitis, diaper area and scalp inspected.

Bedside complete skin exam as an inpatient or long-term-care consult: patient in a hospital bed with limited mobility, must be log-rolled and repositioned, dressings, lines and gowns moved aside, variable room lighting; sacrum, heels, skin folds and feet inspected.
Head-to-toe screening exam at a community skin-cancer screening event or mobile screening van: brief, portable setup, members of the public partially disrobed, quick inspection and referral decision.

sources.title: SquareMind raises $18M for robotic dermatology platform - The Robot Report
sources.claim: SquareMind's Swan is a robotic arm that autonomously acquires standardized full-body dermoscopic-level images of a patient standing in a clinic exam room; it is an imaging device only — it does not touch the patient, part hair, inspect mucosa or nail folds, palpate, or render the diagnosis, which the dermatologist retains.
sources.transferJustification: Directly on task: whole-body skin imaging. It substantiates only the image-capture sub-step of a complete skin examination, not diagnosis, palpation, or inspection of hair-covered, mucosal, interdigital and intertriginous sites.

sources.title: SquareMind raises $18M led by Sonder Capital for its full-body skin-scanning robot — TFN
sources.claim: Reporting on the same system confirms that the robot's output is reviewed by physicians and that clinical judgment/diagnosis remains with the dermatologist, i.e., the machine does not deliver the examination's accepted output.

sources.title: Early detection of skin cancer with FotoFinder Bodystudio automated total body mapping (ATBM) - FV Hospital
sources.claim: The most widely deployed automated total-body mapping hardware (FotoFinder ATBM/bodystudio, a motorized camera system operated by clinic staff) is explicitly positioned as an aid that cannot substitute for the dermatologist's full-body skin exam.
sources.transferJustification: Same task (total-body skin examination). Cited as the deployed automated imaging system whose vendor/clinic documentation states it does not complete the exam.

sources.system: Vectra WB360 3D total-body photography with ML triage
sources.developer: Canfield Scientific / Memorial Sloan Kettering-led challenge
sources.title: Automated triage of cancer-suspicious skin lesions with 3D total-body photography | npj Digital Medicine
sources.claim: State-of-the-art automated analysis of 3D total-body photography (Vectra WB360, a fixed camera array rather than a moving machine) is framed and validated as triage that narrows lesions for expert evaluation, not as a replacement for the clinician's full-body examination.
sources.transferJustification: Same task domain. Shows the imaging-plus-AI pipeline still outputs a shortlist for dermatologist evaluation, and the capture device is a static camera apparatus, not a machine acting on the patient.

sources.title: Performance, Safety, and Patient Experience of an Autonomous Robotic Phlebotomy Device: A Multicenter Trial
sources.claim: Autonomous clinical robots that contact patient skin exist (a robotic phlebotomy device tested in a multicenter trial), but they operate on a single presented body part placed into a fixture and perform venipuncture, providing no capability for whole-body inspection, dermoscopic judgment, or diagnosis.
sources.transferJustification: Related task (autonomous robot acting on patient skin in a clinic). Transfer fails: it handles one fixtured arm for a needle stick and yields no skin-surface inspection or diagnostic assessment, so it cannot substantiate completion of a complete skin examination.

tasks.label: Diagnose and treat pigmented lesions such as common acquired nevi, congenital nevi, dysplastic nevi, Spitz nevi, blue nevi, or melanoma.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Office visit in a dermatology clinic exam room: patient points out a single mole of concern. Dermatologist takes history, palpates and inspects the lesion, applies a contact dermatoscope, judges it a benign common acquired nevus / blue nevus / seborrheic keratosis, reassures the patient, documents, and sets a return interval. No procedure performed.

Total-body skin examination of a higher-risk patient (many or clinically atypical/dysplastic nevi, prior melanoma, fair skin). Patient undresses and is repositioned; dermatologist inspects scalp, digits, buttocks, dermoscopes dozens of lesions, orders/compares total body photography and serial digital dermoscopy, and decides which lesions to monitor and which to sample.

Clinic procedure room: biopsy of a suspicious pigmented lesion. Mark site, inject local anesthetic, perform deep shave/saucerization or punch excision to full lesion depth, achieve hemostasis (electrocautery or suture), dress the wound, place and label the specimen for pathology, then review the dermatopathology report and communicate results and next steps.

Definitive treatment of a histologically confirmed melanoma or severely dysplastic nevus: wide local excision with prescribed margins on trunk, limb, or face in an office procedure room or ambulatory surgery suite, layered closure or flap/graft (or coordinated referral for sentinel node biopsy), plus staging and follow-up planning.

Pediatric or special-case evaluation in clinic: congenital melanocytic nevus or suspected Spitz nevus in a moving, uncooperative child. Measure and photograph the lesion over time, dermoscope through hair and irregular contour, counsel parents, and decide between observation, staged excision, or biopsy under sedation.

sources.developer: Dermavision Solutions (study at Hospital Clínic Barcelona)
sources.title: Autonomous Total Body Photography Device Shows Comparable Quality to Traditional Dermoscopic Imaging
sources.claim: An autonomous robotic total body photography and dermoscopic imaging device (DeviskanR, Dermavision Solutions) captured whole-body and dermoscopic images of patients in a hospital dermatology department with quality comparable to manual dermoscopy; diagnosis and management decisions were still made by dermatologists reading the images.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated skin image acquisition. It covers only the imaging sub-step of examining pigmented lesions; the device performs no palpation, produces no diagnosis itself (two dermatologists read the images), and performs no biopsy or excision, so it does not complete a diagnose-and-treat instance.

sources.title: SquareMind raises $18M for Swan skin imaging robot backed by Fred Moll's Sonder Capital
sources.claim: SquareMind's Swan robot uses a robotic arm to autonomously acquire standardized full-body dermoscopic images of a patient standing in a private clinic exam room; the accompanying AI supports review while physicians retain clinical judgment. The company was still raising money to bring the system to market.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic dermoscopic imaging of the whole skin surface in a clinic exam room. It substantiates only image capture; the diagnostic decision remains with the dermatologist and no treatment step is performed.

sources.system: ARTAS iX Robotic Hair Restoration System
sources.title: ARTAS Robotic Hair Transplants | Robotic FUE Hair Transplants
sources.claim: The ARTAS iX robot, FDA-cleared and in commercial use in hair-restoration clinics, autonomously images the scalp (stabilized by a skin tensioner), selects follicular units and punches ~1 mm cores; a physician gives the local anesthetic and technicians manually remove the dissected grafts.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: image-guided sub-millimetre punching of human skin in a clinic, the nearest deployed analogue to a punch biopsy. Transfer is only partial: ARTAS works on a shaved, tensioner-fixtured scalp of screened patients, does not diagnose lesions, does not anesthetize, does not retrieve or handle specimens, and does not close wounds, so it cannot complete a pigmented-lesion biopsy instance.

sources.title: Robot performs first realistic surgery without human help | Hub
sources.claim: State-of-the-art autonomous soft-tissue surgery remains at the animal/ex-vivo laboratory stage: Johns Hopkins' STAR performed autonomous laparoscopic bowel anastomosis in live pigs (2022) and SRT-H autonomously performed gallbladder-removal steps on pig cadaver tissue (2025). No autonomous robot performs skin excision or closure on human patients.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous soft-tissue cutting and suturing. It bounds the state of the art — laboratory animal/cadaveric tissue under research conditions — and therefore cannot substantiate autonomous biopsy or wide local excision of pigmented lesions on human patients in a clinic.

sources.title: The AI from Skin Analytics that caught 20,000 cancers in the UK is now certified for use on a standard smartphone
sources.claim: The only autonomous skin-cancer decision systems in clinical deployment are software: Skin Analytics' DERM issues autonomous clinical decisions on lesion images in NHS pathways, but the images are captured by a human clinician with a dermatoscope/smartphone, and the system performs no physical act.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous lesion triage. It is software-only — a human performs the physical imaging and all treatment — so under the definition used here it is not a robotic system and cannot support a positive judgment.

tasks.label: Perform incisional biopsies to diagnose melanoma.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Outpatient dermatology exam room: 3–4 mm punch biopsy of the most atypical/thickest portion of a large pigmented lesion on trunk or proximal extremity. Dermatologist marks the site, injects lidocaine with epinephrine, preps, punches full thickness to subcutis, lifts the plug with forceps and cuts its base with iris scissors, obtains hemostasis, places 1–2 sutures, and places/labels the specimen in formalin with an accurate requisition.

Outpatient exam room: scalpel incisional (elliptical) partial biopsy of a large (>1.5–2 cm) suspicious pigmented lesion on the back, shoulder, or thigh, oriented along skin tension lines, cut through dermis into fat, specimen removed intact with minimal crush artifact, undermining, electrocautery hemostasis, layered/simple suture closure, dressing and wound-care instructions.

Outpatient exam room: partial biopsy of a facial, ear, or scalp lesion (e.g., lentigo maligna on cheek/nose, near eyelid or vermilion), sometimes multiple scouting biopsies of one large lesion; thin, mobile, cosmetically sensitive skin over nerves and vessels; patient reclined or seated, talking, blinking, minor movement.

Outpatient exam room: broad shave (saucerization/scoop) partial biopsy of a broad flat pigmented macule, or biopsy of an acral lesion on palm/sole with thick stratum corneum; flexible blade or deep shave to appropriate depth to capture the base, aluminum chloride/cautery hemostasis, no sutures.

Procedure room: nail-unit biopsy for suspected subungual melanoma — digital block, tourniquet, nail plate avulsion or window, incisional biopsy of the pigmented matrix band a few millimeters wide, specimen oriented on paper/ink for pathology, hemostasis and bulky dressing.

Difficult-patient conditions in clinic or at hospital bedside consult: anxious or pediatric patient, tremor, dementia, wheelchair-bound or bedbound patient, obesity or awkward site (intertriginous fold, posterior scalp, back requiring prone positioning); biopsy performed with assistant holding/positioning, sometimes on anticoagulated skin that bleeds briskly.

sources.system: ARTAS / ARTAS iX (Restoration Robotics, now Venus Concept)
sources.title: RESTORATION ROBOTICS, INC. — THE ARTAS SYSTEM 510(k) Summary K103428
sources.claim: The ARTAS robotic hair-restoration system autonomously identifies, punches, dissects and extracts ~1 mm follicular-unit grafts from a live patient's scalp in a clinic, under physician supervision; it is FDA-cleared and commercially deployed in hair-restoration practices.
sources.transferJustification: Closest existing autonomous skin-penetrating procedure on live humans: image-guided punching of scalp skin in a clinic. It does not transfer to melanoma biopsy completion — the punch is 0.9–1.1 mm and hair-shaft-guided rather than 3–4 mm to subcutis at a physician-chosen atypical site, and the robot performs no anesthesia, no diagnostic specimen retrieval/labeling into formalin, no hemostasis and no closure.

sources.title: ARTAS Robotic Hair Restoration How It Works: The AI Decision Engine Explained Step by Step
sources.claim: ARTAS uses a coaxial 0.9 mm sharp inner punch and 1.1 mm blunt outer punch to score epidermis/upper dermis and dissect follicular units, i.e. shallow small-diameter punching rather than full-thickness diagnostic sampling.
sources.transferJustification: Documents the geometry and depth of the only commercially deployed autonomous skin-punching robot, showing it does not reach the depth or specimen-integrity requirements of a diagnostic melanoma biopsy.

sources.title: SquareMind Raises $18 Million to Redefine Skin Exams With Robotics and AI
sources.claim: The only robot commercialized for dermatology clinic exam rooms, SquareMind's Swan, performs contactless full-body dermoscopic imaging; it does not perform any invasive procedure, and dermatologists retain all diagnostic and procedural acts.
sources.transferJustification: Establishes the state of deployed dermatology robotics in the exact E2 setting of this task (clinic exam room): imaging only, no incision, anesthesia, tissue removal or wound closure.

sources.developer: Children's National / Sheikh Zayed Institute (Axel Krieger et al.)
sources.title: Supervised Autonomous In Vivo Robotic Surgery on Soft Tissues is Feasible and Outperforms Standard Surgery Techniques
sources.claim: The Smart Tissue Autonomous Robot ... supervised autonomous soft-tissue suturing/anastomosis in live anesthetized pigs in a research operating setting using near-infrared fluorescent markers placed on the tissue.
sources.transferJustification: Autonomous suturing is the closure step of an incisional biopsy, but the demonstration is on marked porcine bowel in an animal research OR, not on a human skin lesion, and covers no other step of the biopsy.

sources.system: SRT-H (Surgical Robot Transformer–Hierarchy) on da Vinci Research Kit
sources.title: SRT-H robot performs surgery without a human controlling its hands for the first time
sources.claim: Johns Hopkins' SRT-H executed the dissection phase of a gallbladder removal autonomously on ex vivo/lifelike tissue models in a laboratory, a 17-task sequence, reported in Science Robotics; it has not been used on live human patients.
sources.transferJustification: Represents the frontier of autonomous soft-tissue cutting/dissection; the environment is a lab bench with ex vivo tissue, so it does not substantiate completing a live-patient skin biopsy in any clinical setting.

sources.title: Blackdot creates AI-powered tattoo device to reduce pain
sources.claim: Blackdot's robotic tattoo machine autonomously drives needles into live human skin in commercial studios, computing penetration depth from imaging of the client's skin, with the client seated in a purpose-built chair.
sources.transferJustification: Shows machine-controlled, vision-guided penetration of living human skin in an institution-controlled facility, but ~0.25 mm ink-depositing punctures involve no tissue excision, anesthesia, hemostasis, closure, or handling of a pathology specimen, so it cannot complete a biopsy.

tasks.label: Perform skin surgery to improve appearance, make early diagnoses, or control diseases such as skin cancer.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Diagnostic skin biopsy in a dermatology clinic exam room: the dermatologist examines the patient, chooses which of several lesions to sample and the technique (shave, punch, or small excisional), marks the site, injects local anesthetic, cuts and removes tissue, obtains hemostasis (chemical or electrocautery) or places sutures, and labels/orients the specimen for pathology. Patient is awake, seated or reclined, may move; lesions occur anywhere on the body including face, ears, scalp, back.

Elliptical excision of a biopsy-proven skin cancer or atypical nevus with clinically judged margins in a clinic procedure room: sterile prep and drape, local anesthesia, design of the ellipse along tension lines, full-thickness excision into fat, undermining, hemostasis, and layered closure with buried absorbable and cutaneous sutures; sometimes a small flap or graft. Includes scar revisions and removal of cysts/lipomas.

Mohs micrographic surgery in a Mohs suite for facial/high-risk skin cancer: staged saucerized excision with beveled edges, tissue mapping, inking, frozen-section preparation and microscopic margin reading, repeat stages on residual tumor, then reconstruction of the defect (side-to-side closure, local flap, or skin graft) on curved facial anatomy near eyelid, nose, lip, or ear.

Destructive and minor office procedures in a clinic exam room: curettage and electrodesiccation of superficial basal/squamous cell carcinoma, cryosurgery of actinic keratoses and warts, incision and drainage of cysts/abscesses, nail surgery (matrixectomy, avulsion), and electrosurgical removal of benign growths. Rapid, multiple sites per visit, awake and sometimes squirming patients.

Cosmetic energy-device resurfacing treatment: a full-face ablative/non-ablative laser or IPL rejuvenation pass delivered in a clinic laser room, with the dermatologist setting fluence and passes, tracking coverage over the curved face, watching skin endpoints/temperature, and protecting eyes and sensitive zones.

Hair restoration surgery (follicular unit extraction) in a hair-restoration clinic: donor-area anesthesia and tensioner placement, punch dissection and harvesting of 1,000-2,500 follicular units, graft sorting, creation of thousands of recipient sites along a designed hairline, and graft implantation, over a multi-hour session with a technician team.

sources.title: Follicular unit extraction with the Artas robotic hair transplant system: an evaluation of FUE yield
sources.claim: The ARTAS robotic hair transplant system autonomously identifies and punch-dissects follicular units in the patient's scalp during FUE hair restoration surgery, without human hand control of the motion; evaluated clinically for graft yield and transection rate.

sources.system: ARTAS iX / iXi Robotic Hair Restoration System
sources.title: ARTAS Robotic Hair Restoration Treatments - Venus Treatments USA
sources.claim: ARTAS iX/iXi is FDA-cleared and sold to clinics for harvesting follicular units, creating recipient sites, and implanting ... during hair transplantation in men with androgenetic alopecia.

sources.developer: Restoration Robotics / Venus Concept (described by Bernstein Medical)
sources.title: Robotic Hair Restoration | ARTAS Robotic Hair Transplant - Bernstein Medical
sources.claim: In clinical use the physician programs punch parameters and supervises, while the robot's optical system scans the scalp, selects follicular units, and sets punch depth automatically; graft sorting and placement are still done by trained staff.

sources.system: Vision-guided skin photo-rejuvenation robot (Muddassir et al.)
sources.title: Robotics Meets Cosmetic Dermatology: Development of a Novel Vision-Guided System for Skin Photo-Rejuvenation
sources.claim: A vision-guided robot manipulator carrying a cosmetic laser, depth sensor and thermal camera autonomously planned and delivered a full facial photo-rejuvenation laser treatment on human volunteers in a laboratory rig.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: cosmetic laser resurfacing/rejuvenation of facial skin. It uses the same class of energy device, the same curved facial anatomy and the same coverage/endpoint control as a dermatologist's resurfacing pass, but it does not cut, anesthetize or close tissue, so it does not transfer to incisional skin surgery.

sources.developer: Children's National Health System / Johns Hopkins
sources.title: Supervised autonomous robotic soft tissue surgery (record)
sources.claim: The STAR system performed supervised-autonomous soft-tissue suturing and bowel anastomosis in live pigs in a research operating setup; it is a sub-step demonstration in animals, not a complete human skin excision and closure.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous suturing of soft tissue. It shares the closure sub-step of excisional skin surgery, but was done on porcine bowel in a research setup with fluorescent markers and covers none of lesion selection, margin judgment, excision, hemostasis or human-quality cutaneous closure.

sources.title: Blackdot's AI Tattoo Machine is Essentially a Robot That Inks Your Skin
sources.claim: Blackdot's AERO robot autonomously maps a client's skin and drives a needle to a controlled depth to place tattoo dots on living human skin in commercial tattoo studios.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: image-guided needle penetration of living human skin at controlled depth. It shows a robot can safely puncture patient skin autonomously, but a tattoo deposits ink at fixed shallow depth and involves no lesion selection, anesthesia, tissue removal, hemostasis or specimen handling, so it does not substantiate biopsy or excision.

tasks.label: Counsel patients on topics such as the need for annual dermatologic screenings, sun protection, skin cancer awareness, or skin and lymph node self-examinations.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

tasks.label: Diagnose and treat skin conditions such as acne, dandruff, athlete's foot, moles, psoriasis, or skin cancer.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Outpatient clinic exam room: medical management visit for a common inflammatory or infectious skin condition (acne, eczema, psoriasis, seborrheic dermatitis/dandruff, tinea pedis). History-taking, visual inspection and palpation of affected skin across variable body sites, occasional bedside test (KOH scraping, Wood's lamp), diagnosis, prescription/injection plan and counseling.

Outpatient clinic exam room: skin cancer screening or 'mole check'. Patient gowned; total-body or focused inspection with handheld dermoscopy, palpation of lesions and nodes, comparison with prior photos/mole maps, diagnosis of benign vs suspicious lesions, and disposition (reassure, monitor, or biopsy).

Clinic procedure room: diagnostic biopsy of a suspicious lesion. Consent, site marking, lidocaine infiltration, shave or 3-4 mm punch biopsy on curved/mobile sites (nose, back, shin), hemostasis or suture, specimen orientation and labeling for pathology, dressing and aftercare instructions.

Clinic exam/procedure room: destruction of benign or premalignant lesions — liquid-nitrogen cryotherapy of multiple actinic keratoses, warts, or seborrheic keratoses, or curettage/electrodesiccation, judging each lesion's identity, freeze time and margin on the fly across many sites on one patient.

Clinic procedure/surgical suite: definitive surgical treatment of skin cancer — excision with marked margins, or Mohs stages with tissue mapping and frozen-section reading, followed by layered closure or flap/graft repair on the face or trunk under local anesthesia.

Clinic or hospital ward consult: injectable and light-based therapy — intralesional triamcinolone into keloids/cysts/alopecia areata patches, drainage of an inflamed cyst, or initiation and dosing of phototherapy/biologic for extensive psoriasis, including bedside inpatient rash consults.

sources.system: FDA-cleared surgical robots (49 systems, LASR classification)
sources.developer: Mount Sinai / Sinai BioDesign review (Lee, Baker, Bederson, Rapoport)
sources.title: Levels of autonomy in FDA-cleared surgical robots: a systematic review (npj Digital Medicine)
sources.claim: Systematic review of all FDA-cleared surgical robots (Dec 2023 database search) finds none above Level 3 conditional autonomy; the only Level 3 systems execute surgeon-approved plans for bone milling, prostate biopsy, and hair follicle extraction — none diagnoses or treats skin disease end to end.
sources.transferJustification: Comprehensive census of clinically cleared surgical robots; establishes that no cleared robot performs autonomous diagnosis or cutaneous procedures (biopsy, excision, closure) on patients, the physical core of this task.

sources.system: ARTAS / ARTAS iX robotic hair restoration system
sources.title: Robotic Hair Restoration | ARTAS Robotic Hair Transplant (Bernstein Medical)
sources.claim: ARTAS iX is a commercially deployed, image-guided robotic arm that automatically dissects follicular units from a patient's scalp in a clinic, but it operates under direct physician supervision and performs only part of the procedure.
sources.transferJustification: Closest deployed robot that cuts human skin under image guidance in a dermatologic clinic; cited to show even this best case handles one sub-step on a fixtured scalp with the physician diagnosing, anesthetizing, planning and finishing — it does not complete a diagnose-and-treat encounter.

sources.system: ARTAS robotic hair restoration (AI decision engine)
sources.developer: Venus Concept (described by Charles Medical Group)
sources.title: ARTAS Robotic Hair Restoration How It Works: The AI Decision Engine Explained Step by Step
sources.claim: ARTAS's automation is explicitly supervised: the physician can intervene, override or adjust parameters in real time, and the vendor-facing description states the system is not fully autonomous.
sources.transferJustification: Clarifies the autonomy level of the most dermatology-adjacent clinical robot; supervision-plus-partial-scope means it cannot stand in for the dermatologist across a whole instance.

sources.title: Hopkins robot is first to perform laparoscopic surgery without assistance from humans
sources.claim: The Smart Tissue Autonomous Robot performed laparoscopic soft-tissue anastomosis on live pigs without human guidance — the frontier of autonomous soft-tissue surgery, achieved in an animal research setting, not on human patients or skin.
sources.transferJustification: Related task (autonomous soft-tissue cutting and suturing); shows autonomous surgery on deformable living tissue exists only as animal-model research, so it cannot substantiate worker-quality biopsy, excision or closure on human patients.

sources.title: Blackdot's AI Tattoo Machine is Essentially a Robot That Inks Your Skin
sources.claim: Blackdot's automated tattoo device autonomously drives a needle into human skin in a commercial studio, mapping the skin surface with camera and laser and executing an operator-loaded design at ~250-micron precision.
sources.transferJustification: Related task (repeated precise needle penetration of living human skin under machine vision). It shows automated skin puncture is feasible on a positioned client, but the machine executes a pre-specified pattern on flat prepared skin — it makes no clinical judgment, removes no tissue, and manages no wound, so it does not transfer to diagnosing and treating skin disease.

sources.title: The World's First Autonomous AI Skin Cancer Detector Approved for Use in Europe
sources.claim: DERM is an autonomous AI that makes independent skin-cancer diagnostic decisions from lesion images and is deployed in the NHS, but it is software running on cameras/smartphones with no manipulator, and it performs no treatment.
sources.transferJustification: Shows the diagnostic half of the task is being automated only by software-only image analysis, which is explicitly not a robotic system and cannot deliver the biopsy, cryotherapy, excision or injection that the task's treatment half requires.

tasks.label: Instruct interns or residents in diagnosis and treatment of dermatological diseases.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Clinic-based precepting in an academic dermatology outpatient clinic: the resident sees the patient first and presents; the attending re-examines the rash or lesion with the resident present, questions the resident on the differential, explains the morphologic clues (distribution, scale, border, dermoscopic pattern), and states the reasoning behind the chosen work-up and therapy. Purpose is served by the verbal/visual explanation.

Procedural teaching in a minor-procedures or Mohs suite: attending talks a resident through a shave/punch biopsy, excision, layered closure, or cryotherapy — describing anatomy, margins, suture choice and pitfalls, correcting technique verbally, and occasionally scrubbing in; the therapeutic act itself is the resident's, the attending's task is the coaching and evaluation of it.

Formal didactics: grand rounds, Kodachrome/clinical-image conferences, board-review sessions, morning report and journal club, where the attending presents cases and images to a group of residents and interns, quizzes them, and explains diagnostic algorithms and treatment guidelines.

Dermatopathology sign-out and slide teaching: attending and resident review glass slides at a multi-headed microscope or on whole-slide digital images, with the attending explaining histologic criteria, clinicopathologic correlation, and how findings change management.

Inpatient consult service and hospital-floor teaching rounds: attending leads residents to see hospitalized patients with severe drug eruptions, cellulitis mimics, blistering disease or graft-versus-host disease, teaching bedside assessment, urgency triage and systemic therapy decisions, then giving written/verbal feedback and evaluations.

tasks.label: Provide therapies such as intralesional steroids, chemical peels, or comodo removal to treat age spots, sun damage, rough skin, discolored skin, or oily skin.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Intralesional corticosteroid injection in a dermatology office exam room: keloid or hypertrophic scar, inflamed acne cyst, alopecia areata patch or prurigo nodule. Dermatologist selects lesions, chooses triamcinolone concentration and volume, inserts a 30G needle into the dermal plane freehand on a curved, mobile body site (earlobe, sternum, scalp, jawline), and injects to a blanching endpoint judged by tissue resistance and visible frosting, repeating at several points while managing patient flinching and pain.

Superficial-to-medium chemical peel of the face (sometimes hands, chest) for photodamage, lentigines, dyschromia or oily skin, in a clinic or physician-supervised medspa treatment room: degrease skin, protect eyes/nares, apply glycolic/salicylic/Jessner/TCA solution evenly with gauze or brush in a set regional sequence, watch continuously for erythema and frost endpoints, fan/cool the patient through the sting, then neutralize or rinse at the right moment.

Liquid-nitrogen cryotherapy of age spots and sun damage (lentigines, actinic keratoses, seborrheic keratoses) in a clinic exam room: pick out which of many lesions on face, scalp, forearms or dorsal hands to treat, aim a cryospray gun or cotton-tipped applicator a few centimeters from the skin, freeze each lesion for a timed interval to a target ice-ball halo, and repeat over 5-30 lesions on a moving, uncomfortable patient.

Comedo extraction / acne surgery in a clinic exam room: after warm compress or a nick with an 18G needle or blade tip, the clinician presses a comedone extractor loop or fingers around each open/closed comedone or milium on the face, nose, back or chest, expressing contents lesion by lesion under a magnifying lamp, blotting and disinfecting, and stopping when a lesion will not express to avoid scarring.

In-office light- or laser-based treatment of pigmentation and photodamage (IPL photofacial, Q-switched/picosecond laser toning, low-fluence resurfacing pass) in a clinic or medspa laser room: eye shields placed, settings chosen for skin type, then uniform pulse-by-pulse coverage of facial cosmetic subunits with overlap control, extra passes on individual lentigines, watching for endpoint erythema/darkening and patient tolerance.

sources.system: Vision-guided robotic skin photo-rejuvenation system (Muddassir et al., PolyU ROMI-Lab)
sources.title: Robotics Meets Cosmetic Dermatology: Development of a Novel Vision-Guided System for Skin Photo-Rejuvenation (IEEE/ASME Trans. Mechatronics)
sources.claim: A vision-guided 6-DOF robot with a depth sensor, thermal camera and Q-switched Nd:YAG laser end-effector autonomously planned and delivered facial photo-rejuvenation laser shots on human volunteers in a university laboratory, achieving more uniform coverage than an experienced practitioner.
sources.transferJustification: Directly relevant to the light/laser instance: Q-switched Nd:YAG toning of facial skin treats the same targets (pigmentation, photodamage) named in the task, on the same object (a live human face), and the paper benchmarks coverage against an experienced practitioner.

sources.title: A Comparative Study on the Application of Robotic Hair Restoration Technology Versus Traditional Follicular Unit Excision in Male Androgenetic Alopecia
sources.claim: The ARTAS robotic hair restoration system uses a multi-axis arm, imaging and AI to identify and punch out individual follicular units from a patient's scalp with 0.1 mm repeatability; it is FDA-cleared and in routine commercial use in hair-restoration clinic procedure rooms under physician supervision.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: image-guided robotic needle/punch work in living human skin inside a clinic room. It shows precise, autonomous skin penetration on patients, but it removes follicles rather than delivering a dosed drug or judging a tissue endpoint, so it does not by itself substantiate intralesional therapy.

sources.system: Blackdot automated tattooing device (also branded AERO at Bang Bang, NYC)
sources.title: Blackdot's AI Tattoo Machine is Essentially a Robot That Inks Your Skin - TechEBlog
sources.claim: Blackdot's robotic tattoo machine maps the client's skin surface with a camera and laser and then autonomously drives a needle to deposit ink into the dermis at controlled depth; machines are in commercial operation in an Austin studio and at a New York tattoo studio.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: repeated autonomous intradermal needle insertion depositing a substance into living human skin at controlled depth in a commercial human-facing studio. It covers the mechanics of skin penetration but not drug dosing, lesion selection, or blanching/tissue endpoints required for intralesional steroid therapy.

sources.title: Luum Precision Lash: the 200 Best Inventions of 2024 - TIME
sources.claim: Luum's autonomous lash robot performs precise cosmetic work millimeters from a reclining paying client's eye in a commercial salon, having applied more than 160,000 eyelash ....
sources.transferJustification: Related task: sub-millimeter robotic manipulation on a live human face in a structured commercial facility. It establishes that face-adjacent robotic service work is feasible in an E2 setting, but the end-effector handles lash fibers, not caustic peel agents, extractors, or syringes.

sources.system: Robotic laser resurfacing / micro-needling platforms (field-level status)
sources.title: Robotic-Assisted Procedures in Cosmetic Dermatology (Journal of Cosmetic Dermatology)
sources.claim: A 2024 review of robotic-assisted cosmetic dermatology reports that, apart from hair-restoration systems, robotic platforms for laser skin resurfacing and ... remain in trial phases rather than clinical deployment.
sources.transferJustification: Context for negative judgments: documents that no robotic system for the resurfacing/peel/injection class of dermatologic therapies has moved past trials into clinical use.

tasks.label: Provide dermabrasion or laser abrasion to treat atrophic scars, elevated scars, or other skin conditions.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Fractional ablative laser resurfacing (CO2 or Er:YAG) of atrophic acne scars on the face in a dermatology office procedure room: topical anesthetic and/or nerve blocks, corneal eye shields, smoke evacuation, physician varies density/energy zone by zone (cheeks vs. temples vs. periorbital), monitors tissue whitening/contraction, feathers treatment into untreated skin.

Fractional laser treatment of hypertrophic, keloid, surgical, or burn scars on trunk or extremities in a clinic treatment room, often combined with laser-assisted delivery of triamcinolone/5-FU: irregular contoured scar tissue of varying thickness, per-scar parameter selection, treating raised edges more aggressively than surrounding skin.

Full-field ablative laser resurfacing (CO2/erbium) for perioral rhytides, photodamage or actinic damage, in an office surgical suite or ambulatory center under local anesthesia with sedation: multiple passes, wiping desiccated tissue between passes, judging depth by tissue color and drag, stopping at papillary/upper reticular dermis.

Motorized dermabrasion with a diamond fraise or wire brush for elevated/raised scars, scar revision, rhinophyma, or traumatic tattoo, in an office surgical suite: skin chilled/tensioned by assistants, bloody field, tactile and visual endpoint (punctate bleeding), feathering edges to avoid demarcation lines.

Focal laser ablation/vaporization of small lesions or single scars (seborrheic keratoses, sebaceous hyperplasia, syringomas, small scar spot treatment) in a brief office visit with the patient seated: lesion-by-lesion targeting, local anesthetic, ablate-and-wipe cycles until the lesion is level with surrounding skin.

sources.developer: Kassir et al., Journal of Cosmetic Dermatology (review of multiple developers)
sources.title: Robotic-Assisted Procedures in Cosmetic Dermatology - Kassir - 2024 - Journal of Cosmetic Dermatology
sources.claim: A 2024 peer-reviewed review of robotics in cosmetic dermatology states that robotic systems for laser skin ... (the closest analogue to laser abrasion) are still in trial phases, while robotic hair restoration is the deployed application.
sources.transferJustification: Directly about the technology class for laser abrasion; establishes that robotic laser resurfacing has not reached clinical deployment as of 2024.

sources.system: Vision-guided robotic skin photo-rejuvenation prototype (industrial manipulator with laser end-effector)
sources.developer: Jinan University Dept. of Dermatology + Hong Kong Polytechnic University / RODS Technology
sources.title: A Split-face Study of Novel Robotic Prototype vs Human Operator in Skin Rejuvenation Using Q-switched Nd:Yag Laser: Accuracy, Efficacy and Safety
sources.claim: A vision-guided robotic prototype delivered Q-switched 1064 nm laser photo-rejuvenation to one half of the faces of 17 human subjects in a university dermatology department, compared against a human practitioner on the other half; the robot was slower than the human operator and achieved only ~60% laser coverage.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robot-delivered facial laser treatment in a dermatology clinic. It is the closest robotic laser-on-face work, but the modality is non-ablative toning with no tissue-removal endpoint, and reported coverage (~60%) and speed fell short of the human operator, so it does not substantiate completion of ablative laser abrasion.

sources.system: Automated facial skin rejuvenation robotic prototype
sources.title: Robotics Meets Cosmetic Dermatology: Development of a Novel Vision-Guided System for Skin Photo-Rejuvenation
sources.claim: The same group's engineering paper describes the system as an automated facial skin rejuvenation ... built on an industrial manipulator with depth camera, proximity sensors and laser, tested on human subjects' faces alongside a human operator.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous laser scanning of a human face in a lab/clinic. Demonstrates trajectory planning over facial contours but only for non-ablative light delivery; it is a research prototype, not a system delivering ablative resurfacing at clinical quality.

sources.title: The Future Of Robotics In Aesthetic Medicine | The AEDITION
sources.claim: EON by Dominion Aesthetic is an FDA-cleared, touchless robotic laser body-contouring system used in aesthetic clinics: a robotic arm scans the patient's body, maps the area, and the laser then treats autonomously for abdominal fat reduction.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous robotic laser energy delivery onto human skin in a clinic. Transfer is limited: EON heats subcutaneous fat non-ablatively over a large flat abdomen at fixed parameters, with no tissue-removal endpoint, no per-zone parameter variation, and no work on contoured facial scars, so it does not substantiate laser abrasion of scars.

sources.title: ARTAS ® Robotic Hair Restoration Treatments | Venus Treatments
sources.claim: ARTAS is an FDA-cleared autonomous robotic system deployed in hair restoration clinics that harvests hair follicles from the scalp with a robotic arm, but it is cleared only for follicular unit harvesting in patients with black or brown straight hair.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous robotic instrument work on live human skin in a clinic with sub-millimetre accuracy, on a tensioner-fixated scalp patch. It shows the environment is achievable but not the capability: punch harvesting of follicles guided by follicle image detection does not establish ablative depth/endpoint control over contoured scarred skin.

sources.title: AI and Robotic Lasers | The Future of Laser Hair Removal – Aesthetic Allure
sources.claim: Commercially offered robotic-arm skin laser platforms for hair removal are operator-directed cobots: the practitioner controls the robotic arm through a tablet application while cameras model the patient.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic delivery of a dermatologic laser to skin in a clinic. It is operator-directed rather than autonomous, so under the autonomy rule it cannot support a positive judgment for laser abrasion.

sources.title: Revolutionizing Aesthetic Medicine and Dermatology with Artificial Intelligence | Modern Aesthetics
sources.claim: The most advanced autonomous robot for facial aesthetic procedures reported in trade press as of 2025, LENA, performs botulinum toxin injections and is described in hedged terms, indicating demonstration rather than routine clinical delivery.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous robotic procedure on a patient's face in an aesthetic clinic. Injection point targeting differs from ablative resurfacing, and the reporting is hedged with no clinical outcome data, so it cannot substantiate completion of laser abrasion.
