tasks.label: Evaluate patients to determine eligibility for cosmetic procedures such as liposuction, laser resurfacing, or microdermabrasion.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Facial laser resurfacing / IPL consult in a private dermatology clinic exam room: dermatologist takes cosmetic and medical history (isotretinoin, herpes labialis, recent tanning, keloid tendency, anticoagulants), inspects the face under bright light and magnification, palpates skin texture, laxity and scarring, assigns Fitzpatrick phototype, screens for suspicious lesions in the treatment field, counsels on risks/downtime and renders a documented eligibility decision.

Eligibility check for superficial procedures (microdermabrasion, chemical peel, dermaplaning) in a clinic or physician-supervised medspa: brief hands-on skin assessment for active acne/rosacea flare, dermatitis, herpes, recent retinoid or sun exposure, skin sensitivity; approve, modify depth/agent, or defer.

Body-contouring / liposuction candidacy evaluation: gowned patient examined standing and supine; pinch test of subcutaneous fat depth, assessment of skin laxity and cellulite, palpation for hernia or diastasis, BMI and weight-stability review, prior surgical scars, standardized photography and area marking, review of comorbidities and anesthesia risk, then go/no-go and alternative recommendation.

Higher-risk or complicated candidate: darker phototypes with post-inflammatory hyperpigmentation risk, keloid history, autoimmune/connective-tissue disease, prior fillers or surgery with palpable nodules, active dermatosis, or unrealistic expectations/body dysmorphic features; requires more detailed exam, possible test spot or labs, and often a declination or altered plan.

Day-of-procedure re-evaluation in the treatment room: verify no new contraindications (sun exposure, cold sore, pregnancy, new medication), inspect and palpate the treatment area, perform a laser test spot and assess the response, confirm final clearance and settings.
Virtual/photo-based cosmetic consultation for a patient at home: review submitted images and history questionnaire by video, give provisional candidacy opinion pending an in-person confirmatory exam.

sources.title: SquareMind raises $18M for robotic dermatology platform - The Robot Report
sources.claim: SquareMind's Swan is a robotic arm in a private dermatology exam room that autonomously acquires standardized full-body dermoscopic-level images of a patient's skin; it is contactless imaging only, the physician retains all clinical judgment, and it was still preparing for commercial launch in April 2026.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated full-body skin-lesion imaging and documentation in a dermatology exam room. It is the closest robotic system operating on patients' skin in this setting, but it performs only a contactless imaging sub-step (no palpation, no history-taking, no risk counselling) and the article states physicians retain full clinical judgment, so it does not complete a cosmetic-eligibility determination.

sources.title: SquareMind Raises $18 Million to Redefine Skin Exams With Robotics and AI (Business Wire)
sources.claim: Swan's image acquisition is automated and paired with AI review software, but clinical decision-making remains with the physician.
sources.transferJustification: Same related task as above (robotic skin imaging); cited to establish that the automated part is image capture and that the eligibility/clinical judgment step is not automated.

sources.system: Robotic telemedical examination system (Franka Emika arms, Module C)
sources.developer: University hospital research consortium (clinical evaluation study)
sources.title: Toward telemedical diagnostics—clinical evaluation of a robotic examination system for emergency patients
sources.claim: A telemedical robotic examination cabin evaluated on emergency patients performs auscultation, percussion and palpation of ... chest and abdomen, but every movement is controlled in real time by a remote physician through a lead robot (continuous teleoperation).
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robot-mediated hands-on physical examination of a patient in a controlled clinical cabin. It shows that even structured robotic patient examination is achieved only under continuous teleoperation, so it cannot support an autonomous positive judgment for hands-on cosmetic eligibility exams.

sources.system: Autonomous robotic palpation via ergodic exploration (force/torque-sensed manipulator)
sources.title: Autonomous Robotic Tissue Palpation and Abnormalities Characterisation via Ergodic Exploration (arXiv)
sources.claim: State-of-the-art autonomous robotic palpation for stiffness mapping is validated only in simulation and on a silicone phantom with ..., not on patients.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous palpation to characterise soft-tissue properties, the closest analogue to pinch-testing fat and assessing skin laxity. Validation is confined to silicone phantoms in a lab, so it does not substantiate patient-quality assessment in any clinical setting.

roles.title: Emergency Medicine Physicians
roles.description: Make immediate medical decisions and act to prevent death or further disability. Provide immediate recognition, evaluation, care, stabilization, and disposition of patients. May direct emergency medical staff in an emergency department.

tasks.label: Select, request, perform, or interpret diagnostic procedures, such as laboratory tests, electrocardiograms, emergency ultrasounds, and radiographs.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Undifferentiated adult in an ED room (chest pain, dyspnea, abdominal pain): after history/exam the physician selects and orders the workup (troponin/CBC/chemistry, ECG, chest X-ray or CT), reads the ECG within minutes, reviews lab and imaging results at the ED workstation, and often adds a brief bedside cardiac/lung/aortic ultrasound before deciding disposition.

Critically ill or trauma resuscitation in an ED resus bay: physician personally performs and interprets an eFAST and cardiac POCUS on a moving, partly undressed patient on a gurney amid a team, with c-collar, monitor leads and lines in the way, and simultaneously orders and interprets ABG, portable chest/pelvis radiographs and stat labs within minutes.

Low-acuity fast-track patient (sprain, laceration, cough, dysuria): physician decides which limited tests are needed, orders extremity or chest radiographs and point-of-care urine/pregnancy/glucose tests, gives the preliminary radiograph read, and occasionally does soft-tissue ultrasound for abscess or retained foreign body.

Pediatric patient in the ED: physician chooses a radiation-sparing pathway (ultrasound rather than CT), performs or requests bedside ultrasound on a crying, moving child with a parent present, and interprets labs and imaging against age-specific norms.

Focused single-question bedside ultrasound on a stable, cooperative adult in a quiet ED room (abdominal aorta screen for aneurysm, IVC/volume assessment, hydronephrosis check, DVT compression study): physician positions the patient supine, acquires the standard views and gives an immediate yes/no interpretation.

Diagnostics performed outside the department: in an ambulance or during transport, at an EMS scene, at a mass gathering or disaster deployment, or an austere/rural site, where the physician performs and interprets ultrasound and point-of-care tests with no hospital infrastructure and variable lighting, space and patient positioning.

sources.developer: Tsinghua University / Beijing Tsinghua Changgung Hospital group (Zihan Li et al.)
sources.title: Beyond hospital reach: Autonomous lightweight ultrasound robot for liver sonography
sources.claim: A 588-g cable-driven autonomous ultrasound robot with an AI agent autonomously acquired standard liver/abdominal planes (including aorta, IVC and portal vein planes) and detected pathology in patients; it was first deployed in a hospital ultrasound department for feasibility evaluation.
sources.transferJustification: Liver/abdominal scanning uses the same probe handling and the same target structures (aorta, IVC) as emergency point-of-care ultrasound, on a supine cooperative patient in a clinical exam room, so acquisition capability transfers to a focused EM aorta/IVC study.

sources.system: Large-scale learning-based autonomous carotid ultrasonography robotic system
sources.title: Towards expert-level autonomous carotid ultrasonography with large-scale learning-based robotic system
sources.claim: A learning-based robotic system carried out fully automated carotid artery ultrasound examinations on human volunteers (122 recruited, 41 in the test set), producing biometric measurements described as approaching expert level.
sources.transferJustification: Autonomous vascular ultrasound acquisition on human necks is the closest published analogue to a physician-performed focused vascular POCUS study (DVT compression, aorta), with comparable probe pressure control and standard-view requirements.

sources.system: Fully autonomous robotic ultrasound system for thyroid scanning
sources.title: A fully autonomous robotic ultrasound system for thyroid scanning
sources.claim: A fully autonomous robotic ultrasound ... scanned thyroid regions on human subjects without sonographer control in a clinical research setting.
sources.transferJustification: Superficial-organ autonomous scanning demonstrates machine-controlled probe placement and image-quality servoing on real people, which is the acquisition half of a physician-performed focused ultrasound exam.

sources.title: Current Status and Pending Developments of Robotic Tele-Echocardiography
sources.claim: A 2025 state-of-the-art review of robotic tele-echocardiography states that autonomous robot-assisted ultrasound replacing the sonographer is still speculative; clinically used robotic ultrasound is remote/human-controlled.
sources.transferJustification: Cardiac ultrasound is a core emergency POCUS application; the review characterises the autonomy frontier for exactly the acquisition step an EM physician performs.

sources.developer: Pilot clinical validation study group (European Heart Journal - Cardiovascular Imaging)
sources.title: Robotic assisted echocardiography, a pilot clinical validation study
sources.claim: Clinical robotic echocardiography validated in patients uses a robot arm holding the probe under continuous human (sonographer) control rather than autonomous scanning.
sources.transferJustification: Same organ and exam type as emergency cardiac POCUS; shows the clinically used form of robotic cardiac ultrasound is human-driven and cannot support an autonomous positive judgment.

sources.title: Vitestro Raises $70 Million in Oversubscribed Series B Financing to Advance Autonomous Robotic Phlebotomy and Commercial Readiness
sources.claim: Aletta, a CE-marked autonomous robotic phlebotomy device, performs the whole blood-draw sequence with the patient's arm fixtured in the device and is being deployed in clinical and ... blood-collection settings in Europe; a multicentre trial reported about 95% first-stick success.
sources.transferJustification: Blood collection is the physical acquisition step of performing laboratory tests; it shows the most mature autonomous diagnostic-acquisition robot handles only a narrow fixtured sub-step in a purpose-built station, not test selection or interpretation.

sources.system: Autonomous trauma diagnostic/interventional robot (Al-Zogbi, IMERSE Lab)
sources.title: When Minutes Matter: Robot Tackles Trauma's Silent Killer
sources.claim: A research robot that autonomously initiates a FAST ultrasound scan for internal haemorrhage during pre-hospital transport is under development at Johns Hopkins; its validation has used 3-D-printed torso phantoms rather than emergency patients.
sources.transferJustification: Directly targets the emergency FAST exam in this task, but as a laboratory prototype tested on phantoms it shows autonomous trauma ultrasound remains pre-clinical.

sources.system: GE HealthCare / NVIDIA autonomous imaging concepts
sources.title: GE HealthCare introduces advanced imaging solutions powered by NVIDIA technology to support timely diagnoses and streamlined clinical workflows
sources.claim: Autonomous X-ray and autonomous ultrasound from a major imaging vendor remain early-stage exploratory concepts shown for clinician feedback at RSNA 2025, not systems performing exams.
sources.transferJustification: Radiography acquisition is one of the diagnostic procedures named in this task; the source shows no autonomous radiographic system is performing exams as of the rating date.

tasks.label: Evaluate patients' vital signs or laboratory data to determine emergency intervention needs and priority of treatment.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

tasks.label: Perform emergency resuscitations on patients.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Adult non-traumatic cardiac arrest arriving at the ED resuscitation bay: physician runs the code — checks pulse/rhythm, directs and verifies compression quality, defibrillates, orders and often personally places an advanced airway, obtains IV/IO access, pushes epinephrine/antiarrhythmics, performs point-of-care echo to find reversible causes (tamponade, PE, hyperkalemia), and decides on ROSC care or termination of efforts.

Critically ill medical patient in the ED in shock or impending respiratory failure (sepsis, massive GI bleed, overdose, anaphylaxis, severe asthma/COPD, status epilepticus): physician performs rapid-sequence intubation, sets ventilation, places central and arterial lines, starts fluids/blood and vasopressors, and titrates to hemodynamic response while the patient moves, vomits, or fights.

Major trauma resuscitation in the trauma bay: physician manages a bloody, immobilized patient — airway with cervical-spine precautions, tube thoracostomy, FAST exam, massive transfusion activation, pelvic binder, hemorrhage control, occasionally resuscitative thoracotomy or REBOA — while simultaneously directing nurses, techs, and consultants under time pressure.

Pediatric or neonatal resuscitation in the ED: small, uncooperative or limp patient, weight-based drug and equipment sizing, difficult small-caliber airway and vascular access (often intraosseous), bag-mask ventilation, precordial thump-free ACLS/PALS algorithms, and parental presence in the room.

Resuscitation outside the controlled department: physician response at the scene or in the field (EMS medical direction, mass-casualty or disaster site, ambulance/helicopter transfer, hospital parking lot or public space at the hospital entrance), with improvised positioning, limited equipment and uncontrolled bystanders and conditions.

sources.title: What Is the LUCAS Device? Mechanical CPR Explained - Biology Insights
sources.claim: Mechanical CPR devices (LUCAS 3) autonomously deliver sustained chest compressions once a human rescuer positions the device on the patient; they are deployed in EDs, ambulances and cath labs. They cover only the compression sub-step of a resuscitation, not airway, access, diagnosis, drug decisions, or team direction.
sources.transferJustification: Related sub-task: mechanical chest compressions are one component of an emergency resuscitation. It does not transfer to the whole task because a human must expose the chest, position the device, and perform every other element of the resuscitation.

sources.developer: Hemmerling et al., McGill University / MUHC
sources.title: First robotic tracheal intubations in humans using the Kepler intubation system - British Journal of Anaesthesia
sources.claim: Robotic tracheal intubation has been performed in humans only under joystick teleoperation from a remote workstation, in a pilot study of 12 consenting elective operating-room patients (2012); no autonomous robotic intubation of emergency patients has been shown.
sources.transferJustification: Related sub-task: emergency airway management. It does not substantiate the task because the human trials were teleoperated, elective, and in an operating room, with no crash-airway conditions.

sources.system: ReFit (Resuscitation based on Functional Hemodynamic Monitoring) / TRACIR
sources.developer: University of Pittsburgh with Carnegie Mellon University
sources.title: Autonomous medical intervention extends 'golden hour' for traumatic injuries with emergency air transport | ScienceDaily
sources.claim: The most advanced autonomous resuscitation research system, ReFit within the TRACIR program, autonomously administered fluids, blood and drugs to hemorrhaging pigs in a laboratory/animal-transport setting; it is a closed-loop infusion controller, not a system that performs procedures on human patients.
sources.transferJustification: Related sub-task: hemodynamic resuscitation of hemorrhagic shock. It does not transfer: the demonstration was in anesthetized swine with vascular access already established, and covers no airway, procedural, diagnostic, or team-leadership element.

sources.system: AURA-CVC autonomous ultrasound-guided robotic central venous catheterization
sources.title: AURA-CVC: Autonomous Ultrasound-guided Robotic Assistance for Central Venous Catheterization
sources.claim: Autonomous ultrasound-guided central venous catheterization remains at the phantom-validation stage and still requires operator feedback in the loop; no clinical deployment on emergency patients is shown.
sources.transferJustification: Related sub-task: emergent vascular access during resuscitation. It does not transfer because validation was on a static phantom with operator feedback, not on a moving, hypotensive human patient.

sources.title: Smart Tissue Autonomous Robot performs laparoscopic surgery on pig soft tissue without human help
sources.claim: The frontier of autonomous robotic intervention on soft tissue is laparoscopic suturing performed by STAR on anesthetized pig bowel in a laboratory operating theatre — a fixtured, single-procedure setting far removed from a multi-procedure human resuscitation.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous invasive intervention on living soft tissue. It marks the ceiling of demonstrated autonomy — one planned procedure on a prepared, immobile, anesthetized animal — and therefore does not substantiate an unscripted multi-procedure resuscitation.

tasks.label: Stabilize patients in critical condition.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Cardiac arrest in the ED resuscitation bay: physician leads ACLS — directs/performs chest compressions, bag-mask and endotracheal intubation, rhythm interpretation and defibrillation, IV/IO access and drug pushes, bedside echo for cardiac standstill, decision to continue or terminate resuscitation.

Critically ill medical patient (septic shock, respiratory failure, DKA, overdose): rapid-sequence intubation of a moving, vomiting or hypoxic patient, central line or IO placement, fluid/vasopressor titration, ventilator setup, repeated reassessment over 30-90 minutes in a crowded resus room.

Major trauma resuscitation: primary/secondary survey, external hemorrhage control and tourniquet/pelvic binder, FAST ultrasound, chest tube or needle decompression, airway control with cervical spine precautions, massive transfusion activation, coordination with surgery, all with a bloody, clothed, agitated patient and a 6-10 person team.

Acute decompensation stabilized without invasive procedures: severe asthma/COPD, flash pulmonary edema, anaphylaxis — positioning, oxygen and BiPAP mask fitting, nebulizers, IM epinephrine/IV nitrates, continuous monitoring and titration until the patient turns around.

Time-critical cardiac/neurologic emergency: STEMI, unstable arrhythmia, large-vessel-occlusion stroke, status epilepticus — exam, procedural sedation and synchronized cardioversion or transcutaneous pacing, thrombolytic administration, airway protection, packaging and handoff for cath lab / thrombectomy / transfer.

sources.title: Safety of mechanical chest compression devices AutoPulse and LUCAS in cardiac arrest: a randomized clinical trial for non-inferiority
sources.claim: Mechanical chest-compression devices (LUCAS piston, AutoPulse load-distributing band) deliver automated chest compressions to cardiac arrest patients in EDs and prehospital care once clinicians position them on the patient; they automate one sub-step of resuscitation only, not airway, drugs, diagnosis or decision-making.
sources.transferJustification: Related sub-task (mechanical chest compressions during cardiac arrest). Cited to show the state of the art automates only one component of resuscitation; the device must be applied by clinicians and performs no assessment, airway, vascular access or drug therapy.

sources.title: A soft robotic device for rapid and self-guided intubation | Science Translational Medicine
sources.claim: A non-electronic soft robotic device self-guides an endotracheal tube into the trachea, demonstrated in airway models and human cadavers, not in live emergency patients; it still must be introduced into the mouth by a human operator.
sources.transferJustification: Related sub-task (emergency airway management). Shows that even the single most-automatable procedure in stabilization is at cadaver/model demonstration stage and requires a human to place and drive the device.

sources.system: auto-RUSS autonomous robotic ultrasound scanning system
sources.developer: Chinese hospital/university research group (Frontiers in Robotics and AI)
sources.title: Autonomous robotic ultrasound scanning system: a key to enhancing image analysis reproducibility and observer consistency in ultrasound imaging
sources.claim: An autonomous robotic ultrasound scanning ... using a 7-DOF arm with force control and visual servoing acquired standard views on healthy volunteers in a research setting; it addresses image acquisition reproducibility, not resuscitative decision-making or intervention.
sources.transferJustification: Related sub-task (bedside ultrasound such as FAST/echo during resuscitation). Cited to show autonomous patient-contact imaging exists only on cooperative healthy volunteers in controlled research settings, far from a bloody, moving crashing patient.

sources.title: Hopkins robot is first to perform laparoscopic surgery without assistance from humans
sources.claim: The most advanced autonomous soft-tissue robotic surgery to date performed laparoscopic bowel anastomosis on an anesthetized pig under human supervision in a laboratory operating room; no comparable system operates on human emergency patients.
sources.transferJustification: Related task (autonomous invasive procedure on soft tissue). Establishes the ceiling of autonomous robotic intervention on a living body: a pre-positioned, anesthetized, surgically exposed animal — far more structured than an undifferentiated critical patient.

tasks.label: Perform such medical procedures as emergent cricothyrotomy, endotracheal intubation, and emergency thoracotomy.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Adult rapid-sequence endotracheal intubation in a hospital ED resuscitation bay for a medical indication (respiratory failure, altered mental status, overdose, sepsis): pre-oxygenate, position, dose and push induction/paralytic, video or direct laryngoscopy, pass the tube, confirm with waveform capnography, secure and set the ventilator.

Airway secured during an active resuscitation in the ED: cardiac arrest with ongoing chest compressions, or blunt/penetrating trauma with cervical-spine immobilization, blood, vomit or secretions in the pharynx, hypotension, and a crowded team working around the stretcher.

Anticipated difficult airway in the ED (morbid obesity, angioedema, facial or neck trauma, airway burns, distorted anatomy): adjunct- or awake-technique intubation with bougie, hyperangulated blade or flexible scope, and a double set-up for surgical rescue.

Pediatric or neonatal emergency intubation in the ED: weight-based drug dosing, size-specific blades and tubes, very small margin for tube size and depth, rapid desaturation, distressed family at the bedside.

Other emergent invasive procedures grouped with these in the ED: tube thoracostomy for pneumo/hemothorax, ultrasound-guided central venous or intraosseous access, pericardiocentesis, transvenous pacing - sterile prep, landmark/ultrasound guidance, incision or needle puncture, device placement and confirmation.

Rare open surgical rescue in the ED: emergent cricothyrotomy for a can't-intubate-can't-oxygenate airway (neck incision, trachea entry, tube placement in under a minute), or resuscitative thoracotomy for traumatic arrest (thoracotomy incision, rib spreading, pericardiotomy, internal cardiac massage, aortic cross-clamp).

sources.title: Emerging technologies in airway management: a narrative review of intubation robotics and anatomical structure recognition algorithms
sources.claim: The Kepler Intubation System, the only robotic intubation platform used for human tracheal intubation (12 anesthetized elective patients with normal airways), is a joystick-driven master/slave device in which a clinician drives the laryngoscope arm; the procedure is teleoperated, not autonomous, and a separate 'semiautomated' mode only replayed a pre-recorded trajectory on a mannequin.

sources.system: surveyed intubation robots (KIS, RNIS, Leng, Lai and others)
sources.developer: multiple academic groups (review published in BioMedical Engineering OnLine)
sources.title: Emerging technologies in airway management: a narrative review of intubation robotics and anatomical structure recognition algorithms - PubMed
sources.claim: A 2025 narrative review of intubation robots and airway anatomy-recognition AI finds the field still pre-clinical: systems remain in testing/validation, and recognition models trained on stable airways degrade in difficult airways, prehospital care and emergency departments where blood, secretions and abnormal anatomy are present.

sources.developer: Haggerty, Hawkes et al., UC Santa Barbara
sources.title: UCSB-designed soft robot intubation device could save lives | The Current
sources.claim: The UCSB soft robotic intubation system self-steers a tube toward the trachea, but it is a non-electronic hand-deployed instrument that a human operator (physician, EMT or paramedic) inserts and holds; testing was on mannequins and cadavers rather than live patients, and it covers only tube passage, not patient assessment, drug administration, confirmation or post-intubation care.

sources.system: HNNet cricothyroid-membrane detection with robot arm (SAVER-inspired first-aid airway system)
sources.title: Autonomous Cricothyroid Membrane Detection and Manipulation Using Neural Networks and a Robot Arm for First-Aid Airway Management, J. Med. Devices
sources.claim: The most advanced robotic work toward a surgical airway is a laboratory prototype that autonomously locates the cricothyroid membrane with a neural network and drives a robot arm to a waypoint within 5 mm; it does not incise the skin, open the membrane or place a tube in a patient.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic first-aid cricothyrotomy. It is the closest published work to emergent surgical airway, but it demonstrates only landmark perception and arm positioning in a lab, so it does not transfer to completing an incision-and-tube surgical airway on a hypoxic patient.

sources.developer: Johns Hopkins University / Children's National Hospital
sources.title: Smart Tissue Autonomous Robot performs laparoscopic surgery on pig soft tissue without human help
sources.claim: STAR performed autonomous laparoscopic small-bowel anastomosis on live pigs in a research operating room under human supervision, with the tissue marked and the field prepared - an elective, planned soft-tissue sub-step rather than an unplanned emergency procedure on a human patient in extremis.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous soft-tissue surgery (cutting and suturing), the capability class an emergency thoracotomy, chest tube or cricothyrotomy would require. Transfer fails: the demonstration is on anesthetized animals in a prepared, fixtured surgical field under supervision, unlike a time-critical resuscitative procedure.

sources.title: SRT-H: A Hierarchical Framework for Autonomous Surgery via Language-Conditioned Imitation Learning
sources.claim: SRT-H, the current frontier of autonomous surgery, executed the dissection and clipping phase of a cholecystectomy fully autonomously on eight ex vivo pig gallbladders mounted on a laboratory bench with a da Vinci research kit; there is no live human patient, no whole procedure, and no emergency context.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous execution of surgical steps. It shows learned autonomy on prepared ex vivo tissue only; emergency airway and thoracotomy demand live, bleeding, moving patients, sub-minute timing and clinical judgment, so the capability does not carry over.

tasks.label: Consult with hospitalists and other professionals, such as social workers, regarding patients' hospital admission, continued observation, transition of care, or discharge.

tasks.label: Conduct primary patient assessments that include information from prior medical care.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Main ED treatment room, undifferentiated adult complaint (chest pain, dyspnea, abdominal pain): physician takes the history, reviews the EMS run sheet, prior ECGs, discharge summaries and outside records in the EHR, performs a hands-on focused exam (auscultation, palpation, pulses, skin, extremities), and forms an initial assessment and plan.

Resuscitation/trauma bay, critically ill or injured patient arriving by ambulance: primary survey (airway patency, breath sounds, pulses/perfusion, GCS/pupils, exposure and log roll) performed hands-on within minutes while integrating the prehospital handoff and any available prior records, directing a team.

Fast-track / minor care area: laceration, sprain, URI, UTI, back pain. Brief history, chart review for allergies, medications, prior imaging and past visits, focused physical exam of the affected area, initial assessment.

Patient who cannot give a history — nursing-home transfer with altered mental status/dementia, nonverbal pediatric patient, or intoxicated patient: physician reconstructs the story from transfer paperwork, family, and prior records and performs a full head-to-toe exam on a sometimes uncooperative patient.

Behavioral-health or agitated patient in a secure ED room: medical screening assessment including review of prior psychiatric admissions and medication history, vital signs and a physical exam conducted with security/nursing present and limited patient cooperation.

Assessment outside a standard ED room — hallway bed during boarding surge, ambulance bay, or field/disaster triage — with crowding, poor lighting, limited equipment and fragmentary prior-care information.

sources.developer: MITI Research Group, University Hospital rechts der Isar / TU Munich
sources.title: Toward telemedical diagnostics—clinical evaluation of a robotic examination system for emergency patients
sources.claim: A robotic telemedical examination cabin with robotic arms was used on real emergency-department patients for vital signs, auscultation, palpation and percussion, but the physician sits in a remote cockpit and controls all devices, i.e. the examination is teleoperated.
sources.transferJustification: Directly the target task's physical component (examination of ED patients); cited to show the closest existing system is remotely driven, not autonomous.

sources.system: Dr. Spot (Boston Dynamics Spot with contactless vital-sign payload)
sources.developer: Boston Dynamics with MIT and Brigham and Women's Hospital
sources.title: Why Boston Dynamics Is Putting Legged Robots in Hospitals - IEEE Spectrum
sources.claim: 'Dr. Spot' carries contactless vital-sign sensors and a tablet so a clinician can interview and triage patients remotely; the medical judgment and interview are performed by the human operator over telepresence.
sources.transferJustification: Related task = remote triage/vital-sign capture in an ED; cited because it is the best-known hospital robot touching patient assessment, and it is a telepresence extension of a human clinician rather than an autonomous examiner.

sources.system: Humanoid surrogate for medical interventions (Unitree H1-based teleoperation system)
sources.developer: UC San Diego (Yip lab) with UCSD School of Medicine
sources.title: Humanoids in Hospitals: A Technical Study of Humanoid Robot Surrogates for Dexterous Medical Interventions
sources.claim: A humanoid robot performed auscultation, abdominal palpation, bag-valve-mask ventilation and intubation on manikins/phantoms in a laboratory, entirely under human teleoperation.
sources.transferJustification: Related task = hands-on physical examination maneuvers (auscultation, palpation) that form part of a primary assessment; cited to show that even these sub-steps are demonstrated only under continuous teleoperation on simulators.

sources.system: auto-RUSS autonomous robotic ultrasound scanning system (7-DoF arm)
sources.developer: academic group (Lin et al., Frontiers in Robotics and AI)
sources.title: Autonomous robotic ultrasound scanning system: a key to enhancing image analysis reproducibility and observer consistency in ultrasound imaging
sources.claim: An autonomous robotic ultrasound scanning ... acquired standard imaging planes on healthy volunteers with force control and visual servoing, showing autonomy for one imaging sub-step only, not history-taking, records review, or an overall clinical assessment.
sources.transferJustification: Related task = autonomous contact-based imaging of a patient's body, a possible adjunct to bedside assessment; cited as the strongest autonomous patient-contact evidence found, which still covers only a narrow imaging sub-step on cooperative healthy volunteers.

tasks.label: Monitor patients' conditions, and reevaluate treatments, as necessary.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Mid-workup reassessment of an undifferentiated adult in an ED treatment bay (e.g., abdominal pain, chest pain, dyspnea): physician returns after labs/imaging return, repeats a focused hands-on exam (abdominal palpation, lung/heart auscultation, checking for new tenderness or edema), rechecks vitals on the monitor, questions the patient about symptom change, and then adds, stops, or changes therapy or moves to disposition.

Critically ill patient in the resuscitation bay (septic shock, respiratory failure, GI bleed, DKA): near-continuous surveillance of telemetry, pressors, ventilator/BiPAP, urine output and repeat blood gases; repeated bedside exams (perfusion, mental status, breath sounds); titration of vasopressors, fluids, insulin and vent settings; escalation to intubation, central line, transfusion, or procedural intervention as the trajectory changes.

Low-acuity recheck after a therapeutic intervention (analgesic, antiemetic, nebulizer, IV fluids): physician revisits the patient 30-60 minutes later, asks about symptom relief, repeats a brief targeted exam (lung sounds, work of breathing, pain on palpation), reviews repeat vitals/pulse oximetry, and decides to re-dose, add therapy, or discharge.

Reassessment of boarded or hallway/waiting-room patients in a crowded ED: patients are in corridor stretchers or lobby chairs, often without continuous monitoring, with family and staff traffic around them; the physician periodically checks in, reviews intermittent vitals and nursing reports, performs a quick exam, and adjusts orders or upgrades acuity if the patient is deteriorating.

Serial reassessment of a trauma patient: secondary/tertiary survey, wound, splint and neurovascular checks, repeat FAST ultrasound, repeat hemoglobin and vitals, log-roll and pain reassessment, with decisions about CT, transfusion, operative consult, or transfer.

Reassessment of an agitated, intoxicated, or psychiatric patient: repeated evaluation of mental status and sedation depth, airway and vital-sign monitoring after chemical sedation, restraint and skin checks, re-dosing sedation or determining medical clearance for psychiatric evaluation, with an uncooperative or combative patient.

sources.system: 'Dr. Spot' (Boston Dynamics Spot with contactless vital-sign payload)
sources.developer: MIT / Brigham and Women's Hospital / Boston Dynamics
sources.title: Brigham and Women's Hospital, MIT use Spot to measure patient vitals (The Robot Report / MIT News)
sources.claim: The best-known robotic patient-monitoring deployment in an emergency department (Spot carrying contactless vital-sign sensors and a telepresence tablet in Brigham and Women's COVID triage tents) was driven by a human operator, with the clinical questioning done by a remote physician; it measured vitals only and did not reassess treatment.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: contactless vital-sign measurement and remote interview of ED patients. It is the closest robotic analogue to bedside monitoring, but it is teleoperated and covers only data capture, not the hands-on exam or the treatment-change decision, so it cannot substantiate completion of this task.

sources.title: Feasibility study on full closed-loop control ventilation (IntelliVent-ASV) in ICU patients with acute respiratory failure - PubMed
sources.claim: Commercial closed-loop ventilation (INTELLiVENT-ASV) autonomously monitors a ventilated patient and adjusts oxygenation and ventilation settings in ICU patients, but it controls a single therapy channel rather than performing a physician's global reassessment.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated titration of one therapy (ventilator settings) in response to monitored physiology, inside a hospital (E2). It shows machine control of a sub-step only; it performs no bedside examination and makes no decisions about other treatments, diagnostics, or disposition, so it cannot complete a whole reassessment instance.

sources.developer: Joosten, Rinehart, Cannesson et al. (academic, Paris-Saclay/UCLA)
sources.title: Control of mean arterial pressure using a closed-loop system for norepinephrine infusion in severe brain injury patients: the COMAT randomized controlled trial
sources.claim: A closed-loop vasopressor infusion system autonomously titrated norepinephrine to a mean arterial pressure target in ICU patients in a randomized trial, again demonstrating automation of a single physiologic control loop rather than full patient reassessment.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated titration of a vasopressor to a hemodynamic target in critical care. It substantiates machine control of one narrow treatment parameter but not the multi-domain monitoring, physical reexamination and treatment-change judgment that the physician task requires.

sources.system: auto-RUSS autonomous robotic ultrasound scanning system (7-DOF arm)
sources.developer: academic research group (published in peer-reviewed journal, indexed on PMC)
sources.title: Autonomous robotic ultrasound scanning system: a key to enhancing image analysis reproducibility and observer consistency in ultrasound imaging
sources.claim: Robotic ultrasound scanning, one hands-on element of bedside reassessment, is still at research stage: autonomous scanning pipelines are being evaluated against physicians in study settings rather than deployed for clinical reassessment.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous acquisition of ultrasound images on a human body, comparable in contact and precision to a repeat bedside FAST/lung scan. It remains a study-stage single-modality acquisition tool and does not perform interpretation-driven reassessment or treatment change.

sources.title: AI nursing robot Nurabot helps Taiwan hospitals combat global healthcare shortage (Fox News)
sources.claim: Hospital-deployed autonomous robots in 2025-2026 perform logistics and patrol tasks (medication and sample delivery, ward patrol, visitor guidance), not patient assessment or treatment decisions.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous mobile work inside a hospital ward (E2). It establishes that hospital robots can navigate clinical space autonomously, but their demonstrated scope excludes physical examination, clinical judgment, and treatment reevaluation.

roles.title: Family Medicine Physicians
aliases: DO Physician (Doctor of Osteopathic Medicine Physician)
Family Medicine PCP (Family Medicine Primary Care Physician)
roles.description: Diagnose, treat, and provide preventive care to individuals and families across the lifespan. May refer patients to specialists when needed for further diagnosis or treatment.

tasks.label: Prescribe or administer treatment, therapy, medication, vaccination, and other specialized medical care to treat or prevent illness, disease, or injury.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Point-of-care prescribing during a routine office visit in a clinic exam room: after evaluating an adult or child, the physician selects a drug, dose, route and duration (antibiotic, antihypertensive, statin, inhaler, antidepressant, insulin titration), checks allergies/interactions/renal dosing and formulary, and transmits an e-prescription to the pharmacy. The act is a licensed clinical decision entered into the EHR; no manipulation of the patient.

Asynchronous or remote prescribing from the clinic office or home workstation: refill authorizations from pharmacy queues, portal-message prescribing, prior authorizations, controlled-substance renewals with PDMP checks, and prescribing at the end of a telehealth visit. Purely decision plus order entry, often in batches of dozens per day.

Administering an injection or vaccination to a cooperative adult in the clinic: influenza/Tdap/shingles/COVID vaccine, B12, depot contraceptive, allergy or IM ketorolac. Physician (or physician acting without support staff) verifies patient, screens contraindications, draws up or takes a prefilled syringe, positions the deltoid/hip, injects, applies a bandage, documents in EHR/registry, and observes for reactions.

Immunizing or treating infants and young children in a clinic exam room: weight-based dosing, multiple simultaneous injections into the thigh, an uncooperative squirming child held by a parent, comforting and distraction, plus post-injection assessment. Also pediatric acute treatment (antipyretic dosing, nebulized albuterol on a crying toddler).

In-office procedures and acute treatments in a clinic procedure room: intra-articular/bursal corticosteroid injection, laceration irrigation and suturing with local anesthetic, abscess incision and drainage, cryotherapy of warts, skin lesion biopsy/removal, IUD insertion, nebulizer treatment, IM epinephrine for anaphylaxis, wound dressing. Tissue is soft and variable; sterile technique and hemostasis required.

Prescribing and treating away from the clinic: nursing-home rounds (order changes, wound care, injections at bedside in cluttered resident rooms), house calls or home-based primary care in patients' homes, and inpatient/hospital-at-home orders. Layout and equipment vary site to site.

sources.title: Aletta for Hospital Leadership - Vitestro
sources.claim: Vitestro's Aletta autonomously performs the complete diagnostic blood-draw procedure on adult patients — vein selection through needle insertion to bandaging — in hospital and laboratory draw rooms, with one human supervisor overseeing up to three devices.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: venipuncture rather than injection. Transfer to adult vaccination/IM injection is close — same setting (institutional outpatient draw/injection room), same object (an unrestrained adult arm), same core act (autonomous imaging-guided needle placement, procedure completion, bandaging), and IM deltoid injection requires less targeting precision than cannulating a vein.

sources.title: Vitestro raises $70m to fuel blood-drawing robot's global commercial readiness - Medical Device Network
sources.claim: Aletta received EU CE marking in 2024 and was launched in European healthcare settings in March 2025; pivotal-trial interim data showed 95% first-stick success, comparable to skilled human phlebotomists.
sources.transferJustification: Same transfer as above: establishes worker-quality reliability and real institutional deployment for an autonomous needle procedure performed on adult patients in a structured clinical facility.

sources.title: Waterloo startup performs first ever robotic intramuscular injection | Waterloo News
sources.claim: The Cobi platform performed an intramuscular vaccine injection on a person fully autonomously using a needle-free jet injector, with no healthcare professional involved; it remained a working prototype rather than a marketed product.

sources.title: Robot Inoculators Accelerate China's Vaccine Rollout - Sixth Tone
sources.claim: Sanofi unmanned vaccination booths trialled in Chinese clinics ran a full flu-vaccination workflow — temperature check, health questionnaire, then machine administration of the injection to an arm placed in a robotic stirrup.
sources.transferJustification: Same task (vaccine administration) but the degree of machine control versus attendant assistance is not documented, so it is treated as unclear and used only as corroboration.

sources.title: Preliminary Evaluation of an Ultrasound-Guided Robotic System for Autonomous Percutaneous Intervention
sources.claim: Fully autonomous end-to-end needle placement for ultrasound-guided percutaneous interventions (the class that includes joint, bursal and spinal injections) has not been validated in any clinical system; work remains at proof-of-concept level.
sources.transferJustification: Directly bears on office needle procedures (joint/bursa injection, aspiration): documents that no cited system performs these autonomously on humans.

sources.title: Robot performs first realistic surgery without human help | Hub, Johns Hopkins
sources.claim: The Smart Tissue Autonomous Robot performed autonomous laparoscopic soft-tissue surgery only on live pigs in a research setting; the 2025 successor executed a realistic procedure on ex vivo tissue, not on human patients in a clinic.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous soft-tissue suturing, the nearest analogue to office laceration repair. It shows the capability exists only in animal/ex vivo laboratory work, not at clinic quality on human patients.

sources.title: MEDICAL POLICY – 1.01.30 Automated Insulin Delivery Systems (Premera)
sources.claim: FDA-cleared automated insulin delivery systems (e.g., Omnipod 5, Tandem Control-IQ) autonomously compute and deliver insulin doses to patients at home without clinician intervention, but only for this one drug and only after a physician prescribes the regimen.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous dose determination and drug administration. It covers only continuous subcutaneous insulin in a patient already prescribed the device, so it does not substantiate a physician's prescribing instance across the drug formulary.

tasks.label: Order, perform, and interpret tests and analyze records, reports, and examination information to diagnose patients' condition.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Chronic-disease / preventive visit result management in a family medicine office: physician orders labs (A1c, lipid panel, CMP, TSH, urine ACR) in the EHR, then reviews returning results in the inbox against the chart, prior trends and medications to decide whether a new condition (e.g., CKD stage 3, hypothyroidism, prediabetes) is present and what further testing is needed.

Acute illness office visit: physician takes history and examines the patient, then performs or directs an in-office point-of-care test (rapid strep or COVID/flu antigen swab, urine dipstick/micro, fingerstick glucose, pregnancy test), reads the result at chairside and integrates it with exam findings to reach a diagnosis and decide on confirmatory testing.

Complex or undifferentiated presentation (e.g., fatigue with weight loss, abnormal outside imaging, multi-specialty patient): physician analyzes outside records, consult notes, radiology and pathology reports and prior labs, sequences a diagnostic workup, and interprets the returned imaging/lab results in clinical context to arrive at a diagnosis.

In-office diagnostic test or minor diagnostic procedure performed by the physician in the exam room: obtaining and interpreting a 12-lead ECG, office spirometry, tympanometry/audiometry, point-of-care ultrasound, dermoscopy with shave/punch biopsy for pathology, or joint aspiration for analysis — then interpreting the tracing/specimen result to diagnose.

Automated in-office screening test amenable to autonomous instrumentation: annual diabetic retinal imaging performed on an automated fundus camera in the primary care office and read to determine whether referable diabetic retinopathy is present, documented as the diagnostic result.

sources.transferJustification: Directly on task: the system performs the test (automated retinal image acquisition) and interprets it to render a diagnostic determination that the physician would otherwise make.

sources.transferJustification: Establishes the physically embodied, machine-controlled component (motorized alignment and capture on a live patient) that pairs with the autonomous diagnostic software.

It substantiates only the sample-collection sub-step in a blood-draw center; it does not order tests, interpret results, analyze records, or produce a diagnosis, so it cannot support completion of any whole instance.

sources.transferJustification: Related task (obtaining a specimen for a point-of-care test). It covers only the swabbing sub-step in a research protocol with an operator supervising; it does not run the assay, integrate exam findings, or diagnose.

sources.transferJustification: Related task (performing a clinical examination to gather diagnostic information). Cited to show the state of the art is teleoperated prototypes, which cannot support a positive judgment.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Outpatient clinic visit for an acute common problem (URI, influenza, UTI, suspected community-acquired pneumonia): take history, review vitals, perform focused physical exam (lung/heart auscultation, throat/ear, abdominal palpation), order/interpret point-of-care test or chest x-ray, prescribe antibiotics/antivirals or supportive care, counsel patient, document and arrange follow-up.

Outpatient chronic disease management visit (hypertension, type 2 diabetes, hyperlipidemia, stable CHF/COPD): review home readings and labs, measure/recheck BP, cardiopulmonary auscultation, edema and diabetic foot exam, titrate medications, order labs/imaging, counsel on adherence and lifestyle, e-prescribe.

Visit with a complex multimorbid older adult (clinic or nursing facility): multiple interacting conditions, polypharmacy reconciliation, cognitive and functional assessment, gait/frailty check, hands-on exam, goals-of-care discussion with family, coordination of specialist care and home services.

Inpatient/hospitalist-style management of an acutely ill adult (pneumonia, CHF exacerbation, cellulitis, sepsis on a general ward): daily bedside exam, review of monitor/lab trends, adjustment of IV antibiotics/diuretics, occasional bedside procedure (e.g., paracentesis, arterial stick), coordination with nursing and discharge planning.

Telehealth/remote management episode: video or phone visit plus review of remote monitoring and portal messages for an acute minor illness or stable chronic condition; no hands-on exam, medication adjustment and e-prescribing, referral if needed.

sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic physical examination, a component of managing and treating illness. It does not transfer to whole-task completion because it is teleoperated and covers only isolated exam manoeuvres, with no history-taking, diagnostic reasoning, or treatment decisions.

sources.title: Performance, Safety, and Patient Experience of an Autonomous Robotic Phlebotomy Device: A Multicenter Trial
sources.claim: An autonomous robotic phlebotomy device (Vitestro Aletta) was evaluated in a multicenter trial in hospital outpatient phlebotomy departments, showing autonomous robots can perform a narrow diagnostic sub-step in a structured healthcare facility.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: venipuncture for diagnostic testing in the same clinic/hospital setting. It substantiates only a single mechanical sub-step of workup; it provides no capability for examination, diagnosis, prescribing, or longitudinal management, so it cannot substantiate completion of this task.

sources.system: Autonomous lightweight ultrasound robot for liver sonography
sources.developer: Tsinghua University / Beijing Tsinghua Changgung Hospital research team
sources.title: Beyond hospital reach: Autonomous lightweight ultrasound robot for liver sonography
sources.claim: An autonomous ultrasound robot performed liver sonography on human subjects in a hospital ultrasound department, demonstrating autonomous robotic acquisition of one diagnostic imaging modality in a clinical setting.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous diagnostic imaging acquisition, one input to managing illness. It does not transfer to the whole task: the robot acquires images of one organ and does not take a history, examine broadly, decide therapy, or prescribe.

sources.title: Diligent Robotics completes 300,000 pharmacy deliveries with Moxi
sources.claim: The largest commercial fleet of autonomous mobile manipulators in US hospitals performs logistics (pharmacy, lab specimen and supply delivery), not clinical assessment or treatment of patients.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous mobile manipulation inside hospitals. It shows what deployed hospital robots actually do (transport), and by contrast confirms no deployed system undertakes physician-level assessment, diagnosis, or treatment.

sources.title: Primary care player Forward shuts down
sources.claim: The most prominent purpose-built automated clinic (a self-contained 'doctor-in-a-box' pod intended to deliver primary care with hardware-based testing) ceased operations after technical failures including self-service blood draws, indicating no working machine-run clinic that manages and treats illness.
sources.transferJustification: Directly relevant: the CarePod was the closest attempt at bringing the patient to a purpose-built machine for primary-care evaluation. Its failure and shutdown mean no cited system completes the task even under an E1 counterfactual.

tasks.label: Provide and manage long-term, comprehensive medical care, including diagnosis and nonsurgical treatment of diseases, for adult patients in an office or hospital.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Scheduled outpatient follow-up in a clinic exam room for an adult with chronic conditions (hypertension, type 2 diabetes, hyperlipidemia, CKD): review interval history and home readings, review labs, perform focused physical exam (cardiac/pulmonary auscultation, edema check, diabetic foot exam), adjust medications, order labs/referrals, counsel patient, and document the encounter.

Outpatient visit for a new or acute complaint (cough, chest pain, abdominal pain, dizziness, rash): take history, perform relevant physical exam (abdominal palpation, throat/ear exam, neuro exam, lymph node palpation), order or perform point-of-care testing (ECG, urinalysis, swab), form a differential, decide on treatment or referral/admission, and prescribe.

Annual comprehensive/preventive visit for an adult: full head-to-toe physical examination, vital signs and body measurements, screening review (cancer screening, immunizations), risk counseling, and updating the long-term care plan.

Daily inpatient rounding on hospitalized adults on a medical ward: bedside assessment and exam of a patient with pneumonia, heart failure, sepsis or delirium, synthesis of overnight events, labs, imaging and nursing reports, adjustment of IV fluids/antibiotics/anticoagulation, discussion with patient and family, coordination with consultants, and discharge planning.

Bedside diagnostic or therapeutic procedure as part of nonsurgical care in hospital or office: e.g., paracentesis, thoracentesis, lumbar puncture, joint aspiration/injection, central line placement, or wound/abscess care — including consent, ultrasound guidance, sterile technique, specimen handling, and post-procedure assessment.

Longitudinal care visit outside the clinic or ward: rounds at a skilled nursing facility or a house call to a homebound elderly patient, performing exam and medication reconciliation in a variable, uncontrolled setting with family caregivers present.

sources.claim: State-of-the-art humanoid robots performing physician-type bedside acts (auscultation, abdominal palpation, ultrasound-guided injection, intubation) do so only under bi-manual human teleoperation in an exploratory feasibility study, not autonomously.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic performance of physical-examination maneuvers and bedside procedures that are components of the internist's encounter. It shows the most capable embodied demonstrations of these components remain fully teleoperated, so they cannot support autonomous completion of the physician task.

sources.title: Vitestro Raises $70 Million in Oversubscribed Series B Funding to Commercialize Autonomous Robotic Blood Drawing Tech
sources.claim: The most mature autonomous clinical-contact robot in routine use, Aletta, performs only one narrow physical step — routine diagnostic venipuncture — in hospital and outpatient phlebotomy departments; it does no history-taking, examination, diagnosis, or treatment management.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: an autonomous needle procedure on a seated patient in a clinical facility. It bounds current capability — an autonomous robot can execute a single, highly standardized contact step, but nothing in the source indicates diagnostic reasoning, examination, or longitudinal treatment management.

sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous physical contact examination of a patient's body region with image interpretation. It is the closest robotic analogue to a physician's exam, but covers one organ-specific imaging step rather than the whole encounter of history, exam, diagnosis and treatment.

sources.transferJustification: Related task: delivering a physician encounter at the bedside of hospitalized adults. Autonomy covers only locomotion; the medical work is performed by a remote human physician, so it cannot substantiate autonomous completion of inpatient rounding.

sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous mobile robot work inside the same hospital wards where internists round. It establishes what autonomous hospital robots actually do there (transport), showing no deployed system performs bedside clinical assessment or treatment management.

tasks.label: Examine patients to obtain information about functional status of areas, such as vision, physical strength, coordination, reflexes, sensations, language skills, cognitive abilities, and mental status.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Outpatient neurology clinic, comprehensive new-patient examination in an exam room: fundoscopy and cranial nerve testing, MRC-graded strength testing against the examiner's resistance, deep tendon reflexes with a hammer, pinprick/vibration/proprioception, finger-to-nose and heel-to-shin, Romberg, tone, and observed gait, on a cooperative ambulatory adult, ~15-20 minutes.

Clinic follow-up, focused exam for a known disorder (Parkinson's disease, MS, neuropathy): passive limb manipulation for rigidity/spasticity, tremor provocation, rapid alternating movements and UPDRS-style motor items, monofilament and vibration testing of feet, tandem gait and pull test, graded against prior visits.

Inpatient hospital consultation at the bedside: patient supine with IV lines, telemetry leads, sometimes restraints, often confused, aphasic or partially uncooperative; the neurologist repositions the patient, coaxes effort, and tests strength, reflexes, sensation and mental status in whatever position is possible, repeating over the admission.

Emergency department acute stroke code: NIH Stroke Scale performed in minutes on a gurney in a crowded resuscitation bay with the patient possibly agitated, vomiting or collared, testing gaze, visual fields, facial palsy, limb drift, ataxia, sensation, language and neglect, with the score driving thrombolysis decisions.

ICU exam of a comatose or sedated ventilated patient: pupillary light reflexes, corneal reflexes, oculocephalic/oculovestibular testing, gag and cough via suction catheter, motor response to central and peripheral noxious stimulation, tone and reflexes, often as a serial or brain-death-protocol assessment.

Memory/cognitive clinic assessment: MoCA or similar bedside cognitive battery plus language and praxis testing administered conversationally and with pencil-and-paper items, combined with a brief physical exam for parkinsonism, frontal release signs and gait.

sources.developer: Technical University of Munich (Berlet, Fuchtmann, Haddadin, Wilhelm et al.)
sources.title: Toward telemedical diagnostics—clinical evaluation of a robotic examination system for emergency patients
sources.claim: A robotic examination system with manipulator arms was clinically evaluated on emergency department patients for vital signs, auscultation, percussion, palpation and swabbing, but the examination is carried out by a remote physician commanding the robot, not autonomously.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: general telemedical physical examination (auscultation, percussion, palpation) on real patients. It is the closest existing robotic system to a hands-on clinical exam, but it is physician-teleoperated and includes no reflex, strength, sensory or coordination testing, so it does not substantiate autonomous completion of a neurological examination.

sources.system: Pepper humanoid robot with affective computing MMSE module
sources.developer: SoftBank Robotics platform; Behaviour Labs / IRCCS Casa Sollievo della Sofferenza consortium
sources.title: Assessing Feasibility of Cognitive Impairment Testing Using Social Robotic Technology Augmented with Affective Computing and Emotional State Detection Systems
sources.claim: A Pepper social robot administered the MMSE to older patients in a geriatric research setting, but only as a spoken cognitive questionnaire and under the supervision of a psychologist; no hands-on neurological examination is performed.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: administration of a bedside cognitive screening instrument. It covers only the verbal cognitive portion of the neurologist's assessment, was clinician-supervised, and involves no physical examination, so it cannot substantiate completion of the mental-status instance as a whole.

sources.title: Preparing for the Clinical Stage: Lab Development and Testing of Socially Assistive Robot for Physical Health Assessments
sources.claim: A mobile socially assistive robot autonomously administered three standardized physical performance tests (30-second chair stand, 4-meter walk, grip strength) with good reliability, but only in laboratory development testing prior to any clinical stage.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: instructing and scoring standardized functional tests of strength and mobility. It shows a robot can cue a cooperative person through a scripted test in a lab, but it does not examine the patient (no resisted strength grading, reflexes, sensation, cranial nerves) and is not clinically deployed.

sources.title: Robot-Assisted Arm Assessments in Spinal Cord Injured Patients: A Consideration of Concept Study
sources.claim: An exoskeleton rehabilitation robot measured arm range of motion, strength and ... parameters in spinal-cord-injured patients, producing metrics comparable to clinical scales, but only after a therapist positions and straps the patient into the purpose-built device.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: instrumented measurement of limb motor function in a purpose-built rehabilitation device. Even at maximum structure (patient fixtured in the machine) it yields kinematic/kinetic parameters for one limb only, not a neurologist's multi-domain examination, so it does not substantiate E1 completion of any instance.

sources.developer: University of Southern Denmark / Lifeline Robotics
sources.title: Autonomous swab robot for naso- and oropharyngeal COVID-19 screening
sources.claim: An autonomous robot station performed naso- and oropharyngeal swabbing of human subjects, showing that autonomous patient-contact robots exist but only for single, scripted, non-interpretive procedures on cooperative seated subjects.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous physical contact procedure on a cooperative patient in a clinical screening station. It transfers only a capability for one fixed motion on a seated head; it involves no elicitation of effort, grading of responses, or clinical interpretation, so it does not carry over to neurological examination.

tasks.label: Perform or interpret the outcomes of procedures or diagnostic tests, such as lumbar punctures, electroencephalography, electromyography, and nerve conduction velocity tests.

instances.label: Read a routine 20-30 minute outpatient or inpatient EEG at a reading workstation: review raw traces and montages recorded earlier by a technologist, separate artifact from epileptiform discharges, grade background and slowing, and dictate a signed report. Purely interpretive desk work in a hospital/clinic reading room.

Perform and interpret a complete outpatient electrodiagnostic study (nerve conduction studies plus needle EMG) in a clinic exam room: position and warm the limb, palpate landmarks, place surface recording/ground electrodes, stimulate nerves at several sites, measure distances, adapt the protocol in real time to findings, then insert a concentric needle electrode into several muscles, judge insertional and spontaneous activity and motor unit morphology by screen and sound, manage patient pain and cooperation, and issue the report.

Perform a diagnostic lumbar puncture at the bedside (ward, ED, or clinic procedure room): consent, position the patient lateral decubitus or sitting, palpate or ultrasound the interspace, sterile prep/drape, infiltrate local anesthetic, advance a spinal needle through ligament into the subarachnoid space (redirecting on bone contact, sometimes on an obese or arthritic patient), measure opening pressure with a manometer, collect and label CSF tubes, dress the site.

Interpret long-term video-EEG in an epilepsy monitoring unit or continuous ICU EEG: review many hours of recording with trend panels, spike/seizure detection software output and synchronized video, classify events, correlate with nursing/clinical notes, and communicate findings to the treating team. Interpretive work at a monitoring workstation.

Interpret other neurodiagnostic studies acquired by technologists — evoked potentials (VEP/SSEP/BAER), autonomic reflex testing, repetitive nerve stimulation traces, remote supervision and interpretation of intraoperative neuromonitoring — reviewing waveforms against normative data and issuing a report from a hospital reading room or remote monitoring station.

sources.title: Performance, Safety, and Patient Experience of an Autonomous Robotic Phlebotomy Device: A Multicenter Trial (Clinical Chemistry)
sources.claim: Vitestro's autonomous robotic phlebotomy device inserts a needle into a patient's vein without a human operator, using near-infrared, ultrasound and Doppler imaging, and was evaluated in a large multicenter clinical trial in blood-collection facilities.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous needle insertion into a patient in a clinical facility. Cited as the frontier of that capability; it does not transfer to this task, because venipuncture targets a superficial vessel imaged directly, whereas lumbar puncture requires deep midline advancement through ligament with tactile loss-of-resistance, opening-pressure measurement and CSF collection, and needle EMG requires real-time interpretation of muscle activity that redirects the needle and selects further muscles.

instances.label: Outpatient clinic, new-patient consultation for cognitive decline/suspected dementia: 45-60 min history from patient and caregiver, bedside cognitive testing (MoCA), full hands-on neurological exam (cranial nerves, tone, strength, reflexes with hammer, sensation, coordination, gait), ordering MRI/labs, formulating the diagnosis and starting therapy, counseling family.

Emergency department 'code stroke': neurologist (in person or via a remote-presence cart) performs a timed NIHSS exam on a patient on a gurney, reviews non-contrast CT/CTA, weighs contraindications, decides on and orders IV thrombolysis, and arranges thrombectomy transfer - all within minutes.

Inpatient consult for suspected CNS infection or acute encephalopathy: bedside exam including meningeal signs and mental status in an agitated or febrile patient, performing a diagnostic lumbar puncture at the bedside, interpreting CSF and imaging, and starting antimicrobial/antiviral and anti-seizure therapy.

ICU/trauma-bay consult for craniospinal trauma (TBI, spinal cord injury): exam of a sedated or obtunded patient in a cervical collar with lines and monitors - pupils, corneal/gag/cough reflexes, motor response to noxious stimulus, sensory level - plus review of CT/MRI, ICP and seizure-prophylaxis management, and prognostic discussion with family.

Outpatient follow-up visits (clinic or video telehealth) for established disease - post-stroke secondary prevention, dementia progression, post-traumatic sequelae: focused re-examination, medication titration, review of interval imaging/labs, caregiver counseling and documentation.

tasks.label: Determine brain death using accepted tests and procedures.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Standard adult brain death evaluation in a tertiary hospital ICU after catastrophic brain injury (anoxic arrest, TBI, large ICH). Neurologist verifies prerequisites (imaging shows adequate cause, core temperature, blood pressure, absence of sedative/paralytic and metabolic confounders), then performs the full bedside cranial-nerve exam on an intubated ventilated patient — pupillary light response, corneal stimulation, oculocephalic maneuver, bilateral cold-caloric irrigation after otoscopic inspection, gag and cough via tracheal suction catheter, noxious stimulation at supraorbital ridge, TMJ and nail beds — then conducts the apnea test (preoxygenation, ABG baseline, ventilator disconnection with oxygen catheter, 8-10 minutes of chest observation, repeat ABG, reconnection), documents the checklist and declares time of death.

Determination in the organ-donation pathway: same full exam and apnea test, with a second qualifying examiner or repeat exam per hospital policy, precise time-of-death documentation on the state/hospital brain death form, notification and coordination with the organ procurement organization, and a bedside family discussion before and after the exam, including allowing family presence during the exam.

Confounded or incomplete clinical exam requiring ancillary testing: severe facial/orbital trauma or globe injury, high cervical cord injury, tympanic membrane perforation, patient on ECMO, or hemodynamic instability/hypoxemia that aborts the apnea test. Neurologist performs whatever exam components are safe, then orders, supervises and interprets an ancillary study (radionuclide cerebral perfusion scan, four-vessel catheter angiography, EEG, or transcranial Doppler) and integrates the result into the determination.

Pediatric or neonatal determination in a PICU/NICU: two separate examinations and two apnea tests by different attending examiners, separated by an age-dependent observation interval (24 h for term neonates, 12 h for older infants/children), on small anatomy with narrow physiologic reserve, plus intensive family communication.

Determination at a community hospital ICU or emergency department where the neurologist is on call and may be supported by tele-neurology: less specialized staffing and equipment, drug-screen and confounder data sometimes incomplete, exam performed at a bedside crowded with ventilator, drips and monitors, and ancillary testing may require patient transport to nuclear medicine or CT.

TCD + NeuralBot 5-axis robotic headset) is an FDA-cleared robotic ultrasound device that autonomously searches for and measures cerebral blood flow; it is applied by a clinician and used with a neurologist, and TCD is only an ancillary adjunct to brain death determination, not the determination itself.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic transcranial Doppler insonation of the middle cerebral .... It is the closest robotic capability to any component of brain death testing (an ancillary cerebral blood flow study), but it performs no cranial-nerve examination or apnea test and requires a clinician to apply the headset and a physician to interpret, so it cannot complete the determination.

sources.transferJustification: Related task: bedside cerebral blood flow monitoring in stroke patients in a hospital. Shows the environment (hospital ICU/stroke unit) is reachable by this device, but the capability is a single imaging measurement, not the multi-step neurologic examination and apnea test that constitute brain death determination.

sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous needle insertion for blood sampling, the closest analogue to the serial arterial blood gas draws inside the apnea test. Transfer fails: the device works on a fixtured arm of a cooperative outpatient in a phlebotomy station, addresses veins rather than radial/femoral arteries, and covers only one sub-step of the instance.

instances.label: Didactic teaching: the neurologist prepares and delivers a lecture, grand rounds talk, or case conference on a neurologic topic (e.g., stroke syndromes, seizure classification, neuroanatomic localization) to medical students, residents, or department staff, fielding questions and discussion.

Inpatient bedside teaching rounds: with a team of students and residents at the patient's bedside on a neurology or stroke service, the attending walks through the history, demonstrates and narrates elements of the neurologic exam, quizzes the team on localization and differential, and gives teaching points.

Outpatient clinic precepting: a student or resident sees a clinic patient and presents; the neurologist questions the reasoning, verifies key exam findings, explains diagnostic and treatment choices, and gives individualized feedback and reading assignments over the course of a clinic session.

In-service training for staff members: teaching nurses, EEG/EMG technologists, or ED staff on protocols such as stroke code activation, NIHSS scoring, tPA administration monitoring, or electrode placement standards, typically in a conference room or unit with slides, checklists, and Q&A.

Procedural supervision and coaching: observing a resident or fellow performing a lumbar puncture, EMG/nerve conduction study, or botulinum toxin injection, giving verbal guidance and correction, occasionally repositioning a hand or needle, and debriefing afterward.

instances.label: Neuroimmunology outpatient clinic (MS/NMOSD/myasthenia): the neurologist examines the patient, selects and initiates or switches a disease-modifying therapy, supervises and troubleshoots infusion therapy (e.g., ocrelizumab, natalizumab, IVIG) in the clinic infusion suite, manages infusion/immune reactions, and occasionally performs a bedside lumbar puncture for CSF studies before or during treatment.

Sleep disorders clinic and attended sleep laboratory: the neurologist reviews polysomnography, prescribes and titrates positive-airway-pressure therapy, fits and adjusts masks/interfaces on the patient, tunes settings for adherence, adjusts oral appliances or hypoglossal-nerve-stimulator programming, and manages narcolepsy/RBD pharmacotherapy with follow-up monitoring.

Behavioral neurology / memory clinic: after cognitive testing and physical exam, the neurologist initiates and titrates dementia therapy (cholinesterase inhibitors, memantine, anti-amyloid monoclonal infusions), oversees MRI ARIA surveillance and infusion administration, treats behavioral and psychiatric symptoms, and instructs the patient and caregiver.

Neuro-oncology at a cancer center or inpatient neuro-oncology service: managing a brain tumor or leptomeningeal-disease patient — prescribing and monitoring chemotherapy/steroids/antiseizure drugs, and performing intrathecal chemotherapy administration via Ommaya reservoir tap or lumbar puncture, with toxicity assessment and dose adjustment.

Neurogenetics clinic (e.g., SMA, Huntington disease, lysosomal/mitochondrial disorders): confirming a molecular diagnosis, counseling the family, and initiating gene-targeted treatment — e.g., intrathecal nusinersen loading/maintenance doses (often with fluoroscopic or ultrasound guidance in scoliotic spines), enzyme-replacement or antisense infusions — with exam-based monitoring of response and adverse effects.
