sources.claim: The most mature clinical robot in neurology-adjacent therapeutics automatically positions and maintains contact of a TMS coil on a patient's head under neuronavigation in clinics; it handles only the coil-placement sub-step of a clinician-prescribed stimulation session, not patient assessment, drug therapy, or any of the listed subspecialty treatments.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic delivery of a brain-directed therapy to a seated patient in a clinic. It bounds what deployed clinical robots do — a single positioning sub-step under clinician supervision — showing no system executes a whole neurologic treatment episode.

sources.title: Doctors Let AI Control Surgery Robot and Perform Gallbladder Removal on Its Own
sources.claim: State-of-the-art autonomous medical robotics reached multi-step soft-tissue surgery only on pig cadavers in a laboratory; no autonomous robot performs invasive procedures on human patients as a physician substitute.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous execution of a multi-step invasive procedure. It marks the ceiling of demonstrated procedural autonomy (ex-vivo animal lab), so the far broader, judgment-laden treatment episodes of a neurologist are unsupported at any environment tier.

tasks.label: Prescribe or administer treatments, such as transcranial magnetic stimulation, vagus nerve stimulation, and deep brain stimulation.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Outpatient neurology clinic: after evaluating a patient, the neurologist selects and prescribes/orders a treatment (drug therapy, a course of TMS, referral for DBS or VNS candidacy), counsels the patient on risks and benefits, and enters the prescription/order and documentation in the EHR. No hands-on procedure.

Movement-disorders clinic: DBS programming/optimization visit. Neurologist interrogates the implanted pulse generator with the clinician programmer/tablet, performs monopolar review, examines the patient for tremor, rigidity and bradykinesia and for stimulation-induced side effects while iteratively changing contacts, amplitude, pulse width and frequency; coordinates medication changes.

Epilepsy clinic: VNS device check and titration. Neurologist places the programming wand/tablet over the chest generator, checks lead impedance and battery, steps output current up, observes the patient for hoarseness, cough or dyspnea during a test stimulation, and sets duty-cycle/AutoStim parameters.

TMS service: initial treatment-planning session for a new patient. Physician screens for contraindications, determines resting motor threshold by eliciting motor responses at varying intensities, localizes and marks the cortical target (with or without neuronavigation), and prescribes the pulse protocol and dose.

TMS suite: routine daily treatment session for an established patient at a previously defined target and dose. Patient is seated, coil is placed and held on the scalp at the planned target for the full train sequence with the position maintained despite head movement; patient is monitored for discomfort or adverse events; session logged.

Clinic procedure room: administering other neurologic treatments in person — EMG- or ultrasound-guided botulinum toxin injections for dystonia, spasticity or chronic migraine; occipital/trigger point nerve blocks; supervision of infusion therapy — on patients whose anatomy and posture vary.

sources.claim: Axilum Robotics' TMS-Robot/TMS-Cobot is a commercial, FDA-cleared robot that, once targets are planned in a neuronavigation system and the patient is registered and seated, automatically positions and holds the TMS coil on the scalp and compensates for head movement for the whole session.

instances.label: Office/clinic medical management of gynecologic disease: evaluate the patient (history, speculum/bimanual exam), then treat non-surgically — prescribe hormonal therapy for endometriosis/PCOS/abnormal uterine bleeding, antibiotics for vaginitis/cervicitis, vaginal estrogen for GSM, or give an in-office IM/depot injection; adjust therapy at follow-up.

Office/clinic minor operative procedures on a woman in stirrups under local or no anesthesia: IUD/levonorgestrel-system placement for bleeding disorders, endometrial biopsy, colposcopy with directed cervical biopsy and ECC, LEEP or cryo/thermal ablation for cervical dysplasia, incision and drainage of a Bartholin abscess, pessary fitting for prolapse.

Major gynecologic surgery in a hospital operating room under general anesthesia: laparoscopic/robotic-assisted or vaginal hysterectomy for fibroids, adenomyosis or malignancy; myomectomy; salpingo-oophorectomy or ovarian cystectomy; prolapse repair — including dissection near ureters/bladder, hemostasis, and management of intraoperative bleeding or adhesions.

Ambulatory day-surgery / same-day operative treatment: hysteroscopic polypectomy or myomectomy, dilation and curettage, endometrial ablation, diagnostic laparoscopy with excision or ablation of endometriosis implants, tubal surgery — under sedation or general anesthesia in an ASC or hospital day-surgery unit.

Emergency and inpatient treatment: ruptured ectopic pregnancy or ovarian torsion taken emergently to the OR, tubo-ovarian abscess requiring drainage and IV antibiotics, severe uterine hemorrhage requiring tamponade/uterine artery intervention, management of post-operative complications on the ward at unpredictable hours.

sources.system: Toumai surgical robot with Neuron multimodal AI
sources.title: No Hands on Deck: The Dawn of Fully Autonomous Surgery — Mewburn Ellis
sources.claim: MicroPort MedBot's Toumai with the Neuron AI model removed a gallbladder in a live pig with minimal human correction in December 2025, but the system is explicitly not approved for human use.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous in vivo laparoscopic organ removal, the nearest analogue to laparoscopic gynecologic surgery; cited to show the frontier remains animal models with no human clearance.

sources.title: Waterloo startup performs first ever robotic intramuscular injection — Waterloo News
sources.claim: The only autonomous robotic drug-administration demonstration found is Cobi, a needle-free intramuscular injection platform shown in a university/startup demonstration; it does not perform clinical assessment or a treatment decision and is not in clinical service.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous administration of an intramuscular injection, the physical delivery step of office medical treatment. It covers only that step in a demo setting and provides no examination or treatment-selection capability, so it cannot complete the instance.

tasks.label: Care for and treat women during prenatal, natal, and postnatal periods.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Routine prenatal office visit in a clinic exam room: greet and interview the patient, review vitals/labs, palpate the abdomen and measure fundal height, obtain fetal heart tones with a handheld Doppler, sometimes perform a cervical/pelvic exam, order and interpret screening tests, prescribe (e.g., iron, Tdap), and counsel on warning signs and plan of care.

Management of labor and spontaneous vaginal delivery on a hospital labor-and-delivery unit: serial digital cervical exams, artificial rupture of membranes, interpretation of continuous fetal heart-rate and tocometry tracings, titration of oxytocin, coaching pushing, hands-on delivery of the head and shoulders, cord clamping, delivery of the placenta, inspection and suture repair of perineal/vaginal lacerations.

Cesarean delivery in a hospital operating room: sterile prep and draping, transverse skin incision, dissection through fascia and peritoneum, low transverse hysterotomy, delivery of the infant and placenta, uterine closure and multi-layer abdominal closure, with intraoperative hemostasis decisions.

Complicated or emergency obstetric care: triage of bleeding or decreased fetal movement, hypertensive disorders/preeclampsia management with magnesium and antihypertensives, postpartum hemorrhage (uterine massage, bimanual compression, uterotonics, balloon tamponade), shoulder dystocia maneuvers, operative vaginal delivery with vacuum or forceps, urgent cesarean for non-reassuring tracing.

Postpartum care: daily inpatient rounds on the postpartum ward (fundal palpation, lochia and incision/laceration checks, breast exam, lactation and contraception counseling, discharge orders) and the 4-6 week postpartum office visit including pelvic exam and contraception placement.

Obstetric diagnostic and bedside procedures: office/point-of-care obstetric ultrasound (dating, growth, presentation, biophysical profile), non-stress testing, amniocentesis under ultrasound guidance, external cephalic version, cervical cerclage placement.

sources.title: SRT-H: A hierarchical framework for autonomous surgery via language-conditioned imitation learning | Science Robotics
sources.claim: SRT-H, a hierarchical imitation-learning surgical robot built on the da Vinci Research Kit, autonomously performed the dissection phase of gallbladder removal on ex vivo pig gallbladders in a laboratory setting — the closest existing analog to autonomous soft-tissue surgery, but not on a living patient and not a complete operation.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous soft-tissue dissection. It is the nearest analog to the surgical portions of obstetric care (cesarean hysterotomy, laceration repair), but it is performed on excised animal tissue in a lab rig with human supervision and voice correction, so it does not substantiate completing an operation on a pregnant patient.

sources.system: Autonomous lightweight ultrasound robot for liver sonography
sources.developer: Tsinghua University / Beijing Tsinghua Changgung Hospital
sources.title: Beyond hospital reach: Autonomous lightweight ultrasound robot for liver sonography
sources.claim: An autonomous lightweight ultrasound robot performed self-directed probe placement and imaging of liver/aorta/IVC planes on human subjects in a hospital ultrasound department, showing autonomous sonography is limited to acquiring specified imaging planes, not conducting a clinical encounter.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous abdominal ultrasound scanning on humans. It bears on the imaging sub-step of prenatal care only; it acquires standard planes of static abdominal organs and does not perform examination, diagnosis, treatment, or any obstetric procedure.

sources.system: MELODY telerobotic ultrasound (robot-assisted obstetric ultrasound, Finnmark)
sources.developer: AdEchoTech / University Hospital of North Norway
sources.title: Introduction of robot-assisted obstetric ultrasound in rural Northern Norway — Acta Obstetricia et Gynecologica Scandinavica
sources.claim: Robot-assisted obstetric ultrasound used clinically for pregnant women in rural Norway is telerobotic: a remote sonographer drives the probe in real time, so the robot is not acting autonomously.
sources.transferJustification: Directly in-task (prenatal ultrasound), but the probe is continuously teleoperated by a remote clinician, which the rules treat as not supporting a positive judgment.

sources.system: Robotic prenatal ultrasound scanning platform (passive-compliance probe positioner)
sources.developer: academic research group (robotic prenatal care platform)
sources.title: Autonomous Robotic Ultrasound Approach for Fetoscope Tracking by Fusing Optical and 2D Ultrasound Data (ResearchGate record)
sources.claim: A research platform aimed explicitly at robotic prenatal ultrasound was tested on pregnant women only under direct physician operation, confirming that obstetric robotic scanning remains human-driven.
sources.transferJustification: Directly in-task (prenatal ultrasound) but physician-operated; establishes the state of the art in obstetric robotics is assistive positioning, not autonomous care.

sources.title: Surgeons use teleoperated humanoid robots to perform live surgery—a world first
sources.claim: The first surgeries completed by humanoid robots, reported mid-2026, were done in a preclinical trial under continuous teleoperation, indicating no autonomous robot performs whole operations on patients.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: whole-operation robotic surgery. It is teleoperated and preclinical, so it cannot substantiate autonomous completion of obstetric surgical or delivery work.

tasks.label: Analyze records, reports, test results, or examination information to diagnose medical condition of patient.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

tasks.label: Perform cesarean sections or other surgical procedures as needed to preserve patients' health and deliver babies safely.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Scheduled/planned cesarean delivery (repeat cesarean, breech, placenta previa) in a hospital labor-and-delivery operating room: prep and drape, low transverse skin and uterine incision, delivery of the infant, placental removal, multi-layer uterine and fascial closure, hemostasis, with an awake regional-anesthetized patient and a scrub/circulating team.

Unscheduled or emergency cesarean (fetal bradycardia, arrest of descent, chorioamnionitis, abruption) started within minutes in a hospital OR, sometimes complicated by dense adhesions, morbid obesity, uterine atony or hemorrhage requiring B-Lynch suture, balloon tamponade, or peripartum hysterectomy.

Obstetric repair and evacuation procedures at or just after vaginal delivery in a labor room or OR: episiotomy and second- to fourth-degree perineal/cervical laceration repair, manual extraction of retained placenta, curettage for postpartum hemorrhage, cervical cerclage placement/removal.

Minimally invasive gynecologic surgery in a hospital OR or ambulatory surgery center: laparoscopic or robot-assisted (surgeon-teleoperated) total hysterectomy, salpingectomy for ectopic pregnancy, ovarian cystectomy, endometriosis excision - port placement, dissection, vessel sealing, colpotomy, vaginal cuff closure.

Vaginal, hysteroscopic and cervical procedures in an OR, ASC or office procedure room: hysteroscopic polypectomy/myomectomy, dilation and curettage, LEEP/cone biopsy, vaginal hysterectomy, tubal sterilization, pelvic organ prolapse repair.

Open abdominal gynecologic surgery in a hospital OR: abdominal hysterectomy, open myomectomy for large fibroids, laparotomy for ruptured ectopic or adnexal torsion, oncologic staging/debulking with adhesiolysis and bowel/bladder proximity.

sources.system: SRT-H (Hierarchical Surgical Robot Transformer, on a da Vinci research kit platform)
sources.title: SRT-H: A hierarchical framework for autonomous surgery via language-conditioned imitation learning - PubMed
sources.claim: The most advanced autonomous surgical system reported, SRT-H, executed only the clipping-and-cutting step of a cholecystectomy, and only on ex vivo pig gallbladders - not a whole procedure and not on a live human patient.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: steps of laparoscopic cholecystectomy. Cited as the ceiling of autonomous soft-tissue surgery - step-level autonomy on excised animal tissue, far short of a whole cesarean or hysterectomy on a live patient.

sources.system: FDA-cleared robotically-assisted surgical devices (da Vinci, Hugo, Senhance, Hominis, etc.)
sources.developer: Intuitive Surgical, Medtronic, Asensus, Memic (regulatory review by FDA)
sources.title: Levels of autonomy in FDA-cleared surgical robots: a systematic review | npj Digital Medicine
sources.claim: All surgical robots cleared for clinical ... in the US, including those used for gynecologic surgery, require the surgeon's direct and continuous control; they have no robotic autonomy.

sources.system: Robotically-assisted surgical (RAS) systems in clinical use
sources.title: Computer-Assisted Surgical Systems | FDA
sources.claim: The FDA states outright that clinically deployed robotic surgery devices - cleared for gynecologic procedures such as hysterectomy - cannot perform surgery without direct ....

sources.title: Advancing obstetric and gynecologic surgery through robotic innovation | Contemporary OB/GYN
sources.claim: Robotic technique in obstetrics and gynecology, including cesarean-related and hysterectomy/myomectomy procedures, is 'robotic-assisted' - the surgeon drives the instruments throughout.

sources.developer: UC San Diego Advanced Robotics and Controls Lab (Michael Yip)
sources.title: Teleoperated Humanoid Robots Reach Live Surgery Milestone | TechRepublic
sources.claim: The July 2026 humanoid-robot surgical milestone (two gallbladder removals on live pigs) was fully teleoperated by surgeons, not autonomous.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: laparoscopic abdominal surgery. Shows the newest general-purpose surgical embodiment in an OR-like setting is surgeon-teleoperated, so it cannot support an autonomous positive judgment for OB/GYN surgery.

sources.system: CUHK embodied-intelligence surgical automation platform (integrated with the Sentire Surgical System)
sources.developer: The Chinese University of Hong Kong (Dou Qi et al.)
sources.title: CUHK's newly-created embodied intelligence platform successfully completes the world's first multi-task surgical automation tests on a live animal
sources.claim: In vivo autonomous surgical robotics is at the level of automating individual sub-tasks in live animal models, presented as a first step toward autonomy rather than completion of whole procedures.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated sub-tasks during live-animal laparoscopic surgery. Establishes the in vivo autonomy ceiling - sub-task automation under surgeon supervision, not whole-procedure completion.

sources.developer: Johns Hopkins University / Children's National Hospital
sources.title: Autonomous Surgical Robots Enhance Precision in the OR - IEEE Spectrum
sources.claim: Even the leading autonomous soft-tissue suturing robot needs surgeon intervention every few stitches, far from the uninterrupted multi-layer closure a cesarean or hysterectomy demands.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous laparoscopic intestinal anastomosis in pigs. Bowel suturing is comparable in tissue handling to uterine, fascial and perineal closure, so its intervention rate bounds what autonomy could deliver for obstetric repair.

tasks.label: Monitor patients' conditions and progress and reevaluate treatments as necessary.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Intrapartum monitoring on a hospital labor & delivery unit: the OB rounds on laboring patients, interprets continuous fetal heart-rate and tocometry tracings, performs digital cervical exams to assess dilation/effacement/station, palpates contractions and fetal lie, checks maternal vitals and labs (e.g., pre-eclampsia workup), then titrates oxytocin, orders amniotomy, or escalates to operative/cesarean delivery.

Prenatal office visit progress check in a clinic exam room: measure fundal height, obtain fetal heart tones by Doppler, review BP/weight/edema, palpate presentation, review interval labs and ultrasound reports, and revise management (start antihypertensive, adjust insulin or thyroid dose, order growth scan/antenatal testing, change delivery timing).

Postoperative or postpartum inpatient rounds on a hospital ward after cesarean, hysterectomy, or vaginal delivery: inspect the incision or perineal repair, palpate the abdomen and uterine fundus, assess lochia, drains, Foley output and ambulation, review vitals/CBC, then adjust analgesia, antibiotics, anticoagulation, or advance diet and discharge.

Gynecologic office follow-up for a chronic problem (abnormal uterine bleeding, fibroids, endometriosis, prolapse, contraception, menopause, infertility): speculum/bimanual pelvic exam or in-office transvaginal ultrasound, review of pathology, labs and imaging, and revision of therapy (change hormonal regimen, check/replace IUD, escalate to surgery).

Remote/asynchronous monitoring from the office or hospital workstation: reviewing lab and pathology results, remotely read non-stress tests and CTG strips, responding to nurse calls and patient portal messages, phone titration of medications, and telehealth follow-up visits with no hands-on exam.

sources.title: MELODY - Remote ultrasound robot | AdEchoTech
sources.claim: MELODY is an FDA-cleared robotic tele-echography system used clinically (including obstetric and pelvic scanning), but the probe is driven in real time by a remote physician and an on-site assistant holds/positions the robot against the patient.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: acquiring diagnostic ultrasound of the abdomen/pelvis, an information-gathering step inside prenatal and gynecologic monitoring. It does not transfer because the clinical acquisition and all judgment are performed by a human operator in continuous control.

sources.system: Autonomous lightweight cable-driven ultrasound robot (AI agent + 588 g 6-DoF arm)
sources.developer: Tsinghua University / Beijing Tsinghua Changgung Hospital
sources.title: Beyond hospital reach: Autonomous lightweight ultrasound robot for liver sonography (arXiv:2510.08106)
sources.claim: A research autonomous ultrasound robot autonomously located liver structures on human subjects and was trialed inside a hospital ultrasound department, i.e. autonomous image acquisition only, with no clinical assessment or treatment change.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous sonographic scanning of a supine adult abdomen, comparable to fundal/obstetric scanning. Shows only sub-step image capture in a feasibility study; no exam of the patient, interpretation, or reevaluation of treatment.

sources.system: Robot-assisted antenatal ultrasound platform (VR teleoperation with autonomous protocol mode)
sources.title: Immersive Virtual Reality Platform for Robot-Assisted Antenatal Ultrasound Scanning (arXiv:2309.03725)
sources.claim: A robotic antenatal ultrasound platform can carry out the standardized ISUOG six-step obstetric scan under sonologist supervision, demonstrated as a research prototype rather than a deployed clinical service.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: obstetric ultrasound acquisition during prenatal monitoring. Autonomy is supervised and unverified outside the lab, and the system produces images only, not an assessment of fetal well-being or a treatment change.

sources.title: Swisslog Healthcare Partners with Diligent Robotics to Enhance Hospital Logistics
sources.claim: Moxi is an autonomous mobile manipulator deployed at scale in US hospitals, but its accepted work is logistics (delivering medications, supplies and lab samples), not patient assessment or clinical decision-making.
sources.transferJustification: Shows the state of autonomous robots on hospital wards where these monitoring instances occur: fetch-and-deliver only, establishing that no fielded ward robot performs bedside examination or reevaluates treatment.

sources.system: Lucid Robotic System (Lucid M1 TCD + NeuralBot)
sources.title: Houston Methodist is first in U.S. to use Lucid Robotic System to monitor brain blood flow noninvasively
sources.claim: The Lucid Robotic System is an FDA-cleared robotic ultrasound headset that autonomously positions a Doppler probe to monitor cerebral blood flow, but it acquires physiologic data under a clinician's guidance and makes no treatment decisions.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated bedside physiologic monitoring in a hospital. It transfers only to sensor placement on a fixed, easily accessible site (the temporal window) and yields data for a clinician; it performs no examination of the abdomen/pelvis and no reevaluation of therapy.

sources.system: CamAPS FX hybrid closed-loop insulin delivery (AiDAPT trial)
sources.title: Automated Insulin Delivery in Women with Pregnancy Complicated by Type 1 Diabetes (NEJM)
sources.claim: Hybrid closed-loop insulin delivery autonomously adjusts insulin to continuous glucose readings and improved glycemic control in pregnancies complicated by type 1 diabetes, i.e. automated titration of a single drug, not physician monitoring of the pregnancy.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: closed-loop 'monitor and adjust treatment' for one biomarker. It does not transfer to the OB/GYN instance, which requires physical examination and reevaluation of the whole treatment plan across many findings.

roles.title: Pediatricians, General
aliases: DO Physician (Doctor of Osteopathic Medicine Physician)
roles.description: Diagnose, treat, and help prevent diseases and injuries in children. May refer patients to specialists for further diagnosis or treatment, as needed.

tasks.label: Prescribe or administer treatment, therapy, medication, vaccination, and other specialized medical care to treat or prevent illness, disease, or injury in infants and children.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Well-child/preventive visit in a pediatric clinic exam room: review the immunization record, screen for contraindications, order and (with staff) administer 2-5 routine vaccines to an infant or toddler held by a parent — correct vaccine, dose, route and site (vastus lateralis/deltoid) on a squirming, crying child — counsel the parent, observe for immediate reactions and document.

Acute sick visit in the office: after history and exam of a child with otitis media, pharyngitis, croup, asthma flare or dermatitis, select therapy, compute the weight-based dose, check allergies and interactions, and issue an electronic prescription to the family's pharmacy plus instructions to the caregiver.

In-office therapeutic procedure on a child: nebulized albuterol with reassessment, IM ceftriaxone or epinephrine, laceration cleaning/closure or wound dressing, splinting a limb, cerumen or nasal foreign-body removal, or abscess incision and drainage — performed on a frightened, moving patient with a parent present.

Chronic-condition management visit: adjust and prescribe ongoing therapy (asthma controller, ADHD stimulant under controlled-substance rules, insulin regimen, growth hormone, allergy immunotherapy), order monitoring labs, and handle refills and school/authorization paperwork.

Inpatient, newborn nursery or urgent care setting: order and oversee treatment — vitamin K and hepatitis B injections for a newborn, phototherapy for jaundice, IV fluids and antibiotics for a dehydrated or septic infant, oxygen and stabilization for respiratory distress — with dose titration and bedside reassessment.

sources.title: Performance, Safety, and Patient Experience of an Autonomous Robotic Phlebotomy Device: A Multicenter Trial (Clinical Chemistry)
sources.claim: The Aletta autonomous robotic phlebotomy ... performs venipuncture without a human operator, achieving 94.5% first-stick success across 1633 patients in routine outpatient use; one supervising professional oversees up to three devices.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: diagnostic venipuncture, the closest demonstrated autonomous needle procedure on a human. Transfer is only partial — the device inserts a needle into an arm the patient places in a fixture and draws blood; it does not select a therapy, prepare or verify a medication dose, or manage a moving infant, so it does not substantiate administering treatment to children.

sources.title: Performance, Safety, and Patient Experience of an Autonomous Robotic Phlebotomy Device: A Multicenter Trial (Clinical Chemistry)
sources.claim: That trial ran only in hospital outpatient phlebotomy departments and enrolled only patients aged 16 or older, i.e. no infants or young children.
sources.transferJustification: Same related task (venipuncture); cited to show the demonstrated population excludes the infants and children that define this pediatric task.

sources.title: Vitestro Achieves CE Marking for Autonomous Blood Drawing Device
sources.claim: Vitestro's autonomous blood-drawing device received CE marking and has been ordered by European hospitals and laboratories, establishing commercial status for autonomous needle procedures on adults.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous venipuncture in adults; establishes maturity of the nearest analogue, not of pediatric medication or vaccine administration.

sources.title: Cobi robot autonomously performs intramuscular injection without needles
sources.claim: Cobi, a University of Waterloo spinoff platform, performed a one-off autonomous needle-free intramuscular injection on an adult; it remains a demonstration system with no clinical validation or pediatric use.

sources.developer: Foxconn with NVIDIA (deployed at Taichung Veterans General Hospital)
sources.title: Foxconn Uses NVIDIA Isaac for Smart Hospital Solutions - Customer Story
sources.claim: State-of-the-art hospital service robots such as Nurabot navigate wards autonomously to transport medication and specimens; they do not administer medication to or perform procedures on patients.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: intra-hospital medication logistics. Cited to bound the state of the art — deployed clinical robots move medication through structured facilities but none administers therapy to a patient.

tasks.label: Examine children regularly to assess their growth and development.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Infant well-child visit (2 weeks-15 months) in a pediatric outpatient clinic: measure weight, recumbent length and head circumference, plot on growth curves, then a hands-on head-to-toe exam (fontanelles, red reflex, otoscopy, cardiac and lung auscultation, abdominal palpation, femoral pulses, Ortolani/Barlow hip maneuvers, skin/genital check) on a squirming, often crying infant held by a parent, plus elicited milestone assessment and parent counseling.

Toddler/preschool well-child visit (15 months-4 years) in clinic: standing height and weight, developmental screening (ASQ/M-CHAT review plus observed language, gait, fine-motor play), and physical exam including ears, mouth/throat, heart, lungs, abdomen and gait on an often fearful, uncooperative, moving child who must be coaxed or briefly restrained.

School-age well-child visit (5-11 years) in clinic: height, weight, BMI, blood pressure, vision and hearing screening, scoliosis/spine check, full physical exam, and assessment of school performance and behavior with a generally cooperative child and a parent present.

Adolescent well visit (12-18 years) in clinic: growth and BMI trajectory, blood pressure, sexual-maturity (Tanner) staging and pubertal exam with chaperone, scoliosis screening, and confidential psychosocial interview about mood, substances and sexual health.

Newborn examination in the hospital newborn nursery/postpartum unit (and the first-week weight-check visit): discharge exam of a naked newborn on a warmer - measurements, tone and reflexes, hip and palate exam, cardiac auscultation, jaundice and weight-loss assessment, feeding adequacy judgment.

Targeted growth/development follow-up visit in clinic for a child with a concern (poor weight gain, short stature, obesity, developmental delay, chronic disease): repeat careful anthropometry, focused physical, dysmorphology and neurologic assessment, comparison against prior growth data, and decision to test or refer.

sources.system: Autonomous robotic auscultation system (Bayesian-optimization stethoscope placement)
sources.developer: University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign (Zhu et al., IEEE RA-L)
sources.title: Automated Heart and Lung Auscultation in Robotic Physical Examinations - IEEE Xplore
sources.claim: First autonomous robotic auscultation system places a stethoscope on the chest of adult volunteers and captures heart/lung sounds; a lab-scale demonstration on 4 cooperative adult subjects, covering only one sub-step of a physical exam.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic chest auscultation on adults. It is one component of a pediatric physical exam, but the demonstration uses still, cooperative adults in a lab and covers none of the measurement, otoscopy, palpation, hip maneuvers, developmental assessment or clinical judgment required on a moving child.

sources.developer: Tsinghua University / Beijing Tsinghua Changgung Hospital
sources.title: Beyond hospital reach: Autonomous lightweight ultrasound robot for liver sonography (arXiv 2510.08106)
sources.claim: An autonomous robotic ultrasound system acquired standard liver imaging planes on patients in a hospital ultrasound department; probe-on-abdomen scanning of cooperative adults, not a general physical examination.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous contact scanning of a patient's torso inside a clinical facility. It shows force-controlled probe placement on adults lying still, but not the multi-modal hands-on exam, child handling, or developmental assessment of a well-child visit.

sources.title: Robots Advance Telemedicine for Pediatric Patients - CHOC Children's health hub
sources.claim: Telepresence robots used in pediatric care are remotely driven by a physician while bedside staff perform any hands-on examination; they provide no autonomous physical examination.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: remote pediatric assessment. Deployed in pediatric facilities, but the robot is a teleoperated audio/video presence and a human clinician performs all physical examination, so it cannot substantiate autonomous completion.

sources.system: Autonomous social robot for autism detection (robotic detection technology)
sources.developer: Academic research group (Frontiers in Psychiatry study)
sources.title: Development and evaluation of robotic detection technology for assessing autism
sources.claim: Autonomous social robots used to observe children for autism-risk behaviors remain very small-sample research studies rather than clinically accepted developmental assessments.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robot-mediated observation of child development. This is the closest evidence for the developmental-assessment portion of the task, but a handful of children and no physical-exam component fall far short of worker-quality completion.

tasks.label: Treat children who have minor illnesses, acute and chronic health problems, and growth and development concerns.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Office sick visit for a minor acute illness (otitis media, pharyngitis, viral URI, conjunctivitis, gastroenteritis) in a pediatric clinic exam room: focused hands-on exam of an often crying, squirming infant or toddler held by a parent (otoscopy, oropharynx, auscultation, abdomen), point-of-care swab if needed, decide on and initiate treatment (prescribe antibiotic, order or give an IM injection, fever/hydration plan), counsel the caregiver, document.

Chronic condition management visit (asthma, eczema, ADHD, allergies, obesity, type 1 diabetes co-management) in clinic: review symptom control and adherence, targeted exam, adjust medication doses, demonstrate and correct inhaler/spacer or injector technique on the child, sometimes give an in-office nebulizer treatment or spirometry, arrange labs and follow-up.

Growth and development concern visit: poor weight gain/failure to thrive, short stature, obesity, speech or motor delay, early or delayed puberty. Measure and plot growth, hands-on exam including Tanner staging or hip/tone assessment, administer developmental screening with the child, then start management (feeding/nutrition plan, labs, growth-hormone or therapy referral) and counsel the family.

In-office or urgent-care minor procedure on a child who may resist: laceration repair with sutures/adhesive, abscess incision and drainage, cerumen removal or ear irrigation, nasal/ear foreign-body removal, wart cryotherapy, splinting, nursemaid's-elbow reduction, or administering an IM/subcutaneous injection, with local anesthesia and restraint/distraction of the child.

Acute treatment of a sicker child in hospital, newborn nursery, or emergency setting: asthma exacerbation needing repeated nebulizers and steroids, dehydration needing IV access and fluids, febrile young infant workup, neonatal jaundice or feeding problems — hands-on assessment, procedures, order set, and repeated bedside reassessment over hours.

Telehealth or telephone treatment episode for a minor problem (rash, pink eye, medication refill, post-visit follow-up), with the child at home on video; the pediatrician relies on caregiver-directed inspection and sends a prescription electronically.

sources.title: SRT-H: A hierarchical framework for autonomous surgery via language-conditioned imitation learning | Science Robotics
sources.claim: The most advanced autonomous surgical manipulation system operates fully autonomously only on excised animal tissue in a laboratory setup, not on awake patients; it is a research demonstration.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous surgical tissue manipulation. Cited as the ceiling of autonomous medical manipulation: even this best case is ex vivo tissue in a rigged lab, so it does not transfer to examining and treating an awake, moving child.

sources.title: Waterloo startup performs first ever robotic intramuscular injection | Waterloo News
sources.claim: An autonomous robot platform demonstrated a needle-free intramuscular injection without a clinician present, but only as a single-step laboratory demonstration, not as a clinical encounter.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: administering an intramuscular vaccine. Relevant because injection is one sub-step of pediatric treatment, but the demo covers only the injection itself on a cooperative adult, not assessment, decision-making, or handling a resisting child.

sources.title: Swisslog Healthcare Partners with Diligent Robotics to Enhance Hospital Logistics
sources.claim: The largest deployed fleet of autonomous mobile manipulators in US hospitals performs supply and medication delivery logistics, not patient assessment or treatment.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: hospital fetch-and-deliver logistics. Shows what deployed clinical-facility robots actually do autonomously (transport), establishing that no deployed hospital robot performs hands-on patient treatment.

sources.system: Autonomous telepresence robot in pediatric ED
sources.title: Children's National Turns to Autonomous Robot to Reestablish Human Touch in the ED | HealthLeaders Media
sources.claim: In a pediatric emergency department, an autonomously navigating telepresence robot lets a physician consult remotely, but hands-on examination still requires an on-site human nurse.

sources.title: Vitestro's robotic blood drawing device meets trial endpoints
sources.claim: An autonomous venipuncture device reached human-comparable first-stick success in a clinical trial, showing narrow single-step patient-contact autonomy for diagnostic sampling rather than treatment.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous venipuncture on a seated patient. Cited because it is the strongest example of autonomous patient-contact procedure work; it covers one fixed sub-step on cooperative adults with the arm fixtured, not a pediatric treatment encounter.

tasks.label: Examine patients or order, perform, and interpret diagnostic tests to obtain information on medical condition and determine diagnosis.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Well-child exam of an infant or toddler (0-3 yrs) in a pediatric clinic exam room: squirming, sometimes crying child on parent's lap or exam table; head-to-toe inspection, otoscopy, oropharyngeal look, cardiac and lung auscultation, abdominal palpation, femoral pulses, hip Ortolani/Barlow, red reflex, fontanelle, plot growth and developmental screen, form an assessment.

Well-child or sports/adolescent physical of a cooperative older child in a clinic exam room: vitals, vision and hearing screen, auscultation, abdominal and thyroid palpation, skin survey, scoliosis forward-bend, Tanner staging, musculoskeletal screen, and determination of normal vs. abnormal findings.

Acute sick visit in a clinic exam room: febrile, coughing or ear-pulling child; targeted exam including otoscopy with cerumen and a moving head, throat and tonsil inspection, neck node palpation, lung auscultation for wheeze/crackles, abdominal exam, hydration and work-of-breathing assessment; decide whether testing is needed and reach a working diagnosis.

Perform and interpret in-office point-of-care diagnostics on a child in the clinic: throat swab for rapid strep, nasal swab for flu/RSV/COVID, urine dipstick or catheter/bag specimen, fingerstick hemoglobin or glucose, tympanometry, pulse oximetry; read the result and integrate it into the diagnosis and plan.

Newborn nursery or inpatient pediatric ward exam: full newborn head-to-toe including reflexes, red reflex, hip exam, cardiac murmur assessment, jaundice/skin check, plus review and interpretation of screening labs (bilirubin, newborn screen, CBC, cultures) to determine diagnosis and disposition.

sources.system: Autonomous robotic auscultation system (Zhu et al., University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign)
sources.title: Automated Heart and Lung Auscultation in Robotic Physical Examinations (IEEE Robotics and Automation Letters)
sources.claim: A research robot arm placed a stethoscope on the chest of adult volunteers and autonomously captured heart and lung sounds of quality comparable to teleoperated capture — the first autonomous robotic auscultation, in a laboratory setting with 4 subjects.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: chest auscultation, one component of the pediatric physical exam. It shows only a single sub-step on cooperative adults in a lab, not the whole exam-plus-diagnosis instance, and not on infants or crying children.

sources.developer: Academic research team (published in Scientific Reports)
sources.title: Autonomous swab robot for naso- and oropharyngeal COVID-19 screening (Scientific Reports)
sources.claim: An autonomous swab robot station collected combined naso- and oropharyngeal specimens from adult volunteers under force control in clinical trials, correlating with manual sampling; it collects specimens only and does not interpret results or diagnose.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: obtaining a pharyngeal specimen, the collection step of an in-office rapid strep/flu test. Transfer is limited: demonstrated on cooperative adults in a purpose-built station, with no test interpretation or diagnostic determination.

sources.title: Autonomous Robotic Phlebotomy Shows High Success Rates in Multicenter Trial (Clinical Lab Products)
sources.claim: Vitestro's Aletta autonomous robotic phlebotomy device performed diagnostic venous blood draws on 1,633 adult patients across three outpatient phlebotomy departments in a multicenter trial, with ~94.5% first-stick success when a suitable vein was found.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: obtaining a blood specimen for ordered diagnostic tests, in a structured outpatient facility (E2). It covers only specimen acquisition on adult patients; it performs no physical examination and makes no diagnosis.

sources.developer: Tsinghua University / Chinese PLA General Hospital
sources.title: Towards expert-level autonomous carotid ultrasonography with large-scale learning-based robotic system (Nature Communications)
sources.claim: UltraBot, a learning-based autonomous carotid ultrasound robot, achieved over 90% scanning success and expert-level measurement accuracy on adult subjects in clinical-oriented validation, showing autonomous contact-based imaging of a cooperative human body region.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: an operator-dependent contact diagnostic procedure on a patient's body. It substantiates autonomous probe placement on still, cooperative adults for one imaging protocol, not multi-modal pediatric examination or diagnostic synthesis.

Longitudinal well-child surveillance across visits: plotting growth and developmental-screening results over time, comparing to prior trajectory, and reevaluating an existing plan such as a feeding regimen, iron supplementation, or an early-intervention referral.

instances.label: Newborn circumcision in a hospital newborn nursery or procedure room: consent, restraining the neonate on a circumstraint board, dorsal penile nerve/ring block, lysing adhesions, applying a Gomco/Mogen clamp or Plastibell, excising foreskin, securing hemostasis, dressing, and monitoring for bleeding and voiding.

Laceration repair in a pediatric office, urgent care, or emergency department: exploring and irrigating a facial, scalp, or extremity wound on a frightened, squirming child (papoose-restrained or parent-held), applying LET or injected lidocaine, closing with sutures, tissue adhesive, or staples, and dressing.

Incision and drainage of a skin abscess or paronychia in clinic or ED: local anesthesia over inflamed tissue, scalpel incision, breaking loculations and expressing pus, irrigation, optional packing or loop drain, and dressing on a crying toddler or adolescent.

Minor dermatologic/nail procedures in the office: shave or punch excision of a skin lesion, cryotherapy or curettage of warts/molluscum, partial nail avulsion for ingrown toenail under digital block, or trephination of a subungual hematoma.

Frenotomy for ankyloglossia on a newborn in the nursery or office: stabilizing the tongue with a grooved director, snipping the frenulum with scissors, achieving hemostasis with pressure/gauze, and confirming improved latch.

Foreign body removal in the office or ED: bead or insect from the ear canal, object from a nostril, splinter or fishhook from soft tissue, or embedded tick, using restraint, magnification, curettes/forceps, and sometimes local anesthesia on an uncooperative child.

sources.title: Johns Hopkins teaches robot to perform a gallbladder removal on a realistic patient - The Robot Report
sources.claim: The most advanced autonomous surgical system reported, Johns Hopkins' SRT-H, performed only a lengthy phase (a 17-task step sequence) of a gallbladder removal, autonomously but on ex vivo pig-cadaver tissue in a research lab, with spoken corrections available from the team; it is a proof of concept, not clinical practice.
sources.transferJustification: Closest evidence to a pediatrician's operative task (autonomous cutting, clipping, tissue handling). It falls short of transfer because it is one phase of one procedure on cadaveric animal tissue in a lab, not a whole procedure on a live child.

sources.title: SRT-H: A hierarchical framework for autonomous surgery via language-conditioned imitation learning | Science Robotics
sources.claim: The Science Robotics paper itself frames the SRT-H result as step-level autonomy within a procedure (eight ex vivo gallbladders), i.e., not a complete operation on a patient.
sources.transferJustification: Establishes the ceiling of autonomous surgery as a step of a procedure on excised animal organs, so no cited system completes a whole pediatric operative instance.

sources.title: Robot performs first laparoscopic surgery without human help | ScienceDaily
sources.claim: The earlier STAR robot performed autonomous laparoscopic intestinal anastomosis, but only in four anesthetized pigs in a research setting, using hand-placed fluorescent tissue markers and a rigid predetermined plan.
sources.transferJustification: Autonomous soft-tissue suturing is the nearest analogue to laceration repair, but it does not transfer: it required marker-tagged, immobilized bowel in an anesthetized animal rather than a conscious, moving child's wound.

sources.system: da Vinci Surgical System (pediatric robot-assisted surgery program)
sources.title: Robot-Assisted Surgery at Nationwide Children's
sources.claim: Robotic surgery actually used on children in hospitals is teleoperated: the surgeon drives every instrument motion from a console.

sources.title: Johnson & Johnson Receives FDA Market Authorization in the U.S. for its OTTAVA Robotic Surgical System
sources.claim: Newly authorized clinical soft-tissue surgical robots remain surgeon-controlled platforms; the July 2026 FDA de novo authorization covers surgeon-operated general surgery procedures, with automation described only as a future direction.

sources.title: US-Based AI Company Completes World's First Fully Automated Dental Procedure on a Human - Oral Health Group
sources.claim: The only reported fully automated robotic procedure on a live human is a dental crown preparation — a one-off first-in-human event on a cooperative adult whose jaw was immobilized by a fitted mouthpiece.
sources.transferJustification: Nearest autonomous-on-live-human procedure. It does not transfer to pediatric operative tasks: rigid tooth substrate on a rigidly fixated cooperative adult, with no incision of living soft tissue, no hemostasis or wound closure, and no handling of a struggling child.

tasks.label: Examine microscopic samples to identify diseases or other abnormalities.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Surgical pathology sign-out in a hospital or reference lab: pathologist examines H&E-stained glass slides (or scanned whole-slide images) from biopsies and resections at a light microscope/workstation, identifies malignancy, grade, margins, and dictates a diagnosis.

Hematopathology: microscopic review of peripheral blood smears and bone marrow aspirate/biopsy slides to classify cytopenias, leukemias, and lymphomas, correlating with flow cytometry and clinical data.

Ancillary stain interpretation: pathologist examines immunohistochemistry, immunofluorescence, special stains, and in-situ hybridization slides to confirm or refine a diagnosis and score biomarkers (e.g., ER/PR, HER2, Ki-67).

Cytopathology: screening and interpretation of gynecologic (Pap) and non-gynecologic cytology and fine-needle aspirate smears, including adequacy assessment and identification of atypical or malignant cells.
Intraoperative frozen section: rapid microscopic examination of a frozen-section slide while the surgeon waits, rendering a diagnosis on margins or lesion identity within minutes.
Autopsy/forensic histology: microscopic examination of tissue sections taken at autopsy to identify disease processes or injury contributing to cause of death, for a medical examiner report.

tasks.label: Diagnose diseases or study medical conditions, using techniques such as gross pathology, histology, cytology, cytopathology, clinical chemistry, immunology, flow cytometry, or molecular biology.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Surgical pathology sign-out in a hospital or reference-lab office: pathologist reviews H&E (and IHC/special stain) slides of biopsies and resections at a light microscope or on a digital whole-slide viewer, correlates with the clinical history, requisition and prior cases, and renders a diagnosis (tumor type, grade, stage, margins) that is dictated into the report.

Cytopathology sign-out: review of Pap tests, fine-needle aspiration smears/cell blocks, and body-fluid cytology cases flagged or screened by cytotechnologists; the pathologist confirms or reclassifies the interpretation (e.g., HSIL, malignant, atypical) and issues the diagnostic interpretation.

Clinical pathology interpretation and consultation: reviewing chemistry, immunology/serology, coagulation, urinalysis and microbiology results, protein electrophoresis and other interpretive assays; deciding whether results indicate a disease state, adding interpretive comments, and advising the ordering clinician on further testing.

Hematopathology/molecular sign-out: interpreting flow cytometry dot plots and gating reports, immunophenotype panels, karyotype/FISH and NGS or PCR molecular results, and integrating them with the bone marrow or lymph node morphology to classify a leukemia or lymphoma.

Gross-based and intraoperative diagnosis: examining and describing a resection specimen macroscopically (and, for frozen sections, inspecting the specimen, reviewing the frozen-section slide, and phoning a rapid diagnosis, e.g., margin status, to the operating surgeon within minutes).

instances.label: Clinical microbiology sign-out: pathologist reviews culture growth reports, Gram stain images/descriptions, identification results (MALDI-TOF, biochemical) and antimicrobial susceptibility panels in the LIS, judges contaminant vs. pathogen, applies breakpoints, and issues an interpreted report with comments to the treating clinician.

Clinical chemistry and urinalysis review: pathologist reviews urinalysis (dipstick plus automated/manual sediment findings), hormonal assay values (e.g., thyroid, cortisol, HCG panels), delta checks, critical values and flagged interference/dilution results, decides on repeat or reflex testing, and writes an interpretive comment.

Fine needle aspiration cytology sign-out: pathologist examines stained FNA smears/cell block sections (glass slides at a microscope or whole-slide images), correlates with radiology and clinical history and ancillary immunostains, and renders a categorized diagnosis (e.g., Bethesda/Milan) in a signed cytology report.

Molecular pathology interpretation: pathologist reviews PCR/qPCR amplification curves, Ct values, controls and NGS variant call files for infectious-disease or oncology assays, assesses run validity, classifies variants for clinical significance, and issues a molecular diagnostic report.

Parasitology and hematology-adjacent smear interpretation: pathologist reviews ova-and-parasite concentrates, malaria thick/thin blood films with parasitemia quantification, and antigen/PCR confirmatory results referred by technologists, and confirms or amends species identification in the final report.

Integrative consultation: pathologist correlates results across microbiology, chemistry, cytology and molecular assays for a complex case (e.g., transplant, fever of unknown origin, occult malignancy), discusses with clinicians or at a tumor/ID board, and documents an integrated interpretive opinion.

tasks.label: Perform autopsies to determine causes of deaths.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Medical examiner/coroner forensic autopsy of a non-violent death (drug overdose, sudden natural death, undetermined) in the office's autopsy suite: external examination and photography, Y-incision, evisceration, organ-by-organ dissection and weighing, collection of blood/vitreous/urine for toxicology, skull sawing and brain removal, tissue sections for histology, then dictation of findings and cause of death.

Forensic autopsy of a violent or traumatic death (gunshot, blunt force, motor-vehicle, homicide, hanging) in an ME autopsy suite: documentation and measurement of wounds, trajectory tracking, recovery of projectiles and trace evidence under chain of custody, layered neck dissection, plus the full internal examination and sampling.

Consented hospital (clinical) autopsy in a hospital morgue on a patient who died on the wards: review of clinical history, full or consent-limited thoracoabdominal evisceration and dissection, examination of surgical sites and devices, extensive histology sampling, clinico-pathologic correlation report.

Perinatal, fetal, or pediatric autopsy in a hospital or ME morgue: small, delicate body; measurements and dysmorphology assessment, radiographic skeletal survey, fine dissection of small organs and congenital heart lesions, placental examination.

Autopsy on difficult remains - decomposed, burned, skeletonized, exhumed, dismembered, or highly infectious cases, sometimes in a temporary or disaster morgue: adapted dissection, anthropologic/odontologic examination, identification work, samples for DNA and toxicology under biosafety precautions.

Limited or minimally invasive post-mortem examination performed instead of a full autopsy (family or religious objection, infectious risk, research MITS protocols): post-mortem CT plus targeted needle-core sampling of organs for histology and microbiology, in the facility's imaging suite.

sources.developer: Institute of Forensic Medicine, University of Zurich / University of Bern
sources.title: Technical note: Semiautomated targeted postmortem computed tomography angiography of the pulmonary arteries using a robotic system
sources.claim: The Virtobot robotic system in a forensic-medicine imaging suite performs automated 3D surface scanning and image-guided post-mortem ... placement/biopsy on bodies; a 2023 technical note reports fully automatic needle placement for targeted post-mortem CT angiography of the pulmonary arteries.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: image-guided post-mortem tissue sampling, the physical core of a minimally invasive autopsy. Same objects (human bodies on a scanner table), same facility, millimetre-scale needle targeting; it does not cover open dissection.

sources.developer: Virtopsy project, University of Bern / University of Zurich
sources.title: Virtobot--a multi-functional robotic system for 3D surface scanning and automatic post mortem biopsy - PubMed
sources.claim: The original Virtobot prototype performed automated surface documentation and image-guided post-mortem soft-tissue biopsy accurately enough for forensic use.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic post-mortem biopsy and body-surface documentation, sub-steps of a minimally invasive autopsy; same workpiece (a corpse in a forensic institute) and comparable precision requirements.

sources.developer: Hamburg University of Technology & University Medical Center Hamburg-Eppendorf
sources.title: Robotic Tissue Sampling for Safe Post-mortem Biopsy in Infectious Corpses (arXiv:2201.12168)
sources.claim: A collaborative-robot post-mortem biopsy system (RPMB) with automatic insertion planning inserted needles and extracted tissue samples from 20 corpses (some SARS-CoV-2 positive) inside body bags under CT guidance at an institute of legal medicine, with mean placement accuracy about 7 mm.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: minimally invasive post-mortem tissue sampling performed in place of a full autopsy; identical objects and setting (human corpses in a legal-medicine CT room), so it substantiates the limited/MIA instance only.

sources.system: SRT-H (hierarchical autonomous surgical robot on da Vinci Research Kit)
sources.title: SRT-H: A hierarchical framework for autonomous surgery via language-conditioned imitation learning - PubMed
sources.claim: The most advanced demonstrated autonomous soft-tissue dissection is a single standardized surgical phase (gallbladder removal) on ex vivo pig tissue in a laboratory; no whole-body procedure has been demonstrated.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous soft-tissue dissection, the nearest capability to autopsy evisceration and organ dissection. It is confined to one standardized phase on a small ex vivo specimen in a lab rig, so it does not carry over to whole-body autopsy.

sources.system: Robotic autopsy saw (cadaveric skull and tissue cutting manipulator)
sources.title: Robotic-Assisted Surgery for Cadaveric Skull Opening: A New Method of Autopsy Procedure (Frontiers in Robotics and AI)
sources.claim: Robotization of autopsy work to date is confined to isolated sub-steps such as a robotic saw for skull opening, evaluated on ten cadavers in a forensic medicine department.
sources.transferJustification: Same task family (autopsy procedure) but only the calvarium-cutting sub-step, with autonomy not established; cited to show the frontier of autopsy automation, not to support completion.

sources.title: Virtual Autopsy in Medicolegal Investigations: A Systematic Review of Accuracy and Practical Utility
sources.claim: Imaging-based (virtual) autopsy remains a complement, not a substitute, for conventional dissection autopsy in medicolegal death investigation.
sources.transferJustification: Cited to show that the non-manual alternative to dissection autopsy does not deliver an accepted equivalent output; it is imaging, not a robotic manipulator.

tasks.label: Obtain specimens by performing procedures, such as biopsies or fine needle aspirations (FNAs) of superficial nodules.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Outpatient FNA clinic, palpation-guided FNA of a palpable superficial nodule (thyroid, cervical lymph node, salivary gland, subcutaneous mass): pathologist consents and positions the patient, palpates and immobilizes the lesion between fingers, preps skin, makes 2-4 needle passes with oscillating in-and-out motion until material appears in the hub, expels material onto slides, makes and fixes/air-dries smears, does an on-site Diff-Quik adequacy check, then achieves hemostasis and dresses the site.

Clinic or ultrasound suite, cytopathologist-performed ultrasound-guided FNA of a sub-2 cm thyroid nodule or deep cervical/axillary lymph node: probe held in one hand while the needle is steered in real time into the lesion, several passes with redirection, smears prepared plus a needle rinse into liquid medium for flow cytometry or molecular testing, adequacy assessed on site.

Clinic procedure room, core needle biopsy of a superficial palpable mass (soft-tissue mass, lymph node) under local anesthesia: skin nick, coaxial or spring-loaded device fired several times under palpation or ultrasound, cores placed in formalin/saline, bleeding controlled and dressing applied.

Inpatient bedside or ED consult FNA: an ill, immobile, or uncooperative patient in a hospital bed with lines, monitors and limited access; awkward positioning and a portable slide-prep setup; specimen must still be adequate for diagnosis on the first visit.

Difficult-case FNA in clinic: anxious or pediatric patient, cystic lesion requiring drainage followed by re-sampling of the residual solid component, bloody/vascular aspirates requiring capillary technique change, or a patient on anticoagulation needing prolonged pressure.

sources.title: Vitestro Launches Aletta™: First Autonomous Phlebotomy Device
sources.claim: Aletta by Vitestro is a CE-marked autonomous robotic phlebotomy device that uses AI-driven Doppler ultrasound to find a vein in a fixtured arm, inserts the needle robotically and fills collection tubes; it was commercially launched in European hospitals and laboratories from March 2025. It obtains blood only — it does not target a lesion or prepare cytology smears.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: ultrasound-guided venipuncture for diagnostic blood collection. It is the closest deployed autonomous percutaneous-sampling system in a structured clinical facility, but transfer to this task is only partial: the target is a large vein in an arm placed in a device fixture rather than a specific palpable or sonographically identified nodule, and the accepted output is filled blood tubes rather than multi-pass cellular aspirate expelled and smeared onto slides.

sources.title: XACT Robotics Announces Completion of Enrollment in Pilot Trial Evaluating Use of its Robotic System to Perform CT-Guided Percutaneous Procedures in the Lung
sources.claim: The XACT ACE robotic system performs hands-free, image-based planning plus robotic needle insertion and steering for CT-guided percutaneous procedures including biopsies; it is FDA cleared and installed in interventional radiology departments. It places the needle only — the physician still acquires and prepares the specimen.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: CT-guided percutaneous needle placement for deep biopsy. It substantiates robotic needle placement to a planned target in a hospital procedure suite, but not the whole instance: the physician defines the trajectory, performs the sampling through the placed introducer, and prepares the specimen, and the system is used for deep CT-visible lesions rather than palpation-guided superficial nodule aspiration with smear preparation.

sources.developer: University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill / Vanderbilt University / University of Utah
sources.title: Autonomous medical needle steering in vivo
sources.claim: A research robot autonomously steered a flexible needle to lung-nodule-sized targets in living tissue, demonstrated in anesthetized pigs in a laboratory/animal-OR setting; targets were selected manually and no specimen preparation was involved.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous needle navigation to a nodule target for biopsy. It shows machine targeting precision comparable to nodule radii, but only in anesthetized animals in a research setting, and it covers needle placement alone rather than the cellular sampling, slide preparation and adequacy assessment that define this task.

sources.developer: Chinese research team (published in Nature Communications)
sources.title: A fully autonomous robotic ultrasound system for thyroid scanning
sources.claim: FARUS, a fully autonomous robotic ultrasound ..., scanned the thyroids of patients in a clinical study, detecting nodules and producing assessments largely consistent with physicians; the system performs imaging only and does not perform needle procedures.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous sonographic localization of thyroid nodules in patients. It substantiates that a robot can find superficial nodules on live patients in a hospital, but it performs no needle insertion, aspiration, or specimen preparation, so it cannot substantiate completion of an FNA.

sources.system: Autonomous 3D-US guided gantry breast biopsy robot (Liang et al.)
sources.developer: academic research group, reviewed in Clinical Breast Cancer
sources.title: Robotics in Screening, Diagnosis and Treatment of Breast Cancer: A Perspective View
sources.claim: Peer-reviewed review evidence indicates that autonomous ultrasound-guided biopsy robots have been evaluated only on ex vivo phantoms (e.g., turkey breast with embedded simulated lesions), not on patients.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous ultrasound-guided needle biopsy of a superficial lesion. This is the closest analogue to superficial-nodule FNA, and it establishes that such autonomy remains at ex vivo phantom stage, supporting a negative judgment rather than completion.

tasks.label: Perform or interpret the outcomes of diagnostic imaging procedures including magnetic resonance imaging (MRI), computer tomography (CT), positron emission tomography (PET), nuclear cardiology treadmill studies, mammography, or ultrasound.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Reading-room interpretation of cross-sectional studies (body/neuro CT, MRI) acquired by technologists: reviewing hundreds of images per study on a PACS workstation, comparing priors, and dictating a signed diagnostic report under turnaround pressure.

Interpretation of radiographs, technologist-acquired ultrasound studies, nuclear medicine scans and PET/CT: reviewing images and tech worksheets, correlating with clinical history, dictating and signing reports in a hospital or outpatient imaging center reading room.

Breast imaging center: batch interpretation of screening mammograms (with tomosynthesis) plus diagnostic mammographic workups \BI-RADS assessment, recall decisions, dictated reports, comparison with prior films.

Radiologist personally performs a diagnostic ultrasound at the scanner in the imaging suite \ targeted breast/thyroid/abdominal scanning or problem-solving after the sonographer: manipulating the transducer on the patient, adjusting gain/depth/Doppler, capturing documentation images, then interpreting and reporting.

Radiologist performs a fluoroscopic diagnostic study (barium swallow/upper GI, cystogram, arthrogram injection) in the fluoro suite: positioning and coaching the patient, timing contrast, running live fluoroscopy, taking spot images, dictating the interpretation.

Nuclear cardiology treadmill stress study in the nuclear medicine/stress lab: supervising or performing the exercise portion with the patient on the treadmill, monitoring ECG/symptoms, timing radiotracer injection, then interpreting perfusion and gated function images.

sources.title: NeuraSignal's NovaGuide Intelligent Ultrasound System Significantly Outperforms Standard of Care for Detecting Stroke-Associated Heart Defects - BioSpace
sources.claim: NovaGuide is an FDA-cleared robotic transcranial Doppler ultrasound platform whose robotic probe pods locate the temporal acoustic window and acquire cerebral blood-flow data without a sonographer; it automates one narrow ultrasound acquisition, not radiologist-level exam performance plus diagnostic reporting.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic acquisition of a diagnostic ultrasound exam on a patient in a hospital. Bears on the 'perform ultrasound' instance, but covers a single fixed protocol (cerebral flow) rather than the varied, indication-driven scanning and signed interpretation a radiologist delivers.

sources.title: Houston Methodist uses AI brain ultrasound to reduce open heart surgery complications | Healthcare IT News
sources.claim: The same robotic TCD system is in clinical use at Houston Methodist; it is described as fully automated with AI assisting waveform reading, i.e. the clinician still reads and interprets.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated ultrasound acquisition inside a hospital (E2 setting); relevant to whether a robot could stand in for a radiologist performing ultrasound, but limited to cerebral Doppler monitoring without diagnostic reporting.

sources.system: Autonomous lightweight ultrasound robot for liver sonography
sources.developer: academic group with Beijing Tsinghua Changgung Hospital
sources.title: Beyond hospital reach: Autonomous lightweight ultrasound robot for liver sonography (arXiv 2510.08106)
sources.claim: A lightweight autonomous ultrasound robot autonomously localized aorta, IVC and portal vein planes on volunteers in a hospital ultrasound department \ an autonomous acquisition feasibility study, not a system issuing diagnostic interpretations.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous acquisition of standard ultrasound planes on humans. Bears on 'perform ultrasound' but stops at plane acquisition for pre-specified targets, without pathology search or reporting.

sources.claim: A 2026 review of autonomous robotic ultrasound reports research-stage autonomy for specific exams (thyroid, carotid) while noting degradation under soft-tissue deformation, calibration drift and noisy image feedback \ no general-purpose autonomous diagnostic sonography at clinician quality.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic image acquisition; establishes the maturity ceiling of robotic scanning relevant to radiologist-performed ultrasound instances.

sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic cardiac ultrasound acquisition; autonomy not established, so treated as teleoperated and unable to support a positive judgment.

sources.title: Radiology gets 68 new FDA-cleared algorithms | Radiology Business
sources.claim: Automation of imaging interpretation is dominated by software-only AI algorithms (1,163 FDA-cleared radiology algorithms as of March 2026) used as detection/triage aids under radiologist oversight; these are not physically embodied systems.
sources.transferJustification: Context for the interpretation instances: the available automation is software-only, explicitly excluded from counting as a robotic system under these rules.
