tasks.label: Recognize or treat complications during and after procedures, including blood pressure problems, pain, oversedation, or bleeding.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Intraprocedural hemodynamic event during a moderately sedated IR procedure in the hospital angiography suite (e.g., vasovagal bradycardia/hypotension during biliary or nephrostomy manipulation, or hypertensive surge). The radiologist reads the monitors, halts or modifies the procedure, positions the patient (legs up/Trendelenburg), directs or gives an IV fluid bolus, atropine or a pressor, reduces sedation, and re-examines the patient before resuming.

Oversedation / respiratory depression during moderate sedation: falling SpO2, apnea or loss of capnography waveform. The radiologist stops sedative dosing, stimulates the patient, repositions the head/performs jaw thrust or places an airway adjunct, increases oxygen, bag-mask ventilates if needed, gives naloxone or flumazenil, and calls anesthesia if the airway is not secured.

Arterial or venous access-site bleeding or expanding hematoma (femoral or radial) noticed in the suite or in the post-procedure recovery bay. The radiologist palpates and inspects the groin/wrist, applies firm manual or device compression for 10-20 minutes, scans with ultrasound for pseudoaneurysm, and escalates to thrombin injection, closure device, or covered stent if it does not settle.

Major intraprocedural hemorrhage recognized on angiography or CT during the case (vessel perforation, capsular tear, bleeding after biopsy or tumor ablation). The radiologist recognizes contrast extravasation or a falling pressure, balloon-tamponades or embolizes with coils/gelfoam or places a covered stent, and coordinates transfusion and resuscitation.

Post-procedure pain, nausea or vagal symptoms in the recovery unit: the radiologist assesses the patient at the bedside, checks the puncture site and dressing, differentiates expected post-embolization pain from a complication, and orders/administers analgesia or antiemetic before discharge or ward transfer.

Delayed complication on the ward or on return to the department hours to days later (retroperitoneal hematoma, pneumothorax after lung biopsy, sepsis or abscess after drainage). The radiologist examines the patient at the bedside, orders and reviews imaging, and performs a bedside intervention such as chest tube/aspiration or repeat drainage, plus resuscitation orders.

sources.developer: Université Libre de Bruxelles / UC Irvine (Joosten, Rinehart, Cannesson) academic consortium
sources.title: Control of Postoperative Hypotension Using a Closed-Loop System for Norepinephrine Infusion in Patients After Cardiac Surgery: A Randomized Trial
sources.claim: A closed-loop vasopressor controller autonomously titrates norepinephrine to an arterial-pressure target in post-cardiac-surgery ICU patients — the closest existing automated treatment of a blood pressure complication — but it acts only on a pre-placed arterial line and pre-loaded drug, does no diagnosis of the cause and no physical intervention, and remains an investigational research device under clinician supervision.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated correction of intraoperative/postoperative hypotension. It bears on the 'blood pressure problems' element of this task, but performance does not carry over: the controller only adjusts one infusion through equipment a clinician has already placed, cannot determine whether hypotension is vagal, hemorrhagic, anaphylactic or sedation-related, and cannot stop the procedure, compress a bleeding site, or support an airway.

sources.title: Johnson & Johnson bails on Sedasys anesthesia device
sources.claim: The only automated sedation-delivery machine ever approved for routine clinical use in the US, which reduced propofol and increased oxygen when it detected oversedation, was withdrawn from the market and is not available today; it also required a clinician present to rescue the airway.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: machine management of procedural sedation depth. Even at its peak it only titrated propofol for healthy ASA I-II endoscopy patients and depended on a trained clinician for rescue; it never performed airway maneuvers, reversal-agent decisions, or bleeding management, and it is no longer marketed.

sources.developer: McGill University / McGill University Health Centre (T.M. Hemmerling)
sources.title: Introducing the world's first intubation robot | Newsroom - McGill University
sources.claim: Robotic airway management in humans has been done only under continuous joystick control by a physician at a remote console, i.e. teleoperation, not autonomous rescue of an oversedated patient.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: securing the airway of a sedated patient, the definitive treatment for oversedation with apnea. It cannot support a positive judgment because it is continuously teleoperated and was demonstrated only on elective, pre-planned intubations.

sources.system: Sentante teleoperated endovascular platform; LIBERTY robot; GenesisX magnetic navigation
sources.title: ECR 2026: Remote Interventional Radiology with Robotics
sources.claim: As of the 2026 European Congress of Radiology, robotic platforms in interventional radiology (Sentante, LIBERTY, GenesisX) are teleoperated navigation systems still working toward routine clinical use; automation of vascular intervention remains limited and no platform manages procedural complications on its own.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: catheter/guidewire work in the angiography suite, which is how a radiologist would embolize or stent an intraprocedural bleed. Performance does not carry over because these systems are driven step by step by the physician; the recognition and decision-making that define this task stay with the human.

sources.developer: Johns Hopkins University (Axel Krieger) / Children's National Hospital
sources.title: Robot performs laparoscopic surgery, suturing intestinal tissue
sources.claim: The most advanced autonomous soft-tissue surgical robot completed a pre-planned bowel anastomosis in an anesthetized pig under human supervision; there is no comparable autonomous system operating on human patients or reacting to unplanned intraoperative bleeding.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous manipulation and suturing of living soft tissue, the physical skill underlying hemostasis. It does not transfer: the demonstration was a single pre-planned suture line in an animal on a prepared field, with no requirement to detect an unexpected complication or choose a treatment.

sources.title: Robotic Phlebotomy Study Signals Automation Shift for Clinical Labs
sources.claim: Autonomous needle-based patient contact in a healthcare facility now works at scale only for a single scripted procedure on a cooperative, stable outpatient — venous blood draw with imaging guidance — which marks the current boundary of clinical robot autonomy.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous image-guided needle placement in a patient's arm, followed by compression of the puncture site. It shows the ceiling rather than transfer: the robot handles one predetermined action on a seated, stable patient and has no capacity to detect a deteriorating patient or select and carry out a rescue treatment.

tasks.label: Perform interventional procedures such as image-guided biopsy, percutaneous transluminal angioplasty, transhepatic biliary drainage, or nephrostomy catheter placement.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Percutaneous image-guided core/FNA biopsy (liver, lung, kidney, retroperitoneal node, soft-tissue mass) under CT or ultrasound in a hospital radiology procedure suite or hospital-owned outpatient imaging center: radiologist reviews prior imaging, positions and preps the patient, sterile field and local anesthetic, plans an angle avoiding bowel/vessels/pleura, advances a coaxial needle with breath-hold coordination, fires multiple cores, checks specimen adequacy, confirms no pneumothorax/bleed, achieves hemostasis and dresses the site.

Image-guided drainage and catheter placement: abscess/fluid collection drain, percutaneous nephrostomy, transhepatic biliary drain, pigtail chest tube, under CT/ultrasound/fluoroscopy in the IR suite or at ICU bedside with a portable ultrasound; needle access to a small target (collecting system, duct, collection), wire exchange, tract dilation, catheter deployment and coiling, contrast confirmation, catheter fixation and bag connection, sedation monitoring throughout.

Endovascular therapy in the angiography suite: diagnostic angiography plus percutaneous transluminal angioplasty/stenting of peripheral or dialysis-access lesions, or embolization; ultrasound-guided arterial/venous puncture, sheath placement, catheter/guidewire navigation through tortuous anatomy under fluoroscopy and contrast, balloon sizing and inflation, treating dissection or spasm, closure device or manual compression hemostasis.

Image-guided vascular access: PICC line, tunneled central venous catheter, dialysis catheter or implanted port, in the IR suite under ultrasound and fluoroscopy; sterile draping, ultrasound-guided deep vein puncture, wire and peel-away sheath, subcutaneous tunneling and pocket creation, tip positioning at the cavoatrial junction, suturing/securement and dressing.

Complex or emergent intervention: TIPS, trauma/GI-bleed embolization, thermal or cryo tumor ablation, urgent drain in an unstable patient; performed in the IR suite (sometimes hybrid OR) with anesthesia support, unpredictable anatomy, intraprocedural decision changes and complication management.

Fixtured or superficial minor procedures in an outpatient imaging center: stereotactic or ultrasound-guided vacuum-assisted breast biopsy with the breast compressed in the stereotactic unit, thyroid FNA, marker clip deployment, superficial lymph node biopsy; cooperative awake patient, short procedure, specimen radiograph and post-procedure compression.

sources.title: FDA Clears the XACT Robot for CT-Guided Percutaneous Procedures
sources.claim: XACT ACE is an FDA-cleared, patient-mounted robot that performs hands-free insertion and non-linear steering of needles/probes to a target during CT-guided percutaneous procedures; the interventional radiologist still plans the trajectory at the console, prepares the patient, and performs all sampling, drainage and post-procedure steps. It is in controlled market release at select US radiology centers.
sources.transferJustification: Directly on task: CT-guided needle placement for biopsy/drainage/ablation, but it covers only the needle-placement sub-step of the procedure.

sources.title: Clinical evaluation of a robotic system for precise CT-guided percutaneous procedures (Abdominal Radiology)
sources.claim: In a prospective two-centre clinical study, 32 abdominal/pelvic biopsies used the patient-mounted CT-guided robot to place 17 G needles with ~1.6 mm accuracy, but planning (target, skin entry, checkpoints) was done by the operator and additional CT checkpoint scans were used to permit stepwise trajectory correction, i.e. the robot performed guided needle placement, not the whole biopsy.

sources.system: FDA-cleared surgical robots (49 systems, incl. interventional radiology)
sources.developer: multiple (review by Nagy/Krieger-affiliated authors, npj Digital Medicine)
sources.title: Levels of autonomy in FDA-cleared surgical robots: a systematic review
sources.claim: A systematic review of all 49 FDA-cleared surgical robots found interventional radiology systems reach at most Level 2 (task autonomy — executing preprogrammed actions for a specific task under surgeon control), with no cleared system at Level 4 or 5; i.e. no cleared device conducts an interventional procedure end to end.

sources.title: Robotic-assisted percutaneous coronary intervention: experience in Switzerland (PMC)
sources.claim: Robotic percutaneous coronary/peripheral intervention with CorPath GRX is remote-controlled: the operator sits in a radiation-shielded cockpit driving guidewires and balloons with joysticks, and manual steps (arterial access, guiding-catheter intubation of the target vessel) are still performed by hand at the table.

sources.system: Ultrasound-guided robotic system for autonomous percutaneous intervention (research prototype)

sources.claim: A 2024 research system for ultrasound-guided autonomous percutaneous needle placement reports that, across the field, no ultrasound-guided robotic system for percutaneous intervention ...; the presented system was evaluated in a bench/phantom setting.
sources.transferJustification: Same modality and target class (ultrasound-guided needle insertion in soft tissue); establishes the state of the art for autonomous percutaneous needle work.

sources.title: Vitestro unveils Aletta robotic phlebotomy device — CAP TODAY
sources.claim: The most advanced deployed autonomous needle robot in healthcare performs superficial peripheral venipuncture end to end (tourniquet, skin prep, AI ultrasound vein finding, puncture, tube filling) in CE-marked commercial use in European blood-collection settings — far short of sterile IR catheter, drain or endovascular work.
sources.transferJustification: Related task (ultrasound-guided needle-into-vein). It does not transfer to radiologist vascular access: no sterile field, no deep vein guidewire/sheath/tunneling, no fluoroscopic tip positioning or suturing, and only a superficial forearm target.

sources.title: FDA clears Quantum Surgical's Epione robot for abdominal cancers
sources.claim: Epione is an FDA-cleared, commercially sold interventional-oncology robot that plans, targets and confirms percutaneous liver/abdominal tumour ablation, but it assists the physician, who performs the needle procedure with the robot's guidance rather than the robot conducting the intervention alone.
sources.transferJustification: Same procedure family as image-guided biopsy/ablation needle placement in the IR suite.

tasks.label: Administer radioisotopes to clinical patients or research subjects.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Routine intravenous administration of a diagnostic radiotracer (18F-FDG for PET/CT, 99mTc agents for bone/cardiac/renal SPECT) to a cooperative adult outpatient, or to a research subject on a PET protocol, in a hospital or freestanding nuclear medicine/PET department: verify patient and prescription, draw and assay the weight-based dose behind shielding, place/confirm a peripheral IV, inject, flush with saline, and record administered activity and residual.

Intravenous diagnostic tracer administration where access is difficult: dose given through an implanted chest port or PICC/central line in an oncology patient, a pediatric or sedated patient, or a bedridden inpatient injected at the bedside or in the ICU with a portable shielded syringe.

Non-injected administration: handing and supervising ingestion of an I-131 or I-123 capsule or oral liquid in a shielded therapy/uptake room (with survey and radiation-safety instructions), or supervising an inhaled administration such as 99mTc-DTPA aerosol or Xe-133 gas through a mouthpiece for a ventilation scan.

Therapeutic radiopharmaceutical given intravenously in a nuclear medicine therapy suite: 177Lu-DOTATATE or 177Lu-PSMA-617 infused over 30-40 minutes from a shielded vial/syringe, or a Ra-223 slow bolus, with pre/post activity assay, extravasation checks, and patient monitoring during infusion.

Catheter- or image-guided delivery of an isotope by the physician: intra-arterial Y-90 microsphere radioembolization in an interventional radiology angiography suite (selective hepatic catheterization, delivery box, fluoroscopic monitoring), or intrathecal In-111 DTPA for cisternography, or intracavitary instillation.

Small-volume special-route injections: intradermal, subareolar or peritumoral 99mTc sulfur colloid for sentinel lymph node mapping in a breast or melanoma patient, and similar intra-articular or intralesional administrations, requiring precise superficial placement at an anatomic landmark on an awake patient.

sources.title: MEDRAD® Intego PET infusion system - Bayer in radiology
sources.claim: MEDRAD Intego is a commercially marketed, fully automated PET infusion system installed in hospital nuclear medicine departments that assays and delivers a patient-specific dose of 18F-FDG or 18F-NaF from ... into the patient's line.

sources.claim: IRIS is in clinical use for therapy infusions at a cancer institute, where it lowered staff exposure during 177Lu-DOTATATE and 177Lu-PSMA-617 patient infusions compared with normal infusion sets.

sources.title: Vitestro Publishes Landmark Peer-Reviewed Multicenter Clinical Study of Autonomous Robotic Phlebotomy in Clinical Chemistry
sources.claim: A multicenter clinical trial of the Aletta autonomous robotic phlebotomy ... in three hospital outpatient phlebotomy departments (1,633 patients) reported 94.5% first-stick success, 0.6% adverse events and 0.3% hemolysis, all better than published manual rates.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous ultrasound-guided peripheral venipuncture. Radiotracer administration requires the same physical act — locating a forearm/antecubital vein on a seated adult and inserting a needle into the lumen — in the same class of hospital outpatient room; only the fluid direction differs, and the metered delivery of the radioactive dose through that access is itself automated by the injectors cited above.

sources.transferJustification: Establishes maturity/deployment status of the autonomous venipuncture system used for the transfer argument above.

tasks.label: Test dosage evaluation instruments and survey meters to ensure they are operating properly.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Daily/weekly constancy check of the dose calibrator in a nuclear medicine hot lab: take the sealed Cs-137 or Co-57 reference source out of its lead pig, lower it into the well insert, select the isotope setting, read the displayed activity, compare with the decay-corrected expected value (±10%), return the source and record the result in the QC log.

Pre-use operational check of a handheld GM or ion-chamber survey meter at the hot-lab bench or radiopharmaceutical dispensing area: verify the calibration sticker date, run the battery check, switch ranges, hold the probe against the dedicated check source, confirm the reading falls in the expected band and that audio/needle respond, and log it.

Periodic (quarterly/annual) dose calibrator QC in the hot lab: accuracy against several NIST-traceable sealed sources, linearity by serial measurement of a decaying Tc-99m or F-18 source (or with a shield set) over many hours, and geometry/volume dependence checks, with calculation of deviations and documentation for the radiation safety file.

Annual calibration verification of portable survey meters and dose-rate instruments in a calibration facility: the instrument is mounted at set distances from a known Cs-137 field, exposed at several points across its ranges, as-found and as-left readings are recorded, pass/fail is judged against tolerance, and a certificate and sticker are issued.

Batch functional checks of other dosage-evaluation instruments in a hospital radiation safety office or hot lab: pocket ion chambers and electronic personal dosimeters charged/zeroed, exposed to a known dose and their readings verified; area monitors and wipe-test well counters given daily check-source and background counts with results logged.

Ad hoc functional check of a portable survey meter at the point of use before a bedside or procedure-room task (e.g., before surveying a Y-90 or I-131 therapy patient, room, or a contamination event): power-on, battery and check-source response confirmed amid patient-room clutter, staff, and time pressure, then the survey proceeds.

sources.title: THEODORICO 2 Robotic Dispenser for Radiopharmaceuticals
sources.claim: Theodorico 2 is a commercially sold robotic dispensing isolator for radiopharmaceuticals in which a robot handles vials through all stages and activity is measured in an integrated dose calibrator and verified in a second dose calibrator.
sources.transferJustification: Dose calibrator constancy/accuracy testing requires exactly this manipulation and measurement: moving a small sealed vial/source into a dose calibrator well and reading the activity, which the robot does unattended with automatic recording.

sources.system: Tema Sinergie Karl 100 multi-dose administration system
sources.title: Karl 100 multi-dose administration system – LabLogic
sources.claim: The Karl 100 automatically handles and uncaps lead pigs and vials of any major brand, perforates septa and dispenses measured activity, with built-in radiation monitoring and 21 CFR part 11 compliant control software.
sources.transferJustification: Retrieving a sealed reference source from its lead pig and presenting it to an activity meter is the manipulation core of a dose-calibrator constancy check; the Karl 100 performs this handling automatically.

sources.system: Tema Sinergie Karl100 at Charing Cross Hospital
sources.title: Charing Cross Hospital invests in the Tema Sinergie Karl100 autoinjector – LabLogic
sources.claim: The Karl100 automated dispensing/administration system has been installed and put into clinical service in hospital nuclear medicine/imaging departments.
sources.transferJustification: Establishes that robotic handling of radioactive vials/pigs with integrated activity measurement is a fielded hospital technology, not a laboratory demonstration.

sources.title: Wizard2 Automated Gamma Counters brochure
sources.claim: Wizard2 automated gamma counters use a robotic sample changer that lifts sample vials from a conveyor into well-type NaI detectors for automated counting sequences, with barcode sample identification and rule-based validation.
sources.transferJustification: Daily QC of well counters and dose calibrators requires repeatedly presenting a standard sealed source to a well detector and logging counts; the robotic sample changer performs precisely this presentation and automated readout.

sources.system: Boston Dynamics Spot with Orbit / Levatas gauge reading
sources.title: Automated Visual Inspection | Boston Dynamics
sources.claim: Spot performs autonomous inspection rounds in industrial facilities, using integrated computer-vision gauge-reading models to read analog displays and raise alerts when readings fall outside the desired range; customers have run thousands of autonomous missions inspecting over 130,000 industrial assets.
sources.transferJustification: The readout-and-judge step of an instrument functional check — reading an analog needle display and flagging out-of-tolerance values — is demonstrated autonomously here on human-designed meters.

sources.system: Maholo LabDroid at the Robotics Innovation Center
sources.developer: Robotic Biology Institute / Institute of Science Tokyo
sources.title: Japan: World-first fully automated medicine lab with humanoids, robots and no humans
sources.claim: A robotics laboratory at the Institute of Science Tokyo runs medical research experiments with ten robots and no on-site human staff, including the dual-arm Maholo LabDroid that transfers precise reagent volumes and operates temperature-controlled laboratory equipment.
sources.transferJustification: Shows robot-only laboratory cells can carry out fine handling of small vessels and operation of benchtop instruments unattended, the manipulation class needed for source-handling QC checks — but only in a facility built around the robots.

tasks.label: Order or perform diagnostic tests such as skin pricks and intradermal, patch, or delayed hypersensitivity tests.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Comprehensive aeroallergen percutaneous panel (~30-60 extracts) applied to the back of a seated/prone adult in an allergy clinic exam room: skin cleaned and gridded, multi-head applicators or lancets pressed at marked sites, 15-20 min wait with observation, wheal/flare measured with a ruler at each site and charted against histamine/glycerin controls.

Focused prick panel of about 10-24 allergens (seasonal aeroallergen screen or a small extract-based food/drug screen) on the volar forearms of a cooperative adult: droplets applied and pricked, 15-20 min timer, wheals measured and recorded.

Pediatric skin prick testing (infant to school-age) in a pediatric allergy clinic: child held on a parent's lap or lying prone, food and aeroallergen extracts pricked on the back, distraction and restraint of a squirming, sometimes crying child, itch control, reading and measuring wheals at 15 min.

Intradermal testing in the clinic procedure room: after negative pricks, graded 0.02-0.05 mL intradermal injections (penicillin/other drug, hymenoptera venom, or aeroallergen confirmation) raising 3 mm blebs at spaced sites on the volar forearm or upper arm, sequential dose escalation with vital-sign observation for systemic reaction, measurement of wheal growth at 15-20 min.

Patch testing and other delayed hypersensitivity tests: 30-80 allergen chambers taped in labeled rows on the patient's back (plus PPD or candida/tetanus intradermal DTH when indicated), instructions on keeping the area dry, patient returns at 48 h for removal and skin marking and again at 96 h for grading of erythema/papules/vesicles.

Ordering serologic and cellular immune workups in the EHR (specific IgE panel, total IgE, immunoglobulin levels, complement, lymphocyte subsets, vaccine titers), selecting the panel, entering the order, and having the specimen drawn at the clinic's or hospital's blood-draw station before results return to the physician.

sources.title: Artificial Intelligence (AI)-assisted readout method for the evaluation of skin prick automated test results | Nature Communications
sources.claim: The SPAT device (Hippo Dx) autonomously performs twelve simultaneous epidermal pricks with fixed allergen dose and controlled force on a patient's forearm and images the arm 15 minutes later for digital wheal measurement; it was operated by nurses in outpatient ENT clinics of several hospitals during a 2023-2024 multicentre study, and is stated to be implemented in clinical practice.

sources.title: Meet the S.P.A.T. | The Skin Prick Automated Test
sources.claim: SPAT is a CE/MDR-certified commercial product: its prick tool applies 12 pricks ... while adapting to the arm surface, selects allergens from a tray of up to 24 identified vials, auto-discards lancets, images the site and produces AI wheal measurements that the physician validates; customer hospitals include UZ Leuven, ZOL Genk and CHU Liege.

sources.title: Skin Prick Automated Test device offers more reliable allergy test results compared to a manual skin prick test - PubMed
sources.claim: In a head-to-head clinical comparison with manual skin prick testing using common inhalant allergens, the automated device produced fewer inconsistent results and a better patient experience, supporting worker-quality output.

sources.title: Evaluation of skin prick location on the forearm using a novel skin prick automated test device (PMC10646417)
sources.claim: In the SPAT procedure the patient simply rests the forearm against the designated location on the device and an operator starts the run from a touchscreen, after which pricking proceeds automatically; the device's prick tool moves to a lancet tray to collect lancets before pricking.

sources.title: Vitestro raises $70m to fuel blood-drawing robot's global commercial readiness - Medical Device Network
sources.claim: Vitestro's Aletta autonomous robotic phlebotomy device received a European CE mark in ... and began being deployed in European healthcare settings (hospital and laboratory blood-draw rooms) in March 2025, with one supervisor overseeing two devices drawing blood from patients.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: venipuncture for ordered laboratory tests. The physician's ordering step is informational; the only physical act in that instance is specimen collection from a seated patient's arm in the clinic, which this robot performs autonomously at reported 95% first-stick success comparable to human phlebotomists.

tasks.label: Conduct physical examinations of patients.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Outpatient allergy clinic exam room: new or follow-up adult with allergic rhinitis/asthma. Physician inspects eyes and nasal mucosa (speculum/otoscope), ears, oropharynx, palpates sinuses and cervical lymph nodes, auscultates lungs and heart, inspects skin, and documents findings while conversing with a partially gowned, seated patient.

Pediatric allergy clinic visit: infant or young child with food allergy, eczema and/or asthma, often squirming on a parent's lap. Requires coaxing, otoscopy and throat inspection, chest auscultation between cries, full skin inspection for eczema distribution, and growth/nutrition assessment.

Skin-focused exam in clinic for chronic urticaria, angioedema or atopic dermatitis: whole-body inspection and palpation of lesions (wheals, lichenification, excoriation), eliciting dermographism by stroking the skin, checking for lip/periorbital swelling, and grading severity (e.g., EASI/SCORAD).

Focused urgent exam in the clinic during procedures — reading skin-prick/intradermal test sites, monitoring after immunotherapy injections or during an oral food challenge — assessing airway, breathing, auscultating for wheeze, checking skin for hives and vitals in a patient who may be reacting.

Hospital inpatient or ED consult at the bedside: patient with drug reaction, angioedema, or suspected immunodeficiency, often with IV lines, monitors, and limited mobility; exam includes airway/oropharynx, lung auscultation, lymphoid tissue and abdominal palpation, and full skin survey.

sources.system: Unitree G1 humanoid with bi-manual teleoperation system (UCSD ARCLab / UCSD School of Medicine)
sources.developer: University of California San Diego (Atar, Liang, Joyce, Richter, Wood, Goldberg, Suresh, Yip)
sources.title: Humanoids in Hospitals: A Technical Study of Humanoid Surrogates for Dexterous Medical Interventions
sources.claim: State-of-the-art humanoid robot attempts at clinical physical-examination tasks (stethoscope use, laryngoscopy, ultrasound, needle tasks) were performed entirely by human teleoperation, with noted limits in force output and sensor sensitivity affecting clinical accuracy.
sources.transferJustification: Directly targets physical examination tasks on patients/manikins, the same task rated here; it shows the leading humanoid attempt is teleoperated, not autonomous, so it cannot support a positive judgment.

sources.system: Autonomous auscultation platform (UR3e arm + RGB-D vision, Lopes et al.)
sources.title: Development of a Collaborative Robotic Platform for Autonomous Auscultation
sources.claim: A collaborative robot arm with 3D vision autonomously located auscultation points and placed a stethoscope on the chest of six human subjects in a laboratory setting; only the auscultation sub-step, not a complete physical examination, was performed.
sources.transferJustification: Auscultation is one component of a physician's physical exam; it is cited to show that only isolated exam modalities have been automated, on healthy volunteers in a lab, without inspection of ears/nose/throat, palpation, or clinical interpretation.

sources.developer: Hallym University, Republic of Korea (In cheol Jeong)
sources.title: iApp: An Autonomous Inspection, Auscultation, Percussion, and Palpation Platform
sources.claim: A proof-of-concept platform automated inspection, auscultation, percussion and palpation of ... abdomen on 30 healthy young subjects, classifying abdominal divisions at 89% accuracy — a research prototype, not a clinical examination producing physician-grade findings.
sources.transferJustification: Closest published attempt at automating the classical four-part physical exam; cited to show the state of the art is limited to abdominal-region signal classification in healthy volunteers, far short of a physician-quality exam.

sources.system: Autonomous total body photography (TBP) and dermoscopic imaging device (JAMA Dermatology cohort study)
sources.developer: Study conducted at two dermatology clinics in Spain
sources.title: Standard Dermatoscope Images vs an Autonomous Total Body Photography and Dermoscopic Imaging Device - PubMed
sources.claim: An autonomous imaging cabin photographed the whole body and captured dermoscopic images of lesions in 316 patients at two dermatology clinics, with image quality non-inferior to manual dermoscopy; it images skin but performs no palpation, no other exam modality, and no clinical assessment.
sources.transferJustification: Automated skin imaging is a partial substitute for the visual-inspection component of a skin-focused exam; cited to show that even the most mature autonomous 'exam' device only acquires images for a clinician to interpret, omitting palpation, dermographism testing and severity grading.

sources.system: Autonomous lightweight ultrasound robot for liver sonography
sources.developer: Tsinghua University / Beijing Tsinghua Changgung Hospital collaboration
sources.title: Beyond hospital reach: Autonomous lightweight ultrasound robot for liver sonography
sources.claim: An autonomous ultrasound robot performed scanning on patients in the ultrasound department of a hospital, demonstrating autonomous physical contact procedures on patients in a clinical environment, but limited to sonographic imaging of specified planes.
sources.transferJustification: Robotic sonography is a related patient-contact diagnostic procedure in a hospital; cited to bound the state of the art — autonomous contact is feasible for a single instrumented imaging task, not for a multi-modality clinical physical examination.

tasks.label: Perform allergen provocation tests such as nasal, conjunctival, bronchial, oral, food, or medication challenges.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Outpatient oral food challenge in an allergy clinic or hospital day unit: physician prepares/verifies graded doses of a suspect food (peanut, milk, egg, sesame), feeds escalating doses to a child or adult every 15-30 minutes, repeatedly examines skin, mouth, chest and abdomen, records vitals, judges equivocal symptoms, decides to stop or continue, and treats reactions (antihistamine, intramuscular epinephrine) before discharge with a verdict.

Medication (drug) challenge or rapid desensitization in clinic or infusion suite: graded oral or IV doses of penicillin/amoxicillin, NSAID/aspirin, or a biologic/chemotherapeutic, with IV access, continuous vitals monitoring, physical assessment between steps, escalation/stop decisions, and management of hypotension, urticaria or bronchospasm.

Bronchial provocation in a pulmonary function lab: baseline spirometry, coached inhalation of escalating methacholine/mannitol doses (or exercise/specific occupational allergen challenge), repeated coached FEV1 maneuvers with quality judgment, stopping at a 20% fall, and administering a bronchodilator with recovery spirometry.

Nasal provocation test in a specialty allergy/ENT or occupational clinic: baseline peak nasal inspiratory flow or rhinomanometry, instillation/spray of diluent then escalating allergen concentrations into the nostrils, timed symptom scoring (sneezing, secretion, itch, obstruction), and interpretation with rescue treatment available.

Conjunctival provocation test in clinic: escalating allergen dilutions dropped into the lower conjunctival sac of one eye with the contralateral eye as control, timed ocular symptom and sign grading (itch, redness, tearing, chemosis), rinsing/treatment on a positive response.

sources.developer: Munich Institute of Robotics and Machine Intelligence, Technical University of Munich (Haddadin group)
sources.title: Autonomous swab robot for naso- and oropharyngeal COVID-19 screening — Scientific Reports
sources.claim: An autonomous force-controlled robot station (SR-NOCS) inserted swabs into the nose and throat of patients in two clinical studies, showing robots can autonomously place an instrument on the nasal/oropharyngeal mucosa in a clinical setting; it does not dose allergens, score symptoms, or manage reactions.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: intranasal/oropharyngeal swab sampling. It transfers only for the delivery sub-step of a nasal challenge (approaching a patient's nasal mucosa with a device autonomously), not for graded allergen dosing, PNIF/rhinomanometry, symptom scoring, stop decisions, or treating a systemic reaction.

sources.title: Evaluation of skin prick location on the forearm using a novel skin prick automated test device (PMC)
sources.claim: The Skin Prick Automated Test (SPAT) device autonomously loads lancets, picks up allergen extracts and applies 10-12 simultaneous pricks to a patient's forearm in hospital allergy/ENT clinics, with AI readout of wheals — automation of allergy skin testing, not of provocation challenges.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: in vivo allergy skin testing. It shows automated allergen application to a cooperative patient in a clinic, but a skin prick is a fixed single-step, low-risk test; it does not involve escalating mucosal/oral dosing, physiologic monitoring between steps, stop rules, or anaphylaxis treatment required by provocation tests.

sources.title: Waterloo startup performs first ever robotic intramuscular injection | Waterloo News
sources.claim: A robot platform performed a needle-free intramuscular injection into a person, showing a robot can deliver a drug dose to a patient; the demonstration is a single injection, not a graded challenge protocol with monitoring and reaction management.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: administering a drug dose to a patient. It covers only the administration sub-step of a medication challenge; there is no evidence of escalating dose protocols, inter-dose clinical assessment, stop criteria, or treatment of an induced hypersensitivity reaction.

sources.system: Adaptive assistive feeding robot (sensor- and prediction-driven fork/arm)
sources.developer: Academic research group (JMIR Formative Research 2026 report)
sources.title: Assistive feeding robot with predictive algorithms (JMIR Formative Research)
sources.claim: Assistive feeding robots autonomously acquire food and deliver bites to a person's mouth using facial landmark and mouth-state sensing, demonstrating robotic delivery of food portions to a human, in laboratory/rehabilitation demonstrations only.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robot-assisted feeding. It transfers only to physically presenting a measured food portion to a patient's mouth; it does not weigh/blind graded allergen doses, monitor for objective allergic signs, decide escalation or termination, or treat anaphylaxis.

roles.title: Hospitalists
aliases: DO Physician (Doctor of Osteopathic Medicine Physician)
Neonatal Intensive Care Unit Hospitalist (Neonatal ICU Hospitalist)
roles.description: Provide inpatient care predominantly in settings such as medical wards, acute care units, intensive care units, rehabilitation centers, or emergency rooms. Manage and coordinate patient care throughout treatment.

tasks.label: Diagnose, treat, or provide continuous care to hospital inpatients.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Daily rounding on a stable general medical/surgical ward inpatient: review overnight events, labs and imaging, go to the bedside for a focused history and physical exam (auscultation, abdominal palpation, wound/line inspection, edema check), adjust the medication and diagnostic plan, write orders and a progress note, and coordinate with nursing and consultants. Patient may be frail, confused, hard-of-hearing, or attached to lines, drains, and telemetry.

Admission of a new inpatient from the ED or direct admit: complete history and physical exam on an undifferentiated, often acutely ill patient, formulate a differential diagnosis, order the initial workup and treatment (fluids, antibiotics, anticoagulation, oxygen), and set goals of care with the patient/family. Time-pressured, information incomplete, patient may be unable to give a history.

Continuous management of a high-acuity ICU/step-down patient: repeated bedside reassessments through the day, interpretation of ventilator and hemodynamic data, titration of vasopressors and sedation, hands-on exam of a sedated or intubated patient, and moment-to-moment adjustment of therapy with the bedside nurse and RT.

Response to acute deterioration on the ward (rapid response or code): rapid bedside evaluation of a hypotensive, hypoxic, or unresponsive patient, immediate hands-on interventions (airway positioning and bag-mask support, checking pulses, applying pads), directing the resuscitation team, and disposition to a higher level of care.

Bedside diagnostic/therapeutic procedures performed by the hospitalist on the inpatient unit: ultrasound-guided paracentesis or thoracentesis, lumbar puncture, arterial blood gas, central or arterial line placement, incision and drainage, or wound care, including consent, sterile setup, the procedure itself on a possibly uncooperative patient, and post-procedure assessment.

sources.title: Performance, Safety, and Patient Experience of an Autonomous Robotic Phlebotomy Device: A Multicenter Trial | Clinical Chemistry
sources.claim: Vitestro's Aletta autonomous robotic phlebotomy device drew blood from patients in a multicenter clinical trial with a 94.5% first-stick success rate and low adverse-event rates, i.e. a single narrow diagnostic sub-step performed autonomously in a clinical facility.
sources.transferJustification: Related task = venipuncture for lab testing, one input to inpatient diagnosis. It does NOT transfer to this task: the robot performs a single fixtured arm puncture on a cooperating, seated patient and makes no diagnostic or treatment decision, whereas the hospitalist instance requires history-taking, multi-system physical examination, clinical reasoning, and ordering/adjusting therapy.

sources.title: Swisslog Healthcare Partners with Diligent Robotics to Enhance Hospital Logistics
sources.claim: The most widely deployed autonomous hospital robot fleet (Moxi) performs materials logistics — supply, lab specimen and pharmacy deliveries through hospital corridors — and does not assess, diagnose or treat patients.
sources.transferJustification: Related task = intra-hospital delivery. Establishes that autonomous mobile manipulators can work reliably in the E2 hospital-ward environment, but the payload-transport skill does not transfer to bedside examination, clinical judgment, or treatment of an inpatient.

sources.title: Telemedicine Robots Motorize Medicine – Continuum
sources.claim: Hospital telepresence robots such as InTouch Health's RP-VITA navigate autonomously but the clinical encounter itself is conducted by a remote human physician driving the robot and speaking through it; the robot performs no diagnosis or treatment on its own.
sources.transferJustification: Related task = remote physician consultation at the bedside. It cannot substantiate completion because the medical work is done by a teleoperating human clinician; only navigation is autonomous, and no hands-on examination or treatment is delivered by the machine.

sources.system: Fully autonomous robotic ultrasound system for thyroid scanning
sources.title: A fully autonomous robotic ultrasound system for thyroid scanning | Nature Communications
sources.claim: A fully autonomous robotic ultrasound ... has been demonstrated for thyroid scanning and nodule assessment, showing autonomy is limited to a single, narrow, pre-specified imaging exam rather than general patient assessment and management.
sources.transferJustification: Related task = point-of-care diagnostic imaging of one organ. It does not transfer: the system scans a single specified region on a still, cooperative subject and outputs an image/classification, while the hospitalist instances require whole-patient assessment, procedural intervention, and continuous management decisions.

tasks.label: Admit patients for hospital stays.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: ED-to-floor admission of a medically stable adult (e.g., pneumonia, cellulitis, CHF exacerbation): hospitalist is paged by the ED, reviews EHR/labs/imaging, goes to the ED bay or ward room, takes a history, performs a hands-on physical exam (auscultation, abdominal palpation, edema/skin check), reconciles medications, decides admission and level of care, enters admission orders and writes the H&P.

Complex, acutely ill or elderly multimorbid admission (delirium, sepsis, GI bleed, possible ICU triage): careful serial exam of a confused or uncooperative patient, collateral history from family/EMS/nursing home, goals-of-care and code-status discussion, level-of-care decision, extensive med reconciliation and admission orders.

Direct admission from a clinic or transfer accepted from an outside hospital: phone/EHR triage of the referring clinician's request, bed and service assignment, then bedside evaluation on the unit at arrival, exam, orders and H&P, often with incomplete outside records.

Overnight nocturnist admission under high volume: several admissions in rapid succession, abbreviated but real bedside history and exam, rapid order entry, brief documentation, and morning handoff to the day team.

Observation-status admission from the ED (chest pain rule-out, syncope, low-risk GI complaint): status determination against payer/utilization criteria, focused exam, protocol order set, and short-stay plan documentation.

sources.system: Robotic physical examination system with automated heart/lung auscultation
sources.title: Automated Heart and Lung Auscultation in Robotic Physical Examinations
sources.claim: A robotic arm system can autonomously position a stethoscope and capture heart and lung sounds on human subjects, but this is a single exam sub-step demonstrated on four subjects in a lab, not an admission encounter.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic auscultation, a component of the admission physical exam. It shows only one exam maneuver on cooperative lab subjects and cannot substantiate the full admission encounter, so it supports no positive judgment.

sources.system: Humanoid robot surrogates (Unitree-class humanoids) for clinical tasks
sources.developer: UC San Diego / UC Berkeley (Atar et al.)
sources.title: Humanoids in Hospitals: A Technical Study of Humanoid Robot Surrogates for Dexterous Medical Interventions
sources.claim: State-of-the-art humanoid robots performing direct clinical ... such as stethoscope placement, laryngoscopy and needle procedures in a hospital-workflow study operate under human teleoperation, not autonomously.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robot-performed bedside clinical procedures including physical examination maneuvers. Because control is teleoperated, it cannot support a positive judgment for autonomous admission exams.

sources.title: Serve Robotics to Acquire Diligent Robotics, Expanding Physical AI Platform Beyond the Sidewalk
sources.claim: The largest commercial autonomous mobile-manipulator deployment in US hospitals performs supply and pharmacy delivery, demonstrating autonomous operation in hospital corridors but no patient assessment, decision-making or order entry.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous hospital logistics. It establishes that robots can navigate E2 hospital settings autonomously, but the admission task's content (interview, hands-on exam, clinical judgment, orders) is entirely outside its demonstrated capability, so it supports no positive judgment.

sources.title: InTouch Health and iRobot Announce First Customers to Install RP-VITA, The New Face of Telemedicine
sources.claim: FDA-cleared hospital telemedicine robots navigate autonomously but exist to bring a remote human physician to the bedside; the clinical encounter itself is conducted by the physician, not by the machine.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robot-mediated acute-care patient consultation, the closest deployed analogue to a robot 'admitting' a patient. The clinical work is performed by a teleoperating physician, so it cannot support a positive judgment.

tasks.label: Attend inpatient consultations in areas of specialty.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Medical consult requested by a surgical or subspecialty service on an inpatient ward (e.g., perioperative risk assessment, management of comorbidities): hospitalist reviews the chart, goes to the bedside, takes a focused history, performs a physical exam (cardiopulmonary auscultation, abdominal palpation, extremity/edema and wound inspection), formulates an assessment and recommendations, writes the consult note, and calls back the requesting team.

Consultation/co-management evaluation in an ICU or step-down unit on a critically ill patient with ventilator, lines, drains and infusion pumps: bedside evaluation of an often sedated or unstable patient, integration of monitor and lab data, exam around equipment, recommendations discussed with intensivist and nursing staff.

Emergency department consult: hospitalist is called to an ED bay to evaluate a patient for admission, performs history and physical under time pressure in a noisy, crowded bay, decides on level of care and initial orders, and negotiates disposition with the emergency physician.

Hospitalist attends a bedside consultation with a specialty consultant (cardiology, infectious disease, nephrology, palliative care) or participates in multidisciplinary rounds: joint bedside examination and discussion, reconciling specialist recommendations with the overall plan, and communicating the plan to the patient and family.

Focused consult on a general medical/surgical ward for a specific problem (delirium, glycemic control, anticoagulation, goals of care, abnormal test result), including repeated brief bedside re-evaluations on subsequent days and updating recommendations as the patient's condition evolves.

sources.system: Unitree G1 humanoid with Inspire Hands Gen4 bimanual teleoperation system (UCSD 'Humanoids in Hospitals')
sources.developer: UC San Diego (Atar, Liang, Joyce, Richter, Yip et al.)
sources.title: Humanoids in Hospitals: A Technical Study of Humanoid Surrogates for Dexterous Medical Interventions
sources.claim: The most advanced attempt to put a humanoid robot into direct clinical tasks (auscultation, abdominal palpation, intubation, ultrasound-guided injection) was performed entirely by teleoperation on manikins and phantoms, with non-clinician operators, and the authors themselves state that autonomous functionality remains future work.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic performance of the physical-examination component of a clinical encounter (auscultation, palpation). It is the closest published attempt at the bedside-exam element of an inpatient consult; it is teleoperated, on simulators, and below clinician quality, so it cannot substantiate autonomous completion of a consult.

sources.title: Humanoids in Hospitals: A Technical Study of Humanoid Surrogates for Dexterous Medical Interventions
sources.claim: The same study reports that even teleoperated palpation and auscultation fell short of clinician-level examination quality, with sensor and dexterity limitations.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: bedside physical examination maneuvers, a required element of an inpatient consultation. Performance does not yet reach clinician quality even under teleoperation, so it cannot carry over to autonomous completion of the whole consult.

sources.developer: InTouch Health with iRobot (now Teladoc Health)
sources.title: Telepresence Robot Gives Patients Access to Remote Physicians
sources.claim: Hospital telepresence robots used for inpatient consults are remote-presence conduits: a human physician conducts the consultation through the robot, so the clinical work is performed by a person, not by the machine.
sources.transferJustification: Directly related: remote inpatient consultation. The robot only navigates autonomously; the consultation itself is continuously conducted by a remote human physician, which the rating rules treat as teleoperation and therefore cannot support a positive judgment.

sources.system: Fully autonomous robotic ultrasound system for thyroid scanning
sources.developer: South China University of Technology (Su, Liu, Ren et al.), published in Nature Communications
sources.title: A fully autonomous robotic ultrasound system for thyroid scanning - PubMed
sources.claim: The state of the art in autonomous robotic patient contact is a single narrow imaging exam: a robot arm that scans the thyroid region without human assistance. It performs one imaging sub-step, not history-taking, general physical examination, clinical reasoning, documentation, or communication with a care team.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous robot-patient physical contact for a diagnostic exam. It shows autonomy is limited to one scripted imaging modality on a cooperative, positioned subject, far short of a whole inpatient consultation.

sources.title: Swisslog Healthcare Partners with Diligent Robotics to Enhance Hospital Logistics
sources.claim: The largest deployed fleet of autonomous mobile manipulation robots in US hospitals performs logistics only — delivering medications, supplies and lab samples — and does not evaluate patients or render clinical assessments.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous robot operation inside hospital wards. It establishes that fielded hospital autonomy is confined to fetch-and-deliver logistics with no patient assessment, so it cannot substantiate performing a consultation.

roles.title: Urologists
aliases: DO Physician (Doctor of Osteopathic Medicine Physician)
roles.description: Diagnose, treat, and help prevent benign and malignant medical and surgical disorders of the genitourinary system and the renal glands.

tasks.label: Diagnose or treat diseases or disorders of genitourinary organs and tracts including erectile dysfunction (ED), infertility, incontinence, bladder cancer, prostate cancer, urethral stones, or premature ejaculation.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Outpatient clinic visit in a urology office: takes history, performs genital exam and digital rectal exam, reviews PSA/urinalysis/imaging, forms a diagnosis and starts medical management for ED, LUTS/BPH, overactive bladder or incontinence, male infertility, or premature ejaculation; documents and orders follow-up.

Office/clinic procedure room: flexible cystoscopy for hematuria or bladder-cancer surveillance, transrectal or transperineal ultrasound-guided prostate biopsy, urodynamics, in-office vasectomy, or catheter/ureteral stent exchange, on an awake patient under local anesthesia.

Hospital operating room: major oncologic or reconstructive surgery — robotic-assisted radical prostatectomy for prostate cancer, radical cystectomy with urinary diversion for bladder cancer, partial nephrectomy, or sling/artificial urinary sphincter placement for incontinence — including tissue dissection, hemostasis, anastomosis and intraoperative decision-making.

OR or ambulatory surgery center endoscopic case: ureteroscopy with laser lithotripsy or PCNL for urethral/ureteral/renal stones, shock wave lithotripsy, TURBT for bladder tumor, or endoscopic BPH resection/ablation, with stent placement and specimen handling.

Inpatient hospital consult and bedside procedure: evaluates obstructive uropathy, urosepsis, gross hematuria with clot retention or post-operative complications on the ward/ICU/ED; performs difficult catheterization, clot irrigation or drain management and directs treatment.

sources.system: FDA-cleared surgical robots (49 systems, incl. da Vinci, AquaBeam, Monarch)
sources.developer: Multiple (review by USC/Johns Hopkins authors, npj Digital Medicine)
sources.title: Levels of autonomy in FDA-cleared surgical robots: a systematic review | npj Digital Medicine
sources.claim: Systematic review of all FDA-cleared surgical robots (2015-2023) classifying autonomy: 86% require continuous surgeon control, the most advanced reach only conditional autonomy for surgeon-approved plans, and none reach high or full autonomy.
sources.transferJustification: Directly covers the robotic platforms used for urologic diagnosis and surgery (prostatectomy, cystectomy, stone surgery, prostate ablation); establishes that no cleared system performs a procedure without a surgeon generating and supervising the actions.

sources.title: Desai Sethi Urology Institute Offers Robotic Aquablation Therapy for BPH - InventUM
sources.claim: The AquaBeam Robotic System is the most autonomous FDA-cleared urologic device: after the surgeon maps the resection contour under ultrasound/cystoscopic guidance, the robot executes the waterjet tissue resection; used in hospitals and ASCs for BPH.
sources.transferJustification: Closest analogue to autonomous urologic treatment: it automates only the resection step of one procedure (BPH) after surgeon planning, anesthesia, scope insertion and hemostasis; it does not diagnose or carry an episode of care end to end.

sources.title: Robotic-Assisted Removal of Kidney Stones for First Patient using MONARCH Platform for Urology | Ethicon
sources.claim: Robotic ureteroscopy/PCNL platform cleared for urology is driven by the urologist with a handheld controller — robot-assisted navigation, not autonomous stone treatment; first human kidney-stone case reported October 2025.

sources.title: New Robotic Assisted Transperineal Needle-Guidance System for Prostate Biopsy and Cancer Ablations Received U.S FDA 510(k) Clearance
sources.claim: Robotic transperineal prostate biopsy system is a needle-guidance platform: the urologist plans trajectories and the robot positions needles; the physician remains in control of the procedure.

sources.system: SRT-H (Surgical Robot Transformer - Hierarchy) on da Vinci Research Kit
sources.title: SRT-H: A hierarchical framework for autonomous surgery via language-conditioned imitation learning - PubMed
sources.claim: State of the art in autonomous soft-tissue surgery: a hierarchical imitation-learning framework performed the gallbladder-removal steps fully autonomously, but only on ex vivo animal tissue in a laboratory setting.
sources.transferJustification: Cholecystectomy is a soft-tissue endoscopic procedure comparable in tissue handling to urologic surgery; it marks the ceiling of demonstrated surgical autonomy — ex vivo animal tissue in a lab, not live patients — so urologic operations are not substantiated.

sources.system: Fully autonomous robotic ultrasound system for thyroid scanning
sources.developer: Academic research group (published in Nature Communications / PubMed indexed)
sources.title: A fully autonomous robotic ultrasound system for thyroid scanning - PubMed
sources.claim: Fully autonomous robotic ultrasound scanning has been demonstrated for thyroid imaging on volunteers in a research setting, identifying nodules without human assistance.
sources.transferJustification: Nearest robotic analogue to an autonomous diagnostic exam; it is a surface imaging task on the neck in a lab demo and does not extend to genitourinary examination, invasive diagnosis, or treatment decisions.

tasks.label: Examine patients using equipment, such as radiograph (x-ray) machines or fluoroscopes, to determine the nature and extent of disorder or injury.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Office/clinic renal-bladder ultrasound: urologist places a curvilinear probe on a patient lying on the exam table, sweeps kidneys and bladder for hydronephrosis, stones, masses, bladder wall changes and post-void residual, and states the diagnostic finding in the note.

Office flexible cystoscopy under topical anesthesia: urologist instills lidocaine gel, passes a flexible cystoscope through the urethra, inspects urethra, prostate and full bladder mucosa for tumors, stones, strictures and bleeding sources, and records extent of disease.

Intraoperative fluoroscopy in the OR: urologist positions the C-arm over a patient in lithotomy, cannulates the ureteral orifice cystoscopically, injects contrast for a retrograde pyelogram, and uses live fluoroscopy to define obstruction/filling defects and guide wire/stent placement.

Fluoroscopy-suite study such as videourodynamics, voiding cystourethrogram or retrograde urethrogram: urologist catheterizes the patient, fills the bladder with contrast, images during filling and voiding, and interprets reflux, leak point, or stricture length.

Clinic scrotal/testicular ultrasound with Doppler or transrectal prostate ultrasound: urologist holds a linear or endocavity probe against/into a sensitive region, evaluates masses, varicocele, torsion or prostate volume/lesions, and reports findings.

Inpatient bedside or ED evaluation: urologist brings a portable ultrasound to a hospital bed (patient with drains, catheters, limited mobility, possibly obtunded) to assess hydronephrosis or bladder distension, often alongside a bedside plain-film (KUB) review, and determines urgency.

sources.system: Autonomous lightweight ultrasound robot for liver sonography (Tsinghua University / Beijing Tsinghua Changgung Hospital)
sources.developer: Tsinghua University School of Biomedical Engineering
sources.title: Beyond hospital reach: Autonomous lightweight ultrasound robot for liver sonography (arXiv:2510.08106)
sources.claim: A 588-gram cable-driven autonomous ultrasound robot with an AI agent autonomously acquires standard liver ultrasound planes and detects pathology in patients; it was first deployed in the ....
sources.transferJustification: Related task: transabdominal diagnostic ultrasound of upper-abdominal organs on a supine patient in a hospital imaging room. It transfers to the urologist's renal/bladder scan because the modality, probe-skin force control, body region (including the hepatorenal window over the right kidney) and clinical setting are the same, and the output is a pathology determination.

sources.developer: Chinese research group (published in Nature Communications)
sources.title: 3.16. A fully autonomous robotic ultrasound system for thyroid scanning — ESPE Yearbook of Paediatric Endocrinology 2024
sources.claim: FARUS, a UR3-mounted fully autonomous robotic ultrasound system, scanned thyroid regions of patients without human assistance and produced nodule detection/TI-RADS assessment; a 19-patient clinical study reported results comparable to manual scans by experienced clinicians.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous small-parts ultrasound examination with AI grading of lesions in patients. It shows that the acquisition-plus-interpretation loop of a diagnostic sonographic exam can be closed autonomously in a hospital exam room, which is the same loop a urologist performs when scanning kidney/bladder.

sources.system: Template Guided Optimal Pivoting autonomous robotic kidney ultrasound prototype
sources.developer: academic research group (paper indexed on ResearchGate)
sources.title: Towards Autonomous Robotic Kidney Ultrasound: Spatial-Efficient Volumetric Imaging via Template Guided Optimal Pivoting
sources.claim: Research toward autonomous robotic kidney ultrasound remains at prototype stage: in-vivo evaluation on two male ... reported kidney localization accuracy of about 7.4 mm, with performance studied largely in simulation.

sources.title: Mendaera Handheld Robotic System Receives FDA Clearance — Imaging Technology News
sources.claim: Mendaera's Focalist handheld robotic system received FDA 510(k) clearance for precise instrument placement during ..., with an initial launch focused on urology; it is a clinician-held needle-placement device, not an autonomous examining system.

sources.title: Twin Robotic X-ray scanner – Multitom Rax | Siemens Healthineers
sources.claim: The Multitom Rax twin robotic ..., installed in hospital radiography/fluoroscopy rooms, automatically positions and aligns its tube and detector arms, but acquisition protocol, patient positioning and interpretation remain with staff.

sources.title: Multicenter phase II study using the Avicenna Roboflex URS robot in robotic RIRS
sources.claim: The Avicenna Roboflex robot for flexible ureteroscopy consists of a surgeon's console ... holding the ureterorenoscope; all endoscope motion is commanded by the surgeon at the console.

tasks.label: Treat urologic disorders using alternatives to traditional surgery such as extracorporeal shock wave lithotripsy, laparoscopy, or laser techniques.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Ureteroscopy with holmium/thulium laser lithotripsy for a ureteral or renal stone: hospital OR or ambulatory surgery center, patient under general anesthesia in lithotomy position; cystoscopic access, guidewire and access sheath placement, navigation of a flexible/semirigid ureteroscope to the stone, laser dusting or fragmentation with basket retrieval, inspection for residual fragments and perforation, ureteral stent placement.

Extracorporeal shock wave lithotripsy for a renal or upper ureteral stone: hospital lithotripsy suite, ASC, or mobile lithotripsy trailer; patient sedated on the lithotripter table, stone localized by fluoroscopy and/or ultrasound, coupling and focal-point alignment, stepwise energy ramping over ~2000-3500 shocks with repeated retargeting for respiratory motion and patient shifting, intra-treatment fragmentation assessment and decision to stop or continue.

Minimally invasive/laser treatment of BPH (HoLEP or ThuLEP, GreenLight photoselective vaporization, Aquablation, Rezum) in a hospital OR: cystoscopic access under anesthesia, identification of adenoma and verumontanum, enucleation/vaporization/ablation of obstructing tissue, morcellation or evacuation of tissue, cautery hemostasis, catheter placement and irrigation.

Laparoscopic or robot-assisted laparoscopic operation (radical or partial nephrectomy, radical prostatectomy, pyeloplasty) in a hospital OR: insufflation and port placement, dissection through variable adhesions and fat, hilar/vascular control, tumor excision or reconstruction with suturing (anastomosis), hemostasis, specimen extraction and port-site closure.

Endoscopic laser/energy treatment of bladder or upper-tract urothelial tumors, urethral or ureteral strictures, and bladder-neck contractures, including office- or clinic-based cystoscopic laser procedures under local anesthesia in an awake, sometimes uncomfortable patient.

sources.title: Desai Sethi Urology Institute Offers Robotic Aquablation Therapy for BPH - InventUM
sources.claim: The AquaBeam Robotic System (Aquablation) is an FDA-cleared, commercially deployed surgical robot that automates the tissue-resection step of BPH surgery, executing a waterjet ablation along a contour the surgeon defines; it does not perform the surrounding procedure.
sources.transferJustification: Directly within the task: Aquablation is one of the non-traditional (non-TURP) urologic treatments urologists deliver.

sources.title: Step-by-step description of the Aquablation surgical treatment for benign prostatic hyperplasia
sources.claim: In Aquablation the surgeon inserts the handpiece, maps the resection contour on transrectal ultrasound, initiates the automated pass with a foot pedal, judges whether additional passes are needed, and then performs cautery for hemostasis; only the ablation pass itself is automatic.
sources.transferJustification: Directly within the task; documents the division of labour between surgeon and robot in the only automated urologic resection device in routine use.

sources.title: Robotic Flexible Ureteroscopy: Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Surgical Efficacy, Safety and Ergonomic Outcomes
sources.claim: Clinical robotic flexible ureteroscopy platforms used for laser lithotripsy are master-slave telemanipulators: the urologist drives scope deflection, rotation, laser firing and basketing from a console; no autonomous stone treatment is performed.

sources.title: Vinci System - an overview | ScienceDirect Topics
sources.claim: The da Vinci system, the dominant platform for robot-assisted laparoscopic urologic surgery, is a teleoperated telemanipulator in which the surgeon controls every instrument movement from a console; it has no autonomous operating capability.

sources.system: Robotically navigated lithotripsy system (robotic catheter + U-Net segmentation)
sources.developer: academic research group (Minim Invasive Ther Allied Technol 2025)
sources.title: Level I/II autonomy in robotically navigated lithotripsy: comprehensive system evaluation and performance assessment
sources.claim: Autonomy in ureteroscopic laser lithotripsy remains at research level: a robotic catheter with U-Net stone segmentation achieves only Level I/II autonomy (automatic targeting and navigation guidance) in system-evaluation experiments, not autonomous treatment of patients.
sources.transferJustification: Directly within the task (laser lithotripsy); establishes that autonomy in this procedure is preclinical and limited to targeting/navigation sub-steps.

sources.title: Doctors Let AI Control Surgery Robot and Perform Gallbladder Removal on Its Own
sources.claim: Even the most advanced autonomous surgical robot demonstrated to date operated on ex vivo animal tissue on a laboratory bench, performing steps of a gallbladder removal - not a urologic procedure on a live human patient.
sources.transferJustification: Related task (laparoscopic cholecystectomy) used to bound the frontier of surgical autonomy relevant to laparoscopic urologic surgery; it shows autonomy is at ex vivo, sub-procedure level.

sources.title: Supervised Endoscopic Tele-controlled Intelligent Lithotripsy
sources.claim: Efforts toward autonomy in endoscopic stone surgery are framed as supervised automation of repetitive sub-steps (navigation, laser approach, trajectory planning) under continuous surgeon supervision, and are at clinical-investigation stage.

tasks.label: Provide urology consultation to physicians or other health care professionals.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Inpatient hospital consult: a hospitalist, intensivist, or surgeon requests urologic input on an admitted patient (e.g., obstructive uropathy, hematuria, urinary retention, post-op urologic complication). The urologist reviews the chart, labs, and imaging, sees the patient, and delivers an opinion and management plan to the requesting team as a consult note and verbal discussion.

Curbside/phone or secure-message consult: a primary care physician, NP/PA, or ED physician calls or messages with a focused question (e.g., interpretation of a PSA trend, incidental renal cyst, catheter management, antibiotic choice for complicated UTI). The urologist gives verbal or written guidance and triage advice, with no patient encounter.

Formal electronic consultation (e-consult) within an EHR: the urologist reviews a referral question, records, labs, and imaging remotely and returns a documented written recommendation (workup, medication, or whether in-person referral is needed) to the referring clinician.

Multidisciplinary tumor board or case conference: the urologist reviews imaging and pathology for genitourinary cancer cases with oncologists, radiologists, and pathologists, and states the urologic surgical/management opinion that is recorded in the conference note.

Telemedicine or outreach consultation to clinicians at a rural clinic, nursing facility, or dialysis unit: video or phone discussion of a patient's genitourinary problem with the on-site clinician or nurse, resulting in a documented recommendation or transfer decision.

Peer-to-peer and educational consultation: advising residents, fellows, or referring physicians on protocols, guideline interpretation, perioperative urologic management, or reviewing a colleague's case for a second opinion, delivered in writing or conversation.

tasks.label: Treat lower urinary tract dysfunctions using equipment such as diathermy machines, catheters, cystoscopes, or radium emanation tubes.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Office/clinic procedure room: flexible cystoscopy in an awake patient with topical lidocaine to evaluate hematuria, LUTS or surveil bladder tumors, including minor therapeutic maneuvers (fulguration of a small lesion, stent removal, urethral dilation, bladder instillation) and patient counseling/consent, with real-time judgment about findings.

Hospital or ASC operating room, anesthetized male patient in lithotomy: endoscopic treatment of BPH/bladder outlet obstruction — monopolar or bipolar TURP (diathermy), holmium/GreenLight laser enucleation or vaporization, Aquablation, Rezum or UroLift — including scope insertion, resection/ablation, hemostasis, chip evacuation and catheter placement.

Operating room, anesthetized patient: transurethral resection of bladder tumor with electrocautery loop (or en-bloc resection), including mapping the bladder, resecting tumor with muscle in specimen, fulgurating the base, avoiding perforation near the dome/ureteric orifices, and placing an irrigating catheter.

Hospital ward, ED or clinic: management of acute urinary retention and difficult catheterization — coudé/filiform-follower or guidewire-assisted catheter placement after failed nursing attempts, cystoscopically-guided catheter insertion, or suprapubic tube placement in a patient with strictures, false passages or an enlarged prostate.

Clinic or OR: other lower-urinary-tract dysfunction treatments — urodynamics-directed therapy, cystoscopic intradetrusor onabotulinumtoxinA injection for overactive bladder, sacral neuromodulation lead placement, urethral stricture dilation/urethrotomy, cystolitholapaxy for bladder stones.

OR/brachytherapy suite: radiation-implant treatment of lower urinary tract malignancy (the modern analog of 'radium emanation tubes') — transperineal prostate seed/catheter implantation under transrectal ultrasound with cystoscopic verification, done jointly with radiation oncology under anesthesia.

sources.title: Procept wins FDA clearance for updated prostate surgery robot | MedTech Dive
sources.claim: The AquaBeam Robotic System is an FDA-cleared surgical robot used commercially in hundreds of US hospitals that resects prostate tissue with a waterjet to treat lower urinary tract ... from BPH; the robot executes only the resection step of a surgeon-run procedure.

sources.title: PROCEPT BioRobotics Announces FDA Clearance of the HYDROS Robotic System, the Next-Generation, AI-Powered Platform for Aquablation Therapy
sources.claim: In Aquablation, the human surgeon performs the cystoscopy/ultrasound setup and maps the treatment contour; the robot then executes that surgeon-defined plan under continuous surgeon monitoring, and the surgeon still handles hemostasis and catheterization — i.e., automation of one sub-step, not the whole procedure.

sources.title: A Novel Transurethral Robotic Platform for Performing En Bloc Resection of Bladder Tumour: Results from the First Phase of the VIABLE Trial
sources.claim: The Virtuoso Endoscopy System performed first-in-human transurethral en-bloc bladder tumor resections in six patients, but every instrument motion is remotely commanded by the surgeon at a console under constant surgeon control — continuous teleoperation, not autonomy.

sources.developer: Annual Review of Control, Robotics, and Autonomous Systems (academic survey)
sources.title: Autonomy in Surgical Robotics | Annual Reviews
sources.claim: Review of surgical robotics autonomy finds that essentially all commercial surgical platforms operate with no decision autonomy; autonomous execution of even single surgical tasks remains at the research level.

sources.system: Concentric tube robot with model-based resection planner and PushCVAE retraction network
sources.title: A Supervised Autonomous Resection and Retraction Framework for Transurethral Enucleation of the Prostatic Median Lobe
sources.claim: Research on supervised-autonomy transurethral enucleation of the prostatic median lobe with a concentric tube robot has been executed only on hydrogel prostate phantoms, not in patients, and covers only the resection/retraction sub-step.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: transurethral prostate enucleation, the same instrument path and tissue as TURP/HoLEP; shows the closest autonomous work is phantom-only, so it cannot substantiate completion in patients.

sources.system: Zamenix R robotic flexible ureteroscopy system
sources.title: Robotic flexible ureteroscopy system, Zamenix R, demonstrates efficacy and safety in initial clinical evaluation for retrograde intrarenal surgery
sources.claim: Robotic flexible ureteroscopy platforms entering clinical evaluation are master-slave systems in which the urologist drives the scope from a console; no autonomous endoscopic urological procedure is in clinical use.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: transurethral endoscopic instrumentation of the urinary tract; the same class of scope-driving robots is teleoperated, indicating no autonomous capability transfers to lower-tract treatment.
