tasks.label: Perform abdominal, pelvic, or retroperitoneal surgeries.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Robot-assisted laparoscopic radical prostatectomy (± bilateral pelvic lymph node dissection) in a hospital OR: urologist ports the abdomen, dissects the prostate off the bladder neck and rectum, spares neurovascular bundles, controls the dorsal venous complex, and hand-sews the vesicourethral anastomosis; console-driven da Vinci instruments, anesthetized patient, variable anatomy and bleeding.

Robot-assisted or laparoscopic partial/radical nephrectomy (transperitoneal or retroperitoneal approach) in a hospital OR: bowel mobilization, hilar dissection and clamping, tumor excision with negative margins under warm-ischemia time pressure, renorrhaphy/bolster placement, specimen extraction and closure.

Open major abdominal/retroperitoneal urologic surgery in a tertiary OR: e.g., open radical cystectomy with ileal conduit or neobladder diversion, retroperitoneal lymph node dissection for testis cancer, or open nephrectomy with caval thrombus; long case, bowel handling, great-vessel exposure, hemorrhage risk, multi-surgeon team.

Minimally invasive reconstructive abdominopelvic case: laparoscopic/robotic pyeloplasty, ureteral reimplantation or ureterolysis, buccal ureteroplasty, or sacrocolpopexy; fine suturing of small-caliber ureter/renal pelvis around stents, in a hospital OR or ambulatory surgery center.

Lower-complexity elective abdominopelvic procedures, often in an ASC or community hospital OR: laparoscopic varicocelectomy, diagnostic laparoscopy/orchiopexy for a nonpalpable intra-abdominal testis, bladder diverticulectomy, or placement of a device with an abdominal/retropubic component (artificial urinary sphincter reservoir, pubovaginal sling).

Urgent or emergency abdominopelvic exploration, often off-hours with an unfamiliar team: renal or bladder trauma exploration for ongoing hemorrhage, repair of iatrogenic ureteral/bladder injury discovered intraoperatively, drainage of an infected obstructed system or perinephric abscess in a septic, hemodynamically unstable patient.

sources.system: SRT-H (Surgical Robot Transformer-Hierarchy) on da Vinci Research Kit
sources.title: SRT-H: A hierarchical framework for autonomous surgery via language-conditioned imitation learning | Science Robotics
sources.claim: SRT-H, a language-conditioned imitation-learning framework running on a da Vinci Research Kit, autonomously executed a long phase of cholecystectomy (gallbladder dissection steps) on ex vivo pig gallbladders on a laboratory bench — step-level autonomy on a sub-portion of one abdominal operation, not a whole operation on a live patient.
sources.transferJustification: Cholecystectomy is an abdominal minimally invasive operation with tissue handling comparable to urologic laparoscopy, so it is the closest published autonomy result; it does not transfer to completing a urologic operation because only one dissection phase was automated, on excised pig tissue on a bench, not on a live patient from incision to closure.

sources.title: Da Vinci Code: First Autonomous Robot Surgery Achieved in Pig Cadavers | Inside Precision Medicine
sources.claim: Independent trade coverage of the same SRT-H result confirms the demonstration was on pig cadaver/ex vivo tissue, covered gallbladder removal steps, and ran slower than a human surgeon.
sources.transferJustification: Same transfer argument as the Science Robotics paper: an abdominal MIS procedure phase, but on cadaveric animal tissue, so it cannot substantiate completing a urologic abdominal/pelvic operation at worker quality.

sources.system: FDA-cleared surgical robots (LASR review; includes da Vinci, Hugo, Mako, Monarch)
sources.developer: multiple manufacturers; review by Icahn School of Medicine at Mount Sinai et al.
sources.title: Levels of autonomy in FDA-cleared surgical robots: a systematic review | npj Digital Medicine
sources.claim: A systematic review of all 49 FDA-cleared surgical robots (2015-2023) found none above conditional autonomy: 86% operate under continuous surgeon control, the most advanced reach Level 3, and no cleared system performs surgery with high or full autonomy.

sources.title: Da Vinci Surgical System - an overview | ScienceDirect Topics
sources.claim: The da Vinci system used for the majority of US urologic abdominal/pelvic operations is a teleoperated master-slave telemanipulator that does not move without the surgeon's immediate control.

sources.title: Robot performs laparoscopic surgery, suturing intestinal tissue - ASME
sources.claim: STAR performed supervised-autonomous laparoscopic intestinal anastomosis in live pigs in a research operating suite — a single suturing step with markers placed and the plan supervised by the research team, not an entire operation.
sources.transferJustification: Intestinal anastomosis is a suturing sub-step of abdominal surgery similar in tissue type and precision to ureteral or vesicourethral anastomosis in urology; it does not transfer to the whole task because only the anastomosis was automated, under human supervision with fluorescent markers, in an animal lab.

sources.title: Towards Fluorescence-Guided Autonomous Robotic Partial Nephrectomy on Novel Tissue-Mimicking Hydrogel Phantoms
sources.claim: Research toward autonomous robotic partial nephrectomy has so far automated only the initial tumor incision, on fluorescent tissue-mimicking hydrogel kidney phantoms, with roughly 1.4 mm incision accuracy.
sources.transferJustification: This is the target urologic operation itself, but only the first incision is automated and only on hydrogel phantoms, so it substantiates a bench sub-step rather than completion of the operation.

sources.title: Waterjet ablation offers minimally invasive option for BPH | Urology Times
sources.claim: The AquaBeam/HYDROS robotic system executes surgeon-mapped waterjet resection of prostate tissue autonomously, but only that resection pass: the urologist performs cystoscopy, builds the treatment contour on live TRUS imaging, and manages hemostasis and catheterization; the approach is transurethral, not an abdominal/pelvic operation.
sources.transferJustification: Closest deployed autonomous urologic tissue removal, but it is a transurethral endoscopic BPH treatment (a different O*NET task) that automates only a surgeon-planned ablation pass under continuous supervision; it does not transfer to performing an abdominal, pelvic, or retroperitoneal operation.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

tasks.label: Refer patients to specialists when condition exceeds experience, expertise, or scope of practice.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

tasks.label: Teach or train medical and clinical staff.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Didactic teaching for urology residents and medical students in a hospital or academic medical center: preparing and delivering lectures, grand rounds, journal club, morbidity-and-mortality conferences, and board-review sessions using slides, imaging, and case material.

Intraoperative teaching in the OR: talking a resident or fellow through steps of a TURP, ureteroscopy, or robotic prostatectomy — narrating anatomy, correcting technique verbally, giving feedback and debriefing afterward, with the trainee performing the operative steps.

Clinic and bedside precepting: reviewing a resident's, PA's, or NP's history, exam findings, imaging and labs on urology patients; explaining diagnostic reasoning and management plans; observing and critiquing office procedures such as cystoscopy or prostate biopsy.

In-service training for nurses, techs, and clinical staff: explaining catheter care and difficult-catheter protocols, urodynamics setup, cystoscope reprocessing, stent/drain management, and new device or EHR order-set rollouts, often as a short talk with a walk-through in the unit.

Skills-lab, simulation, or CME workshop instruction: leading trainees through a dry-lab/robotic simulator or cadaver/animal-model course, demonstrating a technique and coaching participants at stations, plus proctoring a colleague adopting a new procedure.

tasks.label: Perform brachytherapy, cryotherapy, high intensity focused ultrasound (HIFU), or photodynamic therapy to treat prostate or other cancers.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: LDR permanent-seed prostate brachytherapy: patient under general/spinal anesthesia in a hospital OR or ambulatory surgery center, dorsal lithotomy, TRUS probe on a stepper, transperineal template grid; urologist acquires volume study, contours with the physicist/radiation oncologist, inserts 20-30 needles through the perineum avoiding pubic arch/urethra/rectum, deposits 60-120 radioactive seeds with real-time dosimetric adaptation, then performs cystoscopy, fluoroscopy/seed count and Foley placement.

Focal or whole-gland HIFU ablation of prostate cancer (Sonablate, Focal One, or transurethral MR-guided ultrasound) in an OR, ASC or MRI suite; anesthetized patient, transrectal or transurethral applicator inserted and positioned by the urologist, MRI-ultrasound fusion contouring of the treatment volume, energy delivery with continuous monitoring for gland swelling, patient motion and rectal-wall safety, then catheter placement and recovery.

Prostate cryoablation (whole-gland, hemi-gland or focal) in an OR; anesthetized patient in lithotomy, TRUS guidance with a brachytherapy template, transperineal placement of multiple cryoprobes plus thermocouples, urethral warming catheter, two freeze-thaw cycles with real-time ice-ball monitoring and adjustment, then probe removal and suprapubic/urethral catheter.

HDR prostate brachytherapy implant: urologist places 15-20 transperineal catheters/needles under TRUS (or MR) guidance in an OR or brachytherapy suite, secures the template, confirms position by cystoscopy/imaging, manages the patient during transport and afterloader treatment, then removes the catheters after delivery. Includes boost and salvage cases.

Less common modalities and sites: photodynamic/vascular-targeted photodynamic therapy with transperineal fiber placement, PDT instillation and light delivery for bladder or upper-tract urothelial lesions via cystoscope/ureteroscope, and cryoablation of small renal masses or other GU tumors; performed in a hospital OR, cystoscopy suite or interventional imaging suite, often after prior treatment with distorted anatomy.

sources.title: Urologists perform first remote robot–assisted HIFU for prostate cancer
sources.claim: Focal One robotic HIFU is a commercially deployed prostate ablation platform, but the procedure is physician-driven: the first transcontinental case in 2025 was remotely operated by one urologist with a second urologist executing on site, i.e., teleoperation rather than autonomy.

sources.title: TULSA-PRO 2026 Coding and Billing Guide
sources.claim: TULSA-PRO delivers the ablation sub-step under autonomous closed-loop control: software reads real-time MR thermometry and automatically controls ultrasound frequency, power and applicator rotation to match a physician-prescribed boundary.
sources.transferJustification: TULSA is transurethral therapeutic-ultrasound ablation of prostate cancer, the same clinical purpose as the HIFU instance; it is the most automated energy-delivery system in this task family.

sources.title: TULSA Gives New Options for Intermediate-Risk Prostate Cancer | Johns Hopkins Medicine
sources.claim: Even with TULSA's closed-loop delivery, the urologic surgeon performs the physical procedure: inserting the urethral applicator and rectal cooling device, positioning the anesthetized patient in the MRI, and adjusting device placement under MR guidance.
sources.transferJustification: Same modality family as the HIFU instance; documents the human-performed portions that no system automates.

sources.title: Reliability of EUCLIDIAN: an autonomous robotic system for image-guided prostate brachytherapy - PubMed
sources.claim: EUCLIDIAN, described as an autonomous robotic system for automatic radioactive-seed placement, has only preclinical reliability evaluation published; no evidence was found of it completing patient implants at clinical standard.

sources.system: ROBiNSon robotic MR-guided HDR needle implant device
sources.title: Robotic MR-guided high dose rate brachytherapy needle implantation in the prostate (ROBiNSon)—a proof-of-concept study
sources.claim: The most advanced in-patient robotic brachytherapy work, ROBiNSon, treated five patients between 2019 and 2023 and only assessed feasibility for a single intraprostatic target ..., far short of a full multi-needle implant.

sources.title: New Robotic Assisted Transperineal Needle-Guidance System for Prostate Biopsy and Cancer Ablations Received U.S FDA 510(k) Clearance
sources.claim: The FDA-cleared iSR'obot Mona Lisa 2.0 is a needle-guidance robot: it lets the urologist plan and position needles for transperineal prostate procedures, with the physician retaining control of the intervention itself.
sources.transferJustification: Transperineal template needle placement under image guidance is the shared core motion of seed brachytherapy, HDR catheter implantation and cryoprobe placement; this is the closest commercially cleared robot to that work.

sources.title: Doctors Let AI Control Surgery Robot and Perform Gallbladder Removal on Its Own
sources.claim: The state of the art in autonomous soft-tissue surgery is SRT-H, which performed gallbladder removal steps on explanted pig tissue in a laboratory, not on live human patients.
sources.transferJustification: Cited as the ceiling for autonomous surgical manipulation on soft tissue; it shows autonomy has not left the ex-vivo laboratory, so it cannot transfer to autonomous intra-prostatic needle/probe work in patients.

roles.description: Diagnose and treat disorders requiring physiotherapy to provide physical, mental, and occupational rehabilitation.

tasks.label: Document examination results, treatment plans, and patients' outcomes.

tasks.label: Examine patients to assess mobility, strength, communication, or cognition.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Outpatient PM&R/musculoskeletal clinic, new patient with back, neck, shoulder or knee pain: physician inspects, palpates for tenderness and landmarks, measures active/passive range of motion, performs graded manual muscle testing (0-5) of multiple myotomes, provocative special tests, reflex hammer and sensory screen, and observes gait; findings synthesized into a documented exam note.

Inpatient rehabilitation unit bedside exam of a stroke, TBI, SCI or amputee patient: strength by manual muscle testing, tone/spasticity by passive stretch (Modified Ashworth), sensation, balance, bed mobility and transfer ability, plus screening of orientation, attention, memory and expressive/receptive language; patient may be weak, hemiplegic, aphasic or partly cooperative.

Acute-care hospital consult (ICU, med-surg, trauma floor): exam of a drowsy, painful or agitated patient around IV lines, drains, casts, catheters and a hospital bed; assess arousal and cognition, limb strength and movement, tone, and mobility/rehab potential with limited patient positioning.

Outpatient follow-up focused on tone and function before/after botulinum toxin, baclofen pump or bracing: goniometric range of motion at several joints, Modified Ashworth grading of multiple muscle groups, distinguishing dynamic spasticity from fixed contracture by palpation and repeated passive movement, plus functional/gait check.

Pediatric rehabilitation clinic exam of a child with cerebral palsy or spina bifida: tone, contractures, selective motor control, sitting/standing/gait, developmental level, and communication/cognition screening in a partly cooperative or distressed child with a parent present.

Rounds at a skilled nursing facility or long-term acute care hospital: exam of an elderly or medically complex patient in a bed or wheelchair in a cluttered resident room, assessing strength, joint range, transfer/ambulation ability, and cognition/communication with limited equipment.

sources.title: Exoskeleton Lab - Kinarm | Interactive Robotics Brain Injury Research
sources.claim: The Kinarm exoskeleton is a commercial robotic assessment platform in which a seated patient's arms are supported by a robot that applies loads and runs standardized protocols quantifying sensory, motor and cognitive function; it is sold as a research facility and covers only part of a clinical exam (no palpation, no strength grading of the whole body, no gait, no language exam) and requires clinicians to set the patient up and interpret results.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: instrumented robotic assessment of upper-limb sensorimotor and cognitive performance. It overlaps the physician's assessment of strength/mobility/cognition, but only for one seated, fixtured upper limb and only for reaching/proprioception/attention tasks, so it does not carry over to a whole physical examination.

sources.developer: Kinarm (BKIN Technologies) / University of Calgary researchers
sources.title: Exoskeleton robot helps researchers shed new light on learning and stroke recovery | University of Calgary
sources.claim: In Kinarm assessments the patient is fixtured into the robot — seated in a wheelchair-mounted exoskeleton interacting with a virtual display — i.e. the work is brought to a purpose-built machine rather than the machine going to the patient.
sources.transferJustification: Same related task as above (robotic sensorimotor/cognitive testing); cited here to establish the environment the system actually requires, not to substantiate completion of the physician exam.

sources.system: Pepper humanoid robot with RoboMate app
sources.developer: SoftBank Robotics / Italian clinical research group (Frontiers in Psychology)
sources.title: Humanoid robots for psychological assessment in mild cognitive impairment: from evaluation to the future of AI-driven data prediction systems
sources.claim: A 100-patient study had the Pepper humanoid administer the MMSE to mild cognitive impairment patients with scores comparable to a neuropsychologist, but the robot's speech and movements were driven through a remote-control app by the therapist with predefined animations and questions, and answers were displayed/managed on an operator tablet, so the demonstration is not autonomous.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robot-administered cognitive screening, which overlaps the 'cognition' element of this task. It cannot support a positive judgment because control was remote and script-triggered by a therapist.

sources.title: I Tried Aescape, the High-Tech Robot Massage—Here's My Review (Parade)
sources.claim: Aescape's autonomous robotic massage table performs force-controlled contact with a human body using 3D body scanning and dual robotic arms without a human therapist, and is commercially deployed at roughly 100 US gym, hotel and studio locations.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous, sensor-guided physical contact with a human body in a structured commercial facility. It shows safe contact and force control on a prone, cooperative body, but involves no limb manipulation against resistance, no palpation for diagnostic findings, no graded strength or tone testing, and no clinical interpretation, so it does not transfer to performing a physician's examination.

sources.title: Robot-Assisted Arm Assessments in Spinal Cord Injured Patients: A Consideration of Concept Study (PLOS ONE)
sources.claim: Robot-assisted arm assessment protocols still depend on a therapist: with the ARMin exoskeleton, passive range-of-motion measurement required the therapist to move the patient's free joint while the robot held the arm in a predefined posture.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic measurement of range of motion and strength in neurological patients, the closest robotic analogue to the physician's strength/mobility exam; cited to show that even in a fixtured rehabilitation-robot setting the clinician performs the manipulation.

sources.system: Humanoid robots in healthcare (general, incl. Moxi)
sources.title: Humanoid Robots in Healthcare: The Future is Here—But Are We Ready? | California Association of Healthcare Leaders
sources.claim: As of 2025, humanoid robots in hospitals were performing logistics and companionship roles rather than direct clinical tasks, with experts noting none had operated successfully in patient-care environments.
sources.transferJustification: General state-of-the-art context for hands-on clinical tasks in patient-care settings; supports negative judgments rather than any positive one.

tasks.label: Provide inpatient or outpatient medical management of neuromuscular disorders, musculoskeletal trauma, acute and chronic pain, deformity or amputation, cardiac or pulmonary disease, or other disabling conditions.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Daily rounds on an inpatient rehabilitation unit: physiatrist evaluates a patient recovering from stroke, TBI or spinal cord injury — reviews overnight events and vitals, performs bedside neuro/musculoskeletal exam (tone, strength, sensation, skin/pressure areas, lines and tubes), adjusts spasticity, pain, mood, bowel/bladder and anticoagulation medications, writes orders, sets therapy intensity, and documents/leads the interdisciplinary plan.

Outpatient clinic visit for acute or chronic musculoskeletal pain (e.g., low back or shoulder pain, post-trauma): history taking, focused musculoskeletal and neurologic examination with palpation and provocative maneuvers, review of imaging/EMG, non-opioid and opioid medication management, therapy prescription, work restrictions, and documentation in the EHR.

Outpatient follow-up of a neuromuscular or spinal cord injury patient: assessment of tone, contracture, ROM, seating/wheelchair and orthotic needs; management of spasticity (oral agents, intrathecal baclofen pump refill/dose changes), neurogenic bladder, autonomic dysreflexia risk, and pulmonary status.

Amputee/prosthetics clinic visit: inspect residual limb skin, wound healing and volume, assess socket fit and alignment, observe gait with the prosthesis, manage phantom and residual limb pain, write the prosthetic prescription and coordinate with the prosthetist.

Acute-care hospital consultation on a medical/surgical or ICU floor (polytrauma, cardiac or pulmonary disease, deconditioning): bedside evaluation amid monitors, drains and precautions, determination of rehabilitation candidacy and level of care, recommendations on pain control, mobilization and DVT prophylaxis, and a written consult note.

sources.title: How Diligent's Robots Are Making a Difference in Texas Hospitals - IEEE Spectrum
sources.claim: The most capable commercially deployed hospital robot performs autonomous fetch-and-deliver logistics (supplies, lab samples, medications) in hospital corridors and rooms; it performs no patient evaluation or clinical management.
sources.transferJustification: Related task = hospital material transport. Capability does not transfer to medical management: Moxi does not examine patients, form diagnoses, or write orders, so it cannot complete any instance of this task.

sources.developer: Technical University of Munich (Klinikum rechts der Isar / MIRMI)
sources.title: Toward telemedical diagnostics—clinical evaluation of a robotic examination system for emergency patients
sources.claim: Robotic patient examination that captures vital signs, auscultation, palpation and percussion exists only as a research examination cabin driven remotely by a physician, not as an autonomous clinician.
sources.transferJustification: Related task = remote physical examination. It shares the hands-on exam element of medical management, but the clinical decisions and the arm motions are supplied by a human physician in the loop, so it cannot substantiate autonomous completion.

sources.system: Autonomous robotic phlebotomy device (ADOPT trial, NCT05878483)
sources.title: Performance, Safety, and Patient Experience of an Autonomous Robotic Phlebotomy Device: A Multicenter Trial
sources.claim: Autonomous medical robotics in patient care is confined to single narrow procedures under protocol, such as venipuncture, evaluated in multicenter trials — far short of whole-visit medical management of disabling conditions.
sources.transferJustification: Related task = autonomous venipuncture on a fixtured arm. It shows autonomy is limited to one scripted procedure on a positioned limb; it provides no diagnostic reasoning, longitudinal management, or prescribing, so it does not transfer to physiatric medical management.

tasks.label: Diagnose or treat performance-related conditions, such as sports injuries or repetitive-motion injuries.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Outpatient PM&R/sports medicine clinic, new patient with an overuse or performance-related complaint (rotator cuff tendinopathy, lateral epicondylitis, patellofemoral pain, hamstring strain): take history, undress/position the limb, palpate for point tenderness, measure range of motion and strength, perform provocative special tests (Neer, Hawkins, Speed's, Finkelstein), inspect gait/mechanics, formulate a diagnosis, and set a treatment plan (activity modification, meds, therapy referral, imaging orders) documented in the EHR.

Outpatient clinic follow-up for a known repetitive-motion or sports injury: brief re-examination (tenderness, ROM, strength, functional testing), review of therapy progress and imaging, adjustment of the rehab prescription, bracing/orthotic decisions, return-to-play or return-to-work clearance.

Clinic procedure room: therapeutic/diagnostic injection for a performance-related condition — ultrasound-guided subacromial, intra-articular, tendon-sheath or trigger-point/dry-needling injection, or PRP — including target selection, patient positioning, sterile prep, probe handling with in-plane needle guidance, drug delivery, and post-procedure check.

Electrodiagnostic lab: EMG/nerve conduction study for a suspected repetitive-motion nerve entrapment (carpal tunnel, cubital tunnel, thoracic outlet), involving surface electrode placement, needle electrode insertion into selected muscles with real-time waveform interpretation, and a diagnostic report.

Sideline, field, or team training-room coverage: acute on-field evaluation of an athlete's injury (ankle sprain, shoulder subluxation, concussion screen, hamstring pull) amid crowds, weather, and time pressure, with immediate on-site decisions about removal from play, splinting/reduction, and disposition.

sources.title: Homepage - Vitestro
sources.claim: Vitestro's Aletta is a commercially deployed autonomous robotic phlebotomy device performing venipuncture on patients in hospital and laboratory blood-draw settings; it is the closest deployed example of an autonomous needle procedure on humans.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous needle insertion in a clinical facility. Cited to bound the frontier for the injection instance. It does not transfer: the arm is fixtured in a device-specific cradle and the target is a superficial forearm vein selected by vessel imaging, whereas a physiatrist's injection requires diagnosing the pathology, choosing a deep musculoskeletal target (bursa, joint, tendon sheath) under freehand ultrasound, and varying patient positioning.

sources.developer: South China University of Technology et al.
sources.title: A fully autonomous robotic ultrasound system for thyroid scanning (Nature Communications)
sources.claim: A fully autonomous robotic ultrasound ... scanned the thyroid of human participants without human assistance and produced images approaching clinician quality; it is a research system covering only image acquisition of one anatomic region.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous diagnostic imaging acquisition on a human. Cited to bound the frontier for the diagnostic-exam and injection instances. It does not transfer to whole-encounter musculoskeletal diagnosis: it acquires images of a single fixed anatomic region on a cooperative supine subject, and performs no history, provocative physical testing, treatment, or clinical disposition.

sources.system: Unitree G1 humanoid with Inspire hands (medical surrogate study)
sources.developer: UCSD Advanced Robotics and Controls Lab
sources.title: Humanoids in Hospitals: A Technical Study of Humanoid Surrogates for Dexterous Medical Interventions
sources.claim: The only study placing humanoid robots into direct clinical tasks including physical examinations and precision needle tasks relied entirely on bi-manual teleoperation, and reported force-output and sensor-accuracy limitations.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robot-performed physical examination maneuvers (palpation, auscultation, ultrasound-guided tasks) on patients/manikins. Cited as the closest attempt at the hands-on examination instances; because it is teleoperated it cannot support a positive judgment.

sources.title: Autonomous Spinal Robotic System for Transforaminal Lumbar Epidural Injections: A Proof of Concept of Study
sources.claim: Autonomous robotic placement of a therapeutic spinal injection has been demonstrated only in a phantom proof-of-concept study, not on patients.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous image-guided therapeutic injection. Directly comparable in modality to the physiatrist injection instance, but it is a phantom study with the target pre-specified, so it does not substantiate completion of a clinic injection encounter on a patient at worker quality.

sources.title: Product focus - AI and robot massage | spabusiness.com
sources.claim: Aescape's autonomous robotic massage table is commercially deployed in gyms, spas and wellness centers and delivers targeted bodywork without a therapist present; it performs no diagnosis and no medically directed treatment.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous hands-on soft-tissue manipulation of a human body in a commercial facility. Cited to bound the frontier of robot 'treatment' of muscle complaints; it does not transfer because the physician instance requires diagnosis, medical judgment and a documented treatment plan, none of which the massage system performs.

tasks.label: Perform electrodiagnosis, including electromyography, nerve conduction studies, or somatosensory evoked potentials of neuromuscular disorders or damage.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Outpatient EMG/NCS laboratory in a PM&R clinic: cooperative adult with suspected carpal tunnel or ulnar neuropathy. Physician measures and marks stimulation sites, applies surface recording/ground electrodes, delivers supramaximal percutaneous stimulation with a handheld stimulator, adjusts position for optimal responses, then performs needle EMG of selected hand/forearm muscles - inserting a monopolar/concentric needle, sampling multiple sites and depths, judging insertional and spontaneous activity by sound and waveform, and grading motor unit morphology and recruitment while coaching graded voluntary contraction. Protocol is modified in real time as findings emerge.

Outpatient lab: suspected cervical or lumbosacral radiculopathy. Limb NCS plus needle exam of limb and paraspinal muscles, requiring repositioning the patient (prone, side-lying), palpating landmarks, deep needle placement near the spine, and correlating myotomal findings to localize the root level; study extended or truncated based on interim findings and patient tolerance.

Outpatient lab: complex or extensive study - polyneuropathy, suspected motor neuron disease, myopathy, or neuromuscular junction disorder with repetitive nerve stimulation and possibly single-fiber technique. Multi-limb, multi-muscle sampling over 60+ minutes, limb warming and temperature control, and continuous on-the-fly redesign of the study to answer the diagnostic question.

Inpatient bedside study on a hospital ward or ICU: obtunded, edematous, or critically ill patient with lines, dressings, contractures, and limited access; portable machine, electrical interference from surrounding equipment, limited voluntary activation so the physician relies on insertional/spontaneous activity and stimulated responses.

Difficult or special-population outpatient study: young child, patient with spasticity/dystonia or tremor, morbid obesity requiring deep or ultrasound-guided needle placement, or anticoagulated patient requiring muscle selection to minimize bleeding risk; heavy verbal reassurance, pacing, and abbreviated protocols.

Evoked potential study: somatosensory evoked potentials for spinal cord injury, myelopathy, or demyelinating disease - scalp/spine/peripheral electrode montage per 10-20 landmarks measured on the patient, repetitive peripheral stimulation, averaging with artifact rejection, and identification of cortical/subcortical peaks; occasionally performed as intraoperative monitoring in an OR.

sources.system: Needle EMG exam robotic simulator (needle-tip localization by electric field potential and camera hybridization)
sources.developer: Academic research group (peer-reviewed biomedical robotics publication)
sources.title: Three-dimensional needle-tip localization by electric field potential and camera hybridization for needle electromyography exam robotic simulator
sources.claim: Robotics applied to needle electromyography exists only as a training simulator: a robotic phantom that localizes the needle tip to teach or assess needle EMG technique. No system inserts EMG needles into patients or interprets the exam.
sources.transferJustification: Directly about needle EMG, but the robot is a simulator/phantom used for training, not a system that performs an electrodiagnostic study on a patient; it therefore cannot support completion of any instance.

sources.title: Comparison of Automated versus Traditional Nerve Conduction Study Methods for Median Nerve Testing in a General Worker Population
sources.claim: Automated nerve conduction testing exists as handheld, human-applied devices with pre-configured biosensors; a person still measures landmarks, places the biosensor array and applies stimulation. No robotic manipulator is involved.
sources.transferJustification: Same task domain (nerve conduction studies), but the device is a hand-applied instrument rather than a physically embodied machine acting under machine control; all physical placement and stimulation is done by a human, so it cannot substantiate robotic completion.

sources.title: TMS-Robot - Transcranial magnetic stimulator by Axilum Robotics | MedicalExpo
sources.claim: The nearest robotic capability for placing a stimulator against a patient's body: a commercial robot that autonomously positions and maintains a TMS coil on the head under neuronavigation, compensating for patient motion, in clinic and research settings.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: placing a stimulation coil on a patient in a clinic. It shows contact positioning of a non-invasive head coil to a navigated target, but not electrode montage layout, percutaneous supramaximal nerve stimulation, intramuscular needle sampling, or real-time waveform interpretation and study redesign, so it does not transfer to electrodiagnosis.

sources.system: Autonomous lightweight ultrasound robot for liver sonography
sources.developer: Tsinghua University / Beijing Tsinghua Changgung Hospital collaboration
sources.title: Beyond hospital reach: Autonomous lightweight ultrasound robot for liver sonography
sources.claim: Autonomous robotic ultrasound scanning has been deployed in a hospital ultrasound department for organ localization and image acquisition on human subjects, demonstrating force-controlled autonomous probe contact with patients.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous force-controlled contact scanning of a patient's body surface in a clinical facility. It substantiates surface probe placement only; it involves no needle insertion into muscle, no nerve stimulation, and no electrophysiologic interpretation, so it cannot substantiate completion of an electrodiagnostic study.

tasks.label: Prescribe therapy services, such as electrotherapy, ultrasonography, heat or cold therapy, hydrotherapy, debridement, short-wave or microwave diathermy, and infrared or ultraviolet radiation, to enhance rehabilitation.

tasks.label: Instruct interns and residents in the diagnosis and treatment of temporary or permanent physically disabling conditions.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Bedside/clinic teaching rounds on a hospital rehabilitation unit: the physiatrist walks residents through a patient's case, explains the differential for a disabling condition (e.g., incomplete spinal cord injury, post-stroke hemiparesis), questions the resident on exam findings and prognosis, and gives verbal feedback and correction on their reasoning.

Supervising and critiquing a resident's independent workup in outpatient PM&R clinic or on consult service: the resident presents the history, exam, and proposed rehab/treatment plan; the attending probes reasoning, corrects the plan, co-signs documentation, and explains the rationale for changes.

Didactic instruction — lectures, journal club, case conferences, board-review sessions, and grand rounds on diagnosis and management of disabling conditions (amputation, TBI, musculoskeletal and neuromuscular disease), delivered in a conference room or by videoconference.

Procedural and exam-skills teaching: narrating and coaching a resident through a musculoskeletal exam, EMG/nerve conduction study, ultrasound-guided injection, or spasticity botulinum toxin injection — the attending explains anatomy, technique, and indications while the trainee performs the act.

Written and administrative instruction: composing formative and summative evaluations, milestone assessments, individualized learning plans, teaching-file cases, and remediation guidance for interns and residents.

tasks.label: Conduct physical tests, such as functional capacity evaluations, to determine injured workers' capabilities to perform the physical demands of their jobs.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Outpatient clinic exam room, workers' comp follow-up: physiatrist performs a hands-on regional physical exam on the injured worker — goniometric range of motion, manual muscle testing with graded resisted maneuvers, palpation, provocative maneuvers (straight-leg raise, impingement tests), plus observed gait, sit-to-stand and a light lift/carry — then assigns specific work restrictions (lifting limits, positional tolerances). Patient is often guarded, painful, and may under-perform.

Formal multi-hour functional capacity evaluation in a rehab clinic FCE lab / work-hardening gym: standardized battery of floor-to-waist and waist-to-shoulder lifts with weighted crates, carries, push/pull sled, grip and pinch dynamometry, sustained positional tolerances, stair/treadmill ambulation, with continuous observation of body mechanics, heart-rate response, pain behavior and effort-validity checks; physiatrist administers or directly supervises and matches results to the written job demands.

Independent medical exam / impairment rating for a workers' comp claim in an IME office: measured goniometry, grip and pinch strength (rapid-exchange testing), sensory and reflex testing, limb circumference, plus observed functional maneuvers, with explicit judgment about consistency of effort and symptom magnification, then a rating and capability opinion written for insurer/employer.

Exercise tolerance testing for work capacity in a hospital exercise lab: skin prep and electrode/BP cuff placement, graded treadmill or cycle-ergometer protocol, continuous monitoring for ischemia, dyspnea, arrhythmia and gait instability, physician decision to terminate the test, then estimation of achievable METs versus the aerobic demands of the worker's job.

On-site job-specific functional testing at the employer's location or an actual work site (warehouse dock, factory floor, construction site, utility yard): worker is observed and tested performing real job duties with real tools, ladders, carts and uneven or cluttered ground, in varying weather and traffic, to judge fitness for that specific job.

sources.title: Evaluation of finger strength and spasticity in hemiplegic patients using hand-finger robotic device: A validity and reliability study
sources.claim: The Amadeo hand-finger robotic rehabilitation system (Tyromotion) is a commercially deployed clinic device whose actuated fingertip sliders move and resist the patient's fingers under machine control to measure finger strength and spasticity; validated against Jamar dynamometry and Modified Ashworth in 161 subjects. It measures one fixtured body segment after a clinician positions the hand.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic measurement of hand strength and passive resistance, which is one measurement component of a physical capability exam. Transfer is limited: the robot acts only on a single hand fixtured in the device, does not position or handle the patient, does not test lifting/carrying or whole-body tolerances, and does not judge effort validity or job-demand match.

sources.title: Statistical measures of motor, sensory and cognitive performance across repeated robot-based testing
sources.claim: Kinarm is a commercially available robotic exoskeleton/end-point assessment system used in hospitals and research labs that runs standardized robotic tasks to quantify sensory, motor and cognitive arm performance in patients, once the patient is seated and set up by staff.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robot-administered quantitative assessment of upper-limb sensorimotor function in a clinic. It substantiates that a robot can run a fixed assessment protocol on a seated patient, but the measured constructs are neurological impairment metrics, not material-handling capacity, effort validity, or job-demand tolerance, and setup and safety remain with staff.

sources.date: 2019 (guidance page; device in clinical use since the 1990s)
sources.title: 9.6.1 Tools used to conduct Functional Capacity Evaluations — Australian Government DVA CLIK
sources.claim: The ERGOS Work Simulator is a commercial computer-controlled, multi-station work-simulation machine used as a component of functional capacity assessment; it presents standardized simulated work tasks and records performance, but is administered and observed by a trained evaluator and covers only part of an FCE.
sources.transferJustification: Directly related: instrumented work simulation is the machine-side of an FCE. It does not substantiate autonomous completion, because the machine measures while a clinician instructs, positions, spots, observes body mechanics and effort, and interprets the results.

sources.title: Functional Capacity Evaluation — ARCON online demo/training
sources.claim: The ARCON FCE system is a commercial 'automated' functional capacity evaluation product, but it is computerized measurement hardware (isometric/dynamic strength stations, ROM, dexterity, endurance instrumentation) plus sequencing software with no manipulator that handles the patient; a human evaluator conducts the evaluation.
sources.transferJustification: Directly related: this is the leading 'automated' FCE product. It is instrumentation and software rather than an embodied machine acting on the patient, so it cannot substantiate robotic completion of the instance.

sources.title: Intelligent Robotics Incorporating Machine Learning Algorithms for Improving Functional Capacity Evaluation and Occupational Rehabilitation
sources.claim: A peer-reviewed occupational rehabilitation paper proposing intelligent robotics for FCE states that no single streamlined robotic system currently simulates the range of standard work tasks needed for functional capacity evaluation; robotic FCE is presented as a future direction.
sources.transferJustification: Directly on-task: it characterises the state of the art for robotic functional capacity evaluation as not yet existing in integrated form.

sources.title: Innovations in Upper Limb Rehabilitation Robots: A Review of Mechanisms, Optimization, and Clinical Applications
sources.claim: A 2025 review of upper-limb rehabilitation robots frames autonomous robotic performance of functional assessment as a prospective capability dependent on future learning from large clinical datasets, rather than a current one.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robot-administered functional assessment in rehabilitation. The review's forward-looking framing indicates autonomous robotic functional assessment is not an established capability as of 2025-2026.

Sports Medicine Medical Doctor (Sports Medicine MD)
roles.description: Diagnose, treat, and help prevent injuries that occur during sporting events, athletic training, and physical activities.

tasks.label: Diagnose or treat disorders of the musculoskeletal system.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Outpatient sports medicine clinic visit for knee, shoulder, hip or back pain: physician takes history, then performs a hands-on musculoskeletal exam (inspection, palpation for point tenderness, passive/active range of motion, strength testing, provocative tests such as Lachman, McMurray, Neer/Hawkins), synthesizes findings into a working diagnosis and treatment plan. Exam room, cooperative but painful patient, variable body habitus.

Diagnostic confirmation in clinic: point-of-care musculoskeletal ultrasound performed by the physician (probe on the limb, dynamic scanning of tendon/ligament/effusion, comparison with contralateral side) and/or interpretation of ordered radiographs/MRI, then rendering the diagnosis to the patient.

Therapeutic office procedure in clinic procedure room: joint, bursal or tendon-sheath corticosteroid injection, joint aspiration, trigger-point injection, or ultrasound-guided PRP/needle tenotomy — includes patient positioning, landmark or ultrasound targeting, sterile technique, needle placement into a small target near neurovascular structures, and post-procedure care.

Immobilization and manual treatment in clinic or athletic training room: applying a cast or splint, fitting a brace, closed reduction of a dislocated shoulder/finger/patella, joint mobilization or osteopathic manipulative treatment, with re-check of neurovascular status.

Event/sideline coverage: acute injury evaluation on the field or court during a game or practice — kneeling over an athlete in uniform and pads, on grass/turf in weather and crowd noise, performing a rapid focused exam, on-site splinting or reduction, and a return-to-play decision.

sources.system: Autonomous lightweight cable-driven ultrasound robot (Tsinghua / Beijing Tsinghua Changgung Hospital)
sources.title: Beyond hospital reach: Autonomous lightweight ultrasound robot for liver sonography
sources.claim: A 588-gram cable-driven autonomous ultrasound robot acquires standard liver imaging planes and flags pathology on real patients in a hospital ultrasound department — the most advanced autonomous patient-contact scanning demonstrated, yet limited to image acquisition of a single organ, not musculoskeletal diagnosis or treatment.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous diagnostic ultrasound on a human patient. It bears on the sports-medicine diagnostic instance because it involves controlled probe contact on a patient, but it covers only image acquisition of abdominal organs and does not include a hands-on musculoskeletal exam, differential diagnosis, or any treatment, so it cannot substantiate completion of a whole encounter.

sources.system: Fully autonomous robotic ultrasound system for thyroid scanning
sources.developer: Tsinghua University / South China University of Technology and collaborators
sources.title: A fully autonomous robotic ultrasound system for thyroid scanning
sources.claim: A research robotic ultrasound system scans the thyroid region of volunteers without human assistance and classifies nodules; it remains a laboratory system operating on a single, easily accessible anatomic region.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous sonographic screening of a body region. Transfer is limited: it performs a fixed scan protocol over a superficial neck region on a still volunteer, not the dynamic, multi-joint, pain-provoking examination and clinical reasoning a musculoskeletal diagnosis requires.

sources.developer: University of Twente Robotics and Mechatronics group
sources.title: ARUS - Automatic Robotic Ultrasound Scanning for Muscle Segmentation and Recognition
sources.claim: The closest musculoskeletal-specific robotic system, ARUS, automates ultrasound scanning of muscle and bone for 3D reconstruction, but it is a laboratory prototype performing operator-selected scanning trajectories, not a clinical diagnostic service.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated musculoskeletal ultrasound imaging. It shares the anatomy of interest but delivers only 3D muscle/bone reconstruction in a lab setting; it does not diagnose an injury, decide management, or perform any therapeutic procedure.

sources.title: AI-Powered Massages? Automated Massage Robots Already at Work
sources.claim: Autonomous robotic massage tables are commercially deployed in gym spas, showing that autonomous force-controlled contact with a human body is feasible in a structured facility — but the service is non-diagnostic wellness bodywork, not physician evaluation or treatment of a musculoskeletal disorder.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous manual soft-tissue work on a human. It does not transfer to physician manual treatment because it applies generic pressure to a supine client without diagnosing a disorder, avoiding injured tissue, mobilizing a joint, or reducing a dislocation.

sources.system: CT-guided robotic needle insertion system (prospective randomized trial)
sources.developer: clinical research group (multicenter trial reported in PMC)
sources.title: Comparison of robotic versus manual needle insertion for CT-guided intervention: prospective randomized trial
sources.claim: Robotic needle placement in medicine remains a physician-directed assistive technology evaluated for CT-guided punctures; the interventionalist plans and supervises the insertion rather than the robot autonomously performing an indicated injection.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: image-guided needle placement in a patient. It is the nearest analogue to a joint injection, but the robot only aligns/advances a needle along a physician-defined trajectory under supervision, so it cannot support an autonomous positive judgment for office injections.

tasks.label: Record athletes' medical histories, and perform physical examinations.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Clinic exam room visit for a new musculoskeletal complaint (knee, shoulder, ankle pain): physician takes/updates the history by interview, then performs a focused physical exam — inspection, palpation for tenderness/effusion, active and passive range of ..., manual strength and neurovascular testing, and provocative special tests (Lachman, McMurray, Neer/Hawkins, ligament stress tests) — grading findings by feel and documenting them in the EHR.

Preparticipation physical evaluation (sports physical) for school or college athletes, often as a mass-screening station event in a gym or in clinic: review of the PPE history form with athlete/parent, height/weight/BP/vision, cardiac auscultation supine and standing with Valsalva, lung and abdominal exam, and a 90-second musculoskeletal screening exam, ending in a clearance decision and signed form.

Athletic training room visit at a team facility (college or professional) before or after practice: brief interval history from athlete and athletic trainer, targeted re-examination of an existing injury (swelling, ROM, strength, stability, gait), sometimes point-of-care ultrasound, and documentation of status and return-to-play progression.

Sideline or on-field evaluation of an injured athlete during competition or practice: rapid history of mechanism and symptoms amid crowd noise and weather, on-turf inspection and palpation, joint stability testing through pads or braces, concussion sideline assessment (SCAT), and a return-to-play or removal decision recorded afterward.

Comprehensive general medical history and physical for an athlete patient in clinic (annual/wellness exam, cardiovascular workup after an abnormal PPE finding, medical clearance after illness): full systems history, vitals, cardiac and pulmonary auscultation, abdominal and skin exam, neurologic screen, documented in the chart.

sources.system: Unitree G1 humanoid with bimanual teleoperation system
sources.developer: UC San Diego (Yip lab) with UC San Diego Health clinicians
sources.title: Humanoids in Hospitals: A Technical Study of Humanoid Robot Surrogates for Dexterous Medical Interventions
sources.claim: State-of-the-art humanoid robot performance of clinical physical-examination tasks (auscultation, abdominal palpation) plus procedures was achieved only through bimanual teleoperation by a human operator, not autonomously.
sources.transferJustification: Directly covers physical examination maneuvers (auscultation, palpation) on human subjects, the physical half of this task; it establishes that the frontier for whole-exam humanoid robots is teleoperation, not autonomy.

sources.system: ProteCT telemedical robotic examination cabin (Franka Emika arms)

sources.title: Toward telemedical diagnostics—clinical evaluation of a robotic examination system for emergency patients
sources.claim: A purpose-built 'robotic examination cabin' covering the modalities of an initial clinical examination was evaluated on real emergency patients, but the examination was conducted remotely by a physician operating the robot arms.
sources.transferJustification: Same task (physician physical examination of a patient) in a purpose-built examination cabin; a physician conducted the telemedical robotic examination during the study, so no autonomous whole-exam capability is demonstrated even at E1.

sources.system: auto-RUSS autonomous robotic ultrasound scanning system (7-DoF arm)
sources.developer: Sun Yat-sen University / Northwestern Polytechnical University
sources.title: Autonomous robotic ultrasound scanning system: a key to enhancing image analysis reproducibility and observer consistency in ultrasound imaging
sources.claim: Autonomous robotic contact examination of humans has been demonstrated only for a single instrumented modality: force-controlled ultrasound probe placement and scanning of a volunteer's thyroid in a research lab.
sources.transferJustification: Related sub-step of examination (imaging a body region with a hand-held probe on a cooperative subject); shows autonomy exists only for one instrumented modality, not for history-taking or manual musculoskeletal examination.

sources.system: Collaborative robotic platform for autonomous auscultation
sources.developer: Instituto Superior de Engenharia do Porto / INESC TEC
sources.title: Development of a Collaborative Robotic Platform for Autonomous Auscultation
sources.claim: Autonomous stethoscope placement on patients has been demonstrated by a collaborative robot arm that locates auscultation points by 3D vision and positions the stethoscope; it performs no other exam component and renders no clinical assessment.
sources.transferJustification: Auscultation is one component of the physical exam; the demo covers only probe placement on a prepared, seated subject and includes no history, palpation, range-of-motion, or special testing.

sources.title: A new knee arthrometer, the GNRB: experience in ACL complete and partial tears
sources.claim: A commercial motorized arthrometer performs an instrumented, automated Lachman test with the limb clamped in a rigid fixture, yielding a knee-laxity measurement — a single exam datum, not an examination.
sources.transferJustification: Automates one provocative test (anterior drawer/Lachman) with the leg fixtured — the E1-style version of a single sub-step of the musculoskeletal exam; it takes no history and examines no other joint or system.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Outpatient sports medicine clinic visit for a musculoskeletal complaint (knee, shoulder, ankle, back). Physician takes history, inspects, palpates for point tenderness/effusion, performs provocative and stability maneuvers (Lachman, McMurray, apprehension, impingement), tests strength and gait, forms a diagnosis, orders imaging, and prescribes bracing, rehab, or medication.

Sideline/on-field acute evaluation during a game or practice at a school, college, or pro athletic venue: assess a downed athlete on turf, screen for concussion (SCAT-style), palpate an injured joint, rule out fracture/dislocation, immobilize or reduce, and decide return-to-play, under time pressure, weather, and crowd noise.

Medical coverage of community events not controlled by an athletic institution: road races, youth tournaments in public parks, ski hills, trailheads. Evaluate heat illness, collapse, dehydration, sprains and abrasions in a tent or on the ground with portable equipment.

Athletic training room / team facility rounds: daily and follow-up examinations of in-season athletes, re-check of swelling and range of motion, hands-on soft-tissue and manual treatment, taping/bracing, and progression of the rehab plan with the athletic trainer.

In-office procedure on an injured athlete: landmark or ultrasound-guided joint/bursa injection or aspiration, casting/splinting of a fracture, or laceration repair, including the pre-procedure exam, consent, sterile technique, and post-procedure instructions.

Clinic evaluation of a non-orthopedic medical problem in an athlete (exercise-induced bronchoconstriction, palpitations, heat illness follow-up, GI or dermatologic issues): auscultation and vital signs, spirometry or exercise-challenge testing, diagnosis, and prescription of an inhaler or other therapy with technique instruction.

sources.system: Teleconcussion telemedicine robot (Mayo Clinic / Northern Arizona University sideline study)
sources.developer: Mayo Clinic (Bert Vargas et al.) with Northern Arizona University
sources.title: Feasibility and accuracy of teleconcussion for acute evaluation of suspected concussion | Neurology
sources.claim: Robot use for sideline athlete evaluation is a telepresence robot driven in real time by a remote neurologist, with an on-site provider still performing the hands-on face-to-face assessment; it is teleoperation, not autonomous examination.
sources.transferJustification: Directly on-task (sideline evaluation of injured athletes), but the robot is continuously teleoperated and cannot perform the hands-on examination, so it cannot support a positive judgment.

sources.system: Teleoperated humanoid robots for medical tasks (as surveyed in a humanoid endoscopic-assistant paper)
sources.developer: Multiple academic groups (cited in 'Humanoid Robots as First Assistants in Endoscopic Surgery')
sources.title: Humanoid Robots as First Assistants in Endoscopic Surgery (arXiv)
sources.claim: The state of the art for humanoid robots performing medical physical examinations is teleoperated demonstrations on mannequins, not autonomous examination of patients.
sources.transferJustification: Physical examination by humanoid robots is the closest analogue to the hands-on exam in this task; the demonstrations are teleoperated and on mannequins, so they do not substantiate autonomous completion.

sources.system: auto-RUSS (autonomous robotic ultrasound scanning system, 7-DOF arm with force control and visual servoing)
sources.developer: Lin, Li, Ruan et al. (academic group, published in Frontiers in Robotics and AI)
sources.title: Autonomous robotic ultrasound scanning system: a key to enhancing image analysis reproducibility and observer consistency in ultrasound imaging
sources.claim: Autonomous robotic ultrasound exists only as a research pipeline scanning healthy volunteers for image reproducibility; it acquires images and does not conduct a clinical examination, reach a diagnosis, or deliver treatment.
sources.transferJustification: Diagnostic imaging of a patient's body surface is a sub-step of the sports medicine exam; the system was validated only on healthy volunteers for image consistency, so it does not substantiate examining, evaluating and treating an injured athlete.

sources.title: Product focus - AI and robot massage | spabusiness.com
sources.claim: The only autonomous robot in routine commercial contact with athletes' bodies delivers preprogrammed table massage in gyms, spas and hotels; it performs no injury examination, diagnosis, or medical treatment.
sources.transferJustification: Soft-tissue treatment of athletes in a fitness facility is adjacent to the hands-on treatment portion of this task, but the system does not examine, evaluate, or diagnose an injury and cannot deliver the instance's accepted output.

sources.title: Robot performs first realistic surgery without human help | Hub (Johns Hopkins)
sources.claim: The frontier of autonomous medical manipulation is a laboratory surgical robot performing a single defined procedure on ex vivo animal tissue; nothing comparable performs an autonomous patient encounter.
sources.transferJustification: Autonomous physical intervention on human-like tissue is the most capable medical robot autonomy demonstrated; it is confined to one procedure on pig cadaver tissue in a lab, showing no system can autonomously examine, diagnose and treat a live athlete.

tasks.label: Examine and evaluate athletes prior to participation in sports activities to determine level of physical fitness or predisposition to injuries.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Mass station-based pre-participation physical evaluation (PPE) event for high school athletes held in a school gym or training room: physician reviews the athlete's history form, checks height/weight/BP/pulse and vision, auscultates the heart supine and standing/with Valsalva, palpates abdomen and pulses, runs the 14-step musculoskeletal screen (gait, duck walk, shoulder/knee ROM, symmetry), notes prior injuries, and signs the clearance form or refers.

Individual office-based sports physical in a sports medicine or primary care clinic: interview of athlete and parent, full head-to-toe exam including cardiac auscultation, palpation of joints, ligament stress tests (Lachman, apprehension), strength/flexibility assessment, discussion of prior concussion or injury, completion of state clearance paperwork.

Preseason physicals for a college or professional team, done in the team's athletic training facility over a day or two: detailed joint-by-joint orthopedic exam of previously injured athletes, laxity and special tests, functional movement/strength and balance testing, body composition, cardiac screening with ECG review, integration with imaging and injury history to set individualized injury-prevention plans and participation status.

Screening at an off-site event such as a tournament, combine, or community screening day held in a hotel ballroom, field tent, or gym with portable tables: abbreviated exam plus targeted evaluation of athletes flagged by history (murmur, prior ACL reconstruction, back pain), with on-the-spot clearance, restriction, or referral decisions under time pressure and crowd noise.

sources.system: Autonomous robotic auscultation platform (collaborative arm + 3D vision)
sources.developer: Academic research group (Applied Sciences / MDPI publication)
sources.title: Development of a Collaborative Robotic Platform for Autonomous Auscultation
sources.claim: A collaborative robot arm with 3D vision can locate auscultation points on a prepared patient and place a stethoscope autonomously; this is a laboratory research platform covering only one sub-step of a physical exam, not a complete clinical evaluation.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: cardiac/pulmonary auscultation, one component of the pre-participation exam. Cited to show the state of the art on the physical-contact portion of examination; it does not cover history-taking, musculoskeletal special testing, or the clearance decision that complete this task.

sources.developer: Academic research group (Frontiers in Robotics and AI)
sources.title: Autonomous robotic ultrasound scanning system: a key to enhancing image analysis reproducibility and observer consistency in ultrasound imaging
sources.claim: Autonomous robotic ultrasound scanning systems can acquire and measure images with force-controlled probe contact in study settings, showing machine-controlled contact examination of a positioned patient is feasible for a narrow imaging sub-step.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: diagnostic imaging of a body region. Comparable in that a machine contacts and scans a human body, but it addresses one imaging modality on a positioned, cooperative subject and does not perform the multi-system physical evaluation or the clearance judgment required here.

sources.title: The Reliability of the GNRB Knee Arthrometer in Measuring ACL Stiffness and Laxity: Implications for Clinical Use and Clinical Trial Design
sources.claim: A motorized knee arthrometer applies standardized loads and measures tibial translation, automating a single orthopedic laxity measurement that a physician would otherwise perform by hand; the limb must be positioned and strapped into the device by a clinician.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: anterior knee laxity testing (an orthopedic special test used in athlete screening). It shows machine automation of one instrumented measurement on a human-fixtured limb, but requires clinician setup and covers none of the remaining exam or the fitness/clearance determination.

tasks.label: Evaluate and manage chronic pain conditions.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: New outpatient clinic consultation for a chronic musculoskeletal pain condition (e.g., chronic patellofemoral pain, knee osteoarthritis, chronic low back pain, chronic tendinopathy): physician takes history, performs a hands-on regional exam (palpation for tender points, range-of-motion and strength testing, provocative special tests, gait observation), reviews prior imaging, forms a diagnosis, and sets a management plan (activity modification, PT referral, medications, bracing). Standard exam room in a clinic or hospital outpatient department.

In-office interventional procedure for a chronic pain condition: consent, positioning, sterile skin prep, diagnostic point-of-care ultrasound of the painful structure, then ultrasound- or landmark-guided corticosteroid/PRP joint or peritendinous injection, trigger-point injection, or dry needling; post-procedure assessment, dressing, aftercare instructions and documentation. Clinic procedure room.

Follow-up visit for ongoing chronic pain management: reassessment of pain and function, brief focused re-exam of the affected region, titration or change of analgesics (including controlled-substance monitoring, PDMP review, urine drug screening decisions), adjustment of the rehab program, referrals to pain medicine/behavioral health/surgery. Clinic exam room.

Evaluation and management of an athlete's chronic overuse pain in a team athletic training room or event medical suite: hands-on exam on a treatment table amid athletic trainers and staff, review of training load, decisions about return-to-play, taping/bracing, injection or medication, coordination with athletic training and PT staff. University or professional team facility.

Complex chronic pain patient (e.g., fibromyalgia, complex regional pain syndrome, persistent post-surgical or post-concussive pain) with central sensitization and psychosocial contributors: extended history, systematic multi-site tender-point and neurologic exam, coordination of a multidisciplinary plan, patient education and counseling on pacing and graded exposure. Clinic exam/consult room.

sources.title: Performance, Safety, and Patient Experience of an Autonomous Robotic Phlebotomy Device: A Multicenter Trial
sources.claim: An autonomous robotic phlebotomy device ... () performed venipuncture on patients in hospital outpatient phlebotomy departments with a 94.5% first-stick success rate and 0.6% mild adverse events - autonomous needle placement in a human in a clinical facility, but only the needle step, with no clinical evaluation, ultrasound targeting of a joint or tendon, or management decision.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous needle insertion into a patient inside a structured clinical facility. It is the closest deployed autonomous needle procedure, but it targets a superficial vein with the arm held in a dedicated fixture and performs no evaluation or management; it does not transfer to diagnosing a chronic pain condition or to placing an injection in a joint, bursa or tendon sheath under ultrasound.

sources.developer: Carleton University with collaborating hospitals (Su, Liu et al.)
sources.title: A fully autonomous robotic ultrasound system for thyroid scanning (Nature Communications)
sources.claim: FARUS, a fully autonomous robotic ultrasound ..., scanned the thyroid of human patients without human assistance and classified nodules, showing autonomous force-controlled probe contact with a patient's body in a hospital setting; it performs no musculoskeletal physical examination, injection, or pain-management decision.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous imaging contact with a patient's body surface, the imaging component of a sports-medicine pain workup. It shows a robot can safely apply a probe to a human and interpret images, but a chronic-pain encounter also requires history-taking, provocative manual testing and a treatment plan, none of which this system attempts.

sources.title: Equinox | The World's Most Advanced Massage
sources.claim: Aescape's fully automated robotic massage tables are commercially deployed in Equinox spas, delivering autonomous soft-tissue work on clients; the system delivers a preset recovery therapy rather than evaluating or managing a chronic pain diagnosis.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous force-controlled contact with a human body for musculoskeletal recovery in an institutional facility. It substantiates safe robot-human physical contact but not clinical evaluation, diagnosis, needle procedures, or medication management for chronic pain.

sources.title: Autonomous Robotic Tissue Palpation and Abnormalities Characterisation via Ergodic Exploration
sources.claim: Autonomous robotic palpation for tissue stiffness mapping and sub-tissue feature detection - the manual core of a musculoskeletal pain exam - remains laboratory research evaluated on soft-tissue phantoms and is framed as an assistive tool, not a clinical examination capability.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic palpation, the hands-on core of a chronic musculoskeletal pain examination. The evidence is phantom-level and explicitly assistive, so it does not substantiate completing a physician-quality exam anywhere.

tasks.label: Attend games and competitions to provide evaluation and treatment of activity-related injuries or medical conditions.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Sideline/on-field coverage of a high school or college football, soccer, or lacrosse game: physician runs onto the field to a downed athlete, performs on-field inspection, palpation, joint stability and neurovascular testing, sideline concussion screening (SCAT/symptom, balance, cognitive testing), applies ice/wrap/immobilization, and makes a return-to-play decision amid crowd noise, weather, and time pressure.

Professional or elite team game coverage: sideline evaluation under league protocols plus procedures in the venue's medical/training room during the game — laceration cleaning and suturing, reduction of a dislocated finger/shoulder, joint aspiration or injection, review of point-of-care imaging, and clearance decisions.

Mass-participation endurance event (marathon, triathlon, cycling race) medical tent: triage and treat exercise-associated collapse, heat illness (rectal temp, ice-bath cooling), hyponatremia, cramps, blisters, road rash and lacerations; obtain vitals, place IV fluids, decide on transport, with high volume in a short window.

Youth/community tournaments, club meets, wrestling and gymnastics events held at parks, rented gyms, or temporary venues with no permanent medical facility: physician works from a med bag on grass, mats, or a parking-lot area, evaluating sprains, fractures, dental/facial injuries, and skin infections and treating or referring.

On-field medical emergency during competition: sudden cardiac arrest (CPR, AED, airway management), suspected cervical spine injury (manual stabilization, facemask/helmet removal, spine boarding), severe fracture-dislocation with vascular compromise, or anaphylaxis — immediate hands-on intervention with the team's emergency action plan and handoff to EMS.

sources.system: DARPA Triage Challenge robotic systems (DART, Coordinated Robotics, UAS-DTU)
sources.developer: DARPA-funded teams (Carnegie Mellon/CMU-led DART, Coordinated Robotics, others)
sources.title: DART and MSAI triumph at DARPA Triage Challenge | DARPA
sources.claim: Autonomous ground and air robots in the DARPA Triage Challenge detected casualties and estimated vital signs and injury signatures in simulated mass-casualty courses, but they only sense and score triage categories; no treatment or hands-on examination is performed.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous casualty triage in the field. It is the closest robotic analogue to sideline injury evaluation, but it stops at remote sensing of vital signs and injury patterns in a competition course; it does not perform palpation, joint stability testing, concussion screening, or any treatment, so it cannot substantiate completion of this task at any tier.

sources.system: Vitestro autonomous blood drawing device (ADOPT trial, NCT05878483)
sources.title: Vitestro's robotic blood drawing device meets trial endpoints
sources.claim: An autonomous robotic phlebotomy device performed venipuncture on patients in a multicenter clinical trial with first-stick success comparable to human phlebotomists, in blood-collection facilities.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous needle insertion into a seated, armrest-fixtured patient. It shows a single treatment sub-step (vascular access) can be automated in a structured clinic, but the patient is positioned in a dedicated device and no assessment, diagnosis, or multi-step injury care is involved, so it cannot carry the whole instance.

sources.title: STAR Robot, Da Vinci Systems: The Rise of the Robosurgeon - MedicalExpo e-Magazine
sources.claim: The Smart Tissue Autonomous Robot executes suturing autonomously after a surgeon selects a plan, but only on fixtured tissue inside an operating room and under continuous surgeon supervision.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous soft-tissue suturing, a sub-step of sideline laceration repair. Performance does not transfer: STAR works on exposed, marked, fixtured bowel tissue in an OR with a surgeon selecting each plan, not on a conscious athlete's scalp or facial laceration during a game.

sources.title: Aescape Secures $83M to Scale AI-Powered Robotic Massage Technology – AlleyWatch
sources.claim: An autonomous robotic massage system is commercially deployed in fitness clubs, delivering programmed soft-tissue work to a client lying on a dedicated table; it does not evaluate or diagnose injuries.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous physical soft-tissue therapy on a human body. It is the most mature deployed body-contact robot, but it operates only on a purpose-built table with the client positioned by the machine, applies pre-selected routines, and performs no injury evaluation or medical treatment.

sources.system: Teleconcussion sideline robot (Mayo Clinic / Northern Arizona University football)
sources.title: 'Doctor' robot could help solve sports-concussion dilemma in rural America | EurekAlert
sources.claim: The only robot actually fielded on athletic sidelines for injury evaluation is a remote-controlled telepresence unit through which a human neurologist performs the concussion assessment; the robot itself does not examine or treat.
sources.transferJustification: Directly on-task (sideline concussion evaluation at games), but the system is a remote-controlled telepresence platform driven by an off-site physician with on-site helpers performing any hands-on steps, so it is teleoperation and cannot support a positive judgment.

sources.system: auto-RUSS autonomous robotic ultrasound scanning system
sources.title: Frontiers | Autonomous robotic ultrasound scanning system: a key to enhancing image analysis reproducibility and observer consistency in ultrasound imaging
sources.claim: Autonomous robotic ultrasound systems can acquire standardized images on healthy volunteers using force control and visual servoing in a laboratory setting.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous diagnostic imaging contact on a human body, a possible component of point-of-care injury evaluation. It transfers only partially: volunteers lie still on a fixed exam couch, the system acquires images rather than diagnosing or treating an injury.
