tasks.label: Supervise the rehabilitation of injured athletes.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Outpatient sports medicine clinic follow-up for an athlete recovering from a major injury or surgery (e.g., ACL reconstruction, ankle fracture, rotator cuff repair): physician reviews the physical therapist's notes, then hands-on re-examines the limb (inspects incision/swelling, measures range of motion, palpates joint lines, performs laxity and manual strength tests), watches gait and a squat/step-down, and on that basis advances or holds the rehabilitation protocol and writes new orders.

Rounds in a high school, college, or professional athletic training room: physician moves among athletes mid-rehab with the athletic trainers, spot-checks progress hands-on (joint stability, effusion, muscle guarding, pain with resisted testing), observes exercise technique and loading, modifies the rehab prescription with the trainer, and sets the next phase's criteria.

Late-stage functional progression and return-to-play testing at the practice field, court, or performance gym: physician observes and assesses sport-specific drills (running, cutting, hop-test battery, agility), checks the limb before and after loading for swelling or instability, and makes the clearance/graded-return decision with the trainer and coach.

Remote or asynchronous oversight between visits: physician reviews written PT/ATC progress reports, force-plate or dynamometer data and video, holds a telehealth or phone check-in, adjusts the written protocol, signs therapy orders and play restrictions, and communicates the plan to the rehab team and athlete.

General clinic visit with a youth or recreational athlete on a home exercise program (e.g., patellofemoral pain, hamstring strain, throwing shoulder): physician re-examines the area, watches the athlete demonstrate the prescribed exercises, corrects technique, and progresses or de-progresses the home program with the parent/athlete.

sources.date: 2019 (device commercially deployed in clinics since the 2000s)
sources.title: Using Human Ratings for Feedback Control: A Supervised Learning Approach with Application to Rehabilitation Robotics
sources.claim: Commercial robotic gait trainers such as the Lokomat deliver repetitive locomotor therapy in rehabilitation clinics, but the session is built around a therapist who prepares and sets up the patient and device and adjusts training parameters; the robot does not evaluate an injury or decide how a rehabilitation program should progress.
sources.transferJustification: Closest related task: robotic delivery of a rehabilitation exercise. It does not transfer to supervising rehabilitation, because the device executes a therapist-prescribed movement pattern under therapist setup and control and performs none of the re-examination, protocol modification, or clearance judgment that constitutes the physician's supervision.

sources.system: Socially Assistive Robot autonomous orthopaedic rehabilitation coaching framework
sources.title: Conceptual Framework for Autonomous Coaching in Orthopaedic Rehabilitation with Socially Assistive Robots
sources.claim: Socially assistive robots proposed for coaching orthopaedic rehabilitation remain research prototypes running predefined exercise scripts with heuristic adaptation and limited autonomy; autonomous coaching of an orthopaedic rehabilitation course is a proposed framework, not a demonstrated deployed capability.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic coaching of rehabilitation exercise sessions. Even this narrower task is not established autonomously in clinics, so it cannot substantiate a robot performing a physician's hands-on re-evaluation and progression decisions.

sources.system: Interactive personalized social robot exercise coaching system (post-stroke rehabilitation)
sources.developer: Carnegie Mellon University research team (Lee et al.)
sources.title: Design, development, and evaluation of an interactive personalized social robot to monitor and coach post-stroke rehabilitation exercises
sources.claim: A research social robot can autonomously monitor and assess a patient performing prescribed post-stroke rehabilitation exercises and give real-time corrective feedback, but this is exercise-form coaching in a study setting, not physician-level re-examination, protocol modification, or return-to-play clearance.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous monitoring of and feedback on rehabilitation exercise performance. It covers only observation and cueing of prescribed exercises; it involves no physical examination of injured tissue, no interaction with therapy staff, and no capability to advance a rehabilitation protocol, so it does not transfer to supervising an athlete's rehabilitation.

tasks.label: Select and prepare medical equipment or medications to be taken to athletic competition sites.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Routine team game coverage: in the athletic training room or team clinic, the physician pulls and packs the sideline bag from cabinets and shelves - gloves, dressings, laceration/suture kit, airway adjuncts, diagnostic tools (penlight, otoscope, BP cuff), tape and wraps, plus oral and injectable medications - checking expiration dates and arranging items in the bag's labeled compartments so they can be found in seconds.

Travel/away-game or tournament medication kit: selecting agents from the team formulary (analgesics, antibiotics, inhalers, epinephrine, antiemetics, some controlled substances), verifying lot/expiry, labeling, counting, and securing them in a lockable travel case with the required documentation, in the team clinic or hospital pharmacy.

Emergency-equipment preparation: inspecting and function-testing the AED (battery/pad status), oxygen cylinder and regulator, suction and intubation kit, spine board, cervical collars, vacuum splints, IV fluids and cold-water immersion/ice supplies, then assembling them on a cart or into a vehicle for the venue.

Mass-participation event (marathon, triathlon, multi-day tournament): assembling bulk supplies for several aid stations in a staging room or warehouse - dozens of identical kits, cases of fluids, wound-care and blister supplies, blankets - packed into labeled bins, palletized and staged for transport.

Off-site top-up and repacking: at the venue itself (locker room, medical tent, back of a vehicle, sideline table), restocking the bag between events or between days of a tournament from whatever stock is on hand, often outdoors, in weather, with no fixed layout.

sources.system: CapSen PiC medical kitting cell (Yaskawa MOTOMAN GP7 + Zivid Two 3D camera)
sources.title: Industry Insights: 3D Vision Technology Advances to Keep Pace With Bin Picking Challenges | Automate (A3)
sources.claim: A commercially deployed vision-guided robotic kitting cell picks a very wide range of medical products (syringes, swabs, pipettes, medicines in packets, tubes and bottles) out of cluttered bins and places them into cartons, running tens of millions of picks over a year.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: industrial medical kitting. Assembling a sideline medical kit is the same physical operation on the same object classes (syringes, swabs, dressings, medicine bottles/packets) at comparable precision - select items per a bill of materials and place them into a case.

sources.system: CapSen PiC + Zivid Two medical kitting and packaging cell
sources.title: Medical kitting with CapSen PiC and Zivid Two
sources.claim: The medical kitting application is a fixtured industrial cell: a six-axis Yaskawa arm with 3D vision picking small, diverse medical products for kitting and packaging.
sources.transferJustification: Same transfer as above; this source documents the purpose-built cell (E1) in which the medical-item kitting is performed.

sources.system: Omnicell XR2 Automated Central Pharmacy System
sources.title: Pharmacy Robot Increases Safety, Efficiency | Owensboro Health
sources.claim: An installed hospital central-pharmacy robot autonomously selects, barcode-verifies, bags, seals and labels the medications for each order.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: inpatient medication order filling. Building a travel medication kit is the same act - pull named drug packages from inventory, verify identity by barcode, label and package them into a container.

sources.title: Apotea Deploys RightPick 3 Item-Handling System from RightHand Robotics to Expedite Operations for Consumers
sources.claim: A robotic piece-picking system is deployed in a pharmacy fulfilment facility, autonomously handling individual pharmacy items for order fulfilment.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: pharmacy each-picking. Demonstrates reliable autonomous grasping of the small, varied, partly deformable packaged items that also make up a medical kit.

sources.developer: Boston Dynamics (deployed with DHL Supply Chain)
sources.title: DHL Supply Chain Achieves First Commercial Deployment of Boston Dynamics' Stretch Robot to Unload Trailers and Containers in the Warehouse
sources.claim: A commercially deployed mobile robot autonomously handles mixed cases in trailers at logistics sites, at up to 700 cases per ..., coping with disordered stacks.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: case handling in logistics. Supports the bulk-bin and case staging portion of preparing supplies for a mass-participation event, where the objects are cartons and bins rather than loose clinical items.

sources.date: 2020-03-31 article (updated 2023-09-22); fleet in 30+ hospitals as of 2024-2025
sources.title: How Diligent's Robots Are Making a Difference in Texas Hospitals | IEEE Spectrum
sources.claim: A hospital mobile manipulator autonomously picks known supplies out of taught supply-room bins and delivers them, but its manipulation is deliberately restricted to structured, pre-taught bins and well-known items rather than general picking.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: hospital supply-room retrieval. Closest existing capability to gathering kit contents inside a human clinical facility; the same source states the picking is 'very structured', which bounds what is achievable at E2.

roles.title: Ophthalmologists, Except Pediatric
roles.description: Diagnose and perform surgery to treat and help prevent disorders and diseases of the eye. May also provide vision services for treatment including glasses and contacts.

tasks.label: Perform comprehensive examinations of the visual system to determine the nature or extent of ocular disorders.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Routine comprehensive adult eye examination in a clinic exam lane (annual/new-patient visit, cataract, dry eye, refractive or general complaints): history, visual acuity and refraction, pupils, motility, confrontation fields, slit-lamp anterior-segment biomicroscopy (lids, conjunctiva, cornea, anterior chamber, lens grading), Goldmann applanation tonometry, pharmacologically dilated fundus exam with 90D lens and indirect ophthalmoscope, then a documented diagnosis and extent of disease.

Glaucoma-focused comprehensive examination: slit-lamp exam, applanation tonometry, gonioscopy with a contact lens placed on the anesthetized cornea to grade the angle, stereoscopic optic nerve head assessment through a dilated pupil, correlated with OCT RNFL scans and automated perimetry, to establish glaucoma type and severity.

Medical-retina examination: dilation, macular examination with a condensing lens at the slit lamp, indirect ophthalmoscopy of the peripheral retina including scleral depression for tears/detachment, integrated with OCT, widefield photos and angiography to grade the nature and extent of diabetic retinopathy, AMD, vein occlusion or retinal breaks.

Focused post-operative or short-interval follow-up examination in clinic or at the ambulatory surgery center: vision check, slit-lamp inspection of wound integrity, anterior-chamber cell and flare, corneal edema, IOL position or bleb, plus IOP measurement, to judge healing and detect complications.

Urgent consult examination at the bedside, in the emergency department, or in a holding area: portable slit lamp, penlight, lid retractors and indirect ophthalmoscope used on a seated, supine or poorly cooperative patient (ocular trauma, chemical burn, acute red eye, suspected papilledema or endophthalmitis), often with pain, photophobia or blepharospasm.

Screening-style evaluation of fundus disease at a community health center, nursing home, employer or mobile screening station, where the determination of whether disease is present and how advanced it is rests mainly on acquired images (non-mydriatic fundus photography, sometimes OCT, acuity and IOP) rather than hands-on biomicroscopy.

sources.system: Robotically aligned OCT (RAOCT), 6-DoF posture-invariant robotic OCT
sources.title: Robotic Optical Coherence Tomography of Human Subjects with Posture-Invariant Head and Eye Alignment in Six Degrees of Freedom
sources.claim: Duke's robot-mounted OCT scanner autonomously finds and aligns to the eye of an unrestrained human subject (standing, seated, reclined or supine) and acquires retinal volumes without head stabilization or an operator; it produces images only, not an ophthalmic examination or diagnosis.
sources.transferJustification: Related task (retinal imaging, one component of the ophthalmic exam): shows a robot can align to and image a human eye in a clinical-grade facility, but it performs no anterior-segment biomicroscopy, tonometry, gonioscopy or diagnostic synthesis, so it does not transfer to the whole examination.

sources.system: Robotic OCT (RAOCT) in the emergency department
sources.title: Robotic Optical Coherence Tomography Retinal Imaging for Emergency Department Patients: A Pilot Study for Emergency Physicians' Diagnostic Performance
sources.claim: A robotic, semi-autonomous OCT system was used on real emergency department patients at Duke University Hospital with acute visual change, headache or focal deficits; the robot acquired retinal OCT images which physicians then interpreted.
sources.transferJustification: Related task (bedside retinal imaging during an urgent eye consult): same patients and setting as the ED consult instance, but the system only supplies images and is described as semi-autonomous, so it cannot substantiate autonomous completion of the bedside examination.

sources.system: Facilitated self-service eye screening with fully automatic fundus camera plus AI grading
sources.developer: Shanghai Eye Diseases Prevention & Treatment Center / Shanghai Eye Hospital program
sources.title: Service Quality and Residents' Preferences for Facilitated Self-Service Fundus Disease Screening: Cross-Sectional Study
sources.claim: Shanghai's community fundus-disease screening program deployed a fully automatic fundus camera that motorizes its own alignment and focus to the patient's pupils with voice guidance, letting residents image themselves without staff; images go to an AI model that returns screening results immediately, in community primary health care institutions.

sources.date: FDA De Novo 2018; product page dated 2026-03
sources.title: LumineticsCore — Digital Diagnostics
sources.claim: LumineticsCore (formerly IDx-DR) is an FDA-cleared autonomous AI diagnostic system deployed in point-of-care offices that grades retinal images and issues a diabetic retinopathy diagnostic report without any physician reviewing the images.
sources.transferJustification: Related task (autonomous determination of presence/severity of one ocular disorder from retinal images): it supplies the diagnostic-decision half of an imaging-based screening evaluation, paired with an automated camera; it does not cover anterior-segment, glaucoma or non-imaging findings.

sources.title: DigitalOptometrics showcasing new autonomous slit lamp at Vision Expo East 2025
sources.claim: The first marketed 'autonomous' slit lamp automates capture, focus and multi-slit imaging of the anterior segment, but the examination workflow still uses an on-site ophthalmic technician and a remote licensed doctor who reviews the captured images and controls the device.
sources.transferJustification: Related task (anterior-segment slit-lamp examination): it is the closest system to the slit-lamp portion of the exam, but capture is triggered and interpreted by humans on site and remotely, so it cannot support an autonomous positive judgment.

sources.system: Autonomous intraocular microsurgical robot for targeted retinal injections
sources.developer: Beijing Institute of Technology / Peking Union Medical College Hospital team
sources.title: Autonomous robotic intraocular surgery for targeted retinal injections | Science Robotics
sources.claim: The frontier of autonomous ophthalmic robotics is intraocular microsurgery on immobilized ex vivo and in vivo animal eyes under a microscope, not examination of patients.
sources.transferJustification: Related task (robotic manipulation inside the eye): cited only to bound the state of the art — it operates on anesthetized, fixated animal eyes under a surgical microscope and performs no examination or diagnosis, so capability does not transfer to examining awake patients.

tasks.label: Diagnose or treat injuries, disorders, or diseases of the eye and eye structures including the cornea, sclera, conjunctiva, or eyelids.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Outpatient clinic visit for an anterior-segment complaint (red eye, dry eye, corneal abrasion or ulcer, conjunctivitis, blepharitis, lid lesion): take history, check acuity, perform slit-lamp biomicroscopy with lid eversion, instill fluorescein/anesthetic drops, measure IOP, culture or scrape if indicated, then diagnose and prescribe treatment.

Clinic follow-up and management of chronic eye disease (glaucoma, diabetic retinopathy, AMD): dilated fundus exam with condensing lens, gonioscopy or applanation tonometry, acquire and interpret OCT/fundus imaging and visual fields, adjust medications, and deliver in-office intravitreal anti-VEGF injection when indicated.

In-office minor procedure in a clinic procedure room: corneal or conjunctival foreign body and rust-ring removal at the slit lamp with needle/burr, chalazion incision and curettage, eyelid lesion biopsy or excision, punctal plug insertion, corneal suture removal, bandage contact lens placement, under topical or local anesthetic on an awake, moving patient.

Operating-room / ASC surgery on the eye and adnexa under microscope: cataract phacoemulsification with IOL, corneal transplant (DMEK/PK), pterygium excision with graft, ptosis repair or blepharoplasty, lid or globe laceration repair; includes draping, speculum placement, incisions, tissue handling, suturing, and intraoperative decision-making.

Office-based laser treatment in a laser suite: selective laser trabeculoplasty, YAG capsulotomy or peripheral iridotomy, retinal photocoagulation, corneal cross-linking, or excimer/femtosecond refractive treatment; includes indication decision, anesthetic and lens placement, docking/aiming, energy titration, and immediate post-treatment IOP/exam check.

Urgent or inpatient consult for ocular trauma or acute vision loss: bedside/ED exam with portable slit lamp and indirect ophthalmoscope, copious irrigation for chemical burn, Seidel testing for open globe, foreign body assessment with imaging, shield placement, and disposition or emergent surgical repair.

sources.title: World's First in Human Fully Robot Assisted Cataract Surgery Performed | Ophthalmology Management
sources.claim: ForSight Robotics' JASPER (formerly ORYOM) performed the first-in-human fully robot-assisted cataract surgery in April 2026, but the platform is a surgeon-controlled console that assists the surgeon through each step rather than operating autonomously.

sources.developer: Institute of Automation, Chinese Academy of Sciences (Gui-Bin Bian et al.)
sources.title: Autonomous robotic intraocular surgery for targeted retinal injections | Science Robotics
sources.claim: The most advanced autonomous intraocular surgical robot reported (ARISE, Science Robotics 2026) performs targeted retinal injections only in eyeball phantoms, ex vivo porcine eyes, and animal eyes — not in human patients.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: intraocular surgical needle placement, the closest published autonomous ophthalmic surgery; cited to show autonomy exists only in animal/ex vivo models, so it cannot substantiate completion of human surgical instances.

sources.system: Steady-hand eye robots with deep-learning autonomous RVC
sources.title: Autonomous robot takes a step towards high precision eye surgery | ICT&health
sources.claim: Johns Hopkins' autonomous steady-hand eye robot performed retinal vein cannulation with deep-learning control only in pig eyes, with 90%/83% success; researchers state clinical application requires further animal then human studies.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: microsurgical needle insertion into retinal vessels; shows the state of the art in autonomous ophthalmic microsurgery is confined to ex vivo animal eyes.

sources.title: Intraocular robotic interventional surgical system (IRISS): Semi-automated OCT-guided cataract removal
sources.claim: The IRISS robot achieved OCT-guided semi-automated cataract lens extraction only on postmortem pig eyes, with incomplete extraction in some eyes.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: cataract lens removal, a core OR surgery step in instance 3; cited to show automation remains at ex vivo animal-eye stage.

sources.title: Robotics in Retinal Surgery: Recent Advances and Applications - Retina Today
sources.claim: Ophthorobotics' automated intravitreal injection device identifies the pupil and performs pars plana injections under supervision, validated in animal studies; it is not a cleared clinical product performing patient injections autonomously.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: intravitreal injection, a component of instance 1; cited because evidence is limited to animal studies under supervision.

sources.system: Eagle Direct Selective Laser Trabeculoplasty (DSLT) device
sources.title: Alcon Completes Acquisition of BELKIN Vision, Expanding Glaucoma Portfolio with Direct Selective Laser Trabeculoplasty (DSLT) Device
sources.claim: Alcon/BELKIN's Eagle DSLT device is an FDA-cleared automated laser that uses eye tracking to target and deliver selective laser trabeculoplasty through the limbus, but it automates only the laser-delivery step of a physician-run treatment encounter.

sources.developer: Duke University (Draelos, Kuo, Izatt et al.)
sources.title: Contactless optical coherence tomography of the eyes of freestanding individuals with a robotic scanner | Nature Biomedical Engineering
sources.claim: A robot-mounted OCT scanner autonomously aligns to and images the eyes of freestanding humans without operator intervention, demonstrating autonomous ophthalmic image acquisition only (not examination, diagnosis, or treatment).
sources.transferJustification: Related task: ocular diagnostic imaging acquisition, a sub-step of instances 0 and 1; cited to show robots can autonomously image an eye but not conduct the exam, form the diagnosis, or treat.

sources.developer: Queen's University / Hotel Dieu Hospital, Kingston (validation study)
sources.title: Validating the use of a stereoscopic robotized teleophthalmic drone slit lamp - Canadian Journal of Ophthalmology
sources.claim: Robotized slit lamps used for anterior-segment examination in eye clinics are remotely operated by an ophthalmologist rather than autonomous.

sources.system: LumineticsCore (IDx-DR) / EyeArt autonomous AI diabetic eye exam
sources.title: Clinical Implementation of Autonomous Artificial Intelligence Systems for Diabetic Eye Exams: Considerations for Success | Clinical Diabetes
sources.claim: Deployed 'autonomous AI' eye diagnostics (LumineticsCore/IDx-DR, EyeArt) are software algorithms attached to a fundus camera that a human operator must position and operate; no robot performs the physical imaging or any treatment.

sources.title: AutoRing: Imitation Learning-based Autonomous Intraocular Foreign Body Removal Manipulation with Eye Surgical Robot
sources.claim: Autonomous robotic intraocular foreign body manipulation has been demonstrated only in a biomimetic eye model in the laboratory, not on patients.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: foreign body removal from the eye, closest analogue to instance 2; cited to show the capability exists only in phantom models.

tasks.label: Provide or direct the provision of postoperative care.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Postoperative day-1 visit after routine cataract/IOL surgery in the ophthalmology clinic: history, visual acuity and pinhole/autorefraction, intraocular pressure, slit-lamp exam of the wound, cornea, anterior chamber cell/flare and IOL position, then adjusting the drop regimen and counseling the patient on activity and shield use.

Later routine postoperative visits (1 week to 1-3 months) after cataract or refractive/corneal surgery: refraction and vision check, IOP, slit-lamp and sometimes dilated fundus/OCT exam, tapering or stopping steroids/antibiotics, spectacle prescription, decision to discharge or schedule YAG, and documentation.

Immediate postoperative care in the ASC/hospital recovery area: checking the patient before discharge, placing or taping the eye shield/patch, writing discharge and medication orders, giving verbal and written instructions, and directing the recovery nurses and technicians.

In-office postoperative procedures at the slit lamp or laser: corneal/eyelid suture removal or adjustment, laser suture lysis or releasable-suture release and bleb needling after trabeculectomy, YAG capsulotomy for posterior capsule opacification, contact-lens/bandage-lens management.

Management of postoperative complications in clinic or OR: pressure spike requiring paracentesis or burping a wound, wound leak with Seidel testing and resuturing, suspected endophthalmitis requiring vitreous tap-and-inject, hyphema, retinal detachment or dislocated IOL requiring a return to surgery.

Remote direction of postoperative care from the office or from home after hours: telephone/portal triage of pain, redness or vision change, verbal orders to nursing staff or optometric co-managers, prescription changes called to pharmacies, and instructions to caregivers about drops and positioning.

sources.title: Clinical performance of an interactive platform based on artificial intelligence in ophthalmology: experience in a third-level reference center
sources.claim: The Eyelib robotized scan (DORIA platform) autonomously acquires visual acuity, refraction, anterior/posterior segment imaging and intraocular pressure in a hospital ophthalmology department, but a technician operates it and ophthalmologists remotely review the data and make all clinical decisions — the robot does not deliver postoperative assessment or treatment itself.
sources.transferJustification: Closest analogue to the measurement portion of a postoperative visit (VA, IOP, imaging) in the same clinic environment; cited to show that even this state-of-the-art robotic eye-exam station only captures data, with the physician's examination, judgment and treatment decisions still performed by a human remotely.

sources.title: DigitalOptometrics to Preview World's First Autonomous Slitlamp at Vision Expo East 2025
sources.claim: The DigitalOptometrics/SlitLED 'autonomous' slit lamp automates anterior-segment image capture, but the clinical review and decisions are made by a remote human doctor viewing the captured images.
sources.transferJustification: Slit-lamp examination is the core physical step of a postoperative eye visit; this is the most advanced automated slit lamp reported, and it is an image-capture device previewed at a trade show whose interpretation and any care decision remain with a remote human doctor.

sources.title: World's First in Human Fully Robot Assisted Cataract Surgery Performed
sources.claim: The most advanced clinical ophthalmic surgical robot performs cataract surgery only under the direct control of a surgeon at a console in an operating room; it is a first-in-human, investigational procedure, not autonomous eye care.
sources.transferJustification: Ocular surgery is the closest robot-executed eye intervention to in-office postoperative procedures (suture lysis, needling, tap-and-inject); it shows such manipulation on human eyes remains surgeon-controlled teleoperation, so it cannot support an autonomous positive judgment.

sources.system: Autonomous intraocular microsurgical robot (targeted retinal injection)
sources.developer: Beijing Institute of Technology et al. (Science Robotics)
sources.title: Autonomous robotic intraocular surgery for targeted retinal injections | Science Robotics
sources.claim: Autonomous robotic intraocular needle procedures (targeted retinal injections) have been demonstrated only in ex vivo porcine and in vivo animal eyes in a laboratory, not on patients in a clinic.
sources.transferJustification: Intraocular injection is the technique used in postoperative tap-and-inject for endophthalmitis; the demonstration is confined to animal eyes on a laboratory bench, so it does not substantiate completing a patient's postoperative complication management at any tier.

sources.developer: Foxconn with NVIDIA and Kawasaki Heavy Industries
sources.title: Could AI nursing robots help healthcare staffing shortages? | CNN Business
sources.claim: Autonomous hospital robots deployed on wards perform logistics and wayfinding (delivering medication, guiding patients), not patient examination, wound/shield care, or clinical direction.
sources.transferJustification: Cited for the recovery-room instance: the leading autonomous hospital ward robot's scope is delivery and guidance, showing no fielded robot performs bedside postoperative patient care such as shield placement or discharge assessment.

tasks.label: Develop or implement plans and procedures for ophthalmologic services.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

tasks.label: Prescribe or administer topical or systemic medications to treat ophthalmic conditions and to manage pain.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Outpatient ophthalmology clinic exam room: after slit-lamp exam, the ophthalmologist selects a topical drug (glaucoma drop, post-op steroid/antibiotic regimen, dry-eye or allergy drop), checks allergies/interactions/formulary, e-prescribes to the patient's pharmacy, and counsels on dosing and taper.

Clinic or hospital consult: ophthalmologist prescribes a systemic drug or analgesic (oral valacyclovir for zoster ophthalmicus, oral antibiotic for preseptal cellulitis, acetazolamide, oral prednisone, NSAID or short opioid course post-op), adjusting dose for renal function and comorbidities; transmitted electronically.

Clinic exam lane: physician personally administers topical medication to the eye - proparacaine before tonometry or foreign-body removal, fluorescein, dilating drops, antibiotic drop/ointment after an epithelial defect - instilling into the conjunctival sac of a blinking, sometimes photophobic or uncooperative patient, confirming delivery and patching when needed.

Retina clinic procedure room: intravitreal injection of anti-VEGF or steroid - verify drug/eye/patient, anesthetize, povidone-iodine prep, lid speculum, measure 3.5-4 mm from limbus, 30G injection into the vitreous, then check perfusion/vision and counsel on endophthalmitis warning signs; often 20-40 per session.

Operating room or minor-procedure room: administering medication as part of a procedure - intracameral antibiotic/miotic at the end of cataract surgery, subconjunctival or sub-Tenon steroid/antibiotic injection, periocular anesthetic block, topical drops on the sterile field.

Emergency department or urgent clinic visit: acute presentations needing immediate drug administration - topical drop series plus oral/IV acetazolamide for acute angle closure, copious irrigation plus drops for chemical burn, intravitreal antibiotics for suspected endophthalmitis, fortified topical antibiotics for corneal ulcer - under time pressure with a distressed patient.

sources.title: Robotics in Retinal Surgery: Recent Advances and Applications - Retina Today
sources.claim: The only automated (non-teleoperated) intravitreal injection platform, Ophthorobotics' head-mounted device, has been shown only in animal studies and operates under clinician supervision.

sources.title: Autonomous robotic intraocular surgery for targeted retinal injections | Science Robotics
sources.claim: An autonomous intraocular injection robot (ARISE) performed targeted subretinal and retinal-vein injections, but only in eyeball phantoms, ex vivo porcine eyes and in vivo animal eyes in a laboratory setup - not on human patients.
sources.transferJustification: Intraocular drug delivery is the closest robotic analogue to administering intravitreal/periocular medication; transfer fails because delivery was only into phantom and animal eyes in a lab, never into a human patient's eye in clinic.

sources.title: ForSight Robotics announces first robot-assisted cataract surgery with JASPER platform | MassDevice
sources.claim: The first ophthalmic robot to operate on a human patient's eye (cataract surgery) is driven by a surgeon at a console, i.e. teleoperated, not autonomous.
sources.transferJustification: Nearest human-patient ophthalmic robotics; it shows that needle/instrument work on live human eyes remains surgeon-driven teleoperation, so it cannot support autonomous medication administration.

sources.title: Aletta - Vitestro
sources.claim: Autonomous needle placement in a human patient exists commercially for blood collection in clinical laboratories, but the device draws blood rather than selecting or administering any medication, and is not ophthalmic.
sources.transferJustification: Venipuncture is the nearest deployed autonomous patient-contact procedure; it does not transfer because this task requires choosing a drug and delivering it to the eye or systemically, and no such administration is demonstrated.

sources.transferJustification: Cited to show the state of the art for getting drops into an eye is a hand-held aid used by the patient; no machine-controlled system instills drops, so nothing supports a positive judgment.

tasks.label: Perform ophthalmic surgeries such as cataract, glaucoma, refractive, corneal, vitro-retinal, eye muscle, or oculoplastic surgeries.

instances.label: Routine age-related cataract extraction with IOL implantation in an ambulatory surgery center: topical anesthesia, 10-20 minute case, 15-40 cases on a list. Surgeon makes clear-corneal incisions, capsulorhexis, hydrodissection, phacoemulsification, cortex removal, IOL injection and wound sealing, and must recognize and manage events such as posterior capsule rupture.

Complex or combined anterior-segment case in an ASC/hospital OR: dense white or brunescent cataract, small pupil, pseudoexfoliation with weak zonules, post-trauma or post-vitrectomy eye, or cataract combined with a MIGS stent or goniotomy. Requires pupil expanders, capsular tension rings, capsule staining, occasional anterior vitrectomy and mid-case plan changes.

Vitreoretinal surgery in a hospital OR under block or general anesthesia: pars plana vitrectomy for retinal detachment, macular hole or epiretinal membrane. Trocar-cannula placement, core vitrectomy, micron-scale membrane peeling on mobile retina, endolaser, fluid-air-gas or silicone oil exchange, sclerotomy closure.

Oculoplastic surgery in an office procedure room or OR under local anesthesia: upper-lid blepharoplasty, ptosis repair, entropion/ectropion repair, dacryocystorhinostomy, or eyelid tumor excision with flap/graft reconstruction. Free-hand marking, incision, cautery, tissue shaping and layered suturing to a functional and cosmetic standard.

Other incisional subspecialty surgery in a hospital OR or ASC: corneal transplant (DMEK/DSAEK/PK) with donor tissue preparation and 10-0 nylon suturing, pterygium excision with conjunctival autograft, trabeculectomy or glaucoma drainage tube, or strabismus muscle recession/resection with intraoperative adjustment.

Laser refractive surgery in a dedicated laser suite: LASIK, SMILE or PRK. Patient docked under the femtosecond laser for flap or lenticule creation, surgeon lifts and reflects the flap or dissects and extracts the lenticule with forceps, excimer ablation under eye tracking, flap repositioning, irrigation and bandage lens; or phakic IOL implantation as an alternative.

sources.title: World's First-in-Human Fully Robot-Assisted Cataract Surgery Performed - Ophthalmology Management
sources.claim: ForSight Robotics' JASPER (formerly Oryom) platform completed a first-in-human cataract surgery start to finish in April 2026, but it is a surgeon-controlled robot that 'assists surgeons with every step'; it is in an early feasibility trial and not approved.

sources.title: Horizon Completes Worlds First Robotics-Assisted Cataract Surgery - Ophthalmology Management
sources.claim: Horizon Surgical Systems' Polaris performed the first in-human robotic-assisted cataract surgeries (10 eyes, El Salvador, October 2025); the surgeon drives instruments with a joystick and the device is investigational, not FDA approved.

sources.title: The rise of robotic cataract surgery: where the field stands and where it's headed - EyeWorld
sources.claim: Trade coverage of the two leading robotic cataract platforms reports the surgeon holds a joystick shaped like a phaco probe and that the technology remains far from autonomous or mainstream.

sources.title: Robotics in Retinal Surgery: Recent Advances and Applications - Retina Today
sources.claim: The Preceyes Surgical System, used for the first robot-assisted retinal operations at Oxford and now owned by Zeiss, is a telemanipulator: the surgeon at a console moves a joystick that drives the arm holding intraocular instruments.
sources.transferJustification: Same task family (intraocular microsurgery): shows the most advanced clinical retinal robot is continuously surgeon-driven, not autonomous.

sources.developer: UCLA Stein Eye Institute / UCLA Mechanical and Aerospace Engineering
sources.title: A Study on Semi-Automated OCT-Guided Robotic Surgery for Porcine Lens Removal - PMC
sources.claim: The most advanced automation demonstrated for intraocular surgery is OCT-guided semi-automated lens extraction by the IRISS robot on 30 post-mortem pig eyes held in a fixture, with surgeon override; it covers only the lens-removal step, not a whole human cataract operation.
sources.transferJustification: Directly the cataract sub-task; establishes machine-executed intraocular steps exist only ex vivo, in a fixtured cadaver eye, and only for part of the procedure.

sources.title: THE ADVANTAGES OF FEMTOSECOND LASER-ASSISTED CATARACT SURGERY - PMC
sources.claim: Commercially deployed femtosecond laser-assisted cataract surgery automates only preparatory steps - capsulotomy, corneal incisions, nucleus fragmentation - after which the surgeon manually performs phacoemulsification, cortex aspiration and IOL implantation.

sources.title: ZEISS SMILE - a femtosecond laser-based solution for Small Incision Lenticule Extraction
sources.claim: In ZEISS SMILE refractive surgery the femtosecond laser cuts the lenticule under computer control, but the lenticule must then be extracted manually by the surgeon, so the machine does not complete the procedure.

instances.label: Clinic visit: ophthalmologist reviews same-day, technician-acquired multimodal studies (macular/RNFL OCT, fundus photos, automated visual fields) on the exam-lane monitor, correlates them with the patient's exam and history, and issues a documented interpretation and management decision (inject anti-VEGF vs observe, escalate glaucoma therapy).

Retinal screening read: color fundus photographs of a diabetic or hypertensive patient acquired on a non-mydriatic camera in clinic or via a tele-retina program; ophthalmologist grades retinopathy severity, decides referral/follow-up interval, and reports the result.

Instrument-mediated in-office test acquisition on a cooperative seated patient: non-contact/rebound tonometry, autorefraction-keratometry, pachymetry, fundus photography, macular/optic-nerve OCT, and optical biometry/keratometry before cataract surgery. Patient sits at a chinrest in a standard instrument room; the test must yield a reliable, artifact-free measurement.

Hands-on contact tests the physician performs at the slit lamp: Goldmann applanation after anesthetic/fluorescein, gonioscopy with a goniolens on the anesthetized cornea, Seidel testing, Schirmer strips under the lid, corneal scraping for culture, forced-duction testing - touching a moving, blinking eye of an awake patient.

Procedural/specialized diagnostics: fluorescein or ICG angiography (IV cannulation, dye injection, timed photography, monitoring for reactions), B-scan ocular ultrasonography with probe and coupling gel on the lid, electroretinography/VEP with electrodes - performed or directly supervised and then interpreted.

Ordering and follow-up of tests outside the eye clinic: ESR/CRP and labs for giant cell arteritis or uveitis workup, MRI/CT of orbits and brain, temporal artery biopsy pathology; the ophthalmologist places the orders, reviews returned results in the EHR, and acts on them.

instances.label: Inpatient or emergency-department consult requested by a hospitalist, intensivist, or ED physician (e.g., suspected endophthalmitis, orbital cellulitis, giant cell arteritis, ocular trauma): the ophthalmologist reviews the chart and findings, forms an assessment, and communicates diagnosis, urgency, and management recommendations to the requesting team, documenting a formal consult note in the record.

Informal 'curbside' or telephone consultation from a primary care physician, optometrist, urgent-care clinician, or nurse practitioner asking how to triage or manage a case (red eye, sudden vision loss, drug ocular toxicity monitoring): the ophthalmologist gives verbal advice on workup, treatment, and whether/how fast to refer.

Outpatient referral consultation: after evaluating a patient referred by another physician, the ophthalmologist dictates or writes a consultation letter/report back to the referring clinician summarizing findings, diagnosis, treatment plan, and co-management instructions.

Store-and-forward teleophthalmology or e-consult: reviewing submitted retinal photographs, OCT scans, or clinical questions in an EHR e-consult queue (e.g., diabetic retinopathy screening for a primary care or endocrinology practice) and returning a graded report and recommendations without seeing the patient in person.

Multidisciplinary case discussion — hospital rounds, tumor board, or a case conference with neurology, rheumatology, oncology, endocrinology, or NICU/pediatrics teams — where the ophthalmologist interprets ocular findings and advises on their implications for systemic diagnosis and therapy.

tasks.label: Perform laser surgeries to alter, remove, reshape, or replace ocular tissue.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Clinic laser room: Nd:YAG posterior capsulotomy for posterior capsule opacification in a pseudophakic patient seated at a slit-lamp laser. Topical anesthesia, often a capsulotomy contact lens; surgeon focuses the aiming beams just behind the IOL optic and fires 10-40 photodisruptive shots in a cruciate/circular pattern to open the capsule without pitting the IOL, then checks IOP.

Clinic laser suite: selective laser trabeculoplasty (SLT) for open-angle glaucoma or ocular hypertension. Anesthetic drops, gonioscopy lens with coupling gel, ~100 low-energy pulses titrated to champagne-bubble endpoint over 180-360 degrees of trabecular meshwork, post-laser IOP check.

Hand-guided clinic or OR lasers: laser peripheral iridotomy, iridoplasty, transscleral or endoscopic cyclophotocoagulation, laser suture lysis, and laser retinopexy at the indirect ophthalmoscope. The surgeon holds a contact lens or probe against the globe, may scleral-depress, and titrates each shot to visible tissue effect on a moving, sometimes uncooperative eye.

Retina clinic: retinal photocoagulation planned on fundus/angiographic images and delivered at a slit-lamp or navigated laser - panretinal scatter for proliferative diabetic retinopathy (1,000+ burns across sessions) or focal/grid treatment of diabetic macular edema, with contact lens or contactless wide-field optics and power titration to burn intensity.

Refractive surgery suite: corneal laser vision correction on a supine patient - femtosecond flap creation plus excimer stromal ablation (LASIK) with manual flap lift and reposition, SMILE with manual lenticule extraction, or one-step transepithelial surface ablation (transPRK); sterile prep, docking/suction or centration, active eye tracking during ablation.

Ambulatory surgery center laser bay: femtosecond laser stage of cataract surgery - patient docked to the laser with a suction patient interface, OCT imaging of the anterior segment, then machine-created capsulotomy, lens fragmentation and corneal/limbal incisions, before undocking for phacoemulsification.

sources.title: FDA clears BELKIN Vision's Eagle device for SLT
sources.claim: The Eagle/Voyager DSLT device automatically locates the treatment target on the limbus and then delivers the full 120-pulse laser trabeculoplasty sequence while an eye tracker compensates for eye movement - i.e. the tissue-altering laser delivery is machine-controlled, not hand-aimed.

sources.title: Alcon Announces U.S. Launch of Voyager DSLT, First-of-its-Kind Treatment for Glaucoma and Ocular Hypertension
sources.claim: The automated DSLT device is fully commercially available in US eye clinics as of February 2025, performing SLT without a gonioscopy lens or manual aiming.

sources.title: Glaucoma Treatments Coming Down the Pipeline
sources.claim: Residual human role in DSLT is limited to coarsely aligning the patient's eye to the device and approving the automatically acquired target; the 360-degree treatment is then delivered almost entirely by the machine. This documents that presentation/alignment of the eye is still done by a person.

sources.title: Randomized Noninferiority Trial of Direct Selective Laser Trabeculoplasty in Open-Angle Glaucoma and Ocular Hypertension: GLAUrious Study
sources.claim: In a multicenter randomized controlled trial, automated image-guided DSLT produced IOP reduction close to that of surgeon-performed manual SLT (20.6% vs 23.6% washout IOP reduction at 6 months), supporting near-worker-quality output.

sources.title: CATALYS Laser - Ophthalmology | ForTec Medical
sources.claim: The Catalys femtosecond laser docks the eye with a suction patient interface, then uses streaming 3D OCT and automated surface-mapping algorithms to guide laser delivery, producing capsulotomies accurate to within 30 microns.

sources.title: Update and clinical utility of the LenSx femtosecond laser in cataract surgery
sources.claim: Femtosecond laser cataract surgery couples anterior-segment imaging to a laser so that capsulotomy, lens fragmentation and corneal incisions are executed with computer-guided accuracy and reproducibility; the LenSx platform alone had been used in over 200,000 procedures.

sources.system: Catalys femtosecond laser (primary posterior laser capsulotomy)
sources.developer: Johnson & Johnson Vision / University Eye Hospital Bochum
sources.title: Safety of femtosecond laser-assisted primary posterior capsulotomy immediately after cataract surgery
sources.claim: In human pseudophakic eyes, the posterior capsule lying between the anterior hyaloid and the IOL optic was identified by the laser's integrated 3D spectral-domain OCT and cut by the femtosecond laser, in a prospective randomized series - a machine-executed posterior capsulotomy.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: Nd:YAG posterior capsulotomy. Same target tissue (posterior capsule behind an implanted IOL), same accepted output (a clear central capsular opening), same micron-scale precision requirement and same avoidance of IOL damage, executed by an imaging-guided laser on a human eye docked to the machine.

sources.system: Catalys Precision Laser System (off-label posterior capsulotomy)
sources.title: Off-Label Use of Femtosecond Laser for Posterior Capsulotomy
sources.claim: Posterior capsulotomy has been performed in pseudophakic human eyes by re-docking the eye to the femtosecond laser after cataract surgery and confirming the capsulotomy position on live OCT before machine-delivered cutting.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: Nd:YAG capsulotomy for posterior capsule opacification. Demonstrates that with the pseudophakic eye fixtured to the laser (E1-style presentation), an OCT-guided laser creates the same posterior-capsule opening the ophthalmologist would create by hand at the slit lamp.

sources.title: Transepithelial photorefractive keratectomy - an analysis of the solutions offered by the industry nowadays
sources.claim: Transepithelial PRK is a single-step, no-touch refractive procedure in which the excimer laser ablates both epithelium and stroma in one machine-delivered sequence with no mechanical instrument contacting the eye; over 825,000 such treatments have been performed with the SCHWIND AMARIS.

sources.title: Clinical Evaluation and Treatment Accuracy in Diabetic Macular Edema Using Navigated Laser Photocoagulator NAVILAS
sources.claim: The Navilas navigated photocoagulator automatically steps the aiming/treatment beam from one pre-planned retinal target to the next until all planned sites are treated, with image-based stabilization compensating for eye movement.

sources.title: Pain and accuracy of focal laser treatment for diabetic macular edema using a retinal navigated laser (Navilas)
sources.claim: Machine-navigated retinal laser delivery achieves surgeon-grade placement accuracy: 96% of visible burns fell within 100 microns of the planned target across 5,423 spots in 54 patients.

sources.title: Focal and panretinal photocoagulation with a navigated laser (NAVILAS)
sources.claim: Navigated retinal laser retains a human trigger: the surgeon verifies target lock and manually actuates the laser, so delivery is machine-guided but physician-initiated.

sources.title: ForSight Robotics Performs World's First Fully Robot-Assisted Cataract Surgery in a Human Patient
sources.claim: The first fully robot-assisted human cataract surgery was performed with a surgeon controlling the platform throughout - robotic ophthalmic surgery outside of the laser platforms remains surgeon-driven, not autonomous.

instances.label: Didactic teaching at an academic medical center: the ophthalmologist gives grand rounds, lectures, or journal-club sessions to residents and fellows on surgical indications, technique steps, and complication management, using slides and recorded surgical video.

Clinic precepting: attending supervises residents seeing patients in the eye clinic, watches or repeats slit-lamp/indirect ophthalmoscopy findings, questions the resident on diagnosis and plan, and explains technique for exams and minor office procedures (injections, lasers).

Intraoperative teaching in the OR: attending sits at the teaching (assistant) side of the surgical microscope while a resident performs cataract or other intraocular surgery, giving continuous verbal coaching on instrument position, force, and sequencing, and debriefing afterward.

Wet lab / simulator instruction: attending demonstrates and then supervises residents practicing capsulorhexis, phacoemulsification, or suturing on porcine eyes, artificial eyes, or a virtual-reality surgical simulator, giving corrective feedback on each attempt.

Ad hoc instruction of other learners: explaining ophthalmic procedures, imaging protocols, or perioperative technique to medical students, technicians, scrub staff, or optometry trainees in clinic hallways, the OR, or via case-based video review.

tasks.label: Conduct clinical or laboratory-based research in ophthalmology.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Clinical trial study visit as site investigator: the ophthalmologist performs the protocol eye examination on an enrolled patient in a clinic exam room — refraction/BCVA check, slit-lamp biomicroscopy, IOP, dilated indirect fundoscopy — grades findings per protocol (e.g., ETDRS/anterior-chamber cell), assesses adverse events, and signs the source documentation.

Protocol imaging session for a study: acquiring the standardized image set (color fundus photographs, macular and ONH OCT, sometimes OCTA) on cooperative enrolled adults at scheduled visits in the clinic's ophthalmic imaging suite, repeating captures until images meet reading-center quality standards and uploading them.

Desk/analytical research work: writing the protocol and IRB submission, extracting retrospective chart or registry data, grading images on a reading workstation, running statistics, and drafting the manuscript or grant, in an academic office.

Wet-lab bench experiment in a university ophthalmology research lab: culturing and differentiating ocular cells (e.g., iPSC-derived RPE), passaging, transfection/treatment, immunostaining, plate-based assays, PCR/western blots, and microscopy readout, with sterile technique at a hood and shared benchtop instruments.

Animal-model ocular research session in a vivarium procedure room: anesthetized rodent or rabbit receives an intravitreal/subretinal injection or laser lesion induction, followed by in vivo imaging (OCT/fundus) or ERG at protocol timepoints, with dosing accuracy and no ocular damage required.

Operating-room based investigational surgery or device study: the ophthalmologist performs the investigational procedure in a human patient (e.g., new IOL implantation, subretinal gene-therapy delivery, novel MIGS device), collects intraoperative specimens (aqueous/vitreous tap) and video, per study protocol.

tasks.label: Analyze patient's medical history, medication allergies, physical condition, and examination results to verify operation's necessity and to determine best procedure.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Elective degenerative case in outpatient clinic (e.g., knee or hip osteoarthritis): surgeon reviews the referral, history of conservative treatment, weight-bearing radiographs, comorbidities and medication/allergy list, and exam findings (range of motion, alignment, stability) to confirm arthroplasty is indicated and choose implant type/approach versus continued nonoperative care.

Soft-tissue/sports injury consultation (rotator cuff tear, ACL rupture, meniscal tear): surgeon correlates MRI findings with symptoms, activity demands, age, and provocative exam maneuvers, checks anticoagulants and anesthesia-relevant allergies, and decides between repair, reconstruction, debridement, or rehabilitation.

Acute trauma/fracture evaluation in the ED or on inpatient consult: surgeon reads plain films and CT, assesses neurovascular status, open-wound contamination, physiologic stability and anticoagulation status, and determines urgency and fixation strategy (ORIF vs. nail vs. external fixation vs. nonoperative).

Complex, revision, or high-risk case (failed prior arthroplasty, infection workup, tumor, deformity, or patient with severe cardiac/renal disease): surgeon integrates prior operative notes, labs and aspirate results, advanced imaging, implant records, and medical/anesthesia clearance to verify that surgery is warranted and to plan the specific reconstruction.

Same-day pre-operative verification: surgeon re-reviews the chart, consent, updated imaging, NPO and anticoagulation status, allergy list and laterality/site marking immediately before the scheduled procedure to confirm the operation and the chosen technique remain appropriate.

tasks.label: Conduct research to develop and test surgical techniques that can improve operating procedures and outcomes related to musculoskeletal injuries and diseases.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Retrospective/registry outcomes research comparing operative techniques (e.g., two fixation constructs or approaches): defining the question and protocol, IRB submission, chart/imaging/registry data extraction, statistical analysis, interpretation, and manuscript or abstract preparation, done in a hospital or academic department office.

Cadaveric biomechanical study in a university bioskills/biomechanics lab: thawing and dissecting fresh-frozen specimens, performing the index and experimental techniques (e.g., suture-anchor repair, locked plating, ligament reconstruction), potting and mounting specimens, running cyclic loading, load-to-failure or kinematic protocols, then reducing and interpreting the data.

Prospective clinical trial or prospective case series in a hospital OR: enrolling and consenting patients, performing the new or modified technique on live patients with intraoperative data capture (fluoroscopy, navigation logs, timing), managing intraoperative deviations, and collecting follow-up outcome measures in clinic.

Implant/instrument and technique development with an industry partner: iterative prototype trials on synthetic bone models and cadaver specimens in a bioskills or company design lab, refining surgical steps and instrumentation with engineers, and drafting the surgical technique guide.

Translational animal-model study in an accredited vivarium surgical suite (e.g., ovine tendon repair, rabbit bone-healing model): performing the experimental procedure on live animals, post-operative care, timed euthanasia and tissue harvest, and histologic/imaging evaluation.
