sources.claim: The most advanced autonomous surgical robot demonstrated to date performs one step of a single soft-tissue procedure on ex vivo animal tissue, not a whole operation or a whole research study.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous execution of surgical steps. It bounds what surgical autonomy exists today; it is step-level, ex vivo and soft-tissue, and includes no design, execution or interpretation of a research study.

sources.title: THINK surgical TSolution-One (Robodoc) total knee arthroplasty
sources.claim: A commercial orthopedic robot autonomously mills bone to a preoperative CT plan, but only as a tool step inside a surgeon-run procedure (exposure, soft-tissue work, implantation and judgment remain human).
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic bone resection in arthroplasty. Shows machine-controlled bone cutting exists in the OR and in cadaver labs, but only as a preplanned sub-step; it does not develop or evaluate a new technique.

sources.system: 6-DOF robotic knee testbench (industrial arm with force-torque sensor)
sources.title: Validation of a Robotic Testbench for Evaluating Biomechanical Effects of Implant Rotation in Total Knee Arthroplasty on a Cadaveric Specimen
sources.claim: Six-degree-of-freedom robotic testbenches autonomously apply programmed load and motion protocols to mounted cadaveric joints in biomechanics labs; humans still dissect, operate on and mount the specimen and interpret the results.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: mechanical testing of cadaveric constructs, i.e. the measurement step of a cadaveric technique study. Transfer is partial only: the robot applies loads, it does not prepare specimens, perform the surgical technique, or interpret the study.

sources.system: Intelligent minimally invasive fracture reduction robot
sources.developer: orthopedic robotics research group (International Orthopaedics prospective controlled study)
sources.title: Robot-assisted closed reduction of femoral shaft fractures: a prospective controlled study
sources.claim: Orthopedic reduction robots used in patient studies plan autonomously but act under surgeon supervision within a conventional surgeon-led operation, not as independent investigators of a new technique.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robot-assisted fracture reduction performed inside a clinical study. Shows robots participate in OR steps under supervision; it does not show a machine performing a whole operation or conducting the trial.

sources.title: Autonomous 'self-driving' laboratories: a review of technology and policy implications
sources.claim: Closed-loop autonomous laboratories that run the full scientific method exist only in chemistry, materials and molecular-biology workflows built around liquid handling, synthesis and characterization equipment.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: fully automated research cycles. Transfer does NOT hold to surgical-technique research: SDL hardware manipulates vials, plates and reagents, not cadaveric dissection, implant fixation, live-patient operating or animal survival surgery.

sources.system: Orthopedic surgical robotic systems in knee arthroplasty (Mako, ROSA, Navio and similar)
sources.developer: multiple (Frontiers in Bioengineering and Biotechnology review)
sources.title: Orthopedic surgical robotic systems in knee arthroplasty: a comprehensive review
sources.claim: In orthopedic surgery, fully autonomous robotic systems are not accepted or in clinical use; current practice keeps the surgeon in control of the operation.

tasks.label: Diagnose bodily disorders and orthopedic conditions, and provide treatments, such as medicines and surgeries, in clinics, hospital wards, or operating rooms.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Outpatient orthopedic clinic visit: new or follow-up patient with knee/shoulder/hip/back pain. Surgeon takes history, performs hands-on musculoskeletal exam (inspection, palpation, range-of-motion and provocative special tests, neurovascular check), reviews X-ray/MRI, reaches a diagnosis, and prescribes medication, therapy, bracing, or schedules surgery. Exam room in a clinic controlled by the practice.

Office-based procedure during a clinic visit: joint aspiration or corticosteroid/viscosupplement injection (knee, shoulder, trigger finger), landmark- or ultrasound-guided; also cast/splint application or removal, suture removal, wound check. Awake, moving patient on an exam table; sterile prep, needle placement, post-procedure assessment.

Elective operation in a hospital or ASC operating room: total knee or hip arthroplasty, arthroscopic meniscectomy/rotator cuff repair, or spinal decompression/fusion. Surgeon positions and preps the patient, incises, dissects soft tissue, protects neurovascular structures, prepares bone, sizes and implants components, balances soft tissue, achieves hemostasis and closes, adapting to intraoperative findings.

Acute fracture/trauma care in the ED or OR: assess an injured limb, interpret radiographs, perform closed reduction with sedation and splint/cast, or take the patient to the OR for ORIF or intramedullary nailing, including reduction, fluoroscopic confirmation, implant fixation and closure. Time-pressured; patient may be unstable or uncooperative.

Inpatient ward work: post-operative rounds on hospital wards — examine wound and dressing, check neurovascular status and drains, remove drains or staples, assess mobility with therapy staff, adjust analgesia/anticoagulation orders, manage complications such as infection or DVT; multi-bed rooms with staff, visitors, lines and equipment.

sources.title: Learn about robotic-arm assisted knee surgery | Stryker
sources.claim: Stryker's Mako robotic-arm system, widely deployed in US operating rooms for knee and hip arthroplasty, is co-manipulated: the surgeon physically guides the arm to resect bone within a virtual boundary, and the surgeon performs exposure, implantation and closure.

sources.date: 2023-10 (500-case clinical review; system in use since 2020)
sources.title: Intra-operative Safety of an Autonomous Robotic System for Total Knee Replacement: A Review of 500 Cases in India
sources.claim: The CUVIS-joint 'active' robot autonomously mills the femoral and tibial cuts in total knee arthroplasty in clinical use, but only that bone-resection step: the surgeon plans the case, exposes the joint, registers anatomy, holds an override, implants components and closes.
sources.transferJustification: Same task domain (orthopedic surgery in an OR), but autonomy covers only bone milling inside a surgeon-performed operation, so it does not substantiate completing a whole surgical or diagnostic instance.

sources.system: SRT-H (Hierarchical Surgical Robot Transformer) on da Vinci Research Kit
sources.title: SRT-H: A hierarchical framework for autonomous surgery via language-conditioned imitation learning | Science Robotics
sources.claim: The most advanced published autonomous surgery result achieves step-level autonomy on gallbladder removal in ex vivo laboratory tissue with a da Vinci research platform — not a complete operation on a live patient, and not orthopedic.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: soft-tissue laparoscopic surgery. Cited to bound the state of the art — autonomy is per-step, ex vivo and supervised, so it does not transfer to completing an orthopedic operation or clinic episode end to end.

sources.title: Robot-Assisted Autonomous Reduction of a Displaced Pelvic Fracture: A Case Report and Brief Literature Review
sources.claim: A robot performing autonomous closed reduction of a displaced pelvic fracture has been reported in patients, but the robot executes only the reduction manoeuvre within an operation planned, monitored and completed (fixation, imaging, closure) by surgeons.
sources.transferJustification: Same task domain (fracture treatment). Cited to show that even the most autonomous orthopedic robots automate a single manoeuvre under surgeon supervision, not the whole reduction-and-fixation instance.

tasks.label: Diagnose or treat disorders of the musculoskeletal system.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Outpatient orthopedic clinic visit: elicit history, perform hands-on musculoskeletal exam (inspection, palpation for tenderness, passive/active range of motion, provocative maneuvers such as Lachman, McMurray, Neer/Hawkins), review radiographs/MRI, reach a diagnosis and set a management plan with the patient. Clinic exam room, standard exam table, patient cooperative but variable body habitus and pain tolerance.

Office- or ED-based non-operative treatment: sterile prep and landmark/ultrasound-guided corticosteroid or viscosupplement injection of knee/shoulder/hip, joint aspiration, trigger finger or carpal tunnel injection, application or removal of casts and splints, closed reduction of a wrist or shoulder dislocation under local/sedation. Clinic procedure room or ED bay; live patient who moves and guards.

Elective primary total knee or total hip arthroplasty in a hospital OR or ambulatory surgery center: positioning and draping, incision and exposure, bone preparation and resection, soft-tissue balancing, trialing, implant impaction/cementing, hemostasis, layered closure. Sterile field, anesthetized patient, scrub team.

Arthroscopic and soft-tissue procedures in the OR: knee meniscectomy/ACL reconstruction, shoulder rotator cuff repair or subacromial decompression, carpal tunnel release. Portal placement, camera navigation in fluid-distended joint, suture anchor placement and knot tying, closure.

Fracture fixation and spine surgery: ORIF of ankle/wrist/hip fracture, intramedullary nailing of femur or tibia, or lumbar decompression and instrumented fusion. Hospital OR with fluoroscopy; distorted anatomy, bleeding, variable fracture patterns, intraoperative plan changes.

Inpatient and ED consultation and follow-up care: bedside evaluation of admitted or ED patients, postoperative rounds, wound and dressing checks, drain and staple removal, decisions on weight-bearing, DVT prophylaxis and discharge. Hospital ward, ED bay, or clinic follow-up room.

sources.title: Learn about robotic-arm assisted knee surgery | Stryker
sources.claim: Stryker's Mako SmartRobotics, the most widely deployed orthopedic robot for knee and hip arthroplasty, is a hand-guided haptic device: the surgeon physically guides the robotic arm to cut bone, and the robot only constrains the cutting boundary. It performs no step of the operation on its own.

sources.title: Technology in Total Hip Arthroplasty: Recent Advancements | Orthopedic Reviews
sources.claim: THINK Surgical's TSolution One (formerly ROBODOC) is the most autonomous orthopedic robot in clinical use: it autonomously mills the femoral cavity to a CT-based plan. Even so, its autonomy is confined to one bone-cutting sub-step; exposure, acetabular component implantation and all soft-tissue work remain manual.

sources.system: ROBODOC / knee arthroplasty robot class review
sources.developer: multiple (review by Frontiers in Bioengineering and Biotechnology authors)
sources.title: Orthopedic surgical robotic systems in knee arthroplasty: a comprehensive review
sources.claim: A 2025 comprehensive review of orthopedic robotic systems in knee arthroplasty classifies the field into passive, semi-autonomous (surgeon-manipulated) and teleoperated systems, with ROBODOC the lone 'fully autonomous' entry — and its autonomy is bone milling only. No system in clinical use performs a complete arthroplasty.

sources.title: Robotic-Assisted Total Knee Arthroplasty - StatPearls - NCBI Bookshelf
sources.claim: Standard clinical reference on robotic-assisted TKA states plainly that these programmable devices assist rather than replace the surgeon, confirming that no commercial orthopedic robot delivers an accepted arthroplasty end-to-end without the surgeon executing the procedure.

sources.title: Minimally Invasive Robotic Spine Surgery | Globus Medical
sources.claim: Globus Medical's ExcelsiusGPS, a leading spine robot, positions a rigid arm along a planned trajectory; the surgeon then places the screws with hand instruments. Robotic spine surgery is trajectory guidance, not autonomous execution of decompression or fusion.

sources.system: SRT-H (hierarchical autonomous surgery framework on dVRK)
sources.title: SRT-H: A Hierarchical Framework for Autonomous Surgery via Language Conditioned Imitation Learning (arXiv 2505.10251)
sources.claim: The 2025 state of the art in autonomous surgery, SRT-H, achieved fully autonomous execution of a surgical step only on ex vivo pig gallbladders in a laboratory — soft-tissue, non-orthopedic, and not on a live patient. This bounds the frontier well below completing an orthopedic operation.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous execution of a multi-step soft-tissue surgical procedure. Cited to establish the ceiling of demonstrated surgical autonomy; it does not transfer to orthopedic operations, which involve live patients, bone cutting, implant placement and closure rather than ex vivo gallbladder dissection.

sources.system: Ultrasound-guided autonomous percutaneous intervention robot (research prototype)
sources.title: Preliminary Evaluation of an Ultrasound-Guided Robotic System for Autonomous Percutaneous Intervention
sources.claim: For needle procedures analogous to office joint injections, a 2024 review of ultrasound-guided interventional robots states that no such system has validated fully autonomous end-to-end needle ... human involvement; the work presented is a laboratory/phantom demonstration.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: image-guided percutaneous needle placement, the core motor act of a joint injection or aspiration. Cited as a negative bound: even this narrower sub-step lacks a validated autonomous clinical system, so office injection encounters cannot be completed robotically.

sources.system: Long bone fracture reduction robots (RepoRobo and successors)
sources.developer: academic (Univ. Regensburg, Shanghai Jiao Tong and others)
sources.title: Novel Robotic System with Semi-Automatic Planning and Collision Detection for Long Bone Fracture Reduction
sources.claim: Robot-assisted long-bone fracture reduction remains a research area; systems perform reduction under surgeon supervision as an assistive sub-step and are not clinically deployed to complete fracture surgery.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: closed/open reduction of long-bone fractures, a component of both the ED reduction instance and the trauma fixation instance. Cited as a negative bound showing only supervised, assistive sub-step capability.

tasks.label: Direct and coordinate activities of nurses, assistants, specialists, residents, and other medical staff.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

tasks.label: Examine instruments, equipment, and operating room to ensure sterility.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Immediately before incision in a hospital OR: the surgeon confirms sterility of the opened instrument sets on the back table and Mayo stand — internal chemical indicators, rigid container filters/locks, wrapper dryness and absence of holes, correct opening technique — and rejects any suspect set so a replacement can be pulled.

Verification of packaged items entering the field: vendor loaner trays, implants, screws and trials in peel-pouches or rigid containers — checking sterile barrier integrity, expiration/lot labeling, indicator change, and whether an immediate-use steam sterilization cycle was documented.

Intraoperative surveillance of the sterile field: noticing breaks in technique (unsterile contact with drapes or gown, drape displacement, C-arm/microscope draping, dropped or contaminated instrument, glove perforation) and directing removal, re-draping or replacement.

Room-level check at the start of the day or after turnover: verifying the OR was terminally cleaned, no visible soil or dust on lights, booms, tables and floors, equipment covers and cords managed, doors closed and traffic/air handling appropriate before the case starts.

Examination of complex reusable and powered equipment before use — drills, saws, reamers, arthroscopy shavers, cannulated and multi-part instruments — for residual bioburden, moisture, staining, and damage that would compromise sterility.

sources.system: Autonomous instrument tray assembly robotic system (robot arm cell)
sources.developer: University of Louisville / University of Massachusetts research team
sources.title: Towards Autonomous Instrument Tray Assembly for Sterile Processing Applications
sources.claim: Most advanced published robotic sterile-processing cell autonomously sorts and packs surgical instruments into trays, but a human technician still performs the inspection step.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: sterile-processing handling of the same objects (surgical instruments and trays). It bears on this task because it shows that even in a purpose-built robotic cell the cleanliness/sterility inspection decision is still left to a human.

sources.system: Automated surgical instrument assembly and inspection system (pallet conveyor, 6-axis robots, vision stations)
sources.developer: ACA / Addtronics Custom Automation (Missouri Tooling & Automation)
sources.title: Case Study: Surgical Instrument Assembly Automation
sources.claim: A purpose-built automated cell cleans a surgical instrument, inspects it with machine vision for debris and damage, and 6-axis robots automatically sort rejected parts into locked reject bins.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated pass/fail cleanliness and integrity inspection of surgical instruments in a fixtured cell with automatic removal of rejects. Comparable objects and a comparable accept/reject output, but only where the work is presented to the machine.

sources.system: Keyence VS Series and medical packaging vision inspection systems
sources.title: Vision Systems for the Medical Device Manufacturing Industry | KEYENCE America
sources.claim: Inline automated machine-vision systems inspect medical device packaging (sterile barrier seals, labels and date print) on manufacturing lines to confirm package integrity and hence sterility of the packaged device.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: verifying sterile-barrier packaging integrity of medical devices — the same check a surgeon makes on a peel-pouched implant (seal intact, no breach, correct labeling/date), performed on a fixtured production line with automatic rejection.

sources.system: No automated cleanliness/sterility verification system (STERIS commentary)
sources.title: Worth a second look | HPN Online
sources.claim: Industry commentary: no automated method exists to confirm instrument cleanliness and sterility, so human visual inspection remains the quality-assurance backbone, especially for lumened and complex instruments.
sources.transferJustification: Negative/context evidence on the identical verification decision (is this instrument clean and sterile?) that the surgeon makes before use; cited only in support of negative judgments.

sources.title: Robots help fight hospital infections | healthcare-in-europe.com
sources.claim: Mobile UV-C robots navigate and disinfect operating theaters and patient rooms in hospitals, but they emit UV to kill pathogens rather than examine instruments, equipment or the room and certify sterility.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: room-level infection control in the same E2 setting (operating theater). Shows robots operate autonomously in ORs, but disinfection is not the examination/verification output this task requires.

sources.system: Robotic sorters/assemblers and autonomous mobile robots in hospital sterile processing
sources.title: Inside the new sterile frontier: AI and robots take over hospital hygiene | Medical Technology
sources.claim: Hospital sterile-processing automation in commercial use covers washing, robotic sorting/assembly for tray accuracy using imaging and RFID/barcode, and autonomous mobile delivery of sterile supplies; sterility verification of instruments is not among the automated functions described.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated handling and checking of surgical instrument sets in hospital sterile processing. Relevant because it delimits what current hospital robots verify (set completeness, logistics) versus sterility.

tasks.label: Examine patient to obtain information on medical condition and surgical risk.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Outpatient orthopedic clinic exam room: exam of a knee, hip or shoulder for a degenerative or sports condition — gait observation, inspection, palpation for effusion and point tenderness, active/passive range of motion, strength, and provocative stability tests (Lachman, McMurray, impingement), integrated with imaging into a surgical-candidacy and risk judgment.

Outpatient clinic spine or peripheral-nerve focused exam: motor strength grading against resistance, dermatomal sensory testing, deep tendon reflexes, straight-leg raise, Spurling, balance and gait, to localize the lesion and judge operative indication.

Pre-operative risk assessment visit (clinic or pre-admission unit): general examination — cardiopulmonary auscultation, peripheral pulses, skin and soft-tissue condition at the planned incision, airway and frailty assessment — combined with comorbidity review to grade fitness for anesthesia and surgery.

Emergency department or trauma bay: exam of an acutely injured patient in pain, sometimes uncooperative or immobilized — deformity, open wounds, distal pulses and sensation, compartment tenderness, log-roll and secondary survey of other limbs — to decide on urgent operative intervention.

Inpatient bedside exam on rounds or a hospital consult: patient in bed with dressings, drains, drapes and lines; wound/incision inspection, neurovascular check, gentle ROM and tenderness assessment to judge post-op or pre-op status.

sources.system: ProteCT telemedical examination cabin (robotic arms + remote cockpit)
sources.developer: Technical University of Munich / MIRMI (Berlet, Feussner, Wilhelm et al.)
sources.title: Toward telemedical diagnostics—clinical evaluation of a robotic examination system for emergency patients
sources.claim: The ProteCT telemedical examination cabin lets a remote physician perform vital-sign checks, auscultation, percussion and palpation on a patient via robotic arms, but every device is driven by the physician from a remote cockpit (teleoperation, not autonomy).
sources.transferJustification: Directly related: robot-mediated clinical examination of emergency patients. It cannot support a positive judgment because the examination is continuously teleoperated by a physician rather than autonomous.

sources.title: The Reliability of the GNRB® Knee Arthrometer in Measuring ACL Stiffness and Laxity: Implications for Clinical Use and Clinical Trial Design
sources.claim: The GNRB is a commercial motorized arthrometer that performs an automated Lachman-type anterior drawer test with the limb clamped in a rigid fixture, producing laxity/stiffness numbers — one instrumented measurement, not a clinical examination.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: instrumented ligament laxity testing, a sub-step of the knee exam. It cannot substantiate the whole instance: a human positions and straps the limb, and the device yields one number rather than inspection, palpation, ROM, neurovascular assessment and an integrated surgical-risk judgment.

sources.system: Fully autonomous robotic ultrasound system for thyroid scanning
sources.developer: Wu, Wang, Cao et al. (academic group)
sources.title: A fully autonomous robotic ultrasound system for thyroid scanning
sources.claim: A research robotic ultrasound system autonomously scans the thyroid region of a person without human assistance, showing autonomous probe placement and force control on human tissue in a research setting.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous contact with a patient's body for a diagnostic imaging sweep. Transfer is limited to gentle probe contact on a cooperative, positioned subject; it does not cover manual provocative joint testing, painful or injured limbs, or forming a diagnosis and surgical-risk assessment.

sources.system: Collaborative robotic platform for autonomous auscultation
sources.developer: Academic group (published in Applied Sciences, MDPI)
sources.title: Development of a Collaborative Robotic Platform for Autonomous Auscultation
sources.claim: A collaborative robot platform autonomously positions a stethoscope using a 3D point cloud of the patient's torso to capture auscultation sounds, but is explicitly designed only to deliver sounds for a physician to interpret.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous placement of an examination instrument on a patient. It substantiates only a sub-step of a pre-operative general exam and explicitly leaves interpretation and diagnosis to a physician, so it cannot complete the instance.

tasks.label: Follow established surgical techniques during the operation.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Elective primary total knee or total hip arthroplasty in a hospital or ASC operating room: patient positioned and draped, surgical approach through skin/fascia/muscle, capsulotomy, bone resection or reaming (often with a haptic or active robotic platform), soft-tissue balancing, trialing, implant impaction/cementing, hemostasis and layered closure, all per the implant's established technique guide.

Arthroscopic sports-medicine procedure (knee meniscectomy/repair or ACL reconstruction, shoulder rotator cuff or labral repair): portal placement, fluid-distended joint, camera and hand instruments, diagnostic survey, debridement, anchor placement and arthroscopic knot tying or graft harvest/passage/fixation, following the standard stepwise technique.

Fracture trauma surgery, frequently urgent/after-hours: closed or open reduction and internal fixation (ankle, distal radius, hip/femur intramedullary nailing, periarticular plating) with fluoroscopic guidance, variable fracture patterns and soft-tissue injury, reduction maneuvers, provisional K-wires, plate/screw or nail placement per AO technique.

Hand, foot and other minor open procedures in an ASC or outpatient OR under local/regional anesthesia: carpal tunnel or trigger finger release, ganglion excision, bunion/hammertoe correction, tendon repair, hardware removal, manipulation under anesthesia — small structures, tourniquet, standard stepwise technique.

Spine procedure by an orthopedic spine surgeon in a hospital OR: laminectomy/discectomy or instrumented fusion with pedicle screws, often with navigation or a screw-guidance robot; subperiosteal exposure, neural decompression, screw/rod placement, decortication and grafting, closure over drains.

Complex or revision case: revision hip/knee arthroplasty, periprosthetic fracture, tumor resection with reconstruction, or complex deformity correction — distorted anatomy, bone loss, scar tissue, implant removal, intraoperative plan changes while still following the established technique for the chosen reconstruction.

sources.title: The current state of robotics in total knee arthroplasty
sources.claim: TSolution One (formerly ROBODOC), an FDA-cleared active orthopedic robot used clinically, autonomously mills all femoral and tibial bone ... in TKA — but this is one step of the operation; the surgeon performs exposure, registration, soft-tissue balancing, implantation and closure.
sources.transferJustification: Same task family (orthopedic operation) but covers only the bone-resection sub-step; it does not substantiate autonomous completion of a whole arthroplasty, which also requires approach, soft-tissue balancing, implant insertion and closure.

sources.title: THINK Surgical Receives FDA Clearance to Market Active Robot for Total Knee Replacement Procedures in the United States
sources.claim: THINK Surgical's active (autonomous-milling) robot for total knee replacement received US FDA clearance and is commercially marketed, establishing that the autonomous bone-cutting capability is deployed in real hospital operating rooms.
sources.transferJustification: Establishes deployment/maturity of the autonomous milling step only; the cleared indication is bone preparation, not conduct of the whole operation.

sources.system: Mako SmartRobotics / ROSA Knee / CORI (semi-active robotic TKA systems)
sources.title: The current state of robotics in total knee arthroplasty — EFORT Open Reviews
sources.claim: The dominant commercial robotic knee platforms (Mako, ROSA, CORI, etc.) are semi-active: the surgeon physically drives the cutting tool inside haptic boundaries, so the robot does not execute the operation on its own.

sources.system: ROBODOC / TSolution-One in total hip arthroplasty
sources.title: A review of robotic-assisted total hip arthroplasty
sources.claim: Even the active hip/knee robots follow pre-programmed cut paths and cannot make intraoperative adjustments; the limb is rigidly fixed in a holder and the surgeon retains manual stop control and performs all other steps.
sources.transferJustification: Same procedure family (THA); documents that the autonomous portion is pre-programmed milling with the femur fixtured, not adaptive conduct of the operation.

sources.developer: Multiple (systematic review, Johns Hopkins et al.)
sources.title: Levels of autonomy in FDA-cleared surgical robots: a systematic review (npj Digital Medicine)
sources.claim: A systematic review of all FDA-cleared surgical robots found essentially all are at low autonomy levels — 86% at Level 1 (robot assistance) and only 6% reaching Level 3 (conditional autonomy for discrete sub-tasks); none perform whole procedures autonomously.

sources.system: SRT-H (Surgical Robot Transformer–Hierarchy) on da Vinci Research Kit
sources.title: SRT-H: A hierarchical framework for autonomous surgery via language-conditioned imitation learning | Science Robotics
sources.claim: The research frontier in autonomous surgery, SRT-H, autonomously performed the gallbladder-removal phase on eight excised porcine gallbladders in a laboratory bench setup — a soft-tissue sub-procedure on ex vivo tissue, not a complete operation on a patient.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous execution of multi-step surgical technique. It is the strongest published autonomous-surgery result, yet it is soft-tissue general surgery on excised tissue in a lab rig, so it does not transfer to completing an orthopedic operation on a live patient.

sources.system: ArthroCut (VLA policy for robotic bone resection)
sources.developer: Tsinghua University (Lu, Zhang, Chen, Liao et al.)
sources.title: ArthroCut: Autonomous Policy Learning for Robotic Bone Resection in Knee Arthroplasty (arXiv)
sources.claim: The most advanced published autonomous orthopedic cutting policy, ArthroCut, executes multi-plane knee resections only on a bench-top plastic knee prosthesis, with 86% average success — below clinical acceptability and covering only the resection step.
sources.transferJustification: Directly relevant sub-step (bone cutting in knee arthroplasty), but performed on a bench-top model, not on a patient, and only for resection — no exposure, balancing, implantation or closure.

sources.system: Intelligent fracture reduction robot (pelvic/femoral closed reduction)
sources.title: Robot-assisted closed reduction of femoral shaft fractures: a prospective controlled study (International Orthopaedics)
sources.claim: An intelligent fracture-reduction robot developed with Beijing Jishuitan Hospital can perform autonomous closed reduction of femoral shaft/pelvic fractures intraoperatively; the surgeon still performs the fixation (intramedullary nailing) and all other steps.
sources.transferJustification: Same instance family (fracture surgery); demonstrates autonomy only for the reduction maneuver in a 15-patient study, with the surgeon performing nailing, imaging judgment and closure.

tasks.label: Manage surgery services, including planning, scheduling and coordination, determination of procedures, or procurement of supplies and equipment.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

tasks.label: Operate on patient's musculoskeletal system to correct deformities, repair injuries, prevent and treat diseases, or improve or restore patient's functions.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Elective primary total knee or total hip arthroplasty in a hospital OR or ambulatory surgery center: positioning and draping, incision and exposure through capsule and soft tissue, bone resection/reaming, trialing and soft-tissue/ligament balancing, cementing or press-fitting implants, hemostasis, and layered closure, with intraoperative decisions on sizing and alignment.

Arthroscopic sports-medicine procedure (knee meniscectomy/repair, ACL reconstruction, shoulder rotator cuff repair or labral repair) in an ASC or hospital OR: portal placement, diagnostic arthroscopy, debridement/resection, graft harvest and tunnel drilling or anchor placement and suture tying, all inside a fluid-distended joint on deformable tissue.

Acute fracture care in a hospital OR, often after hours and semi-urgent: closed or open reduction of a distal radius, ankle, hip or femur fracture; intramedullary nailing or plate-and-screw fixation under fluoroscopy, with contaminated or comminuted bone, bleeding, and improvised reduction maneuvers.

Smaller extremity procedures in an ASC or hospital OR: carpal tunnel or trigger finger release, tendon or nerve repair, ganglion excision, bunion correction, hardware removal, Achilles repair — short cases, small incisions, delicate soft tissue dissection near nerves and vessels, and fine suture closure.

Complex/major reconstruction in a hospital OR: lumbar decompression and instrumented fusion, revision hip or knee arthroplasty, periprosthetic fracture, bone tumor resection with reconstruction, or debridement for prosthetic joint infection — long cases with distorted anatomy, scar tissue, bone loss, and improvisation.

sources.system: FDA-cleared surgical robots (49 systems incl. da Vinci, Mako, TSolution One)
sources.developer: Multiple (reviewed by Mount Sinai / Icahn School of Medicine)
sources.title: Levels of autonomy in FDA-cleared surgical robots: a systematic review (npj Digital Medicine)
sources.claim: Systematic review of FDA-cleared surgical robots finds the overwhelming majority operate under continuous surgeon control, the most advanced reach only conditional autonomy for a single sub-task (e.g., bone milling), and none perform whole procedures autonomously.

sources.title: The current state of robotics in total knee arthroplasty (PMC)
sources.claim: The most autonomous commercial orthopedic robot autonomously mills the femoral and tibial bone cuts in total knee arthroplasty under surgeon supervision, but only that sub-step; exposure, soft-tissue balancing, implant insertion and closure remain surgeon work.
sources.transferJustification: Related sub-task (autonomous bone resection within TKA); cited to bound how much of the operation machines actually execute.

sources.title: Monogram robot marks autonomy milestone; Stereotaxis catheter cleared (MedTech Dive)
sources.claim: First 'fully autonomous' saw-based robotic ... bone cutting was performed on a living patient in a hospital OR in India in July 2025 as part of a 102-patient clinical trial; the FDA cleared the system as semi-autonomous, and the robot executes the resections, not the whole operation.
sources.transferJustification: Related sub-task (autonomous bone resection during TKA in a hospital OR); shows the current autonomy frontier stops well short of a complete arthroplasty.

sources.title: Robotic-assisted total knee arthroplasty with MAKO is associated with improved functional outcomes (Bone & Joint Open)
sources.claim: The market-leading orthopedic robot for knee and hip arthroplasty is a hand-guided haptic arm under continuous surgeon control, not an autonomous system.

sources.title: Advancing spine surgery: Evaluating the potential for full robotic automation (ScienceDirect)
sources.claim: Commercial spine surgery robots provide trajectory guidance for screw placement but lack autonomy; full robotic automation of spine surgery remains prospective.

sources.system: SRT-H (Surgical Robot Transformer - Hierarchy) on a da Vinci Research Kit
sources.title: SRT-H: A hierarchical framework for autonomous surgery via language-conditioned imitation learning (Science Robotics)
sources.claim: The research frontier in autonomous surgery achieves step-level autonomy on soft tissue in ex-vivo animal specimens, not complete operations on live human patients.
sources.transferJustification: Related task (autonomous soft-tissue laparoscopic surgery): cited to bound the state of the art — autonomy is demonstrated only for isolated steps on ex-vivo animal tissue, so it does not transfer to whole musculoskeletal operations on patients.

sources.title: An Arthroscopic Robotic System for Meniscoplasty with Autonomous Operation Ability (PMC)
sources.claim: Autonomous arthroscopic orthopedic robotics exists only as a laboratory prototype: a meniscoplasty robot that autonomously plans and executes a resection path was validated in bench experiments, not in patients.
sources.transferJustification: Related task (autonomous arthroscopic meniscus resection); cited because it is the closest system to instance 1 and is confined to bench validation, so it cannot complete the clinical instance.

tasks.label: Provide consultation and surgical assistance to other physicians and surgeons.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Inpatient/ED consultation: the orthopedic surgeon is paged by an ED physician or hospitalist to evaluate a patient with a fracture, dislocation, septic joint, or postoperative musculoskeletal problem. At the bedside the surgeon reviews imaging, palpates the limb, checks neurovascular status and range of motion, then communicates a plan to the requesting physician and often performs a bedside procedure (splint/cast application, closed reduction with sedation, joint aspiration) on an unfixtured, sometimes agitated or obese patient in a crowded bay.

Scrubbing in as assistant/co-surgeon on another surgeon's case in a hospital OR: e.g., assisting a neurosurgeon on a spine exposure, a trauma or oncologic surgeon on a limb-threatening injury or tumor resection, or a partner on a revision arthroplasty. Work includes patient positioning and limb traction, retraction and soft-tissue exposure, fracture reduction under fluoroscopy, hardware handling, suction/hemostasis, and closure, in a bloody, deformable field with case-specific anatomy.

Outpatient specialty consultation on referral from primary care, rheumatology, or another surgeon: history, hands-on joint and gait examination (palpation, stability and provocative tests, range of motion), review of radiographs/MRI, sometimes an in-office aspiration or corticosteroid injection, then a written opinion and recommendation returned to the referring physician in a clinic exam room.

Purely informational consultation: curbside phone call, e-consult, or tele-review of imaging and labs for another physician (e.g., advising a hospitalist on weight-bearing status or an ED doctor on whether transfer is needed), with no physical contact with the patient, done from an office or workroom.

Urgent intraoperative consultation: called mid-case into another surgeon's OR for an unexpected musculoskeletal problem (iatrogenic periprosthetic or acetabular fracture, bone involvement requiring resection/fixation, hardware failure), scrubs in on short notice, assesses the exposed anatomy directly, and performs or directs the orthopedic portion of the operation.

sources.title: Robot performs first realistic surgery without human help – Johns Hopkins Malone Center
sources.claim: State of the art in autonomous surgical execution: the SRT-H system autonomously performed a phase of gallbladder removal on ex vivo pig tissue in a laboratory, learning from videos of surgeons; it is a research proof of concept, not a system that assists a surgeon through a whole operation on human patients.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous execution of one phase of a soft-tissue operation. It bounds what autonomy exists for intraoperative work; it does not transfer to serving as a surgical assistant/co-surgeon (positioning, exposure, retraction, reduction, closure) on live human anatomy.

sources.system: FDA-cleared surgical robots (49 systems, e.g., da Vinci, Mako, ROSA)
sources.title: Levels of autonomy in FDA-cleared surgical robots: a systematic review (npj Digital Medicine)
sources.claim: Systematic review of all 49 FDA-cleared surgical robots found the overwhelming majority provide only robot assistance under continuous surgeon control; none reach high or full autonomy.
sources.transferJustification: Covers the entire commercial surgical-robot field, including orthopedic platforms, establishing that no cleared system operates a case with limited intervention.

sources.system: TSolution One Total Knee Application (formerly ROBODOC)
sources.title: THINK Surgical Receives FDA Clearance of Second-Generation Active Robot – Ortho Spine News
sources.claim: An FDA-cleared orthopedic 'active' robot autonomously mills bone to a preoperative plan in a hospital operating room, but only for that bone-preparation step of a knee or hip replacement performed by the surgeon.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous bone cutting inside a fixtured limb in an OR. It is the strongest autonomous orthopedic capability in clinical use, yet it executes one planned sub-step and cannot examine a patient, judge a plan, or assist another surgeon through a case.

sources.title: MAKO Robotic Systems (Stryker) – Liv Hospital
sources.claim: The most widely used orthopedic robotic platform is hand-guided: the surgeon moves the instrument and the robot only constrains the cut, so it is not autonomous.
sources.transferJustification: Directly describes the dominant orthopedic OR robot; shows the intraoperative robotic capability available to orthopedic surgeons requires continuous human control.

sources.system: Intelligent minimally invasive fracture reduction robot / orthopaedic surgical navigation system
sources.developer: Beijing Jishuitan Hospital team (Wu Xinbao et al.)
sources.title: Robot-assisted closed reduction of femoral shaft fractures: a prospective controlled study (International Orthopaedics)
sources.claim: A fracture-reduction robot performed the reduction manoeuvre along a planned path in human femoral shaft fracture surgery in an operating room, with the surgeon planning, supervising, and performing the rest of the operation (incision, nailing, fixation).
sources.transferJustification: Related task: closed fracture reduction, a manoeuvre an orthopedic consultant performs at the bedside or when assisting another surgeon. Only the traction/alignment step is machine-executed after surgeon planning; assessment, anaesthesia, imaging interpretation and fixation remain human.

sources.title: RoboNurse-VLA: Robotic Scrub Nurse System based on Vision-Language-Action Model (arXiv)
sources.claim: Research robotic scrub nurse systems can autonomously grasp and hand surgical instruments on voice command, demonstrated in a laboratory setting rather than a live operating room.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: non-sterile-field OR assistance (instrument handover). Even this narrowest form of surgical assistance is only a lab demonstration, and it involves rigid tools rather than patient-side assisting on living tissue.

tasks.label: Conduct research to develop and test surgical techniques that can improve operating procedures and outcomes.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: IRB-approved prospective clinical study of a technique modification (e.g., a modified thoracoscopic repair of esophageal atresia or a change in ostomy closure technique): the pediatric surgeon performs the study technique on enrolled infants/children in the children's hospital OR, records intraoperative metrics (time, blood loss, conversions), and follows post-op outcomes over months.

Retrospective / registry-based outcomes research on an operative technique (NSQIP-Pediatric, institutional chart and operative-video review): defining variables, abstracting records, reviewing recorded operative video for technical steps, statistical analysis, and manuscript/abstract preparation in the office and conference room.

Preclinical large-animal work in the institutional animal surgical suite/vivarium: developing and testing a new technique or device in a porcine, rabbit, or fetal-lamb model (anesthesia, survival surgery, serial imaging, necropsy and histology), with veterinary staff and IACUC oversight.

Ex vivo / bench / simulation lab testing of candidate technique variants: suturing or anastomosis trials on phantom bowel, ex vivo porcine tissue, or 3D-printed neonatal models; measuring leak/burst pressure, suture spacing, task time and error; iterating the technique with residents and engineers.

Translational device/technique feasibility work with engineers and industry: benchtop prototype iteration followed by first-in-human or early feasibility use of the new instrument or approach on selected pediatric patients in the OR, with intraoperative data capture and regulatory/safety documentation.

sources.title: Johns Hopkins teaches robot to perform a gallbladder removal on a realistic patient - The Robot Report
sources.claim: The SRT-H system autonomously executed a lengthy phase of a ... on ex vivo pig tissue mounted in a lifelike patient model, responding to occasional spoken corrections from the research team. This is the current frontier of autonomous surgical execution — a single, pre-trained procedure phase in a lab setting, not the design or evaluation of a new technique.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: performing a surgical step. It bears on the physical execution sub-step of surgical-technique research (animal/ex vivo testing), but the system executes a technique its human developers specified; it does not formulate, vary, measure, or evaluate a technique.

sources.developer: Johns Hopkins University / Children's National (Sheikh Zayed Institute for Pediatric Surgical Innovation)
sources.title: Smart Tissue Autonomous Robot performs laparoscopic surgery on pig soft tissue without human help
sources.claim: STAR autonomously performed laparoscopic small-bowel anastomosis in four live pigs, outperforming manual comparison groups, in a highly controlled animal-lab setting using specially marked tissue and a predetermined plan.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: preclinical animal surgery. It shows a robot can execute one fixed suturing technique in an animal lab, but the surrounding research episode (protocol, anesthesia, model creation, outcome measurement, necropsy, analysis) was performed by human investigators.

sources.developer: Sheikh Zayed Institute for Pediatric Surgical Innovation, Children's National Health System
sources.title: Supervised Autonomous Robotic Soft-Tissue Surgery Demonstrated | GlobalSpec
sources.claim: An earlier STAR study run by pediatric surgical researchers performed autonomous in vivo intestinal anastomosis in four surviving pigs; the robot was the object of the study, while the human investigators designed the protocol, prepared the models, and evaluated the outcomes.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: preclinical technique-testing surgery in a pediatric surgical research institute. Directly comparable objects and setting to the animal-lab instance, but it substantiates only robotic execution of a human-designed technique, not conduct of the research.

sources.title: Breaking Barriers in Robotic Soft Tissue Surgery: Conditional Autonomous Intestinal Anastomosis (arXiv:2107.01288)
sources.claim: In the ex vivo bench testbed, STAR performed conditional-autonomous anastomosis on phantom bowel tissue as one arm of a human-designed comparison against manual laparoscopy and da Vinci teleoperation; specimen preparation, tissue orientation setting, and the outcome measurements were done by the human researchers.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: bench/ex vivo trial execution. Same objects (phantom bowel, sutures) and fixtured lab testbed as the bench-testing instance, but the robot supplies only the operative arm of an experiment that humans conceived, prepared, measured and analyzed.

sources.developer: Johns Hopkins; Shanghai MedBot; Institute of Automation, Chinese Academy of Sciences
sources.title: No Hands on Deck: The Dawn of Fully Autonomous Surgery
sources.claim: As of early 2026, autonomous surgical robotics remains confined to ex vivo organs and live-animal proof-of-concept work (SRT-H, MedBot's Toumai/Neuron pig cholecystectomy, ARISE intraocular injections); no system operates autonomously on human patients, and none is cleared for it.
sources.transferJustification: Establishes the ceiling for the clinical instances: autonomous operation on live human patients (let alone neonates and children enrolled in a technique trial) has not been demonstrated or approved anywhere.

sources.title: Autonomous 'self-driving' laboratories: a review of technology and policy (R. Soc. Open Sci.)
sources.claim: Self-driving laboratories close the hypothesis–experiment–analysis loop autonomously, but only in chemistry, materials science and liquid-handling biology workflows.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous experimentation. Transfer does NOT hold — SDLs handle vials, plates and reagents on fixed benches, not living tissue, anesthetized animals, or child patients, and no SDL has been shown to design or evaluate a surgical technique. Cited only to bound the negative judgments.

tasks.label: Examine fetuses, infants, children, and adolescents, and diagnose health issues to determine need for intervention, such as surgery.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Outpatient pediatric surgery clinic: surgeon inspects and palpates a child (inguinal hernia, hydrocele, undescended testis, umbilical hernia, neck or abdominal mass), examines a squirming or crying toddler with a parent holding them, takes history from parent, correlates with prior imaging, and decides whether operative repair is indicated and when.

Emergency department or inpatient surgical consult on a child or adolescent with acute abdominal pain or blunt trauma: serial abdominal exam for guarding/rebound, exam of an anxious or uncooperative patient, integration of labs and CT/ultrasound, decision for appendectomy, operative exploration, or observation.

NICU examination of a premature or newborn infant in an incubator/on a ventilator (suspected necrotizing enterocolitis, malrotation, esophageal atresia, gastroschisis, congenital diaphragmatic hernia): gentle exam of a fragile, lines-and-tubes-covered neonate, assessment of abdominal wall, perfusion and stability, with radiographs, deciding on urgent operation or drain placement.

Inpatient ward or post-operative rounds: examining a recovering child's wound, stoma, drains and abdomen to detect leak, abscess, obstruction or wound infection and determine whether reoperation, drainage or non-operative management is needed.

Fetal care center prenatal consultation: reviewing or performing/directing fetal ultrasound and fetal MRI for an anomaly (CDH, myelomeningocele, sacrococcygeal teratoma, CPAM), assessing severity with maternal-fetal medicine, and determining candidacy for fetal intervention or postnatal surgery.

sources.developer: Technical University of Munich / University Hospital rechts der Isar (MITI Research Group)
sources.title: Toward telemedical diagnostics—clinical evaluation of a robotic examination system for emergency patients
sources.claim: ProteCT is a robotic tele-examination cabin that lets a remote physician perform auscultation, percussion and palpation with force feedback on emergency-department patients; it was evaluated on adults and is operated continuously by the remote clinician, not autonomously.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robot-mediated adult physical examination in an ED. It is the closest system to physical examination of a patient, but the examining intelligence is a continuously teleoperating human physician, so under the autonomy rule it cannot support a positive judgment for autonomous pediatric examination and surgical decision-making.

sources.system: Autonomous lightweight liver ultrasound robot (588 g cable-driven robot + AI agent)
sources.developer: Tsinghua University / Beijing Tsinghua Changgung Hospital
sources.title: Beyond hospital reach: Autonomous lightweight ultrasound robot for liver sonography
sources.claim: An autonomous cable-driven ultrasound robot acquires standard liver ultrasound planes and detects pathology on adult subjects, deployed in a hospital ultrasound department; it performs image acquisition only, not clinical examination, history integration or a surgical-intervention decision.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous diagnostic imaging of the adult abdomen in a hospital imaging suite. Transfer to this task fails: subjects are cooperative relaxed adults, the robot obtains images rather than performing inspection/palpation of a child, and no surgical-need determination is produced.

sources.system: Fully autonomous robotic thyroid ultrasound system
sources.developer: Tsinghua University (Department of Automation) and collaborators
sources.title: A fully autonomous robotic ultrasound system for thyroid scanning
sources.claim: A fully autonomous robotic ultrasound ... scans the thyroid region of adult subjects without human assistance and flags malignant nodules, showing autonomous scanning plus classification is limited to a single narrow imaging exam of a cooperative adult.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous imaging-based screening of one organ in adults. It does not transfer to examining infants and children and deciding on surgery, which requires hands-on inspection and palpation of uncooperative pediatric patients, history from caregivers, and an operative judgment across many possible diagnoses.

tasks.label: Examine instruments, equipment, and operating room to ensure sterility.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Pre-incision check of the sterile setup in a children's hospital OR: after the scrub team opens and arranges trays for a pediatric case, the surgeon reviews the back table and Mayo stand, confirms wrappers/rigid containers were intact and sterilization indicators changed, that drapes and the sterile field are correctly established, and calls for re-processing of anything questionable before starting.

At the point of use during a case: the surgeon examines an individual instrument handed up (neonatal fine forceps, micro needle holder, laparoscope/optic, bipolar tip) for residual debris or bioburden, moisture, corrosion, misalignment or malfunction, and rejects and replaces it if suspect.

Checking sterile-packaged items before they are opened onto the field: peel-packed implants, sutures, single-use devices, endoscopic accessories — verifying seal/barrier integrity, no punctures or wetness, indicator changed, item within date, then accepting or discarding.

Intraoperative surveillance of the room and team for sterility breaches: draped equipment (C-arm, operating microscope, laparoscopic tower, robotic arms, light handles), gowned personnel brushing non-sterile surfaces, items dropped below field level, door traffic and airflow; the surgeon calls out breaches and directs correction.

Sterility check outside the main OR: a bedside NICU procedure, PICU or ED/trauma-bay procedure, where the surgeon inspects a smaller improvised setup (portable tray, prep, drapes, limited assistants and space) and judges whether it is adequately sterile to proceed.

sources.system: RIF Robotics PacR robotic tray assembly work-cell
sources.title: RIF Robotics Corp | Southeast Venture Showcase
sources.claim: RIF Robotics' PacR is an enclosed robotic work-cell (6-DOF arm plus cameras) that autonomously identifies surgical instruments, distinguishes visually similar instruments by close-up inspection, and picks and places them to assemble trays; it has been piloted in Wellstar hospital sterile processing departments. Its demonstrated output is instrument identity and tray assembly, not a sterility/cleanliness verdict.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated handling and close-up machine examination of the same objects (surgical instruments) the pediatric surgeon inspects; cited to show what machine examination of instruments currently delivers (identity/placement), and that a cleanliness or sterility verdict is not among its demonstrated outputs.

sources.system: RIF Robotics robotic tray assembly system (Wellstar Windy Hill pilot)
sources.developer: RIF Robotics Corp. / Catalyst by Wellstar
sources.title: RIF Robotics pioneers autonomous surgical tray assembly - Catalyst by Wellstar
sources.claim: As of the Wellstar pilot write-up, RIF's system still requires a human technician to inspect each instrument for bioburden and functionality; automatic bioburden inspection was described as a forthcoming feature rather than a demonstrated one.
sources.transferJustification: Same related task (sterile-processing instrument inspection); establishes that the cleanliness/sterility judgment remains human even in the most advanced deployed instrument-handling robot cell, so it cannot support a positive judgment for instrument sterility checks.

sources.system: Autonomous instrument tray assembly system (Staubli TX2-60L cell)
sources.developer: University of Louisville / UMass (Sankaranarayanan, Chitalia et al.)
sources.title: Towards Autonomous Instrument Tray Assembly for Sterile Processing Applications (arXiv:2602.01679)
sources.claim: A fully automated laboratory robotic cell (6-DOF Staubli TX2-60L with a dual electromagnetic gripper, calibrated vision, YOLO12 + ResNet perception) autonomously sorts surgical instruments and packs them into sterile trays with 3D-printed fixtures, evaluated against human-assembled trays. It automates assembly, not inspection for sterility.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous machine handling and perception of surgical instruments in a purpose-built cell. Cited to bound what E1 instrument-handling robots do today — identification, sorting and packing — with no sterility or bioburden verdict.

sources.title: Vision system inspects seal quality on flexible packaging | Vision Systems Design
sources.claim: DWFritz Automation's ASI system performs 100% inline inspection of sterile-barrier medical device packages on a production line: an automated conveyor and a gantry-mounted vacuum chuck pick up and move each package over nine-camera optical arrays, detecting seal defects below 50 microns so that sterile products remain sterile; it runs integrated into a customer production line under PLC control.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: verifying that a sterile barrier package containing surgical devices is intact and the contents can be presumed sterile — the same accept/reject judgment the surgeon makes on a peel-packed item, on the same class of packaging, at finer precision (<50 micron defects) with machine handling and automatic rejection.

tasks.label: Examine patient to obtain information on medical condition and surgical risk.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Outpatient pediatric surgery clinic: preoperative consultation for an elective problem (inguinal hernia, hydrocele, undescended testis, pilonidal disease). Surgeon inspects, palpates the groin/abdomen/scrotum, checks for reducibility, listens to heart and lungs, assesses growth, airway and comorbidity, with an often crying or squirming child and a parent present, then judges operability and anesthetic risk.

Emergency department or urgent inpatient consult for a possible acute surgical abdomen or trauma: surgeon palpates for localized tenderness, guarding, rebound and masses, examines wounds and perfusion, repeats exam over hours in a distressed, uncooperative or nonverbal child, and decides urgency and operative risk.

NICU/PICU bedside evaluation of a premature or newborn infant in an incubator amid lines, tubes and monitors: inspection of abdominal wall and stoma, gentle palpation for distension/tenderness, auscultation of bowel sounds, assessment of anomalies (gastroschisis, NEC, atresia) and physiologic stability for surgery.

Day-of-surgery reassessment in the pre-op holding area or operating room, including exam under anesthesia: confirming anatomy and side/site, re-examining a mass or anorectal/genital anatomy, airway and cardiopulmonary check, final surgical-risk determination before incision.

Postoperative ward or follow-up clinic exam: inspecting incisions, drains and dressings, palpating the abdomen for distension or collection, checking bowel function and perfusion, to determine complications and the risk of reoperation.

sources.system: Fully autonomous robotic ultrasound system for thyroid scanning (Su et al.)
sources.developer: Shenyang Institute of Automation / Chinese Academy of Sciences collaborators
sources.title: A fully autonomous robotic ultrasound system for thyroid scanning | Nature Communications
sources.claim: A fully autonomous robotic ultrasound arm can scan the thyroid region of human subjects without human assistance and flag malignant nodules — a narrow imaging sub-step on a cooperative, seated adult, not a whole clinical examination or surgical-risk assessment.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: diagnostic ultrasound scanning of a patient's neck. It is the closest robotic analogue to hands-on patient examination, but it covers only image acquisition on a cooperative adult and does not perform inspection, palpation for tenderness, auscultation, or the clinical judgment of operability that the pediatric surgeon's exam requires.

sources.title: Remote robotic ultrasound in children: now a reality - AdEchoTech
sources.claim: The only robotic system routinely used to examine children physically, MELODY tele-echography, is remotely operated by a clinician holding a probe-shaped controller; the robot itself makes no examination decisions.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robot-mediated ultrasound examination of pediatric patients in a clinic. It shows the pediatric examination setting is reachable by a robot arm, but the clinical act is entirely teleoperated, so it cannot support an autonomous positive judgment.

sources.system: Dr. Spot (Boston Dynamics Spot with contactless vital-sign sensing)
sources.developer: MIT / Brigham and Women's Hospital / Boston Dynamics
sources.title: Mobile Robotic Platform for Contactless Vital Sign Monitoring - PMC
sources.claim: Hospital mobile robots used for patient assessment (Dr. Spot at Brigham and Women's ED) only take contactless vital signs and relay telemedicine video, and are driven by clinical staff.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic bedside patient assessment in an emergency department. It demonstrates only remote vital-sign capture under human teleoperation, with no touch-based examination or risk judgment, so it does not transfer to the surgeon's examination.

tasks.label: Follow established surgical techniques during the operation.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Common minimally invasive pediatric general surgery in a children's hospital OR: laparoscopic appendectomy, inguinal hernia repair, cholecystectomy, pyloromyotomy, fundoplication in a child or infant. The surgeon executes the standard stepwise technique — port placement, exposure, dissection of planes, ligation/division, closure — adapting to variant anatomy, bleeding, and adhesions, with an anesthetized patient and a scrub team.

Open neonatal/infant reconstruction for congenital anomalies: esophageal atresia/TEF repair, congenital diaphragmatic hernia repair, gastroschisis/omphalocele closure, Hirschsprung pull-through, anorectal malformation repair. Millimeter-scale, friable tissue in a 2-4 kg neonate; fine suturing of anastomoses per established technique, in an OR adjoining the NICU.

Complex elective oncologic and thoracic operations: Wilms tumor nephrectomy, neuroblastoma resection off great vessels, lung lobectomy for CPAM, mediastinal mass excision, Nuss bar placement for pectus excavatum — following the standard oncologic/technical steps (node sampling, vessel control, specimen extraction) over several hours.

Emergency or urgent operations: perforated appendicitis with abscess, malrotation with midgut volvulus (Ladd procedure), incarcerated hernia, necrotizing enterocolitis laparotomy, blunt/penetrating abdominal trauma. Distorted anatomy, contamination, active bleeding, and time pressure while still adhering to established technique.

Minor/adjunct operative procedures done by the pediatric surgeon in the OR or at the bedside: tunneled central venous catheter or port placement, gastrostomy tube placement, lymph node or mass biopsy, abscess drainage, circumcision, foreign-body retrieval — short, protocolized, but performed on small, unfixtured, moving pediatric anatomy.

Fetal and perinatal interventions: fetoscopic laser for twin-twin transfusion, fetoscopic or open myelomeningocele repair, EXIT procedure — performed on a fetus through the gravid uterus with ultrasound/fetoscopic guidance, following a tightly defined established technique under maternal anesthesia.

sources.system: SRT-H (Surgical Robot Transformer - Hierarchy), on a da Vinci Research Kit
sources.title: Johns Hopkins' AI-powered, voice-controlled robot performs autonomous surgery
sources.claim: The most advanced autonomous surgical demonstration to date, Johns Hopkins' SRT-H, autonomously performed the dissection phase of gallbladder removal on eight ex vivo (dead) pig gallbladders in a lab rig — a step of one operation on adult-sized excised tissue, not a whole operation on a living patient.
sources.transferJustification: Cholecystectomy dissection is the closest published analogue to 'following established surgical technique' autonomously. Transfer to the rated task fails: the work was on excised adult porcine tissue in a bench setup, covered a phase rather than an accepted end-to-end operation, and involved no live physiology, bleeding control, closure, or pediatric-scale anatomy.

sources.title: Smart Tissue Autonomous Robot performs laparoscopic surgery on pig soft tissue without human help
sources.claim: The earlier STAR system autonomously performed a laparoscopic small-bowel anastomosis in live pigs, but only with pre-placed fluorescent tissue markers and a predetermined plan, under human supervision — a single suturing task inside a research animal-lab operating suite.
sources.transferJustification: Bowel anastomosis is a core step of neonatal and general pediatric operations, so it is the most relevant related task. It nonetheless substantiates only one sub-step, in a marked and pre-planned animal-lab preparation, and not completion of any operation.

sources.system: Toumai robot with Neuron multimodal surgical model
sources.title: AI surgery: Chinese robot conducts complex operation on pig without human intervention
sources.claim: The furthest reported autonomous execution of a multi-step operation is MicroPort MedBot's Toumai/Neuron performing biliary surgery on a 30 kg live pig in a company animal lab, completing 88% of steps on the first attempt with supervising surgeons correcting the remainder; the company states it does not imply safety or efficacy in humans.
sources.transferJustification: Biliary surgery on a live large animal is the nearest analogue to following established technique through a whole operation. Transfer fails: 12% of steps needed human correction, the subject was an adult-sized pig rather than a child, and the developer disclaims human applicability.

sources.system: 49 FDA-cleared surgical robots (incl. da Vinci, Mako, ROSA, Monarch)
sources.developer: various (review by Icahn School of Medicine at Mount Sinai)
sources.title: Levels of autonomy in FDA-cleared surgical robots: a systematic review
sources.claim: A systematic review of all FDA-cleared surgical robots (2015-2023) found that no cleared clinical surgical robot exceeds conditional autonomy; the overwhelming majority merely assist a surgeon who directs every action.

sources.system: da Vinci Xi / Si robotic surgical system in pediatric practice
sources.title: Seven years of pediatric robotic-assisted surgery: insights from 105 procedures
sources.claim: Clinical pediatric robotic surgery is entirely teleoperated: children undergo procedures with a surgeon driving a da Vinci console, and platform size limits restrict use in infants and neonates.

sources.system: da Vinci surgical system (pediatric application review)
sources.title: Application and prospects of robotic surgery in children: a scoping review
sources.claim: Reviews of robotic surgery in children note that instrument size and port-spacing requirements limit robotic platforms in infants, the population in which much pediatric surgery is performed.
