automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

tasks.label: Interpret results of preoperative tests and physical examinations.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

tasks.label: Manage surgery services, including planning, scheduling and coordination, determination of procedures, or procurement of supplies and equipment.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

tasks.label: Monitor patient's recovery, making follow-up visits and using postoperative assessment techniques, such as blood and imaging tests.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Daily inpatient postoperative rounds on a pediatric surgical ward: bedside visit to a child 1-5 days after appendectomy or other abdominal surgery — take down the dressing and inspect the incision, palpate the abdomen, auscultate for bowel sounds, inspect drain/NG/ostomy output, assess pain and mobilization, review overnight vitals and CBC/CMP in the chart, order or interpret repeat labs or an ultrasound/CT, adjust the plan (feeds, antibiotics, drain removal, discharge), and brief the family and nursing staff.

Outpatient clinic follow-up 2-6 weeks post-op (hernia repair, orchiopexy, pyloromyotomy, laparoscopic appendectomy) in a pediatric surgery clinic exam room: an often frightened, squirming toddler or a modest adolescent on a parent's lap or the table — inspect and gently palpate the incision for seroma/infection/recurrence, remove steri-strips or remaining sutures, check testis position or scar quality, review or order an ultrasound/labs, counsel the family, and document/close the episode of care.

NICU/PICU follow-up of a neonate after complex surgery (gastroschisis silo, congenital diaphragmatic hernia, TEF repair, NEC laparotomy): examine a fragile intubated 2 kg infant surrounded by lines, tubes and monitors — assess abdominal distension and stoma/wound, check drain and gastric output, review serial chest/abdominal radiographs, contrast studies and blood gases, and coordinate with neonatology on feeds, ventilation and next imaging.

Hands-on bedside/clinic follow-up procedures done as part of the recovery assessment: removing a Penrose or JP drain, changing or packing a wound dressing, opening and probing a superficial wound infection, assessing and troubleshooting a gastrostomy tube site, or removing staples — performed on a moving, often crying child with a parent present.

Remote/asynchronous postoperative monitoring: reviewing returned blood work and imaging reports in the EMR, comparing with the operative course, a telephone or video check-in with the family, reviewing parent-sent wound photos, and deciding whether the child needs to be seen, re-imaged, or admitted.

sources.title: Vitestro unveils Aletta robotic phlebotomy device – CAP TODAY
sources.claim: Vitestro's Aletta is a CE-marked, commercially launched autonomous robotic phlebotomy device that performs the complete venous blood draw on (adult) patients in hospitals and laboratories, with one supervisor overseeing multiple devices; it covers only the blood-collection step, not a surgeon's postoperative assessment, and is not used on infants or small children.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: obtaining a blood specimen, one input to the 'blood tests' element of postoperative monitoring. It is cited to show the state of the art on the closest automatable sub-step; it does not cover physical examination of a post-op child, interpretation, or the care decision that constitutes the instance, and it operates on cooperative adult arms fixtured in an armrest.

sources.developer: Lin et al., academic group (Frontiers in Robotics and AI)
sources.title: Autonomous robotic ultrasound scanning system: a key to enhancing image analysis reproducibility and observer consistency in ultrasound imaging
sources.claim: An autonomous robotic ultrasound scanning ... () using a 7-DOF arm with force control and visual servoing acquired reproducible thyroid images on phantoms and volunteers in a laboratory study; it is a research demonstration of the imaging sub-step, not a clinical postoperative assessment system for children.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: acquiring a diagnostic ultrasound, the 'imaging tests' sub-step. Cited to bound the state of the art: autonomous scanning is demonstrated only on phantoms and cooperative adult volunteers in a lab, on a fixed anatomical target, not on post-operative infants with wounds, drains and dressings, and it does not perform the surrounding clinical assessment.

sources.title: Diligent Robotics completes 300,000 pharmacy deliveries with Moxi - The Robot Report
sources.claim: Diligent Robotics' Moxi mobile manipulator is deployed and operating autonomously in more than 30 US hospitals, but its work is logistics — delivering medications, lab specimens and supplies through corridors — with no patient examination or clinical assessment.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous mobile manipulation inside hospitals. Cited to establish the actual ceiling of deployed hospital robotics — navigation and item transport in E2 corridors — and to show that no deployed system performs bedside examination or postoperative clinical assessment of patients.

tasks.label: Operate on fetuses, infants, children, and adolescents to correct deformities, repair injuries, prevent and treat diseases, or improve or restore patients' functions.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Common general pediatric operations in a children's hospital operating room: laparoscopic or open appendectomy, inguinal/umbilical hernia repair, pyloromyotomy, orchiopexy in children aged roughly 1-17 under general anesthesia, with a scrub team, live tissue handling, hemostasis, and closure.

Neonatal and infant congenital-anomaly repair: esophageal atresia/tracheoesophageal fistula, gastroschisis/omphalocele closure, congenital diaphragmatic hernia repair, Hirschsprung pull-through, laparotomy for necrotizing enterocolitis. Millimetre-scale, friable tissue in a 2-4 kg patient, tight physiologic margins, OR adjacent to the NICU.

Minor/ancillary operative procedures in a hospital OR or ambulatory surgical suite: tunneled central venous catheter or port insertion, gastrostomy tube placement, lymph node or soft-tissue mass biopsy, abscess drainage/debridement, exam under anesthesia. Short cases, high volume, still open surgical access on an anesthetized child.

Complex oncologic, thoracic and reconstructive resections in a tertiary children's hospital OR: Wilms tumor nephrectomy, neuroblastoma resection with vessel dissection, lung resection, chest-wall correction (Nuss bar). Multi-hour cases, intraoperative decision-making, variable anatomy distorted by tumor.

Emergency trauma and acute abdominal surgery: exploratory laparotomy for blunt or penetrating injury, control of splenic/hepatic bleeding, incarcerated hernia, perforated viscus. Unplanned, time-critical, unstable physiology, anatomy obscured by blood and injury.

Fetal intervention at a specialized fetal care center: fetoscopic laser ablation for twin-twin transfusion syndrome, open fetal myelomeningocele repair, EXIT procedure. Operating on a moving fetus through the maternal uterus under ultrasound/fetoscopic guidance.

sources.system: SRT-H (Hierarchical Surgical Robot Transformer, built on da Vinci Research Kit dVRK-Si)
sources.title: Robot performs first realistic surgery without human help - Johns Hopkins Malone Center for Engineering in Healthcare
sources.claim: The most advanced autonomous surgical robot reported (SRT-H, Johns Hopkins, Science Robotics July 2025) autonomously executed one lengthy phase of a gallbladder ... on ex vivo porcine tissue in a lifelike bench model, with spoken human corrections available - not a complete operation and not on a human patient.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: a phase of adult-scale laparoscopic cholecystectomy on ex vivo pig tissue. Cited as the state of the art bounding this task; it does not transfer to pediatric surgery because it covers only one procedural phase, uses cadaveric animal tissue in a bench setup rather than a live human child, and involves no patient positioning, access, hemostasis in a perfused patient, or closure.

sources.system: Toumai surgical robot with Neuron multimodal AI model
sources.title: No Hands on Deck: The Dawn of Fully Autonomous Surgery - Mewburn Ellis
sources.claim: As of early 2026 the only reported in vivo autonomous robotic abdominal surgery was a gallbladder removal on a live pig by MicroPort MedBot's Toumai with the Neuron model (Dec 2025), not peer reviewed, with about 88% of steps completed unaided and the remainder requiring correction; no autonomous surgery on human patients had been performed.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: adult-scale cholecystectomy in a live pig. Cited to bound the state of the art; it does not transfer because it is a single-organ animal demonstration with human corrections, not a completed human pediatric operation, and the same source notes human trials are seen as a possibility only within the next decade.

sources.system: da Vinci Xi / da Vinci surgical system in pediatric surgery
sources.developer: Intuitive Surgical (deployed at UF Health, Nationwide Children's, Johns Hopkins Children's Center and other US children's hospitals)
sources.title: How Robotic Surgery Is Reshaping Pediatric Care Safely and Effectively - UF Health
sources.claim: Clinical robotic surgery on children, including in infants, is performed with the surgeon in continuous control at a console; the robotic system is a teleoperated tool and does not act autonomously.

sources.system: da Vinci Xi robot-assisted pediatric surgery program

tasks.label: Perform transplantation operations, such as organ transplants, on fetuses, infants, children, and adolescents.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Kidney transplant in a child or adolescent (deceased- or living-donor graft) at a pediatric transplant center: open or robot-assisted extraperitoneal/intraperitoneal implantation, iliac or aortocaval vascular anastomoses, ureteroneocystostomy, intraoperative volume and perfusion management for a small recipient.

Liver transplant in an infant or small child (often <10 kg, biliary atresia) using a technical-variant graft (left lateral segment/split): recipient hepatectomy with portal hypertension, 2-3 mm hepatic artery anastomosis under loupes/microscope, portal vein and hepatic vein reconstruction, Roux-en-Y hepaticojejunostomy, management of reperfusion.

Heart transplant in an infant or child, frequently with congenital heart disease and prior palliative operations: cardiopulmonary bypass, recipient cardiectomy, tailored aortic/arch, pulmonary artery and atrial reconstruction to fit donor-recipient anatomy, weaning from bypass with inotropes/ECMO backup.

Complex or salvage transplant: re-transplantation after graft failure, extensive adhesions from prior surgery, portal vein thrombosis or absent vessels requiring conduits/jump grafts, coagulopathy and hemodynamic instability, often emergent status-1A overnight case.

Lung, intestinal, or multivisceral/combined abdominal transplant in a child: long operation, multiple visceral and vascular anastomoses, ostomy creation or bronchial anastomoses, extensive prior surgical anatomy.

Donor-side and bench work performed by the pediatric transplant surgeon: deceased-donor procurement or living-donor left-lateral-segment hepatectomy, then back-table (bench) preparation of the graft on ice — splitting, trimming, arterial/venous reconstruction with fine suture before implantation.

sources.system: SRT-H (Surgical Robot Transformer-Hierarchy) on a da Vinci Research Kit
sources.developer: Johns Hopkins University (Krieger lab) with Stanford
sources.title: Johns Hopkins teaches robot to perform a gallbladder removal on a realistic patient - The Robot Report
sources.claim: The most advanced autonomous surgical robot demonstrated as of mid-2026 (SRT-H, Johns Hopkins) autonomously performed one lengthy phase of a gallbladder ... on ex-vivo porcine tissue in a laboratory, not a complete operation and not on a human patient; the team states completing a whole surgery autonomously is still a future goal.
sources.transferJustification: Closest related task: autonomous soft-tissue laparoscopic surgery. It bounds what autonomous surgical robots can do; a gallbladder-removal phase on ex-vivo pig tissue is far short of a whole pediatric organ transplant with vascular and biliary reconstruction.

sources.developer: Johns Hopkins University / Children's National Hospital
sources.title: Robot performs first laparoscopic surgery without human help -- ScienceDaily
sources.claim: The earlier STAR system autonomously performed intestinal anastomosis in live pigs, but only that single sub-step, with specially marked tissue, in a highly controlled laboratory setting following a predetermined plan.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous suturing/anastomosis of soft tissue. Anastomosis is a component of transplantation, but this was a single sub-step on marked bowel in live pigs, not the whole transplant operation on a child.

tasks.label: Provide consultation and surgical assistance to other physicians and surgeons.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Inpatient/ED bedside surgical consultation requested by a pediatrician, hospitalist, neonatologist or ED physician: pediatric surgeon goes to the ward/ED bay, examines the child (abdominal palpation, wound/stoma inspection, assessing guarding in a crying toddler), reviews imaging and labs, discusses with family and the requesting team, and documents an operative or non-operative recommendation.

Intraoperative assistance/exposure provided to a surgeon of another specialty in a shared case at the children's hospital OR: e.g., opening and closing the abdomen and placing the peritoneal catheter for a neurosurgeon's VP shunt, providing abdominal access for urology/orthopedic spine exposure, or obtaining central/vascular access on a small infant. Requires scrubbing, tissue handling, retraction, hemostasis and suturing on a live child under drapes.

Second-attending/co-surgeon assistance in complex neonatal or congenital cases (CDH repair, esophageal atresia, sacrococcygeal teratoma, oncologic resection): continuous adaptive assistance — retraction of friable neonatal tissue, suction, exposure, clamping, suture-tying — coordinated in real time with the primary surgeon's plan and with anesthesia.

Urgent intraoperative call-in when another surgeon or obstetrician encounters an unexpected finding (bowel injury during a laparoscopic case, unanticipated anomaly at cesarean/EXIT, bleeding in a small child): surgeon scrubs into an in-progress case, assesses an already-disturbed field, and either assists or takes over the repair.

Telephone/telemedicine or curbside consultation with a referring physician at an outside hospital or clinic: reviewing transmitted imaging and history, advising on management, resuscitation and whether/when to transfer, with no hands-on contact with the patient.

sources.system: SRT-H (Hierarchical Surgical Robot Transformer, on dVRK-Si)
sources.title: SRT-H: A hierarchical framework for autonomous surgery via language-conditioned imitation learning | Science Robotics
sources.claim: The most capable autonomous surgical robot demonstrated to date (SRT-H) completed multi-step gallbladder dissection fully autonomously, but only on ex vivo porcine tissue on a laboratory bench, not on human patients and not as an assistant to a human surgeon.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous execution of a surgical procedure step. It bounds the state of the art for robot manipulation of soft tissue; it does not transfer to the rated task because it operates on excised animal tissue in a bench setup and does not perform adaptive assistance to a human surgeon or any clinical judgment.

sources.developer: Johns Hopkins University / Children's National Hospital
sources.title: Smart Tissue Autonomous Robot performs laparoscopic surgery on pig soft tissue without human help
sources.claim: STAR performed an autonomous laparoscopic intestinal anastomosis on a live pig under human supervision — the leading in-vivo autonomous soft-tissue result, still an animal-lab demonstration of a single suturing task.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous suturing of soft tissue in vivo. Comparable tissue type to pediatric bowel work, but the demonstration is a single pre-planned anastomosis in an anesthetized pig with the bowel exposed and marked, not real-time assistance to another surgeon on a child.

sources.system: Robotic Scrub Nurse (RSN) with laparoscopic video analysis
sources.developer: academic research group (published in Int. J. CARS / PMC)
sources.title: Robotic scrub nurse to anticipate surgical instruments based on real-time laparoscopic video analysis
sources.claim: Research robotic scrub nurses that autonomously anticipate and hand instruments — the narrowest, most structured slice of intraoperative assistance — manage only about 72% of handovers autonomously in study conditions.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: intraoperative support to the operating surgeon. Even this sub-step — passing instruments, with no patient contact — is not at worker reliability, so it cannot substantiate the far harder role of a surgical first assistant handling live tissue.

sources.title: Da Vinci Surgical System - an overview | ScienceDirect Topics
sources.claim: The surgical robots actually deployed in hospital ORs, including pediatric cases, are telemanipulators under continuous surgeon control, with no autonomous movement.
sources.transferJustification: Directly relevant: this is the robotic hardware present in pediatric ORs. Because it is continuously teleoperated, it cannot support a positive judgment under the limited-intervention rule.

sources.developer: Beijing Yakebot Technology / Peking University School of Stomatology
sources.title: Implant placement with an autonomous dental implant robot: A clinical report
sources.claim: Autonomous robotic surgery on human patients exists only for rigid, pre-planned, image-registered drilling tasks such as dental implant placement, where the anatomy is immobilized and the trajectory is planned before the robot moves.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous execution of a surgical step on a human patient. It does not transfer: the jaw is rigidly fixtured and the plan is fixed in advance, whereas surgical assistance to another surgeon requires continuous adaptation to deformable tissue and to another operator's changing plan.

sources.developer: InTouch Health (with iRobot), now Teladoc Health
sources.title: Telepresence Robot Gives Patients Access to Remote Physicians
sources.claim: Robots used for remote specialist consultation at the bedside are mobile telepresence platforms driven by a human physician at a remote station; they convey audio/video and cannot perform the physical examination of a child.
sources.transferJustification: Directly relevant to the bedside-consultation instances: the deployed system is a conduit for a human consultant, teleoperated, and performs no examination, so it cannot substantiate autonomous completion.

roles.title: Acupuncturists
roles.description: Diagnose, treat, and prevent disorders by stimulating specific acupuncture points within the body using acupuncture needles. May also use cups, nutritional supplements, therapeutic massage, acupressure, and other alternative health therapies.

tasks.label: Maintain and follow standard quality, safety, environmental, and infection control policies and procedures.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Clean Needle Technique during a routine treatment in the clinic's treatment room: perform hand hygiene, open single-use sterile filiform needle packets without touching shafts, swab each of 8-20 points with 70% alcohol, insert and retain needles on a draped patient lying prone/supine, keep a clean field on the tray table.

Post-treatment sharps handling: collect the used filiform needles and guide tubes from the tray/field, verify the count against the number inserted so none is retained or dropped, deposit needles directly (no recapping) into an FDA-cleared sharps container, seal and replace the container when at the fill line.

Between-patient treatment-room turnover: strip and discard used table paper and face-cradle cover (or bag soiled sheets/bolster covers for laundry), disinfect table, face cradle, bolsters, hooks and high-touch surfaces with an EPA-registered disinfectant at correct dwell time, re-dress the table with fresh covering, empty trash, restock swabs and needles.

Reprocessing reusable items and running clinic sterilization/safety procedures: wash and high-level disinfect glass/silicone cupping cups, gua sha tools and electroacupuncture clips; load, run and unload the tabletop autoclave for reusable items; run and log the weekly spore test; check moxa/fire-safety equipment and disinfectant dilutions.

Clinic waste and supply logistics under the exposure-control plan: haul sealed regulated-medical-waste boxes and biohazard/soiled-linen bags to the locked holding area for pickup, run and transfer clinic laundry, and restock each treatment room with gloves, alcohol swabs, sterile needle packs, hand sanitizer and sharps containers.

Off-site infection control: house call, hospice room, or community/event acupuncture — set up a clean field on an unfamiliar surface, use hand sanitizer without a sink, carry and use a portable sharps container, wipe down a borrowed recliner or kitchen chair, and pack out all regulated waste.

sources.title: Performance, Safety, and Patient Experience of an Autonomous Robotic Phlebotomy Device: A Multicenter Trial (Clinical Chemistry)
sources.claim: Vitestro's Aletta autonomous robotic phlebotomy device performs the needle procedure on patients autonomously, including applying 70% alcohol antisepsis to the skin before inserting a sterile single-use needle; it is CE-marked and in clinical use in European hospitals and laboratories.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: diagnostic venipuncture. The infection-control operations are the same ones the acupuncturist's clean-needle instance requires — antiseptic skin prep, no-touch handling of a sterile single-use fine needle, and controlled needle placement at sub-millimeter precision on a patient presented to the device in a fixtured arm cradle.

sources.title: Performance, Safety, and Patient Experience of an Autonomous Robotic Phlebotomy Device: A Multicenter Trial (Clinical Chemistry)
sources.claim: In a multicenter clinical trial the device operated with one supervising professional per three machines and achieved clinical-grade reliability and low adverse-event rates, i.e. worker-quality output with limited intervention.
sources.transferJustification: Same related task (venipuncture); establishes that the autonomous aseptic needle procedure meets clinical acceptance standards rather than being a demonstration.

sources.title: Vitestro unveils Aletta robotic phlebotomy device — CAP TODAY
sources.claim: Aletta is CE-marked and is designed to carry out the whole patient-side needle procedure, including skin preparation and post-procedure bandaging, without a human performing the steps.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: venipuncture. Shows the full aseptic needle workflow (skin prep through disposal of the used set and dressing) is executed by the machine, which is the infection-control conduct the acupuncture instances require.

sources.title: Automation in IV Pharmacy Compounding — RoboticsTomorrow
sources.claim: Enclosed robotic IV compounding cells manipulate syringes and needled transfer sets that are presented to them in dedicated fixtures inside an ISO-classified enclosure in hospital pharmacies.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: sterile IV compounding. It is the closest demonstrated case of a machine picking, using and discarding needled sharps to a healthcare infection-control standard, with each item presented in a fixture inside a purpose-built enclosure — the E1 form of the acupuncturist's sharps-handling instance.

sources.title: Ballad Health expands patient safety with new robotic pharmacy technology
sources.claim: Robotic sterile compounding cells that handle syringes and needles are installed and running in US hospital central pharmacies.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: sterile compounding. Establishes that enclosed robotic cells handling syringes/needles are in routine hospital service, not prototypes.

sources.title: European Commission procurement triggers wider deployment of innovative disinfection robots across Europe's hospitals
sources.claim: Autonomous UV-C disinfection robots are commercially deployed in hospital rooms, but they only irradiate surfaces; manual cleaning of visible contamination and of linens is still required.

sources.system: Intelligent Autonomous Wiping and UV-C Disinfection Robot (POSTECH)
sources.title: Transforming hospital sanitation: Autonomous robots for wiping and UV-C disinfection — TechXplore
sources.claim: A research robot that physically wipes surfaces and then applies UV-C was run autonomously and validated in a working hospital, showing surface wiping can be automated in a structured healthcare facility.

sources.title: Somatic — Autonomous Bathroom Cleaning Robots
sources.claim: Somatic's autonomous bathroom cleaning robot cleans and disinfects fixtures and floors and picks up trash in commercial buildings during normal operations, but it does not handle linens or re-dress furniture.

sources.title: Diligent Robotics completes 300,000 pharmacy deliveries with Moxi — The Robot Report
sources.claim: Diligent Robotics' Moxi mobile manipulator autonomously fetches and delivers supplies and pharmacy items throughout more than 25 US hospitals, having completed over a million deliveries.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: hospital supply logistics. Restocking treatment rooms with gloves, swabs and needle packs is the same fetch-and-deliver operation with the same objects and the same facility conditions.

sources.system: ST Engineering T3 autonomous mobile robot
sources.title: Transforming Hospital Operations with Autonomous Mobile Robots — ST Engineering
sources.claim: Autonomous mobile robots move linens, equipment and waste through hospital corridors and lifts as a commercial service.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: hospital waste and linen transport. Hauling sealed regulated-waste boxes and soiled-linen bags to a holding area is the same operation with the same loads in the same class of facility.

sources.title: Automated Washer/Sterilizers — Infection Control Today
sources.claim: Indexing tunnel washer-disinfectors in central processing departments automatically wash, disinfect and dry instrument trays presented on their conveyor at high throughput to a validated standard.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: reprocessing surgical instruments. Cupping cups, gua sha tools and e-stim clips are simpler, smooth, autoclavable items; presented on racks in a purpose-built washer-disinfector line the cleaning/disinfection cycle is the same and is validated to a stricter standard.

sources.title: Intelligent robots for commercial laundries — IFR case study
sources.claim: Robotic cells now pick individual limp textiles from bulk and feed them into laundry machines in commercial laundries, but this capability lives inside a laundry cell and does not cover stripping or re-dressing furniture.

tasks.label: Treat patients using tools, such as needles, cups, ear balls, seeds, pellets, or nutritional supplements.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Routine multi-point filiform needling session in a private acupuncture clinic treatment room: patient partly undressed, supine or prone on a padded table; practitioner palpates to locate 8-20 points across back, limbs, abdomen and scalp, adjusts depth and angle to body build and region, inserts with guide tubes, elicits de qi, sometimes attaches electro-stim leads, leaves the patient 20-30 minutes, then withdraws, counts and disposes of needles.

Cupping treatment in the clinic: glass fire cups or plastic suction cups placed over the back, shoulders or hips, retained 5-15 minutes or slid over oiled skin; practitioner watches skin color and patient tolerance, adjusts suction, then breaks the seal and removes cups, wiping and inspecting the skin.

Auricular therapy in the clinic: ear seeds, vaccaria pellets, magnets or press tacks placed with tweezers on millimeter-scale auricular points inside the convoluted ear of a seated, unrestrained patient, secured with small adhesive tape and checked for retention; patient instructed on self-pressing.

Dispensing and administering nutritional supplements/herbal formulas from the clinic dispensary: selecting bottles or weighing and packing granules per the treatment plan, labeling, and handing the product to the patient with dosing instructions at the end of a visit.

Needling in a shared or institutional setting: community acupuncture in a room of recliners with several patients treated in rotation, or hospital/integrative-clinic bedside treatment (oncology, pain service) where the patient is in a bed or infusion chair with lines and gown limiting access, mostly distal arm, leg and ear points.

Treatment away from a controlled facility: home or hospice visit, sports event tent, or workplace pop-up; equipment carried in, patient positioned on whatever surface is available, variable lighting and hygiene, needling plus cups or ear seeds delivered in that setting.

Comparable object (hypodermic needle), millimetre precision, and a clinical setting; but the patient's arm is cradled in a purpose-built station and only one site is needled, so it substantiates machine needling of a fixtured body region, not free multi-point body-wide acupuncture.

tasks.label: Identify correct anatomical and proportional point locations based on patients' anatomy and positions, contraindications, and precautions related to treatments, such as intradermal needles, moxibustion, electricity, guasha, or bleeding.

instances.label: Routine clinic visit: adult patient prone or supine on a treatment table in a private acupuncture or integrative-medicine clinic; practitioner locates standard back, trunk and limb points (e.g., BL lines, ST36, LI11) using bony landmarks, proportional cun measurement and palpation for tenderness, applying routine precautions (needle depth over thorax, avoid varicose veins) before needling.

Distal points on hands, feet and forearms with the patient seated or the limb resting on a support; small anatomical targets between tendons/metacarpals requiring millimetre accuracy and palpation of a tender depression.

Head, face, scalp and auricular points: very fine targets (auricular zones a few millimetres apart, facial motor points), often with hair, glasses, cosmetics or a reclined/seated head position, plus precautions about vessels, eyes and temporal area.

Patients with atypical anatomy or heightened risk where proportional measurement must be adapted and contraindications judged: obesity or marked edema, very thin frail elderly, pregnancy (forbidden points), scars/tattoos/skin lesions, anticoagulant or bleeding-disorder patients before bleeding/cupping/guasha, pacemakers before electroacupuncture, neuropathy before moxibustion.

Locating points for heat and adjunct modalities in the clinic: moxibustion (moxa stick, warm-needle, moxa box) over back/abdomen/limb points with burn precautions on skin temperature and distance, and placement sites for press/intradermal needles on the back or limbs.

Off-site treatment: house call, hospice or nursing-home bedside, workplace or sports-event chair treatment, or community acupuncture in a shared room; variable patient positioning, clutter, poor lighting, no dedicated table.

tasks.label: Insert needles to provide acupuncture treatment.

instances.label: Routine full-protocol treatment in a private acupuncture clinic: patient gowned and lying prone/supine on a treatment table; practitioner palpates landmarks and proportional (cun) measurements, swabs, and inserts 8-20 filiform needles (0.16-0.30 mm) into back, shoulder, neck and limb points at varied depths and angles, elicits de qi, retains 15-30 min with periodic manipulation, then withdraws, counts and disposes of every needle while watching for bleeding, faintness or discomfort.

Distal limb/hand/foot points on a supine or seated patient (e.g., LI4, PC6, ST36, SP6, LR3, wrist and ankle points): small targets over tendon and bone, shallow or obliquely angled insertions of a few millimetres to ~25 mm, often combined with electro-stimulation leads clipped to needle handles, in a clinic treatment room.

Head, face, ear and scalp needling in a clinic: auricular points, facial cosmetic needling, scalp-line needling; very shallow oblique threading of fine needles into thin, mobile tissue millimetres from eyes, ears and hairline, on a patient who blinks, swallows and speaks during the procedure.

Trunk needling over chest, upper back, abdomen and hip in a clinic: depth-critical points where over-insertion risks pneumothorax or organ injury, on patients of widely varying body habitus (thin, obese, elderly with lax skin), with respiratory motion changing tissue depth during insertion.

Treatment inside an institutional health facility: hospital inpatient bedside, oncology infusion suite, VA or integrative pain clinic; patient in a bed or recliner with IV lines, monitors and blankets, accessible only from constrained angles, needles inserted, retained and removed around equipment and staff traffic.

Off-site treatment taken as found: house calls, hospice or nursing-home rooms, community pop-up/mobile clinics, sports-team or event tents; patient on a portable table, chair, sofa or bed in a space with variable lighting, clutter, pets and no fixed layout.

instances.label: Routine weekly follow-up in a private acupuncture clinic: patient with chronic low-back or neck pain returns; practitioner asks how symptoms changed since the last session, reviews pain scale and function, notes any post-needling soreness, and decides whether to keep or alter the point prescription; the decision and rationale are stated to the patient and charted.

Mid-course re-evaluation after a package of 5-10 sessions (e.g., migraine, insomnia, infertility support, chemotherapy side effects): practitioner compares current status against baseline intake measures and decides to continue, taper frequency, add adjunct modalities (cupping, herbs, dietary/lifestyle advice), or change the diagnostic pattern and treatment strategy.

Non-response or adverse-response review: patient reports no improvement, symptom aggravation, bruising, or lightheadedness after prior treatment; practitioner evaluates the outcome, judges the cause, and recommends an altered approach (fewer/shallower needles, different technique or points, added modality) or refers the patient to a physician for workup.

Goal-met discharge or maintenance planning: practitioner concludes the treatment course achieved its aim and recommends a maintenance schedule, self-care/home instructions (stretching, moxa, acupressure, diet), and criteria for returning to care.

Telehealth or phone/portal check-in between visits: practitioner elicits the patient's response to the last treatment remotely and advises a change of plan, schedule, or herbal formula before the next in-person appointment.

Documentation and coordination outcome review: practitioner writes progress notes and functional-outcome updates for an insurer, employer, integrative clinic, or referring physician, and recommends continued, modified, or discontinued acupuncture treatment in that report.

Non-face-to-face analysis: telehealth or herbal consultation, case review with a supervisor or student, insurance/records documentation, where the practitioner reasons from reported and previously recorded findings to state or justify a diagnosis in writing.

instances.label: Private acupuncture clinic: at the end of a visit the practitioner takes a pre-packaged patent formula (bottle of teapills/capsules, tincture, or sealed granule bottle) off the in-office dispensary shelf, applies a dose label, bags it, hands it to the patient at the front desk and explains dose, frequency, how long to take it, expected side effects and interactions with the patient's medications.

Clinic dispensary, custom granule formula: practitioner scoops/weighs 6-14 concentrated herbal granule powders from stock jars on a gram scale per the individualized prescription, mixes, fills a jar or per-dose packets, labels with scoop/dose and frequency, and instructs the patient on mixing with hot water, duration and cautions.

Clinic or attached herbal dispensary, raw bulk herbs: practitioner weighs irregular dried roots, bark, seeds, flowers and mineral items from bulk apothecary drawers into daily decoction packets, checks substitutions and toxic-herb limits, bags and labels the set, and teaches the patient the cooking/decocting method, dosing schedule and warnings.

Formula ordered from an outside herbal pharmacy (e-script to a central granule or raw-herb fulfillment dispensary): the pharmacy fills, packages and labels the custom formula and ships it to clinic or patient; the practitioner verifies the received order, hands it over or confirms receipt, and counsels the patient on dosing, duration, side effects and drug interactions.

Hospital-based integrative medicine or oncology clinic / community acupuncture clinic: dispensing from an institutional herbal formulary, reconciling the formula against the patient's charted prescription drugs and chemotherapy, documenting in the EHR, and counseling the patient (sometimes with the care team present) on dose, duration, side effects and interactions.

House-call or mobile practice: practitioner brings a stocked kit to the patient's home, hospice room or worksite, selects and portions the formula on a kitchen table or bedside, labels it, and explains dosing, duration, side effects and interactions to the patient or caregiver.

tasks.label: Apply heat or cold therapy to patients using materials, such as heat pads, hydrocollator packs, warm compresses, cold compresses, heat lamps, or vapor coolants.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Acupuncture clinic treatment room: after needling the low back, knee or abdomen, the practitioner wheels an infrared/TDP heat lamp over the exposed region, sets height, angle and intensity, asks the patient about comfort, leaves it running 15-25 minutes with periodic checks for overheating or skin reddening, then turns it off and swings it clear before removing needles.

Clinic: an electric heating pad, microwaved rice/gel pack or warm moist compress is fetched, covered with a cloth barrier and laid on a non-needled region (shoulders, abdomen, neck, feet) of a draped patient lying on the treatment table; comfort confirmed, left ~15 minutes, then removed and the skin inspected.

Integrative/multi-modality clinic: a hydrocollator moist hot pack is lifted with tongs from a ~74 C tank, drained, wrapped in a terry cover plus towel layers, carried to the table and laid over the prone patient's back or shoulders on top of draping; the practitioner returns after 15-20 minutes, removes it, checks skin and returns the pack to the tank.

Clinic: a cold gel pack or ice bag is taken from the freezer, wrapped in a towel and applied to an acutely inflamed joint, strain, or a bruised/hematoma needle site, sometimes secured with an elastic wrap while the patient sits or lies; monitored 10-15 minutes with skin checks, then removed.

Clinic: vapor coolant (ethyl chloride / fluoromethane) is sprayed in sweeps over a trigger point or painful band from ~30 cm, often while the practitioner passively stretches the muscle, or briefly over a site to numb skin before needling; skin watched for frosting.

Off-site work: house call, hospice bedside, or bedside round in a shared clinic/hospital room, where the practitioner heats a pack in a household microwave or uses a cold pack from the patient's own freezer and applies it to a patient in a home bed, recliner or wheelchair amid furniture, pets and clutter.

sources.claim: An intelligent moxibustion robot is in service in a hospital rehabilitation treatment room in Shanghai: after a doctor selects acupoints on a tablet, the robot arm aligns and hovers a burning moxa heat source over acupoints on the patient's back and delivers 30 minutes of heat therapy.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: moxibustion. It is the same act as positioning a heat lamp on a patient — holding a radiant heat source at a controlled distance over an exposed body region of a patient lying on a clinic treatment table for ~20-30 minutes, keeping skin temperature safe. Objects (patient's back/limbs), precision (centimetre-level distance to skin), and environment (clinic treatment room) are the same, and burning moxa with ash is strictly harder to manage than an electric lamp.

instances.label: Clinic treatment room: patient prone on a treatment table for chronic low back or mid-back pain / muscular tension. Acupuncturist palpates the paraspinal and gluteal tissue, then applies 10-25 minutes of tuina (rolling, kneading, pressing, thumb pressure on tender points) over the lumbar, thoracic and gluteal region, varying depth to patient feedback.

Clinic treatment room: patient prone for shoulder-blade/upper-back tension or posterior leg complaints (sciatic-type pain, tight hamstrings/calves). Soft-tissue tuina and sustained pressure over trapezius/rhomboid region, glutes, hamstrings and calves, with pressure graded to tolerance.

Clinic treatment room: neck, occiput, scalp, face and jaw work for cervical pain, tension headache, migraine or TMJ. Practitioner cradles and rotates the head, applies fingertip pressure at suboccipital points, along the cervical spine, temples and masseter, with very fine force control near vulnerable structures.

Clinic treatment room: discrete acupressure at distal and anterior points - hands, wrists, forearms, lower legs, feet, ear, abdomen - for systemic complaints such as nausea, insomnia, anxiety, digestive problems or menstrual pain, often applied while needles are retained or as a needle-free alternative; sustained thumb/fingertip pressure at small, individually located points.

Clinic treatment room: sessions in which the practitioner must lift, support and move the patient - limb and joint tuina with passive range-of-motion, traction and stretching for frozen shoulder, hip or knee complaints; side-lying work for pregnant patients; light graded pressure for frail elderly patients and pediatric tuina on a child's hands and forearms.

Off-site delivery: house call, hospice or nursing-home bedside, or chair-based acupressure at a community or corporate event. Patient is in a bed, recliner or portable chair in a room laid out however it is found; practitioner adapts positioning and technique to the space.

sources.title: AI-powered massage robot to start product evaluation in the United States and clinical trial in Singapore
sources.claim: EMMA, an autonomous TCM tuina massage robot, has been deployed in TCM clinics, physiotherapy centres ..., delivering tens of thousands of treatment hours.

sources.title: EMMA - World's First AI-Powered TCM Tuina Massage Robot

sources.title: Satisfaction and Feasibility Evaluation of an Electronic Massager-Expert Manipulative Massage Automation (EMMA): A Pilot Study

sources.title: I Tried Aescape, the High-Tech Robot Massage-Here's My Review
sources.claim: Aescape's fully automated robotic massage table is in commercial service in gyms, hotels and spas; a first-hand review reports it works the back, shoulders, glutes and posterior legs but not the hands, arms, feet, neck ... front of the body.
sources.transferJustification: Related task is therapeutic soft-tissue massage on a clothed client lying on a table; same objects (human body), same graded-pressure manual technique and force control used in tuina/shiatsu on the back and limbs, delivered in the same kind of treatment room.

sources.transferJustification: Same related task (table-based soft-tissue massage) as above; establishes sustained autonomous operation with paying clients rather than a one-off demonstration.

sources.title: Massage Envy Introduces Aescape Robotic Massage at Select Franchised Locations
sources.claim: Aescape robots are being introduced at Massage Envy franchised bodywork locations in the US, i.e. inside professional massage-therapy premises rather than a purpose-built robot cell.
sources.transferJustification: Related task is professional therapeutic massage delivered in a bodywork clinic; the physical act (pressure applied to back, shoulders, glutes, legs of a client on a table) matches the manual portion of tuina/acupressure work.

sources.title: Robotic Massage - Massage & Bodywork magazine (ABMP)
sources.claim: Trade-press review of the two leading commercial massage robots states their programmed protocols cover the region from the glutes to the upper back and shoulders.
sources.transferJustification: Related task is professional soft-tissue massage; establishes the body regions robotic systems actually service, which bounds which acupressure/tuina instances they could complete.

sources.title: Capsix - Discover Technology
sources.claim: Capsix's iYU massage robot offers a fully autonomous mode requiring no human intervention, and its arm covers the body from the shoulders to the ...; it is offered to gyms, hotels and clinical/spa operators.
sources.transferJustification: Related task is table-based therapeutic massage of the posterior body; same body regions and force-controlled pressure application as the manual portion of tuina, in the same kind of human-work facility.

sources.title: AI and Massage: Robotic Therapists That Hit the Spot
sources.claim: Independent report of iYU confirms its working envelope: the robotic arm reaches from the shoulders to the ..., i.e. posterior body only.
sources.transferJustification: Same related task (soft-tissue massage); cited to bound the body regions robotic systems can treat.

tasks.label: Apply moxibustion directly or indirectly to patients using Chinese, non-scarring, stick, or pole moxa.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Clinic treatment room: patient prone/draped on a treatment table; practitioner holds a lit moxa stick (pole moxa) 1-3 cm above lumbar, sacral or shoulder points (e.g., BL23, GV4, ashi areas), using circling/pecking/hovering technique for 10-30 minutes, watching skin color and the patient's heat report, tapping ash into a tray and extinguishing the stick afterwards.

Clinic treatment room: patient supine; suspended moxa stick or handheld pole moxa over abdominal/pelvic points (CV4, CV6, CV8) or chest, often for cold-type digestive, menstrual or fertility complaints; 10-20 minutes, adjusting height to the patient's comfort and protecting sensitive tissue.

Clinic: short suspended-moxa applications to distal limb points on a seated or reclined patient (ST36, SP6, LI4, BL67 for breech presentation), 5-10 minutes per point, usually bilateral; a minority are done at bedside on home or hospice visits.

Warm-needle moxibustion during a needling session: practitioner rolls moxa punk onto, or slides a pre-formed moxa cap over, the handles of already-inserted needles, lights each one, places foil/card shields under them to catch falling embers, monitors several burning needles at once until they burn out, then clears ash and removes needles.

Contact-placed indirect moxibustion: cones of moxa punk on ginger or garlic slices or on salt in the navel, or a moxa box/stick holder strapped over the abdomen or low back; practitioner places the medium, forms and lights cones, replaces them as each burns down, and repositions when the patient reports it is too hot.

Direct non-scarring moxibustion: rice-grain or thread-size cones twisted from fine moxa wool, stuck to the skin over the point with a trace of ointment, lit with an incense stick and snuffed or lifted off at the patient's first sharp heat sensation; 3-9 repetitions per point, several points per session, avoiding blisters.

sources.system: Intelligent moxibustion rehabilitation robot (Shanghai Junkong Robotics / Xiong Genliang team)

sources.claim: Junkong/SUES intelligent moxibustion robot performs suspended moxa-stick therapy on back acupoints of patients in a hospital treatment room, with 3D acupoint localization, infrared temperature control, adaptive distance and automatic ash/smoke removal; one therapist supervises up to eight units; Class II medical device, >1000 patients served, patient-reported burns down 90%.

sources.developer: Chen Rixin / Xie Dingyi team, Jiangxi University of Traditional Chinese Medicine
sources.title: 机器人也能做艾灸！手法稳定，疗效更有保障 (World Federation of Chinese Medicine Societies, from China TCM News)
sources.claim: Heat-sensitive moxibustion robot treats patients lying prone or supine in the treatment room of the Jiangxi University of TCM affiliated hospital, autonomously scanning for the sensitized acupoint region and reproducing 28 classical moxa-stick manipulations with built-in smoke removal.

sources.developer: Jiangxi University of Traditional Chinese Medicine
sources.title: 热敏灸机器人载誉前行 科创赋能产业高质量发展-江西中医药大学
sources.claim: The heat-sensitive moxibustion robot has obtained Chinese Class II medical device registration plus manufacturing and distribution licences and is formally on the market, with standardized moxibustion protocols built in.
