sources.developer: Shenzhen Bao'an District TCM Hospital & Shenzhen Taiaide Robot Technology Co.
sources.title: 围观！深圳医院的机器人会康复、洗消、艾灸…… (Shenzhen Municipal Health Commission)
sources.claim: A moxibustion robot co-developed with Shenzhen Bao'an TCM Hospital has been in clinical use there for four years; AI vision identifies acupoints, the flexible arm reaches them and performs five different moxibustion techniques with precise temperature control and smoke extraction.

sources.developer: Chengdu University of TCM / Chengdu Fifth People's Hospital
sources.title: Effectiveness and Safety of Moxibustion Robots on Primary Dysmenorrhea: A Randomized Controlled Pilot Trial - PubMed
sources.claim: Randomized controlled pilot trial in 70 patients compared a moxibustion robot with manual moxibustion delivering moxa heat to the abdominal point Guanyuan (CV4) over three menstrual cycles, with burns and other adverse events measured as safety endpoints.

sources.system: 灵手艾灸理疗机器人 (Lingshou moxibustion therapy robot)
sources.title: 热疗机器人在网络病治疗中的应用 (Chinese Journal of Engineering, USTB)
sources.claim: Peer-reviewed review of thermal-therapy robots describes the Lingshou moxibustion robot: a mobile collaborative arm with moxa head, vision system and compliant force control that recognizes acupoints over the body region to be treated and executes circling, back-and-forth and sparrow-pecking moxa techniques.

sources.developer: Shanxi Acupuncture and Moxibustion Hospital & North University of China
sources.title: Intelligent Moxibustion Robot in the Treatment of Low Back Pain | Clinical Research Trial Listing
sources.claim: Registered randomized controlled clinical trial (NCT05704127) of a six-DOF 'intelligent thunder-fire moxibustion' robot applied to low back pain patients at a specialist acupuncture-moxibustion hospital.

roles.title: Dental Hygienists
roles.description: Administer oral hygiene care to patients. Assess patient oral hygiene problems or needs and maintain health records. Advise patients on oral health maintenance and disease prevention. May provide advanced care such as providing fluoride treatment or administering topical anesthesia.

tasks.label: Record and review patient medical histories.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

tasks.label: Feel and visually examine gums for sores and signs of disease.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Routine adult recall prophylaxis visit in a general dental operatory: hygienist reclines the patient, uses mirror, air/light and gloved fingers to inspect and palpate the free and attached gingiva of all quadrants, checks for redness, edema, bleeding, recession, ulcers/aphthae, denture sores and tissue tone, and charts findings for the dentist.

New-patient comprehensive assessment in a dental office including a full intra- and extraoral soft-tissue/oral-cancer screening: bimanual palpation of floor of mouth, tongue borders, buccal mucosa, vestibules and palate plus neck/lymph node palpation, distinguishing normal anatomy from indurated or suspicious lesions and flagging referrals.

Periodontal maintenance or post-therapy reassessment on a patient with active disease: inflamed, friable, bleeding tissue, possible abscess or exudate expressed by finger pressure, healing surgical or implant sites, tobacco or medication-related tissue changes; findings must be compared to prior charting.

Pediatric or adolescent patient in a general or pediatric practice: small mouth, limited cooperation and movement, eruption gingivitis, orthodontic-appliance tissue trauma, herpetic or traumatic ulcers; exam performed quickly between wiggles with parent present.

Medically complex or special-needs adult in the operatory: limited mouth opening, gag reflex, involuntary movement, xerostomia, mucositis or candidiasis, anticoagulant-related bleeding; tissue must be retracted and palpated gently while monitoring patient tolerance.

Off-site public-health hygiene visit: nursing-home bedside, school-gym or Head Start mobile clinic, or a client's home, using portable light and chair, patient possibly in a wheelchair or bed, variable lighting and positioning, screening gums for sores, denture irritation and disease.

sources.title: Perceptive Completes World's First Fully Automated Dental Procedure on a Human Using AI-Driven Robotic System
sources.claim: Perceptive's AI-driven robotic arm autonomously prepared a tooth for a crown on a live human patient in a dental clinic setting, the first fully automated dental procedure ...; the work is hard-tissue cutting, not soft-tissue assessment.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous robotic tooth preparation in the same environment (a dental operatory, patient in the chair). It shows a robot can work intraorally under machine control, but it images and cuts hard tissue on a rigidly splinted arch; it does not touch, palpate, or diagnose gingival soft tissue, so it does not substantiate completion of a gum examination.

sources.title: The future of dentistry through robotics | British Dental Journal
sources.claim: Independent dental-literature account confirming the July 2024 autonomous robotic crown-preparation procedure on a human patient, the most advanced autonomous intraoral robotic work reported.
sources.transferJustification: Related task (crown preparation) cited to bound the state of the art for autonomous intraoral robotics; it involves rigid tooth structure rather than palpation or visual diagnosis of gingival disease, so capability does not transfer to this task.

sources.title: RobOralScan: Learning Active Intraoral Scanning for Robotic Dental Reconstruction
sources.claim: A reinforcement-learning robotic system autonomously plans intraoral scanner motion to reconstruct tooth and adjacent gum surfaces; it is a research prototype producing geometry, with no soft-tissue palpation or disease assessment.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated intraoral scanning covers some of the same surfaces a hygienist inspects, but it outputs 3D geometry for prosthodontic workflows, is validated on hardware models rather than as a clinical exam, and provides no tactile assessment or pathology judgment.

sources.title: Autonomous swab robot for naso- and oropharyngeal COVID-19 screening | Scientific Reports
sources.claim: An autonomous, force-controlled robot station inserted swabs into the mouth and throat of human subjects in clinical studies, showing autonomous robot contact inside the oral cavity, but only for sample collection, not tissue examination.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous intraoral instrument insertion on live people demonstrates safe force-controlled entry to the mouth, but the robot performs no inspection or palpation of gingiva and makes no diagnostic determination, so it cannot complete this task.

sources.title: Autonomous Robotic Tissue Palpation and Abnormalities Characterisation via Ergodic Exploration
sources.claim: Autonomous robotic palpation that estimates tissue stiffness and localises abnormal inclusions has been validated only on silicone phantoms, not on patients' oral soft tissue.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic palpation for detecting abnormal tissue. It is the closest analogue to feeling gums for sores, but it operates on flat phantom surfaces outside the body, so it does not substantiate an intraoral gingival exam on patients.

sources.system: Clinical dental robotic systems (navigation/haptic guidance, e.g. implant robots)
sources.title: Dental Robotics | Liv Hospital
sources.claim: Clinical dental robots in service today are assistive and surgeon-guided rather than autonomous, and none perform oral soft-tissue examination.

tasks.label: Examine gums, using probes, to locate periodontal recessed gums and signs of gum disease.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Routine adult recall patient in a general dental practice operatory: hygienist reclines the patient, retracts cheek/tongue, walks a manual or constant-force electronic periodontal probe into the sulcus at six sites per tooth on ~28 teeth, feels for the pocket base, notes recession from the CEJ and bleeding on probing, and records the full-mouth chart in ~5-10 minutes.

Patient with moderate-to-severe periodontitis or heavy calculus in the operatory: deep irregular pockets, inflamed friable bleeding tissue, furcations and implants requiring plastic probes, suppuration and mobility checks; probing is tender so the hygienist modulates force, pauses, and re-probes to confirm findings before charting.

Screening-level gum examination (PSR) on an adolescent, child, or new patient with limited chair time: probe swept around each sextant, visual assessment of gingival color, contour and recession, worst score per sextant recorded, and a decision made about whether full charting is needed.

Difficult-to-manage patient in the operatory: limited mouth opening, strong gag reflex, dental anxiety, tremor, dementia or intellectual disability; the hygienist coaches, repositions, works in short bursts, stabilizes with fingers, and still obtains usable probing depths and gingival findings.

Off-site public-health or mobile hygiene visit: nursing-home bedside or wheelchair, school gym, or community van; portable light and instruments, patient not in a dental chair, variable posture and lighting, probing depths and gum findings recorded on a portable chart for referral.

sources.title: Robot Dentist: Startup's Bot Could Save Time in the Chair - IEEE Spectrum
sources.claim: Perceptive's AI-driven dental robot autonomously performed a crown preparation on a live human patient in a dental chair, with the arm rigidly coupled to a bite block so head motion is compensated mechanically; the system remained a first-generation prototype not cleared for commercial use.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic crown preparation inside a live patient's mouth. It shares the operatory setting and sub-millimetre control, but it is hard-tissue drilling along a pre-planned OCT path with the tool rigidly coupled to a bite block; it involves no gentle (~0.25 N) insertion of a probe into the gingival sulcus, no six-site depth/recession/bleeding readings, and no judgment about signs of gum disease, so it does not substantiate completion of periodontal probing.

sources.title: Hesytech | AI-Guided Robotic Dental Hygiene
sources.claim: Hesytech advertises an AI-guided robotic dental hygiene arm whose planned modules include periodontal probing, scaling and polishing, but the company's own site states the system is still under development; no demonstration results on patients are shown.
sources.transferJustification: Directly targets this task (periodontal probing) but is an announcement of intent with no demonstrated performance, so it cannot support a positive judgment.

sources.developer: Technical University of Munich (Haddadin et al.)
sources.title: Autonomous swab robot for naso- and oropharyngeal COVID-19 screening (Scientific Reports)
sources.claim: An autonomous, force-sensitive swab robot station performed naso- and oropharyngeal sampling on 52 human subjects in two clinical studies, showing autonomous impedance-controlled instrument insertion into a live person's mouth and nose.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous insertion of a slender instrument into a live human's oral cavity under force control. Targeting is centimetre-scale (pharyngeal wall) with a soft swab and no measurement output; periodontal probing needs 0.5 mm probe tips walked into sulci at six sites per tooth with sub-millimetre depth readings and tissue-response interpretation, so capability does not carry over.

sources.title: RobOralScan: Learning Active Intraoral Scanning for Robotic Dental Reconstruction (arXiv)
sources.claim: RobOralScan is a reinforcement-learning pipeline for autonomous robotic intraoral scanning of teeth and adjacent gums, trained and evaluated in a bounded oral workspace with zero-shot sim-to-real trials on a physical robot-scanner rig; it is non-contact scanning and has not been run in patients' mouths.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated intraoral sensing of teeth and gingiva. It is optical, non-contact, and demonstrated only on hardware rigs and simulation rather than live patients, so it substantiates neither contact probing of the sulcus nor clinical periodontal assessment.

sources.developer: University of Salerno (Pagliara, Ferrentino et al.)
sources.title: Haptic bilateral teleoperation system for free-hand dental procedures (arXiv)
sources.claim: State-of-the-art robotic assistance for free-hand periodontal work such as scaling remains a haptic bilateral teleoperation system in which a human operator's motions and forces drive the robot end-effector holding standard clinical tools.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: free-hand periodontal instrumentation (scaling) with a robot. It is continuously teleoperated, so by the autonomy rule it cannot support a positive judgment, and it indicates that robotic soft-tissue periodontal work is not yet autonomous.

tasks.label: Clean calcareous deposits, accretions, and stains from teeth and beneath margins of gums, using dental instruments.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Routine adult recall prophylaxis in a general dental office operatory: seated patient in a dental chair, light-to-moderate supragingival plaque, calculus and coffee/tea stain; hygienist uses ultrasonic scaler plus hand scalers/curettes around every tooth surface and just below the gingival margin, then polishes, with mirror, suction and water spray, in a 30-45 minute appointment.

Periodontal maintenance / quadrant scaling and root planing on a patient with 4-6 mm pockets and moderate subgingival calculus on root surfaces, often with topical/local anesthesia; requires tactile exploration with an explorer, instrumentation deep in the pocket adapted to root anatomy and furcations, bleeding tissue, and verification that root surfaces are left smooth and deposit-free.

Heavy-buildup patient who has not been seen in years: tenacious calcified deposits bridging lower anteriors and molars, heavy tobacco/betel/chlorhexidine stain, inflamed bleeding gingiva and sensitivity; long or multi-visit debridement with heavy ultrasonic use and hand instrumentation.

Child or adolescent prophylaxis in a general/pediatric dental office: small mouth, mixed dentition, limited cooperation and movement, sometimes fixed orthodontic appliances requiring cleaning around brackets and wires.

Patient with restorations and implants (crowns, veneers, implant abutments) requiring instrument selection that will not scratch restorative surfaces, plus removal of calculus and stain around margins.

Medically complex, elderly or special-needs patient, sometimes seen in a nursing-home or hospital dental clinic setting: limited mouth opening, strong gag reflex, wheelchair transfer or bedside positioning, involuntary movement, xerostomia-related heavy deposits.

sources.title: Fully-automatic robot dentist performs world's first human procedure
sources.claim: Perceptive's AI-driven robotic arm autonomously performed a complete crown preparation on a live human patient (Barranquilla, Colombia) using OCT volumetric imaging; it is a one-off demonstration, not FDA-cleared or deployed, and covers restorative cutting rather than calculus removal.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: crown preparation (cutting tooth structure) on a live patient in a dental operatory - same objects and environment as hygiene scaling. Transfer does NOT carry: the robot cuts a pre-planned geometry on a rigidly braced crown surface, whereas the rated task requires tactile/optical detection of variable calcareous deposits and sub-gingival instrumentation inside periodontal pockets against soft tissue; no scaling, root planing or stain removal has been demonstrated, and the source notes the robot is not FDA-approved with no rollout timeline.

sources.system: Shapeshifting microrobotic superstructures (magnetic iron-oxide nanoparticle swarm)
sources.developer: University of Pennsylvania (Koo / Steager, CiPD & GRASP Lab)
sources.title: Shapeshifting microrobots can brush and floss teeth | Penn Today
sources.claim: Penn's magnetically controlled iron-oxide microrobot swarms removed biofilm/plaque from mock and extracted human teeth in a laboratory proof-of-concept; they address soft biofilm, not calcified calculus, and were still preparing for animal studies in 2025.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated plaque/biofilm removal from teeth. Transfer does not carry to this task: the swarm removes soft biofilm on bench-mounted extracted teeth, not calcified deposits, accretions or stains removed with dental instruments beneath the gum margin in a live patient, and it has not been used clinically.

sources.developer: Beijing Baihui Weikang / Peking University School of Stomatology (China)
sources.title: The evolution of robotics: research and application progress of dental implant robotic systems | International Journal of Oral Science
sources.claim: Autonomous in-mouth robotic instrumentation on live patients exists only for implant surgery: the Yakebot autonomous dental implant robot prepares the implant bed and places implants in patients in dental hospital operatories under CBCT-based planning with a rigid patient marker splint.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous drilling in a live patient's mouth in a dental clinic. Transfer does not carry: the robot follows a pre-planned osteotomy axis into bone registered to a rigid splint, whereas removing calculus requires searching tooth and root surfaces for unmapped deposits, adapting curette angulation to root morphology and working sub-gingivally against mobile soft tissue; no scaling capability is reported.

sources.system: Hesytech AI-guided robotic dental hygiene system
sources.title: Hesytech | AI-Guided Robotic Dental Hygiene
sources.claim: The only company marketing an autonomous robotic dental hygiene system (scaling, polishing, periodontal probing) states on its own site that the system is not yet built and is recruiting pilot clinics - an announcement of intent, not a demonstration.

sources.title: Robotic and Microrobotic Tools for Dental Therapy - PMC
sources.claim: A peer-reviewed review of robotic and microrobotic tools in dentistry reports essentially no robotic systems performing periodontal instrumentation; robotic work on teeth is limited to toothbrush-motion simulation in vitro.

tasks.label: Provide clinical services or health education to improve and maintain the oral health of patients or the general public.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Routine adult prophylaxis at a private general dental practice: 40-60 minute recall appointment in a standard operatory; hygienist removes supragingival and subgingival plaque/calculus from ~28 teeth with ultrasonic and hand instruments, polishes with prophy cup and paste, flosses, on an awake, talking, moving patient with saliva, tongue and cheeks to retract, and reports findings to the dentist.

Periodontal therapy in a general or periodontal practice: quadrant scaling and root planing or periodontal maintenance on a patient with pocketing, bleeding and heavy subgingival calculus; includes probing/charting, topical or infiltration local anesthesia, tactile subgingival deposit detection on curved root surfaces, irrigation, and post-op instructions.

Pediatric/preventive services: child prophylaxis plus fluoride varnish application, and pit-and-fissure sealant placement (isolation, etch, rinse, dry, resin placement, light cure, occlusion check), in a pediatric/general operatory or a portable school-based sealant clinic, with behavior management of a squirming, sometimes uncooperative child.

Chairside individualized oral health education during an appointment: disclosing plaque and showing the patient deposits in their own mouth with a mirror, demonstrating brushing/interdental technique on the patient and on a typodont, dietary, tobacco-cessation and denture/implant-care counseling tailored to that day's clinical findings, then documenting the instruction.

Group or public oral health education outside the operatory: classroom lesson with toothbrush/typodont demonstration and hands-on distribution at an elementary school, a health-fair or community-clinic screening booth, or a caregiver/staff in-service on mouth care at a nursing home.

sources.title: The future of dentistry through robotics | British Dental Journal
sources.claim: Perceptive's AI-controlled dental robot autonomously performed a crown preparation on one live human patient in July 2024 — the state of the art for autonomous intraoral work is single-tooth hard-tissue cutting along a pre-planned path, not hygiene instrumentation.
sources.transferJustification: Related task = restorative crown preparation. I do NOT claim transfer to dental hygiene: the robot cuts one rigidly registered tooth along a pre-planned path, whereas prophylaxis requires whole-mouth tactile detection and removal of subgingival deposits on curved roots without soft-tissue trauma. Cited to show the ceiling of demonstrated capability.

sources.developer: Yakebot Technology Co. (Beijing) / Stomatological Hospital of Air Force Medical University
sources.title: Efficiency for robotic-assisted extraction of completely impacted supernumerary teeth in children: a randomized controlled trial (BMC Oral Health)
sources.claim: Autonomous dental robots (Yakebot) perform planned bone resection for impacted tooth extraction on patients in a hospital dental department under RCT conditions — i.e., autonomous robots do operate inside standard dental clinical facilities, but only for pre-planned hard-tissue surgery.
sources.transferJustification: Related task = oral surgery osteotomy. Transfer to hygiene is not claimed: the robot follows a CBCT-planned osteotomy path with rigid splint/marker registration, which does not supply the compliant, tactile, whole-mouth soft-tissue-adjacent instrumentation a prophylaxis requires. Cited to establish what autonomous dental robots actually do in clinics.

sources.developer: University of Pennsylvania (Koo/Steager, Center for Innovation & Precision Dentistry)
sources.title: Shapeshifting microrobots can brush and floss teeth | Penn Today
sources.claim: Automated plaque/biofilm removal by magnetically driven microrobots has been shown only in the laboratory on mock and extracted human teeth mounted to mimic mouth position; no patient use.
sources.transferJustification: Related task = biofilm removal. Externally steered by magnetic fields (autonomy unclear) and demonstrated in vitro on extracted teeth, so it cannot substantiate completion of a clinical prophylaxis, which also requires calculus removal, polishing and patient management.

sources.system: Hybrid force-tracking impedance-controlled autonomous tooth-brushing robot
sources.title: Hybrid Force Tracking Impedance Control-based Autonomous Robotic System for Tooth Brushing Assistance of Disabled People
sources.claim: The closest robotic 'tooth cleaning' on people is a laboratory autonomous assistive tooth-brushing arm for disabled users with force/impedance control — brushing only, not professional scaling, polishing or fluoride/sealant application.
sources.transferJustification: Related task = assisted toothbrushing. Brushing plaque from accessible surfaces is far below hygienist prophylaxis (subgingival calculus removal, polishing, assessment), and the work is a lab prototype, so it does not substantiate completion of any clinical instance.

sources.title: Hesytech | AI-Guided Robotic Dental Hygiene
sources.claim: A commercial 'AI-guided robotic dental hygiene' offering exists only as a development-stage announcement, with no demonstrated procedure on patients.
sources.transferJustification: Directly on-task (robotic scaling/polishing) but roadmap-stage only; per the evidence rules an announcement of intent cannot support a positive capability judgment.

sources.title: Dental health education through the brushing ROBOTUTOR: A new learning experience - PubMed
sources.claim: Robot/media-mediated dental health education has not been shown to match clinician-delivered instruction; the evaluated modes underperformed clinician demonstration.
sources.transferJustification: Directly on-task (oral health education delivery). Cited as the only located evaluation of a robotic dental-education device; it does not substantiate worker-quality substitution for hygienist-delivered instruction.

tasks.label: Chart conditions of decay and disease for diagnosis and treatment by dentist.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Routine recall/prophylaxis visit in a general dental practice: hygienist records six-point probing depths, recession, bleeding points, mobility and furcation for each tooth into the practice-management software (e.g., Dentrix, Eaglesoft, Open Dental) via keyboard, voice-activated charting, or by calling numbers to an assistant.

Restorative/hard-tissue charting in a general practice: recording existing restorations, crowns, missing teeth, and suspected caries or defective margins observed during the hygiene appointment and on radiographs onto the odontogram, flagged for the dentist's confirmation at the exam.

New-patient comprehensive documentation: full-mouth periodontal chart plus restorative chart, soft-tissue/oral-pathology findings, caries risk assessment, radiographic interpretation notes, and periodontal disease classification entered in the electronic health record before the dentist's diagnosis.

Charting in institutional or specialty settings (periodontal practice, community/FQHC clinic, school sealant program, hospital, military or correctional dental clinic), often on standardized forms or portable/tablet software, sometimes paper-based, with a recorder assisting.

Post-treatment documentation and chart maintenance: writing narrative clinical notes on conditions found, comparing to prior charts to note changes, flagging areas for the dentist's review, correcting or verifying previously charted conditions, and attaching intraoral photos/radiographs to the record.

tasks.label: Expose and develop x-ray film.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Recall/prophy visit in a general dental operatory: hygienist drapes the cooperative adult patient with a lead apron, selects exposure factors, seats 2-4 bitewing receptors (sensor/PSP/film) in holders against the posterior teeth, has the patient bite and hold, aligns the tube head/PID to the beam-aiming ring, exposes each image from behind the barrier, then processes/reviews the images, retakes any with cone cuts or overlap, and saves them to the chart.

Individual periapical images on an adult (suspected caries, periapical pathology, endodontic check, implant site) in the operatory: receptor placed apically in the palate or floor of the mouth, angulation adapted to individual anatomy (shallow palate, tori, gag reflex, crowding), tube aligned by paralleling or bisecting technique, exposed, processed and checked for apex coverage.

Full-mouth series (14-20 intraoral images) on a new adult patient in the operatory: sequential receptor placements in all sextants including anterior and third-molar regions, repeated repositioning of holder and tube head, patient comfort/gag management over 15-20 minutes, all images processed, mounted and checked for diagnostic quality.

Extraoral imaging in the office's pano/CBCT room: patient prepped (jewelry, glasses, dentures removed, apron placed), positioned standing or seated with chin rest, bite stick and temple clamps, midsagittal and Frankfort planes aligned with the positioning lasers, tongue-to-palate instruction given, machine program selected and exposure cycle run, image reviewed for ghosting/positioning errors.

Pediatric patient (age 4-10) in a general or pediatric operatory: size 0/1 receptors, behavior guidance and reassurance, quick placement in a small mouth with an active tongue, occasional parent assistance, reduced exposure settings, images processed and retakes minimized to limit dose.

Radiographs on patients with limited cooperation or access outside a standard operatory - a nursing-home resident in a wheelchair or bed, or a child in a school-based mobile clinic - using a handheld portable X-ray unit and PSP plates, working around limited mouth opening, tremor, seating and room layout that differ at every site.

sources.title: Perceptive completes automated dental procedure with AI-driven robot
sources.claim: Perceptive's AI-driven dental robot completed a fully automated crown preparation on a human patient in a dental clinic, showing that a robot arm can work autonomously inside a live patient's mouth; the procedure was a one-off demonstration, the system is still under development, and it uses OCT scanning rather than X-ray imaging - it does not place radiographic receptors or align an X-ray tube.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic tooth preparation in the mouth. It shows intraoral robotic manipulation in a dental operatory, but the workpiece is a rigidly braced single tooth cut from a pre-made 3D plan; it does not demonstrate seating a rigid image receptor against soft palatal/floor-of-mouth tissue, managing the tongue and gag reflex, or aligning an X-ray beam to the receptor plane, so it does not transfer to exposing a radiographic series.

sources.title: Autonomous swab robot for naso- and oropharyngeal COVID-19 screening | Scientific Reports
sources.claim: The SR-NOCS force-controlled robot autonomously inserted swabs into the nose and oropharynx of human subjects in two clinical studies totalling 52 suspected COVID-19 patients, with results correlating with manual sampling - the closest demonstrated autonomous robotic manipulation inside a human mouth.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: inserting an instrument into a patient's mouth autonomously. It transfers only partially: the swab follows a single midline path to the pharyngeal wall, whereas an intraoral radiograph requires seating a rigid rectangular receptor parallel to a specified tooth's long axis, retracting soft tissue, having the patient bite to hold it, and then aligning the collimated beam to within a few degrees - none of which is demonstrated.

sources.title: GRMC Installs New Twin Robotic X-Ray System | Guadalupe Regional Medical Center
sources.claim: The Multitom Rax twin robotic ... uses two ceiling-mounted robotic arms that automatically position and align the X-ray tube and flat-panel detector in hospital imaging rooms; it is FDA-cleared and installed in US hospitals, but it automates tube/detector alignment only - a radiographer still prepares and positions the patient and there is no intraoral capability.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic positioning of X-ray hardware around a human patient in a structured clinical room. It substantiates automated source/detector alignment but not the receptor placement, patient positioning or exposure decisions that constitute the hygienist's radiographic task.

sources.system: Velopex Intra-X automatic dental X-ray film processor
sources.title: Velopex - Intra-X X-Ray Film Processor (Dental City)
sources.claim: Automatic dental film processors develop exposed intraoral film unattended once the film is fed in, delivering dry finished radiographs in about four minutes; they automate only the developing sub-step, with a human unwrapping and feeding the film.

sources.title: Dental CR scanner, Dental phosphor plate scanner - All medical device manufacturers (MedicalExpo)
sources.claim: Automated intraoral phosphor-plate scanners read, digitise and erase an exposed PSP plate automatically after the operator inserts it, automating the modern equivalent of film developing but not the exposure work.

tasks.label: Attend continuing education courses to maintain or update skills.

tasks.label: Apply fluorides or other cavity preventing agents to arrest dental decay.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Routine fluoride varnish on a cooperative adult or teen after prophylaxis in a private general-practice operatory: isolate and dry the dentition with gauze/air and suction, paint a unit dose of varnish over all surfaces of 28-32 teeth with a microbrush in 1-3 minutes while managing tongue, lips and cheeks, then give post-op instructions.

Fluoride varnish on a young child (age 1-6) in a pediatric or general office, often knee-to-knee or in a partly reclined chair, with a squirming, crying or gagging patient, short working windows, primary dentition, and a caregiver present.

Tray-delivered fluoride (APF gel or foam) or 5-minute in-office gel treatment: load and seat upper and lower trays over the arches, keep the patient upright with saliva ejector in place for ~4 minutes, remove trays and wipe excess.

Silver diamine fluoride applied to specific active carious lesions (often root caries in elderly or special-needs patients, or arrested-caries treatment in children): protect lips/gingiva with petroleum jelly, isolate with cotton rolls, dry the lesion, apply one drop with a microbrush for ~1 minute to the lesion only, blot excess, avoid staining soft tissue.

Community/portable program: fluoride varnish applied in a school gym or classroom, Head Start center, mobile dental van, or nursing-home bedside, to a queue of children or to frail residents, using portable lighting and no dental unit, often with minimal chair support.

sources.title: Perceptive Completes World's First Fully Automated Dental Procedure on a Human Using AI-Driven Robotic System | Business Wire
sources.claim: Perceptive's AI-driven robotic arm performed an automated crown preparation on a live human patient in a dental setting - the closest demonstrated robotic intraoral work on a conscious patient - but it is a single-tooth cutting procedure, not application of a topical agent, and is not cleared for sale in the US.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic crown preparation on a patient's tooth in a dental operatory. It shares the objects (teeth of a conscious patient) and exceeds the precision needed for varnish application, but it operates on one rigidly referenced tooth with a bur; it does not dispense or spread a coating over all surfaces of a full dentition, manage saliva, or retract tongue and cheeks, so it does not substantiate completion of this task.

sources.developer: Perceptive Technologies with Harvard School of Dental Medicine
sources.title: First in-human intervention using a semi-automated robot for tooth restorative treatment
sources.claim: Perceptive's semi-automated robotic tooth preparation system completed preplanned crown preparations in six human patients, confirming the state of the art in robotic intraoral treatment is single-tooth restorative preparation, not preventive agent application.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic tooth preparation in human patients. Same environment and objects, higher precision, but the workflow is planned per single tooth and described as semi-automated under clinician supervision; nothing in it covers dispensing and painting fluoride varnish or SDF across tooth surfaces.

sources.system: Autonomous dental implant robotic system (FZ-DISAS-I; Yakebot)
sources.developer: Sichuan Fengzhun Robot Technology Co; Beijing Yakebot Technology
sources.title: Accuracy of an autonomous dental implant robotic system in dental implant surgery - The Journal of Prosthetic Dentistry
sources.claim: Autonomous dental implant robots (Yakebot, FZ-DISAS-I and similar r-CAIS systems) place implants inside patients' mouths in dental clinics under optical tracking with a tooth-borne positioning marker, showing autonomous intraoral tool positioning on live patients, but only at a single planned osteotomy site with a human surgeon opening and retracting the field.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous intraoral drilling/implant placement in a dental chair. It establishes that robots can work safely inside a conscious patient's mouth in a clinic, but it depends on CBCT planning and a rigid tooth-borne marker, addresses one site, and involves no coating application or full-arch surface coverage, so it does not substantiate fluoride application.

sources.title: Swarm of tiny robots scrub teeth | National Institutes of Health (NIH)
sources.claim: Magnetically actuated microrobot swarms for plaque and biofilm removal remain proof-of-concept on mock and extracted human teeth; researchers state clinical testing and an in-mouth device are still to come.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated in-mouth cleaning/antimicrobial treatment. It targets the same surfaces but has not been performed in a patient's mouth and does not deliver a professionally applied fluoride agent, so it cannot support completion of this task at any tier.

sources.title: World's First Oral Care Robot Brushes Your Teeth Automatically
sources.claim: The nearest automated in-mouth consumer device, the g.eN mouthpiece toothbrushing robot, runs a preset brushing cycle after the user bites down; it performs home brushing, not a professional topical fluoride treatment, and must be placed by the user.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated in-mouth brushing with a mouthpiece. The device is inserted and held by the person, delivers dentifrice rather than a professionally applied varnish/gel/SDF dose, and provides no clinician-quality coverage verification, so it does not substantiate the hygienist's fluoride application task.

tasks.label: Maintain dental equipment and sharpen and sterilize dental instruments.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Full instrument reprocessing cycle in a general/periodontal practice: hygienist carries contaminated cassettes and loose hand instruments (scalers, curettes, mirrors, explorers, probes) from the operatory to the sterilization area, rinses/runs the ultrasonic or instrument washer, dries and inspects, packages into pouches or wrapped cassettes with chemical indicators, seals and labels, loads and runs the steam autoclave, unloads and stores sterile packs.

Sharpening hand instruments: restoring the cutting edges of sickle scalers, universal and Gracey curettes with an Arkansas/ceramic stone or a motorized sharpener, judging wear, holding correct blade-to-stone angle, preserving instrument contour, testing edge on an acrylic stick, and retiring instruments worn too thin.

Handpiece, prophy angle and ultrasonic scaler upkeep: flushing and purging waterlines through the handpiece, external cleaning, internal cleaning/lubrication (oil device or automatic maintenance unit), changing and torquing ultrasonic inserts/tips, checking O-rings and water flow, then bagging and autoclaving the handpiece.

In-situ dental unit and operatory equipment maintenance: shocking and flushing dental unit waterlines, replacing treatment straws/filters, running evacuation-line cleaner through HVE and saliva ejector, emptying and cleaning suction traps and amalgam separator, refilling self-contained water bottles, wiping/checking chair, light, and x-ray arm.

Sterilizer and sterilization-area upkeep and monitoring: cleaning/descaling the autoclave chamber and trays, draining and refilling distilled water reservoirs, replacing gaskets and filters, running weekly biological (spore) tests and reading results, checking chemical indicators, logging cycles, and troubleshooting failed cycles or error codes.

sources.system: Steelco ATS / M-ATS Self-Driving Robot Transfer System and R-APPIT packing robot
sources.title: Automation - SteelcoBelimed
sources.claim: SteelcoBelimed sells CSSD automation in which shuttle/self-driving transfer systems automatically load and unload washer-disinfectors and sterilizers, and the R-APPIT packing robot wraps, tapes and labels instrument trays without manual intervention — i.e. machine loading and sterile packaging of reprocessed instruments in a purpose-built automated line.
sources.transferJustification: Related task is hospital surgical-instrument reprocessing: the same washing, packaging, sterilizing and storing chain applied to comparable stainless hand instruments, at equal or higher regulatory quality, so performance carries to dental cassettes/instrument packs.

sources.system: Gibotech automated sterilization central (CSSD robot cells, automated sterile storage)
sources.title: Automated sterilization central | Gibotech
sources.claim: Gibotech has installed robotic sterile-processing centrals in operating hospitals (Køge 2011, later Rigshospitalet and Herlev), using articulated robots, mobile robots, vision and automated sterile-instrument storage to handle surgical instrument loads through the sterile workflow.
sources.transferJustification: Related task is hospital instrument reprocessing/sterile storage; the robots handle instrument baskets and sterile packs through washers, sterilizers and storage — the same physical chain a dental hygienist performs with cassettes.

sources.system: Autonomous instrument tray assembly system (Stäubli TX2-60L + YOLO12/ResNet perception)
sources.title: Towards Autonomous Instrument Tray Assembly for Sterile Processing Applications (arXiv:2602.01679)
sources.claim: A fully automated robotic cell ... Stäubli TX2-60L arm, vision-based instrument recognition and a custom gripper autonomously sorts individual surgical instruments and packs them into sterile trays, with high perception accuracy and fewer instrument-to-instrument collisions than human-assembled trays.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: sterile processing tray assembly. The objects (small stainless hand instruments), the sorting/inspection judgment and the packing precision match dental cassette set-up, so capability transfers to dental instrument packaging.

sources.system: RIF Robotics autonomous surgical tray assembly system
sources.title: RIF Robotics pioneers autonomous surgical tray assembly - Catalyst by Wellstar
sources.claim: RIF Robotics ran a pilot inside a hospital sterile processing department in which its vision-trained robotic arm autonomously assembled a minor surgical tray alongside sterile processing technicians.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: sterile processing instrument sorting/tray assembly in a hospital SPD; same class of small stainless instruments and identification/placement accuracy needed for dental instrument set-up after sterilization.

sources.system: Berger RSP series robotic grinding/sharpening cells (e.g. RSP/1S, RSP/2B/1S/1L)
sources.title: Robotic grinding and polishing systems | Berger Gruppe
sources.claim: Berger Gruppe builds and sells robotic sharpening cells in which the robot guides the workpiece against sharpening/grinding stations, including a cell for sharpening surgical micro scissors and blades and a cell that grinds and sharpens manicure instruments — fine steel hand instruments of the same scale as dental curettes.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic sharpening of surgical micro scissors and manicure instruments — comparable object size, steel hardness and edge-angle precision to dental scalers/curettes, performed with the workpiece fixtured in a robot cell.

sources.title: Omnisharp Robotic Sharpening Machine • Argus
sources.claim: The Omnisharp is a commercially offered fully automated dual-arm robotic sharpening machine: operators load used blades in trays, and the system scans each blade's profile, sets sharpening angles automatically, sharpens, and flags worn or damaged blades for removal.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: re-sharpening worn cutting edges of used hand tools presented in trays, including judging wear and retiring damaged blades — the same decisions a hygienist makes when sharpening dull curettes, with the work fixtured for the machine.

sources.system: FANUC LR Mate 200iD with force sensing (robotic material removal / sharpening)
sources.title: Robotic Cutting, Deburring, Polishing, Buffing & More | FANUC America
sources.claim: FANUC sells force-controlled robotic material-removal cells in which a small six-axis robot with force sensing performs automated grinding and polishing to precise, repeatable geometry.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: force-controlled robotic grinding/sharpening of hardened steel to a specified geometry — the contact-force and angle control needed to restore a curette's cutting edge without altering its contour.

sources.system: Remtec robotic random part picking / machine tending cells (FANUC + Cognex vision) at S.S. White Technologies
sources.title: Case Study: S.S. White Technologies Vertical Pouch Process Benefits from Robotic Automation
sources.claim: Remtec designed and delivered vision-guided robotic part-picking cells for S.S. White Dental that load small dental bur components into process fixtures and into pouch (packaging) machines and apply color-code stripes.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic picking and fixturing of small dental instruments (burs) and feeding them to pouch machines — the same object class, gripping precision and pouch-packaging step as dental instrument packaging before sterilization.

sources.system: W&H Assistina TWIN automatic handpiece reprocessing/maintenance device
sources.title: W&H - Perfectly maintained in just 10 seconds
sources.claim: The W&H Assistina TWIN is a commercially deployed automatic dental handpiece maintenance device that, in a 10-second machine-controlled cycle, flushes the spray channels with cleaning solution and oils all rotating parts, processing up to 360 instruments per hour before sterilization.

tasks.label: Maintain patient recall system.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

tasks.label: Feel lymph nodes under patient's chin to detect swelling or tenderness that could indicate presence of oral cancer.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Routine adult recall/prophylaxis visit in a private general dental practice: patient reclined in the operatory chair, hygienist bimanually palpates submental and submandibular nodes as part of the extraoral head-and-neck screening, judging size, mobility, consistency, and asking the patient about tenderness; findings charted as WNL or flagged.

New-patient or high-risk adult exam in a group practice/DSO: challenging anatomy (obese or short neck, heavy beard, elderly loose tissue, prior neck surgery or radiation, tobacco/alcohol user); hygienist must distinguish a firm fixed node from normal glands or muscle and re-palpate a previously noted area for change.

Pediatric or adolescent patient in a dental practice or school-based sealant/hygiene program: small anatomy, wriggling or apprehensive child, frequently soft mobile reactive nodes from recent infection that must be distinguished from concerning findings and explained to the parent.

Community health center, hospital-based or military/institutional dental clinic: medically complex, disabled, or wheelchair-seated patients, sometimes with limited neck mobility, language barriers, or needing gentle handling; palpation done as part of a documented oral cancer screening protocol.

Portable/mobile settings: nursing-home bedside, school gym or van-based mobile clinic, or community health-fair screening; patient seated in a portable chair, wheelchair, or bed, variable lighting and positioning, hygienist standing or kneeling to reach under the chin.

sources.system: FARUS (fully autonomous robotic ultrasound system for thyroid scanning)
sources.developer: Su et al., Chinese research group (published in Nature Communications)
sources.title: A fully autonomous robotic ultrasound system for thyroid scanning | Nature Communications
sources.claim: The most advanced autonomous robots that contact a human neck perform ultrasound imaging (thyroid scanning), not manual palpation; FARUS autonomously scans the thyroid region of human participants and identifies nodules, but produces images rather than a palpation finding and cannot elicit or judge tenderness.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous force-controlled contact with the human neck to detect abnormalities. Transfer fails for this task: the output is a sonographic image of the thyroid, not a tactile assessment of submental/submandibular nodes, and no tenderness or node-mobility judgment is produced.

sources.system: Collaborative robotic arm palpation with Hunt-Crossley viscoelastic estimation
sources.title: Towards Robotised Palpation for Cancer Detection through Online Tissue Viscoelastic Characterisation with a Collaborative Robotic Arm
sources.claim: Robotic palpation aimed at cancer detection is demonstrated only on silicone samples with embedded hard intrusions standing in for tumors, on a lab benchtop with a collaborative arm — not on human patients.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic palpation to find stiff inclusions in soft tissue. It does not substantiate this task because the substrate is a silicone phantom, not a patient's neck, and no clinical-quality lymph node assessment is reported.

sources.system: SeeBelow robotic palpation and tactile exploration system
sources.title: SeeBelow: Sub-dermal 3D Reconstruction of Tumors with Surgical Robotic Palpation and Tactile Exploration
sources.claim: State-of-the-art tactile tumor localization by robotic palpation is performed on surgical training phantoms with 3D-printed rigid tumors, using a Franka Panda arm with a custom force-sensing probe.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic tactile search for embedded masses. Does not transfer: rigid printed tumors in a bench phantom differ from small, mobile, variably firm cervical nodes in living tissue, and no human-subject testing is reported.

sources.title: Autonomous Robotic Tissue Palpation and Abnormalities Characterisation via Ergodic Exploration
sources.claim: Continuing 2026 work on autonomous robotic palpation remains at the level of force-sensor-based stiffness mapping of tissue samples in the laboratory, framed as motivation toward detecting tumours or swollen lymph nodes rather than a clinical capability.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous palpation for abnormality detection. Does not transfer: it maps stiffness over tissue samples in a lab and reports no examination of a human neck or clinical lymph node findings.

sources.system: iApp autonomous inspection, auscultation, percussion and palpation platform
sources.developer: Academic group (published in Frontiers in Physiology)
sources.title: iApp: An Autonomous Inspection, Auscultation, Percussion, and Palpation Platform
sources.claim: Automated physical-examination platforms that touch human subjects (inspection, auscultation, percussion, palpation of the abdomen) remain proof-of-concept and only classify anatomical regions rather than detect pathology.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous machine palpation of a human body region during a physical exam. Does not transfer: the system classifies abdominal regions on healthy subjects and detects no masses, swelling, or tenderness.

tasks.label: Administer local anesthetic agents.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: General dental practice operatory: before quadrant scaling and root planing, the hygienist reviews health history/vitals, dries the mucobuccal fold, applies topical, then gives one or two maxillary buccal infiltrations (2% lidocaine with epinephrine), aspirating before deposit and testing for profound anesthesia; adult, cooperative patient in the dental chair.

Mandibular anesthesia for lower-quadrant root planing: inferior alveolar nerve block plus lingual and long buccal injections located by palpated landmarks (coronoid notch, pterygomandibular raphe), needle advanced ~20-25 mm to bone contact, aspiration in two planes, slow deposit, and supplemental re-injection if the block is incomplete.

Localized/supplemental anesthesia: greater palatine, nasopalatine, or intraligamentary (PDL) injection at a sensitive site, often with a computer-controlled delivery handpiece; very small tissue targets, dense palatal tissue, high patient sensitivity, careful pressure and volume control.

Non-injectable local anesthetic: placing benzocaine/lidocaine topical gel on a cotton applicator at a specific dried mucosal site pre-injection, or delivering subgingival lidocaine-prilocaine periodontal gel (Oraqix) with a blunt applicator tip into pockets before scaling, with dwell time and removal.

Anxious, pediatric, or medically complex patient in a community/school-based or dental-school clinic: dose limited by weight and medical history, patient may move, gag, or become faint; hygienist repositions, reassures, monitors for adverse reaction (syncope, positive aspiration, allergy) and adjusts technique mid-procedure.

sources.title: US-Based AI Company Completes World's First Fully Automated Dental Procedure on a Human - Oral Health Group
sources.claim: Perceptive's AI-driven dental robot performed an autonomous crown preparation on a human patient in a dental clinic; its demonstrated scope is hard-tissue restorative work (imaging and drilling), not administering local anesthetic.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous intraoral tooth preparation. It shows a robot can work inside a patient's mouth on hard tissue, but the demonstrated capability does not include locating soft-tissue injection landmarks, aspirating, or depositing anesthetic, so it does not substantiate this task.

sources.system: FZ-DISAS-I autonomous dental implant robotic system (ADIRS)
sources.developer: Sichuan Fengzhun Robot Technology Co., Ltd
sources.title: Accuracy of an autonomous dental implant robotic system in dental implant surgery - The Journal of Prosthetic Dentistry
sources.claim: In clinical use of autonomous dental implant robots, local anesthesia is administered by the human clinician before the robot begins; the robot's autonomous work is preprogrammed osteotomy drilling and implant placement under surgeon supervision.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous intraoral implant drilling in living patients. Same environment (dental operatory) and same patient anatomy, yet the article records that the local anesthesia step is performed by a human before the robot operates, showing the injection is outside current robotic dental capability.

sources.system: Computer-controlled local anesthetic delivery (CCLAD) systems (e.g., The Wand/STA, Dentapen)
sources.title: Inferior Alveolar Nerve Block - StatPearls - NCBI Bookshelf
sources.claim: The most automated dental anesthesia products in clinical use are computer-controlled delivery systems: clinician-held handpieces that regulate flow rate, while the clinician still selects the site, inserts and holds the needle, and aspirates.
sources.transferJustification: This is the same task performed with the most automated equipment available; the device automates only fluid delivery through a hand-held handpiece, so it cannot support autonomous completion.

sources.title: Vitestro Unveils Aletta: The World's First Autonomous Robotic Phlebotomy Device (ARPD)
sources.claim: Aletta is a CE-marked autonomous robotic phlebotomy device that identifies veins with AI-driven Doppler ultrasound and performs robot-controlled needle insertion for blood draws in hospital and laboratory settings; its target is arm veins, not intraoral injection sites.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous needle insertion into a living person. It is the closest deployed analog, but it targets a superficial forearm vein imaged by ultrasound with the arm fixtured; intraoral anesthesia requires landmark-based deep soft-tissue targeting inside a mobile open mouth with aspiration, which this system has not been shown to do.

sources.developer: Lifeline Robotics / University of Southern Denmark
sources.title: Lifeline Robotics automates COVID-19 human test capacity
sources.claim: The closest autonomous robot for intraoral soft-tissue contact is a throat swab robot that inserts a swab into a human's mouth, developed in 2020 as a research/startup prototype; it samples the pharynx rather than placing medication at a specified mucosal site.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous insertion of an applicator into a patient's mouth. It shows oral-cavity entry is feasible, but the pharynx is a large midline target and the demonstration involves no site-specific drying, metered gel placement, dwell time, or drug delivery, so it does not substantiate topical anesthetic administration.

tasks.label: Remove excess cement from coronal surfaces of teeth.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Chairside cleanup immediately after the dentist seats a permanent crown, bridge, onlay or veneer on a cooperative adult: the hygienist/assistant wipes and picks away extruded resin or RMGI luting cement from the coronal surfaces, margins and interproximal contacts with an explorer/scaler and floss during the short gel-phase window, under mirror, air and suction, leaving no residue at the gingival margin.

Recall prophylaxis appointment where set, hardened cement remnants are found on coronal surfaces around older crowns, bands or restorations; removed with hand scalers and ultrasonic tip amid saliva, bleeding gingiva and limited direct vision, on several teeth, without scratching restorations or enamel.

Post-orthodontic clean-up after band/bracket removal on an adolescent: residual cement and adhesive removed from labial and interproximal coronal enamel of many teeth using hand scaler and slow-speed carbide bur, followed by polishing, with no visible remnant and no enamel gouging.

Pediatric or special-needs patient (stainless steel crown, space maintainer or orthodontic band just cemented): excess cement removed from coronal surfaces in a small, moving mouth with a short cooperation window, requiring behavior management and rapid work.

Excess cement at and just apical to the gingival margin of an implant-supported cement-retained crown: meticulous removal with plastic/titanium-safe instruments and floss, verified by explorer, floss shreds and sometimes a radiograph, avoiding scratching the abutment or traumatizing peri-implant tissue.

sources.title: Fully-automatic robot dentist performs world's first human procedure (New Atlas)
sources.claim: Perceptive's dental robot autonomously performed a crown preparation (cutting coronal tooth structure) on a live human volunteer in a dental operatory, guided by handheld OCT volumetric imaging — the most advanced demonstrated autonomous work on coronal tooth surfaces.
sources.transferJustification: Related task = robotic crown preparation. It shows autonomous instrument work on coronal tooth surfaces in a live mouth, but it removes tooth structure to a pre-planned 3D geometry; excess-cement removal instead requires perceiving a thin, irregular film of set cement at margins and interproximal contacts and selectively removing it (including with floss) without abrading enamel or gingiva. No such perception/manipulation has been demonstrated, so the transfer does not carry.

sources.title: Perceptive | Meet Modern Dentistry (company site)
sources.claim: Perceptive's robotic/OCT system remains a prototype: it is not FDA-cleared and not offered for sale in the US, so there is no deployed system performing restorative clean-up chairside.

sources.developer: University of Salerno (Pagliara, Petrone, Ferrentino, Russo et al.)
sources.title: Haptic bilateral teleoperation system for free-hand dental procedures (arXiv:2503.21288)
sources.claim: The state of the art for robotic free-hand periodontal instrumentation (scaling/root planing with an ultrasonic scaler on coronal/root surfaces) is a haptic bilateral teleoperation system validated only in vitro on a dental model with artificial calculus; the authors state robotic solutions for free-hand dental procedures are lacking.
sources.transferJustification: Related task = removing deposits (calculus) from tooth surfaces with a hand/ultrasonic instrument, mechanically the closest analogue to removing set cement. The system is human-teleoperated and tested only on a phantom, so it cannot support a positive judgment for autonomous cement removal.

sources.developer: Yakebot (Beijing) / reviewed in Int. J. Oral Science
sources.title: The evolution of robotics: research and application progress of dental implant robotic systems
sources.claim: Autonomous dental robots that do work in clinics on patients are confined to implant surgery: Yakebot autonomously drills the implant bed and places implants along a CBCT-planned path using a rigid marker splint, i.e., a fixtured, pre-planned bone-drilling task rather than deposit clean-up on tooth surfaces.
sources.transferJustification: Related task = autonomous intraoral robotic surgery on patients in a dental operatory. It substantiates that robots can work in the mouth under rigid registration, but only for pre-planned osteotomy trajectories; it provides no capability for detecting and removing residual cement from coronal surfaces, interproximal contacts or gingival margins.

tasks.label: Conduct dental health clinics for community groups to augment services of dentist.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: School-based preventive clinic: hygienist hauls portable chairs, lights and handpieces into an elementary school gym or classroom, screens 20-60 children over a day, charts findings, applies fluoride varnish and places pit-and-fissure sealants, manages squirming/anxious kids, and sends referral letters home.

Community health fair or church/community-center event: booth with mirror and headlamp, brief visual screenings and oral-cancer checks on walk-up adults of all ages, one-on-one brushing/flossing instruction, distribution of toothbrush kits, triage and referral to the supervising dentist; crowded, noisy, no dental chair.

Head Start / preschool or WIC site: 'lift-the-lip' caries screening of toddlers held knee-to-knee with a caregiver, fluoride varnish application, supervised toothbrushing drills, and parent/teacher education, with consent forms and records for the sponsoring program.

Long-term care facility clinic: oral assessments of frail residents in wheelchairs or beds (some with dementia or resistant behavior), portable prophylaxis and denture cleaning, palliative care of sore tissues, plus in-service training of nursing aides.

Mobile dental van or portable clinic day at a rural site, shelter, or migrant camp: full prophylaxis including ultrasonic and hand scaling of calculus, radiographs, sealants and varnish for a scheduled roster of patients under a dentist's general supervision.

Oral health education session for a community group (senior center, scout troop, PTA, high-school health class): presentation, typodont brushing/flossing demonstration, denture and tobacco-cessation counseling, Q&A, handing out supplies and screening/consent forms.

sources.title: Perceptive Completes World's First Fully Automated Dental Procedure on a Human Using AI-Driven Robotic System
sources.claim: Perceptive's AI-driven robotic arm autonomously prepared a tooth for a crown on a human patient in a dental operatory - the only demonstrated autonomous intraoral robotic procedure on a person; it is a single restorative step, not screening, prophylaxis, varnish/sealant placement, or running a clinic session.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic crown preparation on a seated dental patient. It shares the intraoral workspace and a live human 'workpiece', but covers one drilling step on one cooperative adult in a fixed operatory; it does not transfer to screening/charting, calculus removal, varnish or sealant placement, child or frail-elder management, or setting up and running a community clinic session.

sources.title: Perceptive | Meet Modern Dentistry
sources.claim: The Perceptive robotic system remains a prototype without FDA marketing clearance and is not available for sale in the ..., so it is not in routine clinical service anywhere, let alone in community outreach clinics.
sources.transferJustification: Same system as evidence 0; establishes maturity limits relevant to whether it could deliver worker-quality output in any setting.

sources.title: Neocis brings in $20M for robotic dental surgeries - The Robot Report
sources.claim: The only FDA-cleared dental robot in wide clinical use (40,000+ implants placed) is explicitly non-autonomous: the surgeon retains control of the instrument at all times, so it cannot substitute for an operator.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robot-guided dental implant placement in a dental operatory. It is the most mature dental robot, but it is human-guided haptic assistance, so it cannot support any positive autonomy judgment for hygienist clinic work.

sources.title: RobOralScan: Learning Active Intraoral Scanning for Robotic Dental Reconstruction
sources.claim: Autonomous robotic intraoral scanning (a prerequisite for robotic examination/screening) is still a research problem evaluated on reconstructed models, with the authors noting that real in-mouth deployment adds errors from restricted access, soft tissue and patient motion.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous robot-arm intraoral scanning to reconstruct teeth and gums, i.e. the sensing step of a screening exam. Even this sub-step is not yet validated in live mouths, so it cannot substantiate completion of a screening-and-treatment clinic.

sources.title: At last: A fully robotic toothbrush for disabled patients
sources.claim: Automated oral-hygiene hardware that exists commercially is limited to mouthpiece-style robotic toothbrushes for home/caregiver use; these brush teeth but do not perform hygienist services such as calculus scaling, screening, varnish or sealant placement.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated toothbrushing of a person's dentition. Objects and workspace overlap (a live mouth), but the device is placed and supervised by a person and performs only brushing, so it cannot deliver the diagnostic, preventive and record-keeping output of a community clinic.

sources.title: Tooth Bot: A Robot for Enhancing Children's Awareness of Cavity Prevention (ACM/IEEE HRI 2025)
sources.claim: Robots used for children's oral-health education are single-purpose demonstration aids that visualize brushing on a tooth model; they act as teaching props rather than conducting a clinic session.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robot-delivered toothbrushing education for children. Closest evidence to the education-only portion of the task, but it is a tabletop model-plus-toothbrush prop in a study, not a system that runs a group session, hands out supplies, screens participants, or answers questions at worker quality.

tasks.label: Make impressions for study casts.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: General dental practice operatory: hygienist takes upper and lower alginate impressions of a cooperative adult for study casts (bleaching trays, nightguard, records). Selects/tries in a stock tray, mixes alginate to correct consistency, seats the loaded tray over the arch while retracting lips and coaching the patient's breathing, holds until set, snaps it out without tearing, rinses/disinfects, and boxes or pours it in stone.

Same operatory, digital route: hygienist captures a full-arch digital impression with an intraoral scanner (e.g., iTero/TRIOS) for study models - retracting cheek and tongue, keeping the field dry and defogged, sweeping occlusal/buccal/lingual surfaces of both arches plus bite registration, then reviewing for voids and rescanning gaps before sending the file.

Orthodontic or pediatric practice: impressions or scans of a child/adolescent for ortho records and retainers - small mouth, fixed appliances or brackets present, patient squirming, gagging or talking; hygienist must reassure, re-seat, and often repeat a failed impression within the appointment.

Challenging adult patient: strong gag reflex, limited opening, medically complex, elderly, partially edentulous with mobile teeth, tori, or removable prostheses; requires tray modification with wax/rope, careful seating and staged removal to avoid dislodging teeth or prostheses, sometimes seated upright with topical anesthetic.

Portable/community setting: school-based program, nursing home resident's room, mobile van or public-health outreach clinic - hygienist takes alginate impressions with portable equipment in a room not built as a dental operatory, with improvised patient positioning, variable lighting, and models poured later off-site.

sources.title: The future of dentistry through robotics | British Dental Journal
sources.claim: Perceptive's robot performed a fully automated crown preparation on a live human patient in a dental setting, showing autonomous robotic tool work inside the mouth; the 3D record of the dentition, however, is acquired with a clinician-held scanner.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic crown preparation. It shares the environment (a live patient's mouth in a dental operatory) and demands high precision, but it is a drilling task on a single tooth held by a rigid intraoral brace; the arch record itself is captured by a hand-held scanner, so it does not substantiate autonomous acquisition of a full-arch impression or scan.

sources.system: Perceptive dental robotics system (hand-held 3D volumetric/OCT scanner)
sources.title: Fully-Automatic Robot Dentist Performs World's First Human Procedure - Slashdot (citing New Atlas)
sources.claim: Perceptive's system acquires its 3D model of the mouth with a hand-held volumetric scanner operated by a person, not by the robot; the robot arm only executes the preparation.
sources.transferJustification: Directly relevant to this task: the digital-impression step of the most advanced clinical dental robot is performed by a human holding the scanner, indicating that impression/scan acquisition is not automated in any fielded system.

sources.system: RobOralScan (Franka Research 3 arm + Huvitz Lilivis SCAN intraoral scanner)
sources.title: RobOralScan: Learning Active Intraoral Scanning for Robotic Dental Reconstruction (arXiv:2606.26955)
sources.claim: RobOralScan is a reinforcement-learning policy for autonomous robotic intraoral scanning; trained in simulation and validated zero-shot on a bench setup where a Franka arm moved a commercial intraoral scanner around a jaw model, reported as a feasibility result.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic digital impression (intraoral scanning), the digital substitute for an alginate impression used to produce study models. Transfer is limited: hardware validation is on a static jaw model on a lab bench, simulated coverage is 92.58% with the scan criterion met in 8 of 10 episodes, and the authors describe only practical feasibility - not clinically accepted full-arch records on live patients with tongue, saliva and movement.

sources.system: Yakebot / Yomi dental implant robotic systems
sources.title: The evolution of robotics: research and application progress of dental implant robotic systems | International Journal of Oral Science
sources.claim: The most autonomous clinical intraoral robots (dental implant systems such as Yakebot) still operate under continuous surgeon supervision with pedal control, after rigid splint registration, and are confined to osteotomy drilling.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic intraoral implant drilling in live patients. It marks the ceiling of clinical intraoral robotics - supervised, splint-registered, single-site drilling - with no demonstrated handling of impression material, trays, or whole-arch soft-tissue retraction.

roles.description: Diagnose, treat, and help prevent diseases using a system of practice that is based on the natural healing capacity of individuals. May use physiological, psychological or mechanical methods. May also use natural medicines, prescription or legend drugs, foods, herbs, or other natural remedies.

tasks.label: Conduct physical examinations and physiological function tests for diagnostic purposes.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Comprehensive/routine physical exam of an adult in a naturopathic clinic exam room: patient gowns and moves between sitting/supine, physician takes vitals, auscultates heart and lungs through/around clothing, palpates abdomen and lymph nodes, inspects skin, performs HEENT exam with otoscope and ophthalmoscope, and integrates findings into a diagnostic impression.

Focused musculoskeletal/neurological exam in the clinic: palpation of spine and joints for tenderness and tissue texture, passive/active range-of-motion and end-feel, orthopedic special tests (e.g., shoulder impingement, straight-leg raise), deep tendon reflexes, strength and gait observation on a patient who moves and reports pain.

In-office instrumented physiological function tests that require applying equipment to the body and coaching the patient: 12-lead ECG electrode placement, spirometry with effort coaching, bioimpedance/body-composition electrodes, heart-rate-variability leads.
Baseline vital-sign measurement at intake or a recheck visit on a cooperative ambulatory adult: blood pressure, pulse, weight/BMI recorded into the chart.

Diagnostic specimen collection in the clinic's draw area: venipuncture for lab panels (tourniquet, vein selection, needle insertion, multiple vacuum tubes, withdrawal and hemostasis), plus occasional finger-stick capillary sampling or throat/nasal swab.

Traditional naturopathic hands-on assessments and sensitive/pediatric exams: radial pulse and tongue diagnosis, iridology, applied-kinesiology muscle testing, visceral palpation; breast, pelvic/Pap or prostate exam where licensed; exam of an infant or uncooperative child.

sources.claim: Lifeline Robotics built an autonomous throat-swabbing robot that collects oropharyngeal samples from a seated person without a clinician holding the swab.
sources.transferJustification: Same task family as clinic specimen collection: an instrument is inserted to a targeted anatomical site on a cooperative seated patient to obtain a diagnostic sample.

sources.system: Pursuant Health self-service health screening kiosk
sources.title: Collaborative study identifies method to make blood pressure monitoring more accessible

sources.transferJustification: Same measurement the clinician performs at intake (blood pressure, pulse, weight); the machine's actuated cuff performs the compression and reading, with the patient's arm presented to the fixed station.

sources.transferJustification: Auscultation is one sub-step of the physical exam; cited to show the state of the art for robot-applied exam instruments on a human torso.

sources.title: Aescape Secures $83M to Scale AI-Powered Robotic Massage Technology
sources.claim: Aescape's autonomous robotic massage tables scan the body and deliver force-controlled contact through arms without a human operator, and are being rolled out commercially to about 60 Equinox fitness locations.
sources.transferJustification: Closest deployed analogue to hands-on musculoskeletal work: autonomous, force-controlled contact with a person's back and limbs in a facility, but it delivers massage strokes and makes no diagnostic assessment.
