sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomously applying a diagnostic instrument to a patient's torso with force control; cited as the ceiling of demonstrated robot-applied diagnostic testing, which is imaging only.

tasks.label: Administer, dispense, or prescribe natural medicines, such as food or botanical extracts, herbs, dietary supplements, vitamins, nutraceuticals, and amino acids.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Clinic exam room, routine visit: after evaluating the patient the ND selects a natural-medicine regimen (multivitamin, fish oil, probiotic, botanical extract), counsels the patient verbally, and issues it as a written/EHR protocol or an online-dispensary (e.g., virtual dispensary) order that the patient fills elsewhere. The ND handles no product; the accepted output is a signed, documented order plus patient instructions.

In-office dispensary of the naturopathic clinic: for a patient leaving a visit, the ND or dispensary staff retrieves the specific bottled/boxed products named in the protocol from stock shelves, verifies them against the order, affixes a patient-specific label with dosing directions, bags them, hands them to the patient at the counter, and records the dispensing in the chart/POS.

Compounding bench in the clinic dispensary: preparing a patient-specific botanical formula - measuring and blending several liquid herbal tinctures by volume into a dispensing bottle, or weighing out bulk dried herbs / herbal granules into a tea or capsule blend - then capping, labeling with the patient's dosing instructions, and logging the formula.

Clinic infusion room: administering IV nutrient therapy (e.g., a Myers'-type vitamin/mineral cocktail). The ND draws up additives, mixes the bag, selects a vein and performs venipuncture/peripheral catheter placement, secures the line, starts and rate-adjusts the infusion, monitors the seated patient for 20-60 minutes for reactions, then discontinues, flushes and dresses the site.

Treatment room: administering an intramuscular or subcutaneous injection (B12/methylcobalamin, vitamin D, lipotropic/MIC, homeopathic biopuncture). The ND draws the dose from a multi-dose vial into a syringe, positions the patient, preps the deltoid or gluteal site, injects, withdraws, applies pressure/bandage, disposes of the sharp, and observes the patient briefly.

sources.title: iA's Smart Unit of Use enables 'seamless and efficient' Rx fulfillment
sources.claim: iA's Smart Unit of Use is a commercially deployed pharmacy robotic system that picks, labels, images and dispenses prepackaged items including prefilled bottles, liquids and OTC products - the same pick/label/hand-off pipeline used to dispense bottled supplements from a clinic dispensary.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: dispensing prescription drugs rather than supplements. Objects are identical in kind (sealed bottles, boxes, liquids of the same size and weight), the required precision is item-identity plus a patient-specific label, and supplements/OTC products are explicitly among the items handled.

sources.system: ScriptPro SP/CRS Robotic Prescription Dispensing Systems
sources.title: ScriptPro Robotic Prescription Dispensing Systems - ScriptPro
sources.claim: ScriptPro robotic prescription dispensing systems are installed in thousands of retail, health-system and ambulatory pharmacies, filling, labeling and capping patient-specific containers behind the pharmacy counter.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: filling and labeling drug prescriptions. Transfers to dispensing capsules/tablets of vitamins and botanical extracts because the objects (solid oral dose forms in stock containers), the counting/labeling precision, and the enclosed pharmacy work cell are the same.

sources.title: Asteres Announces 1,000 ScriptCenter Unit Milestone in 38 U.S. States
sources.claim: Asteres ScriptCenter automated pickup kiosks, with 1,000 units installed across 38 US states, complete the hand-off step by releasing the labeled, patient-specific package to the identified patient without staff involvement.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: releasing a filled prescription to the patient rather than a supplement bottle. Same object class (bagged/bottled retail health products), same verification requirement (right patient, right item), so the hand-off step of in-office dispensing transfers.

sources.system: HollySys MD Series TCM Granule Dispensing Equipment (MD6180)
sources.title: Granules dispensing machine - MD6180 - Hollysys
sources.claim: HollySys MD-series equipment automatically identifies, weighs, allocates and packages traditional Chinese herbal formula granules according to the prescriber's order, and is in use in more than 11,000 hospitals - i.e. automated compounding and dispensing of patient-specific botanical formulas.
sources.transferJustification: Essentially the same task in another tradition: weighing and blending herbal/botanical extracts into a patient-specific formula per a physician's prescription. Objects (concentrated botanical extract granules) and gravimetric precision match naturopathic bulk-herb and granule compounding.

sources.title: ARxIUM Celebrates Major RIVA Milestone
sources.claim: ARxIUM's RIVA robotic IV compounding cells, installed in hospital pharmacies worldwide, have prepared more than nineteen million doses in USP <797>-compliant ISO Class 5 environments, performing accurate volumetric fluid measurement and transfer into syringes and IV bags.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: sterile IV admixture rather than herbal tincture blending or vitamin-bag mixing. Transfers because both are accurate multi-source liquid measurement and transfer into a labeled patient-specific container; RIVA's tolerance requirements are stricter than tincture compounding.

sources.title: Robots revolutionize drug dispensing at Shanghai Seventh People's Hospital
sources.claim: Two ABB robots work as an autonomous cell inside Shanghai Seventh People's Hospital's pharmacy, taking medicines off circular shelves and preparing them for distribution to patients.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: hospital drug dispensing at a hospital that practises both Chinese and Western medicine. Same objects (boxed/bottled medicines on shelving) and same output (correct item assembled for a named patient) as clinic supplement dispensing.

sources.title: Vitestro Achieves CE Marking for Autonomous Blood Drawing Device
sources.claim: Vitestro's Aletta device autonomously performs ultrasound-guided venipuncture on patients' arms with 95% first-stick success, comparable to ... phlebotomy; it is CE-marked and in limited market release at European hospitals and laboratories.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: diagnostic blood draw. It substantiates autonomous, clinically acceptable needle insertion into a living patient's arm at a purpose-built station, which is the hard perceptual/manipulation core of giving an IM/SC injection; it does not cover catheter placement or infusion management.

sources.title: Vitestro's robotic blood drawing device meets trial endpoints
sources.claim: Vitestro's device met its trial primary endpoint with 95% first-stick success, within the manual venipuncture range, establishing worker-comparable reliability for autonomous needle insertion in humans.
sources.transferJustification: Same transfer as above: quantifies that autonomous needle insertion into a patient's arm reaches human-comparable reliability, supporting the injection instance but not infusion monitoring.

sources.title: Robot performs autonomous needle-less injection
sources.claim: Cobionix's Cobi platform performed an intramuscular injection on a person autonomously, locating the injection site and delivering the dose by needle-free jet without a healthcare professional involved.
sources.transferJustification: Direct: autonomous intramuscular injection of a dose into a patient, the same act as a B12 or lipotropic injection, differing only in that the dose is jet-delivered from a cartridge rather than drawn from a vial.

tasks.label: Administer treatments or therapies, such as homeopathy, hydrotherapy, Oriental or Ayurvedic medicine, electrotherapy, and diathermy, using physical agents including air, heat, cold, water, sound, or ultraviolet light to catalyze the body to heal itself.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Constitutional hydrotherapy in the clinic's hydro room: patient undressed on a treatment table, alternating hot and cold wet towels laid on chest/abdomen and then back, patient wrapped in sheets and wool blankets, turned prone midway, skin and warming response palpated, often with damp sine-wave electrode pads placed under the back; also sitz baths, contrast baths, wet-sheet wraps.

Hands-on bodywork on a treatment table in the clinic: Ayurvedic abhyanga oil massage, Chinese tuina, therapeutic soft-tissue/trigger-point work, hot-stone application; therapist adapts pressure to tissue response and patient feedback over a 30-60 minute session.

Acupuncture / Oriental medicine needling session: locating acupoints by palpation on a draped patient, inserting and manipulating filiform needles to obtain deqi, retaining 15-30 minutes with periodic checks, then removing and counting needles; sometimes combined with cupping, gua sha or moxa.

Applicator-based physical medicine modality in a clinic treatment room: coupling gel and moving a therapeutic ultrasound head over a shoulder or low back for 8-10 minutes, or positioning a shortwave diathermy drum, or placing TENS/interferential/microcurrent electrodes and running a timed session while monitoring patient comfort.

Light and heat therapy: photobiomodulation/low-level laser or infrared applied over a painful region for a set dose, UV or heat-lamp exposure over a body area, or supervised infrared sauna session; patient positioned, area exposed, dose and time set, patient monitored and area cleaned afterward.

Administering a homeopathic remedy in the office dispensary: retrieving the indicated remedy and potency from the dispensary shelf, dosing pellets or liquid into a vial or dispensing into the patient's mouth/cup, labeling and handing it to the patient with dosing instructions.

sources.title: Product focus - AI and robot massage | spabusiness.com
sources.claim: Aescape's AI-driven robotic massage table performs full massage sessions on clients without a therapist present, in fitness/wellness club settings; the vendor states the system is entirely autonomous with only a staff call button as backup.

sources.title: Massage Envy Introduces Aescape Robotic Massage at Select Franchised Locations
sources.claim: Aescape robotic massage is being introduced commercially at Massage Envy franchised locations in the US, i.e. sold as a substitute for a human-delivered massage service inside a human-work facility.

sources.title: AI-powered massage robot to start product evaluation in the United States and clinical trial in Singapore
sources.claim: The EMMA massage robot delivers traditional Chinese medicine tuina-style massage to patients and has logged tens of thousands of treatment hours in TCM clinics, physiotherapy centres ....

sources.title: A robot to assist in transcranial magnetic stimulation (TMS / rTMS) - Axilum Robotics
sources.claim: The Axilum TMS-Robot autonomously executes a planned energy-delivery session: it positions a therapy applicator (stimulation coil) against the patient's body, maintains contact with force control, and compensates for patient movement throughout the session in clinical settings.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic delivery of an electromagnetic therapy applicator to a body region for a timed treatment session. Transfer holds for diathermy/electrotherapy/ultrasound-head application: same object (a seated or reclining patient), same act (place an applicator on the body surface, maintain contact force, hold or sweep it for the treatment period), in the same kind of clinic treatment room, at looser positional tolerance than TMS neuronavigation requires.

sources.developer: ASA Laser / Cutting Edge Laser Technologies
sources.title: Robotic M6 MLS Therapy Laser

sources.claim: A moxibustion robot in service at a Shanghai rehabilitation hospital autonomously executes a half-hour heat therapy over acupoints on a patient's back after the clinician selects points and technique on a tablet.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous application of a controlled heat source over a specified region of a patient's back for a set treatment time — the same physical agent (heat) and body surface targeting used in naturopathic heat/light therapy.

sources.system: auto-RUSS autonomous robotic ultrasound scanning system
sources.title: Autonomous robotic ultrasound scanning system: a key to enhancing image analysis reproducibility and observer consistency in ultrasound imaging
sources.claim: An autonomous robotic ultrasound scanning ... () uses force-feedback control and visual servoing to run a fully autonomous pipeline of transducer placement and skin-contact scanning on human subjects.

Therapeutic ultrasound uses the same head-on-skin coupling and continuous sweeping over a small region, with lower targeting precision required than diagnostic imaging.

Administering a homeopathic remedy in a dispensary is the same physical act — select the labeled vial/potency from the shelf and deliver it to the patient — with comparable object size and precision.

Attends a professional conference or seminar (e.g., state association or AANP annual convention), sitting in lecture sessions, taking notes, networking with colleagues, and occasionally joining hands-on skills workshops (e.g., physical medicine, IV therapy technique).
Self-directed study: reading peer-reviewed journals, monographs, and botanical/pharmacology updates; reviewing cases and evidence to keep clinical knowledge current.

Participates in a residency, preceptorship, or mentorship relationship — either shadowing/being supervised by an experienced clinician, or supervising a student/resident in a teaching clinic, with case discussion and feedback.
Administrative upkeep of professional development: tracking CE credits, retaining certificates, completing license-renewal attestations, and enrolling in postgraduate certificate programs.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Periodic wellness visit in the naturopathic clinic exam room: hands-on screening physical examination of an adult patient — heart/lung auscultation, thyroid and abdominal palpation, lymph node check, skin/oral inspection, otoscopy — with on-the-spot judgment about which findings warrant follow-up.

Baseline risk-factor measurements at a periodic visit in the clinic: seated blood pressure, pulse, temperature, SpO2, height, weight/BMI, recorded into the chart for hypertension/obesity risk screening.

In-office venipuncture on a cooperative adult for screening panels (lipids, fasting glucose/A1c, CBC, thyroid, vitamin D): tourniquet, vein selection, draw of two to four tubes, labeling and packaging for the reference lab.

Administering an immunization in the clinic (influenza, Td/Tdap, travel vaccine) where scope permits: verify identity and contraindications, draw up or prepare the dose, deltoid IM or SC injection, bandage, brief observation, and registry documentation.

Point-of-care infectious-disease screening in the clinic: collect a throat/nasal swab specimen from a seated patient, transfer it to the assay cartridge or transport tube, and run/read the rapid test.

Offsite community outreach screening event (health fair in a church hall, farmers market tent, employer break room, or pop-up clinic): walk-up blood pressure checks, fingerstick glucose/cholesterol, risk questionnaires, and sometimes flu shots, in a venue set up for the day.

sources.claim: Vitestro's autonomous blood-drawing robot (ARPD/Aletta) met all endpoints in the pivotal phase of the ADOPT trial in Dutch hospital outpatient labs, with a 95% success rate on an adult outpatient population.

sources.title: Vitestro raises $70m to fuel blood-drawing robot's global commercial readiness
sources.claim: The Vitestro device obtained an EU CE mark in ... began being deployed in European healthcare settings (hospital outpatient blood-draw clinics in the Netherlands and Denmark) from March 2025.

sources.title: Automated Phlebotomy Firm Vitestro Eyes 2027 Commercial Launch of Robotic Blood Draw Device
sources.claim: Trade coverage notes the robot's performance is in the range of trained human phlebotomists (93–97% first-stick) with a low adverse-event rate, though placements in Dutch and Danish hospitals have so far been within clinical trials rather than routine care.

sources.title: Robot performs autonomous needle-less injection
sources.claim: Cobionix's Cobi platform performed an autonomous intramuscular injection using needle-free jet injection, with the robot detecting the patient, verifying ID, mapping the injection site with LiDAR and delivering the dose without a healthcare professional; a one-off laboratory demonstration, not a validated clinical deployment.

sources.developer: hospital research team (Journal of Medical Systems study)
sources.title: An Assessment of an Inpatient Robotic Nurse Assistant: A Mixed-Method Study
sources.claim: The Florence robotic nurse assistant autonomously navigated a hospital general-medicine ward, identified patients, and measured vital signs (SpO2, blood pressure, temperature) in a 67-patient study.

sources.title: Higi | Telehealth and Telecare Aware
sources.claim: Automated higi health stations — machines that actuate an arm cuff and take blood pressure, pulse, weight and BMI and record the results — are deployed at scale in US pharmacies, supermarkets and workplaces for walk-up risk-factor screening.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated cuff-based blood pressure, pulse, weight and BMI measurement on a seated member of the public. Same measurement work, same instrumentation and precision as the vitals/anthropometric screening a clinician performs at a periodic visit, performed unattended in institution-controlled premises.

sources.title: The LINGCAI-II System: A Sampling Robotic System for Autonomous Oropharyngeal Swab Sampling
sources.claim: The LINGCAI-II robotic sampling system performs oropharyngeal swab collection and downstream sample handling autonomously, validated in a clinical trial with 116 COVID-19 patients at a robot sampling workstation.

sources.title: Autonomous swab robot for naso- and oropharyngeal COVID-19 screening
sources.claim: An autonomous swab robot station (SR-NOCS) collected combined naso- and oropharyngeal screening specimens from human subjects with results fully correlated with manual sampling and high subject acceptance.

tasks.label: Perform venipuncture or skin pricking to collect blood samples.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Routine venous blood draw in the naturopathic clinic's draw chair/exam room: cooperative adult with visible, palpable antecubital veins; tourniquet, alcohol prep, 21G needle or butterfly, 1-4 labeled vacutainer tubes in correct order of draw, gauze and bandage, tubes inverted and set aside for courier pickup.

Adult with challenging but workable venous access in the clinic: high BMI, elderly, on anticoagulants, or small/deep antecubital veins requiring careful palpation and warming; a usable vein still exists in the antecubital fossa; standard multi-tube draw.

Difficult access in the clinic where no usable antecubital vein is available: dehydrated, chemotherapy/IV-scarred, or fragile-veined patient requiring hand or forearm veins, small-gauge butterfly, repositioning, and sometimes a second attempt or a different arm.

Capillary collection by skin prick in the clinic: lancet fingerstick (occasionally heel/earlobe) for point-of-care glucose/HbA1c/lipids, or milking drops onto a dried blood spot card for hormone/micronutrient panels; requires warming the finger, wiping the first drop, and controlled milking to fill spots without clotting.

Pediatric patient or highly anxious/needle-phobic adult in the clinic: coaching and distraction, positioning or parental holding, supine draw for vasovagal risk, small-volume tubes, and monitoring for fainting after the stick.

Off-site collection: house call, employer/community health fair, or retreat setting; blood drawn with a portable kit on a chair or folding table, variable lighting and surfaces, samples packed for transport.

sources.title: Performance, Safety, and Patient Experience of an Autonomous Robotic Phlebotomy Device: A Multicenter Trial (Clinical Chemistry)
sources.claim: Vitestro's Aletta autonomous robotic phlebotomy device performed venous blood draws in a multicenter trial in Dutch outpatient phlebotomy departments, with 94.5% first-stick success overall and high success in difficult-access, obese, and elderly patients.

sources.title: Performance, Safety, and Patient Experience of an Autonomous Robotic Phlebotomy Device: A Multicenter Trial (Clinical Chemistry)
sources.claim: The same trial documents that the device performs the venipuncture autonomously with one trained professional supervising up to three devices, and describes the full sequence: alcohol spray, ultrasound/Doppler vein selection in the antecubital area, tourniquet, needle insertion, tube filling and inversion, needle withdrawal.

sources.title: Autonomous Robotic Phlebotomy Shows High Success Rates in Multicenter Trial | Clinical Lab Products
sources.claim: The trial was run in institutional outpatient phlebotomy departments of Dutch hospitals and labs (Amsterdam UMC, St. Antonius, OLVG Lab, Result Laboratory), i.e., structured human clinical facilities, with 1,633 patients in the routine-use cohort.

sources.title: Aletta® - Vitestro
sources.claim: Aletta performs the complete blood collection procedure end to end without a human operator, including tourniquet placement, vein identification, needle insertion, tube changing/inversion and bandaging.

sources.title: FAQ - Vitestro
sources.claim: Aletta is CE-marked and commercially launched in Europe; it is limited to adult patients in outpatient phlebotomy ..., is arm-venipuncture only (no capillary/fingerstick), and aborts when no suitable vein is identified, handing the patient to staff for manual phlebotomy.

sources.title: Vitestro Unveils Aletta™: The World's First Autonomous Robotic Phlebotomy Device™ (ARPD™)
sources.claim: Aletta received CE marking and an initial commercial launch in Europe, with safety and comfort validated in over 4,000 patients.

tasks.label: Perform mobilizations and high-velocity adjustments to joints or soft tissues, using principles of massage, stretching, or resistance.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Soft-tissue treatment of the posterior trunk and legs: patient prone on a treatment table in the naturopathic clinic, draped; ND applies effleurage/petrissage, myofascial release and trigger-point compression to thoracolumbar paraspinals, glutes, hamstrings and calves, varying depth and dwell by tissue response for 10-25 minutes.

Soft-tissue treatment of the cervical spine, upper trapezius/suboccipitals, jaw, chest wall, forearms/hands or feet: patient supine or side-lying, ND works small, delicate regions by hand, cradling the head or holding a limb, with continuous palpatory feedback near vulnerable structures.

High-velocity, low-amplitude adjustment of a spinal or rib segment: after motion palpation identifies a restricted segment and contraindication screening, the ND positions the patient (side-posture lumbar, supine thoracic, cervical rotation), takes up slack and delivers a short thrust, then reassesses.

Low-velocity graded mobilization of spinal, sacroiliac or costal joints: ND stabilizes adjacent segments and applies oscillatory posterior-anterior or rotational glides (grades I-IV) at the specific restricted level, modulating force to end-feel and patient guarding.

Mobilization and passive range-of-motion work at a peripheral joint (shoulder, hip, knee, ankle, wrist) for stiffness or capsular restriction: ND holds the limb, applies distraction and accessory glides through available range, working into resistance over several minutes.

Assisted stretching and muscle-energy/resistance techniques: ND takes hamstrings, hip flexors, pectorals, shoulder girdle or cervical muscles to end range, has the patient contract against the ND's counterforce, then lengthens further through the new barrier over repeated cycles.

sources.title: News: Aescape: The First Fully Automated Massage Table | AMTA
sources.claim: Aescape's AI-driven robotic massage table performs autonomous massage sessions on clients in commercial wellness clubs; it scans the body and executes the treatment without a therapist operating it.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: therapeutic massage of the posterior body. It transfers to the ND's soft-tissue instance because the object (human back/gluteal/hamstring soft tissue), the technique (force-controlled compression and gliding strokes over tissue), and the setting (treatment room with a table) are the same.

sources.title: I Tried Aescape, the High-Tech Robot Massage—Here's My Review - Parade
sources.claim: Aescape tables are in routine commercial service at roughly 100 sites in gyms, hotels and spas; reviewers note the robot does not treat the hands, arms, feet, neck ....
sources.transferJustification: Same related task (posterior-body massage); the quoted coverage limits also delimit which ND soft-tissue instances a cited system can and cannot serve.

sources.title: Massage Envy Introduces Aescape Robotic Massage at Select Franchised Locations
sources.claim: Massage Envy, a mainstream massage clinic franchise, began offering Aescape robotic massage as a service option at franchised locations, i.e. the robot is sold as a substitute for a therapist-delivered session.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: paid soft-tissue massage delivered in a clinic-type facility; substitution for the human therapist's session is direct evidence of acceptable output quality for that treatment.

sources.title: Satisfaction and Feasibility Evaluation of an Electronic Massager—Expert Manipulative Massage Automation (EMMA): A Pilot Study
sources.claim: EMMA, an autonomous robotic massager, is in routine clinical use delivering tui-na style soft-tissue treatment in traditional Chinese medicine clinics.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: clinician-prescribed therapeutic soft-tissue massage. It transfers because EMMA delivers pressure-controlled deep soft-tissue work on patients in a clinic treatment room, the same objects and setting as the ND's soft-tissue instance.

sources.title: AI-powered massage robot to start product evaluation in the United States and clinical trial in Singapore
sources.claim: EMMA units have accumulated tens of thousands of patient treatment hours across TCM clinics, physiotherapy centres and ....
sources.transferJustification: Related task: therapeutic massage in licensed clinical facilities; the volume of treatment hours in clinics and physiotherapy centres shows sustained worker-substituting operation in an E2 setting.

sources.title: Capsix - Discover Technology
sources.claim: Capsix's iYU massage robot, built on a KUKA LBR Med arm, is offered in a fully autonomous configuration that massages a user with no human involvement, installed in a small dedicated room.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: back soft-tissue massage on a human body; same objects and force ranges as the ND's soft-tissue work, delivered in an ordinary treatment room.

sources.system: Robotic massage (cobot) intervention, Kerautret et al.
sources.developer: Université Claude Bernard Lyon 1 / Capsix-affiliated authors
sources.title: Comparative Efficacy of Robotic and Manual Massage Interventions on Performance and Well-Being: A Randomized Crossover Trial
sources.claim: A randomized crossover trial compared robot-delivered back soft-tissue massage against massage by a physical therapist and found comparable objective and subjective outcomes.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: therapist-delivered back massage. Direct head-to-head comparison with a physical therapist on the same body region supports that robot output on posterior soft tissue is of comparable quality.

sources.title: Robotic-Assisted Shoulder Rehabilitation Therapy Effectively Improved Poststroke Hemiplegic Shoulder Pain: A Randomized Controlled Trial
sources.claim: A purpose-built shoulder robot delivered joint mobilization and stretching to patients lying supine in an inpatient hospital department, reducing hemiplegic shoulder pain in a randomized controlled trial.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: clinician-delivered passive joint mobilization and stretching of the shoulder. Same operation the ND performs on a peripheral joint, on human patients, with the limb coupled to the device.

sources.system: Portable ankle rehabilitation robot (robot-guided passive stretching)
sources.developer: Rehabilitation robotics research group (Zhang et al.)
sources.title: Effects of robot-guided passive stretching and active movement training of ankle and mobility impairments in stroke
sources.claim: A robot delivered guided passive stretching and movement training of the ankle to chronic stroke patients over six weeks, with the robot group improving more than an instructed home exercise program.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: clinician-applied passive stretching to end range with force control. Transfers to the ND's assisted-stretching instance for limb muscle groups: same mechanical operation (take joint to barrier, hold, modulate torque) on a fixtured human limb.

tasks.label: Treat minor cuts, abrasions, or contusions.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Naturopathic clinic exam room: patient presents with a superficial abrasion or scrape (knee, hand, forearm). ND inspects the wound, irrigates with saline, wipes away dirt/debris and dried blood, applies an antiseptic or botanical topical (e.g., calendula), covers with a non-adherent pad and tape or an adhesive dressing, and gives aftercare instructions. Patient is seated/unrestrained and may flinch; wound size, shape, contamination and body location vary.

Small superficial laceration needing closure: ND achieves hemostasis with pressure, cleans and explores the cut, decides on closure (adhesive strips, skin glue, or simple sutures where state scope allows), possibly infiltrates local anesthetic, closes the wound edges, then dresses it and advises on tetanus status and infection signs.

Contusion / soft-tissue bruise: ND palpates the area to assess swelling, tenderness and range of motion, rules out fracture, then applies cold pack and an elastic compression wrap, or applies topical arnica/homeopathic ointment and elevates the limb; instructs on icing schedule.

Follow-up wound check and dressing change in the clinic: ND peels off an adhered dressing without damaging healing tissue, inspects for infection, re-cleans, may remove adhesive strips or sutures, and applies a fresh dressing over an irregular, moist, partly healed wound.

Treatment outside the clinic: house call, community/mobile clinic, wilderness or event first-aid setting; ND cleans and dresses a cut or abrasion with a portable kit, working with variable lighting, no exam table, and the patient positioned wherever practical.

sources.system: Autonomous tape handling framework for robotic wound redressing (Liang, Yip lab, UCSD)
sources.developer: University of California San Diego (Michael Yip lab)
sources.title: Towards Autonomous Tape Handling for Robotic Wound Redressing
sources.claim: Research framework (UCSD) automates only two sub-steps of wound redressing — detaching adhesive tape and placing tape — evaluated on skin phantoms, tape rolls, and anatomical leg/hip/heel models, with partial (not complete) tape removal per attempt; it is a laboratory demonstration, not whole wound care.
sources.transferJustification: Closest published work to the dressing sub-step of treating cuts/abrasions: same objects (gauze, adhesive tape, skin). It shows only sub-steps succeed, on phantoms, so it cannot substantiate completing the whole clinical instance at any tier.

sources.system: DLR MIRO / MICA robotic waterjet debridement system
sources.developer: German Aerospace Center (DLR) with clinical collaborators
sources.title: Robotic waterjet wound debridement – Workflow adaption for clinical application and systematic evaluation of a novel technology
sources.claim: Autonomous robotic waterjet debridement (DLR MIRO robot with ERBEJET probe) generated cleaning paths and cleaned wounds automatically, but only in a laboratory bench setup on ex vivo porcine skin, as a feasibility study; not on live patients.
sources.transferJustification: Wound cleaning/debridement is the core of treating a contaminated abrasion. The system is autonomous but works on fixed ex vivo tissue in a lab rig, so it supports at most a sub-step in a purpose-built setting, not clinician-quality treatment of a live patient's wound.

sources.title: Aletta® - Vitestro
sources.claim: Vitestro's Aletta autonomous robotic phlebotomy device performs a complete needle-based procedure on a live human arm placed in the machine's armrest, including placing the bandage afterwards; CE-marked, used in multicenter clinical trials and ordered by a hospital.
sources.transferJustification: Related task (venipuncture) shows an autonomous machine can act on a live human's skin and apply a bandage in a clinic. Transfer is limited: the puncture is created by the machine at a site it chose, on a fixtured arm, with no irrigation, debris removal, wound assessment or closure — the substance of treating a cut or abrasion.

sources.system: Autonomous Robotic Phlebotomy Device (ARPD), ADOPT trial NCT05878483
sources.title: Performance, Safety, and Patient Experience of an Autonomous Robotic Phlebotomy Device: A Multicenter Trial
sources.claim: Peer-reviewed multicenter trial of the autonomous robotic phlebotomy device evaluated performance, safety and patient experience in real clinical blood-draw settings.
sources.transferJustification: Establishes that the venipuncture robot is genuinely autonomous and clinically evaluated on patients, bounding what autonomous skin-contacting medical robots have actually achieved: a single fixtured needle-stick, not wound cleaning, closure or dressing.

sources.title: Robot performs first realistic surgery without human help | Hub
sources.claim: Autonomous soft-tissue suturing has been achieved only in research on animal tissue under highly controlled conditions with marked tissue and supervision, not on human patients or skin lacerations.
sources.transferJustification: Suturing is the closure sub-step for a laceration. Even the leading autonomous suturing systems work on marked animal tissue in a lab OR under supervision, so they do not substantiate closing and dressing a patient's laceration at clinician quality.

tasks.label: Perform minor surgical procedures, such as removing warts, moles, or cysts, sampling tissues for skin cancer or lipomas, and applying or removing sutures.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Destructive treatment of a benign superficial lesion (common wart, plantar wart, skin tag, seborrheic keratosis) in a naturopathic clinic exam room: identify lesion, pare/prep, apply liquid nitrogen cryospray or cantharidin/topical acid or light curettage on an awake, unrestrained patient at a variable body site (hand, foot, neck, trunk), judge freeze time/endpoint, dress, give aftercare instructions.

Shave excision or 3-4 mm punch biopsy of a mole or suspicious pigmented lesion for pathology: mark lesion, infiltrate lidocaine, cut/punch to correct depth on curved mobile skin, lift and transect specimen, place it in labeled formalin, achieve hemostasis (aluminum chloride or electrocautery), dress and document.

Excision of an epidermoid/sebaceous cyst or small lipoma: sterile prep and drape, local anesthetic infiltration, elliptical or linear incision, blunt dissection of the capsule free of surrounding tissue without rupture, hemostasis, layered closure with sutures, dressing.

Applying sutures: closing a surgical excision defect or repairing a simple traumatic laceration in the office — irrigation and debridement as needed, anesthesia, approximating wound edges, placing and tying interrupted/subcuticular sutures at correct tension and spacing, cutting tails, dressing.

Follow-up visit suture removal and wound check: inspect the healing wound, clean, grasp each knot with forceps, cut the loop with a blade or scissors, withdraw the suture without dragging external material through tissue, apply steri-strips/dressing on an awake patient.

sources.system: ARTAS iX / iXi robotic hair restoration system
sources.title: ARTAS® Robotic Hair Restoration Treatments
sources.claim: ARTAS iX is an FDA-cleared, commercially deployed clinic robot that uses machine vision to identify and punch-dissect follicular units (0.9-1.0 mm cores) from a tensioned human scalp and to create recipient sites; it executes only the harvesting/site-making step under physician supervision, with graft retrieval, anesthesia, hemostasis and closure done by clinic staff.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic follicular-unit punch harvesting from human skin. It is the closest deployed analogue to a punch biopsy (same object — live human skin; sub-millimetre depth control; same outpatient clinic setting), but it works only on flat, mechanically tensioned scalp in a narrow patient indication and performs only the coring step, so it does not deliver a completed biopsy, excision, or closure.

sources.system: FDA-cleared surgical robots (review incl. Mako, Artemis, ARTAS)
sources.title: Levels of autonomy in FDA-cleared surgical robots: a systematic review (npj Digital Medicine)
sources.claim: A systematic review of FDA-cleared surgical robots found that autonomy at the level of generating and executing a patient-specific plan exists only for bone milling, prostate biopsy and hair-follicle extraction; no cleared system autonomously performs skin lesion excision, cyst removal, suturing, or suture removal.
sources.transferJustification: Survey of the whole cleared-device field; establishes the absence of any cleared autonomous system for the soft-tissue cutting, excision and suturing steps that make up this task.

sources.developer: Johns Hopkins University / Children's National Hospital
sources.title: Robo-Surgeon Successfully Sews Pig Intestine (Scientific American)
sources.claim: The STAR robot performed autonomous laparoscopic intestinal anastomosis suturing on live anesthetized pigs in a research operating room, but required human-placed fluorescent markers and researcher adjustments, operating autonomously for only part of the procedure.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous soft-tissue suturing. Transfer is limited — bowel tissue exposed and marked by a human in an animal research OR, partial autonomy, no wound prep, anesthesia or dressing — so it does not substantiate completing an office skin closure end to end.

sources.title: SRT-H: A hierarchical framework for autonomous surgery via language-conditioned imitation learning (Science Robotics / PubMed)
sources.claim: SRT-H autonomously executed all steps of a gallbladder removal, including clip application and cutting, on eight ex vivo pig gallbladders in a laboratory setup using a da Vinci Research Kit; it has not been used on live human patients.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous soft-tissue dissection and removal of a structure. Demonstrated only on excised animal organs mounted in a bench setup, not on live human skin lesions, and without anesthesia, specimen handling or wound closure.

sources.title: Fully-Automatic Robot Dentist Performs World's First Human Procedure (Slashdot / New Atlas)
sources.claim: Perceptive's AI-driven dental robot performed a complete crown preparation on a live human patient in a dental clinic setting, showing autonomous robotic cutting on a human is achievable for a rigid, splint-fixtured target; the system was not yet FDA-cleared.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous robotic tissue cutting on a human patient in a clinic. Transfer to this task fails on the workpiece: a tooth is rigid and immobilized by a splint, whereas warts, moles, cysts and wounds are deformable, mobile skin requiring anesthesia, specimen handling and suture closure.

sources.title: Surgeons Use Teleoperated Humanoid Robots to Perform Live Surgery – a World First
sources.claim: The 2026 state of the art for humanoid robots in surgery is teleoperation: two humanoid robots completed procedures on large animals under continuous surgeon control, with autonomy stated as a future goal.
sources.transferJustification: Shows that general-purpose robotic surgical manipulation as of mid-2026 remains teleoperated on animals, so it cannot support any positive judgment for autonomous office procedures.

roles.title: Orthoptists
roles.description: Diagnose and treat visual system disorders such as binocular vision and eye movement impairments.

tasks.label: Evaluate, diagnose, or treat disorders of the visual system with an emphasis on binocular vision or abnormal eye movements.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Pediatric strabismus/amblyopia workup in a pediatric ophthalmology clinic exam room: age-appropriate visual acuity, cover-uncover and alternate prism cover test at distance and near, ocular motility in nine gaze positions, stereoacuity and fusion testing, assisting cycloplegic retinoscopy, then documenting findings and a management recommendation. Child is 6 months to 8 years old, often restless, crying, or non-verbal; the orthoptist must hold fixation targets, chase fixation, judge small refixation movements, and neutralize with loose prisms/prism bar in seconds.

Adult complex diplopia / neuro-ophthalmic evaluation in a hospital eye clinic: history, Maddox rod or prism cover measurements in nine gaze positions plus head tilts, Bielschowsky head-tilt test, Hess/Lees screen, binocular single vision field, forced duction interpretation, saccade/pursuit and nystagmus observation; interpret pattern (cranial nerve palsy, thyroid eye disease, myasthenia, skew) and recommend prism or referral.

Treatment/management visit in clinic: prescribing and physically applying adhesive occlusion patches or Bangerter filters, cutting and applying Fresnel press-on prisms to spectacle lenses, checking prism/spectacle fit, teaching and supervising orthoptic exercises (convergence insufficiency training, stereograms), and counseling the patient/family on compliance.

Pre- and post-operative strabismus surgery assessment in a hospital eye service: repeat prism cover measurements at multiple distances and gazes to plan surgical numbers, prism adaptation testing, and post-op day-1/week-1 alignment and diplopia checks, sometimes in the pre-op holding area on a patient in a gown on a gurney.

Inpatient bedside or emergency department consult (stroke, head trauma, cranial nerve palsy, ICU patient): portable occluder, prism bar, near target and penlight used at the bedside with the patient supine or semi-recumbent, poor cooperation, lines and monitors around, variable lighting; produce alignment/motility findings and diplopia management advice for the neurology or ophthalmology team.

Community or school vision screening / outreach clinic session: acuity testing, cover test, stereo screening and photoscreening of many children in a school gym, health-department clinic or mobile unit; identify amblyopia risk factors and refer, with brief counseling of parents or teachers.

sources.system: Automated strabismus evaluation devices (eye-tracking, video-oculography, photographic systems) — class review
sources.developer: University of Iowa / Iowa City VA (Hartness et al.)
sources.title: Automated strabismus evaluation: a critical review and meta-analysis
sources.claim: Systematic review/meta-analysis of automated strabismus evaluation devices (eye trackers, photographic/AR systems) finds they correlate with, but do not replace, clinician prism cover testing; the reviewed systems are measurement instruments, not machines that conduct a full orthoptic evaluation, diagnosis and treatment.
sources.transferJustification: Directly about the measurement step of this task (ocular deviation quantification); shows only partial, screening-grade automation of one sub-step, with no manipulation, diagnosis or treatment.

sources.system: STARE (Strabismus screening Test using Augmented Reality and Eye-tracking)
sources.title: Feasibility study of an automated Strabismus screening Test using Augmented Reality and Eye-tracking (STARE)
sources.claim: STARE, an augmented-reality headset plus eye-tracking strabismus test, was evaluated only as a feasibility screening tool in a small adult-dominated cohort against orthoptist-performed alternate prism cover test; it is a headset display/camera device, not a manipulator, and was administered by clinic staff.
sources.transferJustification: Same measurement (horizontal deviation) as the orthoptic prism cover test, but feasibility-stage screening only, with clinician setup and interpretation.

sources.developer: reported in Indian Journal of Ophthalmology (clinical device report)
sources.title: Motorized semi-automated prism bar technique for enhanced strabismus measurement
sources.claim: A motorized prism bar device for measuring ocular deviation moves the prism bar in fixed increments at the push of a ... by the examiner, with the patient in a chin-and-headrest; the clinician still performs cover testing, judges neutralization and interprets results.
sources.transferJustification: Closest actuated hardware for the prism-neutralization step of this task; it is button-driven by the examiner, so it is teleoperated and cannot support a positive judgment.

sources.title: Vision test kiosks elicit state patient safety alert
sources.claim: Eyebot S1 is an autonomous self-service vision-testing kiosk deployed in retail (Walmart/Sam's Club, Zenni) that captures refraction, lensometry and acuity for adults 18-64 and routes results to remote eye care providers; optometric associations warn it is not a substitute for a clinician's examination.
sources.transferJustification: Related task (automated refractive vision testing) in the same clinical domain; it is a sensing/display kiosk for cooperative adults that neither measures binocular alignment clinically nor diagnoses or treats binocular vision disorders.

sources.title: Contactless, autonomous robotic alignment of optical coherence tomography for in vivo evaluation of diseased retinas
sources.claim: Autonomous robotic alignment of an OCT scanner to a seated patient's eye was demonstrated in a retina clinic with image quality comparable to technician-operated OCT — currently the most advanced autonomous robotic ophthalmic interaction, but limited to non-contact retinal imaging of cooperative seated adults.
sources.transferJustification: Related task (robot positioning an ophthalmic instrument to a patient's eye in clinic) shows autonomous robotic eye-directed imaging, but no prism/occluder manipulation, no fixation management of uncooperative children, and no diagnosis or treatment.

sources.system: Humanoid surrogates for medical interventions (Unitree H1-class humanoid teleoperation system)
sources.developer: UC San Diego (Atar, Liang, Richter, Yip et al.)
sources.title: Humanoids in Hospitals: A Technical Study of Humanoid Robot Surrogates for Dexterous Medical Interventions
sources.claim: Humanoid robot surrogates performing hospital physical-examination and needle tasks were driven by a whole-body teleoperation system, i.e., a human operator manipulated the medical tools through the robot.
sources.transferJustification: Related task (robot performing bedside physical examination maneuvers with handheld instruments); it is explicitly teleoperated, so it cannot substantiate autonomous completion of orthoptic examination or patching.

sources.developer: academic study reported in Optometry and Vision Science
sources.title: Social Robot Can Motivate Patching Compliance For Childhood Amblyopia
sources.claim: The only robot reported in amblyopia patching therapy, 'Mirrly', was studied qualitatively for caregiver perceptions of a social robot supporting patching adherence; it does not apply patches or deliver orthoptic treatment.
sources.transferJustification: Directly touches the treatment half of this task (patching), but the robot only provides social encouragement in a perception study; no physical treatment delivery is demonstrated.

tasks.label: Examine patients with problems related to ocular motility, binocular vision, amblyopia, or strabismus.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Pediatric ophthalmology / hospital eye clinic: full orthoptic examination of a young, partly cooperative child (age 1-7) referred for suspected esotropia or amblyopia — history, age-appropriate acuity (preferential looking/matching), fixation preference, cover/uncover and alternate prism cover test at distance and near, ocular motility in nine gaze positions, stereopsis, convergence, often with cycloplegic input; requires coaxing the child, holding accommodative targets, occluders and prism bars near the face.

Adult outpatient eye clinic: examination of a patient with new diplopia or a motility disorder (cranial nerve palsy, thyroid eye disease, myasthenia, decompensated phoria) — measured prism cover test in nine gaze positions and head tilt, Hess/Lees screen or Goldmann field of binocular single vision, ductions/versions, fusional amplitudes, saccades/pursuit, symptom interpretation.

Strabismus surgery workup in an ophthalmology practice: pre-operative and post-operative measurement of angle of deviation at distance/near, with and without correction, in cardinal gazes, plus fusion/stereo testing, to plan or verify surgical dosing; cooperative adult or older child at a standard exam lane.

Neuro-rehabilitation or inpatient bedside consult: examining a stroke/TBI or low-mobility patient on a ward or in a rehab gym — assessment adapted to a patient who cannot sit at instruments, using hand-held targets, occluders, prisms, torch and red glass, often with reduced attention and head positioning limits.

Community/school vision screening or off-site outreach clinic: screening children for strabismus, amblyopia risk and binocular anomalies with portable equipment in a school room or community health setting, including cover test, motility, stereotest and acuity, and triage/referral decisions.

sources.developer: Duke University (Draelos, Izatt, Kuo et al.)
sources.title: Contactless optical coherence tomography of the eyes of freestanding individuals with a robotic scanner
sources.claim: Duke's robotically aligned OCT autonomously positions an imaging scanner to a free-standing or seated patient's eye without a chinrest, tracking eye position — the closest existing autonomous robotic system that works on a patient's eye in a clinic.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous robotic ophthalmic imaging. It shows a robot can safely align an instrument to a patient's eye, but it acquires retinal OCT volumes only; it does not occlude eyes, break fusion, measure deviation angles in gaze positions, test stereopsis/fusion or assess amblyopia, so it does not substantiate completion of an orthoptic examination.

sources.transferJustification: Related sub-step: automated measurement of the angle of ocular deviation. It is an optical instrument with electronic shutters rather than a machine that manipulates objects, it covers only one component of the examination, and it requires a cooperative, head-stabilized adult, so it cannot deliver the whole examination at worker quality.

sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated refraction in an eye-care lane. It shows motorized ophthalmic instruments can run a patient through a standardized measurement, but it measures refractive error and acuity only; it performs no cover testing, motility assessment, fusion/stereo testing or amblyopia workup, so it does not transfer to the orthoptic examination.

tasks.label: Perform diagnostic tests or measurements, such as motor testing, visual acuity testing, lensometry, retinoscopy, and color vision testing.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Ocular motor/alignment testing on a cooperative older child or adult in a hospital eye-clinic exam lane: cover-uncover and alternate prism cover test at distance and near, versions/ductions in nine gaze positions, near point of convergence, fusional amplitudes - orthoptist holds occluder, prism bars and fixation targets, watches refixation movements and records deviations in prism dioptres.

Assessment of a preverbal or poorly cooperative young child (often on a parent's lap) in a pediatric clinic room: fixation-and-following behaviour, preferential-looking (Teller/Cardiff) or picture/matching acuity, cover testing with toys and lights, plus cycloplegic retinoscopy with lens bars - requires coaxing, rapid improvisation and reading brief, fleeting responses.

Visual acuity testing of a cooperative adult or school-age child in a clinic exam lane: distance and near charts, each eye occluded in turn, unaided and with current spectacles/pinhole, recorded in logMAR/Snellen.

Objective and subjective refraction on a cooperative teenager or adult in the clinic lane: retinoscopy or autorefraction followed by refinement in phoropter/trial frame, with the final prescription recorded.
Lensometry at the clinic bench: the patient's own spectacles are measured for sphere, cylinder, axis, add and prism, optical centres located, and the readings recorded in the chart.
Colour vision testing (Ishihara/HRR plates, monocular, at set distance and illumination) and other sensory tests (stereoacuity booklet/Frisby, Worth 4-dot with red-green goggles) in the clinic room.

sources.transferJustification: Directly covers the visual-acuity and refraction (retinoscopy-equivalent) measurements named in the task; the machine presents optotypes, occludes and changes lenses via motorized optics and records the result.

tasks.label: Provide nonsurgical interventions, including corrective lenses, patches, drops, fusion exercises, or stereograms, to treat conditions such as strabismus, heterophoria, and convergence insufficiency.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Pediatric ophthalmology clinic: refractive/prismatic management of accommodative esotropia or symptomatic heterophoria — re-measuring the deviation with cover test and prism bar, choosing the spectacle/prism correction, cutting and press-applying a Fresnel prism onto the child's own spectacle lens, checking the fit and alignment on the child's face, and counseling the parent on wear.

Occlusion (patching) therapy for amblyopia in a 3–6 year old at a hospital eye clinic: setting the daily patching dose, applying the adhesive patch to the periocular skin of a wriggling, often resisting child (or fitting an occluder/Bangerter filter to the glasses), demonstrating the technique to the caregiver, and adjusting the regimen at follow-up.

Pharmacologic treatment in clinic: instilling atropine (penalization) or cycloplegic/diagnostic drops into the eye of a squeezing, tearful child or an anxious adult, positioning the lids, confirming the drop reached the eye, and instructing the caregiver on home dosing and side effects.

In-office fusion/vergence therapy session for convergence insufficiency in a school-age child or adult: Brock string, pencil push-ups, prism-bar jump vergences, vectograms/stereograms and accommodative flippers — holding and moving targets, watching the patient's eye alignment, suppression and diplopia reports, and adapting difficulty and pacing through the session.

Setting up and reviewing a home orthoptic exercise program: assembling take-home stereogram cards, anaglyph glasses, Brock string or computer-based exercises, demonstrating them on the patient, correcting technique, and re-checking compliance and progress at a follow-up visit (clinic, occasionally school/community outreach clinic).

sources.title: Contactless, autonomous robotic alignment of optical coherence tomography for in vivo evaluation of diseased retinas
sources.claim: A robotically aligned OCT scanner autonomously positions an imaging head to a seated/standing person's eye and acquires diagnostic-quality retinal images without a technician, showing autonomous non-contact robot alignment to a human eye in an eye clinic — but it only images the eye; it does not deliver any therapy, apply patches, instill drops, fit prisms or coach vergence exercises, so it does not substantiate completion of this treatment task.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous robotic ophthalmic imaging. It establishes only sensing/alignment near a cooperative adult's eye; it performs no manipulation of patches, drops, lenses or therapy targets and makes no treatment decisions, so capability does not transfer to providing nonsurgical orthoptic interventions.

sources.title: Luum Precision Lash: the 200 Best Inventions of 2024 (TIME)
sources.claim: LUUM's Precision Lash system uses machine-vision-guided robot arms to place individual eyelash extensions on a reclining adult client's closed eye in a retail studio, demonstrating fine manipulation immediately adjacent to the human eye; it works only on still, cooperative adults in a purpose-built chair and performs no clinical assessment or therapy.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic application of adhesive-bonded material to the eyelid margin of a cooperative adult. It is the closest demonstrated periocular robotic manipulation, but it requires an immobile, consenting adult and provides no drop instillation, patch dosing, prism fitting or adaptive therapy judgment, so it cannot complete any instance of this task.

sources.system: ARTAS iX Robotic Hair Restoration System
sources.title: ARTAS® Robotic Hair Restoration Treatments
sources.claim: The ARTAS iX robotic system autonomously harvests hair follicles from a patient's tensioned scalp in a clinic under physician supervision — an example of an FDA-cleared robot performing a precise physical procedure on a human body — but it operates on a rigidly fixtured scalp with a single repetitive punch action and has no analogue for pediatric eye treatment or therapy coaching.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous robotic procedure on a human patient in a clinic. Transfer fails because the workpiece is a fixtured, anesthetized scalp with one stereotyped action, whereas orthoptic interventions require patient-specific treatment selection, handling of uncooperative children, and adaptive coaching.

tasks.label: Develop or use special test and communication techniques to facilitate diagnosis and treatment of children or patients with disabilities.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Hospital/ophthalmology-clinic orthoptic assessment of an infant or toddler (0-3 y) held on a parent's lap: obtaining fixation and following behavior with toys and lights, preferential-looking acuity cards (Teller/Cardiff), Hirschberg/Bruckner, cover-uncover and prism cover testing with hand-held occluder and prism bar, while the child squirms, cries and looks away and must be re-engaged; results must be reliable enough for the ophthalmologist's surgical/refractive decisions.

Clinic assessment of a preschool/school-age child (3-8 y) using child-adapted tests: matching-card picture optotypes (Kay/LEA/HOTV), stereotests, ocular motility in nine positions, near point of convergence, prism cover test at distance and near, with games, praise, simplified instructions, repeated re-instruction and physical repositioning of the child's head and of the occluder.

Assessment of a patient with a disability - a nonverbal child with cerebral palsy or severe intellectual disability, an autistic child needing a low-stimulus adapted approach, or an adult with stroke/brain injury or dementia - in a clinic room or at the bedside: choosing and improvising behavioral tests, using communication aids and gestures, positioning a wheelchair or supporting the head, working around nystagmus, poor head control or aversion to touch.

Treatment-facilitation session in the clinic: applying and checking adhesive occlusion patches or Fresnel prisms on the child's spectacles, demonstrating and coaching convergence/fusion exercises, using reward charts, stickers and picture schedules to gain cooperation, and instructing child and parents on the home regimen and compliance.

Developing or adapting the special techniques and materials themselves: designing and preparing picture/matching charts, social stories and visual schedules for a specific child, assembling and laminating a bespoke test kit, and arranging the exam room (lighting, distraction removal, seating) for a patient with sensory or physical impairments.

sources.title: Contactless, autonomous robotic alignment of optical coherence tomography for in vivo evaluation of diseased retinas
sources.claim: A robot autonomously aligns an OCT scanner to the eye of a seated, unconstrained patient and acquires diagnostic retinal volumes on real clinic patients, but performs imaging only - no interactive behavioral testing and no manipulation of occluders, prisms or targets, and only with cooperative adults.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic ophthalmic examination/imaging in an eye clinic. It is the closest robotic system that examines a human eye autonomously, so it bounds what robots can do here; it aligns optics to a still adult eye rather than performing the interactive, behaviorally adapted acuity and alignment testing of children this task requires.

sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated eye examination. It shows a machine can position optics near an unconstrained human eye in a clinical room, but it images cooperative adults and performs none of the special pediatric/disability-adapted tests or communication in this task.

tasks.label: Provide training related to clinical methods or orthoptics to students, resident physicians, or other health professionals.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Didactic teaching session: an orthoptist delivers a lecture or case-based seminar on strabismus, amblyopia, or binocular vision testing to orthoptic students or ophthalmology residents in a classroom or conference room, using slides and imaging, and fields questions.

Clinic-side demonstration: the orthoptist performs a clinical method (cover/uncover and alternate prism cover test, Hess/Lees screen, sensory fusion and stereo testing, motility assessment) on a patient or a fellow trainee while narrating the technique and rationale so trainees learn how it is done.

Direct supervision in clinic: a student or resident performs measurements on a real patient while the orthoptist observes, corrects hand position or fixation targets verbally, re-checks the measurement, and gives immediate coaching and feedback.

In-service training for other health professionals (ophthalmic technicians, nurses, pediatricians, school screening staff) on vision screening protocols and use of specific equipment, delivered in a clinic conference room or on-site at the referring facility.

Preparing and administering training materials and assessments: writing protocols and teaching handouts, reviewing recorded or logged trainee cases, completing competency evaluations, and delivering written or verbal performance feedback.

tasks.label: Participate in clinical research projects.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Serving as a study examiner in an academic eye department: performing protocol-specified orthoptic and functional assessments on enrolled participants (ETDRS best-corrected visual acuity, cycloplegic refraction, prism-and-alternate-cover-test alignment in multiple gaze positions, ocular motility, stereoacuity, fusion), many of them children or patients with strabismus/amblyopia, with masked-examiner rules and per-protocol repeat testing.

Acquiring protocol ocular imaging on trial participants in the clinic's imaging room: seating and instructing the participant, entering the study ID, capturing OCT and colour fundus images of both eyes to the sponsor/reading-centre quality standard, checking image quality, repeating poor captures, and exporting/uploading the images.

Recruiting and screening: reviewing clinic lists for eligible patients, approaching them, explaining the study, taking written informed consent/assent, verifying inclusion and exclusion criteria, randomising, and scheduling follow-up visits.

Research data work at a desk: recording measurements on source documents, entering data into the eCRF, resolving monitor queries, cleaning and analysing datasets, and preparing abstracts, posters, papers and conference presentations.

Site logistics and study upkeep: preparing the study room and standardised test materials (charts, prisms, lighting checks), performing and documenting equipment calibration and maintenance, maintaining the investigator site file and regulatory documents, stocking and packaging study materials, and hosting monitoring visits.

tasks.label: Assist ophthalmologists in diagnostic ophthalmic procedures, such as ultrasonography, fundus photography, and tonometry.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Ophthalmology clinic imaging room: cooperative adult patient (already worked up/dilated if needed) is seated at a tabletop retinal camera or OCT; orthoptist positions chin/forehead on the rest, aligns to the pupil, captures color fundus photos and/or macular and optic-nerve OCT of both eyes, checks image quality, repeats poor captures, and saves the study to the chart for the ophthalmologist.

Ophthalmology clinic workup lane: cooperative adult patient has intraocular pressure measured before the ophthalmologist's exam using a non-contact (air-puff) or rebound tonometer; orthoptist seats the patient, obtains reliable readings on both eyes, repeats outliers, and records the values.

Clinic pretesting station: cooperative adult receives ancillary automated non-contact measurements ordered by the ophthalmologist — visual acuity screening, autorefraction/keratometry, non-contact optical biometry — with the orthoptist seating the patient, running the instrument, and transferring the printout/data to the record.

Pediatric or uncooperative patient (toddler in a parent's lap, child with nystagmus, elderly patient with dementia, wheelchair or stretcher patient): orthoptist coaxes and physically steadies the head, uses handheld or portable instruments (handheld tonometer, portable/RetCam-style fundus camera, photoscreener), times the capture to fleeting fixation, and repeats until the ophthalmologist has usable images or readings.

Contact diagnostic procedures assisting the ophthalmologist: instilling topical anesthetic, applying coupling gel, and performing or setting up ocular ultrasonography (A-scan axial length, B-scan through the closed lid), ultrasound pachymetry, or applanation tonometry on a reclined or slit-lamp-seated adult, then cleaning/disinfecting probes.

Chairside assistance during the ophthalmologist's examination or in-office procedure: instilling dilating/fluorescein drops, holding the patient's lids or head, handing and preparing instruments and lenses, adjusting the chair/slit lamp for the physician, steadying the patient during photography of an in-office procedure, and cleaning between patients.

tasks.label: Perform vision screening of children in schools or community health centers.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Preschool / Head Start / community-health-center screening of 3-5 year olds: orthoptist greets a squirmy, often shy child, positions them at 1 m, uses a handheld photoscreener/autorefractor, coaxes fixation, repeats invalid captures, attempts LEA-symbol acuity with an adhesive occluder, observes lids and red reflex, records results and issues referral.

Elementary-school mass screening (K-5) in a gym, cafeteria or nurse's office: class-by-class flow, child stands at 10 ft, one eye occluded with paddle/patch, matches or names optotypes, near card, stereo (Random Dot E) and sometimes color vision; screener judges effort and peeking, re-tests, documents and flags referrals.

Middle/high-school screening of cooperative older children in a school health room: distance acuity with and without existing glasses, sometimes a handheld autorefractor reading, brief history, documentation and referral notice to parents.

Community health center clinic room: full orthoptic screening of a child brought by a parent - visual acuity, cover/uncover and alternate cover test with an occluder, ocular motility, near point of convergence, stereoacuity, Bruckner/red reflex; clinical judgment on referral and discussion with the caregiver.

Screening of infants, toddlers, or children with developmental disabilities / nonverbal children in early-intervention or special-education settings: behavioral techniques (fix-and-follow, preferential looking/Teller cards, Hirschberg light reflex), physical handling of a distressed or resistant child, improvised positioning on a caregiver's lap.

sources.transferJustification: Related task: daily health screening of preschoolers by an autonomous machine in an institutional child setting. It shows young children can be routed to a machine at throughput, but the measurement is a gross visual inspection for redness, blisters and fever, not the photorefraction, visual acuity or cover-test judgments a vision screening requires, so it does not substantiate completion of this task.

sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous robotic alignment of an optical sensor to a human eye without a chinrest. It is the closest robotic capability to holding a photoscreener on a child, but it was demonstrated only on cooperative adults in a dim lab room as a feasibility study, and performs none of the subjective acuity or binocular tests a pediatric vision screening comprises.

sources.transferJustification: Related task: contactless robotic ocular imaging of unrestrained patients in a clinical facility. An operator still triggers each acquisition, and the modality (retinal OCT in adults) does not cover acuity testing, occlusion or cover testing in children.

sources.transferJustification: Related task: unattended automated vision testing of adults in a retail setting. It measures acuity and refraction but is a sensing kiosk rather than a manipulating robot, and the vendor restricts it to adults, so it does not substantiate screening children.

sources.claim: Preschool vision screening in community programs is performed with handheld photoscreeners and autorefractors (plusoptiX S12C, Retinomax K+3) that are aimed and operated by a human screener who positions and engages the child; the automation is in the optics, not in an autonomous machine.
sources.transferJustification: Documents the actual state of practice for the instrument-based portion of this task: the devices are human-held tools requiring an operator to position, aim and re-attempt on the child, so they are not robotic systems completing the instance.

sources.title: Towards expert-level autonomous carotid ultrasonography with large-scale learning-based robotic system

sources.transferJustification: Related task: an autonomous robot placing a clinical sensor on a person's body in a healthcare facility. It shows robots can acquire clinical measurements on cooperative adults, but a pediatric vision screening additionally requires eliciting subjective responses from a child, occluding eyes and judging eye movements, which this does not transfer to.

tasks.label: Analyze samples of biological material for chemical content or reaction.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: High-volume routine chemistry and immunoassay in a hospital or reference core laboratory equipped with total laboratory automation: barcoded vacutainer tubes arrive continuously by pneumatic tube or courier, are centrifuged, decapped, aliquoted and routed to analyzers on a track; the technologist monitors the line, resolves flags, and releases results (most auto-released).

Mid-size hospital/clinic laboratory (roughly 2,000-5,000 tests/day) with compact automation or bench analyzers: tech receives racks of tubes, centrifuges, loads chemistry/immunoassay analyzers, prioritizes STATs, handles dilutions and reruns on flagged results, reviews and reports.

Small hospital, clinic, or physician-office laboratory: low daily volume, tech personally spins, uncaps, racks and loads a benchtop chemistry/immunoassay analyzer, runs calibrators and controls, pipettes occasional manual/semi-automated reactions, and reports the results.

STAT critical-care whole-blood chemistry: heparinized syringes or capillaries hand-delivered or tubed to a stat lab (or near-patient device), injected into a blood gas/electrolyte/co-oximetry analyzer, result verified and phoned within minutes.

Esoteric/specialty chemistry in a reference or academic laboratory: LC-MS/MS therapeutic drug monitoring, drug-of-abuse confirmations, steroid/vitamin panels, electrophoresis; batch build with calibrators and QC, extraction/protein precipitation sample prep, chromatographic review before release.

Problem and atypical specimens: body fluids (CSF, pleural, peritoneal, dialysate, synovial), 24-hour urines, specimens in cups/syringes/non-standard containers, short, clotted, hemolyzed or grossly lipemic samples requiring assessment, manual aliquoting, off-line dilution and manual result filing.

instances.label: High-volume hospital core lab or reference lab: routine serum/plasma chemistry and immunoassay panels (BMP/CMP, lipids, enzymes, cardiac markers) on barcoded primary tubes; specimens are received, centrifuged, decapped, aliquoted, routed to analyzers, results reviewed against QC/delta rules and released, tubes archived for add-ons.

Small or mid-size hospital/clinic laboratory without a track line: technologist centrifuges tubes, loads racks onto benchtop chemistry/immunoassay analyzers, runs calibration and QC, dilutes or reruns flagged specimens, and verifies/releases chemistry results, often overnight with a single tech.

Routine urinalysis: chemical (dipstick/reflectance) analysis of urine for protein, glucose, ketones, blood, pH, plus automated particle/sediment screening; high daily volume of variable, turbid or contaminated specimens in cups and tubes.

STAT cerebrospinal fluid and other body fluids (pleural, peritoneal, synovial): small-volume specimens in non-standard sterile tubes; glucose, protein, lactate chemistry plus cell counts, with rapid turnaround required and appearance noted.

Specialized chemistry on commercial automated platforms: therapeutic drug monitoring, immunosuppressants, vitamin D by LC-MS/MS, serum protein electrophoresis/HbA1c; sample loaded as primary tube on a dedicated automated analyzer, with QC and technical review.

Esoteric / laboratory-developed assays: broad urine drug confirmation panels and other LDT LC-MS/MS or manual assays requiring extraction, derivatization, batch calibration, and chromatogram integration and interpretation by the technologist.

tasks.label: Collect and study blood samples to determine the number of cells, their morphology, or their blood group, blood type, or compatibility for transfusion purposes, using microscopic techniques.

instances.label: Routine CBC with automated differential in a hospital or reference core laboratory: EDTA tubes arrive by courier/pneumatic tube, are racked or fed on an automation track, aspirated by a high-volume hematology analyzer that enumerates RBCs, WBCs and platelets and produces a 5/6-part differential with morphology flags; results released after rule-based review.

Reflex peripheral blood smear on a flagged routine sample (WBC roughly 1.5-30 x10^9/L): make and stain a wedge smear, examine it under oil immersion, perform a 100-cell differential and comment on RBC/platelet morphology, then report the verified differential.

Difficult morphology review: extreme leukocytosis or leukopenia, suspected leukemia/blasts, dysplasia, plasma cells, schistocytes, or malaria/babesia thick-and-thin smear screening; technologist scans the whole smear, classifies abnormal cells, decides on pathologist referral and adds interpretive comments.

Hospital transfusion service pretransfusion workup: ABO/Rh forward and reverse typing, antibody screen, and crossmatch of donor units for a surgical or transfusion-dependent patient, reading graded agglutination reactions in gel/column or tube technique and resolving routine discrepancies before releasing units.

Collecting the specimen at an outpatient draw station: seat an ambulatory adult patient, verify identity, apply tourniquet, select and palpate a vein, perform venipuncture, fill and invert the ordered tubes in order of draw, label, and bandage.

Collecting the specimen at the inpatient bedside or from a hard-stick patient: draws in a hospital bed, ICU, or pediatric/neonatal setting (heel stick, small veins, edematous or oncology patients), with the patient recumbent, lines in place, and limited arm access.
