tasks.label: Supervise histology laboratory activities.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Daily workflow oversight in a hospital or reference histology lab: the lead histotechnologist monitors specimen accessioning volume and turnaround times, assigns staff to grossing, processing, embedding, microtomy, staining and coverslipping stations, reprioritizes STAT/frozen-section and biopsy cases, and adjusts coverage when a backlog or absence occurs.

Quality assurance oversight: reviewing daily QC logs, control-slide and special-stain/IHC control results, monitoring recut and repeat rates, block/slide labeling audits, signing off on documentation, and directing corrective action for out-of-spec results under CLIA/CAP requirements.

Personnel supervision: orienting and training new histotechnicians and students, performing documented competency assessments and direct observation of technique, scheduling shifts and time off, conducting performance reviews, and coaching or disciplining staff.

Administrative and compliance supervision: writing and revising SOPs, managing reagent and consumable inventory and vendor ordering, budgeting and capital-equipment justification, preparing for CAP/JCAHO inspections, and meeting with pathologists and lab management about service issues.

Incident and problem escalation oversight: responding when an instrument (processor, stainer, microtome) goes down or a specimen mix-up, mislabel or tissue-quality problem is reported; investigating root cause, coordinating vendor service and rerouting work, and reporting the event.

tasks.label: Teach students or other staff.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Bench-side one-on-one instruction of a histotechnology student or newly hired technician in the histology lab: explaining and demonstrating embedding orientation, microtome sectioning technique, block facing, floating out sections, and correcting the trainee's technique as they practice on their own blocks.

Informal in-lab coaching of staff on SOPs, reagent handling, stain chemistry, and troubleshooting of artifacts (chatter, folds, weak H&E, IHC background) — explaining causes and corrective actions during routine work, often while both people look at slides or the instrument display.

Formal didactic teaching: a lecture, slide presentation, or in-service to a histotechnology program class, pathology residents, or lab staff on topics such as fixation principles, immunohistochemistry theory, safety, or new regulatory requirements, followed by questions.

Competency assessment and structured feedback: observing a staff member perform a procedure, scoring against a checklist, documenting results in the training record, and discussing deficiencies and remediation plans with the employee.

Orientation and instrument walkthroughs for other staff (grossing assistants, residents, cross-trained MLS staff, or vendor-trained users): touring the lab workflow, explaining specimen accessioning and labeling rules, and walking through operation of a processor, stainer, or coverslipper.

tasks.label: Perform electron microscopy or mass spectrometry to analyze specimens.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Hospital/reference EM laboratory: diagnostic transmission EM of a renal biopsy. Take the resin-embedded, ultrathin-sectioned, contrasted copper grids, load them in the specimen holder, insert into the TEM, screen at low magnification to locate glomeruli, then capture a documented series of micrographs of capillary loops (GBM, foot processes, electron-dense deposits) at several magnifications, measure GBM thickness, and archive images for the pathologist within the biopsy turnaround time.

Hospital/academic EM laboratory: diagnostic TEM of other tissue - skeletal muscle or nerve biopsy, respiratory cilia for primary ciliary dyskinesia, unclassified tumor, or viral inclusions. Grids are screened for sparse, variable diagnostic features; the technologist hunts the section, decides what is diagnostic, and captures/annotates a micrograph set.

Academic/research core EM facility: research-support electron microscopy on prepared blocks and sections - serial-section array tomography or FIB-SEM slice-and-view volume runs, or cryo-EM grid screening and single-particle data collection - typically long unattended acquisitions producing large image datasets for investigators.

EM laboratory: scanning electron microscopy of specimens - specimen mounted on a stub or wafer and sputter-coated, loaded into the SEM chamber, imaged at a range of magnifications (sometimes with EDS elemental analysis), images documented for the requesting pathologist or investigator.

Research/clinical mass spectrometry lab attached to pathology: MALDI imaging mass spectrometry of a mounted tissue section - matrix applied to the ITO slide with a sprayer, slide loaded into the MALDI instrument, region of interest defined, raster acquisition run, ion images generated and checked against the H&E for quality.

Pathology/clinical mass spectrometry lab: LC-MS/MS analysis of tissue-derived or clinical samples (e.g., microdissected amyloid digests, tissue extracts, drug/analyte quantitation). Samples aliquoted into vials or plates, calibrators and QC placed in the rack, autosampler loaded, method run, chromatograms and QC reviewed and results released.

tasks.label: Perform quality control analyses to ensure accuracy of test results.
Conduct blood tests for transfusion purposes and perform blood counts.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Hospital core/hematology lab, day shift: batches of EDTA tubes arrive by courier and pneumatic tube; tech checks labels and specimen integrity, mixes and loads racks onto a high-throughput automated hematology analyzer line, runs daily QC and calibration checks, monitors flags, reruns/dilutes as needed, and releases CBC with automated differential results.

Flagged CBC follow-up in the same hospital lab: prepare and stain a peripheral blood smear (wedge smear), scan under the microscope, perform a 100-cell WBC differential, assess RBC morphology and platelet estimate, and report the manual differential on abnormal/flagged specimens.

Hospital transfusion service, routine pre-transfusion testing: load patient EDTA tubes, gel/solid-phase cards and reagent red cells; perform ABO/Rh typing, antibody screen and serologic or electronic crossmatch on a walk-away immunohematology analyzer; run QC, review reaction images, resolve simple discrepancies and report.

Transfusion service bench work done by hand in tubes or gel cards: direct antiglobulin test, weak D confirmation, cord blood ABO/DAT, donor unit antigen typing, and routine antibody identification panels — pipetting, incubating at 37 C, washing, centrifuging and grading agglutination.

STAT/off-shift and complex serology: emergency-release and massive transfusion protocol crossmatching under time pressure, warm/cold autoantibody workups requiring elution, adsorption, or prewarm techniques, discrepant ABO resolution, interruptions from clinicians, with a lone tech covering the bench.

Small community hospital lab, clinic or physician office lab: low daily volume; run CBCs on a compact benchtop hematology analyzer, spin and read a micro-hematocrit, perform slide/tube ABO-Rh typing or run a small automated blood bank instrument, while multitasking across other bench sections.

instances.label: Routine peripheral blood smear review in a hospital hematology lab: a Wright-Giemsa stained slide flagged by the CBC analyzer is placed under the microscope, scanned at 50x/100x oil, ~100-200 WBCs classified, RBC and platelet morphology graded; findings are common/reactive (left shift, atypical lymphocytes, mild anisopoikilocytosis, adequate platelets).

Complex/critical blood smear examination: suspected acute leukemia or myelodysplasia, blast identification and quantification, schistocyte counting for suspected TMA, resolution of platelet clumping or RBC agglutination; STAT and clinically consequential, in a hospital or reference hematology lab.

Gram-stained smear reading in a clinical microbiology lab: direct patient specimens (sputum, wound, CSF, tissue) and positive blood culture smears examined at 100x oil immersion; report bacterial morphotypes, yeast, and quantify WBCs/squamous epithelial cells for specimen adequacy; blood culture Grams are critical-value calls.

Urine sediment microscopy in a core lab: centrifuged sediment (often Sternheimer-Malbin stained) examined at low and high power to enumerate RBCs, WBCs, epithelial cells, casts, crystals, bacteria and to spot dysmorphic cells or pathologic casts.

Body-fluid cell differential on a stained cytospin (CSF, synovial, pleural, peritoneal) in a hospital lab: low cellularity, STAT turnaround, differentiate neutrophils/lymphocytes/monocytes-macrophages and flag malignant or atypical cells.

Special stained smears for organisms/parasites in a hospital or reference lab: Giemsa thick and thin films for malaria, trichrome/concentrate stool ova-and-parasite preparations, auramine-O or Kinyoun acid-fast smears; long scan times over many fields, screening mostly negative slides for rare positives.

instances.label: High-volume hospital or reference microbiology lab, front-end: routine liquid and liquid-based swab specimens (urine cups, ESwab wound/throat/genital swabs, sputum, stool) are accessioned, uncapped, inoculated onto primary agar media, streaked for isolation, labeled, and loaded into incubators; Gram slides prepared where ordered.

Same lab, post-incubation work-up: plates read for growth and colony counts, negatives reported/discarded, isolated colonies picked and subcultured to purity, MALDI-TOF targets spotted and AST inoculum suspensions prepared, ID/AST instruments loaded and results generated.

Blood cultures and other bottle/broth cultures: bottles received and loaded into a continuous-monitoring incubator, monitored to positivity, then Gram smear prepared and the bottle subcultured to solid media, incubated, and identified (MALDI-TOF) with AST; negatives finalized after 5 days.

Obtaining the specimen directly from the patient: technician performs venipuncture at an outpatient draw station or bedside to collect blood specimens (routine tubes and blood culture sets) for laboratory analysis.

Non-routine specimens needing manual bench/biosafety-cabinet manipulation: tissue, bone and biopsy specimens requiring homogenization, mycobacterial specimens requiring digestion/decontamination, fungal cultures, anaerobic work-up, and specimens arriving in nonstandard containers (syringes, cups, aspirates).

Small community hospital, clinic or physician-office lab with a manual micro bench and a limited menu (urine cultures, throat/wound cultures): tech plates by hand with loops, streaks for isolation, incubates, reads plates and performs rapid biochemicals/manual ID.

tasks.label: Collect blood or tissue samples from patients, observing principles of asepsis to obtain blood sample.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Outpatient/clinic draw station: cooperative adult with usable antecubital veins presents with a routine requisition; technician verifies ID, seats patient, applies tourniquet and alcohol, performs multi-tube venipuncture in order of draw, inverts and labels tubes, bandages the site and sends specimens to the lab.

Inpatient bedside draw on a hospital ward (or nursing-home round): patient in bed or chair, wristband ID check, arm positioning constrained by IV lines, gowns, bed rails and roommates; timed morning-round collection carried out at the bedside.

Draw-station venipuncture on a harder-than-average but still accessible adult: elderly, high BMI, or self-reported difficult venous access, where a usable antecubital vein can still be found by palpation or imaging.

Hard sticks and non-routine patients: fragile, scarred, collapsed or thrombosed veins (oncology, dialysis, IV drug use), mastectomy/fistula-restricted arms, hand or wrist alternate-site draws, pediatric venipuncture, and urgent/STAT ED or ICU draws on agitated or unresponsive patients.

Capillary collection: adult fingerstick for small-volume or point-of-care tests, and infant/child heelstick or fingerstick into microtainers, including warming, wiping the first drop and coaxing adequate flow with poor perfusion.
Non-blood specimen collection in the clinic: throat/nasopharyngeal or buccal swab taken from a seated patient with aseptic single-use swabs, placed into transport medium and labeled.

sources.title: Performance, Safety, and Patient Experience of an Autonomous Robotic Phlebotomy Device: A Multicenter Trial (Clinical Chemistry)

sources.title: Performance, Safety, and Patient Experience of an Autonomous Robotic Phlebotomy Device: A Multicenter Trial (Clinical Chemistry)

Clinical microbiology bench: urine, wound, respiratory specimens and MRSA/VRE/GBS screening swabs are plated to agar, incubated, plates read for significant growth, colonies picked for MALDI-TOF identification and antimicrobial susceptibility testing, and results reported.

Hospital transfusion service: patient sample tested for ABO/Rh grouping, antibody screen and serologic crossmatch on gel-card technology, with positive screens reflexed to 11-cell antibody identification panels before units are issued.

Quality control, calibration and materials verification in the same lab: running two or three levels of control material at defined intervals on each analyzer, calibrating assays, testing new reagent/consumable lots and proficiency-testing samples against acceptance criteria before patient testing resumes.

tasks.label: Cut sections of body tissues for microscopic examination, using microtomes.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Routine clinical histology lab: facing/trimming a formalin-fixed paraffin-embedded block on a rotary microtome, cutting 3-5 µm ribbons of ordinary soft tissue (GI biopsies, breast, prostate, gyn, skin shaves), floating on a warm water bath, picking up on a labeled slide and draining/drying for H&E. High volume, dozens to hundreds of blocks per shift.

Cutting multiple levels, serial sections, and extra unstained charged slides from FFPE blocks for immunohistochemistry, special stains and molecular work (e.g., 3 levels plus 10 unstained recuts), including recuts from archived blocks pulled days or weeks later.

Difficult FFPE blocks requiring adapted technique: decalcified bone and bone marrow cores, fatty/adipose and breast blocks, fibrous uterus, eye, nail, tiny fragile core biopsies where the tech must re-face carefully, ice-soak, change blade angle or cold-plate the block to get a full, ribbon-quality section without losing tissue.

Frozen sectioning in a cryostat for intraoperative consultation or Mohs surgery: embedding fresh unfixed tissue in OCT on a chuck, orienting and freezing, trimming, cutting 5-10 µm sections with the anti-roll plate, picking up on a slide by hand and handing to staining, all within a 10-20 minute turnaround while a surgeon waits.

Research and specialty sectioning: oversized/large-format (mega) blocks, plastic/resin-embedded specimens for high-resolution or EM work, whole-mount and animal-tissue blocks for research studies, often serial sections collected in order at nonstandard thicknesses.

tasks.label: Embed tissue specimens into paraffin wax blocks, or infiltrate tissue specimens with wax.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Hospital/reference histology lab, embedding bench: technician embeds routine small biopsies (GI endoscopic biopsies, skin punch/shave, needle core biopsies, prostate cores) — opens each processed cassette, transfers fragments with warm forceps into a base mold, orients them (mucosa on edge, cores laid straight), tops with paraffin and cassette, chills on cold plate, one block per case at ~30-60 s each.

Same lab: embedding sections from larger surgical/resection specimens (colon, breast, uterus, TURP/TURB chips, LLETZ, skin excisions >2 cm) — often multiple tissue pieces per cassette to be laid flat and parallel in standard or large molds.

Tissue processing / wax infiltration: technician loads racks or baskets of grossed cassettes into an automated vacuum-infiltration processor, selects a validated protocol (dehydration, clearing, molten paraffin infiltration under vacuum/heat), runs it overnight or as a rapid run, then unloads the wax-infiltrated cassettes for embedding.

Difficult-to-orient or delicate specimens: minute multiple fragments (needing biopsy pads, bags or gels), tubular structures (vas deferens, artery, fallopian tube) that must be embedded on their side, curved skin ellipses, decalcified bone, fatty tissue prone to floating out of the mold.

Non-routine block formats and rework: oversized/mega-cassette blocks and whole-mount sections (e.g., whole prostate, brain, large lung slices), unusual research embedding molds, and re-embedding/repairing blocks where tissue is mis-oriented, cracked, or lifted after the first attempt.

tasks.label: Mount tissue specimens on glass slides.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Routine surgical-pathology paraffin blocks in a hospital or reference histology lab: after facing/trimming, the tech floats the 3-5 µm ribbon on a warm water bath, picks one section onto a labeled charged slide with correct orientation and no folds/bubbles/contaminants, drains and racks it for drying, matching slide to block accession. High volume (hundreds of slides per shift), bench workstation with microtome, water bath, hot plate.

Multiple levels / serial sections and unstained slides from the same paraffin block for special stains, IHC or molecular work: several sections mounted in defined order onto several charged/positively-charged slides, section placement standardized for downstream staining platforms and scanners; antigenicity and section integrity must be preserved.

Frozen sections during intraoperative consultation: in the cryostat at -20 to -30 °C the tech flattens the curling section with a brush/anti-roll plate and picks it up by touching a room-temperature slide to it, within a few minutes of receiving the specimen; OCT-embedded fresh tissue, fatty or friable, time-critical.

Hard or awkward but standard-size paraffin blocks: decalcified bone/marrow cores, heavily fatty or fibrous tissue, tiny needle biopsies and cell blocks, where sections compress, crack or shred and require careful flotation, flattening and placement on standard 1x3 in slides.

Large-format / whole-mount work: prostate, breast lumpectomy or brain megablocks and eyes mounted on oversized (2x3 in or larger) slides, whole-mount sections that must be floated flat and positioned by hand without tearing, often in academic or specialty labs.

Specialty and research mounting outside the routine paraffin workflow: research cryosections onto capture/membrane slides (LCM, spatial transcriptomics), resin semithin sections, sections mounted with tape-transfer for difficult tissue, touch preps/cell-block smears; varied slide types and one-off protocols.

tasks.label: Stain tissue specimens with dyes or other chemicals to make cell details visible under microscopes.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Routine H&E staining of a batch of paraffin sections in a hospital or reference histology lab: tech collects freshly cut/dried slides, loads them into staining racks, selects the H&E protocol on a linear/batch autostainer, monitors reagent levels and rotation, and checks resulting nuclear/cytoplasmic contrast before coverslipping.

Immunohistochemistry / in-situ hybridization staining runs in a clinical AP lab: labeled slides loaded onto an automated IHC platform with antibody and detection reagents, protocol selected per marker, controls included, run monitored and stained slides checked against control tissue.

Special (histochemical) stains ordered by pathologists — GMS, PAS/diastase, trichrome, iron, Congo red, reticulin, mucicarmine, acid-fast — performed either on an automated special-stains platform or by hand at the bench with freshly prepared reagents, timed differentiation and control slides.

Rapid staining of frozen sections during intraoperative consultation in a frozen-section room next to the OR: 1–4 slides fixed and dipped through a short H&E sequence under strict time pressure, with occasional rapid IHC, then handed to the pathologist within minutes.

Academic/industry research lab staining: customized IHC, immunofluorescence or multiplex protocols on FFPE or frozen research sections, run on a programmable research staining platform with user-defined incubation times, temperatures and reagents.

Niche manual procedures with no automated menu: enzyme histochemistry on fresh-frozen muscle/nerve biopsies (NADH, ATPase at set pH), oversized/whole-mount or thick sections, and stains requiring microscope-controlled differentiation judged by eye and re-dipped as needed.

tasks.label: Freeze tissue specimens.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Intraoperative frozen section in a hospital histology/frozen-section room: fresh unfixed surgical specimen arrives from the OR, technician orients it in a cryomold or on a chuck with OCT, and snap-freezes it on the cryobar/heat extractor or flash chiller within minutes so the pathologist gets a diagnosis inside the ~20-minute turnaround.

Mohs/dermatologic frozen section in a clinic or dermatopathology lab: thin, curled skin margin must be flattened so epidermal edges lie in one plane, embedded in OCT (often with paper/cellulose aids) and frozen without ice-crystal artifact for complete margin visualization.

Research/biobank snap-freezing: fresh tissue aliquots are placed in cryovials, foil or cryomolds, quenched in liquid nitrogen or isopentane/dry ice, labeled/barcoded, logged, and transferred to -80 C or LN2 vapor-phase storage under a written SOP.

Orientation-critical specialty freezing: muscle biopsy mounted transversely on cork with gum tragacanth and plunged in isopentane cooled by LN2, renal biopsy frozen for immunofluorescence, nerve biopsy — technique and orientation determine whether the specimen is diagnostically usable.

Routine ancillary freezing in the histology lab: freezing residual/backup tissue for possible extra levels or fat stains, re-freezing OCT blocks on the cryostat quick-freeze shelf between levels, and returning frozen blocks and specimens to freezer storage with logging; not time-critical.

tasks.label: Operate computerized laboratory equipment to dehydrate, decalcify, or microincinerate tissue samples.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Hospital/reference histology lab, end of day: tech collects the day's grossed cassettes (100-300) from grossing, loads them into processing baskets/magazines, loads the retort of an automated tissue processor, selects the overnight dehydration/clearing/paraffin-infiltration protocol, starts the run, and unloads the hot, paraffin-filled cassettes the next morning for embedding.

Same-day / STAT runs during the shift on a rapid or continuous processor (microwave or continuous-flow instrument): small batches of biopsies and urgent cases loaded through the day, protocol selected, processed cassettes retrieved and passed to embedding, with a quick check that tissue is adequately processed.

Routine decalcification of small calcified specimens (bone-marrow trephines, small bone fragments) using a standardized, pre-validated EDTA or acid protocol on a decalcification unit or timed bath in the histology lab; specimen placed in the vessel, protocol run, rinsed, and passed to processing.

Decalcification of large or variable calcified specimens (resected bone, teeth, heavily calcified breast tissue): agent and time chosen for the specimen, endpoint judged by physical probing, chemical test or cabinet radiography, specimen returned for further decal if needed, then rinsed and processed.

Reagent and consumable handling that comes with running the processor: responding to an 'reagent exhausted / rotate reagents' prompt, swapping and refilling 5 L formalin, ethanol and clearing-agent containers, draining waste and used paraffin, running a clean cycle and wiping wax from the retort before the next load.

Research or specialty work in a hospital research/university lab: microincineration/ashing of mounted tissue in a muffle furnace for mineral study, or running a non-routine processing protocol (vacuum oven, microwave processor, special research schedule) on a small number of samples.

tasks.label: Archive diagnostic material, such as histologic slides and blocks.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: High-volume hospital/reference histology lab: at end of day the tech collects glass H&E and IHC slides returned from pathologist sign-out (or from the WSI scanner racks), sorts them into accession-number order, files them into slide cabinets/trays or long-term slide boxes, and records the archive location in the LIS.

Same lab: paraffin blocks returned from microtomy/sign-out are cleaned of excess wax, sorted by accession number and filed into block storage drawers, racks or archive boxes, with location recorded and box ranges labeled.

Retrieval from the archive on request (recuts, special stains, molecular testing, outside consults, tumor board, medico-legal requests): locating the specific slide or block in the archive, checking it out in the tracking log, releasing it, and re-filing it when returned.

Periodic archive housekeeping: consolidating older slides and blocks into archive boxes, labeling and shelving them in a lab storage/records room or preparing them for off-site storage, and purging or discarding material that has passed the retention period, with records updated.

Archiving non-standard diagnostic material: formalin wet-tissue containers held for the retention window and then discarded, cytology smears and liquid-based slides, frozen-section slides and blocks, oversized/mega blocks, cell blocks, EM grids, plus associated requisition paperwork, each going to its own storage format.

tasks.label: Maintain laboratory equipment, such as microscopes, mass spectrometers, microtomes, immunostainers, tissue processors, embedding centers, and water baths.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Daily microtome (and cryostat) upkeep at the cutting bench: brush and vacuum paraffin shavings from the stage and chuck, unclamp and discard the used disposable blade into a sharps container, load a fresh blade, solvent-wipe the blade holder and specimen clamp, oil/lubricate moving parts, decontaminate the cryostat chamber with alcohol, and initial the maintenance log.

Water baths, slide dryers, hot plates and the embedding center: drain the flotation bath, wipe out the paraffin film and floating tissue debris, refill with distilled water, verify temperature against a thermometer, empty and scrape wax trays and the paraffin drip tray on the embedding center, refill paraffin pellets/tank, and record checks.

Hands-on tissue processor service: check reagent levels, drain exhausted formalin/alcohol/xylene at the fill-drain ports into waste carboys and charge fresh reagent, empty the used-paraffin waste container, clean the retort walls, level sensors and lid seal of tissue debris and wax, wipe the paraffin baths, and replace carbon/exhaust filters.

Routine instrument-driven fluid upkeep: rotating solutions through processor stations, running the manufacturer's programmed cleaning/flush cycle on the processor or stainer at end of run, and confirming levels and cycle completion — work done by starting the instrument's own automated routine rather than by disassembly.

Stainer, immunostainer and coverslipper upkeep: refill bulk buffer/wash and DI water containers, empty bulk and hazardous waste containers, wipe and clean wash blocks, aspiration probes, dispensers and slide trays, replace tubing or probes, dispose of used stain and xylene from staining dishes, and run prime/flush.

Microscopes and ancillary instruments (balances, pH meters, occasionally a mass spectrometer in research settings): clean objectives and eyepieces with lens paper, check illumination and alignment, dust and cover the scope, verify temperature/calibration checks on ancillary devices, and complete preventive-maintenance logs or schedule vendor service.

roles.description: Conduct tests on pulmonary or cardiovascular systems of patients for diagnostic, therapeutic, or research purposes. May conduct or assist in electrocardiograms, cardiac catheterizations, pulmonary functions, lung capacity, and similar tests.

tasks.label: Conduct electrocardiogram (EKG), phonocardiogram, echocardiogram, stress testing, or other cardiovascular tests to record patients' cardiac activity, using specialized electronic test equipment, recording devices, or laboratory instruments.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Resting 12-lead EKG on an inpatient or clinic outpatient: tech brings the cart to the bed/exam room, explains the test, exposes and preps the skin (wipes, shaves if needed), palpates intercostal spaces and landmarks to site 6 precordial and 4 limb electrodes on varied body habitus, connects leads, acquires an artifact-free tracing, repeats if wandering baseline/muscle noise, removes electrodes and transmits the trace to the reading cardiologist.

Complete transthoracic echocardiogram in a hospital or clinic echo lab on a cooperative ambulatory patient: position patient in left lateral decubitus, apply gel, obtain parasternal long/short axis, apical 4/2/3-chamber, subcostal and suprasternal windows with 2D, M-mode, color, spectral and tissue Doppler, coach breathing, make chamber/valve measurements, and store a complete study for interpretation (~40-60 min).

Portable bedside study on an acutely ill patient in ICU/ED/CCU or OR: limited or full echo (or urgent 12-lead EKG) on a patient who cannot be positioned well, with lines, drains, dressings, telemetry wires, ventilator, obesity or poor acoustic windows; tech improvises windows and electrode sites and still returns a diagnostic study quickly.

Exercise treadmill or pharmacologic stress test (with or without stress echo): hook up stress electrodes with skin prep, obtain baseline EKG and BP, run the Bruce protocol while continuously watching rhythm/ST changes and the patient, take serial BPs, capture immediate post-exercise apical/parasternal images within seconds, and respond to symptoms or arrhythmia by stopping the test and summoning help.

Ambulatory/continuous monitoring hookup in clinic: apply Holter, event or patch monitor electrodes with skin prep, secure leads, verify signal, instruct the patient on the diary and hygiene, then remove and download/scan the recording at return; also telemetry lead placement and lead-fault troubleshooting on the ward.

Non-invasive vascular exam in a vascular lab: carotid duplex screening/exam with B-mode sweep of common/internal/external carotids bilaterally, intima-media and lumen measurement, plaque detection, plus color/pulsed Doppler; also ankle-brachial index or venous duplex on a cooperative outpatient.

instances.label: Cardiac catheterization lab during a diagnostic cath or PCI: the technologist watches the continuous ECG rhythm, arterial/hemodynamic pressure waveforms, and cuff blood pressure on the monitoring console, recognizes ST changes, arrhythmias, or a falling pressure, and calls them out verbally to the interventional cardiologist at the table.

Exercise or pharmacologic stress test in a cardiology clinic: the technician watches the 12-lead ECG and takes/reads serial blood pressures and heart rate at each stage, judges ST depression, ectopy, or hypotensive response against termination criteria, and notifies the supervising physician immediately.

Electrophysiology lab or device implant procedure: the technologist monitors surface ECG, intracardiac signals, heart rate and blood pressure throughout ablation or pacemaker/ICD placement, and alerts the electrophysiologist to rhythm changes, capture loss, or hemodynamic deterioration.

Telemetry/central monitoring station or Holter-review workstation: the technician observes multiple patients' continuous ECG traces and vital-sign trends on displays, distinguishes true arrhythmias from artifact and false alarms, and notifies the nurse or physician of clinically significant findings.

Bedside monitoring during a therapeutic or diagnostic procedure outside the cath lab (cardioversion, TEE, stress echo, tilt-table, ICU procedure): the technologist watches ECG rhythm, heart rate, and automated blood pressure on a portable monitor and verbally reports abnormalities to the physician performing the procedure.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Resting 12-lead ECG in an outpatient cardiology clinic or hospital unit: verify patient identity, explain the test, have the patient disrobe to the waist and lie supine on the exam table, clean/shave/abrade skin sites, place 10 adhesive electrodes at precise anatomic landmarks (intercostal spaces, midclavicular/axillary lines), position limbs and drape for comfort and modesty.

Transthoracic echocardiogram prep in an echo lab: gown the patient, assist an often elderly or frail patient onto the stretcher, roll and position in left lateral decubitus with left arm behind the head, place 3-lead ECG electrodes, apply gel, adjust pillows/table tilt and drape; reposition (supine, subcostal, sitting) during the study.

Cardiac catheterization / EP lab prep: transfer a premedicated or sedated patient from stretcher to the narrow procedure table, position supine with arms tucked or abducted, apply ECG electrodes and defibrillator pads, clip/shave groin or wrist access sites, perform sterile skin prep and full-body draping, align patient under the C-arm.

Exercise or pharmacologic stress test prep: vigorous skin prep (shaving, alcohol, abrasion) for motion-tolerant electrodes, place 10 electrodes plus lead harness and belt/pouch, fit BP cuff, prep an IV/imaging site, instruct and steady the patient onto the treadmill or bicycle, then reposition on an imaging table between stress and rest phases.

Bedside or ambulatory hookup: portable ECG, telemetry or Holter/event-monitor application on an ICU, ER or ward patient who may be obese, confused, agitated, in pain, or encumbered by lines, drains and dressings, done in a cramped bedside space with the bed and patient body repositioned by hand.

sources.system: Lucid Robotic System (Lucid M1 TCD + NeuralBot/NovaBot headset), NovaGuide Intelligent Ultrasound
sources.date: 2026-04 (article); FDA-cleared and in hospital use since ~2019
sources.title: Robotic ultrasound for stroke — Houston Methodist
sources.claim: The Lucid/NovaGuide robotic TCD system autonomously searches for and adjusts ultrasound probes against a patient's head in hospital inpatient and outpatient settings, but clinical staff still seat/position the patient and fit the robotic headset; the robot performs no patient preparation.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous placement/adjustment of an ultrasound probe on a patient's head. It shows a robot can make controlled contact with a patient's body in a hospital, but it does not undress, transfer, physically position, shave, skin-prep, electrode or drape a patient, which is what this task requires.

sources.system: Robotic tele-echocardiography systems (review of the field)
sources.title: Current Status and Pending Developments of Robotic Tele-Echocardiography (JACC: Cardiovascular Imaging) — PubMed
sources.claim: State-of-the-art robotic echocardiography on real patients is remote teleoperation of the probe by a sonographer; autonomous robot-assisted ultrasound remains prospective, and no reviewed system prepares or positions the patient.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic cardiac ultrasound on patients, the procedure this task prepares for. It is teleoperated and confined to probe manipulation, so it cannot substantiate autonomous patient preparation or body positioning.

sources.developer: academic groups (e.g., Imperial College London, Georgia Tech/Stanford)
sources.title: Learning garment manipulation policies toward robot-assisted dressing | Science Robotics
sources.claim: Robotic dressing/undressing of a person — the closest analogue to gowning, disrobing and draping a patient — remains a laboratory research problem with mannequins and able-bodied volunteers, not a clinically deployed capability.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: manipulating garments on a human body, needed for gowning/disrobing/draping a patient. Only lab-scale demonstrations exist, so it cannot substantiate completion of clinical patient preparation.

sources.system: Robotic patient positioning systems / 6-DoF treatment couches (e.g., proton therapy positioners)
sources.developer: multiple vendors (e.g., LEONI, IBA, Mevion installations)
sources.date: 2010 (review); technology in routine clinical use since
sources.title: Patient positioning in the proton radiotherapy era | Journal of Experimental & Clinical Cancer Research
sources.claim: Computer-controlled robotic treatment couches move an already set-up patient to sub-millimetre positions in radiotherapy vaults, but therapists first transfer, undress, align and immobilize the patient on the couch.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: positioning a patient for a diagnostic/therapeutic procedure. Transfer is limited: the couch translates a tabletop with a human already placed and immobilized on it; it does not move body segments (e.g., into left lateral decubitus), prep skin, or apply electrodes, so it does not carry the whole instance.

tasks.label: Attach electrodes to the patients' chests, arms, and legs, connect electrodes to leads from the electrocardiogram (EKG) machine, and operate the EKG machine to obtain a reading.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Routine resting 12-lead ECG on an ambulatory adult outpatient in a clinic/hospital ECG room: patient gowned and supine on an exam table; tech wipes/preps skin, peels and applies 10 disposable adhesive electrodes at limb sites and palpated precordial landmarks (V1 4th ICS right sternal border through V6 mid-axillary), snaps/clips the lead wires, runs the machine, checks the tracing for artifact or lead reversal, repeats if needed, then removes electrodes.

Bedside 12-lead ECG on an inpatient in a ward or ICU room: patient in bed, often with IV lines, telemetry pads, dressings, oxygen tubing, gown and bedding to move; access to the chest is partly obstructed, patient may be frail, obese, confused or unable to lie flat; portable cart brought to the bedside and reading obtained without disturbing lines.

STAT/urgent ECG in an emergency department or during a rapid response: time-critical (minutes), patient diaphoretic, in pain, restless or vomiting, chest hair or moisture interfering with adhesion, staff crowded around; tech must place electrodes fast, get an artifact-free tracing, and often repeat serial ECGs.

Electrode hook-up for exercise stress testing, telemetry or a Holter/event monitor: skin prep by shaving, abrading and alcohol wiping, Mason-Likar torso placement, electrodes taped/strapped so they survive walking or running, lead wires bundled into a harness, signal quality verified on the machine at rest and during motion.

Special-population ECGs in a facility: pediatric or infant patients (small chest, right-sided leads, uncooperative child), bariatric patients, women requiring breast displacement for correct precordial placement, or patients with amputations, dressings, tremor or skin conditions that force modified electrode sites and coaching of the patient.

sources.system: Unitree G1 bimanual teleoperation system for medical procedures
sources.developer: UC San Diego (Yip lab) with UC San Diego Health
sources.title: Humanoids in Hospitals: A Technical Study of Humanoid Robot Surrogates for Dexterous Medical Interventions
sources.claim: The closest demonstrated humanoid work on bedside clinical procedures (auscultation, palpation, ventilation, intubation, ultrasound-guided injection) on a Unitree G1 is performed entirely by human teleoperation, not autonomously, and the authors report force and sensitivity limitations.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: hands-on bedside patient procedures with medical tools on a torso. It is the nearest analogue to placing ECG electrodes on a patient, but it is teleoperated throughout, so it cannot substantiate autonomous completion of the ECG hook-up.

sources.system: Automated robotic platform for remote auscultation
sources.developer: AIST (National Institute of Advanced Industrial Science and Technology), Japan
sources.title: Toward Fully Automated Robotic Platform for Remote Auscultation
sources.claim: A research platform autonomously positions an electronic stethoscope on the chest at cardiac auscultation landmarks using LiDAR-based body-surface registration with passive force limiting; results are preliminary landing-position estimation, not a complete clinical examination.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomously bringing a rigid sensor to anatomically defined chest positions. It shows landmark estimation and safe contact, but involves no handling of peel-and-stick adhesive electrodes, no limb sites, no lead-wire connection, and no acquisition of a diagnostic-quality 12-lead record.

sources.title: Vitestro gains CE mark for autonomous blood drawing robot
sources.claim: An autonomous robotic phlebotomy device (Aletta) that inserts a needle into a seated patient's arm is CE marked and in clinical use in European blood-collection settings, having met a 95% first-stick endpoint in trials.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: an autonomous body-contact diagnostic procedure in a structured clinical facility. Transfer to ECG hook-up is limited: the patient's arm is fixtured in the device and one rigid needle is inserted, whereas the ECG task requires exposing the chest, manipulating ten deformable adhesive electrodes onto palpated torso and limb landmarks and clipping lead wires.

sources.developer: First Affiliated Hospital of Sun Yat-Sen University
sources.title: Autonomous robotic ultrasound scanning system: a key to enhancing image analysis reproducibility and observer consistency in ultrasound imaging
sources.claim: An autonomous robotic ultrasound scanning ... using a 7-DoF arm with force control and visual servoing achieves reproducible probe contact and image acquisition, evaluated mainly on phantoms with some human-subject measurements.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous force-controlled contact with a human body surface to acquire a diagnostic signal. It does not cover adhesive-electrode manipulation, multi-site placement on limbs and chest, or lead-wire connection, so it does not substantiate the ECG hook-up task.

tasks.label: Adjust equipment and controls according to physicians' orders or established protocol.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Echocardiography exam in a hospital echo lab or at the bedside: the tech selects the transducer and preset per the ordered study, then continuously adjusts probe placement/pressure and machine controls (depth, gain/TGC, focus, sector width, color scale, spectral Doppler baseline, sweep speed) to obtain the protocol's standard views and Doppler measurements, plus any extra views the reading cardiologist orders.

Vascular/neurovascular ultrasound study in a hospital vascular lab or outpatient clinic (carotid duplex, venous duplex, transcranial Doppler, ABI): the tech positions and angles the probe and adjusts Doppler controls — insonation depth, sample volume, angle correction, PRF/scale, wall filter, gain — to acquire and optimize the flow signals required by the accreditation protocol.

Cardiac catheterization / interventional lab: throughout a case the tech adjusts the imaging chain and monitoring gear on the physician's verbal orders — C-arm angulation and table position, collimation/shutters, frame rate and exposure settings, zeroing and leveling pressure transducers, setting contrast injector volume/rate, configuring IVUS/FFR and hemodynamic recording consoles.

Resting ECG, Holter/event/telemetry setup in a clinic, inpatient unit or ECG department: configuring the ECG cart (lead configuration, 10 mm/mV gain, 25 mm/s speed, filter settings, patient demographics), programming ambulatory monitors for the ordered recording duration and triggers, and setting telemetry alarm limits per unit protocol.

Exercise stress test in a cardiology stress lab: loading and running the ordered treadmill protocol (Bruce/modified Bruce), advancing or modifying stages, setting the automated BP cuff interval, adjusting ECG display/filters and printing intervals, and changing or terminating the protocol when the supervising physician orders it or endpoints are reached.

EP lab or device clinic: adjusting the programmed stimulator output/drive train, ablation generator power and temperature limits, mapping-system settings, or pacemaker/ICD programmer parameters step by step as the electrophysiologist calls for them.

sources.title: Houston Methodist is first in U.S. to use Lucid Robotic System to monitor brain blood flow noninvasively
sources.claim: The Lucid Robotic System (Lucid ... with NeuralBot) is an FDA-cleared robotic transcranial Doppler platform deployed in US hospitals that autonomously positions the ultrasound probes and continuously adjusts the insonation/detection settings to find and maintain cerebral blood-flow signals.
sources.transferJustification: Transcranial Doppler is a vascular study performed by cardiovascular/vascular technologists; the robot performs exactly the adjustment work of this task — probe angulation and Doppler depth/gain optimization to protocol — in a hospital setting.

sources.title: Robotic Transcranial Doppler Improves PFO Detection After Stroke
sources.claim: In a clinical study of PFO detection after stroke, the robotic TCD probes scanned and optimized the middle cerebral artery signal autonomously while being run by staff without TCD skills.
sources.transferJustification: Same task family: the machine performs the probe/control adjustment that a vascular technologist would perform, in a hospital study setting, at diagnostic quality.

sources.title: Towards expert-level autonomous carotid ultrasonography with large-scale learning-based robotic system - PubMed
sources.claim: UltraBot is a fully autonomous, learning-based carotid ultrasound robot validated on human subjects with reported human-expert-level performance and over 90% success in clinical-oriented validation.
sources.transferJustification: Carotid duplex is core vascular-technologist work; autonomous probe positioning plus imaging-parameter optimization to a full scanning protocol is the same adjustment work this task describes.

sources.developer: academic team, Beijing Tsinghua Changgung Hospital collaboration
sources.title: Beyond hospital reach: Autonomous lightweight ultrasound robot for liver sonography
sources.claim: An autonomous lightweight ultrasound robot was deployed in a hospital ultrasound department and autonomously acquired standard aorta, IVC and portal vein planes on volunteers starting from randomized positions.
sources.transferJustification: Aorta and IVC plane acquisition is vascular ultrasound; it shows autonomous probe/imaging adjustment on real people inside a working hospital imaging department (E2 setting).

sources.system: AI robotic echocardiography agent (deep RL probe controller)
sources.title: RESEARCH: New AI-powered robotic system performs heart ultrasounds without guidance
sources.claim: A Concordia-developed reinforcement-learning agent on a robotic ultrasound platform autonomously located standard cardiac views on a cardiac phantom, outperforming remote human operators in bench testing.

sources.title: Robotic assisted echocardiography, a pilot clinical validation study
sources.claim: Robotic assisted echocardiography validated clinically on patients is operated by a sonographer with a hand-held remote controller, i.e. teleoperated rather than autonomous.

sources.title: The Biggest Challenge for CNC Machine Tending with a Robot: Solved!
sources.claim: A commercial machine-tending robot cell operates the tended machine's own control panel — a button actuator presses the Start control and sensors read the machine's status lights — so the cell runs the machine's controls without a human at the panel.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: operating a machine's physical controls to a set program. Comparable objects (panel buttons/knobs), comparable precision (cm-level presses), in a fixtured cell — the E1 analogue of setting a diagnostic console to protocol values.

sources.system: AI-supported interactive robotic arm for automated testing
sources.developer: Conrad et al., published in Advanced Intelligent Systems (Wiley)
sources.title: Lowering the Entrance Hurdle for Lab Automation: An Artificial Intelligence-Supported, Interactive Robotic Arm for Automated, Repeated Testing Procedures
sources.claim: An AI-supported robotic arm autonomously ran repeated bench testing procedures, including loading specimens into an instrument, pressing the instrument's start button, and reading the instrument display with a camera to record results.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: setting and running an instrument through its own controls per a protocol, then verifying the reading on the display — the same class of action as configuring an ECG cart or hemodynamic console, on a fixtured bench.

sources.system: ARTIS pheno robotic C-arm angiography system
sources.title: FDA Clears Robot-Supported ARTIS Pheno Angiography System From Siemens Healthineers
sources.claim: The ARTIS pheno is an FDA-cleared robotic C-arm angiography system used in hospital cath labs whose motorized arm recalls stored memory positions and follows the table, but position recall is initiated and held by the operator.

tasks.label: Check, test, and maintain cardiology equipment, making minor repairs when necessary, to ensure proper operation.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Start-of-shift readiness check of ECG carts and echocardiography systems in a hospital or clinic cardiology department: power up, confirm the machine's self-test/calibration, visually inspect transducers, lead wires, patient cables and electrode connectors for cracks or breaks, check battery charge and paper/gel/electrode stock, wipe down surfaces, and record the QC log.

Pre-procedure equipment check in an installed cath lab or EP lab suite: verify the hemodynamic recording system channels and waveform display, level and zero fluid-filled pressure transducers, check the contrast injector, defibrillator/external pacing box and IVUS/FFR consoles, confirm cable routing and connections around the table before the case.

Troubleshooting and minor repair between or during studies: tracing baseline noise or a flat lead to a damaged lead wire, snap or connector, swapping the cable or lead set, replacing a fuse or battery, clearing a printer/paper jam, reseating a loose connector or module, then re-running the device to confirm the fix and escalating anything beyond a minor repair to clinical engineering.

Scheduled QC and preventive maintenance: treadmill/ergometer speed-and-grade calibration for stress testing, ultrasound phantom or test-pattern image QC on echo systems, NIBP/sphygmomanometer calibration checks, high-level cleaning/disinfection of transducers, checks of Holter/telemetry download stations, and completion of maintenance documentation.

Portable and wearable device turnaround in an equipment workroom: Holter monitors, event recorders and telemetry transmitters returned from patients are inspected for damage, cleaned, batteries replaced, docked for data download, function-verified on a test station, and restocked into patient kits.

sources.title: Moxi — Diligent Robotics
sources.claim: The largest deployed fleet of hospital mobile-manipulation robots performs fetch-and-deliver logistics (supplies, lab samples, medications) in hospital corridors; no equipment checking, testing, calibration or repair function is part of the deployed capability.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous hospital logistics. Cited to bound what deployed hospital robots do in the same E2 setting - transport, not inspection, functional testing or repair of clinical devices - supporting negative judgments at E2.

sources.title: MATT the Smart Device Test Automation Robot | Adapta Robotics
sources.claim: A commercial test-automation robot physically operates handheld electronic devices (touch, buttons, UI) at a fixed test station and runs diagnostic verification of returned devices on refurbishment lines, producing automated pass/fail results.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated functional check-out of returned handheld electronics in refurbishment. Objects (battery-powered handheld monitors with screens, buttons and ports), precision and the fixtured bench setting are comparable to bench-testing a returned Holter/telemetry recorder.

sources.title: Airobotics battery-swapping platform keeps drones flying around the clock
sources.claim: A deployed robotic docking station autonomously removes and replaces the battery module of a returned device in a purpose-built cell, without human handling.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic battery exchange on a returned field device docked in a fixture. Same object class (battery pack in a compartment), similar insertion precision, and a purpose-built station - the E1 analogue of replacing batteries in returned ambulatory monitors.

sources.title: trophon®3 | Nanosonics
sources.claim: Automated high-level disinfection of ultrasound transducers is performed by a commercial closed-cycle machine in clinical departments, but the probe is loaded and unloaded by a person and no inspection, functional test or repair is performed.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated reprocessing of a cardiology transducer. Cited because it covers only the disinfection sub-step of equipment upkeep and still requires a human to present and retrieve the probe, so it cannot substantiate a whole maintenance instance.

sources.system: Deep RL industrial insertion system (Google Brain / UC Berkeley)
sources.title: Deep Reinforcement Learning for Industrial Insertion Tasks with Visual Inputs and Natural Rewards
sources.claim: Research robots autonomously perform electric connector plug insertion in fixtured benchtop cells, showing that mating cables/connectors is achievable under purpose-built conditions, though only as an isolated assembly step.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous connector mating in a fixtured cell, the closest analogue to swapping an ECG lead set or reseating a patient cable; it substantiates only the insertion sub-step, not fault diagnosis or verification of a clinical device.

tasks.label: Supervise or train other cardiology technologists or students.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Clinical supervision of a student sonographer or trainee technologist during live echocardiogram/vascular studies in a hospital imaging lab: watching the trainee scan, coaching probe handling and protocol order verbally, judging whether images meet diagnostic standards, and intervening with instruction when the trainee struggles.

Orienting and training a newly hired technologist in a cath lab or EP lab: walking them through department protocols, equipment operation (hemodynamic monitoring, IABP, defibrillator), sterile-field roles, documentation, and signing off when they can work independently.

Retrospective review and feedback: reviewing a trainee's completed studies, ECG strips, or worksheets on a workstation, marking deficiencies, completing competency checklists and evaluation forms, and discussing corrections with the trainee.

Didactic and in-service teaching: giving lectures, case reviews, or vendor in-services to students and staff, and demonstrating techniques on simulators, phantoms, or volunteer models in a classroom or lab.

Day-to-day supervision of a small tech team in an outpatient cardiology clinic or mobile/stress-testing service: assigning cases, monitoring workload and turnaround, answering procedural questions, troubleshooting problems, and enforcing safety and QA policy.

tasks.label: Compare measurements of heart wall thickness and chamber sizes to standard norms to identify abnormalities.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

tasks.label: Maintain a proper sterile field during surgical procedures.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Scrubbed role in a hospital cardiac cath lab during a diagnostic cath or PCI: performs surgical hand antisepsis, gowns and gloves, preps radial/femoral site with chlorhexidine, drapes the patient and the C-arm/table, sets up and organizes the sterile back table (catheters, wires, manifold, contrast, sheaths), passes devices to the interventionalist, keeps the field dry and uncontaminated, and recognizes and corrects breaks in technique (dropped wire, drape lifted, non-sterile personnel leaning in) for a 30-90 minute case.

Non-scrubbed circulating/monitoring role during a cath or EP case: opens sterile packages and delivers contrast, balloons, stents and saline onto the sterile field using aseptic technique without touching it, positions equipment and lead shields around the drapes, watches the whole room for sterility breaches and calls them out, controls door traffic, and replaces contaminated items mid-case.

Scrubbed assist in an EP lab for an ablation or a pacemaker/ICD implant: wide chest/groin prep and full-body draping, sterile pocket incision field maintained for 1-3 hours, handling of sterile leads, generators, sheaths and cautery, covering imaging equipment (ICE catheters, mapping cables) with sterile covers, and maintaining sterility while equipment is repositioned.

Hybrid OR structural-heart case (TAVR, MitraClip, EVAR): full surgical prep neck-to-knees, multi-layer draping with a large team, sterile probe/camera covers, two or more sterile tables, frequent handoffs and equipment moves, and strict OR-level sterile discipline over a long case.

Bedside or ancillary procedure outside the lab: temporary transvenous pacer, IABP, pericardiocentesis or arterial line assist in an ICU/ED room, or a vascular access procedure — establishing a small sterile field on a portable table in a cramped room with monitors, family, and unpredictable patient movement.

sources.system: Robotic Scrub Nurse (RSN), TUM Klinikum rechts der Isar / MITI research group
sources.title: Robotic scrub nurse to anticipate surgical instruments based on real-time laparoscopic video analysis | Communications Medicine
sources.claim: A robotic scrub nurse that autonomously anticipates and hands laparoscopic instruments was demonstrated only in a simulated surgery in a university hospital OR; it performs instrument handover, not patient prepping, draping, or maintenance of the sterile field itself, and it must be positioned in a field that humans create and keep sterile.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: intraoperative instrument handover. It does not transfer to maintaining a sterile field: the demonstration covers only passing tools within a field already prepped, draped and policed by humans, and was done in simulation rather than on patients.

sources.title: For the First Time, Newly Developed Robot Assists Doctors and Nurses in Operating Room | NYP
sources.claim: The Penelope Surgical Instrument Server handed and retrieved instruments in a real operation at NewYork-Presbyterian in 2005 under voice/gesture command; it never prepped or draped a patient, never enforced sterile technique, and the product did not reach sustained clinical use.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: instrument passing in an OR. It does not transfer: sterile-field creation (skin antisepsis, draping, back-table setup) and continuous contamination monitoring were performed by the human team, and the robot itself was draped and staged by humans.

sources.system: Humanoid OR assistants (staged-integration framework; no deployed system)
sources.developer: npj Digital Medicine authors (Kernbach et al.)
sources.title: Humanoid robots could take on low-risk operating room tasks before assisting surgical teams
sources.claim: As of mid-2026, humanoid robots supporting sterile conditions and preparing operating rooms are proposed as a staged future pathway requiring pre-clinical validation, not an existing deployed capability.
sources.transferJustification: Cited only as context showing intent rather than demonstrated capability; it is not used to support any positive judgment.

sources.system: Automated SPD instrument tray assembly system (Staubli TX2-60L cell)
sources.title: Towards Autonomous Instrument Tray Assembly for Sterile Processing Applications (arXiv:2602.01679)
sources.claim: The closest demonstrated robotic capability in the sterile chain is benchtop sorting and packing of instruments into trays in a sterile processing department cell, using a fixed Staubli arm and a calibrated overhead camera — away from any patient and any live procedure.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: assembling sterile instrument trays. It does not transfer to this task: the work occurs in a fixtured back-of-house cell with no patient, no draping, no aseptic delivery to a live field, and no monitoring or correction of sterility breaches during a procedure.

tasks.label: Observe ultrasound display screen and listen to signals to record vascular information, such as blood pressure, limb volume changes, oxygen saturation, or cerebral circulation.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Lower-extremity arterial physiologic study in a hospital or office vascular lab: technologist wraps brachial, thigh, calf, ankle (and toe/PPG) cuffs on a supine patient, applies gel, holds a continuous-wave Doppler probe over brachial/dorsalis pedis/posterior tibial arteries, listens for return of flow during cuff deflation, and records segmental pressures, ABI/TBI and pulse-volume-recording waveforms at each level.

Lower-extremity venous duplex to rule out DVT (or reflux study): technologist scans femoral, popliteal and calf veins with graded transducer compression, color and spectral Doppler with distal augmentation, watching the display and listening to the Doppler signal; done in the vascular lab or portable at the bedside in an ICU/ED room around lines, drains and dressings.

Extracranial cerebrovascular (carotid/vertebral) duplex in the vascular lab: bilateral B-mode plaque assessment plus color and angle-corrected spectral Doppler velocities at CCA, bulb, ICA, ECA and vertebral arteries, with waveforms recorded and stenosis-grading measurements documented.

Transcranial Doppler / cerebral circulation study: insonating the middle cerebral and other intracranial arteries through the temporal window to record blood-flow velocities (vasospasm monitoring after subarachnoid hemorrhage), emboli detection, or agitated-saline bubble study for right-to-left shunt; performed at the bedside in a neuro ICU/OR or in the outpatient lab.

Abdominal/visceral and graft surveillance duplex in the vascular lab: aortic aneurysm measurement, renal or mesenteric artery duplex on a fasting patient, or bypass-graft/stent surveillance along the limb, requiring deep-vessel insonation, angle-corrected velocities, and adaptation to body habitus and bowel gas.

Upper-extremity vein mapping / dialysis access assessment: mapping arm vein and artery diameters, depth and patency for AV fistula creation, or fistula flow-volume surveillance, performed in an in-center dialysis clinic or vascular lab with the patient's arm extended on a support.

sources.system: Lucid Robotic System / NeuralBot (later NovaGuide Intelligent Ultrasound)
sources.title: Houston Methodist is first in U.S. to use Lucid Robotic System to monitor brain blood flow noninvasively
sources.claim: The Lucid Robotic System (Lucid ... TCD + NeuralBot) is an FDA-cleared robotic transcranial Doppler platform whose robotic headset autonomously positions the probes and continuously optimizes the cerebral blood-flow signal; Houston Methodist deployed it clinically in 2019 for inpatient and outpatient brain blood-flow assessment and emboli detection.

sources.title: Safety and efficacy of a novel robotic transcranial doppler system in subarachnoid hemorrhage (Scientific Reports)
sources.claim: In a neuro ICU, the NovaGuide robotic TCD system acquired middle cerebral artery blood-flow velocities in subarachnoid hemorrhage patients (48 scans) with strong agreement with CTA for vasospasm and no adverse events around EVDs/central lines; the headset moves the transducer automatically so a trained sonographer is not required.

sources.title: Fully Automated Transcranial Doppler Ultrasound for Middle Cerebral Artery Insonation (Journal of Neurosonology and Neuroimaging)
sources.claim: A head-to-head study compared a registered vascular technologist with the fully automated robotic TCD system for bilateral MCA insonation in 86 subjects, showing the robot is a practical alternative to manual TCD for recording MCA velocities.

sources.title: Towards expert-level autonomous carotid ultrasonography with large-scale learning-based robotic system (Nature Communications)
sources.claim: UltraBot, a 7-DOF robot arm driven by an imitation-learning foundation model, autonomously performs carotid ultrasound scanning, biometric measurement and plaque screening on human volunteers with over 90% success and expert-level accuracy; demonstrations are on volunteers positioned at a bespoke robot workstation, not in routine clinical workflow.

sources.title: Vexev's VxWave System Successfully Meets Clinical Endpoints in Landmark Study Evaluating Robotic Ultrasound Scanning for Mapping Vascular Access at U.S. Renal Care Dialysis Clinics
sources.claim: The VxWave robotic tomographic ultrasound system performed upper-limb vascular mapping exams on 120 chronic kidney disease patients inside U.S. Renal Care dialysis clinics, with the probe driven by the robot rather than a human hand, producing a 3D vascular model and report; 94% scanning success and 100% data adequacy for access-creation planning.
sources.transferJustification: Vein mapping is the same act of observing the ultrasound display and Doppler signal to record vascular information (vessel diameter, depth, patency, flow) on a limb; the robot both acquires and reports these measurements.

sources.title: Robotic Assisted Transcranial Doppler Monitoring in Acute Neurovascular Care: A Feasibility and Safety Study (PubMed)
sources.claim: A feasibility and safety study of robotic-assisted TCD monitoring in acute neurovascular care (ICU/emergency settings) found the robot as reliable as manual TCD for detecting blood-flow velocities, supporting wider use for cerebral hemodynamic monitoring.

tasks.label: Assist physicians in the diagnosis and treatment of cardiac or peripheral vascular treatments, such as implanting pacemakers or assisting with balloon angioplasties to treat blood vessel blockages.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Scrub-assist at the table during a coronary angioplasty/stent (PCI) in a hospital cath lab: gowned and gloved in the sterile field, preparing and flushing catheters, purging and mounting balloons/stents on wires, handing guide catheters, 0.014" guidewires, balloons and stents to the interventionalist on verbal request, managing the manifold and contrast, torquing wires, and reacting in seconds to dissection, no-reflow, or hemodynamic collapse.

Monitoring/circulating role during a PCI or diagnostic cath: running the hemodynamic recording system, operating the power contrast injector, positioning the C-arm and table controls, opening sterile supplies onto the field, drawing up and passing heparin/contrast/verapamil per physician order, documenting the procedure log, watching rhythm and pressures and calling out changes.

Assisting a permanent pacemaker or ICD implant in the EP/cath lab: sterile prep and drape of the pectoral site, handing introducers, sheaths and pacing/defibrillator leads, connecting alligator clips to the pacing system analyzer, capturing threshold, sensing and impedance measurements at physician direction, assisting device interrogation/programming and closure supplies.

Assisting a peripheral vascular intervention (iliac/SFA balloon angioplasty, atherectomy, thrombectomy) or an EP study/ablation, sometimes in a hybrid OR: larger-bore sheaths, long 0.035" wires and shaft catheters, contralateral access, connecting mapping/ablation catheters and irrigation, managing ACT checks and inflation devices.

Peri-procedural patient handling: transferring and positioning the patient on the cath table, clipping and antiseptic prep of groin/wrist, applying ECG electrodes and defib pads, draping, then after the case removing the femoral sheath and holding manual pressure 15-20 minutes or managing radial band deflation to hemostasis while monitoring the patient for vagal reaction or bleeding.

sources.title: The ROB-OSTIAL Study protocol (NCT05634538)
sources.claim: The CorPath GRX robotic PCI system is FDA-cleared and commercially installed in cath labs, but it robotizes the interventionalist's device manipulation under joystick control from a cockpit; a human bedside assistant must still load interventional equipment into the single-use cassette. It does not perform the technologist's assist role and is not autonomous.
sources.transferJustification: Closest deployed robot in the cath lab. It substitutes for the physician's wire/balloon manipulation, not for the technologist's scrub or monitoring duties, and it is continuously teleoperated, so it cannot support a positive judgment for this task.

sources.title: Safety and Feasibility of a Novel, Second-Generation Robotic-Assisted System for Percutaneous Coronary Intervention: First-in-Human Report
sources.claim: A second-generation robotic PCI system requires a person at the bedside to load the guidewire, balloon and stent into the disposable cassette; the robot only translates cockpit commands into device motion.
sources.transferJustification: Documents that the cath-lab robot preserves, rather than replaces, the bedside device-preparation and loading work that is the core of the technologist's scrub-assist instance.

sources.system: learning-based autonomous guidewire navigation systems (review of endovascular robotics)

sources.transferJustification: Establishes that autonomous handling of guidewires/catheters — the objects this task's scrub-assist instances center on — is not achieved outside phantoms/animal benches, in any environment.

sources.developer: Ng et al., Advanced Intelligent Systems
sources.title: Large Language Model-Embedded Intelligent Robotic Scrub Nurse with Multimodal Input for Enhancing Surgeon-Robot Interaction

It is described in the literature as 'partly autonomous', covers only tool handover (not catheter prep, contrast, hemodynamics or lead testing), and is a single one-off case, so it cannot substantiate whole-instance completion.

sources.title: Swisslog Healthcare Partners with Diligent Robotics to Enhance Hospital Logistics
sources.claim: Autonomous mobile manipulators are deployed in US hospitals, but their demonstrated work is last-mile logistics — delivering medications, supplies and lab samples — not sterile procedural assistance.
sources.transferJustification: Shows what autonomous hospital robots actually accomplish in an E2 facility: fetching and transporting items. This covers at most a sub-step of the circulating instance and none of the sterile, patient-contact, or physician-paced elements.

tasks.label: Assess cardiac physiology and calculate valve areas from blood flow velocity measurements.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Transthoracic echo for suspected aortic stenosis in a hospital echo lab: on the cart or offline workstation the tech measures LVOT diameter, traces pulsed-wave LVOT VTI and continuous-wave aortic jet VTI, and computes aortic valve area by the continuity equation plus dimensionless index, peak and mean gradients, entering values on the study worksheet for the reading cardiologist.

Mitral valve assessment in an outpatient cardiology clinic: mitral inflow pressure half-time-derived valve area, mean diastolic gradient, planimetered orifice where feasible, and estimated pulmonary artery systolic pressure from the tricuspid regurgitant velocity, with results reconciled against 2D findings.

Quantification of regurgitation or prosthetic valve function: PISA-derived effective regurgitant orifice area and regurgitant volume, stroke-volume-based methods, prosthetic valve effective orifice area and dimensionless velocity index compared with reference values for the implanted device.

Invasive hemodynamic assessment in the cath lab during a structural heart or valve case: the tech assists with pressure gradient recording and cardiac output (Fick or thermodilution) and derives valve area by the Gorlin formula, reporting values in real time to the operator.

Technically difficult study: poor acoustic windows, obesity, ventilated or post-op patient, atrial fibrillation requiring beat averaging, or discordant low-flow low-gradient aortic stenosis where the tech must cross-check methods, judge which measurements are reliable, and flag inconsistencies.

tasks.label: Operate diagnostic imaging equipment to produce contrast enhanced radiographs of heart and cardiovascular system.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Elective diagnostic coronary angiography in a hospital cath lab: tech positions the patient and table under the angiographic C-arm, sets FOV/collimation/frame rate, moves the gantry through the standard series of LAO/RAO cranial/caudal angulations called by the operator, coordinates hand or power-injector contrast delivery with cine acquisition, coaches breath-hold, checks each run for foreshortening/panning/exposure and repeats, then archives the study.

Imaging during PCI (balloon/stent) on a stable patient: prolonged fluoroscopy with repeated angulation changes, magnification and roadmapping, contrast injections through the guide catheter timed to device positioning, table panning to keep wire tip and lesion in field, dose management over a 60-90 minute case.

Peripheral/vascular contrast angiography (lower-extremity runoff, carotid, renal, aortogram) in the cath lab or hybrid suite: power injector programmed for volume/rate/rise, stepping/bolus-chase table travel, DSA acquisition with patient motion artifacts, oblique views to open bifurcations.

Emergency STEMI or unstable-patient angiography, often off-hours: rapid setup on a moving, uncooperative or intubated patient, abbreviated view sets, imaging around CPR/IABP/ventilator lines, immediate re-runs as the physician works to restore flow.

Imaging support for structural/EP procedures (TAVR aortic root angiograms, venograms for CRT lead placement, pericardial or ablation cases) in a cath lab or hybrid OR: contrast runs at specific gantry angles co-registered to CT overlay, fluoro for device deployment, sterile-field constraints.

Contrast-enhanced cardiac CT angiography / CT suite work: patient on the CT table with ECG gating, IV and power injector connected, bolus-tracking ROI placement, breath-hold coaching, scan range planning, review of enhancement and motion artifacts, re-scan decisions.

sources.title: Corindus Launches technIQ 1 Smart Procedural Automation Series for CorPath GRX Cath lab Robotic System
sources.claim: CorPath GRX is the leading commercial cath-lab robot; it manipulates guidewires and catheters under the interventionalist's remote control, with only pre-programmed device-movement automations (technIQ). It does not operate the X-ray imaging chain or deliver contrast autonomously.

sources.transferJustification: Related task (robotic coronary intervention) in the identical environment; shows the state of deployed cath-lab robotics is teleoperation of devices, not autonomous operation of the angiography system.
