tasks.label: Inject contrast medium into patients' blood vessels.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Diagnostic coronary angiography in a hospital cath lab: the technologist manages the contrast source and manifold/injector and delivers repeated small boluses (~5-10 mL) into coronary catheters, timed to each cine acquisition, purging air, alternating saline flushes, and watching the pressure waveform for damping.

Left ventriculography, aortography, or peripheral/renal runoff in a cath lab or hybrid suite: a large-volume, high-flow bolus (roughly 20-40 mL at 10-20 mL/s) delivered through a pigtail or angiographic catheter with a power injector programmed for volume, flow rate, rise time and pressure limit.

Cardiac CT angiography or CT venography in an imaging suite: contrast injected through a peripheral IV; the technologist confirms IV patency, connects the injector patient line, runs a programmed multiphase protocol with saline chaser and bolus tracking, and watches the arm/site for extravasation.

Contrast echocardiography for LV opacification in the echo lab: ultrasound contrast agent (Definity/Lumason) given through an existing peripheral IV as a slow hand bolus with flush or as a continuous pump infusion, titrated to the images being acquired.

Agitated-saline bubble study for PFO/shunt detection: saline plus a small air volume agitated between two syringes through a three-way stopcock and hand-injected rapidly through a peripheral IV, timed to the sonographer's imaging and the patient's Valsalva release, in the echo lab or at the bedside.

Urgent/emergent case (STEMI activation, unstable or agitated patient) in the cath lab or hybrid room: contrast injections delivered under time pressure while the team is resuscitating, with patient movement, suboptimal access, and rapidly changing operator commands.

sources.title: Performance, Safety, and Patient Experience of an Autonomous Robotic Phlebotomy Device: A Multicenter Trial | Clinical Chemistry
sources.claim: The Aletta device performs venipuncture on a patient's peripheral vein autonomously (NIR + ultrasound + Doppler vein selection, needle insertion, tube filling, bandaging) with one professional supervising up to three devices; the patient places an arm into the machine's cradle.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: cannulating a patient's peripheral vein with a needle under image guidance. This is the vessel-access act that precedes peripheral contrast injection - same vessels, same patient population, comparable millimetre precision - so it shows a machine can enter a blood vessel autonomously when the arm is presented in a purpose-built cradle. It draws blood rather than injecting, so it substantiates access, not the contrast delivery itself.

sources.title: Vitestro Publishes Landmark Peer-Reviewed Multicenter Clinical Study of Autonomous Robotic Phlebotomy in Clinical Chemistry
sources.claim: In a 1,633-patient multicenter trial in Dutch outpatient phlebotomy departments the autonomous device achieved 94.5% first-stick success when it found a suitable vein, with 0.6% mild adverse events; patients without an identifiable vein were referred to human phlebotomists.
sources.transferJustification: Same transfer as above: quantifies that autonomous machine vascular access reaches human first-stick rates, but only with the patient's arm fixtured in the device and only for blood withdrawal.

sources.title: MEDRAD MARK 7 ARTERION OPERATION MANUAL Pdf Download | ManualsLib
sources.claim: The Mark 7 Arterion angiographic injector, standard equipment in cath/angio labs, executes an operator-programmed injection (volume, flow rate, pressure limit, up to four phases) into the patient's vasculature once armed and triggered; the machine, not the hand, meters the contrast.

sources.title: Automated Contrast Injection System Insights into Flow Rate Parameters and Pressure - ACIST Medical
sources.claim: The ACIST CVi is an automated, software-controlled, motor-driven contrast injection system used for coronary and angiographic injections in cath labs, with active safety sensors (air detection, pressure) and integrated hemodynamic monitoring; injection rate is modulated in real time by the operator's handheld AngioTouch controller.

Cited to show the state of the art in robotic vascular access inside a real procedure room is still human-directed and pre-commercial, supporting the negative E2 judgments.

tasks.label: Set up 24-hour Holter and event monitors, scan and interpret tapes, and report results to physicians.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Outpatient cardiology clinic/diagnostics room: hook up a 24-hour Holter on a typical adult — locate anatomical landmarks (intercostal spaces, sternal borders), clip hair, abrade and clean skin, peel and apply 5-7 adhesive electrodes, snap and dress lead wires, secure the recorder, verify artifact-free waveforms on all channels, and instruct the patient on the diary and precautions.

Clinic application of an adhesive patch monitor / event / mobile cardiac telemetry recorder: prep and position a single-piece patch or event recorder on the left chest, activate/pair the device, confirm signal and transmission, and teach the patient to trigger events and mail the device back.

Non-standard hookup: inpatient at the bedside on a ward or telemetry unit (bed rails, IV lines, dressings, limited mobility, confused or bariatric patient), or an outpatient with a very hairy, diaphoretic, or fragile chest, or a pediatric patient — requiring repositioning, extra skin prep, re-taping, and artifact troubleshooting.

Return visit: peel electrodes and adhesive off the patient's skin without injury, clean residue, inspect skin, collect the diary, retrieve the recorder and download/upload the recording, and clean/reset the device for reuse.

Scanning station at a clinic or independent diagnostic testing facility: dock the returned recorder or load its media, run the Holter analysis software over the full disclosure, edit beat classifications, exclude artifact, tabulate arrhythmia burden and correlate with the diary, generate the preliminary report, and route/flag results to the physician.

sources.title: Aletta for Hospital Leadership - Vitestro
sources.claim: Aletta is a commercially launched (CE-marked) autonomous robotic phlebotomy device that performs every step of a blood draw on adult patients in hospital and laboratory phlebotomy rooms, including placing the bandage — the closest deployed example of a robot autonomously performing a skin-contact procedure on a patient.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous venipuncture with adhesive bandage placement on a patient. It shows a robot can locate subcutaneous anatomy and contact skin safely in a clinic, but the arm is presented in a fixed rest and only one adhesive is placed at the puncture site; it does not show hair clipping, skin abrasion, or placement of 5-7 electrodes at palpated torso landmarks with waveform verification.

sources.title: Performance, Safety, and Patient Experience of an Autonomous Robotic Phlebotomy Device: A Multicenter Trial
sources.claim: A multicenter trial of the autonomous robotic phlebotomy device was run in outpatient phlebotomy departments of three Dutch hospitals, with the device replacing manual phlebotomy in routine use.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: patient-contact diagnostic sample collection in a structured clinical facility (E2). Establishes the frontier of autonomous robot-on-patient procedures; the procedure is single-site needle insertion on a fixtured forearm, not multi-electrode chest hookup.

sources.claim: An autonomous lightweight ultrasound robot was deployed in a hospital ultrasound department and autonomously scanned human subjects, showing robots can make controlled probe contact with a patient's torso under closed-loop control.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous localization of anatomy on a human torso and force-controlled skin contact in a hospital department. It shows torso-contact autonomy but involves a single rigid probe held by the robot, not peeling and adhering electrodes, skin preparation, or lead-wire connection.

sources.claim: An AI/force-control framework enabled a robot to autonomously mate multiple cable connector types in real-world automotive assembly, demonstrating autonomous docking/insertion of small electrical connectors in a purpose-built cell.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous insertion of small electrical connectors under force control in a fixtured industrial cell. This is the physical act required at a scanning station — docking a returned recorder or inserting its media into a reader — with comparable object size and precision when the device is presented fixtured.

aliases: Travel OB Ultrasound Tech (Travel Obstetrics Ultrasound Technician)
roles.description: Produce ultrasonic recordings of internal organs for use by physicians. Includes vascular technologists.

tasks.label: Observe screen during scan to ensure that image produced is satisfactory for diagnostic purposes, making adjustments to equipment as required.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Obstetric or gynecologic study in an OB clinic or hospital imaging room: transabdominal fetal biometry/anatomy survey (and often transvaginal pelvic imaging), continuously watching the screen through fetal motion and maternal breathing, changing depth, focus, harmonics, gain and probe window, and swapping to the endocavitary probe, until every required view is diagnostic.

Complete abdominal or renal survey on an outpatient in a hospital/imaging-center ultrasound room: liver, gallbladder/CBD, pancreas, spleen, kidneys, aorta; the sonographer re-optimizes gain/TGC/depth/frequency per organ, coaches breath-holds, changes acoustic windows (intercostal, subcostal) and repositions the patient (decubitus, erect) whenever bowel gas, rib shadow or body habitus degrades the image.

Complete vascular duplex study in an accredited vascular lab: carotid/vertebral, lower-extremity venous with compression, or arterial. Requires continual B-mode optimization plus color/spectral Doppler set-up — angle correction, sample-volume placement, PRF/scale, wall filter, baseline — to produce clean, measurable waveforms at each level.

Focused superficial/small-parts study on a cooperative outpatient in a clinic exam room: thyroid nodule survey, small-joint/soft-tissue imaging, or supplemental whole-breast screening. Single well-defined target near the skin surface, standard protocol, image quality maintained mainly by probe contact/angle and routine gain-depth optimization.

Focused single-target deep study or monitoring exam in a hospital unit or outpatient room: limited RUQ/liver standard planes, AAA screening, IVC/aorta assessment, or transcranial Doppler monitoring/bubble study — the operator hunts for the acoustic window and keeps the target structure and signal optimally displayed for the duration of the study.

Imaging outside the ultrasound suite: portable bedside exam in ICU/ED/OR on an immobile or critically ill patient (lines, dressings, restricted positioning, poor windows, ambient light), or holding and continuously re-optimizing the image during an ultrasound-guided procedure (biopsy, paracentesis, vascular access) while the needle and target move.

TCD + NeuralBot) is an FDA-cleared, fully autonomous robotic ... platform in clinical use at US hospitals; the robotic headset places and continuously self-adjusts the probes to keep a usable cerebral blood-flow signal — i.e., it performs the monitor-and-adjust loop itself.

sources.claim: ARTHUR, a commercial ultrasound robot built on the KUKA LBR Med cobot, autonomously scans patients' hands for rheumatoid arthritis assessment and is already in use in hospitals, having been trialled with patients at Svendborg Hospital.

tasks.label: Decide which images to include, looking for differences between healthy and pathological areas.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: General abdominal study: while scanning liver, gallbladder, pancreas, kidneys and spleen, the sonographer judges which frozen frames and cine clips to store — the standard protocol views plus extra documentation of a suspicious hepatic lesion, gallstone, or hydronephrosis, distinguishing it from normal parenchyma and from artifact.

Obstetric/gynecologic study: deciding which fetal anatomy survey images, biometry frames, and adnexal/endometrial views to include, adding targeted images when an anomaly, placental abnormality, or ovarian mass is seen, and excluding poorly insonated or duplicate frames.

Vascular duplex study (carotid, lower-extremity venous or arterial, dialysis access): choosing which grayscale, color, and spectral Doppler images and waveforms to record to document plaque, stenosis severity, thrombus extent, or reflux, against normal segments of the same vessel.

Echocardiographic study: selecting which 2D cine loops, M-mode, color and spectral Doppler images to store to document valvular disease, chamber enlargement, wall motion abnormality or effusion, judging image quality and diagnostic adequacy for the reading cardiologist.

Small-parts study (breast, thyroid, scrotal, superficial musculoskeletal): deciding which images of a nodule, cyst, or tear to include, typically two orthogonal planes with and without measurement calipers, plus comparison images of adjacent normal tissue.

Portable/bedside or emergency exam under time pressure with a limited-cooperation patient: choosing a minimal but diagnostically adequate image set that documents the acute finding (free fluid, DVT, effusion) and its absence elsewhere, often with degraded image quality.

tasks.label: Operate ultrasound equipment to produce and record images of the motion, shape, and composition of blood, organs, tissues, or bodily masses, such as fluid accumulations.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Complete diagnostic abdominal / general imaging exam in a hospital or outpatient imaging department: patient supine on an exam table, sonographer applies gel and sweeps a curvilinear probe to document liver, gallbladder and ducts, pancreas, spleen, both kidneys, aorta/IVC in multiple planes, coaching breath-holds, repositioning the patient (decubitus, erect) to clear bowel gas, taking measurements and recording a protocol image set.

Obstetric or gynecologic exam in an OB clinic or imaging department: transabdominal fetal survey with biometry (BPD, HC, AC, FL), placenta, amniotic fluid, fetal heart motion and Doppler, or a pelvic/transvaginal study with endocavitary probe insertion, ovary and endometrial documentation; requires chasing a moving fetus and adapting to maternal habitus.

Duplex exam requiring bilateral, segment-by-segment spectral Doppler documentation: carotid duplex for stenosis (CCA/ICA/ECA/vertebral velocities both sides), lower-extremity venous compression study for DVT along the whole leg, or peripheral arterial/graft surveillance, performed in a hospital vascular lab.

Cerebrovascular/vascular screening study of narrow protocol: carotid plaque and intima-media-thickness screening scan in a clinic ultrasound room, or transcranial Doppler insonation/monitoring of the middle cerebral artery at the neuro-ICU bedside for vasospasm or emboli.

Portable bedside exam performed with a wheeled machine in an ICU room, ED bay, OR or inpatient ward: limited abdominal/renal, bladder, venous DVT or procedural-marking study on a patient who cannot be moved, working around bed rails, lines, dressings and awkward patient positions.

Small-parts / superficial exam in a clinic or imaging suite: thyroid survey with nodule measurement and characterization, hand and wrist joint ultrasound for synovitis, or breast ultrasound, using a linear high-frequency probe with the region of interest exposed and the patient stationary.

sources.system: UltraBot (Franka Emika Panda arm + learning-based scanning models)
sources.title: Towards expert-level autonomous carotid ultrasonography with large-scale learning-based robotic system - Nature Communications
sources.claim: UltraBot, a 7-DOF robot arm holding an ultrasound transducer driven by imitation-learned networks, autonomously performs a guideline-based carotid scanning protocol (locating the bifurcation, transverse and longitudinal common-carotid sweeps) plus automatic intima biometrics and plaque segmentation, with >90% success across a diverse subject population including subjects with plaque.

sources.system: NovaGuide Intelligent Ultrasound / Lucid Robotic System (NeuralBot headset)
sources.title: Safety and efficacy of a novel robotic transcranial doppler system in subarachnoid hemorrhage - Scientific Reports
sources.claim: The NovaGuide robotic transcranial Doppler system uses a headset whose robotic probes automatically move to find and hold cerebral artery signals; it was evaluated on 48 scans of subarachnoid-hemorrhage patients in a neuro ICU and is intended to work without a trained sonographer.

sources.system: Lucid Robotic System (Lucid M1 TCD + NeuralBot)
sources.developer: NovaSignal / NeuraSignal, deployed at Houston Methodist
sources.title: Robotic Ultrasound for Stroke - Houston Methodist On Medicine
sources.claim: The FDA-cleared Lucid Robotic System (Lucid M1 TCD plus NeuralBot robotic headset) is in clinical use at a US hospital to collect cerebral blood flow data, reducing the need for skilled personnel to apply and manipulate the probe.

sources.system: ARTHUR (KUKA LBR Med-based arthritis ultrasound robot)
sources.developer: ROPCA ApS / University of Southern Denmark
sources.title: Ultrasound robot ready for arthritis patients, thanks to Danish researchers - SDU
sources.claim: ARTHUR is a CE-marked, fully automated clinical ultrasound robot that scans 11 joints per hand autonomously in rheumatology clinics, handling about four patients per hour; it is sold and in routine clinical use in European hospitals.

sources.title: Automated ultrasound system ARTHUR V.2.0 with AI analysis DIANA V.2.0 matches expert rheumatologist in hand joint assessment of rheumatoid arthritis patients - PubMed
sources.claim: In a clinical study of RA patients, the automated ARTHUR V.2.0 robot successfully scanned 564 of 660 hand joints (85.5%) and, with DIANA V.2.0 AI scoring of synovial hypertrophy and Doppler, achieved repeatability comparable to expert rheumatologists.

sources.system: FARUS (fully autonomous robotic ultrasound system for thyroid scanning)
sources.title: A fully autonomous robotic ultrasound system for thyroid scanning - Nature Communications
sources.claim: FARUS, a fully autonomous robotic ultrasound ..., scans the thyroid region of human participants without human assistance in a real clinical setting, producing images close in quality to clinician-acquired scans and detecting nodules with data for ACR TI-RADS scoring.

sources.system: Autonomous lightweight cable-driven liver ultrasound robot
sources.developer: Tsinghua University / Beijing Tsinghua Changgung Hospital
sources.title: Beyond hospital reach: Autonomous lightweight ultrasound robot for liver sonography (arXiv 2510.08106)
sources.claim: A 588-gram abdomen-mounted autonomous ultrasound robot, deployed in the ultrasound department ..., autonomously acquires three standard liver-related planes (aorta, IVC, portal vein) at expert level in 11 unseen volunteers and 6 patients — a narrow subset of, not a complete, abdominal protocol.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: focused liver/vessel plane acquisition. Cited to show the boundary — it uses the same probe, patients and imaging department as a general abdominal exam, but covers only three planes, so it does not carry over to a full multi-organ abdominal protocol.

sources.title: Towards Standardized Acquisition with a Dual-probe Ultrasound Robot for Fetal Imaging - PMC
sources.claim: Fetal-imaging robots remain assistive/teleoperated: the iFIND dual-probe fetal ultrasound robot was only permitted to scan non-pregnant healthy volunteers pending clinical approval, and commercial prenatal robotic ultrasound relies on a remote human sonographer with a local assistant holding the robot on the patient.

sources.title: A Review and Perspective of Techniques for Autonomous Robotic Ultrasound Acquisitions
sources.claim: A 2026 review of autonomous robotic ultrasound acquisition finds that most systems remain semi-autonomous, requiring human collaboration and physician adjustment and control throughout the acquisition, and often human placement of the initial probe position.

sources.title: Robotic prenatal ultrasound for rural areas - AdEchoTech
sources.claim: Commercial prenatal robotic ultrasound is explicitly a telemedicine configuration: a remote specialist drives the probe while an untrained local technician holds the robot against the patient.

tasks.label: Observe and care for patients throughout examinations to ensure their safety and comfort.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Outpatient imaging center or hospital ultrasound suite, routine adult abdominal/pelvic/thyroid/soft-tissue exam: greet and identify patient, help them undress and onto the table, position and drape for modesty, apply warm gel, watch breathing/pain responses and skin color through a 30-45 minute scan, adjust pillows and bolsters, wipe gel off, assist patient off the table and out safely.

Obstetric/gynecologic exam in a women's imaging clinic: pregnant patient positioned supine or with a left lateral wedge, monitored for supine hypotension, dizziness, nausea and bladder discomfort; chaperoned transvaginal scan with draping and consent; emotional support and reassurance (or containment of distress on an adverse finding); assist patient up from the table.

Portable bedside exam on an inpatient (ICU, ED, med-surg room): frail or sedated patient with IV lines, drains, chest tubes, oxygen and telemetry; sonographer clears space around the bed, works with nursing staff to log-roll or prop the patient, protects lines and wounds, watches monitors and patient status during the scan, maintains isolation precautions, and leaves bed rails up and call bell in reach.

Patients requiring extra physical or behavioral care: bariatric patients, elderly patients with dementia, post-operative patients in pain, non-verbal or pediatric patients; requires mechanical lift or two-person transfers, fall prevention, gentle restraint or distraction, coordination with family or caregiver, and continual reassurance during positioning changes.

Vascular lab / echo exam: carotid duplex, lower-extremity venous or arterial study with cuffs, or stress echocardiography; multiple position changes (supine, prone, decubitus, sitting), Valsalva and augmentation maneuvers, cuff-pressure and probe-pressure tolerance, patient watched for symptoms such as dizziness, chest pain, or claudication throughout.

Acute event during an exam: patient becomes vasovagal or faint, hypotensive, seizes, reports chest pain, or reacts to an ultrasound contrast agent; sonographer must recognize the change, stop the scan, keep the patient from falling off the table, lower the head/raise legs, summon the radiologist or code team, and stay with the patient.

sources.title: Remote and Telerobotic Ultrasound Imaging | Methodist DeBakey Cardiovascular Journal
sources.claim: State-of-the-art clinically deployed robotic ultrasound (e.g., AdEchoTech Melody) is teleoperated and still requires a human healthcare worker physically with the patient to position the patient and the probe frame; the robot performs no patient care.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: performing the ultrasound scan itself. It bears on this task because the deployed robotic sonography systems automate only probe manipulation and explicitly retain a human at the patient's side for positioning and patient handling.

sources.system: Autonomous lightweight cable-driven liver ultrasound robot
sources.developer: Tsinghua University / Qinghai Provincial People's Hospital
sources.title: Beyond hospital reach: Autonomous lightweight ultrasound robot for liver sonography (arXiv 2510.08106)
sources.claim: The most advanced autonomous ultrasound robots automate probe placement and image acquisition on consenting volunteers/patients in research and screening deployments; the reported capability is imaging, with no autonomous patient positioning, comfort management, or monitoring of patient distress.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous sonographic scanning of a human abdomen. Shows the frontier of robot-patient physical contact in ultrasound: force-limited probe motion on a cooperative, already-positioned subject, with no evidence of patient observation, comfort care, or response to distress.

sources.developer: Foxconn with NVIDIA and Kawasaki Heavy Industries
sources.title: Nurabot to assist nurses with routine tasks | Digital Watch Observatory
sources.claim: Autonomous hospital humanoid/service robots deployed in wards perform logistics and wayfinding (medication delivery, ward patrol, guiding people), not hands-on patient care during examinations.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: mobile robot work inside hospitals. It marks the boundary of deployed hospital robot capability — navigation and transport — and shows no deployed system takes over attending to a patient's safety and comfort.

sources.system: Moxi and other robotic nurse assistants
sources.title: This Humanoid AI Robot Is Being Tested in Hospitals—Plus 7 More Transforming Healthcare | Nurse.org
sources.claim: Robotic nurse assistants used in US hospitals are limited to non-patient-facing support work such as delivering specimens and supplies and collecting linens.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: in-hospital robotic assistance to clinical staff. Directly relevant because it characterizes what autonomous hospital robots actually do, and excludes patient-contact care of the kind this task requires.

sources.title: This Humanoid AI Robot Is Being Tested in Hospitals—Plus 7 More Transforming Healthcare | Nurse.org
sources.claim: Robots designed to lift and transfer patients (e.g., RIKEN's Robear) remain operator-controlled research prototypes rather than autonomous deployed systems for patient handling.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: physically lifting and repositioning patients, which is the physical core of assisting patients on and off exam tables. Cited to show this capability exists only as an operator-guided prototype, so it cannot support a positive judgment.

sources.title: MEDi the robot brings smiles to patients | Texas Children's
sources.claim: Social robots that provide comfort/distraction to patients during procedures are deployed in children's hospitals, but they are tools wielded by child life specialists during procedures rather than autonomous caregivers responsible for patient safety.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: providing comfort to a patient during a medical procedure. Relevant to the 'comfort' half of this task, but the robot is directed by a human specialist and performs no physical care or safety monitoring.

tasks.label: Provide sonogram and oral or written summary of technical findings to physician for use in medical diagnosis.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

tasks.label: Select appropriate equipment settings and adjust patient positions to obtain the best sites and angles.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Complete/multi-organ abdominal ultrasound in an outpatient hospital imaging suite: liver, gallbladder and ducts, pancreas, spleen, kidneys, aorta/IVC. Sonographer selects preset/depth/gain/focus/harmonics, coaches breath-holds, rolls the patient to left-lateral or decubitus positions, and works subcostal and intercostal windows around ribs, bowel gas and body habitus.

Focused single-organ or single-vessel exam in a clinic or imaging room: AAA/aorta screening, limited liver survey, IVC/portal vein, or a superficial small-parts study (thyroid, scrotum). Patient supine or seated, one anatomic region, standard planes, routine gain/depth/frequency selection.

Obstetric/gynecologic exam in an OB imaging room: transabdominal fetal biometry, anatomy survey, presentation and heart activity, plus endovaginal scanning when needed. Requires maternal repositioning (tilt, bladder state), probe angling around a moving fetus, transducer changes and preset/TI-MI setting selection.

Carotid/cerebrovascular duplex in a vascular lab: patient supine with head turned and extended, neck windows worked in transverse and longitudinal, gain/PRF/wall-filter and Doppler angle set for bilateral ICA/CCA/ECA/vertebral coverage and plaque assessment.

Peripheral vascular duplex in a vascular lab: lower-extremity venous DVT study or arterial mapping. Reverse Trendelenburg or leg externally rotated/dependent, serial compression maneuvers, augmentation, angle-corrected spectral Doppler at multiple levels, repeated repositioning of both patient and probe.

Portable bedside study on an inpatient unit, ICU, ED or OR: machine wheeled to a crowded bedside, patient uncooperative, sedated or with lines, drains and dressings; sonographer physically repositions or props the patient, works limited windows around obstacles and re-optimizes settings for poor penetration.

sources.title: Towards expert-level autonomous carotid ultrasonography with large-scale learning-based robotic system - PubMed
sources.claim: UltraBot is a fully autonomous learning-based carotid ultrasound robot that autonomously positions and angles the probe to cover the carotid anatomy, validated clinically on human subjects with over 90% success and expert-level accuracy.
sources.transferJustification: Direct: autonomously choosing probe site, angle and contact to obtain diagnostic carotid views is exactly the site/angle optimization this task describes.

sources.system: Autonomous lightweight ultrasound robot for liver sonography
sources.developer: Tsinghua University / Beijing Tsinghua Changgung Hospital
sources.title: Beyond hospital reach: Autonomous lightweight ultrasound robot for liver sonography (arXiv:2510.08106)
sources.claim: An autonomous 588-gram abdomen-mounted ultrasound robot was deployed in a hospital ultrasound department and autonomously located standard abdominal planes (aorta, IVC, portal vein) on freely breathing subjects, adjusting compression, translation and yaw/pitch itself.
sources.transferJustification: Direct: the robot autonomously searches for and optimizes the imaging plane (site and angle) for named abdominal structures, the core of this task for a focused abdominal study.

sources.system: FARUS (fully autonomous robotic ultrasound system for thyroid scanning)
sources.title: (PDF) A fully autonomous robotic ultrasound system for thyroid scanning
sources.claim: FARUS, a fully autonomous robotic ultrasound ... for thyroid scanning, autonomously scanned the thyroid from upper to lower pole while keeping the gland centered, and its image-quality metrics were compared against groups of physicians.
sources.transferJustification: Direct: autonomous probe placement and angle/centering control for a superficial small-parts exam is the site/angle optimization this task covers.

sources.system: Concordia deep reinforcement learning ultrasound visual servoing robot
sources.developer: Concordia University (Zakeri et al., IEEE T-MRB)
sources.title: New AI-powered robotic system performs heart ultrasounds without guidance
sources.claim: A deep-RL cardiac ultrasound robot that autonomously moves the probe to find standard cardiac views was tested only on a cardiac ultrasound training phantom, with real-patient testing named as future work.

sources.title: Feasibility of a 5G-Based Robot-Assisted Remote Ultrasound System for Cardiopulmonary Assessment of Patients With Coronavirus Disease 2019
sources.claim: Robotic ultrasound actually used at patient bedsides (including COVID wards and care centers) is teleoperated: a remote physician drives the probe through a master console over a network link.

sources.system: Autonomous robotic POCUS lung imaging system
sources.developer: Frontiers in Robotics and AI (Tsumura et al. / academic consortium)
sources.title: Autonomous Robotic Point-of-Care Ultrasound Imaging for Monitoring of COVID-19–Induced Pulmonary Diseases
sources.claim: An autonomous robotic point-of-care lung ultrasound system for COVID monitoring was evaluated on a full-torso phantom rather than on patients at the bedside.

sources.system: Robot-assisted DVT ultrasound examination using virtual fixture
sources.developer: Technical University of Munich (Jiang, Navab et al.)
sources.title: Robot-Assisted Deep Venous Thrombosis Ultrasound Examination Using Virtual Fixture
sources.claim: A robot-assisted DVT ultrasound system generated scan trajectories automatically from an MRI atlas and acquired planned limb vascular structures on six volunteers, but the demonstrated output is a 3D vessel sweep, not a full duplex protocol with compressions and spectral Doppler.
sources.transferJustification: Related task (robotic limb-vessel screening) shows probe alignment to a vessel, but a venous duplex additionally requires compression maneuvers, augmentation and angle-corrected Doppler that are not demonstrated.

sources.system: iFIND-v2 / iFIND-v3 robotic ultrasound for fetal imaging
sources.title: Robotic-assisted Ultrasound for Fetal Imaging: Evolution (arXiv:1902.05458)
sources.claim: The iFIND fetal-imaging robots have been tested on volunteers for abdominal and fetal scanning, but the reported testing is mechatronic feasibility with operator involvement rather than autonomous acquisition of the obstetric standard planes.

tasks.label: Determine whether scope of exam should be extended, based on findings.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: General abdominal ultrasound in a hospital or outpatient imaging department: while reviewing acquired images, the sonographer notes an unexpected finding (e.g., an incidental renal or hepatic mass, free fluid, gallbladder wall thickening) and judges whether the exam should be extended beyond the ordered protocol to include additional organs or views, per department protocol and radiologist consultation.

Obstetric/gynecologic exam in a clinic or hospital: sonographer observes a suspected fetal anomaly, abnormal placental location, short cervix, or adnexal mass and decides whether to add transvaginal imaging, extended fetal anatomy views, or Doppler assessment beyond the ordered study.

Vascular study in a vascular lab or hospital: technologist finds thrombus, high-grade stenosis, or unexpected aneurysm and decides whether to extend the protocol (e.g., add the contralateral limb, extend to iliac/vertebral segments, add Doppler waveforms) and whether the finding is a critical result requiring immediate notification.

Echocardiography in a cardiology lab or inpatient unit: sonographer identifies an unexpected effusion, valve lesion, shunt, or wall-motion abnormality and decides whether to add off-axis views, saline contrast, or additional Doppler measurements beyond the ordered study.

Portable/bedside exam in the ED, ICU, or at a patient's bedside under time pressure and limited access: sonographer weighs an equivocal or urgent finding against patient tolerance, ordering context, and available time, and decides whether to extend the scope or terminate and escalate to the interpreting physician.

tasks.label: Obtain and record accurate patient history, including prior test results or information from physical examinations.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

tasks.label: Coordinate work with physicians or other healthcare team members, including providing assistance during invasive procedures.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Hospital radiology procedure room: sonographer assists a radiologist during an ultrasound-guided invasive procedure (core biopsy, thoracentesis, paracentesis, abscess drain, cyst aspiration). Localizes and marks the target, preps sterile probe cover, then holds and continuously fans/angles the transducer to keep the advancing needle tip in plane while the physician works, responds to spoken direction ('go medial', 'hold there'), watches the patient's breathing and comfort, captures pre/post documentation images, and confirms the specimen with the physician.

Real-time consultation with the interpreting physician: sonographer brings a completed or in-progress study to the radiologist's workstation, presents the images and preliminary observations, flags a critical or unexpected finding (DVT, ruptured ectopic, large AAA, testicular torsion), and then returns to the patient to acquire the additional views, Doppler, or decubitus repositioning the radiologist asks for before the study is signed off.

Portable/bedside exam in ICU, ED or NICU: sonographer coordinates with nurses, respiratory therapists and residents to get access to the patient, times the scan around other care, asks staff to help roll the patient or move lines/drains, works around ventilators and pumps, then reports urgent results directly to the ordering physician and documents the handoff.

OB/GYN and outpatient clinic: sonographer alerts the OB or maternal-fetal-medicine physician to an abnormal finding mid-exam, hands off for confirmatory scanning, and assists during procedures such as amniocentesis, CVS or follicle aspiration by holding the transducer to guide and track the needle while the physician performs the puncture, with the patient awake and moving.

Vascular lab / OR and interventional support: vein mapping or duplex results communicated directly to the surgeon, providing duplex guidance during ultrasound-guided vascular access, sclerotherapy or line placement, or performing intraoperative/completion duplex in the operating room while maintaining sterile technique and coordinating with the surgical team.

Materials leg of team coordination inside the hospital: carrying labeled biopsy/fluid specimens from the ultrasound suite to the lab or pathology, fetching procedure kits, sterile probe covers and supplies from central supply or pharmacy, and ferrying requisitions/paperwork between departments during or after a procedure.

sources.title: Diligent Robotics completes 300,000 pharmacy deliveries with Moxi - The Robot Report
sources.claim: Moxi, an autonomous mobile manipulator, is deployed in more than 30 US hospitals and has completed over a million intra-hospital deliveries, including 300,000 pharmacy deliveries and 100,000 autonomous elevator rides, i.e. it moves materials between departments in an operating hospital without an operator.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: intra-hospital material transport. It transfers to the materials leg of sonographer team coordination (specimens to the lab, kits from central supply) because the objects, distances, corridors and institutional access controls are the same.

sources.title: Moxi — Diligent Robotics
sources.claim: The developer states Moxi's deployed duties include running patient supplies, delivering lab ... and fetching items from central supply for clinical staff.
sources.transferJustification: Same transfer as above: lab-sample and supply running is exactly the materials-handling portion of coordinating with other healthcare team members around an ultrasound-guided procedure.

sources.developer: Johns Hopkins University / Siemens Healthineers collaborators
sources.title: AURA-CVC: Autonomous Ultrasound-guided Robotic Assistance for Central Venous Catheterization
sources.claim: The most advanced autonomous ultrasound-guided needle system for a real procedure (central venous catheterization) plans, scans, reconstructs vessels and inserts, but has only been demonstrated on a commercial phantom, not on patients, and it replaces the operator rather than assisting one.
sources.transferJustification: Closest available analogue to the sonographer's probe-holding assist during a needle procedure; cited to show the state of the art is phantom-only and therefore does not substantiate completion on patients at any tier.

sources.title: Robotic guidance for ultrasound-guided percutaneous procedures: a prospective multispecialty feasibility study
sources.claim: Focalist, an FDA-cleared handheld robotic ultrasound needle-guidance device, was used in patients across a range of ultrasound-guided percutaneous procedures, but the clinician holds the device and directs targeting throughout, so the human operator remains continuously in the loop.
sources.transferJustification: Directly related to the ultrasound-guided procedure assist instance; cited to show that the clinically deployed device is hand-held and physician-directed, i.e. continuous human control, so it cannot support a positive judgment.

sources.system: Fully autonomous robotic ultrasound system (Su et al.)
sources.developer: Chinese Academy of Sciences / collaborating hospitals
sources.title: A fully autonomous robotic ultrasound system for thyroid scanning | Nature Communications
sources.claim: A research robotic ultrasound system can autonomously scan the thyroid region of human subjects and flag nodules, showing autonomous probe placement on people is possible in a controlled research setting, but only for a fixed screening protocol with no team interaction.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous ultrasound image acquisition on human subjects. Cited to bound the state of the art: acquisition of a fixed protocol is automatable, but responding to a physician's ad-hoc requests and consulting on findings is not demonstrated.

tasks.label: Prepare patient for exam by explaining procedure, transferring patient to ultrasound table, scrubbing skin and applying gel, and positioning patient properly.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Outpatient imaging center or clinic ultrasound room: ambulatory adult arrives for abdominal, OB, pelvic or small-parts exam. Sonographer verifies identity, explains the exam and answers questions, has the patient change and get onto the table (adjusting table height, light hand assist), drapes with sheets/towels, exposes the scan area, applies warmed gel, and positions the patient supine and then repositions (left/right decubitus, arm overhead, breath-hold coaching) as the exam requires.

Vascular lab / vascular suite: carotid, venous or arterial duplex on an often elderly patient. Sonographer explains the study, helps the patient up onto the exam table, positions supine with head turned and chin extended, pillow under knees, legs externally rotated or bed in reverse Trendelenburg, exposes and cleans the skin (wiping lotion, residue, working around dressings), and applies gel to multiple sites during set-up.

Portable/bedside exam on a hospital inpatient (med-surg floor, ICU, ED bay): sonographer moves furniture and equipment to get the machine bedside, explains the procedure to a patient who may be sedated, intubated or confused (or to family), lowers rails, untucks linens, rolls or props the patient with pillows while protecting IV lines, drains, leads and dressings, exposes and wipes the skin, applies gel and cleans it off afterward.

Non-ambulatory or mobility-impaired patient brought to the ultrasound room by wheelchair or stretcher: sonographer explains the transfer, secures lines and oxygen, performs a safe transfer to the ultrasound table using a slide board, sit-to-stand aid, ceiling lift or two-person assist, then positions a frail, obese or painful patient with wedges and pillows, drapes and applies gel.

Pediatric, neonatal or highly anxious patient: sonographer explains the exam in age-appropriate terms, calms the child, enlists a parent to hold or distract, positions a small squirming child or scans a neonate through incubator ports, uses warmed gel and minimal exposure, repositioning repeatedly as the child moves.

Mobile ultrasound service visiting a nursing home, assisted-living room or private residence: sonographer works in a room taken as found, clears furniture, explains the exam to the resident, positions the patient on a bed or recliner with pillows and rolled towels rather than an exam table, exposes and wipes skin, applies gel and cleans up.

sources.system: FARUS (fully autonomous robotic ultrasound system for thyroid scanning)
sources.developer: Tsinghua University and collaborating hospitals (published in Nature Communications)
sources.title: A fully autonomous robotic ultrasound system for thyroid scanning | Nature Communications
sources.claim: State-of-the-art fully autonomous robotic ultrasound (FARUS) automates probe placement and thyroid scanning on human participants, but the surrounding patient preparation - applying gel to the neck skin and getting the participant into the required supine, head-turned position - is performed by humans.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic ultrasound scanning of the very patients this prep task serves. It shows the most advanced clinical robotic sonography still depends on a human to gel the skin and position the patient, i.e. the prep task itself remains unautomated.

sources.system: Autonomous lightweight ultrasound robot for liver sonography
sources.developer: Tsinghua University / Beijing Tsinghua Changgung Hospital
sources.title: Beyond hospital reach: Autonomous lightweight ultrasound robot for liver sonography (arXiv:2510.08106)
sources.claim: An autonomous lightweight ultrasound robot was deployed in a hospital ultrasound department and autonomously acquired standard liver planes on patients; its autonomy covers probe manipulation and image interpretation only, with patients prepared and positioned by clinical staff.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous sonographic scanning in a real hospital ultrasound department. It establishes the frontier of robotic sonography (probe handling) while showing no robotic coverage of patient transfer, skin prep or body positioning.

sources.developer: Purdue University / IIT Delhi / AIIMS (Raina et al.)
sources.title: UltraGelBot: Autonomous Gel Dispenser for Robotic Ultrasound (arXiv:2406.19678)
sources.claim: Automatic ultrasound gel application by a robot arm exists only as a research end-of-arm tool evaluated on phantoms, not on human patients.
sources.transferJustification: Directly addresses the gel-application sub-step of this task; evaluated only on a phantom in a lab, so it cannot substantiate gel application on a real patient, let alone the whole prep instance.

sources.developer: RIKEN and Sumitomo Riko Company Limited
sources.title: The strong robot with the gentle touch | RIKEN
sources.claim: Robots that physically lift and transfer a patient between bed, wheelchair and other surfaces exist only as experimental, caregiver-guided prototypes, not autonomous deployed systems.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: patient transfer between surfaces, the transfer element of this task. It is an experimental prototype guided by a caregiver's touch, so it cannot support a positive judgment for autonomous transfer of a patient onto an ultrasound table.

sources.title: Photos: US firm claims 'world's first' autonomous in-hospital patient transport robot
sources.claim: The autonomous patient-handling robots actually entering hospitals move stretchers along corridors; they attach to a stretcher and transport it, and do not transfer patients between surfaces, drape, clean or position them.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: moving patients within a hospital. It bounds current deployed capability - autonomous stretcher transport in corridors - and shows no deployed system performs bed-to-table transfer or patient positioning.

sources.title: Diligent Robotics Unveils Moxi 2.0, Advancing The Largest Fleet of Deployed AI-Powered Mobile Manipulation Robots
sources.claim: The largest deployed fleet of hospital mobile manipulators performs supply, medication and lab-sample delivery alongside staff, with no patient-contact tasks such as transferring or positioning patients.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous mobile manipulation inside hospitals. It marks the boundary of deployed hospital robot capability (logistics, no patient handling), supporting the negative judgment for patient prep.

sources.title: Robots closer to performing bed baths (w/ Video)
sources.claim: Robot-performed cleaning/wiping of a human's skin has been demonstrated only in laboratory research, using a compliant arm with a specialized bath-mitt end effector on a volunteer's limb.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous robot contact and wiping of human skin, the closest analogue to the skin-cleaning element of this task. It remains a 2010 lab demonstration on a limb and does not cover draping, gel, transfer or positioning at clinical quality.

tasks.label: Maintain records that include patient information, sonographs and interpretations, files of correspondence, publications and regulations, or quality assurance records, such as pathology, biopsy, or post-operative reports.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

tasks.label: Record and store suitable images, using camera unit connected to the ultrasound equipment.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Hospital or outpatient imaging suite, complete abdominal / renal / scrotal / MSK study: while scanning a supine patient on a stretcher, the sonographer freezes, scrolls cine, selects and captures 30-60 representative images and clips of liver, gallbladder (including decubitus views), CBD, pancreas, spleen, kidneys, aorta, annotates and measures each, and archives the set to PACS in time for same-day read.

OB/GYN department or clinic: obstetric biometry and fetal anatomic survey, or transvaginal pelvic study; the sonographer must capture the protocol-mandated views (BPD, HC, AC, FL, cardiac outflow tracts, endometrium, ovaries, Doppler), each frozen at the correct plane and moment, labeled and measured, then stored to PACS.

Vascular lab: carotid, lower-extremity venous (DVT/reflux) or arterial duplex; the technologist documents B-mode, color and spectral Doppler waveforms with angle-corrected velocities at many named sites bilaterally, capturing and storing an image or clip at each site plus a worksheet-linked image set.

Portable bedside exam in an ICU, ED, OR or inpatient room: cramped space, lines, dressings and a patient who cannot be repositioned; the sonographer captures the required images and clips on a portable cart or handheld system and transmits/stores them to PACS wirelessly.

Outpatient imaging center: thyroid/neck small-parts exam (transverse and longitudinal images of both lobes, isthmus, nodule documentation with measurements) and automated whole-breast supplemental screening, with the resulting image set archived to the reading workstation/PACS.

Mobile sonography: portable unit taken to a private home, nursing facility or mobile van; variable lighting, furniture and patient positioning; sonographer captures the study's images and stores/uploads them for later interpretation.

sources.system: FARUS (fully autonomous robotic ultrasound system for thyroid scanning)
sources.developer: Peter Xiaoping Liu et al. (Carleton University / collaborating Chinese hospital group)
sources.title: A fully autonomous robotic ultrasound system for thyroid scanning | Nature Communications
sources.claim: FARUS, a fully autonomous robotic ultrasound ..., locates and scans the thyroid without human assistance, producing images the authors report as high-quality relative to sonographer-acquired images, and was evaluated on human participants including patients in a real clinical setting.
sources.transferJustification: Related task is autonomous acquisition of a thyroid ultrasound image set; recording and storing suitable images is intrinsic to it, since the system must judge image adequacy, capture the transverse/longitudinal planes and retain them for diagnosis.

sources.system: Autonomous lightweight ultrasound robot for liver sonography
sources.developer: Tsinghua University / Beijing Tsinghua Changgung Hospital
sources.title: Beyond hospital reach: Autonomous lightweight ultrasound robot for liver sonography (arXiv 2510.08106)
sources.claim: A 588-gram body-mounted autonomous ultrasound robot autonomously acquires standard liver imaging planes at expert level on volunteers and patients; it was run in a hospital ultrasound department, in a high-altitude under-resourced city, and outdoors.
sources.transferJustification: Related task is autonomous acquisition of standard liver planes; capturing and retaining those planes is the same act as recording suitable images, but it covers only a few planes of one organ, not a full study's documentation set.

sources.system: ABUS (automated breast ultrasound; e.g., Invenia ABUS, ACUSON ABVS)
sources.title: Automated Breast Ultrasound Screening for Dense Breasts (Ultrasonography, PMC6960307)
sources.claim: Automated breast ultrasound (ABUS) systems move the transducer automatically in a scan box to acquire hundreds of slices per breast volume, i.e. the image capture itself is machine-controlled rather than hand-guided.
sources.transferJustification: Related task is automated whole-breast image acquisition; the machine performs the sweep and generates the stored image set, though a technologist still positions the scan head on the breast between the three or more views.

sources.title: Automated Breast Ultrasonography (ABUS) in the Screening and Diagnostic Setting: Indications and Practical Use
sources.claim: After an ABUS acquisition the volume data is processed and transferred automatically to the interpretation workstation, so the recording and archiving step is performed by the machine rather than by the sonographer.
sources.transferJustification: Directly covers the storage/archiving half of this task for the automated breast exam; the acquisition half is covered by the same system's automated sweep.

sources.title: GE Healthcare Introduces Invenia Automated Breast Ultrasound (ABUS) 2.0 for Dense Breast Imaging
sources.claim: Invenia ABUS automated breast ultrasound is a commercial product installed at hundreds of clinical breast-imaging facilities worldwide, with a 2.0 generation launched for dense-breast screening.
sources.transferJustification: Establishes deployment maturity and the structured-facility (breast imaging center) setting in which the automated acquisition-and-archiving evidence above is used.

tasks.label: Clean, check, and maintain sonographic equipment, submitting maintenance requests or performing minor repairs as necessary.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: End-of-exam turnover in a hospital/clinic ultrasound room after a routine abdominal, OB, breast or vascular study: wipe residual gel from the transducer head and cable, apply an approved low-level disinfectant wipe and observe the wet contact time, wipe the console, keyboard, touchscreen and monitor, wipe the exam table and change linens, refill/replace the gel bottle in the warmer.

Reprocessing an endocavity (transvaginal/transrectal) or TEE probe after an invasive exam: remove the sheath, pre-clean at point of care, carry the probe to the reprocessing area, run cleaning and high-level disinfection (automated reprocessor or manual soak), rinse/dry, hang or store in the drying cabinet, and record the cycle for accreditation logs.

Scheduled deeper cleaning and equipment checks on the ultrasound system (start/end of day, weekly): thorough wipe-down of the cart, monitor arm and cable hooks; remove and clean or replace the air filter; inspect probe lenses, strain reliefs, cables and connector pins for cracks or delamination; check casters, brakes and power cord; verify monitor/image quality with a test or phantom; restock supplies (gel, wipes, covers, probe holders).

Cleaning and readying a portable/point-of-care unit after bedside exams in the ICU, ED or OR: wipe machine surfaces, probes and cables at the bedside, remove gel spills, disinfect handles and wheels before leaving an isolation room, then return the cart to its bay and plug it in to charge.

Minor troubleshooting and repairs during or between exams: swap a failed transducer, reseat or reroute a connector, reboot a frozen system, replace thermal printer paper or a fuse, replace a broken caster, probe holder or keyboard cover, tighten a monitor arm.

Handling a fault that exceeds minor repair: tag the unit out of service, move it to the service area, file a work order with biomedical engineering or the vendor, arrange a loaner, then verify function and image quality after the engineer's visit.

sources.system: Ethos Automated Ultrasound Probe Cleaner Disinfector
sources.title: Automation of Cleaning - CS Medical
sources.claim: Ethos (CS Medical) is an FDA-cleared benchtop automated cleaner-disinfector that performs both cleaning and high-level disinfection of soiled transvaginal, transrectal and surface ultrasound probes in a single 18-minute machine-controlled cycle.

sources.system: Ethos Automated Ultrasound Probe Cleaner Disinfector
sources.title: Ethos ® Automated Ultrasound Probe Cleaner Disinfector
sources.claim: With Ethos the probe is loaded soiled (only the cover removed, no manual pre-clean step) and the machine runs the validated cleaning and disinfection cycle, printing and logging the reprocessing record used for accreditation.

sources.system: TEEClean Automated TEE Probe Cleaner Disinfector
sources.title: CS Medical announces FDA clearance of TEEClean Automated TEE Probe Cleaner Disinfector
sources.claim: TEEClean is an FDA-cleared automated cleaner-disinfector dedicated to TEE probes: after loading, the device cleans, high-level disinfects for five minutes, runs five rinse cycles and prints a verification report; it is in routine hospital use for TEE reprocessing.

sources.title: trophon® Technology | Nanosonics
sources.claim: trophon is a widely deployed automated ultrasound probe high-level disinfection unit that converts hydrogen peroxide to mist inside a closed chamber once an operator loads the probe; it requires a manual gel-removal/pre-clean wipe before the cycle.

sources.system: Intelligent Autonomous Wiping and UV-C Disinfection Robot
sources.title: Transforming hospital sanitation: Autonomous robots for wiping and UV-C disinfection
sources.claim: A research mobile manipulator combining physical wiping with UV-C was assessed in a hospital: it navigates autonomously and uses a robot arm to wipe high-touch surfaces. It addresses generic room surfaces, not gel-soiled transducers, keyboards, touchscreens or cable connectors on imaging equipment.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: contact wiping/disinfection of hospital high-touch surfaces. Transfer to sonographic equipment fails: it is a prototype tested on flat room surfaces, with no evidence of gel removal from transducer lenses, wipe-and-dwell disinfection of consoles/keyboards, or safe handling of probes and cables.

sources.title: Somatic - Autonomous Bathroom Cleaning Robots
sources.claim: Somatic's bathroom cleaning robot autonomously sprays, wipes and rinses restroom fixtures and is deployed in hospitals and airports; its spray-based method and fixture-scale precision do not transfer to delicate ultrasound electronics.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous spray-and-wipe cleaning of hard surfaces in an institutional facility. Transfer fails for sonographic equipment: high-pressure disinfectant spray would damage transducer lenses, connectors, keyboards and touchscreens, and no probe handling is demonstrated.

sources.date: in use since c. 2010s; survey paper 2016
sources.title: A multicentre survey of the condition of ultrasound probes - PMC
sources.claim: Electronic probe testers such as ... are used to detect transducer element faults, but they are bench instruments operated by a technician on a probe that a person connects; no robotic system inspects an ultrasound system's cables, filters and image quality end to end.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: checking sonographic equipment condition. It covers only the electro-acoustic test of a hand-connected probe, not the visual inspection, filter cleaning, phantom imaging and restocking that make up the check instance, and its autonomy is not established.

tasks.label: Supervise or train students or other medical sonographers.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Clinical preceptor in a hospital or imaging-center ultrasound room observes a sonography student performing a study on a patient, watches the live image and probe handling, gives verbal corrections and coaching, and decides when the student may proceed unassisted.

Instructor in a program scan lab demonstrates transducer technique on a volunteer model or phantom (probe angle, pressure, imaging planes, knobology) and coaches students through repeated practice until they obtain diagnostic images.

Review of a trainee's completed image sets, worksheets, and preliminary findings after the exam: critiquing image quality and measurement accuracy, discussing pathology recognition, and completing competency checklists and evaluation forms.

Orienting a newly hired or cross-training sonographer to the department: protocols, machine presets, PACS workflow, scheduling, infection control, and patient-care expectations; monitoring their first weeks of independent cases.
Lead or senior sonographer conducts in-service education, journal-club or CME sessions, and staff meetings for the imaging team; answers technique questions and disseminates protocol changes.
Supervisory duties over sonography staff: assigning cases, monitoring productivity and QA metrics, counseling on performance issues, and documenting corrective action.

tasks.label: Perform medical procedures, such as administering oxygen, inserting and removing airways, taking vital signs, or giving emergency treatment, such as first aid or cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR).

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Routine vital signs (blood pressure, pulse, sometimes SpO2/temperature) taken on a cooperative, ambulatory outpatient in an imaging suite or prep area before/after an echocardiogram, vascular, or abdominal ultrasound; the patient sits or lies still and can present an arm; values are recorded in the study record.

Vital signs and basic monitoring on a non-ambulatory patient during a portable/bedside exam (ICU, ED, med-surg bed, stretcher or wheelchair): patient encumbered by IV lines, dressings, telemetry, sometimes obese, confused or unable to move an arm; the sonographer must pick a usable limb, place cuff/probe, and act on abnormal values.

Repeated vital-sign measurement and monitoring during a dynamic protocol - exercise treadmill or dobutamine stress echo, or a contrast-enhanced study - with BP and heart rate taken at each stage on a moving or pharmacologically stressed patient while watching for symptoms.

Patient becomes unwell during a scan (vasovagal near-syncope, hypotension, nausea, hypoglycemia, chest pain): the sonographer stops the exam, repositions the patient and table, administers supplemental oxygen by nasal cannula or mask, takes vitals, gives basic first aid, and summons help.

Acute emergency in the imaging department: the patient arrests or stops breathing; the sonographer calls a code, checks responsiveness and pulse, begins chest compressions, brings the AED/crash cart, and assists with bag-mask ventilation or oral airway insertion until the code team arrives.

sources.title: Performance, Safety, and Patient Experience of an Autonomous Robotic Phlebotomy Device: A Multicenter Trial (Clinical Chemistry)
sources.claim: Aletta, an autonomous robotic phlebotomy device, performs the whole venipuncture sequence on a seated outpatient's presented arm at a purpose-built station, including automatically applying the tourniquet (pressure band) to the arm, imaging-guided needle insertion, and bandaging.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated blood draw. It substantiates that a machine can autonomously handle a cooperative outpatient's arm presented in a fixture and apply an inflatable band and sensors to it - the physical act underlying cuff-based vital-sign measurement - at higher precision than a BP/pulse reading requires, in the same outpatient clinical setting.

sources.title: Performance, Safety, and Patient Experience of an Autonomous Robotic Phlebotomy Device: A Multicenter Trial (Clinical Chemistry)
sources.claim: In routine use in Dutch outpatient phlebotomy departments the device achieved a 94.5% first-stick success rate over 1633 patients with a 0.6% mild adverse-event rate, with one trained professional supervising up to three devices (limited intervention).
sources.transferJustification: Same related task (automated blood draw); establishes worker-quality reliability and supervision-only intervention for an autonomous machine performing a contact procedure on a patient's fixtured arm.

sources.title: Collaborative study identifies method to make blood pressure monitoring more accessible (Emory University)
sources.claim: FDA-cleared self-service health stations autonomously measure blood pressure and pulse on a cooperative person whose arm is placed in the station's fixed cuff; a JAMA Cardiology analysis used nearly 1.3 million adult users' kiosk blood-pressure measurements, indicating clinically usable output at scale.
sources.transferJustification: Same task (taking vital signs), performed by a machine-controlled station that inflates a cuff on the presented arm, computes blood pressure and pulse and records the result without a health worker; only the fixtured presentation of the arm differs from the worker's version.

sources.title: About - Pursuant Health
sources.claim: These automated vital-sign stations are a mature, widely fielded product line rather than a prototype: over 4,600 installations that have performed hundreds of millions of screenings including blood pressure, pulse and weight.
sources.transferJustification: Same task (measuring vital signs); establishes deployment maturity of the automated measurement station cited above.

sources.system: Dr. Spot (Boston Dynamics Spot with vital-sign camera payload)
sources.title: Mobile Robotic Platform for Contactless Vital Sign Monitoring (Cyborg and Bionic Systems)
sources.claim: The leading mobile-robot approach to hospital vital-sign taking (Dr. Spot, tested at Brigham and Women's Hospital) is contactless and driven by a human operator, so it does not show autonomous vital-sign taking at a patient's bedside.

sources.title: LUCAS 3, v3.1 chest compression system | Stryker
sources.claim: Mechanical CPR systems deliver compressions only after rescuers recognize arrest and manually position patient and device; they are an adjunct within a human-run resuscitation, not an autonomous responder.

sources.title: Development of artificial intelligence-driven biosignal-sensitive cardiopulmonary resuscitation robot (Resuscitation)
sources.claim: An AI-driven CPR robot that adapts compressions to biosignals has only been shown as a proof of concept in pigs, not in human cardiac arrest response.

sources.title: A soft robotic device for rapid and self-guided intubation (Science Translational Medicine)
sources.claim: The most advanced self-guiding airway device is a soft robotic intubation aid demonstrated in manikins and cadavers and inserted by a person, not a system that places an airway autonomously in a live patient.

tasks.label: Maintain stock and supplies, preparing supplies for special examinations and ordering supplies when necessary.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Routine restock of ultrasound exam/procedure rooms in a hospital imaging department or outpatient clinic: pulling gel bottles and refilling gel warmers, boxes of transducer covers, disinfectant wipes/high-level disinfection supplies, gloves, towels, linens, ECG electrodes and paper from the department supply room and placing them into room cabinets, drawers, wall bins and cart drawers between patients.

Preparing supplies for a special examination: assembling and setting up what a specific study needs before the physician arrives - sterile biopsy/paracentesis tray, sterile transducer cover and sterile gel packets, needle guide, drapes, specimen containers, contrast agent kit, checking package integrity and expiration dates and opening items onto a sterile field in the procedure room.

Periodic stock/par-level check and ordering: walking the department supply room and exam rooms, counting or scanning labeled bins, noting low, missing, expired or recalled items, and entering a requisition in the materials-management system or notifying central supply.

Receiving and putting away deliveries: cartons of gel, covers, kits and linens arrive from central supply or a vendor at the department; the sonographer opens cartons, verifies contents against the packing slip, stocks storeroom shelves with first-expire-first-out rotation, and breaks down and discards packaging.

Stocking the portable/mobile setup: loading gel, covers, wipes, linens, kits and cleaning supplies onto a portable ultrasound cart (or a mobile-service vehicle) before ICU/OR/bedside rounds, and replenishing the cart between rounds in hospital corridors and patient units.

sources.title: Amazon debuts its first-ever warehouse robot — 'Vulcan' — with a sense of touch
sources.claim: Amazon's Vulcan robot autonomously picks and stows individual inventory items into shelf bins at production fulfillment centers, at speeds comparable ..., covering about 75% of the item catalog.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: warehouse stow. Placing loose consumable items into labeled shelf bins at a station where the storage pod is presented to the robot is the same physical operation as restocking supply-room bins, with comparable object mix (boxed, bagged, bottled small goods) and precision.

sources.title: ORB: Operating Room Bot, Automating Operating Room Logistics through Mobile Manipulation
sources.claim: A mobile manipulator restocked operating-room supplies from a cart onto marked storage-shelf bins with 96% success in a simulated OR setup using ArUco-marked bins.
sources.transferJustification: Same task (hospital supply restocking and retrieval), but demonstrated only in a laboratory 'simulated OR setup' with fiducial-marked bins and three trained object classes, i.e. an environment engineered around the machine.

sources.title: AI Flying Off the Shelves: Restocking Robot Rolls Out to Hundreds of Japanese Convenience Stores
sources.claim: Telexistence's TX SCARA autonomously restocks beverage shelves in FamilyMart convenience stores from a fixed track installation, scanning shelves to find low stock, with ~98% autonomous success and rare remote-operator recovery; rolled out to 300 stores.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: retail shelf restocking. Transfer is limited: the robot is rail-mounted at one purpose-built refrigerated case and handles a single, standardized product class, so it shows machine-side restocking only where the workspace is built around the robot.

sources.title: Schnuck Markets deploys Simbe inventory tracking AMRs chainwide
sources.claim: Simbe's Tally autonomously navigates grocery store aisles scanning shelves; at Schnucks its real-time inventory data was integrated into the chain's automated replenishment/ordering system across the chain.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: shelf inventory audit and reorder. Counting labeled bins/facings on open shelving in an institution-controlled facility and generating replenishment orders is the same work as a par-level check in a department supply room, where bins carry printed/QR labels.

sources.title: From case unloading to picking and beyond with DHL and Boston Dynamics
sources.claim: Boston Dynamics' Stretch autonomously unloads cases from trucks and containers in DHL warehouses at roughly 700 cases per hour, with ten units deployed across three countries by mid-2025.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: receiving cartons. Handling and moving delivered cases of goods is the carton-handling half of receiving supply deliveries; it is done where the trailer/conveyor presents the load to the machine.

sources.title: Automated Pharmacy Storage System - Swisslog BoxPicker
sources.claim: Swisslog's BoxPicker is a robotic high-density storage and retrieval system used in hospital pharmacies that fully automates putting medication packages into stock and picking them, with digitized inventory and first-expire-first-out handling.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: stock put-away and inventory control inside a hospital. Boxed medical goods are loaded at an input station and the machine stores, tracks and rotates them by expiry — the same stock-keeping output as shelving supplies, achieved inside a purpose-built enclosure.

sources.title: Ballad Health expands patient safety with new robotic pharmacy technology
sources.claim: Omnicell IVX Station robotic compounding systems that prepare sterile doses under aseptic conditions are installed and running in a hospital central-fill pharmacy at Ballad Health.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: aseptic preparation of sterile disposables. The robot manipulates syringes, needles, vials and bags inside an ISO-classified enclosure — comparable objects, sterility requirement and precision to assembling the sterile consumable set for an ultrasound-guided procedure, but only inside a purpose-built cell.

sources.title: Swisslog Healthcare Partners with Diligent Robotics to Enhance Hospital Logistics
sources.claim: Diligent Robotics' Moxi mobile manipulator is deployed in more than 25 ... for autonomous point-to-point delivery of supplies, medications and lab samples, with over one million deliveries completed; its hospital work is transport, not item-level shelf stocking.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: intra-hospital supply transport. It establishes what robots actually do in the E2 clinical setting (fetch and deliver sealed items), and by omission that no fielded hospital robot stocks exam-room cabinets item by item.

sources.system: Autonomous supermarket stocking mobile manipulator (Ridgeback/Tiago-class platform)
sources.title: From Pixels to Shelf: An Integrated Robotic System for Autonomous Supermarket Stocking with a Mobile Manipulator
sources.claim: An integrated mobile-manipulator shelf-stocking system achieved over 98% pick-and-place success across more than 700 stocking events, but only in laboratory experiments replicating supermarket conditions with ArUco-marked shelves, and the authors report performance still inferior to human workers.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: shelf stocking of packaged consumer goods, comparable in size and grasping difficulty to gel bottles and boxes of covers; it supports stocking only where shelves are marked and the scene is engineered, and the authors state it is not yet at human worker quality.
